dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-habtoor-city.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors who work with Middle Years students from the Jumeirah and canal corridor: subject specialists who have marked against MYP criterion descriptors, know how an MYP 5 report converts into Diploma subject choices, and teach in the evening slots Al Habtoor City families can actually keep.

intro.heading: Why this search comes from Al Habtoor City in particular
paragraphs: Al Habtoor City is three residential towers on the Dubai Water Canal, wedged between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Habtoor Palace, with Business Bay on one side and Al Safa and Al Wasl on the other. It has no school inside it. Every family living there drives out, and that single fact shapes the whole tutoring question. A parent in a villa community can plausibly ask a neighbour's cousin who teaches at the local school. A parent in a tower on the canal is asking a different question: who, within a sensible radius, actually knows the MYP well enough to be useful, and how long will they spend in a car getting to us?

The honest answer is that the radius is the wrong unit. Dubai's Middle Years cohort is thinly spread. KHDA's 2024-25 figures put 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum taking 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian schools 26 per cent, American 14 per cent and International Baccalaureate schools 7 per cent. The IB share is the smallest of the four. Within it, the Middle Years Programme is smaller again, because several Dubai IB schools run a British middle school and only pick the IB up at Diploma. So the pool of people near Al Habtoor City who have taught MYP Individuals and Societies, or marked an MYP Design portfolio, is small enough that geography stops being a useful filter.

This page is written as a comparison, because that is the question Al Habtoor City parents keep asking. If we lived in Al Safa instead, or in Business Bay, or across in Jumeirah 1, would the answer change? The schools change. The drive changes. The number of tutors advertising locally changes. What does not change is the shape of the problem: an MYP 4 student losing marks on criterion C in Sciences needs someone who has read the Sciences criterion C descriptors, and that person is almost never the nearest available adult with a maths degree.

The MYP is also the programme most often misdiagnosed at home. There are no public exam papers to point at, grades arrive as criterion letters with numbers out of eight, and the final 1-7 subject grade comes from a published grade boundary table your child's school applies. A parent looking at "Criterion B: 4" has no way of knowing whether that is a content gap, a command-term problem, or a presentation issue in how the work was written up. A tutor who has actually marked MYP work can tell the difference inside one lesson, and that diagnosis is most of the value.

So the practical answer for an Al Habtoor City family is this. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled around the drive home rather than inside it. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. What you get instead is a match on the subject group and the criterion, and a 7pm slot that survives a bad evening on Sheikh Zayed Road.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-habtoor-city.programmesIntro: Al Habtoor City children sit in several different programmes depending on which gate the car goes to in the morning. These are the four routes that matter most in this corridor, and what tutoring looks like inside each.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups studied together, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight. There is no end-of-year paper in most subjects; the grade is built from tasks across the year, which means a weak term is hard to recover from later. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project and, in some schools, external eAssessment. Tutoring here is mostly about criterion literacy: teaching a student to read what criterion C asks for and answer that, rather than writing more.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP is the minority middle-school route even inside IB schools, because several continuum schools run IGCSE at 16 and only take the IB up again at Diploma. For an Al Habtoor City family that means a child in MYP 4 may have classmates heading for IGCSE and classmates heading straight for the Diploma, and the subject choices made in MYP 4 start to diverge accordingly.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment weighted between 20 and 25 per cent of the grade. UAE schools sit the May session, with a second session in November. The step up from MYP is less about content than about volume: a DP1 student is suddenly managing six separate internal deadlines alongside the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma results feed directly into the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process and into admissions at the Dubai campuses of overseas universities. The Ministry publishes a clear subject-and-grade rule for the British track, but no published IB points threshold we have been able to read on moe.gov.ae, so any figure you are quoted for the IB should be checked against the Ministry or the school's own counsellor.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than subjects, finishing with the Grade 5 Exhibition. Reports describe approaches to learning rather than marks, which is exactly why parents moving from a British or Indian primary find them hard to read. Tutoring at this stage is usually reading fluency, number sense and written expression, built so it supports the inquiry rather than running a parallel curriculum.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools within reach of the canal corridor run the PYP, including Jumeirah Baccalaureate School in Al Safa and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai in Al Jaddaf. Families who intend to stay in the IB through to Diploma benefit from keeping the inquiry habits intact; families who expect a move into a British school at Year 7 usually want a quiet programme of number and spelling work alongside.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year, externally examined alternative to MYP 4 and 5, taken at most British-curriculum schools in Dubai. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics; Pearson codes look like 4MA1. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Tutoring is paper-shaped: past papers, mark schemes and command terms, with a tier decision in some Cambridge and Pearson subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Al Habtoor City sits inside a stretch of Dubai dominated by British schools, so plenty of children in the towers are doing IGCSE rather than MYP. The two programmes assess almost nothing the same way, and a tutor who teaches one competently is not automatically useful for the other, which is the single most common mismatch we see in this corridor.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-habtoor-city.subjectsIntro: MYP students study all eight groups at once, so the request we get from Al Habtoor City is rarely a whole subject. It is one criterion inside one group. These are the places marks actually go missing.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where capable students stall, because it wants a general rule justified, not a correct answer. The Extended pathway in MYP 4 and 5 is also the gate to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level later.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.levels: Integrated or separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics
subjects.description: Criterion B asks for a method a stranger could repeat, criterion C for analysis and evaluation of the student's own data. Most lost marks sit in criterion C: the graph is drawn, the trend is described, and the evaluation of method limitations never arrives. We teach that section as a structure, not as a writing task.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criterion A rewards knowledge of specific terminology and examples; criterion D wants evaluated sources and a defensible judgement. Students raised on a British history curriculum tend to narrate. The fix is command-term drilling: analyse, evaluate and justify ask for three different shapes of paragraph, and MYP marking notices which one arrived.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.levels: English, plus other first languages by school
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Criterion A is the hard one because it asks for interpretation supported by close reference, not summary. The practical work is annotation discipline on unseen extracts, and learning to write about how a writer builds an effect rather than what happens in the passage.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.levels: Phases 1-6, usually French, Spanish or Arabic
subjects.description: Four criteria across listening, reading, speaking and writing, with the phase deciding the expected standard. The common Dubai problem is a child placed in a phase above their comfort because of years of exposure rather than measured ability. Tutoring tends to be phase-appropriate output practice and a lot of structured speaking.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The portfolio is the assessment, and it fails on documentation rather than on making. Students build a working product and lose criterion A marks for a thin research stage. We work on the design cycle write-up, which is where almost all the available marks sit.

subjects.name: MYP Arabic
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Support here is usually reading fluency in Standard Arabic for first-language students and vocabulary building plus script confidence for additional-language students.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Marked on knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on performance. The written and reflective criteria are often the ones that pull a grade down, since practical ability does not carry the whole mark. Support is normally short and focused on the planning and reflection documents.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, responding. As in Design, the process journal carries the marks. A student with real ability can sit at a 4 because the developmental record is thin. Tutoring is journal structure, artist research and the language of critical response rather than technique coaching.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: The capstone: a self-directed project with a process journal and a report, externally moderated. A supervisor at school signs off the process. A tutor may teach planning, research method, referencing and reflection, and may give feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write, draft or produce any part of the project itself.

sections.heading: What an MYP tutor search from Al Habtoor City is actually asking
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in Al Habtoor City means, in practice, one-to-one teaching in one of the eight MYP subject groups for a student in MYP 1 to MYP 5, delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time. There is no school inside Al Habtoor City, so there is no local teacher pool attached to the development. The useful filter is subject group and criterion, not distance.

That answer sounds like a dodge until you count. Dubai's IB schools hold roughly 7 per cent of private school enrolment, and only some of those carry the MYP through to age 16 rather than switching to IGCSE. A parent searching for someone nearby who has marked MYP Sciences criterion C is therefore drawing from a thin pool, and the people advertising most visibly in a given neighbourhood are rarely the specialists. The correct response to a thin local pool is to widen the pool, not to lower the specification.

The second thing the search is asking is about time. A family in a canal tower is doing two school runs a day on Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Safa's side streets. If a tutor also has to make that drive, the session costs an hour of travel at both ends, that hour gets priced in, and the slot becomes fragile: one accident on the trunk and the lesson is gone. Removing the journey removes the fragility, which is the practical argument before any argument about teaching quality.

So the honest framing for this page is a comparison rather than a sales pitch. Al Habtoor City, Business Bay, Al Safa and Al Wasl are four very different places to live and four almost identical places to buy MYP tutoring, because the thing that is scarce is subject expertise and the thing that is abundant is bandwidth.

sections.heading: Al Habtoor City against the next neighbourhood over
paragraphs: This is the comparison parents in the towers actually want. Four areas, all within fifteen minutes of each other in the middle of the night and forty-five in the evening, with genuinely different school access and genuinely different local tutor markets. The table below sets out what changes between them and what does not.

What changes is school access and the realistic earliest start. From Al Safa or Al Wasl, where the school gate is a five-minute drive, a 4.30pm session is a reasonable thing to book for the whole term. From Al Habtoor City, Business Bay or a Palm frond, the same booking will be missed often enough to be annoying, and a 6pm or 7pm slot is the sensible choice. That has nothing to do with the tutor and everything to do with the road.

What does not change is the thing you are shopping for. In all four areas, the number of locally available adults who have marked an MYP Design portfolio or taught Individuals and Societies criterion D is small. In all four, the quoted in-home rate carries a travel premium. In all four, the Personal Project in MYP 5 has to be the student's own work. Move house across the canal and the answer to the tutoring question stays the same; only the start time moves.

There is one real difference worth naming. Villa communities in Al Safa and Al Wasl have informal tutoring networks that tower developments do not, so parents there hear recommendations more easily. That is a difference in information flow, not in quality, and it is worth remembering when a neighbour's recommendation is competing with a subject specialist you have actually trialled.

sections.heading: MYP criteria by letter, and where a 5 turns into a 7
paragraphs: Every MYP subject is marked against four criteria, each out of eight, and the subject's 1-7 grade comes from the total against a published boundary table the school applies. This is the single most useful thing a parent can learn, because it turns a vague report comment into a specific target. A student sitting on 5s across the board is not weak; they are usually strong on one criterion and systematically missing what another criterion asks for.

The pattern is consistent enough to be diagnostic. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, rewards accurate subject terminology and worked application. Students who revise content do well here. Criterion B rewards process: in Sciences a repeatable method, in Mathematics a justified general rule, in Design a research stage with real analysis. Criterion C rewards the handling of results or the making of the thing. Criterion D rewards evaluation and reflection, and it is the most commonly abandoned, because it comes last and students run out of time.

The highest-yield work in a tutoring session is therefore usually not more content. It is reading the actual descriptor for the band above the one the student is in, and rewriting one paragraph of their own recent work to match it. Students find this startling the first time. The descriptor for a 7-8 band in criterion D almost never asks for more words; it asks for a judgement that is justified against the evidence the student themselves produced.

The table below sets out what each criterion is called across the subject groups most often requested from this corridor, with the mark allocation and what the top band is asking for. Exact criterion names and strands are set by the current subject guide, and your child's school is the authority on which version it is running.

sections.heading: What Middle Years tutoring costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure, because that is what a family budgets. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate work puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 for a mid-tier tutor, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published monthly packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. The gap between those two package prices is the travel.

Converted to an hourly view, the market splits into recognisable tiers. University-student and budget online tutoring is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit between AED 150 and AED 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted between AED 180 and AED 500, with Bestimate's band at AED 180 to AED 350. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tutoring reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

Those are market figures published by other providers, not IB Gram prices, and they are worth checking yourself before you accept any quote. What a parent can verify is narrower than it looks: the stated rate, whether it is per hour or per lesson, whether travel is inside or outside the number, the cancellation terms, and what happens if the match is wrong. Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for Dubai publish no price at all, so a provider that gives you a number before the call is already doing something unusual.

For a Middle Years student the volume question matters more than the rate. MYP marks accumulate across the year from classwork, so one weekly hour sustained over a term usually does more than a crash block before a report. That makes the cheaper end of the mid tier, held for longer, a better buy than a short burst of premium support, and it is the opposite of what families instinctively do.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project: a self-directed piece of work with a goal the student sets, a process journal kept across the year, and a report that is externally moderated. It is the first time most IB students carry sole responsibility for a long piece of work, and it is the first place academic honesty stops being an abstraction.

The boundary is simple to state and routinely broken in this market. A tutor may teach research method, referencing conventions, how to evaluate a source, how to keep a process journal that actually evidences development, and how to write a reflection that answers the criterion. A tutor may read the student's own draft and say where a paragraph fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write any part of the project, may not restructure a draft on the student's behalf, and may not supply a model report to be adapted. One provider in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments. That is a malpractice trigger for the student, not a shortcut.

We say this plainly on every page because the risk sits with your child, not with the provider. A moderator who sees a report written in an adult register, or a process journal that shows no development, has grounds to question authenticity, and the school's supervisor is the person who has to sign the process off. The practical defence is a journal that shows real, dated, sometimes messy progress, which is exactly what good coaching produces and ghostwriting destroys.

A useful test for parents considering any provider: ask what their tutor will do with a weak draft. The honest answer is that they will mark it against the descriptor and send the student back to rewrite it. Any answer involving the tutor improving the text directly is an answer about the provider's risk appetite, not about teaching.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the Diploma your MYP 4 student has not chosen yet
paragraphs: Middle Years decisions are quietly exam decisions. A student in MYP 4 picking the Standard rather than Extended mathematics pathway has narrowed what they can comfortably take at Higher Level in the Diploma two years later. By the time the consequence is visible, in DP1, the gap is a term of work rather than a conversation.

The calendar behind that is worth knowing even in MYP 3. UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, with a second session in November. Diploma Internal Assessments are due to school deadlines many months before the papers, so a DP2 student is finishing coursework in the same window they should be revising. For students who take the British route at 16 instead, Cambridge runs June and November series in the UAE, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only and is not a UAE route.

One detail parents rarely hear: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge's own exams officers' guide states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That is the school's job, but it is a good question to ask. For Pearson, the November 2026 final International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The table counts the MYP 5 year backwards, because that is the year where a drifting student becomes a problem that a single term cannot fix. IB session dates are not restated here; confirm them with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, since those are the only authorities on them.

sections.heading: KHDA, the inspection report and the mandatory UAE subjects
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. If you move emirate, your regulator changes, and so does the inspection framework your school is judged under.

KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Parents in Al Habtoor City read those bands as a ranking, which is only half useful. The more informative part of a report is the subject-level and phase-level judgement underneath the headline: a school rated Good overall may be Very Good in secondary English and Acceptable in secondary mathematics, and that distinction tells you exactly where private support is likely to be needed. Read the subject tables, not the badge.

Alongside the licensed curriculum, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The rules are specific. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic must be the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

Two further points matter if you are buying support in these subjects. KHDA requires schools to ensure all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach them, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That shapes what honest tutoring in Arabic or Islamic Education looks like: reinforcing the school's own material and building language fluency, not importing a parallel syllabus. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry permit, approval or accreditation, and describes none.

sections.heading: What happens when nobody local covers the subject group you need
paragraphs: The genuinely difficult requests from this corridor are not mathematics. They are MYP Design with a digital design focus, Language Acquisition in a specific phase, Individuals and Societies with an Economics strand, and Arabic as a first language for a student who has been in an English-medium school since nursery. Those are the subjects where a local search returns nobody useful, and where families most often settle for a generalist.

Our position on this is disclosed rather than hidden. If no suitable specialist is free in the slot you want, you are told so, with the earliest realistic alternative. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable for a niche subject, the match may be a tutor based elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, and that is stated before you book rather than concealed behind a local-sounding phone number. Two providers ranking for Dubai searches route UAE parents to Indian numbers without saying so; the delivery is the same, but hiding it is a trust problem.

The fallback matters most in two situations. The first is a mid-year arrival into MYP 4, where a student is behind in three subject groups at once and sequencing matters more than intensity. The second is MYP 5 in the second half of the year, where the Personal Project, the route decision and content gaps are all live at once. In both cases the useful first step is a free trial lesson used as a diagnostic, not as a sales call.

If the match is wrong, say so after the first paid session and you are matched again. That is a more useful promise than any claim about tutor quality, because it is the only one you can test cheaply. No tutor, however experienced, can guarantee a grade, and any provider offering one is telling you something about their marketing rather than their teaching.

process.title: Free trial lesson used as a diagnostic

process.title: Weekly slot built around the drive home

When the next report arrives, you can see whether the criterion that was targeted actually moved, which is the only honest measure of whether the tutoring is working.

A family in a canal tower can hold a 7pm Tuesday for a whole term, which is the thing that actually produces progress in a programme where marks accumulate week by week rather than arriving in one examination.

faqs.question: Is there an MYP tutor who actually lives near Al Habtoor City?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but it is the wrong question. Al Habtoor City has no school inside it, and IB schools account for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, with the Middle Years Programme a subset of that again. The number of adults within a short drive who have marked MYP criterion descriptors is small. Searching by distance filters out the people who can help and keeps the people who are merely available. Lessons here run online, one-to-one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which removes distance from the decision entirely and lets you choose on subject group instead.

faqs.question: Would the answer be different if we lived in Al Safa or Al Wasl instead?
faqs.answer: The start time would change; the recommendation would not. From Al Safa or Al Wasl the school gate is a few minutes away, so a 4.30pm session is realistic across a whole term. From a canal tower, Business Bay or a Palm frond, 6pm or later is the slot that survives the week. What stays identical in all four areas is the scarcity of MYP subject specialists, the travel premium inside in-home quotes, and the requirement that the Personal Project be the student's own work. Villa areas do have better informal recommendation networks, which is an information difference rather than a quality one.

faqs.question: What do the criterion letters on my child's MYP report mean?
faqs.answer: Each MYP subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each out of eight, and the school converts the total using a published boundary table into the 1-7 subject grade. Broadly, A is knowing and understanding, B is process or investigation, C is communicating or processing results, and D is evaluation and reflection. A student on 5s is usually strong on one criterion and systematically missing what another asks for. That is why the most productive first tutoring session rewrites one paragraph of the student's own recent work against the descriptor for the band above.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP 5 Personal Project without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach research method, referencing, source evaluation, process-journal discipline and reflective writing, and may read the student's own draft and say where it fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write, draft or restructure any part of the project, and may not supply a model report to adapt. The school supervisor remains the authority on the process. The defensible version produces a journal showing dated, sometimes untidy development, which is also what a moderator expects to see from genuine work.

faqs.question: How much should MYP tutoring cost a family in the canal corridor?
faqs.answer: Budget monthly rather than hourly. Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts a weekly one-hour session at about AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Published packages in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. For Middle Years students, a cheaper rate sustained across a term usually beats a short premium block.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tutoring in Dubai more expensive than online?
faqs.answer: Because the car is in the price. Published in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and monthly packages show the same gap. A tutor crossing from Al Barsha to Al Habtoor City at 5pm spends an hour travelling for a one-hour lesson, and that time is billed to someone. You are also buying a fragile slot, since one incident on Sheikh Zayed Road cancels the session. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 4 and has to choose Standard or Extended maths. Does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more than the school conversation usually suggests. The Extended pathway in MYP 4 and 5 is the comfortable route into Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the Diploma, and students who take Standard and then aim at Higher Level AA typically arrive in DP1 with a term of algebraic fluency to make up. If your child is considering engineering, economics, physics or mathematics at university, treat the MYP 4 decision as a Diploma decision. If they are not, Standard is a perfectly sound choice and Applications and Interpretation is a real route.

faqs.question: Will five years of MYP leave my child ready for the Diploma workload?
faqs.answer: It prepares them well for the thinking and badly for the volume. MYP students arrive in DP1 comfortable with inquiry, extended writing and reflection, which IGCSE students often are not. What catches them is load: six subjects, three Internal Assessments running at once, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, all with school deadlines months before the examination session. The students who struggle are usually organised badly rather than taught badly, which is why MYP 5 bridging work tends to focus on content gaps in the intended Higher Level subjects plus deadline management.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Habtoor City actually run the Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: The nearest IB continuum option is Jumeirah Baccalaureate School in Al Safa. Across the canal, Swiss International Scientific School Dubai in Al Jaddaf and North London Collegiate School Dubai in Sobha Hartland sit in the same cluster, and Raffles World Academy in Umm Suqeim and Dubai International Academy Al Barsha are the deeper IB provision slightly further out. Most of the schools immediately around Al Habtoor City are British curriculum and run IGCSE at 16 instead. These schools are named as local context; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Does a Middle Years tutor working with an Al Habtoor City family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee, applied for through its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection rating tell me about whether we need a tutor?
faqs.answer: Less than the detail underneath it. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, but the headline band is an average across phases and subjects. A school rated Good overall can be Very Good in secondary English and Acceptable in secondary mathematics, and that second line is the one that predicts where your child will need help. Read the subject and phase tables in the published report rather than the badge, then compare them against the criterion letters on your child's own report card.

faqs.question: My child has Arabic as a mandatory subject and is drowning in it. What can be done?
faqs.answer: Arabic is required in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the expectations and language of instruction differ. For additional-language students the usual gap is script confidence and vocabulary rather than grammar, and sustained short sessions work better than intensive blocks. One constraint worth knowing: for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so honest support reinforces the school's own material rather than importing another syllabus.

faqs.question: Can we book a session for 4.30pm if we live in one of the canal towers?
faqs.answer: You can book it, but think about whether you will keep it. Al Habtoor City families are doing a school run that ends on Sheikh Zayed Road or the canal crossings between 4pm and 6pm, and a 4.30pm start gets missed often enough to disrupt the rhythm that makes Middle Years tutoring work. Most families in the towers settle on 6pm or 7pm, which holds for a whole term. Lessons are recorded, so a genuinely lost evening is recoverable, but a slot you can actually keep is worth more than an early one you cannot.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is available for the subject group we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with the earliest realistic alternative, rather than matched to a generalist. The hardest requests from this corridor are MYP Design with a digital focus, Language Acquisition in a specific phase, the Economics strand of Individuals and Societies, and first-language Arabic for a student schooled in English. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match may be a tutor based elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, and that is stated before you book. If a match turns out to be wrong after the first paid session, you are matched again.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring halfway through the MYP 5 year?
faqs.answer: No, but the sequencing changes. In the second half of MYP 5 the Personal Project, the route decision at 16 and any content gaps are all live at the same time, so the first job is deciding what to leave alone. Usually that means stabilising the Personal Project process, closing gaps only in the subjects the student intends to carry at Higher Level or into IGCSE, and accepting that one or two criterion scores will not move this year. A trial lesson used as a diagnostic is the quickest way to see which of those applies.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-habtoor-city.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB MYP tutor in Al Habtoor City, the useful first move is to read out what the last report actually said: which subject group, which criterion letter, which task went wrong. That takes fifteen minutes and produces a specific match rather than an approximate one. From there, a free trial lesson puts your child's own marked work in front of a subject specialist, and you get a written note on which criterion is costing marks before anything is paid. Lessons run online, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time, in a slot that survives the evening drive. Whether you live on the canal, in Al Safa or across in Business Bay, that is the same answer, and it is the honest one.

intro.heading: The timetable problem comes before the teaching problem
paragraphs: Parents in Al Jaddaf do not usually abandon tutoring because the tutor was poor. They abandon it because the session was at the wrong time. A Year 8 student who gets home at 16:10, eats, and sits down at 17:30 for an hour is working at a sensible point in their day. The same student at 19:30, after football and homework, is present but not learning, and by the fifth week somebody quietly cancels. That is the most common failure in middle-school tutoring and it is a scheduling failure.

The Middle Years Programme makes this worse than it would otherwise be, for a reason specific to how it is assessed. There is no external exam looming in MYP Years 1 to 4, so nothing forces urgency, and a session that is merely inconvenient gets dropped rather than moved. By the time MYP Year 5 arrives with the Personal Project and the transition to the Diploma, two years of small gaps have become a real one. Choosing a slot that survives a term is therefore a bigger decision than it looks.

So this page starts with the clock. Al Jaddaf sits on the creek between Dubai Healthcare City and Ras Al Khor, with Culture Village to the north, Festival City across the water and Sobha Hartland inland to the south. Those four directions produce four different arrival times, because a creek-side campus five minutes away and a Festival City school on the far side of the Garhoud crossing do not deliver a child home at the same hour, whatever the bell says.

What makes online delivery useful here is not convenience in the abstract. It is that a session which requires no travel by anybody can start at 16:30 and finish before the evening collapses, and can be moved by twenty minutes on a day when the bus is late without anyone losing a journey. A tutor driving to the creek cannot do that; the trip is committed hours in advance. The flexibility is the point, not the novelty.

Below: what MYP actually assesses and why Year 9 can look like nothing is being measured, the eight subject groups and the four criteria each one is marked against, the gap that opens between MYP and the Diploma, the Personal Project and the firm limits on a tutor's involvement, the mandatory UAE subjects running alongside, and a realistic weekly shape for an Al Jaddaf household. There is also what middle-school support costs in this market, with every AED figure attributed to the provider that published it, because MYP rates sit below Diploma rates and that fact alone should change when a family spends. Teaching is delivered one to one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.programmesIntro: The MYP sits in the middle of a three-stage IB school career, and what tutoring is for differs sharply at each stage. Here is what each one asks and where support is worth buying.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, physical and health education, and design. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, every criterion marked out of eight, and the grades a student sees are built from those criterion scores rather than from test percentages. MYP Year 5 culminates in the Personal Project.
programmes.countryNote: In the schools around Al Jaddaf the MYP years are where tutoring demand is lowest and the return on it is highest. There is no external exam to create pressure, so families wait. Meanwhile the habits that decide Diploma grades, particularly structured writing and the processing and evaluating criterion in sciences, are being built or not built. A session a week in MYP Year 4 costs less than a term of Year 13 rescue work.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma that most MYP students progress to, with six subjects taken at Higher or Standard Level alongside Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment moves to external papers with internal assessments attached to each subject, which is a different kind of demand from criterion-based MYP marking.
programmes.countryNote: The transition out of MYP is where the gaps show. Students arrive in the Diploma having been assessed against descriptors for five years and meet mark schemes, command terms and timed papers for the first time. Schools inland from the creek, with larger Diploma cohorts, tend to bridge this explicitly; smaller campuses often cannot, which is why a bridging block in the summer before DP1 is worth considering.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The inquiry-led primary programme that feeds the MYP, organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than discrete subjects, finishing with the Exhibition. Literacy and numeracy foundations are built here, and they are the floor under everything the MYP later assesses.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving into Al Jaddaf from a non-IB system frequently arrive at the PYP-to-MYP boundary, and the adjustment is real: a child used to tests and ranks meets criteria and descriptors. Two or three sessions explaining how MYP marking works, to the parent as much as the student, prevents a term of misreading reports as worse than they are.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.subjectsIntro: MYP students take all eight subject groups every year, which is why the programme feels broad and why tutoring needs a clear target. Below is what each group assesses and where support tends to be needed.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, statistics and probability, assessed on knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The investigating patterns criterion is where marks are lost: students find the pattern and never generalise or justify it.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Integrated or discrete biology, chemistry and physics, assessed on knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Processing and evaluating is the criterion that predicts Diploma science grades, because it is where graphing and uncertainty first appear formally.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Analysis of literary and non-literary texts, with criteria covering analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. The most common gap is structural: students who have strong ideas and no paragraph architecture score below their comprehension on the organising criterion.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: A second language taught in phases rather than year groups, assessed on comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Arabic as an additional language is the most requested in this corridor, often alongside French or Spanish.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: History, geography and economics content, assessed on knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Source-based questions are where the marks concentrate, and students routinely describe a source rather than evaluating its reliability or purpose.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The design cycle: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. An often-overlooked subject that carries real marks and teaches the documentation discipline the Personal Project later demands. Students lose marks by building something good and documenting it poorly.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Visual arts, music, drama or dance, assessed on knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The written reflection component is where tutoring helps most, since many students can perform or create well and write about it thinly.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Assessed on knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The planning and reflecting criteria are written work, which surprises families who assume the subject is entirely practical.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units and ATL skills
subjects.description: Approaches to learning skills, taught across subjects: research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills. Rarely tutored directly and often the real problem behind a scatter of mediocre criterion scores in otherwise capable students.

sections.heading: When the school day actually ends around Al Jaddaf
paragraphs: The bell time is not the arrival time, and the arrival time is what determines whether a session works. Around Al Jaddaf the variation is wide enough to matter. A student at a creek-side campus a few minutes away can be home, changed and ready by 16:00. A student crossing from Festival City in pick-up traffic may not sit down until 16:45. One at a school inland beyond Meydan, on a bus with multiple stops, can arrive after 17:00. Those are three different tutoring arrangements, not one.

Buses complicate it further and in a direction most parents underestimate. A school bus serving several communities takes considerably longer than a parent driving the same distance, and the student arrives having already spent forty minutes sitting still. For a Year 7 or Year 8 student that journey consumes a measurable share of the day's concentration before any learning begins. A session scheduled on the assumption of a car journey will consistently land at the wrong point.

The table below sets out the realistic shape for each direction out of Al Jaddaf. The numbers are not promises about any particular school; they are the pattern families in this corridor describe, and they exist so you can pick a starting slot rather than discover the right one by failing at two wrong ones. Check your own arrival time across a normal week before fixing anything, because a term of sessions at a bad time is a wasted term.

One scheduling habit is worth more than the rest. Book a slot you can keep in the busiest week of the term, not in the quietest. Every family can manage 17:00 on a Tuesday in October. The question is whether it still works in the week of the production, the swimming gala and two assessment deadlines, because that is the week that decides whether the arrangement holds or quietly ends.

sections.heading: Why MYP Year 9 can look as though nothing is being assessed
paragraphs: Parents arriving in the MYP from an exam-based system often cannot tell whether their child is doing well, and the reason is structural rather than evasive. MYP assessment is criterion-based. Each subject is marked against four criteria, each criterion out of eight, against published descriptors that say what a particular band of work looks like. There is no percentage, no class rank, and no external exam until the Diploma. A report that says a student scored 5 on criterion B is precise and informative, and it does not feel like information if you are expecting 68 per cent.

This has a practical consequence that is easy to miss. A student can drift for two years without any single alarming result. Criterion scores of 4 and 5 across the board look unremarkable, and they are, which is exactly the problem: unremarkable in MYP Year 4 becomes a struggle in DP Year 1, when the same student meets mark schemes and timed papers. The gap did not appear suddenly in Year 12; it was simply never flagged by anything that looked like a bad grade.

Reading an MYP report usefully takes about twenty minutes and is worth doing properly once a year. Look at the criteria rather than the subject totals, and look across subjects rather than down them. A student scoring well on knowing and understanding and poorly on communicating, in three different subjects, does not have three subject problems. They have one writing problem, and it is cheaper and faster to fix than three subjects' worth of content support.

That cross-subject pattern is the single most useful thing a tutor can be given. Send the report and say nothing else, and a tutor who knows the programme will usually identify the pattern unprompted. If they talk about subjects rather than criteria, they are reading the document the way a parent does rather than the way the programme intends, which tells you how much MYP experience is behind the conversation.

No percentages or rank, so steady drift produces no alarming result

sections.heading: The four criteria, and which one your child is losing marks on
paragraphs: Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, and although the names differ between subject groups the structure does not. Broadly, criterion A asks what the student knows, criterion B asks how they inquire or investigate, criterion C asks how they communicate or create, and criterion D asks how they evaluate, reflect or think critically. Knowing which of the four is costing marks turns a vague worry into a four-session job.

The pattern across the Al Jaddaf students we see is consistent enough to predict. Criterion A is rarely the problem; students who attend and pay attention generally know things. Criterion C, communicating, is the most common weakness and the most fixable, because it is about structure rather than ability: paragraphs that begin with a claim, data presented with the units and the uncertainty, working set out so a reader can follow it. Criterion D is the second most common and the one that most reliably predicts Diploma difficulty, because evaluation is the skill the Diploma is built on.

The table below maps the four criteria across the subject groups most often asked about in this corridor, with what each one actually rewards. Take it to your child's latest report and find the low number. In most cases it is in the same column across several subjects, and that column is where a short tutoring block should be aimed.

What this approach replaces is the default response to a disappointing MYP report, which is to buy content tutoring in the subject with the lowest overall grade. That is usually the wrong target. The subject grade is an aggregate; the criterion score is the diagnosis. Working from the aggregate means paying to re-teach material the student already knows, while the structural weakness that produced the low score stays exactly where it is.

sections.heading: MYP Year 5 and the Personal Project: what a tutor may do
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the piece of work that ends the MYP, and it is the first time most students manage a sustained independent project with a supervisor rather than a teacher. It asks for a goal, a process journal kept throughout, a product or outcome, and a report reflecting on all of it. Students who have never documented a process find the journal the hardest part, and the journal is not optional padding; it is evidence the assessment depends on.

Where tutoring helps is in the structure and the discipline rather than the content. A goal narrow enough to be achievable and specific enough to be assessable is the single decision that determines how the project goes, and it is usually made badly, in a week, under time pressure. A tutor who asks hard questions about scope at the start is worth more than one who helps tidy a report at the end. The same is true of the journal: twenty minutes a week recorded as it happens is straightforward, and reconstructing six months of process in April is not.

The limits are firm and they are the same limits that apply to every piece of assessed IB work. The Personal Project must be the student's own. A tutor may question the goal, teach how to keep a process journal, explain what the criteria reward, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any part of the report, produce the outcome, or edit the text into its final form. Providers in this market sell completed coursework; a student who submits it is facing an academic-honesty finding rather than a shortcut.

There is a practical reason to say this plainly to any prospective tutor before hiring them. The answer sorts the market quickly. Somebody who explains where the line sits, and describes how they work inside it, has supervised real IB students through this. Somebody who offers to make sure the project is finished to a high standard has told you what they are actually selling, and the consequences of that fall entirely on your child.
bullets: Scope the goal narrowly at the start; this decision determines the project
The process journal is assessed evidence, kept weekly, not reconstructed later
A tutor may question, teach and give feedback on the student's own draft
No tutor may write the report, produce the outcome, or edit it to completion

sections.heading: The gap between MYP Year 5 and DP Year 1
paragraphs: Students leaving the MYP for the Diploma meet three new things at once, and none of them is content. The first is the mark scheme. After five years of criterion descriptors, a Diploma paper awards marks for specific points, and a student who writes a thoughtful answer missing the two marked points scores less than one who writes two crisp sentences. That is a technique, it is learnable, and almost nobody teaches it deliberately.

The second is the command term. Describe, explain, deduce, evaluate and justify each demand a different structure and a different length, and the mark allocation tells a candidate how much to write. MYP tasks rarely work this way. Students arrive in DP Year 1 writing the same amount for every question, which costs marks at both ends: too little for the four-mark questions and wasted time on the one-mark ones.

The third is pace. Diploma papers are timed tightly and MYP assessment generally is not. A student who has always had enough time to think meets a paper that does not allow it, and the first mock reflects that rather than their understanding. This is the most common reason a strong MYP student receives a disappointing first Diploma report, and it is also the most straightforwardly fixable, given timed practice and somebody marking it.

The implication for an Al Jaddaf family is a question of timing rather than quantity. Six sessions in the summer between MYP Year 5 and DP Year 1, aimed at mark schemes, command terms and timed writing, land on all three gaps before they cause damage. The same six sessions in November of DP Year 1 are remedial and cost the student a term of confidence. Schools with larger Diploma cohorts inland from the creek often bridge this explicitly; smaller campuses frequently cannot.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches certain subjects regardless of its licensed international curriculum, and MYP families are sometimes surprised by how firm the requirements are. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. These subjects sit alongside the eight MYP groups rather than inside them.

The organisational rules are specific and worth knowing, because they explain a timetable that may otherwise look arbitrary. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic are required to hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete and checkable credential point. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

That last rule has a direct bearing on how tutoring in these subjects should be described, and we will be precise about it. A tutor can support a student with the material the school teaches, build vocabulary and writing fluency in Arabic, and help a student organise and revise. Nobody should be offering an alternative syllabus or supplementary content for the mandatory subjects, because the content is prescribed. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership of any kind, and does not claim any.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs, and why this is the cheap window
paragraphs: Market rates for middle-school tutoring in Dubai sit below Diploma rates, which is the opposite of how families usually allocate a budget. Published figures put budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and roughly AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for a qualified subject tutor. The Bestimate rate survey for Dubai estimates monthly spend on weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band. In-home visits run AED 180 to 350 in that survey, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500.

The arithmetic that matters is not the hourly rate but what the hour is buying at each stage. An MYP Year 4 hour spent building paragraph structure or graphing discipline is working on something that will be assessed for the following six years. A DP Year 13 hour spent on the same skill is working against a deadline, at a higher rate, with less time for it to take hold. Families who spend evenly across a school career get more for the money than families who spend nothing until a mock grade frightens them, and that is the whole argument for buying support during the MYP.

None of those figures is an IB Gram price list. Our arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation about which criterion is actually costing marks, because the useful answer for an MYP student is usually a short block rather than a year of weekly sessions. A tutor who looks at a report and says no support is needed yet has given you something worth more than a term of lessons, and parents should treat that answer as a good sign rather than a lost sale.

Context on cost is worth adding, because tutoring spend sits inside a larger education budget. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total package of AED 2.5 billion. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with International Baccalaureate provision at 7 per cent of enrolment.

sections.heading: A weekly shape that survives the term, and how to start
paragraphs: The arrangement that works for MYP students in this corridor is smaller than families expect. One session a week, forty-five to sixty minutes, at a time tested against real arrival times, aimed at one criterion rather than one subject, with a piece of the student's own marked work in front of both people. That is enough for most MYP problems, and it is sustainable across a term in a way that two sessions a week is not.

Start by sending the latest MYP report and one marked piece of work. The report shows the cross-subject pattern and the marked task shows what it looks like in practice. From those two documents a tutor who knows the programme can usually name the criterion and the fix, and tell you roughly how many sessions it needs. That conversation costs nothing and it is the difference between a four-session block and an open arrangement that drifts for a year.

A free trial lesson runs before any payment, on the student's own work rather than a generic diagnostic. For a middle-school student the thing to watch in the trial is not whether the tutor is impressive but whether the student talks. A session where an eleven-year-old listens politely to a good explanation for fifty minutes is a session that will not change a criterion score. Ask afterwards what the student actually did, and judge from that.

On availability, we will be straightforward. MYP support in the earliest workable slots, 16:30 to 17:30 Gulf Standard Time, is the most requested window on the entire UAE schedule, because every family in every emirate wants it for the same reason. In a busy term it may not be free. When that is the case we say so and offer a different time, a tutor whose hours overlap the Gulf evening from another time zone, or a weekend morning, rather than putting a Year 7 student into a 19:30 slot where nothing useful will happen.

faqs.question: What time can an MYP session realistically start for a family in Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which direction the school is in. From a creek-side campus in Al Jaddaf or Healthcare City, a student can be home and settled by 16:15, so 16:30 works and is the strongest slot available in this corridor. From Festival City across the Garhoud crossing, pick-up traffic pushes it to 17:00. From Nad Al Sheba or Mohammed Bin Rashid City, often by bus with multiple stops, 17:45 is realistic and a weekend morning is usually better for younger students. Check your own arrival time across a normal week before fixing any slot.

faqs.question: Why does my child's MYP report not tell me whether she is doing well?
faqs.answer: Because MYP assessment is criterion-based rather than percentage-based. Each subject is marked against four criteria, each out of eight, against published descriptors describing what a band of work looks like. There is no percentage, no rank and no external exam until the Diploma. A score of 5 on criterion B is precise information, and it does not feel like information if you are expecting 68 per cent. Read across subjects by criterion rather than down subjects by total: the same criterion low in three subjects is one problem, not three.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion is usually the one costing marks?
faqs.answer: Criterion C, communicating, in most of the students we see in this corridor. It is about structure rather than ability: paragraphs that start with a claim, data presented with units and uncertainty, working laid out so a reader can follow it. Criterion D, which covers evaluating, reflecting or thinking critically depending on the subject group, is the second most common and the one that best predicts Diploma difficulty. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is rarely the problem for a student who attends and pays attention, which is why content tutoring so often misses.

faqs.question: Is MYP Year 4 too early to bring in a tutor?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest and most effective year to do it, which is the opposite of how most families allocate the budget. Published Dubai rates for middle-school support sit below Diploma rates, and an hour spent building paragraph structure or graphing discipline in MYP Year 4 works on a skill that will be assessed for the next six years. The same hour in DP Year 13 is remedial, more expensive, and up against a deadline. There is no external exam in the MYP to create urgency, which is precisely why the drift goes unnoticed.

faqs.question: How much help can a tutor give with the MYP Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Real help, inside firm limits. A tutor may challenge whether the goal is narrow enough to be achievable and specific enough to be assessable, teach how to keep a process journal as the work happens, explain what the criteria reward, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any part of the report, produce the outcome, or edit the text into final form. The project must be the student's own work under IB academic-honesty rules, and providers selling completed coursework are selling a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: What changes when my son moves from MYP Year 5 into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Three things at once, and none of them is content. Mark schemes replace criterion descriptors, so a thoughtful answer that misses the marked points scores less than two crisp sentences that hit them. Command terms start setting answer length, with the mark allocation as the instruction. And papers are timed tightly where MYP assessment generally is not. A strong MYP student who receives a poor first Diploma report has usually met all three at once rather than suddenly stopped understanding the subject.

faqs.question: Should we book two sessions a week for an MYP student?
faqs.answer: Rarely. One session of forty-five to sixty minutes a week, aimed at one criterion with the student's own marked work in front of both people, handles most MYP problems and is sustainable across a term. Two sessions a week competes with homework, activities and sleep, and the usual result is that both get cancelled by November rather than one being kept. If the diagnosis genuinely needs more time, a longer weekend block is better than a second weekday evening for a student in Years 7 to 9.

faqs.question: Which subjects are compulsory in Dubai alongside the MYP?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 where a school's year begins in April. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory subject lesson.

faqs.question: Can a tutor provide extra material for Arabic or Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Not additional or alternative content, no. For the mandatory UAE subjects, KHDA guidance states that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. What a tutor can legitimately do is support a student with the material the school teaches: build vocabulary and writing fluency, work through set texts, and help with organisation and revision. Schools are also required to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a checkable credential point.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring hold a twelve-year-old's attention?
faqs.answer: It depends on the session design rather than the medium. A session where the student writes, draws, annotates and talks for most of the hour holds attention at any age. A session where an adult explains well for fifty minutes does not, in a room or on a screen. The thing to watch in a trial lesson is how much the child actually does. One real advantage for younger students is timing: a session needing no travel can start at 16:30, which is a far better point in a twelve-year-old's day than 19:30.

faqs.question: What should I send to get a useful first conversation?
faqs.answer: Two documents and one fact. The latest MYP report, one piece of marked work, and the time your child is genuinely home and settled on a normal weekday. The report shows the cross-subject criterion pattern, the marked task shows what it looks like on the page, and the arrival time determines whether any arrangement will survive. From those three things a tutor who knows the programme can usually name the criterion, propose a number of sessions, and tell you if the answer is that nothing is needed yet.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying more for a tutor who comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: The premium is real and it buys travel. The Bestimate survey records in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. For families in Nad Al Sheba or Mohammed Bin Rashid City the quotes sit at the top of that range because of the distance. The flexibility cost matters too: an in-home session cannot shift by twenty minutes when a bus is late, because the journey is already committed. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: My daughter is in MYP Year 2 and seems fine. Is there anything to do?
faqs.answer: Probably nothing involving payment, and a tutor who tells you that is worth keeping on file. The useful free moves are reading the report by criterion rather than by subject, asking the form tutor which approaches-to-learning skills she is weakest on, and checking whether her written work has any structure at all. If communicating scores well across subjects and she can lay out an argument or a calculation clearly, the foundations are doing their job. Revisit at the end of MYP Year 3, before the subject choices start mattering.

faqs.question: What if the 16:30 slot we need is already taken?
faqs.answer: That window is the most contested on the entire UAE schedule, because every family in every emirate wants it for the same sensible reason. In a busy term it may genuinely not be free. When that happens we say so rather than placing a Year 7 student in a 19:30 slot where very little useful will happen. The alternatives we offer are a different weekday time, a tutor in another time zone whose hours overlap the Gulf evening, or a weekend morning block, which for younger MYP students is often better than any weekday option anyway.

intro.heading: The real question in this part of Dubai is usually not which tutor but which system
paragraphs: Al Khail Gate sits in the Al Quoz corridor along Al Khail Road, between the industrial areas and the newer developments of Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills and the Dubailand belt. Children here travel out to a wide spread of schools, and that spread includes both IB continuum schools and British-curriculum schools running IGCSE. The consequence is a conversation we have constantly with families from this community: our child is in the MYP and we are not sure we understand it, and the school across Al Khail Road does IGCSE instead.

That question deserves a straight answer rather than advocacy. Both systems are respected, both lead to strong post-sixteen options, and both are capable of producing a bored student or a stretched one depending on the school rather than the framework. What differs is the shape of the assessment, the kind of work rewarded, the amount of external examination at sixteen, and how legible the whole thing is to a parent who was educated in a percentage-based system.

The legibility point is not trivial and it is the reason many families consider moving. An MYP report shows four criterion levels per subject, each from zero to eight, and a subject grade from one to seven. It does not show a percentage, a class rank or a mark out of a hundred. Parents reading it for the first time often cannot tell whether their child is doing well, and that uncertainty is uncomfortable enough to make an IGCSE school with its familiar grades look like a simplification.

It is also solvable without changing school. Laying out the four criterion levels per subject side by side and finding the outlier takes five minutes and converts the report into a diagnosis. A low criterion in one subject points at a named skill. A low criterion of the same type across three subjects points at one problem with three symptoms. That reading is the single most useful thing a parent new to the programme can learn, and it is free.

So this page does two jobs. It compares the MYP with IGCSE on the things that actually differ, including what transfers if a family does move, so that the decision can be made on information rather than on familiarity. And it explains what MYP tutoring actually consists of, which is criterion-specific work rather than general subject revision, because that distinction is where most money in this area gets either well spent or wasted.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. For MYP work the format is well suited, because so much of the teaching involves reading a task sheet, a rubric and a set of descriptors side by side, which works better on a shared screen than on a kitchen table.

sections.heading: MYP against IGCSE at sixteen: the comparison this community is actually making
paragraphs: Two schools a short distance apart on either side of Al Khail Road can offer a fourteen-year-old genuinely different experiences of the next two years. In the Middle Years Programme the student continues an eight-subject-group framework assessed internally against four criteria per subject, with a Personal Project in the final year and no external examination series at sixteen in most schools. In an IGCSE school the student narrows to a set of subjects, each ending in externally marked papers in a June or November series, with grades issued by Cambridge or Pearson.

That difference produces different pressures rather than different amounts of pressure. The MYP spreads assessment across the whole year in many pieces, which suits students who work steadily and disadvantages those who need a deadline to focus. IGCSE concentrates it into a series, which suits students who revise well under pressure and punishes those who leave things late. Neither is objectively kinder; they fail different children in different ways.

The external-grade question is the one families weigh most. IGCSE produces a certificate recognised everywhere and legible to any employer, school or admissions office. The MYP produces an internally assessed record and, where a school offers it, an optional certificate route. For a family who may relocate internationally, the portability difference is real and practical. For a family staying in Dubai and intending the IB Diploma, staying in the continuum removes a transition that otherwise has to be managed.

The table compares the two on what actually differs. We have tried to write it so that a parent could use it to argue either way, because that is what an honest comparison looks like. Our own position is narrow: for most students the school matters far more than the framework, and a strong MYP school beats a weak IGCSE one and vice versa.

sections.heading: Al Khail Gate against the communities next to it: does the answer change?
paragraphs: It is fair to ask whether this comparison is really about Al Khail Gate or about Dubai generally, so here is the local version. Within a short radius of this community sit Al Quoz with its established and largely Indian-curriculum provision, Dubai Hills with IB continuum options, Al Barsha South with newer British-curriculum schools, and the Dubailand belt further out with a mix. A family here genuinely has both systems available on comparable bus routes, which is not true everywhere in the emirate.

What differs between those areas is not the educational logic but the practical arithmetic: how long the bus takes, what time the child gets home, and therefore what an evening can hold. A student at an Al Quoz school is frequently home by 15:30 and can manage an earlier session. A student travelling to Motor City or Sports City arrives considerably later and needs a 17:30 slot or after. That is the difference worth planning around, and it applies regardless of which framework the school teaches.

The conclusion on the system question is therefore the same across all these neighbourhoods, and it is deliberately unexciting: the individual school matters more than the framework, and the child's working style matters more than either. A steady, self-directed student will do well in an MYP school with good teaching. A student who needs an external deadline will do better in an IGCSE school. Choosing a framework in the abstract and then finding a school to fit it is the wrong order.
