sections.heading: What transfers between the two systems, and what does not
paragraphs: If a family does move, the practical question is what the student arrives with and what they lack. The answer is more encouraging in one direction than the other, and it is worth knowing before the decision rather than after it. A student moving from the MYP into an IGCSE course arrives with strong investigative habits, research skills and written communication, and typically lacks examination technique: writing to a mark allocation, working at speed under timed conditions, and the particular register IGCSE mark schemes reward.

A student moving from IGCSE into a continuum school arrives with content coverage and examination discipline and typically lacks the criterion literacy the MYP assumes: reading a rubric, planning to descriptors, documenting a process, and keeping a journal while work is happening rather than reconstructing one afterwards. Both gaps are real and both are closeable in a term of focused work, which is a more useful framing than treating either move as a catastrophe or as a trivial switch.

The timing of the move matters more than the direction. A move before the start of an IGCSE course is straightforward. A move partway through one means joining a two-year syllabus already under way, which requires the receiving school to say precisely what they expect an incoming student to have covered. That is a specific question with a specific answer and it should be asked in writing before anything is agreed.

The table maps what transfers subject by subject. It is a starting hypothesis rather than a conclusion, because individual schools vary far more than frameworks do, and any student should be assessed on their own work rather than on their previous system's reputation.

sections.heading: Reading an MYP report without a percentage in sight
paragraphs: The single most common reason families in this community consider leaving the programme is that they cannot tell how their child is doing. That is a legibility problem rather than a quality problem, and it is solvable in five minutes a term. Each subject shows four criterion levels, each from zero to eight against published descriptors, and a subject grade from one to seven derived from them using boundaries published in the subject guide. Your school can show you the conversion it applies.

The first reading is within a subject. Lay the four levels side by side and look for the outlier. Levels of six, six, three and six point at one specific skill rather than at the subject, and lifting that one is the shortest route to a different grade, because the four contribute together. Levels of four, four, four and four point at something else, usually task literacy or self-management rather than a subject weakness, and the plan should differ accordingly.

The second reading is across subjects. A low criterion of the same type in three subjects at once is one problem with three symptoms, usually about structure or about documentation rather than about content in any of them. That pattern is invisible when a report is read subject by subject, which is how everyone reads it, and spotting it is the most valuable five minutes a parent can spend each term.

Then ask the school three specific questions: which task produced the lowest criterion level, what its task-specific clarification asked for, and what a higher level would have looked like on that task. Those get precise answers, because teachers can point at the rubric. Asking how my child is doing gets a reassuring answer that changes nothing. For a working parent in this community, sending those three questions in writing often produces a better reply than a crowded parents' evening does.

sections.heading: The parts of the MYP with no IGCSE equivalent
paragraphs: Three features of the programme have no direct counterpart in an IGCSE course, and they are worth understanding both for their own sake and because they form part of the comparison. The first is interdisciplinary units, assessed against their own criteria, where two or more subjects are combined around a shared inquiry. Students frequently treat these as a lesser task; the levels count the same as any other, and the criteria reward the integration rather than the content from either subject.

The second is service as action, a requirement to engage with the community and reflect on it, which is not graded in the way a subject is but is a requirement of the programme. Families sometimes look for tutoring support with it and there is very little a tutor should usefully provide: the value depends on the student doing and reflecting on their own activity. Where students struggle it is almost always with record-keeping rather than with the activity, and the coordinator at school is the right person to ask.

The third is the Personal Project in the final year, a student-directed piece of work with its own criteria and a process journal. The most common failure is scope: a goal too large to finish or too vague to evaluate, and the problem stays invisible until the deadline is close. A tutor can help enormously in the first fortnight by asking what exactly will exist at the end, how success will be judged, and what happens in week one. A tutor must never write, draft or produce the Personal Project or any part of it.

These three are also where the programme's claimed advantages become concrete. A student who has completed an interdisciplinary unit properly, kept a live journal through a Personal Project and reflected honestly on service has rehearsed exactly the skills the Diploma core later demands. That is a real benefit and it is also contingent on the school running those elements well, which is a question to ask on a school visit rather than to assume.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring consists of, and what it should cost
paragraphs: MYP support is criterion-specific rather than subject-general, and that distinction decides whether money is well spent. A student with a low investigating-patterns criterion in mathematics does not need more equations; they need practice at generalising from a pattern and justifying the generalisation, which is a different activity. A student with a low processing-and-evaluating criterion in sciences needs data-handling and evaluation practice rather than more content. Tutoring that ignores the criteria is general revision with an IB label on it.

In practice that makes most MYP arrangements shorter than families expect. A single weak criterion, worked on properly against real task sheets with the descriptors translated into concrete actions, usually shifts within a term. Where the pattern across subjects points at task literacy or self-management, the work is even more general and even shorter: reading the clarification before starting, planning to descriptors rather than to a word count, and self-assessing against the rubric before submission.

On cost, published Dubai bands put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300, and an in-home visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the fee. Monthly estimates run about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band for one weekly subject. Those figures come from published provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table and are the market rather than our price list.

The honest guidance for a family in this community is to buy one subject for one term, aimed at one criterion, and to measure the result against the next report, which is a public number rather than an impression. If the criterion has moved, the work was right. If it has not, change the approach or the tutor rather than adding hours. Open-ended monthly renewal suits a provider more than a family, and in a framework as specific as this one it is rarely necessary.

sections.heading: Bus routes, shared tables and the evening that works
paragraphs: Children in Al Khail Gate travel to a wide spread of schools, mostly by bus, and arrival times vary more here than in a neighbourhood built around one school. Students at Al Quoz schools are often home by 15:30. Students travelling to Dubai Hills or Al Barsha South arrive a little later. Students going out to Motor City, Sports City or the outer Dubailand communities arrive considerably later still, and setting a session time from the school's finish bell rather than from the actual bus arrival is the commonest scheduling mistake.

The practical rule is to take the real arrival time and add about forty minutes for food and a change of clothes. For most families here that puts the workable slot at 17:00 to 17:30 or after. A slot booked earlier in optimism tends to be rescheduled by the third week, and a rescheduled session in a programme where tasks are set over several weeks is a genuine setback rather than an inconvenience.

Study space needs a short conversation. The table is usually shared, so headphones are equipment rather than a luxury, a hard surface matters, and squared paper, a ruler and the student's own calculator rather than a phone should be ready before the first session. For MYP work in particular the screen is used heavily, because so much of the teaching involves having the task sheet, the rubric and the student's draft open side by side.

Ramadan shifts the pattern for several weeks and schools adjust hours. The arrangement that works is fewer and shorter sessions moved to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, with lighter work set between them, agreed before the month begins. In the MYP this matters because tasks run over weeks rather than overnight, and a fortnight of drift during a long task is harder to recover than a missed homework.

sections.heading: Honest limits, permits and what to verify
paragraphs: We hold no view that requires a family to buy anything from us, and on the system question we will say plainly when staying put is the right answer. Where we can help is in explaining both frameworks accurately, saying what transfers if a move happens, and providing criterion-specific support if a family stays. What we cannot do is tell you which of two schools is better, because that depends on the schools rather than on the frameworks, and the people who can tell you are the schools themselves and other parents at them.

Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, any specific amount should be treated as unverified.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page here will claim one. We operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE, we run no home visits anywhere in the Emirates, and we do not enter candidates for examinations or perform Ministry equivalency. We publish no success rates, satisfaction scores or star ratings, because we could not produce the data behind any of them.

What to verify independently: the school's own criterion-to-grade conversion and assessment policy, which the school will share; which tasks produced which levels, from the subject teacher; what Personal Project support is permitted, from the supervisor; and the inspection record, on the regulator's own site. Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with ADEK in Abu Dhabi, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

faqs.question: Should our child stay in the MYP or move to an IGCSE school in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: That depends on four things rather than on the frameworks: what your child is like, what the two actual schools are like, how long you expect to be in Dubai, and what route is intended after sixteen. The MYP spreads assessment across the year, which suits steady workers and disadvantages students who need a deadline. IGCSE concentrates it into an external series, which suits the reverse. For most students the individual school matters more than the framework, and a strong MYP school beats a weak IGCSE one.

faqs.question: Why does the MYP report have no percentages on it?
faqs.answer: Because the programme does not use them. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked from zero to eight against published descriptors, and the four levels combine into a subject grade from one to seven using boundaries published in the subject guide. Your school can show you the conversion. The consequence is that two students with the same grade can have entirely different problems, and that a single weak criterion can hold a grade down while the other three are strong. Reading the four levels side by side is where any plan starts.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in Al Khail Gate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. Sessions here are one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For MYP work the format genuinely helps, because most of the teaching involves having the task sheet, the task-specific clarification, the rubric and the student's own draft open side by side, which works considerably better on a shared screen than on a crowded table.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE better recognised than the MYP if we leave the UAE?
faqs.answer: IGCSE is widely recognised internationally and produces an external certificate that any school, employer or admissions office can read without explanation. The MYP is offered in fewer schools in some countries and its record is internally assessed, with an optional certificate route where a school provides it. For a family who may relocate, that is a genuine practical consideration rather than a comment on educational quality. For a family staying in Dubai and intending the IB Diploma, staying in the continuum removes a transition that would otherwise need managing.

faqs.question: If we move from MYP to IGCSE, what will our child be missing?
faqs.answer: Mostly examination technique rather than content. MYP students typically arrive with strong investigative habits, research skills and written communication, and lack practice at writing to a mark allocation, working at speed under timed conditions, and the particular register IGCSE mark schemes reward. That gap is closeable in a term of focused work. The bigger practical question is timing: joining partway through a two-year IGCSE course means arriving into a syllabus already under way, so ask the receiving school in writing what they expect an incoming student to have covered.

faqs.question: With one criterion's worth of effort available, which one do we pick?
faqs.answer: The one furthest behind the others in that subject, and the answer is on the report. Levels reading six, six, three and six mean one specific skill is holding the grade down, and lifting it is the shortest route to a different number because the four criteria contribute together. If all four sit at a similar middling level, the issue is more likely task literacy or self-management than any subject skill, and the plan should address that instead. Spreading effort across four criteria often fails to cross a boundary at all.

faqs.question: What does criterion-specific support actually look like in a session?
faqs.answer: We take the student's real task sheet and its task-specific clarification, read the descriptors for the level they are aiming at, and translate each phrase into a concrete action on that particular task. For a low investigating-patterns level in mathematics, that means practising generalising from a pattern and justifying the generalisation, not working more equations. For a low processing-and-evaluating level in sciences, it means data handling and evaluation writing. The distinction between that and general revision is where the money is either well spent or wasted.

faqs.question: How many weeks before a criterion level shifts on the next report?
faqs.answer: For a criterion weak because of a missing procedure, often a single term. Reading the clarification before starting, planning to descriptors rather than to a word count, documenting a process while it happens, and self-assessing against the rubric before submission are habits rather than knowledge, and they show up on the next report. A criterion weak because of a genuine content or skill gap takes longer and depends on how often it is assessed. We measure against the next report because a criterion level is a public number and an impression is not.

faqs.question: What part of the Personal Project is a tutor actually allowed to touch?
faqs.answer: With the planning and the thinking, yes; with the work, no. A tutor can help a student interrogate their own goal, settle a realistic scope, build a staged timeline, keep the process journal properly, and respond to the student's own journal with the questions a supervisor would ask. A tutor must never write, draft or produce any part of the project, or supply material for a student to adapt. The project is supervised in school and your child's supervisor is the authority on exactly what help is permitted in their case.

faqs.question: Do interdisciplinary units matter as much as subject units?
faqs.answer: Yes, and students routinely treat them as a lesser task. They are assessed against their own criteria and the levels count like any others, and what they reward is the integration of two or more subjects around a shared inquiry rather than the content from either one. A student who writes a competent piece about the history and a competent piece about the science, without connecting them, has missed the point the criteria are measuring. It is worth asking the school how the unit will be assessed before the work starts.

faqs.question: Which three questions get a useful answer from an MYP subject teacher?
faqs.answer: Three specific questions rather than one general one. Which task produced the lowest criterion level, and what did its task-specific clarification ask for? What would a higher level have looked like on that task? And which criterion would the department prioritise if we could only work on one? Teachers answer those precisely because they can point at the rubric. Asking how my child is doing produces a reassuring reply that changes nothing. Sending the questions in writing beforehand often works better than a crowded evening.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost for a family in this community?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai bands put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300, and an in-home visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the fee. Monthly estimates run about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band for one weekly subject. Those come from published provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table rather than from us. Most MYP arrangements are shorter than families expect, because criterion-specific work is finite.

faqs.question: Our child is in MYP 5 and heading for the Diploma. What should we prepare?
faqs.answer: Technical fluency rather than content. MYP students usually arrive in the Diploma strong on inquiry, research and reflection, which genuinely helps with the Extended Essay, internal assessments and Theory of Knowledge, and short on the automatic algebraic manipulation that higher level mathematics and the sciences assume from the first week. The Diploma also applies command terms literally where MYP descriptors are more holistic. Six to eight sessions in the summer, aimed only at the subjects actually chosen, closes most of that gap.

faqs.question: What time should sessions be given the bus journey from here?
faqs.answer: Set it from the actual bus arrival rather than the school's finish time, and add about forty minutes for food and a change of clothes. Students at Al Quoz schools are often home by 15:30 and can take an earlier slot. Students travelling to Dubai Hills or Al Barsha South arrive a little later, and students going out to Motor City or Sports City considerably later. For most families here that means 17:00 to 17:30 or after. A slot booked optimistically early is usually rescheduled by the third week.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-khail-gate.closingHeading: Send the report, and tell us if the bigger question is live
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-khail-gate.closingBody: If the problem is a criterion, it is probably one term of specific work and the next report will show whether it moved. If the problem is that the report is unreadable, five minutes laying the four levels side by side usually solves it without anybody being hired. And if the real question is whether to stay in the programme or move across Al Khail Road to an IGCSE school, tell us, because the answer depends on your child and on two actual schools rather than on frameworks, and we will say plainly when staying put is right. The trial lesson is free and works on your child's own task. Everything runs one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What MYP support in Al Khawaneej costs, and what the money is really for
paragraphs: Al Khawaneej is a villa district on Dubai's eastern edge, which has two consequences for a tutoring budget. The first is that almost nobody attends school inside the community: the morning run goes out to Mirdif, Al Mizhar, Al Rashidiya, Academic City or Dubai Festival City, and the evening return is the constraint on when a lesson can start. The second is that the tutors who will drive out that far price the drive into the hour. A parent comparing quotes is often comparing fuel and Dubai traffic, not teaching.

Middle Years Programme tutoring is also priced oddly across this market. Because MYP 1 to MYP 3 carry no external examination, agencies treat them as junior work and quote them cheaply. Because MYP 5 sits one year away from the Diploma Programme, the same agencies reprice it as exam coaching. Neither price reflects what the work actually is. MYP grades are produced by four published criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight, and a child loses marks in a specific one of those four. Diagnosing which is the entire job.

So this page is written as a cost page. It publishes the AED bands the Dubai market charges, attributed to whoever published them. It shows what an in-home visit adds once travel is counted. It lists, bluntly, the three ways Al Khawaneej families spend money on MYP support that changes nothing: buying more hours in a subject that is already passing, buying homework supervision and calling it tutoring, and paying a premium for a tutor who has never read a criterion descriptor.

The honest position on delivery comes first, because it changes the arithmetic. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. That is not a compromise dressed up as a feature. It is why a child in Al Khawaneej 2 can work with a Sciences specialist who has taught criterion C for years, instead of whoever was willing to drive past Mushrif Park at six in the evening.

What follows is organised to be read by someone with a calculator open. Rate bands first, then the waste, then the four criteria your invoice should be buying, then the Personal Project timeline counted backwards, then the permit question every UAE parent should ask and almost none do. Nothing here is a price list for IB Gram, and nothing here is a market average dressed up as a quote. Where our own cost matters, the answer is a free trial lesson followed by a conversation, because a sensible number depends entirely on how many subject groups are actually in trouble and how many weeks the weak criterion needs. One group for six weeks and three groups for a year are different products at different prices, and no honest provider can tell you which you need before looking at a marked piece of work.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.programmesIntro: Al Khawaneej children sit across three IB programmes depending on which school the morning run reaches. The notes below say what each stage demands and what a tutor can realistically change inside it, with the local detail that decides whether support is worth buying this term.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is transdisciplinary: children work through units of inquiry rather than separate timetabled subjects, and reporting is written against learner-profile attributes instead of percentages. There are no external examinations and no criterion marks. The useful tutoring targets at this stage are narrow and mechanical: number fluency, reading stamina, and the written structure a child will need the moment MYP criteria start being applied to their work.
programmes.countryNote: In the eastern suburbs the PYP is offered principally at Uptown International School in Mirdif, which runs the full continuum. Families in Al Khawaneej 1 and 2 who intend to stay on an IB track usually make the decision at this point, because moving from a British primary into MYP 1 means meeting criterion-referenced marking for the first time with no transition year.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and four assessment criteria per group marked 0 to 8. Tasks are set against a statement of inquiry and a global context, and the final grade on a report is a conversion from criterion totals, not an average of test scores. This is why a child can revise hard and see nothing move: the marks were lost in investigating or in communicating, and more content revision does not touch either.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 is where Al Khawaneej parents usually call. The Personal Project lands in the same year as the first serious conversation about Diploma subject choices, and a child juggling both while travelling thirty minutes each way to school has very little slack. Starting support in MYP 4 costs the same per hour and removes the scramble.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Assessment is mostly external, sat in the May session that UAE schools use, with internal assessment contributing a fixed share of each subject grade. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra homework: it carries additional syllabus content and, in several subjects, an additional paper.
programmes.countryNote: Deira International School and Universal American School, both reachable from Al Khawaneej via Dubai Festival City, offer the Diploma. The practical point for an MYP family is that Higher Level choices made at the end of MYP 5 are difficult to reverse after the first term, so the diagnostic work belongs in MYP 5, not in Year 12.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It suits a student who wants IB rigour in two or three subjects alongside an applied qualification rather than the full six-subject Diploma, and it is assessed through a mix of DP external papers and course-specific coursework.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by a small number of Dubai schools and is rarely the reason an Al Khawaneej family looks for a tutor. It matters here mainly as a fallback worth naming: a student struggling with the full Diploma load has routes other than dropping out of IB entirely, and a tutor should say so rather than sell more hours.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.subjectsIntro: MYP marks are awarded by subject group, and each group has its own four criteria with its own failure mode. The notes below name the criterion letters as a child's teacher uses them, because that is the language on the report you are trying to change.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each out of 8. Most lost marks sit in B and D: students can calculate but cannot generalise a pattern into a rule, or they solve a real-life task without ever stating what the model assumes.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B is where marks vanish: a hypothesis with no scientific reasoning behind it, or a method that never names the controlled variables, caps the mark regardless of how good the practical was.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.levels: English, Arabic and other first languages
subjects.description: Criterion A analysing, B organising, C producing text, D using language. Strong readers routinely lose criterion A because they summarise plot instead of analysing how a writer's choices produce an effect. That is a technique problem with a short fix, not a reading-ability problem.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Marked by phase rather than year group, with criteria covering listening, reading, speaking and writing. A child placed in the wrong phase will look weak on paper while doing nothing wrong. Checking the phase against the descriptors is the first thing a tutor should do, and it costs one session.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D separates the grade 5 from the grade 7: evaluating a source's reliability and recognising a counter-argument, rather than listing what happened in order.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Criterion A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. Students lose most heavily on A and D, because the design cycle rewards documented research and honest testing against stated specifications, not the quality of the finished object.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B developing skills, C thinking creatively, D responding. The process journal carries the marks. A student with real talent and a thin journal will be marked below a methodical peer, which parents often read as unfair marking rather than a documentation gap.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. Half the available marks are written. A sporty child can sit well below their performance level because the planning and reflection components were treated as paperwork.

subjects.name: MYP Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed separately on evaluating, synthesising and reflecting across two subject groups. These units are frequently the lowest marks on an MYP report because no single teacher owns them, and students treat them as a project rather than an assessed task with its own descriptors.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal and a report. It is the student's own work throughout. A tutor may teach project planning, question the scope and give feedback on drafts; no tutor writes the report or supplies the product.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP tutor in Al Khawaneej costs per hour
paragraphs: Market rates for Middle Years Programme support in Dubai run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, and roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for an in-home visit once travel is priced in. Those bands are not ours. They are drawn from what Dubai providers publish: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 for budget online work, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai rate table at AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist exam-level work, with in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500.

The spread is wide because the word tutor covers three different products. At the bottom sits a university student checking homework, which is a supervision service and priced accordingly. In the middle sits a trained subject teacher who can mark against the criteria. At the top sits a specialist in one subject group at one level, usually with examining or senior teaching experience. For MYP 1 to MYP 3, the middle tier is normally sufficient. For MYP 5, where the Personal Project and the Diploma decision land together, the middle tier is where most of the useful work gets done too, which is worth knowing before anyone sells you the top of the range.

Monthly packages circulating in this market give a second reference point. Online blocks of eight sessions appear at around AED 799 a month; in-home blocks of four two-hour sessions appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Bestimate's own monthly estimate for a single weekly hour runs AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. IB Gram publishes no fixed price list for the UAE, because a sensible figure depends on how many subject groups are genuinely in trouble. The trial lesson is free, and the number comes after it.

sections.heading: Why MYP is priced below the Diploma, and when that pricing is wrong
paragraphs: Agencies discount MYP work because there is no external examination to point at. No exam, no stakes, cheaper hour. That logic holds for MYP 1 and MYP 2, where the real purpose of support is habit formation and the cost of waiting a term is close to zero. It stops holding somewhere in MYP 4, and by MYP 5 it is simply wrong, because two things with permanent consequences happen in that year: the Personal Project is completed and the Diploma subject choices are made.

The Diploma decision is the expensive one. A student who picks Higher Level Chemistry on the strength of a grade 6 that was carried by criterion A, with criterion C sitting at 3, will meet the Higher Level internal assessment eighteen months later with the exact weakness nobody addressed. Fixing that in Year 12 costs specialist rates for a full academic year. Diagnosing it in MYP 4 costs a term of ordinary sessions. Same weakness, very different invoice, and the cheap version is the early one.

There is a mirror-image error worth naming, because Al Khawaneej families make it often. A child in MYP 2 with one weak report triggers four subjects of tutoring, four afternoons a week, at a point in the programme where the marks carry no forward weight at all. That is a large monthly spend buying reassurance. The defensible version is one subject group, one session, six weeks, and a review against the school's next report before any extension.

sections.heading: Three ways Al Khawaneej families waste money on MYP tutoring
paragraphs: The first is buying hours in the subject the child already passes. It happens because that subject is the one the child will tolerate being tutored in. A report showing grade 6 in Mathematics and grade 4 in Individuals and Societies very often produces Mathematics tutoring, because the student agrees to it. The money is spent, the household is calmer, and the grade that was falling keeps falling.

The second is paying tutoring rates for homework supervision. A tutor who sits with a child while they finish set work is providing a useful babysitting-plus service and should be priced as such, somewhere near the bottom of the market band. Charged at AED 250 an hour for a year, it becomes a significant line in the household budget with no criterion mark attached to it. The test is simple: ask which criterion letter last week's session targeted. If the answer is not a letter, you are not buying tutoring.

The third is the travel premium, and in Al Khawaneej it is the largest of the three. An in-home visit from a tutor based in Jumeirah or Dubai Marina is an hour of teaching inside two and a half hours of the tutor's working day, and the rate reflects it. The same money online buys either more frequent contact or a genuinely narrower specialist. The comparison table further down this page sets that out line by line, including what the drive actually costs in tutor-pool terms rather than only in dirhams.

sections.heading: The four criteria your invoice should be buying
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group is marked against four criteria, lettered A to D, each scored from 0 to 8. The four add to 32, and the school converts that total into the 1 to 7 grade that appears on the report. The conversion is the reason parents find MYP reporting opaque: a child can lose a whole grade band while answering more questions correctly than last term, because the loss came from one criterion that content revision never touches.

This is also where a tutor earns the rate. A competent MYP tutor opens the first session by asking for the breakdown, not the grade. If the school publishes criterion marks on the report, the weak letter is visible immediately. If it does not, two pieces of recent marked work show it clearly enough. In Sciences the usual culprit is criterion B, inquiring and designing, where a hypothesis without scientific reasoning or a method that never names controlled variables caps the mark no matter how carefully the experiment was run.

In Mathematics the pattern differs. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is usually fine in Dubai schools because it is what classwork drills. Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where students stop: they can compute terms but cannot generalise to a rule and justify it. Criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, is the other common gap, and it is a writing problem as much as a maths one, because the marks sit in stating assumptions and evaluating whether the model was sensible. Both respond quickly to targeted practice, which is why naming the letter matters more than adding hours.

sections.heading: Counting the MYP 5 Personal Project backwards from submission
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the only piece of MYP work with a deadline a family will remember years later, and it is assessed on planning, on applying skills, and on reflecting. Not on the quality of the object produced. A student who builds something impressive and documents it thinly scores below one who sets a modest goal, records the process honestly and reflects on what went wrong. Parents consistently find this counter-intuitive, and it is the single most useful thing to understand before paying anyone for project support.

Schools set their own internal deadlines, usually with a proposal in the first term of MYP 5, supervisor check-ins across the year, and a report plus process journal extracts at the end. The failure mode is predictable: a student chooses a goal in October, does nothing until the holidays, and then writes a report about a process that was never recorded. The process journal cannot be reconstructed afterwards without it being obvious, and the marks for applying skills and reflecting depend on it existing contemporaneously.

What a tutor may do here is narrow and should be stated plainly, because this is where some providers in this market cross a line. A tutor may teach project planning, challenge a goal that is too broad to evidence, model what a reflective entry looks like, and give feedback on the student's own draft. No tutor writes the report, supplies the product, or edits a draft into something the student could not have produced. IB academic honesty rules make the student's authorship the point of the exercise, and a breach is the student's problem, not the provider's.

sections.heading: Online versus an in-home tutor driving out to Al Khawaneej
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search term implies, so here it is without evasion. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The case for online delivery to Al Khawaneej therefore has to stand on its own merits, and in this particular community it is unusually strong for reasons of geography rather than ideology.

Al Khawaneej sits at the eastern limit of the city. A tutor travelling from Jumeirah, Dubai Marina or Business Bay at the hour a school child is free will spend forty to sixty minutes each way. That tutor has to charge for the trip, directly or by quoting a rate that absorbs it, and will only accept a slot that justifies the journey, which is why in-home bookings in the eastern suburbs cluster into inconvenient times and collapse when traffic does. The tutor pool shrinks to those willing to make the drive, and willingness to drive is not correlated with knowing criterion B in MYP Sciences.

Online, the pool is everyone available at Gulf Standard Time who teaches that subject group. A session can start at 17:30 after a Festival City school run without anyone budgeting for the return leg. Two siblings on different timetables can both be taught on the same evening. Written work is screen-shared and annotated live, which for criterion C in Mathematics is better than a tutor leaning over a notebook. Nothing here requires pretending that online suits every child; it requires being honest that for this postcode the trade-offs favour it.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed to deliver, and KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidelines required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. MYP families frequently discover this as a surprise on a report card, because the subject sits outside the eight MYP groups and is sometimes reported separately.

The rules are more specific than most parents realise. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies for Arab students is taught primarily in Arabic; non-Arabs study Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details matter for planning support. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which means tutoring here is consolidation of the school's own material rather than an alternative scheme. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate approval from KHDA to teach them, which is a credential a parent can reasonably ask about.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you are about to pay actually permitted to teach here?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced private tuition work permits, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The consequence parents should act on: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. What is publishable is that the permit is free and takes two working days, which removes any excuse a tutor might offer for not holding one. Asking is not rude. It is the one compliance question in this market with a clear, cheap, documented answer.

A second rule applies in Abu Dhabi and is worth knowing even from Dubai, because tutors move between emirates. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, and never arrange for a child's own classroom teacher to be paid privately for the same subject.

sections.heading: What happens when no MYP specialist is free
paragraphs: No tutoring platform covers every subject group at every level at every hour, and claiming otherwise is how families end up with a mismatched tutor in week one. For MYP work the common gaps are predictable: Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education are requested far less often than Mathematics and Sciences, so the pool of tutors who genuinely know those criterion descriptors is thinner, and Language Acquisition in a less common language can take longer to staff.

The honest process when that happens has three steps. The first is to say so, with an estimate of how long a match will take rather than a vague reassurance. The second is to offer the nearest useful alternative and name it as an alternative: a Sciences specialist can do a great deal for a Design student whose problem is criterion A research, because the underlying skill is the same, but a family deserves to be told that is what is happening. The third is to decline the booking where neither applies, which is less profitable and considerably better for everyone.

This also governs who teaches. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a niche MYP subject group, the match may be a specialist elsewhere teaching over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time. That is disclosed before anything is booked, not discovered later from an accent or a timezone slip. Nothing about the delivery changes, because nothing about the delivery was ever in-person in the UAE.

process.title: Send the report, not the worry
process.description: Share the most recent MYP report and two pieces of marked work. Criterion letters on the report shorten diagnosis to minutes. Without them, two marked tasks in the weak subject group do the same job. Describing the problem in words is the slowest route and the one most likely to point at the wrong subject.

process.title: Agree the slot against the school run
process.description: For an Al Khawaneej address this usually means 17:00 or later on a weekday, and earlier on a Saturday. Fixing the time before choosing the tutor avoids the common failure where a good match is agreed and then quietly abandoned because the slot never worked.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: The trial is a diagnostic session, not a sales call. By the end you should have a named criterion, an explanation of why marks are lost there, and a view on how many weeks the repair takes. If none of that arrives, the match is wrong and should be changed before money moves.

process.title: Run six weeks, then check the school's own marks
process.description: Six weeks is long enough for a criterion score to move and short enough that a bad match is not expensive. Review against the school's reporting rather than the tutor's impression, then extend, change subject group, or stop.

process.title: Stop when the mark holds
process.description: Open-ended tutoring is how a reasonable monthly spend becomes a permanent one. When the weak criterion has held at the target level across two assessments, end the block. Coming back for the MYP 5 project and the Diploma decision is cheaper than never leaving.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level diagnosis, not general revision
whyPoints.description: MYP grades are produced by four lettered criteria per subject group. Support that does not name which letter it is targeting is revision with a tutor attached. Every session here starts from the weak criterion and the marked work that shows it.

whyPoints.title: Published market rates, attributed
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page come from named Dubai providers and from Bestimate's Dubai rate table, with each figure attached to whoever published it. We do not quote them as our prices, and we do not pretend a market has no prices because it suits us.

whyPoints.title: One-to-one over live video, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson is one-to-one on live video at Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Saying that clearly costs us some enquiries and saves every family that would otherwise have been disappointed.

whyPoints.title: A clear line around assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. No tutor here produces a Personal Project, an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay. Several providers in this market blur that line; an IB academic-honesty finding falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: The permit question asked out loud
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free and takes two working days, so there is no reasonable excuse for a tutor not holding one. We publish the rule, the resolution it comes from and the official application route rather than hoping nobody asks.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before booking
whyPoints.description: Where no specialist covers a niche MYP subject group, you are told, given a time estimate, and offered either a named alternative or an honest decline. Nobody is quietly matched to a tutor who has never read the relevant criterion descriptors.

faqs.question: What does an IB MYP tutor in Al Khawaneej charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates for Middle Years Programme support in Dubai run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour online for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 180 to 500 an hour for an in-home visit once travel is included. Those bands come from published provider rates: Unitors from AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, Bestimate's Dubai table at AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist work. Budget online options sit lower, from AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. IB Gram publishes no fixed UAE price list, because the right figure depends on how many subject groups are genuinely weak. The trial lesson is free and the quote follows it.

faqs.question: Why do Al Khawaneej agencies quote MYP hours below Diploma hours?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, by roughly AED 50 to 100 an hour at the same tutor tier, because there is no external examination to coach for. That discount is reasonable in MYP 1 to MYP 3 and misleading in MYP 5, where the Personal Project and the Diploma subject decision both land. A weak criterion identified in MYP 4 costs a term of ordinary-rate sessions to fix. The same weakness discovered in Year 12 costs specialist rates for a full academic year. The cheap moment to buy MYP support is earlier than most families choose.

faqs.question: Why has my child's MYP grade dropped when their test scores went up?
faqs.answer: Because MYP grades are not averages of test scores. Each subject group is marked against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, and the total out of 32 converts to the 1 to 7 grade on the report. A child can answer more content questions correctly and still lose a grade band if the marks were lost in, say, criterion B in Sciences, where a method that never names controlled variables caps the score. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown. The weak letter explains the drop in a way the grade never will.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion do students in Dubai lose most marks on?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject group, and that is the point. In Sciences it is criterion B, inquiring and designing: hypotheses without scientific reasoning, methods missing controlled variables. In Mathematics it is B and D, investigating patterns and applying maths in real-life contexts, both of which require generalising and justifying rather than calculating. In Language and Literature it is criterion A, analysing, where strong readers summarise plot instead of examining a writer's choices. In Individuals and Societies it is criterion D, thinking critically. None of these improve with more content revision.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's MYP Personal Project in Al Khawaneej?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may teach project planning, challenge a goal too broad to evidence, demonstrate what a reflective journal entry looks like, teach the research or technical skill being applied, and give feedback on the student's own draft. No tutor writes the report, supplies the product or edits a draft into something the student could not have produced. The project is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, so the process journal has to be the student's own contemporaneous record. Reconstructing it afterwards is visible to any experienced supervisor.

faqs.question: What time can an Al Khawaneej MYP lesson realistically start on a weekday?
faqs.answer: For most Al Khawaneej 1 addresses, 17:00 is the earliest that holds reliably. School runs leave the community for Mirdif, Al Mizhar, Al Rashidiya or Academic City, so a child is rarely home before 16:15, and Al Khawaneej 2 families driving to Festival City should plan for 17:30. Families whose children attend locally in Mirdif can manage 16:00. Fixing the slot before choosing the tutor matters more than it sounds: the usual reason a good match quietly fails is a time that never actually worked.

faqs.question: Do you send an MYP tutor to our villa in Al Khawaneej?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For this community that is usually the better trade anyway: a tutor travelling from central Dubai spends forty to sixty minutes each way at exactly the hour your child is free, and prices the journey into the rate. Online, the pool is every specialist available at your time, and a 17:30 start costs nobody a commute.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an MYP student in Al Khawaneej need?
faqs.answer: One, in one subject group, is the defensible starting point. The common error here is four subjects across four afternoons in MYP 2, which is a large monthly spend buying reassurance at a stage where the marks carry no forward weight. Where a report shows two weak groups, two shorter sessions on separate evenings cost less than two full hours and fit an activity schedule better. Review after six weeks against the school's own marks, then extend, switch subject group, or stop. Open-ended weekly hours are how a sensible spend becomes permanent.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to study Arabic and Islamic Education on the MYP?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The rules are detailed: separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in three of the subjects, Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs, and no additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission. Tutoring in these subjects consolidates the school's own material rather than substituting an alternative scheme.

faqs.question: Does my MYP tutor need a UAE permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, issued by MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time via its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published. Ask to see the permit before the first paid session.

faqs.question: Is MYP eAssessment something we need to budget for?
faqs.answer: Only if your child's school offers it. MYP eAssessment is the optional route to the IB MYP Certificate, combining on-screen examinations with moderated ePortfolios, and many Dubai schools do not use it at all. Ask the school directly before buying anything described as eAssessment preparation. Where a school does run it, the useful support is practice under on-screen conditions and portfolio discipline rather than extra content, which is a short finite block rather than a year of weekly hours.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 4 and we are deciding Higher Level subjects. Is tutoring worth it now?
faqs.answer: This is the highest-value moment to buy support, and most families miss it. A grade 6 carried by criterion A with criterion C sitting at 3 looks like a safe Higher Level choice and is not: the same weakness meets the Diploma internal assessment eighteen months later, at specialist rates, with an external deadline attached. A term of ordinary sessions in MYP 4 either closes the gap or tells you honestly that a different Higher Level choice is wiser. Both outcomes are worth more than the invoice.

faqs.question: Do you teach MYP Design and Arts, or only maths and science?
faqs.answer: Both, but availability differs and pretending otherwise would waste your time. Mathematics, Sciences and English Language and Literature are well covered and usually matched within a few days. Individuals and Societies takes about a week. Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education are requested less often, so the pool of tutors who genuinely know those criterion descriptors is thinner and a match can take a week or more. Where no specialist is free, we say so, offer a named subject-adjacent alternative, or decline rather than deliver a mismatch.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective MYP tutor before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Four questions settle it. Which criterion letter are we targeting, and what evidence points there? What will you do differently from what the school already does? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? And what will you not do with the Personal Project? A tutor who answers the first with a grade rather than a letter has not read the descriptors. One who hesitates on the fourth is selling something that puts your child's IB registration at risk, not tutoring.

faqs.question: Are Dubai school fees rising, and does that change the tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household budget that means the tutoring line is not competing with a fee rise this year. It also means the market has little pressure to discount, so the AED bands published above are a reasonable planning assumption rather than a ceiling to negotiate down from.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.closingHeading: Start with one criterion, one subject group, and a free trial lesson
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.closingBody: If you have an MYP report with criterion marks on it, that document is most of the diagnosis. Send it with two pieces of marked work from the weakest subject group, tell us what time the Al Khawaneej school run actually ends, and take the free trial lesson. You should finish it knowing which lettered criterion is costing the grade, why, and roughly how many weeks of one-to-one work it takes to move. Lessons run over live video on Gulf Standard Time. If we cannot staff the subject group properly, we will say so rather than book you in and improvise.

intro.heading: The programme with no examination is the one where money disappears
paragraphs: There is a reason Middle Years tutoring is where families lose the most money without noticing. In an IGCSE year there is a public examination, a syllabus you can look up, past papers you can mark, and a grade at the end that either moved or did not. The Middle Years Programme has none of that for most of its five years. There are four criteria per subject scored zero to eight, a conversion to a one-to-seven grade using boundaries the school rarely volunteers, and a report twice a year that most parents cannot read.

In that information vacuum, spending feels like action. A report arrives with a 4 in sciences, a family in Al Mamzar hires a weekly science tutor at the going rate, and a term later the report still shows a 4 because nobody worked on the criterion that was actually low. The tutor was competent, the sessions were pleasant, and the money bought a feeling. That pattern repeats across this district and across the city, and the only defence against it is reading the report before spending anything.

So this page is organised around cost. What the Dubai market charges, with sources. What each band genuinely buys and where it adds nothing. The five purchases that reliably produce no measurable change in a Middle Years report. The free interventions - and there are several - that outperform paid tutoring at this stage. And the one component, the Personal Project, where late money cannot help at all because the marks depend on records written months earlier.

Al Mamzar's position adds a specific wrinkle. The neighbourhood sits against the Sharjah border, no IB school is in it, and the nearest provision is in Al Garhoud, Dubai Festival City and Mirdif. IB programmes are about 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, concentrated away from this district, so a Middle Years family here is usually the only one on their street. That means no local word-of-mouth to sanity-check a price against, which is exactly the condition in which an unreasonable rate goes unchallenged.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Mamzar or anywhere else in the UAE; a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The honest cost consequence is simple: the travel premium that sits inside a visiting rate - and which is larger to this district than to most - is not in the price because the journey does not happen. That is a real saving rather than a discount, and it is the one claim on this page that needs no qualification.

One more framing point before the numbers. Tutoring in this programme should be bought the way a repair is bought rather than the way a subscription is: with a named fault, a stated cost, and a test afterwards of whether the fault was fixed. The sections that follow give you each of those - the market bands and what each one genuinely buys, the five purchases that produce nothing, the single competence worth paying a qualified rate for, the four free interventions that frequently outperform paid work, and the one component where late money cannot help at any price.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-mamzar.programmesIntro: What support is worth buying changes sharply across the five Middle Years years. These are the stages, costed by what each one can actually deliver.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, years one to three
programmes.description: The years where paid subject tutoring returns least. Nothing is externally examined, criterion scores are genuinely formative, and the skills that matter - reading a task sheet, planning backwards from a deadline, keeping a usable record - are cheap to teach and expensive to buy repeatedly. Three weekly subject sessions at this age removes the unstructured time in which independent habits form.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Mamzar family the comparison worth running is against the local tuition-centre market, which is well developed in Deira and Al Qusais and considerably cheaper per hour. For routine consolidation and supervised homework at this age, a centre is frequently better value than a one-to-one rate, and we would say so rather than argue otherwise.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, years four and five
programmes.description: Where targeted spending starts to pay. Subject choices narrow, mathematics separates into standard and extended, and criterion scores begin to carry weight with Diploma coordinators. A block aimed at one named criterion in one subject, measured by the school's next report, is the only Middle Years purchase whose effect a parent can verify afterwards.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP 4 mathematics decision is the highest-value conversation available in this programme and it costs nothing to have. Extended mathematics is the realistic preparation for Diploma Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level; standard mathematics generally is not, and the consequence appears in Year 12 rather than at the point of choosing.

programmes.name: The Personal Project, MYP 5
programmes.description: Twenty-four marks across three criteria - planning, applying skills and reflecting, at eight each - with the process journal as the evidence base for all three. The only Middle Years component with a hard deadline, and the one where late spending is genuinely worthless, because planning and reflecting marks depend on records written as the work happened.
programmes.countryNote: The rescue request we receive most often from this district is for a Personal Project four weeks from a school deadline with an empty journal. The honest answer is that no amount of money recovers those marks, and we say so rather than taking the booking. Fifteen minutes a week from the start costs nothing and is worth more than any late intervention.

programmes.name: After MYP 5: the Diploma transition
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. The shift is from criterion-referenced tasks to published weightings and external papers, and the first set of examination-style marks disorients even strong students. A summer block before Year 12 is the best-value spend in this whole sequence.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Mamzar family the Diploma decision has a travel dimension too. If the school offering the Diploma sits across the creek or east in Mirdif, that is a two-year commitment to a particular journey at sixteen, and it is worth weighing while the MYP 5 subject plan is still open.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-mamzar.subjectsIntro: These are the Middle Years subject groups Al Mamzar families ask about, with the criterion that usually explains the report and a note on whether paid support is worth it.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where paid support pays, because generalising and justifying is a teachable skill most students are never shown explicitly.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Processing and evaluating is the criterion worth buying work on; general science tutoring against a low overall grade is the classic waste.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. A strong analysing score with a weak organising score is two or three sessions of structural work rather than a term of reading - one of the cheapest fixes in the programme.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Assessed by phase rather than year group, so a low score may reflect placement rather than performance. Worth asking the school which phase applies before paying for anything, because the answer sometimes dissolves the problem.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. Thinking critically carries the marks and needs source and perspective evaluation, which is a skill rather than content and therefore responds quickly to targeted work.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Marked on the design cycle rather than the product. A student producing impressive objects with thin documentation is losing marks under two criteria, and the fix is documentation habits - which also transfer straight into the Personal Project.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: The process journal carries more weight than students expect, so a capable performer with a thin journal loses marks across two criteria. Paid specialist tuition in an arts discipline is among the thinnest supply in this district.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Written criteria mean a highly capable athlete can score poorly, which is a frequent source of confusion on reports here. Rarely worth paid tutoring; usually worth a conversation with the teacher about which criterion is low.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what each band actually buys
paragraphs: Published rates in this city separate into identifiable bands, and the useful exercise is matching the band to the need rather than assuming more is better. At the budget end, Tutopiya publishes online rates from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which generally means a university student. That is entirely adequate for supervised homework, routine practice and keeping a twelve-year-old on task, which is a large share of what Middle Years families actually need.

The qualified-tutor band sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. For Middle Years purposes this band buys something specific: a tutor who can read a criteria descriptor and work on the skill it describes rather than on the subject it sits in. That is the competence the programme requires, and it is not the same as subject knowledge.

Above that, specialist rates run AED 200 to 450 and above - TutorChase quotes around AED 270, Bestimate's specialist band runs to AED 450 and higher, and BartyED sits at around AED 650 for examiner-led sessions. For the Middle Years Programme that band is rarely justified, because there is no external examination to specialise in and no mark scheme that rewards examiner familiarity. Paying it for MYP 2 mathematics is paying for scarcity that does not apply.

In-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and advertised packages run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. For a younger student who needs a person present, the premium is defensible. For criterion work on a shared screen with the school's own task sheet open, it buys nothing additional - and the journey to Al Mamzar is longer than average.

sections.heading: The five Middle Years purchases that reliably produce nothing
paragraphs: These five account for most of the wasted Middle Years spending we see, and none of them involves a bad tutor. Each is a sensible-looking purchase aimed at the wrong thing, which is why it survives for a whole term before anybody notices. All five are avoidable with ten minutes spent on the report first.

The first is buying a subject when the report named a criterion. A 4 in sciences with a high knowing-and-understanding score and a low processing-and-evaluating score is a data-handling gap, and weekly general science tutoring will not touch it. The second is paying a specialist rate for a programme with no external examination - the specialist band exists because Higher Level Diploma expertise is scarce, and that scarcity does not transfer to MYP 2.

The third is three weekly subject sessions for a disorganised eleven or twelve-year-old. The problem is approaches to learning, one tutor can address all of it, and three sessions a week removes the unstructured time in which independent habits would otherwise form. The fourth is a Personal Project rescue in the final month, which cannot work because the planning and reflecting marks depend on contemporaneous records.

The fifth is the quietest: continuing a block past the point where it stopped producing. Because the Middle Years Programme has no external measure, a block can roll on for a year on the strength of the student seeming happier. The defence is to name a criterion at the start and let the school's next report be the measure, then stop, change or continue on that evidence rather than on impression.

sections.heading: What you are actually paying for: criteria literacy
paragraphs: The competence that makes a Middle Years tutor worth a qualified rate is not subject knowledge - plenty of cheaper tutors have that. It is the ability to read a criteria descriptor and teach the specific skill it names, which is a narrower and rarer skill than it sounds. A descriptor for criterion C in sciences describes what processing and evaluating data looks like at each band, and a tutor who can turn that into six weeks of work is doing something a subject tutor usually cannot.

Here is the test, and it costs nothing in a trial lesson. Hand the tutor your child's school task sheet with its criteria descriptors attached and ask what band the last piece of work sat in and why. A criterion-literate tutor will point at specific sentences in the descriptor and specific features of the work. A subject tutor will talk about the content being right or wrong, which is a different conversation and not the one the report is reporting.

The second test is about the conversion. Ask what the student's criterion total out of thirty-two converts to, and whether they know that the boundaries differ by subject. A tutor who says the school publishes those boundaries and that you should ask for them is being straight with you. One who treats twenty-two out of thirty-two as a fixed percentage has not worked in this programme.

Those two questions sort the market faster than any credential list, and they matter because this is the one competence worth paying the qualified band for in the Middle Years Programme. Below it, cheaper supervision is adequate. Above it, the specialist band buys examination expertise that has nothing to apply to. Criteria literacy is the narrow thing the price should be bought for, and it is checkable in ten minutes.

sections.heading: Four free things that outperform paid tutoring at this stage
paragraphs: This is the part of the page that costs us bookings, and it is the most useful part for a family in this district. Four interventions cost nothing, and in the Middle Years Programme each of them routinely produces more than a term of paid tutoring would. They are worth doing before any money is spent, not instead of spending it thoughtfully afterwards.

The first is asking the school for the grade boundaries. The conversion from a criterion total out of thirty-two to a one-to-seven grade differs by subject, and without the boundaries a parent cannot tell whether twenty-two marks is a comfortable 5 or a borderline 4. That single piece of information frequently changes how urgent a situation is, in both directions, and it takes one email.

The second is asking the subject teacher which criterion is low and what band descriptor the student is missing. Teachers answer this question when it is asked directly and specifically, and the answer is the brief any tutor would need anyway. Many families discover at this point that one teacher's concern is narrower than the report suggested.

The third is the process journal habit in MYP 5 - fifteen minutes a week, dated, written as the work happens. It is free, it underpins all three Personal Project criteria, and no later purchase replaces it. The fourth is backwards planning: sitting down with the student and a calendar, taking each internal deadline and working back to what must exist by when. That is the single skill the programme rewards most and the one least often taught at home.

sections.heading: Centres, groups and siblings: spending across a household
paragraphs: Al Mamzar, Hor Al Anz and Al Qusais have a real and well-priced tuition-centre market, and a page about cost that ignored it would be dishonest. For routine consolidation, homework supervision and structure at MYP 1 to 3, a term package at a local centre comes in well below a weekly one-to-one rate and delivers something one-to-one does not: a peer group and an externally imposed routine.

The limitation is targeting. A centre working with a dozen students cannot read one student's criteria descriptors and build six weeks around a named criterion. That is arithmetic rather than criticism. So the sensible split is by need: centre or group for routine, one-to-one for a diagnosed criterion. Most families in this district would be better off buying both at different stages than buying one-to-one continuously.

Sibling arrangements are the other place money is saved or wasted. Households here frequently have children on different curricula - one in the Middle Years Programme at a school in Al Garhoud, one on CBSE at a school in Al Qusais. The instinct is to find one tutor for both, and it is almost always wrong: CBSE support is cheaper and deeper locally, Middle Years criteria work needs a different competence, and one person covering both does neither well.

Where a household does have two Middle Years students, online delivery produces a genuine saving that in-home cannot. Two sessions can run back to back on the same evening with no second journey for anybody, and the second appointment costs no travel. From a district where visiting travel is longer than average, that is a meaningful difference in the monthly number rather than a talking point.
