sections.heading: The Personal Project: where late money buys nothing
paragraphs: Every Middle Years page should state this plainly because it is the one place a family can waste a significant sum in a fortnight. The Personal Project is marked out of twenty-four across three criteria - planning, applying skills and reflecting, eight marks each - and the process journal is the evidence base for all three. Two of those criteria depend on records written as the work happened, which means they are already substantially determined by the time a panic sets in.

A student four weeks from a school deadline with an ambitious goal and an empty journal has done real work and cannot evidence it. Planning marks need the goal, success criteria and resource thinking recorded at the start. Reflecting marks need dated reflections across the whole period, on skills and on the goal, not a closing paragraph headed reflection. Reconstructed journals read exactly like reconstruction to a marker, and writing them is also a question of honesty rather than only of effectiveness.

So the honest answer to a late request is that no purchase recovers those marks, and we give that answer rather than taking the booking. What can still be done legitimately in the final weeks is limited and worth naming: helping the student structure a report they write themselves, checking it against the published criteria for clarity, and making sure the product is measured against the success criteria the student stated.

The money that does work on this component is spent early and is small. Three or four sessions at the start - testing whether the goal is achievable with the time and resources available, explaining what each criterion rewards, and establishing the fifteen-minute weekly journal habit - protects twenty-four marks for a fraction of what a rescue would cost. That is the clearest example in this programme of timing mattering more than spending.

sections.heading: The honesty line, and the one credential you can verify
paragraphs: The Personal Project is where honesty and cost intersect, because the cheapest-looking way to protect twenty-four marks is to have somebody else produce the work. The boundary is clear. A tutor may test whether a goal is achievable, explain what each criterion rewards, model how a journal entry is written, ask the questions that produce genuine reflection, and comment on a draft the student has written.

A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product or write the report. The school authenticates that the work is the student's own, and if that authentication is untrue the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever helped or whoever was paid. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price; the seller keeps the fee and the candidate carries the whole risk, which is the least favourable trade available to a family.

Materials follow the same logic. We reference the IB subject guides and the Personal Project guide, cite them and point to the official source rather than reproducing them, because they are the board's copyright. Where a school's own unit plans and task sheets are the working material, those belong to the student and stay with the student rather than being circulated.

The verifiable credential is the permit, and it is free to check. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule - so treat any quoted penalty figure as unverified.

sections.heading: KHDA, fees and the border five minutes away
paragraphs: Private education in Dubai is overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The sector ran 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with International Baccalaureate programmes at 7 per cent of enrolment. Inspection reports are public, name subject-level strengths, and are the most useful free document available to a family comparing two Middle Years schools.

On the cost side, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household budgeting tutoring against fees, that holds one large line steady, which is worth knowing when deciding what the tutoring line can absorb.

Al Mamzar's position next to the Sharjah boundary makes the regulator map practically relevant. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so fee and curriculum approval, not only inspection, sits with the emirate. A family here with one child in Dubai and one in Sharjah is dealing with two frameworks. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi, the Department of Knowledge covers Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Within Dubai, the mandatory UAE subjects apply to the Middle Years Programme as to every other curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated against a forty-minute lesson unit, separate classes are required for Arab and non-Arab students in several of those subjects, and additional or different content needs prior permission from the Ministry of Education - which limits what any paid tutor may legitimately offer in them.

faqs.question: What does an IB MYP tutor cost in Al Mamzar, and what should we actually pay?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, which generally means a university student, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online, up to AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist work. For the Middle Years Programme, the budget band covers supervision and routine adequately, and the qualified band is worth paying where a tutor must read a criteria descriptor and teach the skill it names. The specialist band has no external examination to apply to in MYP 1 to 4.

faqs.question: Why is Middle Years tutoring the easiest money to waste?
faqs.answer: Because there is no independent measure. In an IGCSE year a public examination tells you whether the spending worked. In MYP 1 to 4 there is no external paper, no syllabus to check against and a report whose criterion scores most parents are never shown how to read. In that vacuum a block can roll on for a year on the strength of a student seeming happier. The defence is to name one criterion at the start and let the school's next report decide.

faqs.question: My daughter has a 4 in sciences. Should we hire a science tutor?
faqs.answer: Look at the criteria first, because the answer is often no. If the knowing-and-understanding score is high and the processing-and-evaluating score is low, she holds the content and cannot handle data - graphs, uncertainty, drawing a conclusion the evidence supports. Weekly general science tutoring will not touch that, and a term later the criterion will still be low. A block aimed at the named criterion, using her school's own task sheets, is the purchase that shows up in the next report.

faqs.question: What can I get for free before paying anybody in this district?
faqs.answer: Four things, and they routinely outperform a term of tutoring. Ask the school for the published grade boundaries, because the conversion from thirty-two criterion marks to a one-to-seven grade differs by subject. Ask each teacher which criterion is low and which band descriptor the work is missing. If your child is in MYP 5, start the fifteen-minute weekly process journal habit. And sit down with a calendar and plan backwards from each internal deadline.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Al Qusais cheaper than one-to-one for MYP?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and for the right need it is the better buy. A term package at a local centre comes in well below a weekly one-to-one rate and delivers a peer group and an externally imposed routine that one-to-one cannot. That suits MYP 1 to 3 consolidation well. What a centre cannot do is read one student's criteria descriptors and build six weeks around a named criterion, because a dozen students are in the room. Split the spending by need rather than choosing one model.

faqs.question: Do you charge extra to come to Al Mamzar?
faqs.answer: We do not come to Al Mamzar at all. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India - so every lesson here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The cost consequence is that the travel component inside a visiting rate simply is not there. Published in-home rates in this market run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and the journey to this district is longer than average.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor can actually read MYP criteria?
faqs.answer: Hand them your child's school task sheet with its criteria descriptors attached and ask which band the last piece of work sat in and why. A criterion-literate tutor will point at specific sentences in the descriptor and specific features of the work. A subject tutor will talk about content being right or wrong, which is a different conversation. Then ask what a total out of thirty-two converts to, and whether boundaries differ by subject - the honest answer is that the school publishes them.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP 5 with an empty Personal Project journal and six weeks left. What can money do?
faqs.answer: Honestly, very little, and we would decline a rescue booking rather than take it. The project is marked out of twenty-four across planning, applying skills and reflecting, and two of those criteria depend on records written as the work happened. A reconstructed journal reads as reconstruction, and writing one raises an honesty question as well as an effectiveness one. What remains legitimate is helping him structure a report he writes himself and checking it against the published criteria for clarity.

faqs.question: We have one child in MYP and one on CBSE. Can one tutor cover both?
faqs.answer: Almost never well, and trying is a common false economy in this district. CBSE support is cheaper and deeper locally, because Indian-curriculum schools are 26 per cent of Dubai's enrolment and a far higher share here. Middle Years criteria work needs a different competence - reading descriptors and teaching the skill they name. Two separate arrangements, one local and one online, usually cost less in total than one compromise and produce more for both children.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for maths tutoring before the MYP 4 decision?
faqs.answer: It is one of the better-value purchases in the programme, provided it targets the right criterion. The extended against standard mathematics decision is the most consequential choice in the Middle Years Programme, and it usually rests on criterion A, knowing and understanding, when it should rest on criterion B, investigating patterns - generalising a rule, testing it and justifying why it holds. A short block aimed at criterion B, with a timed task marked against the descriptors, is also the evidence a school will respond to.

faqs.question: Does the school fee freeze change what we can spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: For some households it does. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family budgeting tutoring against fees, that holds the largest line steady. It is worth planning the tutoring line against that rather than against an assumed fee rise.

faqs.question: How many sessions should a first MYP block be?
faqs.answer: Six to eight, with a named criterion and an end date at the school's next reporting cycle. Shorter than that and the criterion has no time to move; longer and you are paying past the point where the evidence arrives. The structure matters more than the number: a named target, the school's own task sheets as material, and the school's report rather than the tutor's opinion as the measure. Then decide to continue, change tutor or stop.

faqs.question: Why is the summer before Year 12 called the best-value spend?
faqs.answer: Because it prevents a problem that costs several times more to repair mid-course. The move from criterion-referenced tasks to published weightings and external papers disorients even strong students, and mathematics is where the gap is real rather than presentational - particularly for students who took standard rather than extended. Six to eight sessions across the summer, before the Diploma starts, is cheaper than the equivalent work bought in the middle of Year 12 when the course is already running at full speed.

faqs.question: What if the subject group we need is one you cannot cover?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than putting a generalist on it. Some Middle Years needs are genuinely thin - a specific arts discipline, a language acquisition phase, or a physical and health education written criterion. When that happens you get three straight answers: how long a match realistically takes, whether the approaches-to-learning work would address part of the problem meanwhile, and whether the school's own department or a local option is the better route. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-mamzar.closingHeading: Read the report before spending anything
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-mamzar.closingBody: If you are considering an IB MYP tutor in Al Mamzar, the honest sequence is this. Ask the school for the grade boundaries. Ask each teacher which criterion is low. Then look at whether what you were about to buy addresses that criterion or merely the subject it sits in. If it does not, do not buy it. If it does, name the criterion, set the school's next report as the measure, and match the rate band to the need rather than to the price that reads as reassuring. The trial lesson and the consultation cost nothing either way.

intro.heading: Why the Al Manara school run decides your tutoring timetable
paragraphs: Al Manara is a villa district with almost no schools inside it. That one fact shapes everything about arranging an IB MYP tutor here. The compounds off Al Manara Street and the streets backing onto Umm Suqeim Road are residential; the schools the children attend sit in Al Safa, Al Wasl, Jumeirah 1, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha. A Year 9 student leaves at 06:45 and gets home somewhere between 15:20 and 16:40, depending on whether the bus turns right onto Al Wasl Road or queues at the Umm Suqeim Road interchange.

Parents here rarely ask first about qualifications. They ask what time a lesson can start. A tutor who can only offer 15:30 is useless to a family whose child is still on Sheikh Zayed Road at 15:50. A tutor who offers 20:30 is useless to a Year 7 who falls asleep at 20:45. The workable window in this neighbourhood is narrow, and it is different for each child in the same villa, because siblings in MYP Year 2 and MYP Year 5 are often at different schools on different bus routes.

Online delivery exists for exactly this reason. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. What that removes is the travel block on both sides. A tutor does not need thirty-five minutes to reach Al Manara from Al Quoz and thirty-five minutes to leave, so the lesson can be booked at 16:30 on a Tuesday and 19:00 on a Thursday for the same child without either slot being padded out to protect a drive.

It also widens who can teach your child. The MYP is eight subject groups, each with its own four criteria, and a Design teacher who can mark Criterion B against the actual descriptors is not necessarily living within a twenty-minute radius of Al Manara. Matching on subject and criterion knowledge rather than on postcode is the whole argument, and a parent can test it in one trial lesson by asking the tutor to mark a returned task and explain the band.

This page is written around that timetable problem. It sets out which schools this neighbourhood actually feeds, what time each ends, how long the drive back takes in the afternoon peak, and the earliest session that is realistic rather than theoretical. It then covers how MYP is assessed, where marks go missing between Year 7 and Year 11, what the Dubai market charges, and where the boundary sits between teaching a Personal Project and interfering with it.

One piece of context before the detail. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, and International Baccalaureate schools accounted for seven per cent of that enrolment against thirty-seven per cent for UK-curriculum schools. The MYP is therefore a minority programme in a very large market, which is why a neighbourhood tutor who happens to be free at 16:30 is far more likely to know Key Stage 3 than to know what Criterion B asks for.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-manara.programmesIntro: Al Manara children sit in all three IB continuum programmes, often within one family. The MYP is the middle one, and the handover points on either side of it are where most tutoring requests from this neighbourhood begin.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and an assessment model that marks against published criteria rather than a syllabus checklist. Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education and Design each carry four criteria lettered A to D. MYP Year 5 adds the Personal Project and, in schools that opt in, on-screen eAssessment leading to the IB MYP Certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP schools sit under KHDA inspection on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and must run Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP whatever the licensed curriculum. For an Al Manara family that means a Year 8 timetable carrying eight MYP subject groups plus the mandatory UAE subjects, which is why the complaint reaching us from this area is usually workload management rather than one weak subject.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Assessment shifts decisively towards terminal written papers, and the criterion language a student spent five MYP years learning is replaced by subject-specific mark schemes and command terms. UAE schools sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP step is the most common reason an Al Manara parent books a tutor for a Year 11 student. The schools this neighbourhood feeds include continuum schools where the same student stays put, and British-curriculum schools where MYP students leave for IGCSE instead. Both routes lead into DP1 somewhere, and the maths and sciences gaps differ sharply between them.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry organised around six themes, with no external examinations and an exhibition in the final year. Reading fluency, number sense and written structure are the three things that carry forward, and weaknesses in any of them surface in MYP Year 1 as an inability to meet Criterion C on communication.
programmes.countryNote: Younger siblings in Al Manara villas are usually in PYP at the same school the older child attends, on the same bus. Booking two children into consecutive online slots on the same afternoon is straightforward; booking two in-home visits on the same afternoon in this part of Jumeirah generally is not, because of what the drive costs the tutor.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-manara.subjectsIntro: MYP subject groups are requested unevenly in Al Manara. Mathematics and Sciences dominate, Design and Individuals and Societies arrive late in Year 5 when the Personal Project collides with everything else, and Language Acquisition requests cluster around French and Arabic.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where Al Manara students lose most: a pattern is spotted, a general rule is written, and the proof or justification that earns the top band is never attempted.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.levels: Integrated and discrete Biology, Chemistry, Physics
subjects.description: Criterion B inquiring and designing and Criterion C processing and evaluating carry the practical work. Students arrive able to write a method but unable to identify a controlled variable precisely enough for the top band, and evaluation collapses into 'the experiment went well'.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criterion A analysing, B organising, C producing text, D using language. The commonest fault in this cohort is strong content with no structural signposting, which caps Criterion B however good the ideas are.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Four criteria covering comprehension of spoken and visual text, comprehension of written and visual text, communicating, and using language. French and Arabic are the two most requested here. Phase placement matters more than year group and is frequently misunderstood by parents.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, thinking critically. Criterion D asks for evaluation of sources and recognition of different perspectives; students describe instead of evaluating and sit in the middle band for years without being told why.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The design cycle is a documentation exercise as much as a making exercise, and marks are lost in Criterion A for a research plan that was written after the product rather than before it.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, responding. The process journal is the assessed artefact as much as the finished piece, and students who work without documenting cannot be credited for what they did.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, reflecting and improving performance. Written components surprise families who assumed this subject was marked on the field.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: A year-long independent project with a process journal and a report, assessed on planning, applying skills, and reflecting. A tutor may coach the process and question the reasoning; the product and the writing must be the student's own.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against its own criteria covering evaluating, synthesising and reflecting. Students treat these units as a second copy of one subject and lose the synthesis marks that are the entire point of the component.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB MYP tutor in Al Manara is actually asking
paragraphs: It is asking whether anyone can teach the Middle Years Programme properly at a time your child is awake and at home. An IB MYP tutor in Al Manara is not scarce because MYP teachers are scarce in Dubai; the city has a large MYP teaching population. It is scarce because the overlap between a tutor's free hours, your child's arrival time and the drive between them is thin, and the drive is the part nobody mentions in the listing.

The MYP compounds that problem. A school offering the full programme runs eight subject groups, and a child who is struggling is usually struggling in two or three. Finding one person within a twenty-minute radius of Al Manara who can mark Mathematics Criterion B and Sciences Criterion C against the published descriptors is a narrow search. Finding two specialists who can each take one subject over video, on different evenings, is not narrow at all.

So the honest answer to the search is this. IB Gram delivers MYP tutoring to Al Manara as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled around the bus rather than around a tutor's commute, and matched on subject group and criterion fluency. There is no tutor arriving at an Al Manara address, from us or from any part of our service in the UAE, because that is not what we sell here. What you get instead is the subject specialist rather than the nearest available adult, and a 16:30 start that is a real 16:30.

The rest of this page is the detail behind that: the school run laid out school by school, the criterion model that decides your child's grade, what the Dubai market charges, and the lines a tutor must not cross on assessed work.

paragraphs: Published finish times and actual arrival times are different numbers, and the gap between them is where tutoring plans fail. A school that ends at 14:50 loads buses until 15:10. The Al Wasl Road and Umm Suqeim Road corridors are busiest between 15:00 and 16:00, which is precisely when those buses are moving. An Al Manara villa on a route with four prior stops receives its child later than the same villa on a route with one.

Treat the arrival column as a window, not a promise, and treat the final column as the earliest slot that will not be routinely missed. Families who book the theoretical slot rather than the realistic one cancel roughly one lesson in four, and a cancelled lesson in MYP Year 5 is the difference between a Personal Project submitted on time and one submitted in a panic.

Two practical consequences follow. First, book the later slot and keep it, rather than the earlier slot and lose it: a 17:30 that always happens beats a 16:30 that happens three weeks in four. Second, if two siblings are on different routes, do not try to make one tutoring afternoon serve both. Consecutive online slots on the same evening cost nothing extra in travel, so there is no reason to compress them.

Thursday is the exception worth planning for. The week ends and so does concentration. For most Al Manara students the productive midweek slots are Monday to Wednesday, with Sunday used for the week's heaviest subject and Thursday left alone or used for a short review.

sections.heading: How MYP grades are actually built: four criteria, 32 marks
paragraphs: Parents moving into the MYP from a British or Indian system expect percentages and find letters instead. Every MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, and each criterion is marked out of 8. That gives 32 raw marks per subject across the year. Those 32 marks convert to a final 1-7 grade using boundaries the IB publishes per subject; the boundaries are not a fixed percentage and should not be guessed at.

The criteria are not interchangeable. In Mathematics, Criterion A is knowing and understanding, B is investigating patterns, C is communicating and D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences, A is knowing and understanding, B is inquiring and designing, C is processing and evaluating, and D is reflecting on the impacts of science. A student can be fluent in content and still sit at 4 out of 8 on Criterion B for two straight years, because nobody has shown them what the 7-8 band descriptor asks for that the 5-6 band does not.

This is why MYP tutoring that treats the subject as content revision does very little. The useful lesson takes a returned task, reads the criterion descriptor aloud, locates the exact sentence in your child's work that caps the band, and rewrites that sentence with the student until the band moves. That is a specific, teachable skill, and it is the single highest-return thing an MYP tutor does.

The table lists the four criteria for the subject groups Al Manara families request most. Use it to read your child's next report properly: a 6, 4, 7, 3 profile is a completely different problem from a flat 5, 5, 5, 5, and the two need different tutoring.

sections.heading: Where Al Manara students lose MYP marks between Year 7 and Year 11
paragraphs: The pattern is consistent enough to predict. In MYP Years 1 and 2 the losses are presentational: working not shown, units omitted, a conclusion that restates the question. These cost Criterion C marks in Mathematics and Sciences and are fixable in three or four lessons, because the content is understood and only the recording is wrong.

In Years 3 and 4 the losses move to investigation. Criterion B in Mathematics asks a student to select a technique, apply it, recognise a pattern, describe a general rule and then justify or prove it. Most students stop after describing the rule. In Sciences the mirror failure is a method that controls the obvious variable and ignores two others, and an evaluation that lists what went wrong without saying what it did to the data. Both are habits, and habits take six to eight weeks of weekly work to replace.

In Year 5 the losses become organisational. The Personal Project, the eAssessment preparation in schools that offer it, and the first serious extended writing in Individuals and Societies all land in the same months. Students who have coped by doing homework the night before cannot cope with a project that has to be worked on over months, and the mark they lose is in planning and reflecting rather than in the product.

A tutor who knows this sequence treats a Year 7 request differently from a Year 10 one. The Year 7 lesson is about recording and precision. The Year 10 lesson is about investigation structure. The Year 11 lesson is largely about time, documentation and holding a plan, and parents in this neighbourhood are frequently surprised that the most valuable MYP tutoring in Year 5 looks less like teaching and more like supervision.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs around Al Manara, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Start from the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is what a family actually commits to. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts weekly one-hour tutoring at AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those two package prices are the clearest statement of what travel costs in Dubai.

Converted to hours, the same market splits five ways. Budget online tutoring, often university students, runs AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at AED 180-500, with Bestimate at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-level tutors reach AED 500-650 or more, with BartyED at AED 650.

Three things move an MYP figure specifically. Year group: a Year 5 Personal Project supervision block is priced closer to DP coursework support than to Year 7 maths. Subject group: Design and Arts have a thinner tutor pool than Mathematics, and thin pools raise prices. And format: the in-home premium in Al Manara is not a quality premium, it is a traffic premium, paid for the forty minutes a tutor spends on Al Wasl Road rather than on your child.

IB Gram publishes no price list on this page. Rates vary by subject group, year and the specialist matched, and the honest route is the free trial lesson and a quoted figure for your actual case. What you can check for yourself is the market: the ranges above are all published by named providers and are worth twenty minutes of your own verification before you commit to anything.

sections.heading: Online versus an in-home visit for a villa off Al Wasl Road
paragraphs: The comparison is worth making properly rather than dismissing. In-home tutoring has real advantages: a younger child concentrates better with an adult in the room, a parent can hear what is happening, and no device has to work. Those are not small things for a Year 7 in MYP Year 2. Any page that pretends otherwise is selling rather than advising.

What the in-home option costs in Al Manara specifically is tutor choice. A tutor willing to drive here for a 16:30 slot has to leave their previous commitment by about 15:45 and will not be free again until 18:30, so they can realistically do two visits an afternoon. That economics forces two outcomes: a higher hourly rate, and a shortlist limited to whoever lives on the right side of the city. If the subject is MYP Mathematics, the shortlist is workable. If it is MYP Design Criterion B or Language Acquisition Phase 5 French, it frequently is not.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so for us the choice is not on the table. What the comparison is for is honesty about the trade: you give up the adult in the room, and you gain the specialist and the schedule. For a Year 9 or Year 10 student the trade is usually worth taking. For a Year 7 who will not sit still, the answer is to put the lesson at the kitchen table with a parent nearby and the camera on, which recovers most of what the in-home format offered.

sections.heading: From MYP Year 5 into DP1: the gap nobody warns you about
paragraphs: Al Manara children leave MYP Year 5 by two different doors. Some stay in a continuum school and move straight into DP1. Others move to a British-curriculum school and sit IGCSE first. The students who struggle most in DP1 are, counter-intuitively, often the ones who came straight through the MYP, because the assessment language changes completely and nobody tells them.

In the MYP, a student is marked against a descriptor that rewards process: investigating, communicating, reflecting. In the DP, a student is marked against a mark scheme that rewards a specific answer to a specific command term. A Mathematics student who was a 7 on Criterion B can lose marks in DP1 for presenting an investigation where the paper wanted a worked solution. A Sciences student fluent in Criterion D reflection finds that DP Paper 1 is multiple choice and rewards none of it.

The content gaps are narrower than the assessment gap but still real. Mathematics: algebraic fluency, function notation and the beginnings of calculus are where MYP Extended students are thinnest against DP expectations. Sciences: quantitative treatment, unit manipulation and significant figures. Language and Literature: the shift from criterion-led analysis to the DP's own assessment components. Individuals and Societies: source evaluation written to a different standard.

A sensible Year 11 tutoring plan in this neighbourhood spends the first half of the year finishing the MYP properly, including the Personal Project, and the second half on the specific skills DP1 assumes. Starting DP content in February is usually a mistake; starting DP habits in February is not.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA set these requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For an Al Manara family that means your child's MYP timetable carries these subjects as well as eight MYP subject groups, and the grades count on the school report.

The rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students; and for non-Arabs, Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is a real constraint on how any tutoring in these subjects can be described. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Practically: if your child is non-Arab and sliding in Arabic as an additional language, that is a Language Acquisition problem and a mandatory-subject problem at once, and tutoring should work from the school's own material rather than imported content. Ask the school which stream your child is in and what the weekly minutes are before booking anything.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with a Personal Project
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP Year 5 is the first piece of work your child owns completely, and it is the first place a tutoring relationship can go badly wrong. The IB's academic honesty rules make the product, the process journal and the report the student's own work. A tutor who drafts any of it exposes the student to a malpractice finding, and no grade is worth that.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. They may explain what the assessment criteria ask for and read the descriptors with the student. They may question a goal that is too broad to document or too narrow to sustain. They may teach the research skills, the referencing conventions and the structure of a reflective entry. They may look at a finished section the student wrote and say which criterion strand it does not yet satisfy, and why. They may hold the student to a weekly schedule when nothing else does.

What a tutor may not do is write, rewrite to completion, supply a goal, supply the content, or edit the student's sentences into their own. The practical test we use is simple: could the student explain, unprompted, why every sentence in their report is there? If not, the tutor has gone too far. We tell families this at the trial lesson because it is better to disagree before money changes hands than after a submission.

The same boundary applies to MYP eAssessment work in schools that offer it, to Design cycle documentation, and to Sciences investigation writeups. Teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own work is the entire service, and it is also, against the essay mills competing for these searches, the genuine difference.

process.title: Tell us the real arrival time
process.description: Not the school's published finish time - the time your child actually walks into the villa, and which days are already taken by sport or Arabic support. The slot is built from that, because a slot built from the timetable gets missed.

process.title: Send one marked task
process.description: A returned MYP task with the criterion marks on it is worth more than a description of the problem. It tells us which criterion is capping the grade and which subject-group specialist to match, before anyone has spent an hour guessing.

process.title: Trial lesson, no charge
process.description: One lesson over live video with the matched tutor. Ask them to mark your child's returned task against the band descriptor out loud. If they cannot do that fluently, they are not an MYP tutor and you should say so and stop.

process.title: Fix the slot for the term
process.description: Same tutor, same time each week, held for the term so it survives half-term and exam weeks. Changes happen by agreement rather than by cancellation, and two siblings can be booked into consecutive slots on one evening.

process.title: Review against the next report
process.description: The test is whether the capped criterion moved, not whether the lessons felt productive. If a criterion has not moved in six weeks, the plan changes or the tutor does, and we say so first.

whyPoints.title: The slot is built around the bus
whyPoints.description: Session times of 16:30, 17:30 and 19:00 exist because of what Al Wasl Road and Umm Suqeim Road do between 15:00 and 16:00. No travel block sits on either side of your lesson, so a booked time is the time the lesson starts.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject group, not radius
whyPoints.description: The MYP runs eight subject groups with four criteria each. Matching on who can mark Design Criterion B or Sciences Criterion C is a different search from matching on who lives near Al Manara, and it produces a different tutor.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level feedback in writing
whyPoints.description: After each lesson you get a short note naming the criterion worked on, the band it currently sits in and what the next band descriptor asks for. That is checkable against your child's next report rather than a general impression.

whyPoints.title: We say what we do not do
whyPoints.description: No tutor arrives at a UAE address; home visits are an India-only service. No coursework is drafted for a student. No grade is promised. Those three limits are stated before payment rather than discovered after it.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, ours quoted
whyPoints.description: The AED ranges on this page are other providers' published figures with the provider named, so you can check them. Our own number is quoted for your subject group, year and format after the free trial rather than guessed at here.

whyPoints.title: Two siblings, two specialists, one evening
whyPoints.description: Without travel, consecutive slots cost nothing extra to arrange. A Year 7 at 16:30 and a Year 11 at 17:30 can have different tutors on the same evening, which is rarely practical with in-home visits in this part of Dubai.

faqs.question: Can an IB MYP tutor in Al Manara start a lesson before 16:30?
faqs.answer: For secondary year groups, rarely. Children in Al Manara attend schools in Al Safa, Al Wasl, Jumeirah, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, and buses arrive back between roughly 15:20 and 16:40 depending on route and stop order. A 16:00 slot is realistic for primary year groups finishing between 13:30 and 14:30, and for a few Jumeirah 1 routes. For everyone else, booking 16:30 or 17:30 and keeping it beats booking 15:30 and missing it. Tell us the actual arrival time, not the published finish time, and we will build the slot from that.

faqs.question: Do you send an MYP tutor to our villa in Al Manara?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service we run only in India. MYP tutoring for Al Manara is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. That is a deliberate model rather than a limitation: it removes the forty minutes of Al Wasl Road traffic from both ends of the lesson, and it means your child is matched with a specialist in the right MYP subject group rather than with whoever happens to live within a short drive of Al Manara.

faqs.question: What do the A to D letters on my child's MYP report mean?
faqs.answer: They are the four assessment criteria for that subject group, each marked out of 8. In Mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The four marks total 32 raw marks, which convert to a 1-7 grade using boundaries the IB publishes per subject. Read the four separately: an uneven profile and a flat one are different problems needing different tutoring.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Manara children usually attend?
faqs.answer: No school sits inside Al Manara itself, so every child commutes. The common clusters are the inland and mid-Jumeirah group, including Jumeirah College, Safa British School, Horizon English School, Jumeira Baccalaureate School and Emirates International School Jumeirah, and the longer Al Sufouh and Al Barsha run, including Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School, Kings' School Al Barsha, Raffles World Academy and Dubai British School Jumeirah Park. We name these as context for scheduling; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: How much does MYP tutoring cost in Dubai each month?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts weekly one-hour tutoring at AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' published figures, quoted so you can check them. IB Gram quotes its own number after a free trial lesson, because it depends on subject group, year and format.

faqs.question: Is MYP Mathematics Criterion B really where most marks are lost?
faqs.answer: In MYP Years 3 and 4 it usually is. Criterion B asks a student to select a technique, apply it, describe a general rule from the pattern they found, and then justify or prove that rule. Most students stop at describing the rule, which caps them in the middle bands however strong their arithmetic is. The fix is specific and teachable: read the top band descriptor, find the missing justification in their own returned task, and write it with them. Six to eight weeks of weekly work usually moves the band.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP Personal Project without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may explain what each criterion asks, question a goal that is too broad to document, teach research and referencing, hold the student to a weekly schedule, and read a section the student wrote and say which strand it does not yet satisfy. A tutor may not write, rewrite, supply the goal or edit sentences into their own voice. The test we use: could your child explain unprompted why every sentence is there? If not, the tutor has gone too far.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Year 5 and the Personal Project has not started. What now?
faqs.answer: Book a finite block rather than open-ended weekly lessons. The problem at this stage is almost never understanding; it is planning, documentation and holding a deadline over months. A short dated series of lessons built backwards from the school's own internal deadlines, with the process journal reviewed each week, is what recovers the planning and reflecting marks. Ask the school for the exact submission dates first, because those dates set the plan, and expect the first two lessons to be about scope rather than content.

faqs.question: Does my child have to take Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the MYP?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required these arrangements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Ask your school which stream your child sits in and what the weekly minutes are before arranging any support.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor in Al Manara more expensive than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because of the drive, not the teaching. A tutor coming to a villa off Al Wasl Road for a 16:30 lesson leaves their previous commitment around 15:45 and is not free again until after 18:30, so they can fit two visits into an afternoon. Market figures reflect that: in-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180-500 an hour including travel, against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor online. The premium buys an adult in the room, which is worth something for a young child, and it buys nothing else.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same villa have lessons on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Easily, and this is one practical advantage of video delivery. Consecutive slots cost nothing extra to arrange because no travel sits between them, so a Year 7 can take 16:30 and a Year 11 can take 17:30 with two different tutors matched to two different subject groups. Arranging the equivalent as two in-home visits in this part of Dubai is usually impractical, because each visit has to carry its own drive. We hold both slots for the term and send separate written notes.

faqs.question: What happens when the MYP ends and DP1 begins?
faqs.answer: The content gap is narrower than the assessment gap. In the MYP your child was marked against descriptors rewarding investigation, communication and reflection; in the DP they are marked against mark schemes rewarding a precise answer to a precise command term. Students who come straight through the MYP are often caught out by that, not by the topics. A sensible Year 11 plan finishes the MYP properly first, including the Personal Project, then spends the second half of the year on algebraic fluency, quantitative work and command-term discipline.

faqs.question: How do I know the tutor actually understands the MYP and not just the subject?
faqs.answer: Test it in the trial lesson, which costs nothing. Send a returned task with the criterion marks on it and ask the tutor to read the relevant band descriptor aloud and explain which sentence in your child's work caps the band. A strong MYP tutor does that fluently and specifically. A subject tutor without MYP experience will talk about content and avoid the descriptor. That one request separates the two faster than any CV, and you are entitled to stop there if the answer is vague.

faqs.question: Is an MYP tutor working in Al Manara required to hold a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service; ask any tutor directly.

faqs.question: What if the lessons are not working after a month?
faqs.answer: Say so, and expect us to say so first. The test is whether the capped criterion moved on the next piece of returned work, not whether the lessons felt useful. If a criterion has not shifted in six weeks, either the plan is wrong or the match is, and both are changeable. We would rather rematch a student in week six than keep a comfortable arrangement running for a term. No grade is promised on this page because nobody honestly can promise one, and a criterion that moves is the measurable thing instead.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-manara.closingHeading: Start with the arrival time, not the timetable
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-manara.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB MYP tutor in Al Manara, the first question is not which tutor; it is what time your child actually gets home. Tell us that, tell us which bus route and which days are already committed, and send one returned MYP task with the criterion marks on it. We will match a specialist in the right subject group, hold a 16:30, 17:30 or 19:00 slot for the term, and run the first lesson over live video at no charge so you can test whether the tutor can read a band descriptor properly. If they cannot, say so and we will rematch. No tutor comes to a UAE address, and no grade is promised.

intro.heading: The comparison that matters is not between neighbourhoods
paragraphs: A family in Al Mankhool searching for MYP help will instinctively compare their district with the ones around it. Karama is across the road, Bur Dubai runs into Al Mankhool without a boundary, Oud Metha's school belt is a short drive, and Al Jaddaf sits just beyond. The question is whether more choice exists a few minutes away, and for this programme the honest answer is that the comparison has almost no content.

MYP provision in old Dubai is concentrated rather than distributed. The continuum schools that run the Middle Years Programme are a small set, the nearest to these districts being over in Al Jaddaf, with others across the creek and out toward Nad Al Sheba. Most schools in Al Mankhool, Karama and Bur Dubai run Cambridge or Pearson qualifications to sixteen instead. So MYP students from this belt attend a handful of campuses, draw on a shared tutor pool, and face identical published rates whichever street they live on.

The comparisons that genuinely change an outcome are ones nobody frames as comparisons at all. Whether MYP or IGCSE is the right route to sixteen for this particular student, which is a real decision with a deadline in this district precisely because both are available nearby. What a criterion grade of 5 actually means set against the percentage a parent is used to reading. Which of the four criteria in a subject group will move fastest with help, since they are not equally responsive. And whether MYP Mathematics should be taken on the Standard or the Extended route, which casts a shadow two years long into the Diploma.

MYP is also the programme most often misunderstood by parents who did not sit it. There are no terminal examination papers in most schools. A grade is not an average of test scores; it is a judgement against published criteria, each marked on a 1 to 8 scale, with the criteria assessing different things - knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, communicating, reflecting, and their equivalents across the subject groups. A student can work hard, improve genuinely, and see no change in the reported grade because the criterion that was weak is still weak.

There is a transition point in this district that produces a disproportionate share of MYP difficulty, and it is not academic. Families moving a child into a continuum school at eleven or twelve from a national or British primary curriculum expect the adjustment to be about content. It is almost always about how work is judged: the student produces something that would have scored well against a mark scheme and it lands in a middling band, because the descriptor wanted a justified decision or an evaluated outcome rather than a correct answer.

So the rest of this page runs the comparisons that are real and is brief about the one that is not. Where the districts differ and where they do not. MYP against IGCSE. Criterion marks against percentages. The four criteria compared for responsiveness. The Mathematics route decision. What the Personal Project is and what transfers from it into the Diploma. And what the published rates in this market are, since those, like the tutor pool, do not vary by postcode.

Assessment is largely by examination against mark schemes, which is a fundamentally different experience from criterion-based judgement.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-mankhool.subjectsIntro: MYP students carry eight subject groups at once, and each is assessed against four criteria rather than by a single mark. Below are the groups, with what the assessment actually rewards in each.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing how texts produce effects, and producing texts for purpose and audience. Students who summarise fluently are rewarded less than students who explain technique, and the shift from one to the other is the main teachable move in this group.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Organised by phase rather than by year group, so two students in the same class can be assessed against different expectations. Marks go on comprehension precision and on producing the right text type, not on conversational fluency.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigation and the use of evidence rather than recall. Students lose marks by narrating what happened where the criterion wanted an evaluation of significance or of competing interpretations, which is a structural habit.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: The inquiring and designing and the processing and evaluating criteria are the direct ancestors of the Diploma's scientific investigation. Learning to control variables and evaluate a method properly here is far cheaper than learning it in Year 12.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Split into Standard and Extended routes in the later years, with Extended carrying the algebraic depth that Diploma Analysis and Approaches Higher Level assumes. The criterion on applying mathematics in real-life contexts is the one students most often neglect.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Assessed on documented process and critical reflection as much as on finished work. Students who produce strong pieces and document them thinly lose marks they had already earned, which is a recording habit rather than an artistic weakness.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Carries written criteria alongside performance, including planning for performance and reflecting on it. Students surprised by a middling grade here are usually strong performers who have not engaged with the written components.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A full design cycle - inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating - with the evaluation criterion the most commonly underwritten. The cycle discipline transfers directly into later independent project work.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An extended independent piece with a school-set deadline, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. The product matters less than the documented process, which is the single fact most students and parents get the wrong way round.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed work drawing on more than one subject group, judged on how disciplines are combined rather than on either in isolation. Students treat them as double homework; the criterion rewards synthesis, which has to be taught explicitly.

sections.heading: MYP against IGCSE, for a student in this district
paragraphs: This is the live comparison in Al Mankhool, because both routes are genuinely available nearby - IGCSE at most of the local schools, MYP at the continuum schools a short journey away. The two prepare a sixteen-year-old for completely different things and suit different students, and the decision is frequently made on convenience when it should be made on fit.

IGCSE assesses by terminal written papers against mark schemes. It rewards examination stamina, recall under time, and the ability to produce what a mark scheme wants. It produces a certificate naming specific qualifications, which receiving schools and universities state requirements in. It also gives a student two years of practice at exactly the skill the Diploma's written papers and A Level both demand.

MYP assesses against criteria, mostly without terminal papers, across eight subject groups simultaneously. It rewards process, design, investigation and reflection, and it produces a student unusually well prepared for the Diploma's internally assessed components, Extended Essay and Personal Project-style independent work. What it does not build is examination stamina, and that gap appears in the first term of Diploma year one or, more sharply, for a student who moves to A Level.

Neither is better. The question is which gap is easier for this particular student to close later, and which strengths matter for the route they are heading toward. The table sets the two side by side on the dimensions that matter at sixteen. Check with the receiving school what it requires, by named qualification, before the decision is finalised.

sections.heading: A criterion grade is not a percentage
paragraphs: The most common source of confusion in an MYP household is the report card, and it is a confusion about arithmetic rather than about effort. Parents accustomed to percentages read a criterion mark of 5 out of 8 and translate it to roughly sixty-two per cent, which is not what it means. Criterion marks are band judgements against descriptors: a 5 describes a particular quality of work, not a proportion of available marks achieved.

The practical consequence is that improvement does not appear where families look for it. A student can produce noticeably better work and remain in the same band, because the band above requires something specific that is still absent - usually a kind of reasoning rather than more of the same. Conversely a small, targeted change can move a band immediately if it supplies exactly what the descriptor asked for. Neither pattern makes sense if the mark is being read as a percentage.

What this means for buying help is straightforward and worth stating. Ask the school for the criterion-level feedback rather than the overall grade, read the descriptor for the band the student is in and the one above it, and identify the specific difference between them. That difference is the target. Schools publish this information and most families never request it, which is why so much MYP tuition is bought as general subject support and produces no reported change.

The table sets out how to read criterion reporting against the percentage instinct. The descriptors themselves are published by the IB and held by your child's school; take the authoritative wording from there.

sections.heading: The four criteria compared: which moves fastest
paragraphs: Across every subject group, MYP assessment uses four criteria, and they are not equally responsive to help. That matters enormously when a family has limited hours, because aiming at the wrong criterion produces a student who is better at something that was never the problem.

The knowing and understanding criterion, or its equivalent, is the content criterion. It responds to teaching and it responds slowly, because it reflects genuine subject knowledge accumulated over time. A student weak here needs sustained work, not a short block. This is the criterion families assume is the problem, and it frequently is not.

The communicating criterion, and the design or inquiry criteria, respond much faster. They assess whether work is structured, presented and justified in the way the descriptor asks for, and a student who already knows the subject can often move a band in a few sessions once somebody has shown them the specific difference between the bands. The reflecting criterion is the fastest of all and the most neglected: students describe what they did where the descriptor wanted evaluation of what it showed and what they would change, and that is a single teachable move.

There is a sequencing point worth adding. Working on a fast criterion first is not a trick to produce a quick number; it is a way of giving a discouraged student visible evidence that the system responds to effort aimed correctly. A student who has worked hard for a term with no reported change tends to conclude that the grade is fixed, and that conclusion does more damage than the original weakness. One band moved deliberately usually restores enough confidence to make the slower content work bearable.

sections.heading: Standard or Extended Mathematics: a decision with a two-year shadow
paragraphs: In the later MYP years, Mathematics splits into Standard and Extended routes, and this is the one MYP decision that reaches two years forward. The Extended route carries additional algebraic depth, and that depth is what Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes. A student who takes the Standard route and later wants Analysis and Approaches Higher Level has a gap, and the gap is not small.

The awkward part is the timing. The route is usually settled in Year 9 or Year 10, long before a student has any view about Diploma subject choices or a degree direction, and often on the basis of current comfort rather than future requirement. A student who is working steadily but not confidently in Year 9 may be placed on Standard, and in Year 11 discover that the Higher Level mathematics their intended route names is now difficult to reach.

The useful response is not to push every student onto Extended. It is to establish, by Year 10, whether any plausible post-sixteen route the student is considering names mathematics, and if so to ask the school what the Extended route requires and whether a move is still possible. That conversation is free, and the alternative - closing the gap in the summer before Year 12, or in the first term of Diploma year one - is not.

Where the Standard route is right and Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is not the plan, nothing is lost. Applications and Interpretation at either level, and Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, are reachable from a Standard MYP route with ordinary preparation. sections.heading: The Personal Project, and what transfers into the Diploma
paragraphs: The Personal Project in the final MYP year is the component families most often misread, and the misreading is consistent: they think it is about the product. A student builds something, organises something or produces something, and the household judges the project by how impressive the result is. The assessment does not work that way. The criteria reward planning, the application of skills, and reflection - the documented process rather than the artefact at the end of it.

That is why ambitious projects with thin process journals score less well than modest projects with rigorous ones. A student who set clear success criteria at the start, recorded decisions and setbacks as they happened, and evaluated honestly at the end against the criteria they set has produced exactly what the descriptors ask for. A student who produced something remarkable and wrote the journal retrospectively in a weekend has not, and the difference is visible to an experienced marker.

The transfer into the Diploma is the strongest argument for taking this seriously. The habits the Personal Project builds - defining a researchable goal, planning a process, documenting decisions, reflecting critically - are precisely what the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and every subject's internal assessment demand two years later. An MYP student who did the Personal Project properly arrives in Year 12 ahead of their IGCSE peers on the independent components, which is where a large share of Diploma difficulty sits.

The boundary for a tutor is the same as it is anywhere in the IB. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, test whether a goal is achievable with the time and resources available, show what a process journal has to contain, read the student's own writing and question reasoning that does not hold. A tutor may not produce the project, write the journal, or draft any part of the report. IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work, and we supply no IB documents, descriptors or exemplars - those are published and owned by the IB and your child's school holds the current versions.

sections.heading: Eight subject groups and one week
paragraphs: An MYP student carries eight subject groups at once, which creates an allocation problem that looks like the one a triple-science IGCSE student faces and is actually harder. There is no single examination to work backwards from, no syllabus to finish, and no obvious signal about which group needs attention. The school reports criterion marks across all eight, and a family looking at that report sees a wall of numbers rather than a priority.

The way through is to read by criterion rather than by subject. Look across all eight groups for the same criterion type: if reflecting is weak in Sciences, Design and Arts simultaneously, the student has a reflection problem rather than three subject problems, and one block of work on evaluation language improves three reported grades. That pattern is extremely common and almost never spotted, because reports are read down the subject column rather than across the criterion row.

Where the pattern is genuinely subject-specific - weak knowing and understanding in Mathematics while everything else is fine - then a subject-group hour is the right purchase, and it will need to run for a term because content criteria respond slowly. The two cases look identical on a report card and need completely different spending, which is why the first conversation should be about the criterion pattern rather than about a subject.

One further note on timing in this district. MYP students from Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai are travelling to a continuum school, so their afternoons are shorter than their IGCSE neighbours'. Combined with eight subject groups producing assessed tasks on their own schedules, the realistic weekly figure for additional support is one hour, occasionally two. A plan that assumes more will fail, and a plan built honestly around one well-aimed hour frequently succeeds.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market, because for one of the two MYP cases it is a reasonable purchase. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, read in October 2026. For a student whose weak criterion is content knowledge in a subject with an ordinary curriculum base, competent general tuition at that level can do real work. What it cannot do is read a criterion descriptor and aim at the band above it, because that requires familiarity with MYP assessment that the examination-oriented end of this market does not have.

Above that, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts qualified online tuition at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Specialist IB provision sits at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home one-to-one including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500. Every one of those figures belongs to the provider named and none is an IB Gram price.

The decision is not which band is best but which the specific job needs. A single-criterion block aimed at reflecting or communicating is short - three or four sessions - and needs somebody who knows the descriptors, so the specialist band is the right place to buy a small quantity. A term of content support in Mathematics needs competence and consistency more than it needs descriptor expertise, and buying it at the specialist rate is overspend. Monthly, one Dubai provider publishes AED 799 for eight online sessions, near AED 100 an hour; in-home monthly packages are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

For context on the wider spend, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, and MYP sessions for Al Mankhool students run one-to-one over live video.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and the subjects that sit alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Two checks any parent can make. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because it is free, no part of a quoted rate is a permit fee, and operating without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Second, the school's inspection report. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes reports on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Across the country, ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates there, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

A tutoring business with premises in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, no regulator accreditation and no UAE office, and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

Finally, the subjects that run alongside the eight MYP groups and are not optional. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year or April 2026 where the year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. For those subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which limits what any tutor can legitimately offer in them.

process.title: Ask for criterion feedback, not the grade
process.description: Request the criterion-level reporting from the school and the descriptor for the band above the one your child is in. That difference is the target, the school already holds it, and almost no family asks for it - which is why so much MYP tuition aims at nothing specific.

process.title: Read the report across, not down
process.description: Look for the same criterion type being weak across several subject groups. Reflecting weak in Sciences, Design and Arts at once is a reflection problem, not three subject problems, and one block of work improves three reported grades.

process.title: Free trial lesson on the student's own work
process.description: A full session at no charge, built around a piece the school has already assessed and commented on. For criterion-based assessment the diagnosis lives in the marked task and the descriptor, not in a conversation about how things are going.

process.title: Pick the narrowest block that fits
process.description: A single-criterion block of three or four sessions where the weakness is communicating, reflecting or design. A term-long subject-group hour only where the content criterion is genuinely weak, since content responds slowly and cannot be shortcut.

process.title: Check the Mathematics route by Year 10
process.description: If any post-sixteen route under consideration names mathematics, establish what the Extended route requires and whether a move is still possible. The conversation is free; closing the gap later in a summer or a Year 12 term is not.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the neighbourhood question
whyPoints.description: MYP provision near these districts sits in a few continuum schools, the tutor pool is shared and the published rates do not vary by street. We say so rather than implying a local advantage, and point the decision at criteria, routes and comparisons instead.

whyPoints.title: Criterion marks read correctly
whyPoints.description: A 5 out of 8 is a band judgement, not a percentage, and improvement inside a band shows as no change on a report card. We work from the descriptor for the band above, which is the only thing that explains why a hard-working student's grade has not moved.

whyPoints.title: The fast criteria targeted first
whyPoints.description: Reflecting and communicating respond in a few sessions; knowing and understanding responds over terms. Where a family has one hour a week, aiming at the responsive criterion produces a visible change and aiming at the slow one often does not.

whyPoints.title: The route decisions flagged early
whyPoints.description: MYP against IGCSE at sixteen, and Standard against Extended Mathematics in Year 9 or 10, both have consequences two years out and deadlines set by the school. We raise them rather than treating the current term as the whole problem.

whyPoints.title: Personal Project help that stays legitimate
