faqs.question: Why does MYP tutoring started after a report rarely seem to help?
faqs.answer: Because of the lag. A task submitted in week four is marked in week six, reported in week eight, read in week nine and acted on in week eleven. By then the unit is finished and the criterion that produced the low mark will not be assessed again for a month. Criterion-based assessment gives repeated chances at the same criterion, but only if the support arrives before the next assessed task. Working from the school's unit calendar rather than the reporting calendar changes what the same number of sessions achieves.

faqs.question: What documents should I get from my child's Dubai MYP school before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Three. The strand-level criterion marks from the reporting portal, which show which of the four criteria is dragging a grade rather than just the grade. The unit overview or assessment calendar per subject group, which shows which criteria the upcoming tasks assess and when. And the date of the next assessed task in the weakest subject. Schools publish or will supply all three. Together they turn a general conversation about progress into a plan with a named target and an end date.

faqs.question: How long before an assessed task should support start?
faqs.answer: Two to three weeks for a technique criterion, longer for anything involving content. If the next Sciences task assesses inquiring and designing, the work on designing a controlled investigation has to happen before the student writes the method, not after it comes back marked. For Design, where the folder is assessed across the whole unit, the useful start is the beginning of the unit. Working from the published unit calendar makes those dates visible at the start of a term instead of in hindsight.

faqs.question: What can an eight-week block realistically change in MYP?
faqs.answer: A criterion that fails on a documented behaviour can move within one unit: naming controlled variables, structuring a reproducible method, quoting precisely instead of at length, writing a reflection that analyses rather than apologises. Those are behaviours a student can adopt in the next task. What eight weeks will not do is close two years of missing content, because content has to be taught and then used across several units. Knowing which case applies before buying is the difference between a measurable outcome and a disappointed review.

faqs.question: Which term of the Dubai school year is best for starting MYP support?
faqs.answer: Term one, and almost nobody does. A student who begins the year having never read a criterion descriptor produces two terms of mid-band work before the first report prompts anyone to act. An hour in week two spent reading the four descriptors for the two weakest subjects changes a year's trajectory. Term two carries the heaviest load and the mid-year reports. Term three is assessment-dense and mostly too late for anything except damage limitation on tasks already in flight.

faqs.question: Why does the Personal Project always slip?
faqs.answer: Because it is the only substantial MYP work with no weekly lesson attached. Nothing pushes it between checkpoints, the checkpoints are months apart, and a student juggling eight subject groups deprioritises whatever nobody is chasing. The result is a product built in a fortnight and a journal reconstructed from memory, which caps the grade however good the product is. The fix is to map the school's checkpoints at the start of MYP 5 and put a review before Ramadan, because that is where the stall usually happens.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect an MYP student's tutoring schedule in Deira?
faqs.answer: The school day compresses and the household evening moves, so sessions in this district commonly shift to after Iftar or to weekend mornings for the month. Online delivery makes that a calendar change rather than a renegotiation with a driver. What should be decided in advance is which work pauses: a weekly criterion block can continue in shorter form, while the Personal Project almost always stalls unless a checkpoint has been deliberately placed before the month starts rather than during it.

faqs.question: Is the summer break worth using for MYP catch-up?
faqs.answer: The final two or three weeks of it, yes. A long break is enough for mathematical fluency and second-language ability to slip measurably, and it is the only stretch of the year with genuinely free time. A short block aimed at the content the next MYP year assumes is the least disruptive support available and among the most commonly skipped. Using the whole summer is usually counterproductive; students return tired to a year that gets harder rather than easier.

faqs.question: Does a 5 on an MYP report mean my child is average?
faqs.answer: It means less than it appears. The grade is a conversion of four criterion marks out of eight each, and the four are rarely equal. A 5 built from three sevens and a three is a narrow, fixable problem. A 5 built from four mid-band marks is a broad one needing a longer plan. The report does not distinguish them; the reporting portal usually does. Ask for the strand-level breakdown before drawing any conclusion about what kind of help is needed.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for a term of MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: Budget by block rather than by hour. Eight one-hour sessions at published Dubai rates runs roughly AED 264 to 520 at the budget end, where Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400 for a qualified online tutor, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; and roughly AED 1,600 to 3,600 or more at specialist rates, where Bestimate's band is AED 200 to 450 and above. For MYP, criterion fluency matters more than the band, so ask about MYP experience directly.

faqs.question: When should a MYP 5 student start preparing for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: In the final term of MYP 5, after the Personal Project is submitted and before the summer. MYP does not build timed written examination technique, because almost nothing in it is a timed written examination, and the Diploma is built on them. Six to eight sessions of timed writing under examination conditions, marked honestly, removes most of the first-term difficulty. Done in September of Year 12 instead, the same work competes with a new school, a new programme and a heavier workload.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our building in Al Muteena for MYP sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. For a calendar-led plan that is the point rather than a compromise: a session can be added at a day's notice when three tasks land in one week, skipped in a quiet week, or moved to a weekend morning, none of which works when a journey has to be arranged.

faqs.question: How many MYP subjects should a block cover at once?
faqs.answer: One, usually, with a second added only if the same criterion is weak in both. Eight subject groups means a family can always find three that look worrying, and spreading eight sessions across three subjects produces no measurable movement in any of them. If the criterion breakdown shows reflection weak across several subjects, that is one target expressed in several places, and a block aimed at reflection can legitimately use tasks from two or three subjects as its material.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory UAE subjects really reduce available study time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and plans copied from elsewhere ignore it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year and instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Schools must also run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of these subjects. A Dubai MYP student therefore carries more than the eight subject groups the programme outline implies.

faqs.question: What should happen at the end of an eight-week block?
faqs.answer: A comparison between the criterion mark that triggered the block and the mark on the task that followed it. If it moved, renew with a new named target. If it did not, change the diagnosis rather than adding hours to the same plan, because repeating an intervention that produced nothing is the commonest way tutoring becomes an open-ended expense. The block ending by default, rather than continuing by default, is what makes that review happen at all.

faqs.question: What if no MYP tutor is available in the week our task is due?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than offering a session that lands after the deadline, which helps nobody. Assessment weeks cluster across whole schools, so demand peaks in the same fortnights across the city and a specific subject group at a specific hour does occasionally come up empty. The honest options are an earlier slot in the same week, a different tutor with a handover, or targeting the following task instead. Booking from the published unit calendar rather than reactively avoids most of this.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-muteena.closingHeading: Get the calendar before you get the tutor
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-muteena.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB MYP tutor in Al Muteena, spend an evening on the school portal first. Pull the strand-level criterion marks for the two subjects that worry you, find the unit overview showing which criteria the next tasks assess, and note the date of the next assessed task. With those three things a block can be planned to land before the task rather than after the report, with one named criterion as its target and an end date that forces an honest review. The trial lesson works on that upcoming task with the descriptors open, and no payment is taken before it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-nahda.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors who work with Middle Years Programme students in Al Nahda, Al Qusais and Al Twar, across sciences, mathematics, language and literature, individuals and societies, and the Personal Project.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near Al Nahda who actually understands the MYP?
paragraphs: The question behind this search is not whether tutors exist. Al Nahda has a deep tutoring market, much of it excellent, most of it built around Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum teaching. What is genuinely scarce is a tutor who has read an MYP criterion descriptor and can tell you what the difference between a 5 and a 7 on criterion C looks like in a real piece of student work. That is the thing your child's school is actually marking, and it is invisible to a tutor working from content alone.

The Middle Years Programme does not assess the way the systems around it assess. There is no percentage. Each subject is marked against four criteria, each on a scale from 0 to 8, giving a maximum criterion total of 32 that the school converts into a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. The criteria differ by subject group: in the sciences they cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In mathematics they cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student can be strong on content and lose half their available marks on the criteria that are not content.

This produces a specific pattern in Al Nahda, where many MYP students have come from or sit alongside Indian-curriculum siblings and cousins. Students arrive at an MYP task with the instincts of a different system: produce a complete, tidy, textbook-correct answer. The MYP task frequently asks them to investigate a pattern, justify a method, evaluate the reliability of a result, or reflect on an application. The content knowledge is already there. The marks are lost in the shape of the response, which is a teachable skill and one a generalist tutor rarely names.

The second scarcity is the Personal Project. In the final MYP year every student completes an independent project assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. Supervision is the school's responsibility, and families often want extra structure around it. That structure is legitimate and valuable; producing the project is not, and we will not do it. A tutor can question a goal that is too vague to assess, teach a student how to evidence their own process, and give feedback on the student's own writing. Anything beyond that is a malpractice risk for the student rather than a shortcut.

One thing to be clear about before you read further. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. MYP tuition for an Al Nahda family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for worked problems, annotated drafts and criterion descriptors on the page beside the task. Given how few MYP-literate tutors live within driving distance of Al Nahda 2, that is precisely how the scarcity problem gets solved.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary education organised around transdisciplinary themes, with the exhibition at the end. There are no criterion marks of the MYP kind, which is why MYP 1 feels like a step change in how work is judged rather than in how much work there is.

programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Assessment returns to examination papers, with an internal assessment component in most subjects. The jump from criterion marking to timed papers is the defining difficulty of MYP 5 into DP1.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-nahda.subjectsIntro: MYP tutoring in Al Nahda is requested subject by subject, and the criteria change with the subject group. These are the ones families here ask for, with what loses marks in each.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Marks are lost in criterion B, where students write a method without identifying what is being controlled, and in criterion C, where a result is described rather than evaluated against the hypothesis it was meant to test.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where most marks go missing: students find the pattern and stop, without generalising it or justifying why the generalisation holds. Criterion D asks for mathematics applied to a real context, which rewards judgement rather than calculation.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis of language rather than summary of content. The commonest loss is retelling the text instead of explaining how a writer's choice produces an effect, which is a habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigating, with sources evaluated for reliability and purpose rather than merely cited. Students lose criterion B and C marks by listing evidence without judging it, and by writing conclusions their sources do not support.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Phase-based rather than year-based, which confuses parents reasonably. The four criteria cover listening, reading, speaking and writing, and a student can sit in different phases in different skills.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The process journal carries most of the marks, and students who build an excellent product while neglecting documented iteration score poorly for reasons they find baffling.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. As in Design, evidence of process is assessed, so a tutor's most useful contribution is often teaching a student how to document their own thinking.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Includes written planning and reflection components that surprise families who expect a practical-only subject. Criterion C and D work can be supported in exactly the same way as any other written reflection.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal as evidence. The commonest failure is a goal too vague to evaluate against, which is fixable in one session if it is caught early.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria, requiring a student to integrate two subject groups rather than answer in both. Students treat these as double homework; the marks are for the synthesis.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. In MYP it usually sits within language acquisition or language and literature depending on the student.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Communication, social, self-management, research and thinking skills. Not graded as a subject, but the reason two students with identical content knowledge receive different criterion marks on the same task.

sections.heading: What MYP actually marks, and why a subject tutor can miss it
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme assesses against criteria, and the criteria are published. Each subject has four, each is marked from 0 to 8, and the four add to a maximum of 32 which the school converts into a grade from 1 to 7. That structure carries two consequences a parent should hold onto. The first is that a quarter of the available marks in every subject sit behind a single criterion, so a student who consistently underperforms on one criterion is capped no matter how well they know the content. The second is that the criteria are not content; they are kinds of thinking.

In the sciences, criterion A covers knowing and understanding, which is the part a conventional subject tutor teaches well. Criterion B covers inquiring and designing, criterion C covers processing and evaluating, and criterion D covers reflecting on the impacts of science. Three of the four are about how a student handles an investigation and its meaning. In mathematics, criterion B asks the student to investigate patterns and criterion D asks them to apply mathematics in a real-life context. A tutor drilling exercise sets is working on criterion A and leaving three quarters of the marks untouched.

This is why the complaint we hear most often from Al Nahda parents is that tutoring made no difference to the grade. Frequently it made a genuine difference to the knowledge and none to the criterion profile, because nobody looked at the criterion profile. The first thing worth asking a school for is the breakdown: not the grade, but the four criterion marks across recent tasks. The pattern in those four numbers tells you what to buy. A student at 7, 4, 4, 6 does not need more content; they need design and evaluation taught explicitly.

The fix is less mysterious than it sounds. Criterion descriptors are written in plain, if dry, language, and students can learn to read them. A tutor who puts the descriptor beside the student's own work, asks which band this paragraph sits in, and then asks what specifically would move it up, is teaching the student to self-mark. That skill compounds for the rest of the programme, which is why we target one criterion per block rather than attempting all four.

sections.heading: How 32 criterion marks become a grade from 1 to 7
paragraphs: Parents find this the most useful single thing on the page, because it converts a set of apparently small numbers into the grade on the report. The four criterion marks are added to give a total out of 32, and the school applies published grade boundaries to turn that total into a grade from 1 to 7. The boundaries are not evenly spaced, which matters: the band widths differ, so a one-mark improvement on a single criterion is sometimes worth a whole grade and sometimes worth nothing at all.

Work an example. A student scoring 5, 4, 5, 4 has a total of 18. A student scoring 5, 5, 5, 5 has 20. Those two students look similar on every individual criterion and can land in different grade bands. That is where tutoring produces visible results fast: you are not trying to transform the student, you are trying to find the criterion where they are one band below their others and move that single number. A criterion profile makes this obvious; a grade on a report card hides it completely.

Schools report in slightly different ways and some use their own internal reporting alongside the criterion totals, so confirm the boundaries your child's school applies with their MYP coordinator. The IB publishes general grade descriptors and the conversion table; the coordinator can confirm which version is in force for your child's year group in a two-line email. Any tutor who claims to know your school's exact boundaries without asking is guessing.

One further point for Al Nahda families comparing children across systems. An MYP grade of 5 is not equivalent to 71 per cent, and it is not comparable to a CBSE percentage or an IGCSE grade in any simple way. The scales measure different things. Treating them as interchangeable is the fastest route to a family arguing about a grade that was actually fine.

sections.heading: A five-minute test for whether a tutor knows the Middle Years Programme
paragraphs: You can establish this on the phone, and you do not need to know the programme yourself to do it. Five questions, all with short specific answers, all impossible to bluff. Ask them of every tutor you consider, including ours. What you are listening for is whether the answers are precise or whether they slide into general talk about holistic education, which is the tell.

The questions are chosen because each one catches a specific kind of ignorance. Asking how many criteria a subject has and what each is marked out of catches the tutor who has never seen an MYP task. Asking what criterion B in sciences covers catches the tutor who knows the structure in outline but has never taught to it. Asking what a criterion total of 20 converts to catches the tutor who has never seen a report. Asking what the Personal Project is assessed on catches the tutor who assumes it is an extended essay. And asking what they would do about a profile of 7, 4, 4, 6 tests whether they can diagnose at all.

This test matters more in Al Nahda than it would in a district with denser IB provision. Where MYP schools are few, the local tutoring supply has had little reason to learn the programme, and a tutor can build a successful practice on Indian-curriculum and IGCSE work without ever meeting a criterion descriptor. That tutor may be excellent and still be the wrong purchase for your child. Our answer is to match on the programme rather than the postcode and to deliver over video, which is the only way the arithmetic works.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: where structure helps and where the line is
paragraphs: In the final MYP year, every student completes a Personal Project: an independent piece of work of their own choosing, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal as the evidence base. Schools supervise it, and most families find their child needs more structure than the school's supervision schedule provides, simply because the project is long and the deadlines are distant until they are not.

Legitimate support is almost entirely about questions and rhythm. The highest-value intervention comes first and takes one session: narrowing a goal until it can actually be evaluated. A student who sets out to raise awareness about plastic has nothing to assess against. A student who sets out to design, test and revise a reusable alternative to one specific single-use item in their own household has a project with criteria attached. Catching this in week two rather than month four changes the entire outcome.

The second intervention is the process journal. Students treat it as paperwork and complete it retrospectively, which destroys its value as evidence of their own thinking. Teaching a student to log a decision and the reason for it, in five minutes, on the day it happens, is a habit that carries the project. The third is feedback on the student's own drafts, which is where a tutor can point out that a reflection is describing what happened rather than judging it.

What a tutor may not do is produce any part of the project. We will not write it, draft sections of it, supply a goal and plan, or edit it to completion. That is not caution for its own sake; IB academic-honesty rules make this a malpractice question, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the tutor. We say this explicitly to students at the first project session, because a thirteen-year-old asked to explain where the line sits should be told clearly rather than left to work it out.

sections.heading: From MYP 5 into DP1: the gap nobody prepares for
paragraphs: The MYP prepares students well for inquiry, research, extended writing and independent work, and it prepares them poorly for a timed written paper, because it does not use many. The Diploma returns to examinations. A student who spent five years being marked against criteria on coursework meets Paper 1 in DP1 and discovers that the skill of writing everything they understand about a topic is now a liability, because the question asked them to state something and move on.

Three things close that gap, and none of them is content. The first is command-term discipline. Diploma questions use defined verbs with defined expectations and marks allocated accordingly. A student who explains when the paper said state wastes time and loses the next question. Drilling the verbs takes a handful of sessions and produces an immediate measurable change.

The second is quantitative volume, specifically for students heading towards a science or mathematics Higher Level. MYP mathematics builds investigation and communication well; it does not generate the sheer number of worked calculations that DP1 chemistry, physics or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches assume. A student can be genuinely strong in MYP maths and still need six weeks of volume before DP1 stops feeling impossible. Saying this in MYP 5 rather than in DP1 October is the whole value of the warning.

The third is timed practice under real conditions. Students who have never sat a ninety-minute paper do not know how fast they write, how long they spend re-reading, or what happens to their handwriting in the last ten minutes. Four timed papers in the final MYP term, marked honestly, is enough to remove the surprise. For Al Nahda families whose children are heading to Diploma provision in Al Twar or Al Garhoud, this is the single most useful block of tutoring available in the MYP 5 year.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs in this market, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Take the bottom of the market first, because for MYP it is a more reasonable starting point than it would be for a Diploma Higher Level subject. Budget and university-student online tutors in Dubai advertise from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For a student who needs content gaps filled in MYP 2 or MYP 3, supervised practice and recall drilling, that band can do real work. What it rarely buys is criterion literacy, so it is the wrong purchase if the problem is a profile of 7, 4, 4, 6.

The next band up is qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that sit IB and IGCSE specialists at about AED 200 to 450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 survey putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium named tutors are advertised as high as AED 650 by BartyED. In-home one-to-one visits, which carry travel inside the rate, are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors.

For MYP specifically, the sensible reading of those bands is that you are paying for criterion literacy rather than for subject prestige. A tutor at the mid band who has marked MYP work against descriptors is worth more to an MYP 4 student than a premium Diploma specialist who has not. That is an unusual conclusion in a market that sells seniority, and it is the honest one. On monthly comparison, advertised packages run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, while Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more at specialist exam-year level.

Every figure above is a market rate attributed to whoever published it and read in October 2026. None is an IB Gram price; we publish a free trial lesson and a consultation instead. The relevant context for an Al Nahda household is that KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. The school line is flat; the tutoring line is the one worth deciding deliberately.

sections.heading: Coverage, fallback and what an Al Nahda parent can check for nothing
paragraphs: MYP tutor supply is thinner than Diploma or IGCSE supply, and nobody in this market says so. Our position is to say it before you book. MYP sciences and mathematics are reasonably covered; MYP Design, Arts and the less common language acquisition phases are not, and a Personal Project supervisor with real MYP experience is scarcer still. Where a UAE-based tutor covers the subject, that is the match, because the term calendar and the time zone already align. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, we say so and offer a tutor from the wider pool working Gulf Standard Time at the same rate band, rather than letting you discover it in lesson one.

Alongside that, four checks cost you nothing. Ask the MYP coordinator for the criterion breakdown on recent tasks rather than the grade, and for the boundaries the school applies. Ask whether your child's school enters students for MYP eAssessment, because it changes what the final year looks like. Read the school's current inspection rating on KHDA's own site, since KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, or on the Sharjah Private Education Authority's site if your child attends school across the boundary.

The fourth check is the permit, and it applies to every tutor in the country. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific figure quoted at you. Ask the question; the answer is free and informative. And note that IB Gram holds no accreditation, approval or licence from KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and operates no UAE centre.

faqs.question: Why do so few tutors near Al Nahda know the MYP?
faqs.answer: Because the local school market gives them little reason to learn it. The provision around Al Nahda, Al Qusais and Muhaisnah is dominated by Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools, with IB continuum provision concentrated in a small number of sites. A tutor can build a full practice here on CBSE and IGCSE work without ever seeing a criterion descriptor. That tutor may teach their subject excellently and still be the wrong purchase, which is why we match on the programme and deliver one-to-one over live video rather than by driving distance.

faqs.question: How is MYP work marked if there is no percentage?
faqs.answer: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked from 0 to 8, giving a maximum criterion total of 32. The school converts that total into a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. The criteria differ by subject group: sciences cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science, while mathematics covers knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Confirm the exact boundaries your child's school applies with the MYP coordinator.

faqs.question: What criterion total does my child need for a 6 or a 7?
faqs.answer: On the published boundaries, a total of 24 to 27 out of 32 gives a grade 6 and 28 to 32 gives a 7, with 19 to 23 giving a 5 and 15 to 18 a 4. The bands are not evenly spaced, so a single mark on one criterion is sometimes worth a whole grade and sometimes worth nothing. That is why we ask for the four criterion marks rather than the report grade: the profile shows exactly which number to move. Check the boundaries in force for your child's year group with the school.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to our home in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. MYP tuition for an Al Nahda family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for worked problems, annotated drafts and the criterion descriptor open beside the task. Given how thin MYP provision is in this part of Dubai, that is how the scarcity is solved: the tutor is chosen for having marked MYP work, not for living close enough to drive.

faqs.question: My son knows the science content but his grade will not move. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because the content sits behind criterion A, which is a quarter of the available marks. The other three criteria in MYP Sciences cover inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student can be strong on knowledge and lose most of the marks in the other three, and no amount of additional content teaching will change that. Ask the school for the four criterion marks on recent tasks; the trailing number tells you what to buy.

faqs.question: What is criterion B in MYP Mathematics and why does it cost marks?
faqs.answer: Criterion B is investigating patterns, and it costs marks because students stop too early. They find the pattern, state it, and consider the question answered. The criterion asks them to generalise the pattern, express the generalisation properly, and justify why it holds. That last step is the one almost never taught in a conventional maths lesson, and it is worth up to eight of the thirty-two marks in the subject. It is teachable in three or four sessions with the descriptor open beside the student's own work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes, and the most valuable help comes first. A tutor can question a goal until it is specific enough to be evaluated, teach the student to log decisions in the process journal on the day they happen rather than retrospectively, and give feedback on the student's own drafts, including pointing out where a reflection describes rather than judges. A tutor may not supply a goal or plan, write or draft any section, or edit the project to completion. We state that boundary to the student at the first session.

faqs.question: What does the MYP Personal Project actually get marked on?
faqs.answer: On criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal providing the evidence. It is not an extended essay and it is not marked on the quality of the finished object alone, which is the misconception that causes most of the disappointment. A student can build something genuinely impressive and score poorly because the documented process is thin, and a student can produce something modest and score well because the planning and reflection are rigorous. Confirm the criteria version in force with your child's coordinator.

faqs.question: Is my child ready for DP1 after MYP 5?
faqs.answer: On content, usually yes. On three specific skills, usually not, and the MYP is not designed to build them. Command-term discipline is the first: Diploma questions use defined verbs with marks allocated against them, and a student who writes an essay when asked to state loses time and marks. Calculation volume is the second, particularly for a science or maths Higher Level. Timed-paper stamina is the third. Four timed papers marked honestly in the final MYP term removes most of the surprise, and that block is the best-value tutoring in the MYP 5 year.

faqs.question: Should we switch from MYP to IGCSE at 14?
faqs.answer: It is a real decision rather than an obvious one, and the right answer depends on the student. The surrounding school market in this part of Dubai is dominated by IGCSE provision, so the switch is logistically easy and families often make it for school-choice reasons rather than academic ones. Content overlaps substantially; assessment culture does not. A student moving from MYP 3 into Year 10 IGCSE needs calculation volume and timed-paper practice rather than new content, and planning that explicitly makes the transition far less painful.

faqs.question: How do I know whether a tutor has genuinely taught MYP?
faqs.answer: Ask five short questions. How many criteria per subject and out of what? What does criterion B cover in MYP Sciences? What grade does a criterion total of 20 give? What is the Personal Project assessed on? And what would you do with a profile of 7, 4, 4, 6? Correct answers are four criteria each out of eight totalling thirty-two, inquiring and designing, a grade 5 on the published boundaries, planning and applying skills and reflecting, and target criteria B and C because the content is fine.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost in Dubai at the cheaper end?
faqs.answer: Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, read in October 2026. For filling content gaps in the earlier MYP years and supervising practice, that band does genuine work. What it rarely buys is criterion literacy, so it is the wrong choice if the problem is a lopsided criterion profile rather than missing knowledge. These are market figures attributed to their publishers; IB Gram publishes a free trial rather than an hourly price list.

faqs.question: Is an expensive Diploma specialist worth it for an MYP student?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is the one place where paying more buys less. A premium tutor advertised at AED 650 an hour by BartyED is priced for Diploma work, and Diploma expertise does not automatically include having marked MYP tasks against descriptors. For an MYP 4 student the more useful purchase is a mid-band tutor who has genuinely taught the criteria, at roughly AED 150 to 300. The exception is the MYP 5 to DP1 bridge, where Diploma experience is exactly what the block requires.

faqs.question: Will my child sit on-screen MYP examinations in the final year?
faqs.answer: It is the optional on-screen examination and ePortfolio route in the final MYP year, leading to the IB MYP Certificate. Whether your child sits it is the school's decision, not yours, and schools in the UAE differ: some enter candidates and many do not. It matters for tutoring because it changes what the final year looks like entirely, replacing some coursework-driven assessment with timed on-screen work. Ask the MYP coordinator directly; it is a one-line answer that determines how the MYP 5 plan should be built.

faqs.question: Do MYP tutors in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Every private tutor in the UAE does, regardless of programme. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an MYP student need?
faqs.answer: One is usually right, and the reason is specific to how MYP is assessed. Criterion work is improved by producing a piece of work, having it marked against the descriptor, and then producing the next one differently. That cycle needs a week between sessions for the student to actually produce something. Two sessions a week make sense when there is a genuine content gap underneath the criterion problem, or during a Personal Project crunch. Beyond that, extra hours tend to replace the student's own work, which is exactly the wrong outcome.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-nahda.closingHeading: Ask for the criterion marks, then ask the tutor five questions
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-nahda.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB MYP tutor in Al Nahda, two steps will tell you almost everything. Ask the school's MYP coordinator for the four criterion marks on recent tasks rather than the grade, and ask any tutor you are considering the five questions set out on this page. The profile tells you what to buy; the questions tell you who can sell it. Then take the free trial lesson, which costs nothing and needs no card details, and watch the tutor put a criterion descriptor beside your child's own work. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we change the tutor at no cost if the match is wrong.

intro.heading: Reading an MYP report, and knowing what to do about it
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme reports differently from every system most Al Quoz parents grew up in. There are no percentages. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, each criterion is marked out of eight, and the four levels are combined and converted to a grade from one to seven using a published scale. A parent reading criterion C level 4 has no intuitive sense of whether that is good, and the report usually does not say.

That gap is the single most common reason a family seeks MYP tutoring in Dubai, and it is worth closing before any teaching is bought. A level four in a criterion is not a general verdict on the work. It is a statement that the response met some of what that specific criterion asked for and not the rest, and the criterion wording says precisely which part. A student who reads the wording before writing can often move a level without learning any new content.

The second reason families come is the Personal Project in MYP 5, which arrives in the same year as mock preparation at many schools and is the first genuinely independent extended piece a student has produced. It has its own criteria, a process journal and a report, and the common failure is not laziness but scope: a project nobody narrowed, begun too late to show a process.

The third reason is the step into the Diploma Programme, which Al Quoz families usually meet with no warning. MYP rewards a different thing from DP1. A student who has learnt to satisfy criteria in Year 10 arrives in DP1 facing externally marked papers with command terms and mark schemes, and the transition is real enough to cost a term if nobody names it in advance.

There is a fourth reason, less often stated, and it is a scheduling one. The MYP carries eight subject groups, interdisciplinary units and Service as Action, and in a Dubai school it carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies on top of all of that. A Year 10 or Year 11 student whose grades slip across several subjects at once is frequently out of hours rather than out of ability, and in that case the useful first response is an audit of the week rather than the purchase of a tutor. We would rather say so than take the booking.

The premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one MYP tuition into Al Quoz homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run in India only. The Al Quoz practicalities are quickly dealt with: housing sits in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3 between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, children travel outwards to school in several directions, and a weekday session realistically starts between 5pm and 5.30pm.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-quoz.programmesIntro: The MYP spans five years and changes character as it goes, so support means something different in each phase. Below, each is described by what the assessment actually asks for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The eight subject groups taught through units with statements of inquiry and global contexts, assessed against four criteria per subject. Nothing external is at stake, which is exactly why these years are the cheapest place to build habits: reading a criterion before writing, investigating a pattern and justifying a generalisation, and keeping a usable record of a process.
programmes.countryNote: Al Quoz families whose children enter an IB school at Year 7 from a British or Indian primary meet criterion reporting for the first time here. A single session explaining how to read the report, and one more on using criterion wording as a checklist, often does more than a term of subject tutoring would.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 10 to 11
programmes.description: Greater depth, more demanding criteria descriptors and, in MYP 5, the Personal Project. Some schools also enter students for on-screen eAssessment or ePortfolio components towards the MYP certificate, which varies by school and must be confirmed with the coordinator rather than assumed.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most Al Quoz MYP demand sits, and the pressure is structural: the Personal Project, the hardest subject criteria and in some schools eAssessment all land in the same year, with Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies continuing alongside. A written family calendar is worth more here than extra study hours.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent extended piece with its own criteria, a process journal and a report, developed by the student across the year with a supervisor. It rewards a narrow goal, a visible process and honest reflection, and it punishes a broad ambition begun in the final term with no record of how it developed.
programmes.countryNote: Personal Project deadlines differ sharply between schools in the Al Quoz and central corridor clusters, sometimes by a full term. That is why advice from a neighbour at another school is frequently aimed at the wrong month, and why the project calendar should come from your own coordinator.

programmes.name: The transition into the Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The move from internally assessed criteria to externally examined papers with command terms and mark schemes. The content step is manageable; the assessment step is not automatic. A student who is fluent at satisfying criteria can write a true, well-organised examination answer and score poorly because it answered the wrong command term.
programmes.countryNote: A summer block of four to six sessions between MYP 5 and DP1 on command terms, timed writing and mark-scheme reading prevents most of the first-term drop that Al Quoz families then spend a year repairing. It is the best available use of that holiday and it is rarely booked.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-quoz.subjectsIntro: The MYP has eight subject groups, each with its own four criteria. Below is what each group assesses and where Al Quoz students most often lose levels, which is usually in the criterion that is least like an examination.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5, standard and extended in MYP 4-5
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where levels go, because generalising a rule and then justifying it is a distinct skill that most students treat as an optional extra.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowledge and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Inquiring and designing is the weak point: hypotheses stated without a reason and variables mentioned without being classified.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Students lose levels on analysing, where responses summarise what a text says instead of examining how it creates meaning, and that distinction is teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed by phase rather than by year group. The common frustration is a student performing well in class and scoring mid-band because the phase descriptors expect a specific range of structures and registers.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the discriminator: using sources to build an argument rather than to decorate one, and recognising a source's limitations explicitly.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Levels are lost by students who build something competent without documenting the design cycle, because the documentation is a substantial part of what is assessed.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than students expect, and a strong final piece with a thin journal scores below a developing piece with a well-documented process.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written criteria matter as much as the practical ones, which surprises students who assumed the subject was assessed on the field.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria, requiring a student to integrate knowledge from two subject groups and reflect on the integration. The common failure is two parallel pieces of subject work presented together, with no actual integration shown.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Planning, applying skills and reflecting, supported by a process journal and a report. Scope is the decisive variable: a narrow goal with a visible process scores well, and an ambitious goal begun late cannot, however impressive the outcome looks.

sections.heading: What an MYP tutor in Al Quoz should do in the first session
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in Al Quoz means one-to-one middle-years teaching at home on a weekday evening. IB Gram delivers that as a live online session into Al Quoz homes on Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a UAE address, because in-person home visits are a service we run only in India.

The first session should not be subject teaching. It should be reading the last report and one piece of marked work side by side, and translating the criterion levels into specific statements about what the work contained and what it did not. That translation is the thing families cannot do alone, and it is frequently the entire intervention required, because once a student knows what criterion C wants they can usually supply it.

A worked example makes the point. A student submits a well-written science investigation and receives a level four in inquiring and designing. The work is fluent and the science is sound. What the criterion asked for was a hypothesis with a reason, variables classified as independent, dependent and controlled, and a method another student could follow. Two of those three were missing. Nothing about the student's understanding of science was the problem.

This is why MYP support is often shorter than parents expect. Where the deficit is criterion literacy, two to four sessions will change levels across several subjects at once, because the habit of reading the descriptor before writing transfers everywhere. Where the deficit is genuinely in content or in a specific skill such as mathematical generalisation, the work is longer, and the first session is how you find out which you have.

sections.heading: The four criteria, and what moves a level
paragraphs: Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight in bands. Across the competitor pages researched for Dubai IB queries, not one explains how a criterion band actually works, which leaves families guessing about the central mechanism of the programme their children are in.

The structure is consistent in shape across subjects even though the wording differs. The lower bands describe a response that states or lists. The middle bands describe one that explains or applies with some success. The upper bands describe one that does so consistently, with justification, and in a way that addresses the full demand of the criterion. The gap between a five and a seven is almost always justification and completeness rather than quality of expression.

That is extremely useful information for a student, because it means the route from a five to a seven is usually additive. The response needs the reason attached to the claim, the variable classified rather than mentioned, the generalisation justified rather than stated, the limitation of the source named rather than implied. These are specific, teachable additions, not vague improvements.

Confirm the current criterion wording for your child's subjects with the school, because the MYP revises subject guides and the wording is the authority. We do not reproduce IB documents, which are the organisation's copyright, so the subject teacher or coordinator remains the source.

sections.heading: The MYP five years, counted forward
paragraphs: MYP support is cheapest early and most urgent late, which is the opposite of how families usually buy it. This table sets out what changes each year and what is worth watching, so an Al Quoz family can intervene at the point where a small amount of work still does a large amount of good.

Years 7 to 9 are where habits form and nothing external is at stake. A student who learns in Year 8 to read a criterion before writing, to classify variables as a reflex and to keep a usable process record is a student who will not need rescuing in Year 11. Two or three sessions in those years are worth considerably more than the same money spent later.

Year 10 is where the criteria descriptors sharpen and standard and extended mathematics routes separate in many schools, which quietly begins the sequence that ends in a Diploma mathematics route choice. Year 11 is the crowded year: the Personal Project, the hardest subject criteria, in some schools eAssessment components, and the mandatory UAE subjects continuing throughout.

The last row is the one families underestimate. The transition into DP1 is an assessment change rather than a content change, and it costs a term when nobody prepares for it. Four to six sessions in the preceding summer on command terms, timed writing and mark-scheme reading is the single most effective MYP-adjacent purchase available, and it sits outside the school year so nothing competes with it.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, planned backwards
paragraphs: The Personal Project fails for one reason far more often than any other: scope. A student picks an ambitious goal, works on it intermittently, and arrives at the deadline with an impressive-sounding outcome and no evidence of a process. The criteria reward the process, so the outcome alone cannot rescue it.

Planning backwards from the school's deadline solves most of it. The report and the completed outcome sit at the end; before them, a process journal that shows decisions being made and changed; before that, applied skills with evidence; before that, a goal narrow enough that progress can be recorded at all. Each of those has a sensible date, and your coordinator holds the real deadline, which differs between schools in this part of Dubai by as much as a term.

The process journal is the component students treat as busywork and examiners treat as evidence. It is not a diary. It records decisions, the reasons for them, what was tried and abandoned, and what the student would do differently. A journal written retrospectively in the final fortnight is visible as such, and it caps the criteria that depend on it.

On the boundary, which matters here as much as in the Diploma: a tutor may narrow the goal, teach what each criterion rewards, ask the questions that expose a plan with no measurable progress, and comment on the student's own journal and report. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of the project. After each session your child should be able to explain and defend every change in their own words, and the school's academic honesty policy governs the rest.

sections.heading: From MYP criteria to DP mark schemes
paragraphs: This is the transition Al Quoz families meet without warning, and it is worth describing precisely because the fix is cheap and the cost of not fixing it is a term of DP1.

The MYP asks a student to satisfy a criterion. The response is theirs to shape, the descriptor is published, and the student can read it before writing. The Diploma asks a student to answer an examination question under time, where the command term dictates the response shape, the mark scheme is not in front of them, and marks are awarded for specific content points in a specific structure. Both are reasonable systems. They reward different behaviours.

The behaviour that transfers badly is comprehensiveness. In the MYP, covering the full demand of a criterion thoroughly tends to score well. In the Diploma, writing everything known about a topic in response to an explain question scores less than answering only what was asked, because unrequested material earns nothing and consumes time that other questions needed. Students who were strong MYP writers are disproportionately affected.

Four to six sessions in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 addresses it: command terms separated and practised, timed writing introduced before it is compulsory, and mark schemes read as documents rather than encountered as verdicts. The same block is the right time for the Diploma subject and level conversation, including the mathematics route, which is confirmed to a school deadline at the end of Year 11 and cannot be revisited afterwards.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: No competitor page researched for this market covers this, and it affects every MYP student in a Dubai private school. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisation rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold appropriate KHDA approval.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools able to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met and a recommendation that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Content is tightly controlled: KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited.

For MYP families the consequence is arithmetic. These subjects sit on top of eight subject groups, interdisciplinary units, Service as Action and, in MYP 5, the Personal Project. A Year 11 student who appears to be slipping across several subjects at once is frequently out of hours rather than out of ability, and the right first response is a timetable audit rather than a tutor. Where support is appropriate in these subjects, it works inside the school's own material.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs, and what it prevents
paragraphs: MYP tutoring is the cheapest tutoring in the IB continuum and the least purchased, for an understandable reason: nothing external is at stake until MYP 5, so nothing feels urgent. The argument for buying it anyway is not about MYP grades. It is about what each small intervention prevents two or three years later.

The market, attributed and dated October 2026, so you can judge any quote. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour; specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Budget online provision starts at Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

Now the prevention arithmetic, which is the honest case for early work. Two sessions on criterion literacy in Year 8 cost a fraction of a term of DP1 repair. One session on mathematical generalisation in Year 9 prevents an exploration in DP1 built on a pattern the student cannot justify. Four sessions in the summer before DP1 on command terms prevents the first-term fall that families routinely spend a year and several thousand dirhams recovering from.

For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the variable line in an education budget, and in the MYP it is the line where a small, early, deliberate spend does the most work.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Quoz, and the limits we state
paragraphs: Send three things: the last report, one piece of marked work with the criterion levels on it, and the school. That is enough for a specialist to translate the levels into specific statements about what the work contained and lacked, and the free trial lesson exists to do exactly that before any payment.

What will not be claimed. No grade promise, because nobody can make one honestly, and in a criterion-referenced system the claim is even less meaningful than usual. No suggestion that tutoring is required for progression into the Diploma, for equivalency or for university admission, because that is a false claim about processes we do not control. No regulator or board approval: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and operates no UAE office or centre. No satisfaction statistics.

A disclosed limit worth stating for the MYP specifically: some subject groups and language acquisition phases are narrower specialisms than Diploma subjects are, so a request for a particular phase at a particular hour may not be coverable immediately. When that happens you are told and given a realistic view of when it opens, rather than being offered a general tutor in place of the specialist you asked for.

One last fact for any conversation with any provider. Individuals offering private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with those operating without one subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here. And IB subject guides and criterion documents are the organisation's copyright, so we work from what your school provides rather than redistributing them.

faqs.question: What does a criterion level of four actually mean on my child's MYP report?
faqs.answer: It means the response met part of what that criterion asked for and not the rest, and the criterion wording states precisely which part. Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, with the four combined and converted to a grade from one to seven. The lower bands describe work that states or lists, the middle bands work that explains or applies with partial success, and the upper bands work that does so consistently and with justification. The gap is usually justification and completeness, not expression.

faqs.question: Does an MYP tutor come to our home in Al Quoz?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. MYP teaching is delivered one-to-one into Al Quoz homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. For a middle-years student the practical benefit is timing: a 5pm session starts when your child gets home rather than after a second car journey, and for Al Quoz families that extra half hour of attention is worth more than it sounds.

faqs.question: My child writes well but keeps getting mid-band levels. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because the response is good writing that does not address every element the criterion names. MYP criteria are checklists as much as standards: a hypothesis needs a reason attached, a variable needs classifying as independent, dependent or controlled, a mathematical pattern needs generalising and then justifying, a source needs its limitation stated. Fluent work missing those elements sits in the middle bands. Two to four sessions on reading the descriptor before writing usually moves levels across several subjects at once.

faqs.question: When should the Personal Project be started?
faqs.answer: Early in MYP 5, and the first task is narrowing the goal rather than beginning the work. The criteria reward a visible process, so a goal that cannot show recordable progress cannot score well however impressive the outcome. Then maintain the process journal continuously, because a journal written retrospectively in the final fortnight is visible as such and caps the criteria that depend on it. Your coordinator holds the real deadline, which differs between Dubai schools by as much as a term.

faqs.question: Where does the line fall on outside help with the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: It falls at writing, and the most useful permitted help is at the start. A tutor may narrow the goal until progress is recordable, teach what each criterion rewards, ask the questions that expose a plan with no measurable milestones, and comment on the student's own journal and report. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of it. The test after a session is whether your child could explain and defend every change in their own words; if not, the line has been crossed.

faqs.question: Why is there no percentage on the MYP report?
faqs.answer: Because the programme is criterion-referenced rather than norm-referenced. Work is judged against published descriptors of what a response must contain, not against a proportion of correct answers or against the rest of the class. That is genuinely more informative once you can read it, because a level tells you which requirement was unmet while a percentage tells you only how much was missed. The cost is that the report is unreadable without the criterion wording, which the school can supply.

faqs.question: Is MYP tutoring worth it when nothing external is at stake yet?
faqs.answer: The case is not about MYP grades; it is about what early work prevents. Two sessions on criterion literacy in Year 8 cost a fraction of a term of DP1 repair. One session on mathematical generalisation in Year 9 prevents a Diploma exploration built on a pattern the student cannot justify. Two on science inquiry and design prevent a capped internal investigation in DP2. These are small, specific interventions at the point where a little work still does a lot of good.

faqs.question: What happens to strong MYP students in DP1?
faqs.answer: They are disproportionately affected by the assessment change, which surprises everyone. The MYP rewards covering the full demand of a criterion thoroughly; the Diploma penalises unrequested material, because an explain question pays only for explanation and the rest consumes time other questions needed. A fluent MYP writer therefore writes a true, well-organised DP answer and scores poorly. Four to six sessions in the preceding summer on command terms and timed writing prevents most of it.

faqs.question: How do interdisciplinary units get marked?
faqs.answer: Against their own criteria, which require a student to integrate knowledge from two subject groups and reflect on that integration. The commonest failure is two parallel pieces of subject work presented together with no actual integration demonstrated, which reads as thorough and scores mid-band. The fix is a single session on what integration means in practice: a conclusion that could not have been reached from either subject alone, with the student saying explicitly how the two combined.

faqs.question: Should my child take standard or extended mathematics in MYP 4?
faqs.answer: It is a smaller decision than the Diploma route choice and it sits on the same path, so treat it as the first step rather than as an isolated one. Extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 builds the algebraic fluency that Diploma Analysis and Approaches assumes rather than teaches. If Higher Level Analysis is a realistic ambition, extended is the route; if it is not, standard taken well is better than extended taken badly. The subject teacher's view, with a timed paper behind it, should settle it.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education affect MYP performance?
faqs.answer: Through the timetable, significantly. They are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. They sit on top of eight subject groups, interdisciplinary units, Service as Action and, in MYP 5, the Personal Project. A student slipping across several subjects at once is often out of hours rather than out of ability.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range. MYP blocks tend to be short, which is the point: a criterion literacy fix is two to four sessions, not a term.

faqs.question: Does my child need the same tutor for every MYP subject?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and often not for long at all. If the deficit is criterion literacy, one tutor working on that habit improves several subject groups at once, because the skill of reading a descriptor before writing transfers everywhere. If the deficit is specific, such as language acquisition phase descriptors or Design cycle documentation, it needs a specialist in that group for a short block. Send one marked piece from two different subjects and the answer is usually obvious.

intro.heading: Why MYP tutoring in Al Quoz 4 is a timetable problem and a criteria problem
paragraphs: Two things make MYP support different. The first is that the Middle Years Programme has no examinable syllabus in the way IGCSE does. Work is assessed against four published criteria per subject group, each scored nought to eight, and a student can know the content while consistently scoring four because they never address what criterion C actually asks for. A tutor who has not read the descriptors cannot fix that, however strong their subject knowledge is.

The second is the clock, and it runs differently from the Diploma one. MYP students in Dubai are eleven to sixteen, and secondary year groups in this part of the city generally finish between 14:30 and 15:15. Buses into Al Quoz 4 then arrive between about 15:00 and 16:00, earlier than for the Year 13s on the same routes. What fills the gap is activity: swimming, football, music, the after-school clubs that are a real part of the week in Dubai and that parents sensibly refuse to cancel for tuition.

The practical consequence is that MYP sessions here cluster at 16:30 and at 18:00, with very little in between, and that Saturday mornings are more valuable than they are for older students. A tutor with a fixed 17:00 slot and nothing else frequently cannot serve an MYP family at all. We ask about clubs before syllabus, because a plan that collides with a Tuesday swimming squad lasts about three weeks.

On delivery: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. That is an India-only service. Lessons for Al Quoz 4 families run live online, one-to-one. For MYP specifically this matters twice over. It removes the tutor's drive, which is what makes a 16:30 start possible at all. And it widens the pool to people who have actually taught the criteria, which locally is a small group, because MYP is a minority programme inside a curriculum that accounts for 7% of private enrolment in Dubai.

Al Quoz 4 students attend schools spread from Al Safa to Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim, and the continuum schools among them run MYP straight into the Diploma without an IGCSE year. That route has one well-known weakness. Students arrive in Diploma year one strong on inquiry and investigation and noticeably weaker on quantitative fluency, because MYP asks less drilling of mathematical technique. The best time to address it is MYP 4 and 5, not Diploma year one, and it is the most useful thing a tutor can do for a student on that path.

Parents often come to this page after a report that gave a 5 in sciences without explaining why. MYP reporting is criterion-based, and a 5 can be arrived at from very different patterns: strong knowledge with weak evaluation, or the reverse. The first job of a tutor is to read the actual criterion scores rather than the summary grade, because those four numbers say precisely where the work is being lost.
