programmes.countryNote: In Dubai these year groups finish earliest, around 14:30 to 15:00, which makes a 16:30 session genuinely possible for an Al Quoz 4 family. It is also the cheapest stage to intervene, because habits formed here carry into MYP 5 and then into the Diploma.

programmes.name: MYP 4 and 5 — the bridge years
programmes.description: Content deepens and the Personal Project arrives in MYP 5, alongside optional on-screen eAssessment leading to the IB MYP Certificate. Subject criteria stay the same four per group, but the descriptors demand more independence: evaluating a method, justifying a choice, recognising the limitations of a model rather than listing them.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the MYP-to-Diploma gap either closes or hardens. Al Quoz 4 students heading into Diploma provision in Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim benefit most from quantitative work here, particularly algebraic manipulation and handling of units.

programmes.name: What MYP leads into
programmes.description: The Diploma assumes investigation skills MYP teaches well and arithmetic fluency MYP drills less. Students who come through MYP generally design better experiments than their IGCSE-educated classmates and solve equations more slowly. Knowing which side of that your child sits determines what a tutor should prioritise in MYP 5.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving this neighbourhood run the full continuum, so the transfer is internal and the student stays put. That makes the gap easier to miss, because nobody changes school and nobody flags it.

programmes.name: The alternative fork at sixteen
programmes.description: Some families move from MYP into IGCSE at fourteen, usually when changing school. The adjustment is real: IGCSE rewards content recall and exam technique where MYP rewarded inquiry and reflection, and a student who has never sat a terminal paper needs explicit teaching on timing and command terms.
programmes.countryNote: Because Al Quoz 4 families choose across three school clusters, this switch happens more often here than in neighbourhoods served by a single continuum school. A short transition block before Year 10 handles most of it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-quoz-4.subjectsIntro: MYP requests from this neighbourhood concentrate in a few subject groups. Each one is listed with what the criteria actually reward, because that is where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Most lost marks sit in processing and evaluating: data presented without analysis, or a conclusion the results do not support.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The investigating-patterns criterion is the one students find alien, because it asks for a general rule and a justification rather than an answer.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Marks are lost on sourcing and on evaluation: describing two viewpoints is not the same as weighing them, and the descriptors are explicit about the difference.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students write fluently and still score mid-band because they summarise rather than analyse. Coaching targets the move from what the text says to how it achieves its effect.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Phase placement matters more than year group, and a student placed a phase too high struggles in a way that looks like weakness.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The design cycle is marked as a process, so documentation of decisions earns marks that students often skip in favour of the finished product.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Planning, applying skills, and reflecting, supported by a process journal. Coaching covers scope, goal setting and the journal habit. The project itself and all of its writing must be the student's own work.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria: evaluating, synthesising and reflecting across two subject groups. Students treat these as double homework rather than a distinct task, which is where the marks go.

subjects.name: Approaches to Learning
subjects.description: Not a subject but a marked expectation inside every subject: research, thinking, communication, social and self-management skills. These are built inside subject work rather than taught separately.

sections.heading: Four criteria, thirty-two marks, one grade: how MYP actually scores
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each scored on a nought-to-eight scale. The four add to a maximum of thirty-two, and that total converts to a final grade from one to seven using published boundaries. A parent reading a report sees the seven-point grade. The useful information is the four numbers behind it, and schools will provide them.

The reason this matters is that identical grades hide opposite problems. Two Year 9 students can both receive a 5 in sciences. One scored seven for knowing and understanding and three for processing and evaluating: they know the content and cannot analyse data. The other scored four across all four criteria: an even, shallow performance needing something different entirely. A tutor who works from the grade rather than the criterion scores will choose wrongly about half the time.

The descriptors themselves are specific and public. Criterion wording distinguishes describing from explaining from evaluating, and it distinguishes applying a method from justifying the choice of method. Students lose marks not because they lack ideas but because they answer the wrong verb. A session spent reading the descriptor aloud with a student and marking their own last piece of work against it frequently moves a criterion by two marks, which is a grade boundary.

What this means practically for an Al Quoz 4 family is that the first request to the school should be for criterion-level data, not a general comment. Ask for the four scores in each subject group, across the last two summatives. With that, a tutor can tell you in one session where the work is leaking and whether it is the same leak in several subjects, which it very often is.

Present the data and restate the hypothesis
Find a general rule and justify why it holds

Describe two views side by side
Explain how the text achieves its effect

Describe what was made and whether it worked

sections.heading: The MYP afternoon in Al Quoz 4, and where a session fits
paragraphs: A Diploma student's evening is shaped by homework. An MYP student's is shaped by activity, and that changes the scheduling question entirely. Middle year groups in the schools serving Al Quoz 4 finish between about 14:30 and 15:15, earlier than the sixth form, and buses deliver students home between roughly 15:00 and 16:00. Then the clubs begin.

Swimming squads, football training, music lessons and the school's own after-school programme occupy most weekday late afternoons for children of this age in Dubai, and they are not negotiable in most households, nor should they be. What that produces is a bimodal slot pattern: a window at about 16:30 for students whose activity is later or on another day, and a window at 18:00 for those who have already finished.

Almost nothing works at 17:00 for this age group in this neighbourhood, which is the exact hour most tutors have free. It is the single most common reason an MYP enquiry does not convert into a lesson, and it is a logistical mismatch rather than a shortage of good tutors. Online delivery helps because a tutor is not spending the gap between 16:30 and 18:00 driving somewhere; two different families can take the two different windows.

Saturday mornings carry more weight here than for older students. A ninety-minute Saturday session suits MYP 4 and 5 work that needs continuity — a mathematics investigation, a Design cycle write-up, a Personal Project planning session — while a short weekday slot handles consolidation. Families who set that pattern in September rarely change it, and families who try to fit everything into a weekday evening usually renegotiate by October.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and what a tutor may touch
paragraphs: The Personal Project runs through MYP 5 and is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, supported by a process journal the student keeps throughout. It is the first genuinely independent piece of work most students meet, and the failure mode is almost always the same: a goal too broad to evidence, chosen enthusiastically in September and still unfocused in January.

The highest-value coaching happens at the start. A goal like 'learn about marine conservation' cannot be evidenced; 'design and test a three-session workshop on plastic waste for Year 5 students at my school' can. Narrowing the goal is a conversation, and it takes one session. Students who have it in the first fortnight produce projects that write themselves; students who do not spend the spring trying to retrofit a process journal they never kept.

The journal is the second thing. It is not a diary of effort, it is evidence of decisions, and the criteria reward it as such. A student who records why they rejected an approach has something to write about in the reflection; one who records only what they did has to invent a narrative later. Establishing the habit in the first month is worth more than any amount of help at the end.

The boundary is absolute and it is explained to the student in the first session. A tutor may question the goal, teach research and planning skills, ask whether a piece of evidence supports a claim, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, draft or restructure the project or its report, and the same applies to any Diploma coursework later. IB academic-honesty rules treat that as malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor. Several services in this market sell completed coursework; that is what they are selling and it is worth recognising.
bullets: Narrow the goal in the first fortnight, not the second term

sections.heading: The MYP-to-Diploma gap, and closing it in MYP 5
paragraphs: Students who come through MYP arrive in Diploma year one with a recognisable profile. They design investigations well, write reflectively, and handle open-ended tasks with more confidence than classmates arriving from IGCSE. They are also, as a group, slower at algebraic manipulation, less practised at working to the clock, and less drilled on the kind of routine technique a terminal examination rewards.

This is not a criticism of the programme. MYP deliberately prioritises inquiry over drilling, and it produces better investigators for it. But Diploma assessment includes timed papers, and timed papers reward fluency. A student who understands how to find a gradient but takes ninety seconds over the arithmetic will not finish. The fix is practice, and MYP 5 is when there is time for it.

The specific items worth addressing before Diploma year one are consistent across subjects: rearranging formulae with confidence, handling indices and standard form, working with units through a calculation, reading values off a graph accurately, and completing a set of routine questions against a clock. None are conceptually demanding. All are habits, and habits take weeks rather than months.

For Al Quoz 4 families whose child is in a continuum school, nobody will flag this, because the student does not change school at sixteen. The transfer is internal, the teachers are often the same people, and the shift in assessment style arrives without an announcement. Asking a tutor to spend the spring of MYP 5 on fluency rather than content is, in our experience, the highest-return decision available on this route.

sections.heading: ATL skills: marked everywhere, tutored almost nowhere
paragraphs: Approaches to Learning sit underneath every MYP subject group: research, thinking, communication, social and self-management skills. They are not a separate course and there is no ATL examination, which is precisely why they get neglected. They nonetheless show up in criterion scores across every subject, because a student who cannot organise a long task or evaluate a source loses marks in sciences, in individuals and societies, and in the Personal Project simultaneously.

Self-management is the one that matters most at this age and the one parents in Al Quoz 4 most often describe without naming. A Year 9 who does the work but hands it in late, or who starts a two-week task the night before, is losing criterion marks for reasons that have nothing to do with ability. Breaking a task sheet into dated steps is a teachable procedure, and it is taught faster in a one-to-one session than in a classroom of twenty-four.

Research skills are the second. Students of this age search competently and evaluate sources poorly, which is a different problem from the one their parents had. Teaching a student to ask who produced a source and why, and to notice when three results are repeating the same original claim, improves individuals and societies criterion scores directly and helps every subsequent piece of written work.

The way to tutor ATL is inside subject work, never as a module. A session on a sciences investigation is also a session on planning and on evaluating sources, if the tutor is deliberate about naming what is being practised. Students who hear the skill named transfer it; students who only get the content do not. That is most of the difference between a tutor who improves one grade and one who improves several.

sections.heading: What MYP tuition costs here, and why it is priced oddly
paragraphs: MYP sits awkwardly in the Dubai tuition market, and the pricing shows it. Budget online tutoring is advertised from around AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, in a band reaching roughly AED 150. A qualified subject tutor online is published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end.

The oddity is that MYP often gets quoted at the lower end on the assumption that younger students need less expertise, when the opposite is closer to true. MYP content is simpler than Diploma content and MYP assessment is less familiar. A tutor who has never read a criterion descriptor will teach the content competently and leave the criterion scores exactly where they were, which is the thing the family wanted changed.

In-home visits are their own band, AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's figures and AED 200 to AED 500 for independent home tutors. For Al Quoz 4, where few tutors live, that premium is largely a journey. Monthly figures matter more at this age than hourly ones, since MYP support is usually a long, low-intensity arrangement rather than an exam sprint: Bestimate's estimate for one weekly hour runs AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market.

None of these are IB Gram prices; they are what the market publishes, cited so a family can check them. What we would say about value at this stage is that a short criteria clinic before a summative often achieves more than months of general support, because it changes how the student reads every task sheet afterwards. That is the cheapest useful purchase in MYP, and it is worth asking for by name.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and the mandatory subjects on your child's timetable
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. For an MYP family the KHDA inspection report is the one public document that says anything about how the programme is actually being delivered.

KHDA also requires subjects that sit alongside the licensed international curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever curriculum they teach, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Mandatory instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit.

This has a direct effect on MYP, which already asks for eight subject groups. Adding mandatory subjects to eight groups fills a timetable completely, and it is why MYP students in Dubai have less discretionary study time than the programme model assumes. Parents who describe their child as having no time to practise are frequently describing an accurate timetable rather than a motivation problem.

On tutoring itself: the UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years, with applications made through MoHRE's app, website or e-services and a two-working-day completion time listed. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts. IB Gram holds no status with KHDA, the IB or any other body, and any platform implying otherwise should be treated carefully.

process.title: Send the criterion scores
process.description: Not the report grade but the four numbers behind it, for the last two summatives in the subject that worries you. Those four say whether the problem is knowledge, inquiry, analysis or reflection, and they frequently show the same weakness repeating across different subjects.

process.title: Tell us the club timetable
process.description: Which afternoons are taken by swimming, football, music or the school's own programme. For MYP in Al Quoz 4 the activity schedule decides the slot far more than the bus does, and the 17:00 hour most tutors have free is usually the one hour a family cannot use.

process.title: Bring a real task sheet
process.description: The actual summative task and the rubric the school issued. A tutor can then teach your child to read criterion C and answer it, using the document they will be marked against rather than a generic version of it.

process.title: Trial in the slot you want
process.description: A free one-to-one lesson at the time you intend to keep, so you test both the tutor and the hour. Ask the tutor afterwards which criterion they would target first and why; a specific answer is what you are looking for.

process.title: Review by criterion each half term
process.description: Progress is checked against movement in the four criterion scores, not against hours delivered. If criterion D has moved from three to five and criterion A was always strong, the plan should change rather than continue.

whyPoints.title: Tutors who have read the descriptors
whyPoints.description: MYP is marked against criteria, and a tutor who has never seen the descriptors will improve the content and leave the scores unchanged. Matching here filters on criteria experience first and subject knowledge second, which is the opposite of how most platforms sort.

whyPoints.title: Slots that fit a twelve-year-old's week
whyPoints.description: The MYP windows in Al Quoz 4 are around 16:30 and around 18:00, with clubs in between. Because lessons are online, two families can take the two different windows and no tutor is driving across Dubai in the gap.

whyPoints.title: Personal Project scoped, not written
whyPoints.description: Coaching concentrates on narrowing the goal and building the process-journal habit in the first month. The project and every word of its report must be the student's own work, and that is stated to the student at the start.

whyPoints.title: Fluency built before the Diploma
whyPoints.description: Continuum students arrive in Diploma year one strong on inquiry and slower on routine technique. Spending the spring of MYP 5 on algebraic fluency, units and timed practice is the highest-return work available on that route, and nobody else flags it.

whyPoints.title: Criteria clinics as finite blocks
whyPoints.description: Three or four sessions built from the school's own task sheet frequently move a criterion by two marks, which crosses a grade boundary. We would rather sell that than a year of general support, because it changes how the student reads every task afterwards.

faqs.question: What does an MYP tutor do differently from a normal subject tutor?
faqs.answer: They work from the criterion descriptors. MYP has no examinable syllabus in the IGCSE sense; every subject group is assessed against four criteria scored nought to eight, and students lose marks by answering the wrong verb rather than by not knowing the content. A tutor who has read the descriptors will mark your child's last piece of work against them and show where the gap is. A tutor who has not will teach good subject content and leave the criterion scores where they were.

faqs.question: How does my child's MYP grade out of 7 get calculated?
faqs.answer: Four criteria per subject group, each scored nought to eight, giving a maximum of thirty-two. That total converts to a one-to-seven grade using published boundaries. The seven-point grade is what appears on the report, but the four numbers behind it carry the information. Two students with the same 5 can have opposite problems: one strong on knowledge and weak on analysis, the other evenly mid-band across all four. Ask the school for the criterion-level scores; they will provide them.

faqs.question: What time do MYP lessons usually run for families in Al Quoz 4?
faqs.answer: Around 16:30 or around 18:00, with very little in between. Middle year groups in the schools serving this area finish between about 14:30 and 15:15 and buses arrive home between 15:00 and 16:00, earlier than for sixth formers. The late afternoon then fills with swimming, football, music and school clubs. That produces two usable windows either side of the activity, and 17:00 — the hour most tutors have free — is the one that collides with everything.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our home in Al Quoz 4 for MYP sessions?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is an India-only service. MYP lessons for Al Quoz 4 families run live online, one-to-one. For this age group the online format also solves a real scheduling problem, because a tutor who is not driving between appointments can take a 16:30 slot for one family and an 18:00 slot for another, which is exactly the pattern MYP families in this neighbourhood need.

faqs.question: Where exactly can a tutor assist on the MYP 5 Personal Project?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes, and that is where the help is actually needed. A tutor can question whether the goal is narrow enough to evidence, teach planning and research skills, establish the process-journal habit, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, draft or restructure the project or its report. The usual failure is a goal chosen too broadly in September — 'learn about marine conservation' rather than something testable — and that is fixed in a single early conversation.

faqs.question: Why did my child's science criterion C score stay low all year?
faqs.answer: Processing and evaluating is the criterion MYP science students most often leave unaddressed, because it asks for analysis of the data and a judgement on the method's validity, and students instead present the data and restate the hypothesis. It reads like a complete answer and scores in the middle band. The remedy is mechanical: take the student's last investigation, read the descriptor aloud, and mark it together. Most students move two marks once they can see what the words are asking for.

faqs.question: Does MYP prepare a student properly for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: For investigation and independent work, very well. MYP students generally design better experiments and handle open-ended tasks more confidently than classmates arriving from IGCSE. What they tend to lack is fluency: faster algebraic manipulation, confident handling of units and standard form, and practice working against a clock, because MYP deliberately drills less routine technique. None of that is conceptually hard. It is habit, and the spring of MYP 5 is the right time to build it.

faqs.question: Is the investigating patterns criterion in maths really that different?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the one MYP mathematics students find most alien. It asks for a general rule describing a pattern and a justification for why that rule holds, not an answer for the cases tested. Students who are quick at arithmetic often score lowest here, because they finish the computation and stop. The teachable move is to write the rule in algebraic form and then test it against a case not yet used. That single habit lifts the criterion reliably.

faqs.question: What are ATL skills and do they really affect grades?
faqs.answer: Approaches to Learning are the research, thinking, communication, social and self-management skills that sit under every MYP subject group. There is no ATL exam, which is why they get neglected, but they show in criterion scores everywhere. A student who starts a two-week task the night before loses marks in sciences, in individuals and societies and in the Personal Project at once. These are best taught inside subject work, with the skill named explicitly so the student can transfer it.

faqs.question: How much does MYP tuition cost in Dubai compared with Diploma tuition?
faqs.answer: It is frequently quoted lower, on the assumption that younger students need less expertise. Budget online tuition is advertised from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour by Tutopiya and EdFlik, in a band to roughly AED 150; qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. For MYP the band matters less than whether the tutor knows the criteria, because content at this level is simple and the assessment model is not. Pay for criteria experience.

faqs.question: Should we switch from MYP to IGCSE at fourteen?
faqs.answer: It depends on where your child is heading and on whether you are changing school anyway. IGCSE rewards content recall and terminal exam technique; MYP rewards inquiry and reflection. A student moving across needs explicit teaching on timing and command terms, which they will not have met. A student staying in MYP into the Diploma keeps the inquiry advantage and needs fluency work instead. Neither route is better in general; the question is which gap you are prepared to close deliberately.

faqs.question: My child understands the work but hands it in late. Can tutoring help?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the target is self-management rather than content. Breaking a task sheet into dated steps, working backwards from the deadline, and building in a checkpoint before the final write-up are teachable procedures, and they move criterion scores because late or rushed work loses marks for reasons unrelated to ability. One-to-one is a better setting for this than a classroom of twenty-four, since the plan can be built around the actual week your child has, clubs included.

faqs.question: Is it better to book one MYP subject group or three together?
faqs.answer: Usually one, chosen by looking at the criterion scores across all of them. The common finding is that the same criterion is weak in several subjects — evaluation, or analysis — and fixing it in one subject transfers to the others at no extra cost, provided the tutor names the skill rather than only teaching the content. Tutoring three subject groups simultaneously at this age fills the week, costs three times as much, and often addresses one underlying habit three times over.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory UAE subjects leave time for MYP homework?
faqs.answer: Less than parents expect. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them and calculating instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. Added to eight MYP subject groups, that fills a timetable. When a student appears not to be practising between sessions, the schedule is often the honest explanation rather than motivation, and a plan should account for it.

intro.heading: Why nobody near you seems to know MYP, and what to do about it
paragraphs: Parents in Al Qusais searching for MYP help usually report the same experience. There are plenty of maths tutors, plenty of science tutors, and almost nobody who can explain why a child who understands the work came home with a 4 in criterion B. The feeling that no one nearby knows this programme is accurate, and the reason is structural rather than geographic. MYP does not examine content in the way IGCSE or the Diploma does. It assesses performance against four published criteria per subject, each scored from 0 to 8, and a tutor who has never read those descriptors is guessing at what the marks are for.

That produces a specific and common failure. A competent maths graduate tutors an MYP 4 student, the student's calculation improves, the report comes back unchanged, and nobody can explain it. The usual cause is that the weak criterion was investigating patterns or communicating - generalising a rule and justifying it, or presenting reasoning so another person can follow it - and the tutoring spent ten weeks on arithmetic that was never the problem. The content help was real. It was aimed at the wrong target.

Al Qusais adds a geographic layer to this. The MYP cohorts nearest this neighbourhood sit mainly in Al Mamzar, Al Garhoud and Festival City rather than in Al Qusais itself, where Indian-curriculum and British-track schools dominate. So a family here is often arranging support for a child who travels to school, in a programme that fewer schools in the catchment run, with a report format that the nearest available tutors have never seen. Searching by distance from Damascus Street is close to the worst possible filter for this particular request.

The honest answer is that MYP support should be matched by subject group and by criterion, over video, from whoever genuinely knows the programme. That pool is small but it exists, and it is far larger than the set of people who happen to live within twenty minutes of Al Nahda Road. This page sets out what an MYP tutor has to know, three tasks you can use to test one in ten minutes, how to read your child's report properly, and what the MYP-to-Diploma transition actually demands.

IB Gram delivers MYP support to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Where we cannot match a subject group and criterion properly, we say so at the match stage with the alternatives and a date rather than filling the slot with someone adjacent and letting a term pass before the next report explains the problem.

programmes.name: MYP years 1 to 3

Each subject carries four criteria scored from 0 to 8, assessed through tasks rather than tests, with key concepts, global contexts and statements of inquiry framing the units. A student can be academically strong and score mid-band simply because they do not know what the descriptors ask for.

programmes.description: The stakes rise. Subject work becomes more demanding, the Personal Project arrives in the final year with its own criteria, and students on an eAssessment pathway face on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate. Workload management becomes as much of a problem as any individual subject.

programmes.name: The transition into the Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The largest step in an IB education and the one most MYP families underestimate. Assessment switches from criteria applied to tasks to timed written papers with mark schemes, plus internal assessments with their own criteria. Students who scored well in MYP by producing thoughtful extended work can struggle badly with a forty-five minute paper.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within reach of Al Qusais run the Diploma, and the summer between MYP 5 and Year 12 is the single best window to prepare for this change. It is also the one most often spent assuming that strong MYP grades will carry across, which they frequently do not.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-qusais.subjectsIntro: MYP help in Al Qusais is asked for by subject group, and the pattern of difficulty differs across them. These are the eight groups with what each one's criteria actually demand.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the one that surprises families - it asks a student to find a rule, express it generally and justify why it holds, which is closer to proof than to calculation.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Inquiring and designing is where most marks are lost: a research question that is not measurable, or a method with no controlled variable identified, caps the score regardless of how well the experiment went.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students who write fluently often score mid-band on analysing because they summarise the text rather than examining how the writer produces an effect. The distinction is teachable and rarely taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed by phase rather than by year group. A student may be in MYP 4 and phase 2 in Arabic or French, and the phase is what the criteria are applied against - a detail that confuses parents comparing their child with a classmate.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the discriminating criterion: evaluating sources, recognising perspective and limitation, and reaching a judgement rather than presenting both sides and stopping.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The most commonly misunderstood subject in the programme, because the marks sit in the documented design process rather than in the finished product. A beautiful outcome with a thin process scores poorly.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. As in design, process documentation carries weight that students who judge their own work by the final piece consistently underestimate. The process journal is assessed, not decorative.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Planning, applying skills, and reflecting, assessed against its own criteria with a process journal and a report. A tutor may teach the criteria, question a goal's feasibility, review a journal entry and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not plan it, produce it or write the report.

sections.heading: What an MYP tutor has to know that a subject tutor does not
paragraphs: The gap is not subject knowledge. A good maths graduate knows more mathematics than an MYP 4 curriculum contains. The gap is assessment literacy, and it has four parts, each of which an MYP tutor uses in every session and a subject tutor has never encountered. The first is the criteria themselves: four per subject group, each scored from 0 to 8, with band descriptors that specify what a student must demonstrate rather than what they must know. Teaching towards a descriptor is a different activity from teaching towards a syllabus.

The second is task-specific clarification. Teachers adapt the general descriptors to a particular task, and those adapted statements are what the work is actually marked against. A tutor who has not seen them is working from the general version, which is like marking an essay against a subject outline rather than a mark scheme. These documents exist in every MYP school and almost no parent thinks to send them.

The third is the programme's conceptual framework: key concepts, related concepts, global contexts and statements of inquiry. A student asked to connect their work to a global context and who treats that as decoration loses marks that have nothing to do with the subject. A tutor who dismisses this framework as jargon will teach good content and leave those marks behind every time.

The fourth is the conversion. Raw criterion scores add to a maximum of 32 and are converted to a 1-7 grade using published grade boundaries. That means a student can lift one criterion by two marks and see no grade movement, or lift two by one mark each and move a whole grade. Knowing where a student sits inside the boundary band is what tells you whether this term's effort will show on the next report - and it is the first thing we work out.

sections.heading: Three tasks that show in ten minutes whether a tutor knows MYP
paragraphs: Qualification lists do not distinguish between an MYP tutor and a subject tutor, so set tasks instead. Each of these takes a few minutes on a first call, requires no knowledge of the programme from you, and produces an answer you can judge. Use them on any tutor in Dubai, ours included.

Task one: name the four criteria for my child's subject group, and tell me which one is usually weakest for students at this level. A tutor who knows the programme answers immediately and specifically - investigating patterns in mathematics, inquiring and designing in sciences, analysing in language and literature, thinking critically in individuals and societies. A tutor who does not will talk about topics or about the student's general ability instead, which is the answer you are listening for.

Task two: here is my child's last report with the criterion scores. What would you work on first and why? The right answer references the conversion - which criterion, lifted by how much, would move the overall grade given where the raw total sits. A weaker answer picks the lowest number without reference to the boundary, which is sometimes right by accident and is not reasoning.

Task three: here is a piece of my child's work and the task sheet. Mark it against the descriptors and tell me which band it sits in. This is the decisive one. A tutor who has done it before asks for the task-specific clarification before answering, gives a band with a reason, and names what would be needed to reach the next one. A tutor who has not will offer encouragement, correct the content, and avoid the band question entirely.

sections.heading: Reading an MYP report properly, and why the overall grade misleads
paragraphs: An MYP report gives four criterion scores per subject, each out of 8, and an overall grade from 1 to 7. Parents in Al Qusais comparing their child with a cousin at a British-curriculum school naturally focus on the overall grade, and that is the least actionable number on the page. It is a conversion of the raw total, so two students with the same grade can have completely different profiles - one even across four criteria, the other strong on two and weak on two - and they need entirely different terms of work.

The useful reading is the shape rather than the level. A profile that is strong on knowing and understanding and weak on the investigative or communicative criterion tells you the student has the content and cannot yet demonstrate it in the form the task demands. That is a teachable, fast-moving problem. A profile that is weak on knowing and understanding and relatively stronger elsewhere tells you the opposite, and the work is slower.

The second thing worth reading is movement across reports rather than position in one. A criterion that has sat at 4 for three reporting cycles is a settled gap and probably has a specific cause the student can name once asked. A criterion that moves between 3 and 6 depending on the task is a consistency problem, usually about planning time or reading the task carefully, and it responds to process work rather than to subject teaching.

Finally, the conversion matters for deciding whether anything will show. Because the raw total out of 32 maps to a 1-7 grade through boundaries, a student at the top of a band needs one mark to move up and a student at the bottom needs several. Knowing which applies prevents the most demoralising outcome in MYP tutoring: a term of genuine improvement that does not change the number on the report, with nobody able to explain why. Ask the school for the boundary table it applies.

sections.heading: eAssessment, the Personal Project, and the boundary a tutor holds
paragraphs: In the final MYP year the programme adds assessments with their own rules, and families should establish early which of them apply. Schools may enter students for MYP eAssessment, which involves on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate, or may assess entirely internally. The two produce quite different final years, and the difference is not always clearly communicated to parents. Ask the MYP coordinator in writing which route your child's cohort is on.

The Personal Project runs in the final year regardless, and it is assessed against its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, supported by a process journal and a report. The most common failure is a goal too large or too vague to evidence - a student sets out to build something ambitious, the process journal records enthusiasm rather than decisions, and the report has nothing specific to reflect on. Screening the goal for feasibility at the start is worth more than any amount of help later.

The process journal is itself assessed, which students consistently treat as a formality. It should record decisions, changes of direction, obstacles and what was learned from each, because those are the raw material of the reflection criterion. A journal that reads as a diary of activity scores poorly however impressive the outcome. This is teachable in a single session and almost never taught.

The boundary is the same as everywhere else in the IB and worth stating plainly. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate the feasibility of a goal, review a journal entry and explain why it is thin, mark a draft report against the descriptors and say that a section is below standard. A tutor may not plan the project, produce the outcome, write the report or redraft it to completion. The work must be the student's own, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student rather than on whoever sold the help.

sections.heading: The MYP to Diploma step, and the summer that decides it
paragraphs: The biggest risk in an MYP education is not a mid-programme dip. It is the transition into the Diploma, where assessment changes shape entirely. MYP rewards extended, thoughtful, well-documented work produced over days against published criteria. The Diploma rewards timed written answers against mark schemes, plus internal assessments with their own criteria and strict honesty rules. A student who has never sat a forty-five minute paper under pressure can lose two grades to the format alone.

The specific gaps are identifiable. Speed and timing, because MYP tasks rarely demand it. Recall under pressure, because MYP work is usually resource-supported. Method marks, because the Diploma awards credit for working rather than only for outcomes. And subject-specific technical content, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, where Diploma courses assume fluency that criterion-based tasks did not require.

The summer between MYP 5 and Year 12 is the right window for this, and it is the most wasted block in the whole IB sequence. There is no competing homework, the student has recovered from the final MYP year, and eight to twelve hours of focused bridging work costs less than a term of remediation in the first half of Year 12. Families in Al Qusais who do this arrive in the Diploma with the format problem already solved.

It also helps to settle subject choices with the Diploma in mind rather than with MYP strengths in mind. A student who scored well in MYP mathematics through investigating patterns may still find Analysis and Approaches hard, because that course examines algebraic fluency under time without a calculator on one paper. Discuss the four Diploma maths courses and the sciences with the coordinator before choices close, and use MYP criterion profiles as evidence rather than the overall grades.

sections.heading: Supply, cost and the fallback when no MYP specialist is free
paragraphs: Stating the coverage position is more useful than implying unlimited availability, and no competing page in this market does it. MYP mathematics and sciences are the easiest subject groups to staff with someone who genuinely knows the criteria. Language and literature and individuals and societies are tighter. Design, arts and language acquisition at a specific phase are genuinely scarce, and the Personal Project is scarce in a different way, because it needs someone who has marked against its criteria rather than someone who is good at projects.

Costs, for context rather than as our price list. Published Dubai market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase listing AED 270; budget platforms advertise far lower, with Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For MYP specifically the budget band carries a particular risk, because criterion literacy is not something a capable undergraduate necessarily has. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel.

Our fallback, stated before any payment: if a tutor who knows your child's subject group and criteria is free in your window, you get one. If not, you are told at the match stage with three options - a different time slot with the right person, a tutor with adjacent expertise starting now while we hold the specialist slot, or a wait with a date attached. For a one-off criterion-translation session the wait is usually short, because that is a single session rather than a weekly commitment.

What we will not do is place a content tutor with an MYP student whose problem is a criterion and let two reporting cycles pass. That failure is invisible while it happens: the sessions feel productive, the student is working, and then the report comes back unchanged. It is the single most common complaint we hear from Al Qusais families about tutoring they bought elsewhere, and avoiding it is most of what this page is about.

sections.heading: KHDA, MYP schools in this catchment, and what inspection ratings do not tell you
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects on a published six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the rating belongs to the school as a whole. For a parent choosing an MYP school around Al Qusais, more useful questions are how long the school has been authorised for the programme, whether the cohort is entered for eAssessment, and how consistently the criteria are explained to students.

That last point matters because MYP is interpreted locally. Two authorised schools can apply the same descriptors with noticeably different strictness, which is why a student moving school mid-programme sometimes sees scores shift without anything changing in their work. It is also why a tutor needs the task-specific clarification from your child's own teacher rather than a generic version downloaded from elsewhere.

The regulator map is worth knowing in this catchment because Al Nahda sits on a border. Dubai is KHDA; Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which u.ae states regulates private education in the emirate and which, with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK; Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education.

Alongside MYP, Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies and stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited due to different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. That load shapes the week any MYP tutoring plan has to fit into. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the IB or any other body named here.

faqs.question: Why does my child's MYP grade not improve even though we have a tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually because the tutoring is aimed at the wrong criterion. faqs.question: Which documents turn a first MYP session from a chat into a diagnosis?
faqs.answer: Three things. The four criterion scores per subject from the last report, not the overall grade. The task-specific clarification sheet the teacher issued with a recent assessment, which is what the work was actually marked against. And a piece of your child's own marked work. With those, a first session can diagnose rather than explore. Without them, the tutor is working from general descriptors and the student's self-report, which is how ten weeks get spent on something that was never the problem.

faqs.question: How do MYP criterion scores become the 1-7 grade on the report?
faqs.answer: The four criterion scores, each out of 8, add to a raw total out of 32, which is converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using published grade boundaries. That conversion is why two students with the same overall grade can have completely different profiles and need different work. It also means a student at the top of a boundary band may need one extra mark to move up while one at the bottom needs several. Ask your child's school for the boundary table it applies.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion causes the most trouble in mathematics?
faqs.answer: Investigating patterns, consistently. It asks a student to find a rule, express it in general terms and justify why it holds - closer to proof than to calculation - and most students meet that demand without anyone explaining it. A child who can calculate fluently and reliably scores in the middle band here, which baffles parents looking at the overall grade. It is teachable and it moves relatively quickly once the expectation is made explicit, often within one reporting cycle.

faqs.question: How can I test whether a tutor really knows the MYP before paying?
faqs.answer: Set three tasks on the first call. Ask them to name the four criteria for your child's subject group and say which is usually weakest. Show them the report and ask what they would prioritise and why, listening for a reference to the grade boundary rather than just the lowest number. Then give them a piece of real work and the task sheet and ask them to name the band it sits in. A tutor who has done this before asks for the task-specific clarification first.

faqs.question: Does my child need weekly MYP tutoring or something shorter?
faqs.answer: Often something shorter. A substantial share of the MYP enquiries we take from this neighbourhood are resolved by one criterion-translation session: reading the report and the task sheet and explaining what the descriptors actually ask for. If the problem was comprehension of the assessment rather than of the subject, nothing more is needed this term. Weekly support makes sense where there is a genuine content gap underneath, or in the final year when the Personal Project and subject work compete.

faqs.question: What is the MYP Personal Project and where do students lose marks on it?
faqs.answer: A final-year project assessed against its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, supported by a process journal and a report. Marks are lost in two places. A goal too large or too vague to evidence, so the journal records enthusiasm rather than decisions. And a process journal treated as a formality, when it is an assessed document whose job is to record decisions, obstacles and what was learned - the raw material the reflection criterion needs. Screening the goal early is the highest-value intervention.

faqs.question: Where exactly does a tutor stop on an MYP Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may teach the criteria, question whether a goal is feasible and evidenceable, review a journal entry and explain why it is thin, mark a draft report against the descriptors and state that a section is below standard. A tutor may not plan the project, produce the outcome, write the report or rewrite it to completion. The work must be the student's own under IB academic-honesty rules, and a breach puts the student at risk rather than whoever sold the assistance.

faqs.question: Is my child's school entering them for MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Ask the MYP coordinator in writing, because it changes the final year substantially and is not always communicated clearly to parents. Schools may enter students for eAssessment, which involves on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate, or may assess entirely internally. A student preparing for on-screen examinations needs timed practice and format familiarity that an internally assessed student does not. Either way, the answer should shape how the final year is planned rather than emerging halfway through it.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from MYP 5 into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Larger than most families expect, and the problem is format rather than content. MYP rewards extended, documented work produced over days against criteria; the Diploma rewards timed written answers against mark schemes. A student who has never sat a forty-five minute paper under pressure can lose ground to the format alone. The gaps are identifiable: speed, recall without resources, method marks, and technical fluency in maths and the sciences. Eight to twelve hours in the summer between usually closes them.

faqs.question: Should MYP grades decide my child's Diploma subject choices?
faqs.answer: Use the criterion profiles as evidence rather than the overall grades. A student who scored well in MYP mathematics largely through investigating patterns may still find Analysis and Approaches difficult, because that course examines algebraic fluency under time with no calculator on one paper. A student strong on knowing and understanding in sciences may be better placed than their grade suggests. Take the four scores per subject to the coordinator before choices close and ask which course they actually point towards.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost around Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates, read in October 2026: a qualified subject tutor online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase publishing AED 270. Budget platforms advertise from around AED 33 to 65 an hour, which for MYP carries a specific risk because criterion literacy is not something a capable undergraduate necessarily has. In-home visits run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel. Those are other providers' figures; we quote against the subject group and the work required.

faqs.question: Do you send MYP tutors to homes in Al Qusais or Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson we arrange runs one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we operate only in India. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the Emirates. For MYP the online format has a practical advantage beyond cost: the pool of tutors who are genuinely criterion-literate is small, and insisting that one of them also lives near Damascus Street reduces it to almost nothing. Matching over video is what makes a proper match possible at all from this neighbourhood.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-qusais.closingHeading: Send the four scores and the task sheet
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-qusais.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB MYP tutor in Al Qusais, the two documents that change everything are your child's four criterion scores per subject and the task-specific clarification sheet their teacher issued with a recent assessment. With those, a first session can say which criterion is actually weak, whether lifting it would move the grade given where the raw total sits, and what the student's work is missing. Some families need that single session and nothing more. Send the subject group, the MYP year and your workable time windows, and we will tell you plainly whether a criterion-literate tutor is free or what the wait is. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.tutorsIntro: These are the MYP specialists currently taking students from Al Rashidiya and the eastern suburbs. Send the task sheet and the rubric with it, because in this programme the rubric is the lesson plan.

intro.heading: The Middle Years Programme is marked against criteria, and nobody explains them
paragraphs: Parents arriving at MYP from any other system have the same experience. A report comes home with numbers against letters, a 5 for criterion A and a 3 for criterion C, and no obvious translation into whether the child is doing well. Then a task sheet arrives with a rubric on the back, and the rubric uses words like "analyse" and "evaluate" in a specific technical sense that nobody has taught the student. The result is a capable child losing marks for reasons that have nothing to do with how much they know.

That is the actual work of MYP tutoring, and it is different work from IGCSE or Diploma tutoring. There is no past paper to drill. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each marked out of eight, and the descriptors are published. A student who reads the descriptor for the level above the one they are achieving, and understands what the difference between those two paragraphs looks like in practice, improves without learning any new content. Most students have never been shown how to do that.

The geography of this district shapes how that work gets delivered. Al Rashidiya sits between Dubai International Airport, Al Garhoud and Nad Al Hamar, with no school inside it. Its MYP students travel, and the nearest IB continuum provision is in the Mirdif direction, which means a collecting bus route and around forty minutes once school finishes. For a Year 7 child that journey is the dominant fact of the afternoon; for a Year 11 student it is an inconvenience. The same slot does not work for both.

So this page treats age as the main variable rather than subject. A Year 7 student needs a shorter session, earlier, with a parent in the house. A Year 9 student needs criteria work and the beginnings of independent study. A Year 11 student in the final MYP year needs the Personal Project handled properly and the transition to the Diploma or to IGCSE planned. Those are three different purchases, and selling them as one hour of MYP tutoring is how families end up disappointed.

One more thing is worth saying before the detail. MYP marks are not an early warning system for Diploma grades in the way parents assume, because the two are measured on different things. A student with middling criterion marks who can investigate and reflect well is often better placed for the Diploma than a classmate with higher grades built on recall. So read a weak criterion as a specific instruction rather than a verdict, and treat a strong one as a real asset even when the overall grade is unremarkable.

IB Gram delivers all of it as live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, with no tutor travelling anywhere. Home visits are a service offered only in India; there is no UAE version, and for a younger child that is a genuine trade-off we discuss honestly rather than talk past. What follows covers the criteria, the eight subject groups, what each age band can absorb after a long bus, the Personal Project timeline, the transitions out of MYP, and the market rates in dirhams with every figure attributed.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.programmesIntro: MYP spans five years and three quite different kinds of student. These are the stages, and what support actually means in each.

programmes.name: MYP years 1 and 2
programmes.description: The settling-in years, where the criteria are introduced and the habits of recording work, meeting deadlines and reading a rubric are either established or not. Content gaps here are small and cheap to fix; organisational gaps are the ones that compound. Sessions are shorter, because a twelve-year-old off a long bus has perhaps forty productive minutes in them.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Rashidiya families this is the age at which the school run bites hardest, because a Year 7 child on a Mirdif bus route is genuinely finished by late afternoon. The honest recommendation here is often a shorter earlier session or a weekend morning, and sometimes it is to leave tutoring alone for a year and fix the routine instead.

programmes.name: MYP years 3 and 4
programmes.description: Where subject-specific demands sharpen and the criteria start to separate students. Mathematics streams into standard and extended routes in many schools, sciences become more quantitative, and the language subjects begin asking for genuine analysis rather than description. This is the most productive window for criteria coaching, because there is still time for the habit to pay off.
programmes.countryNote: In this part of Dubai, Year 9 is also when schools decide who takes extended mathematics and who does not, and that decision follows a student into Diploma course choice two years later. Ask which route your child is being placed in and on what evidence, because a standard-route student who later wants Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level has ground to make up.

programmes.name: MYP year 5 and the Personal Project
programmes.description: The final MYP year, carrying the Personal Project and, in some schools, MYP eAssessment. The Personal Project is an independent piece of work assessed against its own criteria, with a process journal that matters as much as the product. It is the first genuinely self-directed project most students attempt, and it is routinely started far too late.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Rashidiya student in MYP5 is usually also deciding between the Diploma Programme and a move to a British-curriculum sixth form, both reachable within an ordinary school run from here. That decision interacts with the Personal Project year, which is why families often want one arrangement covering both the project and the transition planning.

programmes.name: Leaving MYP: Diploma or IGCSE
programmes.description: Two quite different crossings. Into the Diploma, the step is from criteria-based tasks to timed papers with mark schemes. Into an IGCSE year at a different school, the step is similar but compressed and arrives with specific syllabus content that MYP does not cover. Either way the gap is technique rather than intelligence.
programmes.countryNote: Both routes exist within reach of Al Rashidiya, with Diploma provision in the Garhoud and Mirdif clusters and British-curriculum sixth forms across the eastern corridor. A summer bridging block of six to ten sessions on timed-answer technique removes most of the first-term shock in either direction, and costs less than the remediation families otherwise buy in November.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.subjectsIntro: MYP students study across eight subject groups, and the criteria differ between them. These are the areas Al Rashidiya families ask about, with what each one's criteria actually reward.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The last two are where capable students lose marks: a correct answer with no explanation of the reasoning, or a real-world task answered mathematically but never interpreted back into the context.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowledge, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Design and evaluation are the sections that separate students, because they require writing about method and limitation rather than reporting a result.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: History, geography and economics content assessed on knowledge, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. The critical-thinking criterion is where marks concentrate and where a student who writes a well-organised description rather than an argument is capped regardless of effort.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Students frequently lose marks under analysing by summarising a text rather than examining how it achieves an effect, which is a teachable distinction and almost never taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehending spoken and written text, and communicating in response. Progress is tracked through phases rather than years, so a student can be in a different phase from their class peers. Knowing your child's phase is essential before any tutoring is booked.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. The process journal carries real weight here, and students who produce good work while documenting none of their thinking lose marks they have genuinely earned.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating. Design is the subject where the criteria are most procedural, which makes it unusually responsive to explicit coaching on what each strand expects at each level.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on performance. The written and reflective strands are often the weak point for students who perform well physically, and they are worth more marks than most families expect.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project assessed against its own criteria, with a process journal that is examined alongside the product. A tutor may teach the criteria, question the student's plan and respond to their journal with questions. A tutor may not produce, write or complete any part of it.

subjects.name: Reading the criteria descriptors
subjects.description: Not a subject but the central skill of the programme. Comparing the descriptor for the achieved level with the one above it, in the student's own work, is the single highest-yield activity in MYP tutoring and requires no new content whatsoever.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Research, organisation, communication and self-management, which MYP assesses implicitly throughout. For Years 7 and 8 these are frequently the real problem, and three sessions on how to keep a workable notebook outperform ten on any subject.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, taught from the school's own approved material. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

sections.heading: How criteria A to D actually work, and why reports confuse parents
paragraphs: Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, and each criterion is marked out of eight against published descriptors. The four criterion marks are then converted into the 1 to 7 grade that appears on a report, using a published set of grade boundaries. That conversion is the reason a report can look mystifying: a student with 6, 6, 5, 3 and a student with 5, 5, 5, 5 have very different problems and can end up looking similar.

What the criteria do not measure is how much the student knows, except in criterion A. The other three measure what they do with it: investigating, communicating, applying, analysing, evaluating. That is why a well-read child who writes beautifully organised description can be stuck at a 4 while a less fluent classmate who argues a point reaches a 6. Effort is not the variable, and telling such a child to work harder makes things worse.

The useful move for a parent is mechanical. Ask the school for the criterion marks rather than only the overall grade, find the lowest one, and read the published descriptor for that criterion at the level achieved and at the level above. The difference between those two paragraphs is the entire tutoring brief. In most cases it names a specific behaviour, such as justifying a choice or evaluating a limitation, that can be practised in a single session and then applied everywhere.

This is also how you test a prospective MYP tutor. Ask them what the difference is between the 5 to 6 band and the 7 to 8 band in criterion C for your child's subject. Somebody who has taught the programme answers with reference to the descriptor's actual language. Somebody who has not talks generally about deeper understanding, which is the answer the report already gave you.

sections.heading: What an eleven year old and a sixteen year old can absorb after the same bus
paragraphs: MYP covers five years and a very wide range of stamina, and tutoring sold at a single session length across that range is wrong at one end or the other. A Year 7 child off a forty-minute collecting bus from a Mirdif school has roughly forty productive minutes in them, and the last twenty of a sixty-minute session are spent being present rather than learning. A Year 11 student can hold a full hour and sometimes needs ninety minutes for project work.

The slot moves with age too. Younger students do better earlier, while they are still awake, and they need a parent in the house, which is a practical constraint on a working household rather than a preference. Older students do better later, once homework is underway and they have something specific to ask about. Trying to run a family's two children in the same slot usually serves neither.

Parents of younger MYP students should also hear the honest version of the online trade-off. A sixteen year old working from a rubric on a shared screen is well served by video; an eleven year old who will not sit still is better served by somebody physically present, and we will say so rather than take the booking. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes under any circumstances, so for that family the right recommendation is a local provider with a verifiable MoHRE private tuition permit.

Where video does work for younger students, two things make the difference: a short session and a visible task. Forty minutes with a task sheet open and one paragraph to rewrite by the end holds a twelve year old's attention. An hour of general discussion does not, and the fault is the format rather than the child.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the journal nobody keeps
paragraphs: The Personal Project sits in the final MYP year and is assessed against its own criteria, with a process journal examined alongside the finished product. The journal is where most marks are lost, because students treat it as paperwork to be assembled afterwards rather than as evidence of thinking produced along the way. A beautiful product with a thin journal scores below a modest product with a thorough one.

The second common failure is the goal. A project goal that is too broad gives nothing to evaluate against, and one that is too easy gives nothing to struggle with, and the criteria reward the struggle. Choosing the goal properly, with stated success criteria the student writes themselves, is most of the work and it happens at the beginning rather than at the end.

A realistic timeline for an Al Rashidiya student is worth writing down, because households here travel often and a lost fortnight is survivable early and fatal late. Start the goal conversation in the first term, keep the journal weekly from the moment the goal is set, build the product across the middle of the year, and leave the final weeks for the report rather than for the making.

The boundary is absolute. A tutor may teach the criteria, question the goal, respond to journal entries with questions and point out where a reflection is not supported by evidence. A tutor may not produce, write, draft or complete any part of the project or the report. One page in the researched competitor set sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is an academic-integrity breach, and the student carries the consequence rather than the seller.

sections.heading: Leaving MYP: the two crossings and what each one costs
paragraphs: At the end of MYP a student in this part of Dubai takes one of two routes, and both are reachable within an ordinary school run from Al Rashidiya. Into the Diploma Programme, usually at the same school or one nearby in the Garhoud or Mirdif clusters. Or across to a British-curriculum sixth form, which in some cases means an IGCSE year first.

The gap in both directions is the same and it is not content. It is the shift from criteria-based tasks, where a student has time and a rubric, to timed papers with mark schemes, where the reward goes to a specific form of answer produced quickly. A student who has spent five years writing considered extended responses can lose marks badly on a paper that wants three precise sentences in four minutes, and nothing about that is a sign of weakness.

Mathematics is the one place where content genuinely matters. A student from the standard MYP mathematics route who wants Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level has algebraic fluency to build, and that is a summer block rather than a conversation. A student from the extended route is usually fine. This is why the Year 9 streaming decision deserves more attention than it gets locally.

A bridging block of six to ten sessions over the summer, aimed at timed-answer technique and, where relevant, algebraic fluency, removes most of the first-term shock on either route. It costs considerably less than the remediation block families otherwise buy in November of the following year, when the student has already decided they are bad at the subject.

sections.heading: What middle-years tutoring costs in Dubai, and what to pay for it
paragraphs: Here is the part most pages leave out. Published Dubai rates, each read on the provider's own public page, so you can open them and check rather than take anybody's word for it.

For MYP specifically, the budget tiers are more defensible than they are for Higher Level Diploma work. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya's published panel starts lower again, and for Year 7 or Year 8 organisational and content support that is a genuine service rather than a compromise. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end.

Where paying up is justified in MYP is criteria coaching in the later years and the Personal Project, because both require somebody who has actually taught the programme and read the descriptors. Where it is rarely justified is routine Year 7 content support, which a competent tutor at a lower band handles perfectly well. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, which is the realistic range for most MYP arrangements.

In-home one to one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online, and the difference is a car journey into this corridor in the afternoon. None of these figures is an IB Gram rate; we publish no rate card on these pages, and the number for your child comes out of the free trial lesson and the conversation after it.
