sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside MYP
paragraphs: Whatever curriculum a Dubai private school is licensed for, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory, and KHDA's guidance states those requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For an MYP student that means a timetable fuller than the eight subject groups suggest, and a family budgeting tutoring hours needs to count the whole week rather than the IB part of it.

KHDA also sets rules about how those subjects are organised. Schools must arrange separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

There is a direct consequence for tutoring in these subjects. KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. Arabic and Islamic Education tutoring therefore works from the school's own approved material, and anybody offering a better or alternative syllabus for them is offering something the regulator does not permit.

One more checkable point worth knowing: schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate KHDA permission to teach those subjects. That applies to schools rather than to private tutors, and it is a useful question to ask your school. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA or the Ministry of Education and claims none; we explain what they require and link to their own pages.

sections.heading: Starting, and the honest conversation about whether to start at all
paragraphs: Send four things: the year group, the subject and its criterion marks rather than the overall grade, a photograph of a recent task sheet with its rubric, and the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. The rubric is the item that matters most, because in this programme the rubric is the lesson plan.

Sometimes the right advice is not to buy tutoring. For a Year 7 student whose problem is that nothing is written down and no deadline is remembered, three conversations about a notebook and a calendar will do more than a term of paid sessions, and we would rather say that than take the money. For a Year 8 student with a genuine content gap in one subject, a short block is the proportionate response rather than an ongoing arrangement.

Where tutoring clearly earns its place is criteria coaching in MYP years 3 to 5, Personal Project method, and the bridging block out of MYP into the Diploma or an IGCSE year. Those three have a visible deliverable and a defensible price, and a parent can judge whether they worked.

The free trial lesson runs forty minutes on your child's own task and rubric, with your child doing the work. Afterwards you receive a written read on which criterion is costing the marks and what the gap to the level above actually is. We ask only for what matching requires, and UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data we hold; the privacy link on this page explains what is kept and how to have it removed.

process.title: Ask the school for criterion marks
process.description: Not the overall 1 to 7 grade but the four criterion marks behind it. A profile of 6, 6, 5, 3 and one of 5, 5, 5, 5 can produce similar grades and need completely different work, and the lowest criterion is the brief.

process.title: Send a task sheet with its rubric
process.description: In MYP the rubric is the lesson plan. A photograph of a recent task with the descriptors on the back tells a specialist more than any report comment, because it shows exactly what the student was asked to do and what the marker was looking for.

process.title: Say the year group, not just the subject
process.description: A Year 7 student and a Year 11 student need different session lengths, different slots and different work. Forty minutes earlier with a parent in the house, or ninety minutes later on project method, are two different purchases.

process.title: Set the slot from the arrival home
process.description: Mirdif, Al Mizhar and Al Khawaneej bus routes put a middle-years student home late and tired. Younger students do better earlier and shorter; long-route families often do better on a weekend morning than on any weekday evening.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: Forty minutes on your child's own task and rubric. Ask the tutor what separates the 5 to 6 band from the 7 to 8 band in the weakest criterion. A specialist answers from the descriptor's own language; a generalist talks about deeper understanding.

process.title: Review after six sessions against criterion marks
process.description: The measure is the criterion mark on the next comparable task, not how the sessions felt. If the weak criterion has not moved we change the approach or the tutor, and if tutoring was the wrong answer we will say that too.

whyPoints.title: The criteria are taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Each MYP subject is marked out of eight against four published descriptors. We work from the descriptor for the level achieved and the one above it, in your child's own work, because that comparison is the highest-value activity in the programme and almost nobody shows a student how to do it.

whyPoints.title: Session length follows the age
whyPoints.description: Forty minutes for a Year 7 student off a long bus, sixty for Year 10, up to ninety for project work in the final year. A single default session length is wrong at one end of MYP or the other, and the shorter session is a judgement rather than a reduction.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you not to buy tutoring
whyPoints.description: For a Year 7 student whose real problem is a missing notebook and an unremembered deadline, three conversations beat a term of paid sessions. Saying so loses us bookings and is the honest answer more often than this market admits.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project is coached, never produced
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the criteria, questions the goal and responds to journal entries with questions. No part of the project or the report is written, drafted or completed by us. One page in this search result sells finished Internal Assessments; the student carries that risk alone.

whyPoints.title: Published rates, each attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here was read on the provider's own public page and credited to them, and none is an IB Gram price. We also say where the budget tiers are genuinely adequate for middle-years work, which is not a thing a seller usually volunteers.

faqs.question: What do the MYP criterion letters on my child's report actually mean?
faqs.answer: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each marked out of eight against published descriptors, and the four marks are converted into the 1 to 7 grade on the report using published boundaries. Criterion A is broadly knowledge; the other three measure what a student does with it, such as investigating, communicating and evaluating. That is why an uneven profile like 6, 6, 5, 3 can hide behind an ordinary-looking grade. Ask the school for the criterion marks, not just the grade, and work on the lowest one.

faqs.question: My child works hard and still gets a 4. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually the analysis or evaluation criterion rather than the content. A student who writes well-organised description can sit at a 4 indefinitely while a less fluent classmate who argues a point reaches a 6, because the descriptors reward what is done with the knowledge rather than how much there is. Telling that child to work harder makes it worse. The fix is reading the descriptor one band above the achieved mark, finding the difference in their own writing, and rewriting a single paragraph to show it.

faqs.question: How long should a tutoring session be for a Year 7 MYP student?
faqs.answer: Forty minutes, not sixty. A twelve year old off a forty-minute collecting bus from a Mirdif school has about that much productive attention in them, and the last twenty minutes of a longer session are spent being present rather than learning. Shorter also works better earlier in the evening, with a parent somewhere in the house. For a Year 11 student the opposite applies: a full hour, later, and sometimes ninety minutes when Personal Project work is underway.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring suitable for a child as young as eleven?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and sometimes not, and we will tell you which. What makes it work at that age is a short session and a visible task: forty minutes with the task sheet open and one paragraph to rewrite by the end holds attention. What does not work is an hour of general discussion, and the fault there is the format rather than the child. A child who genuinely will not engage with a screen is better served by somebody physically present, and IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes under any circumstances.

faqs.question: When does the Personal Project need to start?
faqs.answer: In the first term of the final MYP year, with the goal conversation first. The project is assessed against its own criteria with a process journal examined alongside the product, and the journal is where most marks are lost because students assemble it retrospectively instead of writing it as they go. Set the goal and the student's own success criteria early, keep weekly dated journal entries from that point, build across the middle of the year, and leave the final weeks for the report rather than the making.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary. A tutor may teach the criteria, question whether the goal is specific enough, respond to journal entries with questions and point out where a reflection is not supported by evidence. A tutor may not produce, write, draft or complete any part of the project or the report. The test for a parent is the feedback: questions your child must go and answer are correct, sentences they could paste in are not. One page in this search result sells completed Internal Assessments outright, and the student bears the consequence.

faqs.question: My child has lost two weeks of the project to a family trip. What now?
faqs.answer: Record the gap honestly and carry on. The process journal is evidence of thinking over time, and a dated gap with a short note explaining it costs far less than a retrospectively invented fortnight, which is both detectable and a serious academic-honesty problem. Households in this district travel often, which is the specific reason to start the project early: a lost fortnight in the first term is absorbed easily, while the same fortnight lost in the final weeks is not recoverable at all.

faqs.question: What is the hardest part of moving from MYP into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Timed papers. Five years of criteria-based tasks with a rubric and time to think do not prepare a student for an examination that rewards three precise sentences in four minutes, and a thoughtful student can lose marks badly on exactly the questions they understand best. The content gap is usually smaller than parents fear, with one exception: a student from the standard MYP mathematics route aiming at Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level has genuine algebraic fluency to build over a summer.

faqs.question: Should my child take extended or standard MYP mathematics?
faqs.answer: If a Higher Level Diploma mathematics course or an engineering route is a possibility, extended, and the decision is usually made in Year 9 on the school's evidence. Standard-route students can still reach a Diploma mathematics course, but the step to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level involves building symbolic fluency that the standard route does not drill. Ask the school which route your child is being placed in and what evidence that rests on, because this choice follows them into course selection two years later.

faqs.question: What is a fair hourly figure for middle-years help around the eastern suburbs?
faqs.answer: Published rates, each read on the provider's own page: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour online, Tutopiya's panel starts lower, Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase quotes AED 270, Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED publishes AED 650. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, which covers most MYP arrangements. None of those is an IB Gram price.

faqs.question: Do I need an expensive specialist for middle-years support?
faqs.answer: Often not, and this is where we differ from most sellers. For Year 7 or Year 8 content and organisational support, a competent tutor in the lower published bands handles it perfectly well. Paying up is justified for two things: criteria coaching in MYP years 3 to 5, which needs somebody who has read the descriptors and taught the programme, and Personal Project method. Spending specialist money on routine Year 8 homework help is a common and avoidable waste.

faqs.question: How many subjects does an MYP student actually study?
faqs.answer: Across eight subject groups: mathematics, sciences, individuals and societies, language and literature, language acquisition, arts, design, and physical and health education. In Dubai, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies also run alongside whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, which makes the week fuller than the eight groups suggest. That matters when a family is working out how many tutoring hours an eleven to sixteen year old can genuinely absorb after a long bus route home.

faqs.question: Can tutoring in Arabic follow a different syllabus from the school's?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA states that for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited, so Arabic and Islamic Education tutoring works from the school's own approved material. Anybody offering a better or alternative Arabic syllabus is offering something the regulator does not allow. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction are different.

faqs.question: What time should an MYP lesson start if we are on an Al Khawaneej route?
faqs.answer: On a weekday, later than you would like, and honestly a weekend morning is usually better. Al Khawaneej and Al Warqa routes are the longest in this corridor, and a middle-years student arriving home after half past four has very little left for a weekday evening session. A Saturday or Sunday morning gives a rested child and a full session, leaves weekday evenings for school homework, and is easier to protect through assessment weeks. The cost is a piece of the weekend.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first MYP session?
faqs.answer: Four things. The year group. The subject and its four criterion marks rather than the overall grade. A photograph of a recent task sheet with its rubric, which is the single most useful document because in this programme the rubric is the lesson plan. And the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history; UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs what is held.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.closingHeading: Start from the rubric, not from the report
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.closingBody: The quickest improvement available to an MYP student in Al Rashidiya costs nothing: ask the school for the four criterion marks instead of the grade, find the lowest, and read the published descriptor at that level and at the level above. The difference between those two paragraphs is what your child needs to do differently, and in most cases it is one nameable behaviour rather than a body of content. If you then want help, send us the year group, the criterion marks, a task sheet with its rubric and the time your child actually gets home, and take the free trial lesson. Sometimes the answer will be a short block, and sometimes it will be that tutoring is not what this needs.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-safa.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work in the Middle Years Programme specifically, which is a different job from Diploma teaching. They mark against criterion descriptors, write task-specific clarifications, and know what a level 7 in criterion C looks like compared with a level 5.

intro.heading: Why MYP reports confuse Al Safa parents more than any other curriculum
paragraphs: Search for an IB MYP tutor in Al Safa and most of what comes back is Diploma Programme marketing with the letters changed. That is a problem, because the Middle Years Programme does not work like the Diploma at all. There is no Paper 1, no subject grade out of 7 arrived at by percentage, and no points total. A student in MYP Year 3 at a school off Al Wasl Road is assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked on a scale of nought to eight, and those four marks are combined into a single figure out of 32 before any grade exists.

That structure is the reason a report card from an Al Safa school can read as a riddle. A parent sees Mathematics: A 6, B 4, C 7, D 5 and has no way to tell whether that is a strong term or a weak one. The criteria are not equally easy to move. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, responds quickly to practice on routine questions. Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where a student either builds a general rule and proves it or does not, and a child can sit at level 4 on that criterion for two years while criterion A climbs.

Al Safa sits in the middle of the densest stretch of international schooling in the emirate. Families here are inside ten minutes of several British-curriculum schools and a short drive from IB continuum schools running the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma end to end. The practical consequence is that a child can move between two schools in the same postcode and find the same MYP year taught with completely different task design, different interim objectives and a different reporting rhythm.

This page is written from the assessment side rather than the neighbourhood side. It sets out the eight subject groups and the criteria each one carries, how criterion levels convert into a grade, what the Year 5 on-screen eAssessment actually asks for, what the Personal Project requires a student to produce and document, and where a tutor is legitimately useful in each of those. It also publishes what MYP support costs in this market in dirhams, because almost nobody ranking for this search does.

Delivery is the part to be plain about. IB Gram teaches Al Safa students one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for working through a criterion B investigation or annotating a Language and Literature extract. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a subject-group specialist that trade is worth making, because the person who understands MYP Sciences criterion C processing and evaluating is not necessarily the person who lives nearest Al Safa Park.

The Personal Project is assessed on process and documentation, not polish

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-safa.programmesIntro: An Al Safa family usually arrives at the Middle Years Programme from a Primary Years Programme classroom or from a British Year 6, and leaves it for the Diploma or for IGCSE. Each of those joins has its own gap, and the tutoring work differs at each one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, assessed continuously against four criteria per group rather than by terminal examination. Students carry ATL skills, key and related concepts, a statement of inquiry per unit, and one of six global contexts. Service as action runs throughout, and Year 5 closes with the Personal Project. Most of the tutoring demand sits in Years 4 and 5, where criterion demands step up sharply and the first real consequences appear.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai runs the MYP in both continuum IB schools and in schools that bolt it onto another primary curriculum, so two Al Safa children in the same MYP year can be working to different interim objectives. KHDA inspects these schools annually on a six-band scale, and inspection reports name assessment quality explicitly, which is why task design varies so visibly between neighbouring campuses.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no formal grading structure, closing with the Exhibition. Children arrive in MYP Year 1 confident at inquiry and unused to being marked against descriptors. The first MYP report is often the first time a parent sees a number attached to their child's work, and the drop from PYP comment-based reporting to criterion levels reads as a decline when it is simply a different instrument.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Safa and Jumeirah schools run PYP and MYP on one campus, so the handover is internal and smoother. Children transferring in from a separate primary school, including from a British Year 6 nearby, hit MYP Year 1 criterion language cold and benefit most from four to six sessions spent purely on what the descriptors ask for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment flips to external examination with a single internal assessment per subject. A student who learned to write to criterion descriptors for five years now has to write to command terms and mark schemes instead, which is a genuine adjustment rather than a continuation.
programmes.countryNote: Al Safa families choosing the Diploma are usually weighing it against a British sixth form two streets away, so the MYP Year 5 decision is a real fork rather than a formality. MYP Mathematics extended is the honest prerequisite signal for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a Year 5 student on the standard route needs that conversation before the option sheet goes in.

programmes.name: IGCSE after MYP
programmes.description: Some Dubai schools run MYP to Year 3 and then move students into Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE for Years 10 and 11. That is a harder transition than MYP to DP, because IGCSE is syllabus-coded and examination-weighted, with content lists a student can tick off. MYP students arriving late into an IGCSE cohort typically need content gap-filling rather than skills work.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Safa this route matters because the neighbourhood's British-curriculum schools and its IB schools sit within the same few kilometres, and families move between them for reasons of fees, siblings or inspection outcome. A child moving from MYP Year 3 into Year 10 IGCSE Mathematics has not covered the same ground in the same order, and the gaps are predictable enough to map in a first session.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-safa.subjectsIntro: The Middle Years Programme does not have subjects in the way a British curriculum does. It has eight subject groups, and the criteria differ between them. Below is what each group assesses and where Al Safa students most often sit a level lower than their parents expect.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: MYP Years 1-5 · standard and extended from Year 4
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is the one that separates students: it requires selecting examples, describing a pattern, writing a general rule and then justifying or proving it. A student who stops at describing the pattern caps at a middle level however good the arithmetic is.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C is where most marks go missing, because it asks for interpretation of data against a hypothesis and an evaluation of method, not a tidy results table. Criterion D needs a genuine evaluation of science in a social context, with sources.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language. Students who read widely often score well on A and lose marks on B, because organizing is assessed on structure made visible to a reader rather than on having a plan in your head. Criterion D covers register and accuracy and responds fast to targeted work on sentence control.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, with the student placed in one of six phases rather than a year group. A phase mismatch is the single commonest cause of a disappointing Language Acquisition grade in Dubai, where Arabic, French and Spanish cohorts are mixed in ability. Assessment is by ePortfolio at Year 5 rather than on-screen examination.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.levels: MYP Years 1-5 · history, geography, economics strands
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D is where strong writers plateau: it rewards weighing interpretations and recognising bias in a source, not fluency. Year 5 sits an on-screen examination here, which means timed source analysis under conditions many students have never practised.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.levels: MYP Years 1-5 · digital and product design
subjects.description: Criteria A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The design cycle is the mark scheme, and students lose heavily by building first and documenting afterwards. A tutor's useful contribution here is process discipline: research with citations, a specification that can be tested, and a plan recorded before any making happens.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.levels: MYP Years 1-5 · visual arts, music, drama
subjects.description: Criteria A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. The process journal carries the marks, not the finished piece, and that surprises families who judge progress by what comes home. Assessed by ePortfolio in Year 5, so the evidence trail matters as much as the outcome.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting on and improving performance. Two of those four criteria are written, which routinely catches out athletic students who assume the subject is graded on the field. Criterion D demands evidence of a plan adjusted over time.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary learning
subjects.description: Assessed in its own right at Year 5 through an on-screen examination that asks a student to combine disciplinary grounding from two subject groups. There is no textbook for it, which is exactly why it is worth rehearsing. The skill is naming what each discipline contributes and then synthesising, rather than writing two half-answers side by side.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: A student-directed project with a goal, a process journal and a report, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. The product is not marked. What is marked is the evidence of process, which means the journal entries made in Year 5 term one decide the grade awarded in term three.

Everything below is within a short drive, and families move between these communities without changing schools. The notes are about timing and school access rather than property.

regions.note: The coastal strip west of Al Safa, with long-established schools and a mix of MYP and IGCSE cohorts. Afternoon traffic along Jumeirah Beach Road makes an in-home tutor's arrival time unreliable between 15:00 and 17:00.

regions.note: Apartment and waterfront communities with newer families, often arriving mid-year from another country's system. Entering MYP Year 3 or 4 part-way through means missing the unit that set up the criterion expectations.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP tutor in Al Safa actually works on
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in Al Safa works on criterion descriptors first and content second. That ordering is not a style preference. In the Middle Years Programme the descriptor is the mark scheme, it is published, and most students have never read theirs. A Year 4 student who can be shown the difference between the level 5 and level 7 wording of Mathematics criterion B has been handed the single most useful piece of information available to them, and it takes one session.

The second thing a tutor works on is the school's own task-specific clarification. Schools are expected to rewrite the generic descriptors for each task so that the wording matches what is actually being assessed. Those clarifications are issued with the task sheet and then usually ignored. Reading them against the generic descriptor shows a student exactly which strand of a criterion the task is testing, and that is where a level moves from 5 to 7 without any new content being learned.

Content work does happen, and in Mathematics and Sciences it is substantial. But the content gap is rarely what the report card is complaining about. A student sitting at level 4 across criterion C in Sciences is not short of knowledge about photosynthesis; they are presenting data without interpreting it against the hypothesis. Naming that precisely, in one subject group at a time, is the work. Al Safa families who book a tutor expecting general homework supervision get less from the arrangement than families who arrive with the last report card and ask which criterion to attack.
bullets: Generic descriptor and school clarification read side by side
One criterion targeted per half-term, not four at once
The last report card used as the diagnostic, not a placement test
Content taught where it blocks a criterion, not as a syllabus sweep

sections.heading: The eight subject groups and the four criteria each one carries
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group has exactly four assessment criteria, labelled A to D, each marked on a scale from nought to eight. The labels are not interchangeable between groups. Criterion C means communicating in Mathematics and Individuals and Societies, producing text in Language and Literature, processing and evaluating in Sciences, and creating the solution in Design. A parent who assumes criterion C is the same thing across a report card will misread it.

The table below sets out all four criteria for each group. It is worth keeping beside the next report, because the pattern across a row usually says more than any single number. A student strong on A and weak on B in Mathematics has a reasoning problem. A student strong on A and weak on D in Sciences has a reading-and-sourcing problem. Those two children need entirely different tutoring and would be given the same thing by a general maths tutor.

Note that two of the four criteria in Physical and Health Education are written rather than practical, and that in Arts the process journal carries criteria A, B and D. Those are the two groups where Al Safa parents are most often surprised by a grade, because the visible output and the assessed output are different things. In both cases the fix is documentation discipline rather than more practice. Language Acquisition is the other outlier: its four criteria are the four language skills, and the student is placed in one of six phases rather than in a year group, so a capable child in too high a phase will score below a weaker child placed correctly. Checking the phase is the first thing to do before booking any Language Acquisition support, and the school will confirm it on request.

sections.heading: How four criterion levels become one grade from 1 to 7
paragraphs: The conversion is arithmetic, then a boundary table. Each of the four criteria is marked out of eight, giving a maximum of 32 for the subject. That total is then read against a boundary table published by the IB to produce the familiar grade from 1 to 7. The important consequence is that the four criteria carry equal weight, so a single weak criterion costs the same as any other and is worth attacking on its own.

Levels are awarded on best fit, not by adding up marks for correct answers. A teacher reads the work against the descriptor and decides which band it sits in overall. This is why two pieces of work with the same number of errors can receive different levels, and why a student who writes less but structures the response to the descriptor often scores higher than one who writes more. It also means a student can rehearse the descriptor language and improve without learning any new mathematics.

Schools in Dubai differ in how often they report criterion levels and whether they report a best single level, a most recent level or an average across the term. Ask the Al Safa school which convention it uses, because it changes what a mid-year report means. Under a most-recent convention, one weak assessment late in the term can drag a grade that a best-fit-across-the-term convention would have left alone, and that is a scheduling question for tutoring rather than a teaching one.
bullets: Four criteria, each 0-8, totalling 32 before any grade is calculated
Equal weighting means the weakest criterion is the cheapest to improve
Best fit, not mark accumulation, so descriptor language carries weight
Ask the school whether it reports latest, best or averaged levels

sections.heading: MYP Mathematics: standard and extended, and the criterion B problem
paragraphs: From MYP Year 4 most Dubai schools split Mathematics into standard and extended. Extended covers additional content and is the honest route towards Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the Diploma. Standard is a complete course in its own right and feeds Applications and Interpretation comfortably. The decision is usually made at the end of Year 3, on evidence that is thinner than parents assume, and it is reversible with effort if it is addressed early in Year 4 rather than in Year 5.

Criterion B is where the real marks are, and it is the part no textbook drills. The task asks a student to select examples, find a pattern, express it as a general rule in correct notation, and then verify or justify that rule. Four distinct actions, each with its own descriptor band. In practice Al Safa students in Years 3 to 5 reliably complete the first two and stop. The written general rule arrives without notation, and the justification is missing entirely, so the level caps regardless of how elegant the pattern-spotting was.

Criterion D is the second recurring loss. It asks for mathematics applied to a real-life context, including identifying the relevant elements of an authentic situation, selecting a strategy, applying it and then explaining the degree of accuracy of the solution. That final strand, commenting on accuracy and on the validity of the model, is skipped by almost everyone. It is also the fastest two levels available in the whole subject, because it is a habit rather than a skill.

sections.heading: MYP Year 5 eAssessment and the Personal Project
paragraphs: Where a school offers them, MYP Year 5 ends in externally validated eAssessment rather than in school-set tests. Five areas are examined on screen: Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, and interdisciplinary learning. Four are evidenced by moderated ePortfolio instead: Language Acquisition, Arts, Design, and Physical and Health Education. The Personal Project is submitted and moderated separately. Not every Dubai school takes the full set, so the first question for an Al Safa family is which components their school actually enters.

The on-screen format is its own obstacle. Stimulus material and the answer box share a screen, there is no margin to annotate, and students who have revised on paper for five years discover this in the examination. Rehearsing the format from the start of Year 5 is worth more than extra content revision in the final month. The interdisciplinary paper deserves separate practice again, because it rewards naming what each discipline contributes before synthesising, and students who have never been asked to do that produce two unconnected half-answers.

The Personal Project is assessed on process, and that is the single most useful sentence a Year 5 parent can hear. The product is not marked. The marks come from the goal and its success criteria, the evidence of skills applied, and the quality of reflection, all documented in the process journal and summarised in the report. Journal entries written in term one determine what can be claimed in term three, which is why coaching that starts in March achieves far less than coaching that starts in September.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs in Al Safa, and who charges what
paragraphs: Start from the monthly figure, because that is the number an Al Safa household actually budgets against. A single weekly hour of mid-tier support works out at roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates, with budget provision landing nearer AED 240 to AED 600 and specialist exam-year support running from AED 1,000 to beyond AED 2,000. Those monthly bands are the useful anchor; the hourly rate is the derived figure, not the other way round.

Working back to the hour, the published market splits into recognisable tiers. University-student and budget online provision advertises from AED 45 to AED 150, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to AED 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, run AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to AED 350. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The gap between the online tier and the in-home tier is the travel premium, and in Al Safa it buys very little. The neighbourhood is small and well connected, so a tutor loses less time reaching it than they would reaching an outer community; what the premium actually pays for is the tutor's unbillable hour in traffic along Al Wasl Road between 15:00 and 17:00, and a selection pool restricted to whoever is willing to make that journey. Every figure above is a market rate published by the named provider, not an IB Gram price. Our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and the quote follows the subject group and the year.

sections.heading: From MYP Year 5 into the Diploma Programme
paragraphs: The MYP to DP transition is the most under-prepared moment in the whole programme, and it is invisible until October of DP Year 1. For five years a student has written to descriptors that reward process, structure and reflection. The Diploma rewards none of those directly. It rewards command terms answered precisely, within a mark scheme, under time pressure, with a single internal assessment per subject instead of continuous criterion-based tasks.

Mathematics is where the mismatch bites hardest. A student who took MYP Mathematics standard and then chooses Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is making a jump that is possible but needs bridging work over the summer, specifically on algebraic fluency and on proof. The same student taking Applications and Interpretation at Standard or Higher Level is well served by the standard route. Sciences present a different gap: MYP criterion C has trained data handling and evaluation well, which is a genuine advantage in the Diploma internal assessment, while the volume of recall content required for Paper 1 is new.

Al Safa families also face a real alternative, because British sixth forms sit within the same few kilometres as the IB continuum schools. A student who thrives on criterion-based, documented, process-heavy work usually does better in the Diploma. A student who has spent five years finding the documentation requirements of Design and Arts exhausting may genuinely prefer three A Levels. That is a fit question rather than a prestige question, and it is better asked in Year 5 term one than after the option sheet has gone in.
bullets: MYP Mathematics extended is the honest prerequisite signal for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level
Command terms and mark schemes replace criterion descriptors from DP Year 1
MYP criterion C work transfers well into Diploma internal assessment
Paper 1 recall volume is the genuinely new demand after the MYP

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed to deliver, and KHDA's published guidelines set out how. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. For an Al Safa MYP family that means a timetable carrying mandatory subjects alongside eight subject groups, which is a workload question nobody raises at open day.

The organisational rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group, stating that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

Two further details matter for planning. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which constrains how any tutoring in them can honestly be described. Support here means helping a student with the school's own set material, not supplying a parallel course.
bullets: Mandatory subjects run alongside the MYP in every Dubai private school
Separate Arab and non-Arab classes are required, not optional

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme has a lower public profile than the Diploma, and that leads families to assume the academic-honesty rules are softer. They are not. The Personal Project is externally moderated, ePortfolios are moderated, and work that is not the student's own is a malpractice matter with consequences that follow the student into the Diploma. A tutor who offers to produce a project report, a Design folio or an Arts process journal is offering the student a risk, not a service.

The boundary is easier to hold than it sounds. A tutor may teach the content, explain the descriptor, ask questions about a draft the student has written, point at a paragraph that does not do what the student thinks it does, and model the same skill on a different example. A tutor may not supply sentences for the student to use, restructure a report into its final shape, or add the citations the student did not find. On the Personal Project specifically, the supervisor at school is the person who signs off process, and a private tutor's involvement should be declarable without anybody being uncomfortable.

This is also where the essay mills in this market expose families. Pages in this niche advertise completed Internal Assessments for a fee, which is an integrity breach that the IB treats seriously and which no amount of care afterwards undoes. The honest version of tutoring is slower and less comfortable: the student writes badly first, gets asked why, and writes again. That is also the only version that produces a student who can sit a Diploma internal assessment two years later without the same help.
bullets: The Personal Project and ePortfolios are externally moderated
A tutor teaches, questions and models; the student writes
Supervisor sign-off at school assumes the work is the student's own
Declarable involvement is the test to apply to any arrangement

process.title: Send the last report card
process.description: Not a wish list and not a placement test. The criterion levels on the most recent MYP report tell us which of the four criteria in which subject group is costing the grade, and that is the whole diagnostic. Al Safa parents who do this get a focused first session instead of a general assessment hour.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a subject-group specialist
process.description: Sixty minutes with a tutor who teaches that subject group, not a generalist. The student brings a recent assessed task and its task-specific clarification. By the end of the hour you have a named criterion to work on and an honest view of whether the match is right.

process.title: Agree one criterion for the half-term
process.description: One criterion, one subject group, one half-term. Spreading across four criteria produces movement nowhere. The plan names what the student will be able to do differently and what evidence will show it, so the next report is readable as progress rather than as noise.

process.title: Weekly sessions against the school's unit plan
process.description: Sessions follow what the school is actually teaching, using the task sheets and clarifications the school issues. Each session closes with a written note naming the criterion worked on and what the student should attempt before the next one. Parents receive that note.

process.title: Review at the next report
process.description: The criterion levels either moved or they did not, and both outcomes are useful. If they moved, the focus shifts to the next weakest criterion. If they did not, the diagnosis was wrong or the tutor is not the right fit, and we change one of those rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: Subject-group specialists, not general tutors
whyPoints.description: MYP Sciences criterion C and MYP Mathematics criterion B are different jobs requiring different people. We match on the subject group and the MYP year rather than on who is available, which is the whole reason online delivery is worth the trade for an Al Safa family.

whyPoints.title: Descriptors read, not summarised
whyPoints.description: Students are shown the actual wording of the level bands for the criterion being worked on, alongside their school's task-specific clarification. Most arrive having never seen either document. Reading them is free and moves levels faster than any amount of additional content.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, honestly described
whyPoints.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Saying so plainly is more useful to an Al Safa parent than a promise that would have to be broken at booking.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, our own quoted after a trial
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are published market rates attributed to the providers who publish them, so you can see where any quote sits. Our own arrangement follows a free trial lesson and a consultation, because the right answer depends on the subject group and the year.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach, question and give feedback on what the student has written. We do not produce Personal Project reports, Design folios or Arts process journals. That line is a feature of the service rather than a limitation of it, and it is the line a moderator assumes exists.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the Al Safa school day
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the actual end of the school day and the actual traffic on Al Wasl Road, with later slots available for students carrying heavy after-school commitments along the Jumeirah strip.

faqs.question: What does an IB MYP tutor in Al Safa actually do differently from a normal tutor?
faqs.answer: The work starts from the assessment criteria rather than the topic. In the Middle Years Programme your child is marked nought to eight on four named criteria per subject group, and the descriptors for those levels are published. An MYP tutor reads them with the student, alongside the school's own task-specific clarification, and identifies which criterion is costing the grade. Content is then taught where it blocks that criterion. A general subject tutor teaches the topic and leaves the criterion untouched, which is why a report card can stay flat after a term of competent homework help.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report shows A 6, B 4, C 7, D 5 in Mathematics. What should I read into that?
faqs.answer: That pattern is a reasoning gap rather than a knowledge gap. Criterion A at 6 says routine content is largely secure. Criterion B at 4 says the investigation work stops at describing a pattern without generalising it into a rule in correct notation and then justifying it. Criterion D at 5 usually means the real-life application was completed but the accuracy and validity of the answer were never discussed. All four criteria carry equal weight towards the total out of 32, so criterion B is the cheapest place to gain, and it is a technique rather than new mathematics.

faqs.question: Should my child take MYP Mathematics standard or extended in Year 4?
faqs.answer: Extended covers additional content and is the honest signal for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the Diploma. Standard is a complete course and feeds Applications and Interpretation comfortably at either level. The decision is usually taken at the end of Year 3 on limited evidence, and it is reversible with bridging work if it is addressed early in Year 4. If your child is secure on criterion A and struggling on criterion B, extended will be hard work rather than impossible; if criterion A is also unsteady, standard is the better base.

faqs.question: What is the MYP Personal Project marked on, and can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: It is marked on process, not product. The assessment covers the goal and its success criteria, the evidence of skills applied, and the quality of reflection, all documented in a process journal and summarised in a report. The finished object is not graded. A tutor can ask the questions a moderator would ask, test whether a goal is specific enough to be assessed, and review journal entries for evidence of decisions. A tutor must not draft the report or supply the journal content, because the project is externally moderated and the work must be the student's own.

faqs.question: How does the MYP eAssessment at Year 5 work?
faqs.answer: Where a school enters students for it, five areas are examined on screen: Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics and interdisciplinary learning. Four more are evidenced by moderated ePortfolio: Language Acquisition, Arts, Design, and Physical and Health Education. The Personal Project is moderated separately. The on-screen format is its own hurdle, because stimulus material and the answer box share one display and there is no paper to annotate. Ask your Al Safa school which components it actually enters, because provision varies between campuses in the same neighbourhood.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our villa in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Lessons for Al Safa students are delivered one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, timed to Gulf Standard Time and to the end of the local school day. For the Middle Years Programme that trade is usually favourable, because the constraint is finding someone who teaches your child's specific subject group rather than someone who lives nearby. In-home provision in this market also carries a travel premium of roughly AED 30 to AED 200 an hour over comparable online rates.

faqs.question: How much does MYP tutoring cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: On Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates, one weekly hour runs about AED 240 to AED 600 a month at budget level, AED 600 to AED 1,200 at mid level, and AED 1,000 to beyond AED 2,000 for specialist examination-year support. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures published by the providers named, not IB Gram prices. Our own quote follows a free trial lesson and depends on the subject group and the MYP year.

faqs.question: Why do two Al Safa schools teach the same MYP year so differently?
faqs.answer: Because the Middle Years Programme prescribes the criteria and the objectives, not the units. Schools design their own units, choose their own contexts and write their own task-specific clarifications, so two campuses a few streets apart can assess the same criterion through entirely different tasks on different timetables. KHDA inspects these schools annually and comments on assessment quality, which is one reason task design varies visibly. For a tutor it means working from your school's actual task sheet rather than from a generic MYP scheme of work.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion is hardest to improve?
faqs.answer: Criterion B in Mathematics and criterion D in Sciences are the two that sit still longest. Mathematics criterion B requires four distinct actions, and students reliably complete the first two and stop, so the level caps no matter how much arithmetic practice follows. Sciences criterion D asks for a reasoned evaluation of science in a social context with sources, which is a reading and writing task inside a science grade. Both respond to technique rather than to content, which means progress is possible in a half-term, but it has to be deliberate and separately practised.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start MYP tutoring in the middle of Year 5?
faqs.answer: For on-screen examination preparation, no, and format rehearsal is still the highest-value use of the time. For the Personal Project, starting late limits what is achievable, because the marks come from a process journal kept across the year and entries cannot honestly be backfilled. If you are mid-Year 5 with the project already running, the useful work is making the remaining reflection and the report structure do their job properly. If you are choosing when to begin, term one of Year 5 is worth far more than term three.

faqs.question: Do your tutors need a UAE permit to teach my child privately?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and MoHRE does not publish a fine schedule. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service through its app, website and e-services system.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover several MYP subject groups for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is usually a poor idea. The criteria differ between groups, so competence in Mathematics criterion B says nothing about Sciences criterion C or Language and Literature criterion B. Where a student needs two subject groups, two specialists working on one agreed criterion each produce more movement than one tutor spreading across both. The exception is a student whose problem is the same in every subject, typically structure and documentation rather than content, where a single tutor working on criterion C writing habits can lift several grades at once.

faqs.question: What time can an MYP session realistically start for an Al Safa family?
faqs.answer: Most schools in and around Al Safa finish between 14:30 and 15:30, and because the neighbourhood's campuses are close, a child is usually home within half an hour. A 16:00 start works on a weekday without a rushed handover, and online delivery removes the second journey of the day that an in-centre arrangement would add. Families along the Jumeirah strip with heavy after-school sport more often take an 18:30 slot or a weekend morning. Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time against the actual school finish, not a nominal one.

faqs.question: Does the MYP prepare a child better for the Diploma than IGCSE does?
faqs.answer: For different things, yes. Five years of criterion-based work builds research, data handling, documentation and reflection habits that transfer directly into Diploma internal assessments, where IGCSE students often start from scratch. What the MYP does not build is recall volume under timed examination conditions, which is exactly what Diploma Paper 1 requires. IGCSE students arrive with that and without the process habits. Neither route is a prerequisite for the Diploma, and the sensible question for an Al Safa family is which demands suit the child rather than which looks stronger.

faqs.question: What do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies mean for an MYP timetable?
faqs.answer: They are mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever international curriculum it is licensed to deliver, so they sit alongside the eight MYP subject groups rather than replacing any of them. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and sets the language of instruction for each group. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For these subjects no additional or different content may be used without prior Ministry of Education permission, so support means working with the school's own set material.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-safa.closingHeading: Start with the criterion, not the hour count
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-safa.closingBody: If you have an MYP report card from an Al Safa school in front of you, the useful next step is not booking a block of hours. It is identifying which of the four criteria in which subject group is holding the grade down, and that is a twenty-minute conversation. Send the report, take a free trial lesson with a tutor who teaches that subject group, and leave the hour with one named criterion to attack and an honest view of whether the match works. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. If no specialist in that subject group is free at the time you need, we will say so rather than offer a generalist.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-satwa.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors an MYP enquiry from Al Satwa is matched against: teachers who work from the criterion descriptors your child's school actually uses, rather than from a generic Year 9 syllabus. You see who is proposed before anything is booked.

intro.heading: The money question nobody answers about MYP tutoring
paragraphs: Middle-years tutoring is the least transparent purchase in Dubai education. Diploma tuition at least has a visible market: parents compare rates, specialists advertise levels, and the exam at the end makes the value argument for itself. The Middle Years Programme has no external examination for most students, no grade boundaries a parent can read, and a report card written in criterion language that means very little to anyone who did not study the system. So families buy hours without a price anchor and without a definition of success, and a surprising amount of that money achieves nothing.

Al Satwa makes this sharper than it needs to be. The neighbourhood sits between Sheikh Zayed Road and the Jumeirah coast - dense, low-rise, mostly apartments, close to Al Jafiliya metro - and it contains almost no international private school inside its own boundary. MYP children living here travel out daily to continuum schools in Jumeirah, Al Safa, Umm Suqeim or the Al Barsha cluster. That journey has a direct effect on the cost of tuition, because every in-home quote an Al Satwa family receives has somebody's drive across central Dubai priced into the hour.

Start with the market, because the numbers are knowable even though nobody publishes them together. At the bottom, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33-52, which buys a capable recent graduate. In the middle, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which is where a trained subject teacher sits. Specialists are quoted AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table running 200-450+. In-home visits are quoted AED 180-500 because travel is inside the rate. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for budget weekly sessions, AED 600-1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000-2,000+ for specialist exam-year work.

Now the part that decides whether any of that is well spent. The MYP marks eight subject groups against four criteria each, labelled A to D, every criterion scored on a published 0-8 band descriptor. A student who knows the content cold can still land a 4 on Criterion C in sciences for presenting data without uncertainties, or a 3 on Criterion B in individuals and societies for an investigation with no clear action plan. That is a format problem, not a knowledge problem, and it is invisible to a tutor who has never read an MYP descriptor. Paying AED 200 an hour for generic Year 9 revision when the lost marks are in Criterion D is the single most common waste in this market.

So this page is organised as a budget rather than a brochure. It gives you the rate bands with their sources, the criteria your money should be buying an understanding of, the four specific places MYP spending goes wrong in Dubai, and the honest comparison between online delivery and an in-home visit from an Al Satwa address. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India - and lessons here are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

No price for IB Gram's own hours appears on this page. A figure typed into a landing page goes stale and tells you nothing about your child's actual subject, year and deadline. The free trial lesson and the conversation after it are where a real number is given.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-satwa.programmesIntro: An MYP enquiry from Al Satwa sits inside a continuum, and where your child is in that continuum changes what an hour is worth. These are the four stages, costed in terms of what support actually does at each one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria scored 0-8 against published band descriptors. Sciences use Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science; mathematics uses Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. There is no external examination for most students, though MYP Year 5 candidates may sit eAssessment for the MYP certificate.
programmes.countryNote: This is the programme in question, and in Dubai it runs alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons. For an Al Satwa family the practical effect is a fuller week than the subject list implies, which is an argument for buying one well-targeted hour rather than three vague ones.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external assessment, no marks, and reporting against conceptual understanding and learner-profile attributes. Support at this stage is cheap in relative terms and disproportionately effective, because what it buys is reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud. Those three things are exactly what the MYP criteria will later demand in written form.
programmes.countryNote: Al Satwa families often arrive in the PYP from a different system mid-year, since central Dubai absorbs new residents constantly. The gap that shows is rarely content. It is the expectation that a child can justify an answer, which is also the cheapest thing to fix before the MYP starts marking it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across Higher and Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, with external papers taking the rest. This is where tuition becomes genuinely expensive in Dubai, because specialist Higher Level teaching is scarce and priced accordingly.
programmes.countryNote: The reason MYP spending matters is the Diploma it leads into. Money spent in MYP Years 4 and 5 on investigation design, data handling and written justification reduces what has to be spent in Year 12, when the market rate for a Higher Level specialist is two to three times a middle-years rate.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and language development. Offered by a small number of UAE schools and frequently confused with the Diploma by families comparing post-16 options on cost and workload.
programmes.countryNote: Worth knowing about at the MYP stage because it changes the arithmetic of what to invest in now. A CP certificate is not the Diploma, and if a UAE federal university is the intended destination, the Ministry of Education equivalency route should be checked directly with the authority before any long-term tutoring plan is built.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-satwa.subjectsIntro: MYP subject groups look familiar and are assessed unfamiliarly. For each one below, the thing worth paying for is the criterion, not the content - because the content is already being taught at school.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Marks go missing in investigating patterns, where students find a rule but never generalise or justify it, and in communicating, where correct working is presented without the notation or structure the descriptor wants.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.levels: Integrated, then Biology, Chemistry and Physics
subjects.description: Inquiring and designing is the expensive criterion: a method with no controlled variables identified caps the band regardless of how well the experiment ran. Processing and evaluating needs uncertainties, anomalies addressed and a limitation that is specific rather than ritual. These are teachable in a handful of hours.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: History, geography and economics content assessed against investigating, knowing and understanding, communicating, and thinking critically. Students lose marks by describing a source rather than evaluating its origin, purpose and limitations, and by writing conclusions the evidence they gathered does not support.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. The common and costly habit is retelling the plot where the descriptor asks for analysis of the writer's choices. Criterion C rewards voice and purpose in creative response, which is often the easiest band for a student to move up quickly.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Assessed by phase rather than year, which confuses parents comparing children. Listening, reading, speaking and writing each carry a criterion, and the phase descriptors assume register and text-type awareness. A strong speaker in a low phase can plateau because the writing conventions were never taught explicitly.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The design cycle is the subject, and the most frequent loss is an evaluation that reports whether the product worked rather than testing it against the specification the student wrote. Portfolio presentation carries real marks.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, responding. The process journal is assessed, not just the final piece, and students who produce strong work with a thin journal lose a criterion. This is the subject where parents most often misjudge where the marks are.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Four criteria including planning for performance and reflecting and improving performance, both of which are written. A physically capable student can score mid-band because the written planning and reflection components were treated as paperwork rather than as half the assessment.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project with a process journal and a report, assessed against planning, applying skills and reflecting. It must be the student's own work. A tutor's legitimate role is interrogating the goal, teaching the research skills and explaining the criteria - never producing the artefact or writing the report.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Dubai students often carry Arabic as an MYP language acquisition course and as a KHDA-mandated school subject with different content and expectations. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs and sets the language of instruction for each, and additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum. Standard Arabic is the required language of instruction for Arab students, the school's curriculum language for non-Arabs, and all teachers of the subject must hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach it.

subjects.name: MYP eAssessment preparation
subjects.description: On-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the MYP certificate, taken by some schools and not others. If your school offers it, the format is unfamiliar and worth a short, scoped block of preparation. If it does not, paying for eAssessment practice is money spent on an exam your child will never sit.

regions.name: Al Bada'a

regions.name: Jumeirah 1 and 2
regions.note: Villa territory along the coast with several of the continuum schools Al Satwa MYP children attend. Ten to twenty minutes outside peak, considerably more at pick-up time.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, with established campuses and a heavy afternoon load at the Al Safa interchange. Families here face the same evening timing squeeze as Al Satwa's.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Coastal and school-dense, a realistic 20-30 minute term-time afternoon journey from Al Satwa. The further the campus, the later a weekday session can honestly start.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs in Dubai, read as a monthly budget
paragraphs: Hourly rates mislead at this stage, because MYP support is rarely a long campaign. Read the market monthly instead. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget tutoring at AED 240-600 a month, mid-range at AED 600-1,200, and specialist exam-year work at AED 1,000-2,000 and above. For a Year 8 or Year 9 student that middle band is usually the realistic planning figure, and it buys roughly four sessions a month with a trained subject teacher.

Underneath that sit the hourly bands, which matter when you are comparing quotes. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33-52; a qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; named specialists run AED 200-450 and beyond, TutorChase at AED 270. Package pricing seen in the Dubai market runs about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

That last comparison is the one to sit with. Half the contact days for roughly twice the monthly outlay is not a premium for better teaching - it is the cost of a car. For a middle-years student, frequency matters more than session length, because criterion technique is built by doing a task, having it marked and doing the next one. Two one-hour sessions a week beat one two-hour session almost every time at this age, and the online package delivers the frequency the in-home package cannot at the same spend.

One piece of context belongs in any Dubai family's budget conversation. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A fee freeze does not make tutoring cheaper, but it does mean a tutoring decision this year is being taken against a stable school bill rather than a rising one.

sections.heading: The four criteria your money should be buying
paragraphs: Here is the single most useful thing a parent paying for MYP support can understand. Every MYP subject is marked against four criteria, each scored 0-8 against a published band descriptor, and the four are not interchangeable. A report showing 7, 7, 4, 6 is not a student who needs general help in that subject. It is a student with a specific, named, documented weakness in one criterion, and the hours should go there.

The criteria are also not equally expensive to move. Knowing and understanding usually responds to content work, which is the cheapest and most widely available teaching there is. The investigation and evaluation criteria respond to technique - method design, controlled variables, uncertainty, limitations - which takes a handful of focused hours and then holds for years. Communication criteria are the slowest, because they track writing development that no amount of paid tuition accelerates past a certain point. Knowing which column you are in determines whether four hours or forty is the honest answer.

This is where most wasted money goes. A family sees a weak subject grade, buys twenty hours of general tutoring in that subject, and gets content revision for a student whose content was never the problem. The marks were lost in Criterion C, and nobody read the descriptor. A tutor who has worked with MYP descriptors asks for the marked task sheet before the first lesson, because the task sheet carries the criterion and the band, and the band carries the diagnosis.

sections.heading: Four places Al Satwa families waste MYP money
paragraphs: The first is paying for content when the loss is format. It is worth repeating because it accounts for more wasted spend than everything else combined. Twenty hours of Year 9 science revision will not move a Criterion B band, because Criterion B is about designing an investigation and no amount of recall practice touches it. Ask for the marked task, find the criterion, buy the technique.

The second is paying a travel premium for a service where travel adds nothing. In-home rates in Dubai are quoted at AED 180-500 an hour, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. From Al Satwa, with its narrow streets and limited visitor parking, a tutor is driving in from the Al Barsha or Jumeirah clusters through late-afternoon traffic. For a thirteen-year-old working on a lab report on screen, the physical presence buys supervision. If supervision is what you need, it is worth paying for. If criterion technique is what you need, you are paying a driver.

The third is buying length instead of frequency. Two-hour sessions look efficient and are usually a false economy at middle-years age, where attention and retention both fall away after about an hour. The published package comparison makes the trade visible: roughly eight online sessions a month against four two-hour in-home visits for more money. Eight contacts produce eight cycles of task, feedback and next task. Four produce four.

The fourth is spending on things that do not exist at this stage. There are no MYP grade boundaries to coach to, there is no external examination for most students, and if your school does not run MYP Year 5 eAssessment then preparation for it is money spent on an exam your child will never sit. Equally, a tutor offering to produce a Personal Project is selling you an academic-honesty problem rather than a service. Ask what the school actually assesses before you buy anything aimed at it.
