sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys from an Al Satwa address
paragraphs: The in-home premium is not opportunism. It is the only honest way to price an hour of teaching that takes a tutor two and a half hours to deliver. From Al Satwa the geography is specific: the tutor is coming from Al Barsha, Jumeirah or Umm Suqeim along Al Wasl Road or Sheikh Zayed Road in the late afternoon, finding visitor parking in a dense low-rise grid, and then reversing the journey. The teaching is unchanged. The cost of producing it has roughly doubled.

What that premium buys is real and should be stated fairly. A person in the room can stop a twelve-year-old drifting, can see a reluctant student's body language, and can hold a household's attention in a way a screen sometimes cannot. For younger MYP students, or in a home where the laptop is also the distraction, that is worth money. Families who choose in-home tuition for those reasons are not making a mistake, and the Dubai market has plenty of providers who deliver it.

What the premium does not buy is specialism. Travel time forces generalism: nobody can specialise in MYP sciences criterion coaching and fill a week from the households within twenty minutes of their own flat. The economics convert specialists into generalists, which is why in-home listings in central Dubai tend to advertise every subject from Year 2 to Year 13. It also introduces failure modes that have nothing to do with teaching - a late start that is not refunded, a cancelled week with no substitute inside the radius, a school event that moves everything.

IB Gram is not an in-home provider in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and lessons for an Al Satwa family are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The table sets out the trade honestly, including the cases where the in-home option genuinely wins.

sections.heading: Spending now to avoid spending later: the MYP to Diploma gap
paragraphs: The strongest financial case for MYP support has nothing to do with MYP reports. It is that Diploma tuition in Dubai is two to three times the price, and much of what Year 12 students pay specialists to fix is work that should have been built in MYP Years 4 and 5. A specialist Higher Level teacher is quoted AED 200-450 an hour and above. A middle-years subject teacher is AED 150-300. Building a skill at the cheaper rate, two years early, is the clearest arbitrage available in this market.

The specific skills are known, because the same gaps appear every year. Uncertainty and error treatment in science practicals: the MYP introduces it, the Diploma Internal Assessment assumes it, and students who never learned it lose a whole criterion in Year 12. Generalising and justifying a mathematical pattern: the MYP calls it investigating patterns, the Diploma calls it the exploration, and it is the same skill. Extended written justification against a command term. Independent research with a narrow enough question. A process journal habit.

None of those are content. All of them are teachable in the MYP at a middle-years rate, and all of them are expensive to retrofit in the Diploma when the clock is running towards the May session. The practical advice for an Al Satwa family in MYP Year 4 or 5 is to spend on technique now rather than on content, because content will be taught again in Year 12 anyway and technique will not.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and why it is also a money question
paragraphs: The MYP Personal Project and every MYP assessment task must be the student's own work. That is an integrity rule, and for a parent paying for support it is also a spending rule, because the most expensive mistake available in this market is buying work rather than teaching. The consequence of a malpractice finding lands on the student, not on the provider who sold the service.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. They can explain what a criterion descriptor means in plain language. They can interrogate a Personal Project goal until the student can state it in one sentence and defend it. They can teach a research method, a data-handling technique or an essay structure. They can mark practice work, explain why a response that reads well lands mid-band, and set another one. They can read a draft the student wrote and respond with questions and comments on it.

What a tutor may not do is produce anything that goes into the submission. Not writing a section. Not rewriting a paragraph to demonstrate how it should sound. Not supplying data, a research question or an artefact. Not editing a draft to completion. In the Diploma market one provider advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the same logic and the same risk apply at MYP level to a Personal Project report.

A simple test for a parent with no IB background: could your child explain every decision in the document unprompted, to a teacher who asks why? If yes, the money bought teaching. If any part of it would have to be looked up, it bought a problem. Ask any tutor to state their own boundary before the first lesson, and treat a vague answer as the warning it is.

sections.heading: Checking the tutor is permitted, before you pay anything
paragraphs: This costs nothing and takes one question. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you by anybody - including by a tutor trying to justify a rate.

The eligible categories are deliberately broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Because it is free and fast, a tutor without one has chosen not to have one.

There is a related rule that matters for a very common Dubai arrangement. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported and should be verified against the current policy document, but the direction is clear: your child's own classroom teacher, paid privately, is the arrangement to decline however kindly it is offered.

Two further points on cost. A premises-based tuition centre in Dubai operates under a KHDA Educational Services Permit, a different licence with initial approval, a maximum six months to complete the steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. And no tutor or platform, including this one, is KHDA-approved - the phrase describes nothing that exists for individual tutors. If a provider charges a premium for approval they do not hold, that is the clearest waste of money on this page.

sections.heading: What a well-spent first month looks like
paragraphs: A concrete plan is more useful than a rate card, so here is what four sessions well spent actually contain for an MYP student in Al Satwa. Session one is diagnostic: the marked task, the criterion sheet and the teacher's comment, read together, with the specific band and the specific descriptor identified. Nothing is taught until the problem is named. A parent who receives a tutoring plan that does not reference a criterion number should ask why.

Sessions two and three teach the technique the descriptor wants, on the student's own next piece of work rather than on a generic exercise. For a science Criterion B that means designing a method with the controlled variables written out before any practical happens. For mathematics Criterion B it means taking a pattern the student found and pushing it to a general statement with a justification attached. The output is a task the student submits, in their own words, having understood why it is structured that way.

Session four closes the loop against the school's own marking. The newly marked task comes back, the band is compared with the previous one, and either the technique held or it did not. That is the only honest measure of whether the money worked, and it belongs to the school rather than to the tutor. A provider who reports progress only against their own internal assessments is reporting on themselves.

After that first month the decision is genuinely open. Some students need a second criterion addressed and buy another short block. Some need nothing further for a term. Some have a broader writing issue that will take longer and should be told so plainly rather than sold a package. The free trial lesson exists so the first of those four sessions costs nothing, and so the diagnosis happens before any block is agreed.
bullets: Session one: name the criterion and the band from the school's own marked task
Sessions two and three: teach the technique on the student's next real piece of work
Session four: compare the new school mark with the old one
Judge the spend against the school's marking, not the tutor's
If the issue is long-term writing development, expect to be told that plainly

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects, and what they add to the week
paragraphs: No competitor page in this search result mentions this, and it changes the arithmetic of how many tutoring hours a Dubai MYP student can absorb. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Those lessons sit on top of eight MYP subject groups.

The organisational rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs.

Two constraints shape what any tutor can honestly offer here. All teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a checkable credential point. And for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited - so support means reinforcing the school's own material and the underlying language skills, not importing a parallel syllabus.

The practical consequence is timetable arithmetic, and it is a budget point. Mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and KHDA advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Add those to eight subject groups and a Dubai MYP week is fuller than the subject list suggests. One well-targeted hour has a far better chance of landing than three scattered ones, and it costs a third as much.

process.title: Send the marked task, not a description
process.description: The fastest route to a useful first lesson is the school's own marked work: the task sheet with the criterion on it, the band awarded and the teacher's comment. That document carries the diagnosis. A description of the problem from memory costs a session to replace.

process.title: Name the subject, the year and the criterion
process.description: "MYP Year 9 sciences, Criterion B scored 4, lab report due in two weeks" can be matched immediately. "Help with science" needs two exchanges first. The more specific the first message, the faster the right teacher is proposed and the less you pay for discovery.

process.title: See the proposed tutor and the reasoning
process.description: You get a named tutor with their subject and MYP experience and the reason for the match. Where availability means the best fit is not free at your preferred hour, you are told that rather than quietly given somebody adjacent.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson at no cost, with the marked task on screen. It is a diagnostic as much as an introduction: by the end you should know which criterion is costing marks and roughly how many hours it needs. Nothing is owed if the answer is no.

process.title: Fix the slot around the school run
process.description: Al Satwa children travel out to school, so arrival home is later than the timetable implies. The weekly slot is set against the real return time and holds each week, and nothing depends on a tutor's drive across central Dubai.

process.title: Review against the school's next mark
process.description: Progress is judged on the next task the school marks, against the same criterion. If the band moved, the money worked. If it did not, the plan changes and you hear why in language you can take to the MYP coordinator.

whyPoints.title: Rates are published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it - EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate - with no invented IB Gram price list. Three of six competitor pages researched in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in a currency UAE parents do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: The plan names a criterion
whyPoints.description: Support is built from the school's marked task and the criterion that lost the marks, not from a generic year-group syllabus. That is the difference between four useful hours and twenty wasted ones, and it is the question to ask any provider before paying.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the rate
whyPoints.description: In-home tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180-500 an hour because a car is priced into it. Online delivery removes that loading, which at comparable monthly spend buys roughly eight sessions instead of four - and frequency is what middle-years progress actually runs on.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is explicit
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nothing is written, redrafted or produced for a student on a Personal Project or any assessed task. In a market where completed coursework is openly sold, that boundary protects your child.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed up front
whyPoints.description: If the right subject teacher has no slot at your hour, you are told, with alternatives and dates. Tutor location is stated rather than hidden behind a local-looking number, and the free trial lesson tests the match before any block is bought.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Al Satwa evening
whyPoints.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, set against when your child actually gets back from a school in Jumeirah, Al Safa or Al Barsha. Ramadan timings and school holidays move the slot rather than cancelling it, and traffic never decides whether a lesson happens.

faqs.question: How much should an Al Satwa family budget monthly for MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: Read the market monthly rather than hourly. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget tutoring at AED 240-600 a month, mid-range at AED 600-1,200 and specialist assessment-year work at AED 1,000-2,000 and above. For a Year 8 or Year 9 student the middle band is the realistic planning figure and buys about four sessions a month with a trained subject teacher. Published online packages run around AED 799 a month for eight sessions. These are market figures, not IB Gram's; a real number for your child's subject and timeline comes from the consultation after the free trial.

faqs.question: Why is an MYP report so hard to act on without a tutor who knows the criteria?
faqs.answer: Because it is written in criterion language for teachers and read by parents. Each subject reports four criteria scored 0-8 against published band descriptors, so a line reading 7, 7, 4, 6 is not a weak subject - it is one named weakness in one criterion. Without knowing which criterion is which, a parent sees a low number and buys general subject revision, which is the most common waste of money in Dubai middle-years tuition. A tutor who works with the descriptors asks for the marked task sheet first, because that sheet carries both the criterion and the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion is cheapest to improve?
faqs.answer: The investigation and evaluation criteria, generally. Sciences Criterion B, inquiring and designing, and Criterion C, processing and evaluating, both respond to technique rather than to content: writing out controlled variables before a practical, handling uncertainties, giving a limitation that is specific rather than ritual. A handful of focused hours can move those bands and the technique then holds for the rest of the programme. Communication and analysis criteria are slower because they track writing development, and no amount of paid tuition accelerates that past a point. Content criteria sit in between and are the most widely available teaching.

faqs.question: Is an in-home MYP tutor worth the extra AED per hour in central Dubai?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on what the problem is. In-home rates in Dubai are quoted at AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and the difference is a car: from Al Satwa a tutor is driving in from Al Barsha, Jumeirah or Umm Suqeim through late-afternoon traffic and finding visitor parking in a dense low-rise grid. What that buys is physical supervision, which genuinely helps a younger or distractible student. What it does not buy is criterion expertise. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to an apartment in Al Satwa?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. Lessons for an Al Satwa family are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the marked task, the criterion sheet and the student's draft are visible to both sides and the annotated version stays with the student. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation: removing travel from the hour is what allows a family in a neighbourhood with almost no international school inside its boundary to work with a subject teacher who knows the descriptors.

faqs.question: Are two-hour MYP sessions better value than two one-hour sessions?
faqs.answer: Usually not at this age. Attention and retention both drop away after about an hour for most eleven to sixteen year olds, and criterion technique is built by a cycle of doing a task, having it marked and doing the next one. Two contacts a week produce two cycles; one long session produces one. The published Dubai package comparison makes the cost side visible too: roughly eight online sessions a month against four two-hour in-home visits for more money. If your child is older, close to an assessment and working on an extended piece, a longer session can be justified.

faqs.question: Should we pay for MYP eAssessment preparation?
faqs.answer: Only if your school actually enters students for it. MYP Year 5 eAssessment leads to the MYP certificate through on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, and some schools offer it while others do not. If yours does, the format is unfamiliar enough to justify a short scoped block of preparation. If yours does not, preparation for it is money spent on an examination your child will never sit - and it is a question with a one-line answer from the MYP coordinator. Ask before buying anything described as exam preparation at this stage.

faqs.question: Where exactly does paid help on a Personal Project stop being allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can interrogate the goal until the student can state and defend it in one sentence, teach research and time-management skills, explain what the planning, applying skills and reflecting criteria actually ask for, and give questions and comments on a draft the student wrote. A tutor cannot write any part of the report, rewrite a paragraph to show how it should sound, supply the artefact or edit the document to completion. The test is simple: if your child cannot explain every decision unprompted, the line was crossed and the risk is theirs.

faqs.question: Does an MYP tutor working with a Dubai family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: A tutor delivering private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE states a two-working-day completion time and lists no fees, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without it face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published so no amount should be quoted at you. Since it is free, ask to see it.

faqs.question: Is money spent in MYP Years 4 and 5 better value than money spent in Year 12?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and the arithmetic is straightforward. Specialist Higher Level Diploma teaching in Dubai is quoted at AED 200-450 an hour and above; a middle-years subject teacher is AED 150-300. Much of what Year 12 families pay specialists to fix is technique the MYP already introduced: uncertainty treatment, method design, generalising a pattern with justification, extended written argument against a command term. Building those two years early at the lower rate is the clearest saving available in this market, because content gets taught again in the Diploma and technique does not.

faqs.question: What should a first month of MYP support actually contain?
faqs.answer: Four sessions with a shape. Session one is diagnostic: the marked task, the criterion sheet and the teacher's comment read together, with the specific band and descriptor named before anything is taught. Sessions two and three teach the technique the descriptor wants, on the student's own next piece of work rather than a generic exercise. Session four closes the loop against the school's new mark on the same criterion. That last step is the only honest measure of whether the spend worked, and it belongs to the school rather than to the tutor.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover several MYP subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Within a group, usually; across groups, be careful. A science teacher can reasonably cover integrated sciences and then biology, chemistry or physics as the subjects separate, because the criteria are shared and the method work transfers. A mathematics teacher covering language and literature is a different proposition, and a listing advertising every subject from Year 2 to Year 13 is telling you it is a generalist. For criterion-level work in a specific subject, ask which subjects the tutor has actually taught and marked in an MYP school rather than which they are willing to attempt.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory UAE subjects affect how many tutoring hours fit in the week?
faqs.answer: They add more than parents expect. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated in 40-minute lesson units, with 25 minutes advised as a minimum lesson length, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs with combined classes prohibited. Add that to eight MYP subject groups and the week is fuller than the subject list suggests, which argues for one well-targeted hour rather than three scattered ones.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Satwa MYP students usually travel to?
faqs.answer: Out of the neighbourhood. Al Satwa contains almost no international private school inside its boundary, so families use the coastal continuum campuses in Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, the inland Al Barsha cluster, or older schools across Sheikh Zayed Road in Oud Metha and Garhoud. A twenty to thirty minute return in term-time afternoon traffic pushes homework and any session later than the school timetable implies, which is the real reason weekday slots need setting against the actual arrival time. Schools named on this page are planning context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA school inspection band tell a parent weighing up tuition?
faqs.answer: More than the headline label does. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak, with the report broken down by subject and by phase. A school rated Outstanding overall can still have a weaker department or a weaker middle-years phase, and that section is the one worth reading if your child is struggling in one subject. Treat it as evidence about the teaching your child actually receives, then decide. KHDA does not rate or approve individual private tutors, so no tutor can claim a band.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-satwa.closingHeading: Spend on the criterion, not on the hours
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-satwa.closingBody: If you are weighing up an IB MYP tutor in Al Satwa, the question that saves the most money is not what an hour costs - it is which criterion is losing the marks. Send the school's marked task with the band and the teacher's comment, name the subject and the year, and you will get a tutor who can tell you which descriptor the work is missing and roughly how many hours it needs. The trial lesson is free, lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time timed to your real school-run return, and no block is agreed until after the diagnosis. If the honest answer is that the issue needs a term rather than a month, you will be told that too.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-sufouh.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work across the MYP subject groups Al Sufouh families ask about from MYP 1 to MYP 5: Mathematics, Sciences, Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies and Language Acquisition.

intro.heading: Why an MYP evening looks empty, and usually is not
paragraphs: A British-curriculum Year 9 parent can tell whether work is happening. There are exercises, a textbook, a set of questions due Thursday, a percentage on a topic test. An MYP parent in Al Sufouh has none of that. Their child is working on a unit, has a summative task in three weeks, and in the meantime appears to be reading, thinking, taking photographs of something for a process journal and occasionally not working at all. The report card, when it comes, contains four numbers out of 8 per subject and no rank, no percentage and no comparison with anyone.

The result is a specific kind of anxiety that produces specific bad decisions. Some families buy a weekly tutor to create visible activity, which fills the evening without touching the criterion that is low. Others buy nothing until MYP 5, when a Personal Project deadline makes the problem suddenly legible. Both responses come from the same cause: no instrument for telling whether a child is on track. This page is mostly an attempt to supply one.

It helps to know what the work actually is. The MYP has eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of 8 - a raw 32 that the school converts to a 1-7 grade using its own published boundaries. Criteria reward documented process as much as correct answers: a conjecture tested and generalised, a method another person could follow, sources interrogated rather than summarised, a reflection that names a specific decision and its consequence. That work is slower than exercises and far less visible, which is why an MYP evening can be productive and look idle.

Al Sufouh is a useful place to write this from, because the strip between Sheikh Zayed Road and the coast holds full IB continuum campuses alongside Knowledge Park, Internet City and Media City. Families here frequently keep a child in one school from FS1 to Year 13, inside one assessment framework the whole way. That is a real advantage and it has one blind spot, covered later on this page: a continuum student may reach DP1 having never been measured against anybody outside their own school.

On delivery, stated before anything else: IB Gram teaches Al Sufouh students one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer in India only. For MYP work the material is the school's own unit documents and the student's marked tasks, which annotate better on a shared screen than across a table, and the small pool of genuinely MYP-experienced tutors in this city is distributed by where the IB schools are rather than by residential street.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-sufouh.programmesIntro: Al Sufouh's campuses include full continuum provision, so the MYP here is usually the middle of a long single-system journey. That changes what each stage is for.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with descriptive reporting and no external assessment, closing with the Year 6 Exhibition. Children arrive in the MYP able to ask questions and often without the sustained writing volume that criterion-marked tasks will start demanding in Year 7.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Sufouh and nearby campuses run the PYP as the start of a continuum through to the Diploma. The useful Year 6 intervention for a family here is writing stamina rather than content, since MYP Criterion C in Language and Literature asks for more sustained text than most PYP classrooms require.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, four criteria each marked out of 8. Units are framed by key concepts, related concepts and global contexts, with Approaches to Learning skills taught across subjects. Assessment is internal and teacher-marked, with the Personal Project in MYP 5 and eAssessment at some schools.
programmes.countryNote: The programme in your search, and the longest stretch of the continuum. In Al Sufouh it sits beside British-curriculum schools running IGCSE in the same year groups, which is why MYP parents here receive confident advice about past papers and revision guides that does not apply to their child at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored out of 45. Assessment becomes largely external for the first time, with Internal Assessments carrying around a fifth of most subject grades.
programmes.countryNote: The point at which a continuum student meets external examiners. The MYP criterion profile predicts this reasonably well: strong investigation and reflection marks travel into Internal Assessment work, while consistently weak reflective criteria predict a struggle with coursework load rather than with content.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Uncommon in Dubai; check the current KHDA school listing rather than an older guide, as provision shifts year to year.
programmes.countryNote: Where it exists within reach of Al Sufouh, the MYP Personal Project is good preparation for the CP reflective project, since both are assessed on documented process. The academic-honesty boundary is identical, and worth agreeing with any tutor before work starts.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-sufouh.subjectsIntro: The eight MYP subject groups and two cross-cutting components, with a note on what the work looks like at home in each - which is the thing parents in this area most often cannot see.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating patterns, C Communicating, D Applying in real-life contexts. At home, B and D look like a child staring at a problem rather than doing exercises, because both require a conjecture, test cases and a generalisation rather than practice questions.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Inquiring and designing, C Processing and evaluating, D Reflecting on impacts. At home, B and C look like planning and data tables, and D looks like reading about an issue - which parents frequently mistake for not working.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.levels: English, Arabic and other school languages
subjects.description: Criteria A Analysing, B Organizing, C Producing text, D Using language. The visible work is drafting, and the invisible work is planning structure. Strong readers lose B marks precisely because they skip the invisible part and write straight through.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria A Comprehending spoken and visual text, B Comprehending written and visual text, C Communicating, D Using language. Phase placement matters more than year group, and a child advanced too early looks weak on all four criteria when the real issue is placement.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating, C Communicating, D Thinking critically. Research-heavy, so the evening work is reading and source selection. A pile of printed sources is not progress; a short note on why two were discarded is.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria A Inquiring and analysing, B Developing ideas, C Creating the solution, D Evaluating. The design cycle is the assessment, so the documentation is the subject. Thinly staffed by tutors across Dubai, which is worth knowing before a request is made late.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Developing skills, C Thinking creatively, D Responding. The process journal is the evidence base for B and C; practice at home without journalling produces improvement that cannot be assessed.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Planning for performance, C Applying and performing, D Reflecting and improving. The written planning and reflection tasks are the ones skipped at home, and they are half the available marks.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed on synthesis across subject groups against their own criteria. Run very differently school to school, so the task-specific clarification is essential. A tutor's experience at one school transfers poorly here.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Criteria A Planning, B Applying skills, C Reflecting, assessed on the process journal and report rather than the product. A tutor may teach project management, questioning and reflective writing; every word of the journal and report must be the student's own.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-sufouh.regionsTitle: Al Sufouh and the corridor its MYP students travel
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-sufouh.regionsIntro: These notes describe how much of an evening each area's commute leaves, because the MYP year-by-year table later on this page depends on knowing what time a child is genuinely available.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Campuses and Knowledge Park within minutes of each other, with the tram running the corridor. A student at a local gate is often home by 3:20pm, which makes this one of the few Dubai areas where a 4:30pm start is realistic for a younger MYP year group.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Dense and vertical along the tram line, with children commuting out to Al Sufouh and Al Barsha gates. Tower lift and parking add a quarter of an hour nobody counts, which matters most for MYP 1 and MYP 2 students whose attention window is shortest.

regions.name: JBR
regions.note: Beachside with the same gate pattern. Marina congestion rather than distance sets the arrival time, so an MYP 3 student here is realistically available from about 4:45pm rather than 4:30pm.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road with its own towers and a mixed school pattern. Parents often work locally in JLT or DMCC, which makes a 5pm session supervised by the household rather than requiring an arrangement.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Low-rise and family-dominated inland of the tram, feeding Al Barsha and Al Sufouh gates. Short on paper, longer in practice at 3:20pm, and the area with the most MYP siblings in different year groups needing different evening shapes.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Established IB provision further inland. The longest return leg in this corridor, so MYP 4 and MYP 5 students here do better with weekend sessions for extended project work than with a tired weekday hour.

regions.name: The Springs and The Lakes
regions.note: Villa communities with large middle-school cohorts. A strong informal tutoring culture operates here, and it is predominantly IGCSE-shaped, which is the source of most of the mismatched advice MYP families in this corridor receive.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: Offshore with one access route and no school. Any arrangement that depends on travel at school-out time will start late, which is why online delivery is not a preference here so much as the only reliable option.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh, Knowledge Park and Media City
schoolClusters.note: The campuses on Al Sufouh's own strip, several running the full IB continuum from PYP through DP. That continuity is the local advantage and the source of the benchmarking blind spot discussed on this page. Students we support attend schools in this cluster; no affiliation is implied.

sections.heading: What MYP homework actually is, and how to tell whether it is happening
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in Al Sufouh spends a surprising amount of the first conversation explaining what the work is, because the absence of exercises reads as the absence of work. MYP tasks are mostly project-shaped: a unit runs for several weeks, builds towards a summative task assessed against two or three criteria, and the preparation is reading, planning, data gathering, drafting and journalling rather than answering questions. There is often nothing to mark on a Tuesday evening, and that is by design rather than by neglect.

The practical problem this creates for a parent is that the usual signals do not work. You cannot check completed exercises. You cannot see a percentage. You cannot ask whether the homework is done, because the honest answer from a conscientious student is often 'sort of'. What you can do is ask three questions that work in this programme: what is the summative task and when is it due, which criteria is it assessed on, and what has been done towards it this week. A student working properly answers all three. A student drifting cannot answer the second.

The second thing worth knowing is where the invisible work is. In Mathematics, Criterion B wants a conjecture, test cases and a generalisation, which looks like a child sitting still. In Sciences, Criterion D wants reflection on the social and ethical dimension of a scientific issue, which looks like reading articles. In Individuals and Societies, Criterion B wants sources selected and evaluated, which looks like browsing. All three are the work. A pile of printed sources is not evidence of progress; a note explaining why two were discarded is.

This is also why buying a weekly tutor to create visible activity is the commonest and most expensive MYP mistake in this area. An hour of worked examples produces something a parent can see and addresses Criterion A, which was usually not the problem. The useful purchase is a diagnosis against the criterion that is actually low, which may well conclude that no weekly arrangement is needed at all.

sections.heading: The five MYP years, and how much of an evening each one needs
paragraphs: The MYP is not one programme with five instances. MYP 1 and MYP 5 differ in demand, in what goes wrong, and in how much of an evening they should reasonably occupy. Treating them the same is how a Year 7 student ends up with a weekly tutoring commitment they do not need and a Year 11 student ends up with none when the Personal Project is due.

In the early years the demand is modest and the failure is translation. A child who has never been marked against a descriptor produces competent work, scores 4, and reads that as a judgement. The whole fix is reading exemplars at different bands and annotating them against the criterion wording, which takes a few sessions and then stops being useful. An MYP 1 or MYP 2 student needing a weekly tutor for two years is a rare case, and a provider who proposes one should be asked why.

The middle years are where documented process starts being demanded in earnest, and where most of the genuine tutoring need in the MYP sits. Sciences wants a designed investigation; Mathematics wants investigation and real-world modelling; Individuals and Societies wants sources interrogated. Students who are quick arrive at conclusions and do not show the working that the criterion rewards. This is the point at which a weekly arrangement in one subject group earns its cost.

The final two years add volume and then the Personal Project. MYP 4 is where eight subject groups, their four criteria each and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirements fill the week completely - and where the problem becomes organisational rather than academic. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project, possible eAssessment and the route decision. The table below gives a realistic evening demand for each year, assuming the Al Sufouh commute pattern described earlier.

sections.heading: The Al Sufouh continuum advantage and its one blind spot
paragraphs: Families on this strip can often keep a child in one school from FS1 to Year 13, inside a single assessment framework the whole way. The advantages are real and underrated. The child never has to learn a new reporting language. The school knows them across a decade. PYP inquiry habits feed MYP investigation criteria, which feed DP Internal Assessments, and nobody has to translate between systems at a transition. For a parent, learning one framework properly instead of three is a genuine saving of effort.

The blind spot is benchmarking. MYP assessment is internal and teacher-marked against published criteria, with school-set grade boundaries converting a raw total out of 32 into a 1-7 grade. There is no rank, no percentage, no cohort comparison and no external marker until eAssessment at the end of MYP 5 - and not every school enters students for that. A continuum student can therefore arrive in DP1 having never once been measured by anybody outside their own school. If the school's boundaries are generous, or if a particular teacher marks kindly, nobody finds out until external assessment.

This is not an accusation about any school; it is a structural feature of internally assessed programmes, and the IB's moderation processes exist partly to address it. But it has a practical consequence for a parent on this strip: you should not treat a stable 6 across five years as proof of external readiness, and you should not panic about a 4 either, because neither number has been calibrated against anything you can see.

The next section sets out four things a family can do about it. None requires buying tuition, and the most useful of them is free. The reason it belongs on this page is that the single most common MYP tutoring enquiry we receive from this corridor is from a family whose child's grades are fine and who cannot shake the feeling that they do not know what the grades mean. That is a reasonable feeling and it has a reasonable answer.

sections.heading: Reading an MYP report card, and benchmarking without an exam
paragraphs: Start by reading the report differently from how it looks. Parents look for a position, a percentage and a trend. The MYP gives criterion marks, a grade from 1 to 7, and often a comment. The table below maps what you are looking for onto what the document actually provides, and what to do with it instead.

Then benchmark with four methods, in order of usefulness. First, ask for the school's grade boundary table - the conversion from a raw 32 to a 1-7 grade. It tells you how far your child is from the next grade, which a criterion profile alone does not. A student on 22 out of 32 might be one mark from a 6 or five marks from it, and those are different situations. Second, ask for exemplars at the band above your child's. Seeing a 7-8 band response to the same task is the most informative document available and schools generally provide it on request.

Third, ask whether the same criterion is low across subject groups. If Criterion D is low in Sciences, Individuals and Societies and Mathematics together, you are looking at one Approaches to Learning skill - critical thinking and reflection - rather than three subject weaknesses, and one intervention addresses all three. Fourth, and only if the first three leave you uncertain, have a specialist read two marked summatives and the clarification grids and give you an external opinion on where the work sits against the descriptors. That is a single session rather than a weekly arrangement, and for most families in this corridor it is the right purchase.

What none of these methods gives you is a national percentile, because the MYP does not produce one. A family that needs that kind of reassurance should know it is not available in this programme and should not buy tutoring in an attempt to manufacture it. What is available is a clear account of which criterion is low, how far from the next grade the student is, and whether the gap is subject knowledge or a transferable skill.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs here, measured against what school already buys
paragraphs: A useful comparison nobody makes: you are already paying for teaching hours. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, so your school fee is a known and currently fixed quantity. Divide your own annual invoice by the number of taught hours in the school year and you get your actual cost per teaching hour. Most families in this corridor have never done that sum, and doing it reframes every tutoring quote they will receive.

Against that figure, the published tutoring market looks like this. Budget online tuition starts at AED 33-52 an hour from Tutopiya and AED 45-65 from EdFlik. A qualified subject tutor working online runs AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one with travel included runs AED 180-500, Bestimate quoting AED 180-350. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650. Monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

For the MYP specifically, two of those bands are poor value and one is actively misleading. The budget band buys supervision and question-bank drilling, and the MYP has no question bank, so what you get is an hour of worked examples addressing Criterion A. The premium band sells examiner credentials, and MYP assessment is internal and teacher-marked, so examiner status is close to irrelevant here. What the MYP needs is criterion literacy, and that lives in the AED 150-300 band.

The structural recommendation follows from the year-by-year table earlier on the page. In MYP 1 to MYP 3, buy a short block rather than a weekly arrangement - the available gain is in translation and it does not need twenty sessions. In MYP 4 and MYP 5, a weekly arrangement in one subject group is defensible. Across all years, a single diagnostic session each term on two marked summatives is often the whole of what a family on this strip actually needs. All figures above are other providers' published rates read during the October 2026 research round, quoted as market context rather than as an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Academic honesty across the MYP, not only the Personal Project
paragraphs: Most discussion of academic honesty in the IB attaches to the Personal Project, the Extended Essay and Internal Assessments, because those are the named pieces of assessed work. In the MYP the boundary applies much more widely than that, and the reason is structural: every summative task is internally assessed coursework. A Sciences investigation, an Individuals and Societies research task, a Language and Literature essay and a Design folder are all work submitted under the student's name and marked against criteria. The same rules apply to all of them.

What that means in a tutoring session is specific. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the criterion, show exemplars, ask why a paragraph is there, and point at where a draft falls short of a descriptor. A tutor may not write, draft, restructure or edit any part of a summative task, a process journal, an investigation write-up or a Personal Project report. The test is simple: if a sentence in the submitted work would not exist without the tutor, the line has been crossed, however gently.

This matters more in the MYP than families realise because the work is produced at home over weeks, often with a parent and a tutor both involved and nobody having agreed what involvement means. A well-meaning tutor who 'tidies up' a draft has done something that in the DP would be malpractice and in the MYP is at best a habit the student will carry into coursework that counts. Agree the boundary explicitly in the first session, in words, and ask the tutor to state it before you ask.

There are operators in this market selling completed assessed work outright, at published prices. That is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller. A family buying 'help with the Personal Project' without asking precisely what help means is buying a risk on their child's behalf. The legitimate version of that help is substantial and worth paying for - criteria explained, research questions stress-tested, reflections questioned until they say something specific - and it leaves every word of the submission the student's own.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Sufouh, and what we will not take on
paragraphs: Begin with documents rather than a booking. Ask the school for the task-specific clarification covering the most recent summative, the unit overview, the marked task itself and the grade boundary table. Those four make criterion-level teaching possible; without the first one a tutor is guessing, however well they know the subject. Then send us the subject group, the MYP year, the criterion marks from the latest report and whatever the school has provided.

From there: we match on subject group and MYP experience, you take a full-length trial lesson at no cost with your child's own marked task on screen, and you judge whether the tutor works in descriptor language or in topics. Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time - 4:30pm is realistic for a student at an Al Sufouh gate, 5:00pm or later for a commute back from Al Barsha or Emirates Hills. Ramadan timings move to post-Iftar slots, and sessions pause in the week a major summative is due.

What we will decline. A weekly two-year arrangement for an MYP 1 student, because the available gain is a short block and selling more than that is selling activity. A request to produce or improve a summative draft, in any subject group. A request for a national percentile, because the MYP does not generate one and no provider can supply it honestly. And a late request in MYP Design, MYP Arts, several Language Acquisition phases or an interdisciplinary unit where we do not have somebody genuinely experienced - in those cases the answer is a waiting position or a no, not a generalist at specialist rates.

The fixed limits apply throughout. No home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. No claimed approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson - the IB authorises schools rather than tutors, and IB Gram holds nothing from any of them. No reproduction of IB documents; we reference and link the official sources and work from your school's own materials. No grade promises, and no published statistics about our own outcomes, because we cannot show the sample, date and method that would make them mean anything.

process.title: Ask three questions at the kitchen table
process.description: What is the summative task and when is it due, which criteria is it assessed on, and what has been done towards it this week. A student working properly answers all three. A student drifting cannot answer the second, and that is the diagnosis before anybody is paid.

process.title: Request the boundary table and an exemplar

process.title: Check whether one criterion is low across subjects
process.description: If the same criterion letter is low in several unrelated subject groups, the gap is an Approaches to Learning skill rather than several subject weaknesses, and one intervention covers all of them. This single check prevents most unnecessary multi-subject spending.

process.title: Review the criterion, with pauses built in
process.description: Every six to eight weeks, compare a new summative against the same criterion, and keep the submission-week pauses in the plan. A grade can stay still while a criterion rises. If the criterion has not moved after a block, change the target, the tutor, or stop.

faqs.question: My child seems to have no MYP homework. Is something wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually not. MYP tasks are project-shaped rather than exercise-shaped: a unit runs for weeks towards a summative assessed against two or three criteria, and the preparation is reading, planning, data gathering, drafting and journalling. There is often nothing to mark on a given evening. Test it with three questions instead of looking for worksheets: what is the summative task and when is it due, which criteria is it assessed on, and what has been done towards it this week. A student working properly answers all three. One who cannot answer the second is drifting, and that is the real signal.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether my child is on track with no rank or percentage?
faqs.answer: Use three free sources before buying anything. Ask the school for the grade boundary table, which shows how many of the 32 raw marks separate your child from the next grade - a student on 22 might be one mark away or five, and those are different situations. Ask for an exemplar at the band above for the same task, which shows what the difference looks like. Then check whether the same criterion letter is low across several subject groups, because that indicates a transferable skill gap rather than several subject problems. Those three answers cover most of what families worry about.

faqs.question: Does a continuum school from PYP to DP have any downside?
faqs.answer: One, and it is structural rather than a criticism of any school. MYP assessment is internal and teacher-marked with school-set grade boundaries, so there is no rank, no percentage and no external marker until eAssessment at the end of MYP 5 - which not every school enters students for. A child can therefore reach DP1 never having been measured by anybody outside their own school. The practical consequence is that a stable 6 across five years is not proof of external readiness, and a 4 is not proof of a problem, because neither has been calibrated against anything visible to you.

faqs.question: Should an MYP 1 student have a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and a provider proposing a two-year weekly arrangement for a Year 7 should be asked why. The characteristic MYP 1 problem is translation: a child who has never been marked against a descriptor produces competent work, scores a 4, and reads it as a verdict. The fix is reading exemplars at two or three different bands and annotating them against the criterion wording, which takes a few sessions and then stops being useful. Most students move a band from that exercise alone. Buying twenty sessions to solve a three-session problem is buying visible activity rather than progress.

faqs.question: Which MYP year actually needs the most support?
faqs.answer: MYP 3 and MYP 4, for different reasons. MYP 3 is where designed investigations start being demanded in earnest, and where quick students lose marks because they reach conclusions without documenting the process the criterion rewards. MYP 4 is where eight subject groups at full demand plus the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirements fill the week, and the problem becomes organisational - evidence not logged as it happens, journal entries not made. MYP 5 then adds the Personal Project and the route decision. MYP 1 and MYP 2 need short blocks, not sustained arrangements.

faqs.question: What does my school fee work out to per teaching hour?
faqs.answer: Divide your own annual invoice by the number of taught hours in the school year, and you will have a figure almost no family in this corridor has calculated. It is worth doing because it reframes every tutoring quote you will receive. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private-school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, so the school side of the equation is currently fixed while tutoring is not. Against your own number, the published tutoring bands of AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor become easier to judge.

faqs.question: Is a premium tutor worth it for MYP work?
faqs.answer: Generally not, and the reason is structural. Premium Dubai rates reach AED 500-650 and upwards, with BartyED publishing AED 650, and what they sell is examiner credentials and reputation. MYP assessment is internal and teacher-marked against criteria, with task-specific clarifications written by the classroom teacher, so there is no external paper for an examiner to have marked. What the MYP needs is someone who can read a clarification grid and work in descriptor language, and that capability sits in the AED 150-300 band. The budget band below it has even less to offer, since there is no question bank to drill.

faqs.question: Does the academic-honesty rule apply to ordinary MYP summatives?
faqs.answer: Yes, to all of them, and this surprises families who think the rule attaches only to the Personal Project. Every MYP summative is internally assessed coursework submitted under the student's name: a Sciences investigation, an Individuals and Societies research task, a Language and Literature essay, a Design folder. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the criterion, show exemplars and point at where a draft falls short. A tutor may not write, draft, restructure or tidy any part of it. The test is whether a sentence in the submitted work would exist without the tutor. If not, the line has been crossed.

faqs.question: What time can an MYP session start for a student at an Al Sufouh gate?
faqs.answer: 4:30pm is realistic, which is earlier than most of Dubai. Al Sufouh gates release secondary year groups roughly between 2:50pm and 3:20pm, and a student living in the same district is often home by 3:20pm. Allow for changing and food and the window opens at about 4:30pm. For a younger MYP year group that window is also shorter at the other end - an MYP 1 student is not usefully working at 6:30pm. If your child commutes back from Al Barsha or Emirates Hills, 5:00pm or 5:15pm is the honest start time.

faqs.question: How do I know whether the gap is subject knowledge or a study skill?
faqs.answer: Look for the same criterion letter repeating across unrelated subject groups. The MYP teaches communication, social, self-management, research and thinking skills across subjects and then assesses them inside subject criteria. Low D marks in Sciences, Individuals and Societies and Mathematics together point at critical thinking and reflection rather than three subject weaknesses. Thin process journals in Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education point at self-management. The useful consequence is that one tutor working on the skill inside one subject group usually lifts the others, which costs far less than three subject tutors.

faqs.question: What should a first MYP session actually contain?
faqs.answer: A reading of your child's own marked summative against the task-specific clarification that the teacher marked it with, producing a statement of which criterion is low and what the band above requires. It should not be a diagnostic test, and it should not be a tour of the topic. If the tutor has not asked for the clarification grid and the marked task in advance, the session will be generic by necessity, because without those two documents there is nothing specific to work from in a programme that publishes no past papers.

faqs.question: Can MYP tutoring help with the Diploma decision at the end of MYP 5?
faqs.answer: It can supply evidence, not advice. A five-year criterion profile says something real about coursework readiness: strong investigation and reflection marks travel well into DP Internal Assessments, because both demand a question framed, a method justified, data handled honestly and limitations named. A student carrying consistent 3s and 4s on reflective criteria will find the Diploma's coursework load heavier than its content. A tutor can read that profile and teach the skills that close the gap. The decision itself belongs to the family, the school and the IB coordinator who knows the child.

faqs.question: My child moved from a British-curriculum school into MYP 3. What should we expect?
faqs.answer: A grade drop that is about format rather than ability. A student trained to produce correct answers writes the answer and stops, which scores on Criterion A and nothing else. The MYP's investigation and reflection criteria want the working visible: test cases, a method someone else could follow, a reflection naming a specific decision and its consequence. Content is rarely the problem for a transferring student. The first useful intervention is reading three exemplars at different bands against the descriptors, which frequently moves a band with no content teaching at all.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups can you not always cover?
faqs.answer: Design and Arts are thinly staffed by tutors anywhere in Dubai, several Language Acquisition phases are hard to match, and interdisciplinary units are harder again because the assessment varies so much between schools that experience at one transfers poorly to another. Mathematics, Sciences and Language and Literature are the easiest to cover. Where a combination is genuinely hard to staff the honest answers are a waiting position, a tutor in the same subject group who can work on the specific criterion, or no. We would rather say that than place somebody learning the framework alongside your child.

faqs.question: Can you tell me where my child sits nationally?
faqs.answer: No, and nor can anyone else honestly, because the MYP does not generate a percentile. Assessment is internal, teacher-marked against published criteria, with school-set boundaries converting a raw total out of 32 into a 1-7 grade. There is no cohort comparison, no national dataset and no rank. A provider offering one is inventing it. What is genuinely available is a clear account of which criterion is low, how many raw marks separate your child from the next grade, and whether the gap looks like subject knowledge or a transferable skill - and those three answers address most of what the percentile question is really asking.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-sufouh.closingBody: An MYP evening that looks empty is usually not, and an MYP report that gives no percentage is not hiding one. Ask for the boundary table and an exemplar at the band above, check whether one criterion is low across several subjects, and ask your child the three kitchen-table questions. If that leaves you uncertain, buy one diagnostic session on two marked summatives rather than a term of weekly lessons. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, from 4:30pm for a local Al Sufouh gate.

intro.heading: Why is an MYP tutor harder to find in Al Twar than an IB tutor?
paragraphs: Because most of the IB knowledge in this part of Dubai is Diploma knowledge, and the two programmes are not variants of each other. Al Twar sits beside a large British and Indian curriculum market with IB continuum provision concentrated in a small number of schools, which means the local tutoring supply has had limited reason to learn how the Middle Years Programme works. A tutor can build a successful practice here on Diploma, IGCSE and CBSE work without ever reading an MYP task sheet.

The gap shows in specific places. MYP tasks are written in command terms arranged by cognitive demand, so a strand that asks a student to state something is asking for a different response from one that asks them to evaluate it, and the marks follow the verb. Language acquisition places students in one of six phases rather than by year group, so two children in the same class can be working to different expectations. Interdisciplinary units are assessed against their own criteria, not against the criteria of the two subjects they combine. None of that is intuitive, and none of it is in a Diploma teacher's working knowledge.

There is a further difference that matters more than it sounds. In the Diploma an examiner marks a student's script against a mark scheme. In the MYP a teacher judges a body of work against descriptors, taking into account what the student has demonstrated across tasks. That changes what useful tutoring looks like: less drilling of answer formats, more teaching a student to read a descriptor and recognise which band their own work sits in. A student who can self-assess against a descriptor has acquired something that keeps paying for the rest of the programme.

For an Al Twar family this produces a practical problem and a practical answer. The problem is that the nearby pool of genuinely MYP-literate tutors is small, and a tutor's IB experience is not a reliable proxy for it. The answer is to test rather than assume: ask what interdisciplinary units are assessed on, ask what a phase means in language acquisition, and ask how a command term changes an expected response. Those three questions separate MYP experience from Diploma experience in about two minutes.

One thing to state plainly. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. MYP tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for worked problems, annotated drafts and the task sheet open beside the descriptor. Given how thinly MYP-literate tutors are spread across this part of Dubai, that is how the matching problem is solved rather than worked around.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-twar.programmesIntro: MYP is five years long and the job changes substantially across them. These are the stages an Al Twar student passes through, and what each one needs.

programmes.name: MYP 1 to MYP 3
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, criterion-based assessment, interdisciplinary units and approaches to learning skills running throughout. Mathematics and sciences are usually taught as single subjects at this stage, with separation into disciplines coming later in most schools.
programmes.countryNote: The useful tutoring in these years is rarely content. It is teaching a student to read a task sheet properly: to notice which command term is used, to see which strand of which criterion is being assessed, and to produce the kind of response the descriptor actually describes.

programmes.name: MYP 4 and MYP 5
programmes.description: Subject groups separate into disciplines in many schools, mathematics splits into standard and extended routes, and the final year carries the Personal Project. Some schools enter students for on-screen eAssessment leading to the IB MYP Certificate and many do not.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Al Twar families start buying tutoring, and where the Diploma-versus-MYP mismatch does most damage, because a Diploma-trained tutor will teach towards examination technique the student does not yet need and skip the criterion work they do.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary education organised around transdisciplinary themes, with the exhibition at the end. There are no criterion marks of the MYP kind, so MYP 1 feels like a change in how work is judged rather than in how much of it there is.
programmes.countryNote: A student moving from PYP into MYP 1 in this cluster usually arrives confident at inquiry and unfamiliar with being measured against a published descriptor. The first useful job is translation, and it is cheaper done in MYP 1 than explained in MYP 4.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme after MYP
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service, with assessment returning to timed written papers and an internal assessment component in most subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Al Twar has Diploma provision locally and in Al Garhoud. The students who move most smoothly are those who practised timed written answers during MYP 5 alongside their criterion work, which almost nobody does unless somebody suggests it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-twar.subjectsIntro: MYP tutoring is requested subject by subject in this district, and the criteria and failure modes change with the subject group. These are the ones families here ask for.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion B asks for inquiring and designing and criterion C for processing and evaluating, so three of the four criteria concern how an investigation is handled rather than what is known. Content teaching alone touches one.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where marks go missing: students find the pattern and stop without generalising or justifying. Criterion D asks for mathematics applied in a real-life context, rewarding judgement over calculation.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. The commonest loss is retelling a text rather than explaining how a writer's choice creates an effect, which is a habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Placed by phase, not by year group, with criteria covering listening, reading, speaking and writing. A student can sit in different phases across skills, which parents find counter-intuitive and schools rarely explain.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigating with sources evaluated for reliability and purpose, not merely cited. Marks are lost by listing evidence without judging it, and by conclusions the sources do not actually support.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating. The process journal carries most of the marks, so an excellent product with thin documented iteration scores poorly.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. Evidence of process is assessed, so the most useful help is often teaching a student to document their own thinking.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Includes written planning and reflection components that surprise families expecting a practical-only subject. The written strands can be supported exactly as any other reflective writing.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria, requiring disciplinary grounding, synthesis across two subject groups and reflection on the process. Students treat them as double homework; the marks are for the synthesis.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal as evidence. A goal too vague to evaluate against is the usual cause of a disappointing mark.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for first-language Arabic.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Communication, social, self-management, research and thinking skills. Not graded as a subject, and the reason two students with the same knowledge receive different criterion marks on the same task.

sections.heading: Command terms on an MYP task sheet, and why they decide the mark
paragraphs: Every MYP task sheet is written in command terms, and the terms are arranged by cognitive demand. A strand that asks a student to state or outline something wants a short, accurate response and nothing more. One that asks them to explain wants reasons. One that asks them to analyse wants the thing broken into parts with relationships identified. One that asks them to evaluate or justify wants a judgement supported by evidence. The descriptor bands are written to match, so a student who explains where the task said analyse cannot reach the top band no matter how much they know.

This is the most common and most fixable cause of a disappointing criterion mark in MYP, and it is almost never what a family is told. A report that says a student needs to develop their analysis is accurate and unhelpful. What the student needs is to notice the word analyse on the task sheet, know what response shape it calls for, and produce that shape. That is teachable in a handful of sessions and it transfers to every subject group at once, which makes it the best-value intervention in the programme.

A Diploma-trained tutor will often miss this, not through carelessness but because the Diploma habit is different. Diploma command terms are drilled against past papers and mark schemes, where the reward is a specific answer format. MYP command terms are drilled against task sheets and descriptors, where the reward is a kind of thinking demonstrated across a piece of work. The vocabulary overlaps and the method does not.

The practical step for a parent is simple and costs nothing: look at the next task sheet your child brings home and find the command terms. They are usually in bold or in the strand wording. Then ask your child what each one is asking them to produce. If they cannot say, you have found the problem and you now know precisely what to buy.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units: assessed separately, understood by almost nobody
paragraphs: Interdisciplinary units are a required part of the MYP and they are assessed against their own criteria rather than against the criteria of the subjects they combine. That single fact explains most of the disappointment they generate. A unit joining sciences and individuals and societies is not asking for a science answer plus a humanities answer; it asks the student to bring grounding from both disciplines together into something neither would produce alone, and then to reflect on what the combination made possible.

Students treat them as double homework and write twice as much, which scores badly. The marks sit in the synthesis: the point at which a scientific mechanism and a social or historical context are used together to say something that needed both. A tutor who has taught interdisciplinary units knows to spend the session on that junction rather than on either subject, which is a different lesson plan from anything a single-subject tutor would produce.

The reflection element is the second place marks go missing. Students narrate: first we researched, then we made a poster. The criterion wants a judgement on what the interdisciplinary approach allowed them to understand that a single discipline would not have, and what its limitations were. That is an unfamiliar kind of writing for a fourteen-year-old, and it is coachable in two or three sessions once somebody names what is wanted.

If your child's school runs these units, ask for the unit's own assessment criteria rather than assuming the subject criteria apply. Teachers provide them readily. A tutor who asks for that document before the session is one who has done this before; a tutor who proposes to help with the science half and the history half separately has told you they have not.
