sections.heading: Language acquisition runs in phases, not year groups
paragraphs: This is the part of the MYP that confuses Al Twar parents most, and reasonably so. In language acquisition students are placed in one of six phases according to their proficiency, not according to their age or year group. A capable MYP 4 student who began French two years ago may sit in an early phase, and an MYP 2 student who speaks the language at home may sit in a later one. The phases describe a continuum of proficiency; the year group describes nothing about it.

Two consequences follow. First, comparing your child's language grade with a classmate's is meaningless unless they are in the same phase, because the descriptors differ. A 6 in phase 2 and a 6 in phase 4 are not the same achievement and were never intended to be read as such. Second, progress in this subject can look flat on a report while the student is in fact moving towards the next phase, which is a conversation worth having with the teacher rather than a reason to buy tutoring.

The criteria cover listening, reading, speaking and writing, and students are frequently uneven across them. A child who reads well and freezes in the interactive task needs speaking practice, not vocabulary lists, and the two are not interchangeable. This is where a tutor who knows the programme is worth paying for: the diagnosis is which criterion is trailing, and the response differs completely by criterion.

For Arabic specifically there is a UAE dimension. Arabic is mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for both groups strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. KHDA also requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for first-language Arabic. Ask the school which stream your child is in before arranging support, because the expectations differ.

sections.heading: MYP mathematics: standard or extended, and what the choice means
paragraphs: By the final MYP years most schools separate mathematics into a standard and an extended route, and the choice matters for what comes next. The extended route covers additional content and pitches tasks at greater demand; the standard route covers the core of the same framework. Both are assessed against the same four criteria, so the criterion profile remains the diagnostic tool in either case, and the route is the school's decision based on evidence it will share if asked.

The consequence shows up at the Diploma transition. A student heading towards Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or towards a science Higher Level, benefits substantially from the extended route, because the Diploma assumes an algebraic fluency the standard route is less likely to have built. A student heading elsewhere loses nothing by the standard route and gains time in a week that has eight subject groups in it.

Where tutoring genuinely helps is criterion B rather than content. Investigating patterns is the strand where MYP mathematics marks reliably go missing, on both routes, because students find the pattern, state it and consider the work complete. The criterion asks them to generalise it, express the generalisation correctly and justify why it holds. That final step is rarely taught explicitly in a crowded maths lesson and is worth a meaningful share of the subject's marks.

Criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, is the second underserved strand. It rewards judgement: choosing a model, stating its assumptions, and saying what the answer means in the situation described. Students who are strong calculators often score poorly here because they compute and stop. Both of these are teachable, and together they are where an MYP maths tutor earns their fee rather than in re-explaining topics the student already understands.

sections.heading: The Personal Project and service as action: what is assessed and what is not
paragraphs: Two parts of the MYP generate a lot of family anxiety and are frequently misunderstood in opposite directions. The Personal Project, completed in the final MYP year, is assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal as the evidence base. Service as action is a requirement of the programme that students document and reflect on, and it is not a graded subject. Families often over-prepare the second and under-plan the first.

For the Personal Project, the highest-value intervention is early and takes a single session: narrowing a goal until it can actually be evaluated against the criteria. A student who intends to raise awareness about something has nothing assessable; a student who intends to design, test and revise a specific thing, documenting each decision, has a project with marks attached. Catching that in week two rather than month four changes the entire outcome, and it is the cheapest useful hour in the MYP.

The second intervention is the process journal, which students complete retrospectively as paperwork and thereby destroy as evidence. Teaching a student to log a decision and the reason for it, in five minutes, on the day it happens, is a habit that carries the project. The third is the reflection, where the criterion wants a judgement on what was learned and what would be done differently, not a narrative of what happened.

What a tutor may not do is produce any part of it. We will not write, draft, restructure to completion or supply content for a Personal Project, and any service that offers to is handing your child a malpractice risk rather than a shortcut. We say that to students at the first project session rather than leaving it implied, because a fifteen-year-old under deadline pressure deserves a clear line. Legitimate support is questioning the goal, teaching journal discipline and giving feedback on the student's own writing.

sections.heading: Why two students with the same knowledge get different criterion marks
paragraphs: The answer is approaches to learning, the five skill categories that run across every MYP subject: communication, social, self-management, research and thinking. They are not graded as a subject and they are the reason two students who know the same content produce work that sits in different bands. A student who cannot plan a multi-stage task will submit something incomplete; a student who cannot evaluate a source will cite a weak one confidently; a student with poor self-management will produce good work late.

This matters for how a parent reads a report. A criterion mark that is lower than the student's knowledge warrants is often an approaches-to-learning problem wearing a subject label. Research skills explain a surprising share of individuals and societies marks. Self-management explains a surprising share of design and arts marks, where documented process is assessed. Thinking skills explain the gap between a student who can explain and one who can evaluate.

It also matters for what tutoring should do. Teaching research skills properly, which means source evaluation, note organisation and knowing when enough has been gathered, improves marks in several subject groups at once. So does teaching a student to break a task into stages with its own deadlines. These are unglamorous sessions and they have the broadest effect of anything available, which is why we often propose them when a family came asking for content help.

For an Al Twar family there is a practical note. These skills are precisely the ones a parent can reinforce without any subject knowledge: asking a child which stage of the task they are on, whether the source they are using would persuade someone who disagreed, and what they would change if they started again. That costs nothing and it is the kind of support that compounds across the whole programme.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs, and where coverage runs thin
paragraphs: Price in this market does not track MYP competence, which is the most useful thing to know before comparing quotes. The published bands, read in October 2026 and attributed to their publishers, are: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 survey agreeing; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate and up to AED 500 independently; and BartyED advertising AED 650 at the premium end.

What matters for MYP is that the premium end of that ladder is priced for Diploma work. A tutor at AED 650 an hour may never have read an MYP task sheet, while a mid-band tutor at AED 200 may have marked them weekly for years. For an MYP 3 or MYP 4 student the mid band with genuine MYP experience is the better purchase, and we would rather say so than sell the more expensive hour. The exception is MYP 5 preparation for the Diploma transition, where Diploma experience is exactly what the block needs.

Monthly, which is how households decide, Bestimate's survey puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 for budget work, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more at specialist level, with advertised packages at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. None of these figures is an IB Gram price; we publish a free trial lesson and a consultation instead.

On coverage, our position is stated rather than concealed. MYP sciences and mathematics are reasonably covered by UAE-based tutors. MYP Design, Arts, the less common language acquisition phases and interdisciplinary unit support are thinner, and a Personal Project supervisor with real MYP experience is scarcer still. Where no UAE-based specialist is free we say so before you book and offer a wider-pool tutor working Gulf Standard Time at the same band, rather than placing a Diploma tutor and letting the mismatch emerge in week three.

sections.heading: What an Al Twar parent can establish for nothing
paragraphs: Four things, none of which costs anything, and together they improve the purchase more than comparing tutoring websites does. The first is the criterion profile. Ask the MYP coordinator or subject teacher for the four criterion marks on recent tasks rather than the reported grade. A profile with one criterion a band behind the others is a precise instruction about what to buy; a grade on a report conceals it entirely.

The second is the task sheet. Look at the next one your child brings home, find the command terms, and ask your child what each is asking them to produce. If the answer is vague you have found the problem yourself, free, and you can buy a short block aimed at exactly that rather than a term of general subject help. For interdisciplinary units, ask the school for the unit's own assessment criteria, which teachers provide readily.

The third is the stream and route. For Arabic, ask which stream your child is placed in, since KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes for both groups because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For mathematics in MYP 4 and 5, ask whether your child is on the standard or extended route and what evidence placed them there.

The fourth is the permit, which is free and therefore a clean honesty test. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted at you. Note also that IB Gram holds no accreditation, approval or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and occupies no UAE premises.

faqs.question: Is a Diploma tutor able to teach my MYP child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is not safe to assume it. The Diploma and the MYP assess differently: Diploma technique is drilled against past papers and mark schemes, while MYP work is judged against descriptors using command terms arranged by cognitive demand. A Diploma specialist may never have read an MYP task sheet, may not know that interdisciplinary units carry their own criteria, and may not know that language acquisition places students by phase. Test for MYP experience specifically rather than taking IB experience as a proxy.

faqs.question: What are command terms and why do they decide my son's mark?
faqs.answer: They are the verbs on an MYP task sheet, arranged by cognitive demand, and the descriptor bands are written to match them. A strand asking a student to state wants a short accurate answer; explain wants reasons; analyse wants the parts and the relationships between them; evaluate or justify wants a judgement with evidence and limitations. A student who explains where the task said analyse cannot reach the top band however much they know. Decoding those verbs is teachable in a few sessions and transfers to every subject.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to our villa in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. MYP tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for worked problems, annotated drafts and the task sheet open beside the descriptor. Given how thinly MYP-literate tutors are spread across this part of Dubai, that is how the matching problem gets solved: the tutor is chosen for having marked MYP work rather than for living nearby.

faqs.question: How are interdisciplinary units assessed?
faqs.answer: Against their own criteria, not against the criteria of the two subjects they combine, which is the fact that causes most of the disappointment. The marks sit in the synthesis: using grounding from both disciplines together to say something neither would produce alone, explaining why the integration was worth doing, and then judging what the approach allowed and limited. Students typically write two separate answers side by side and narrate the activities. Ask the school for the unit's own criteria; teachers provide them readily.

faqs.question: Why is my daughter in a different language phase from her classmates?
faqs.answer: Because language acquisition places students by proficiency rather than by year group, across six phases. A capable older student who started the language recently may sit in an early phase, while a younger student who hears it at home may sit in a later one. The phases describe a continuum and the year group says nothing about it. One consequence is that comparing grades across phases is meaningless, since a 6 in an early phase and a 6 in a later one are deliberately different achievements.

faqs.question: My child reads well in French but freezes when speaking. What helps?
faqs.answer: Targeted work on the specific criterion that is trailing, which here is the oral and interactive one rather than vocabulary. Language acquisition assesses listening, reading, speaking and writing separately, and students are frequently uneven across them. Buying general language tutoring for an uneven profile spreads the hours over three skills that are already fine. Ask which criterion is lowest, then buy practice in that one: unprepared speaking, with a tutor who will not fill the silences, is what changes it.

faqs.question: Do Arab and non-Arab students study Arabic in the same class?
faqs.answer: No, and that is a requirement rather than a preference. Arabic is mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for both groups strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA also requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for first-language Arabic. The stream decides what the expectations are, so establish it before arranging any support.

faqs.question: Should my child take standard or extended MYP mathematics?
faqs.answer: It depends on where they are heading and the school decides it on its own evidence, which it will share if asked. The extended route covers additional content at greater demand and is better preparation for an analytical Higher Level route in the Diploma or for a science Higher Level. The standard route covers the core of the same framework and loses nothing for most other destinations, while giving back time in a week that already holds eight subject groups. Raise the question in MYP 4 rather than MYP 5.

faqs.question: Where do MYP maths marks actually go missing?
faqs.answer: Mostly in criterion B, investigating patterns, on both routes. Students find the pattern, state it, and consider the task finished. The criterion asks them to generalise it, express the generalisation correctly and justify why it holds, and that final step is rarely taught explicitly in a crowded lesson. Criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, is the second underserved strand: it rewards choosing a model, stating assumptions and saying what the answer means, and strong calculators often compute and stop.

faqs.question: Does a polished final product carry the Personal Project mark?
faqs.answer: No. It is marked on criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal providing the evidence, rather than on the quality of the finished object alone. That misconception is behind most of the disappointment this component causes. A student can build something impressive and score modestly because the documented process is thin, and a student can produce something modest and score well because the planning and reflection are rigorous. Confirm the version of the criteria in force with your child's coordinator.

faqs.question: How early should the Personal Project be started?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's deadline implies, because the slowest and most valuable stage is narrowing the goal. A student intending to raise awareness about something has nothing assessable; one intending to design, test and revise a specific thing while documenting each decision has a project with marks attached. Settle that in the first weeks, establish the journal habit of logging a decision and its reason on the day it happens, and the rest of the project becomes considerably easier to supervise honestly.

faqs.question: Is service as action graded?
faqs.answer: No. It is a requirement of the programme that students engage with and document, reflecting on what they did and what it meant, rather than a graded subject with criterion marks. Families frequently over-prepare it and under-plan the Personal Project, which is assessed. The useful parental contribution is to make sure the documentation actually happens as the activity happens, rather than being reconstructed later, and then to leave it alone. Tutoring is rarely the right purchase here.

faqs.question: Why do two students with the same knowledge get different marks?
faqs.answer: Approaches to learning, the five skill categories running across every MYP subject: communication, social, self-management, research and thinking. They are not graded as a subject and they explain most of the gap. A student who cannot stage a multi-part task submits something incomplete; one who cannot evaluate a source cites a weak one confidently; one with weak self-management produces good work late. A low criterion mark is frequently an approaches-to-learning problem wearing a subject label.

faqs.question: Is an expensive tutor better for MYP work?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is one place where paying more reliably buys less. The premium end of the Dubai market, with BartyED advertising AED 650 an hour, is priced for Diploma work, and Diploma expertise does not include having marked MYP tasks against descriptors. For an MYP 3 or MYP 4 student a mid-band tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 with real MYP experience is the better purchase. The exception is an MYP 5 block preparing for the Diploma transition, where Diploma experience is the point.

faqs.question: What should I ask an MYP tutor in the first conversation?
faqs.answer: Three questions that separate MYP experience from Diploma experience in about two minutes. What are interdisciplinary units assessed on? What does a phase mean in language acquisition, and how does it differ from a year group? And how does a command term change the response a strand expects? Precise answers to those indicate somebody who has worked inside the programme. General enthusiasm about holistic education, or an answer that reaches for past papers and mark schemes, indicates somebody who has not.

faqs.question: How can I help without knowing the subjects?
faqs.answer: More than you would expect, because the broadest-effect skills need no subject knowledge. Ask your child which stage of the task they are currently on, and whether the stages have their own deadlines. Ask whether the source they are using would persuade somebody who disagreed with them. Ask what they would change if they started again. Those three questions reinforce self-management, research and reflection, which between them explain a large share of criterion marks across every subject group, and they cost nothing.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-twar.closingHeading: Test for the programme, not for the brand
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-twar.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB MYP tutor in Al Twar, two free steps will tell you most of what you need. Ask the coordinator or subject teacher for the four criterion marks on recent tasks rather than the reported grade, and look at the next task sheet your child brings home to see whether they can tell you what each command term is asking for. Then put the three MYP questions on this page to any tutor you consider, including ours. The trial lesson costs nothing, needs no card details, and should be run from your child's own task sheet. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Why MYP tutoring costs more than it should, and how to stop that
paragraphs: Middle Years Programme tutoring is bought differently from IGCSE tutoring, and that difference is expensive. An IGCSE parent buys a tutor for a known examination with a known date. An MYP parent buys a tutor because a report arrived with a 5 on it and nobody in the house can say whether 5 is acceptable. Without an external benchmark, the arrangement tends to continue indefinitely. We meet Al Warqa families who have paid for weekly support in the same subject for three consecutive years with no mechanism for deciding when to stop.

At the rates Dubai providers publish, a weekly session with a qualified online tutor runs AED 150 to 300 an hour, which is AED 600 to 1,200 a month. Repeat that across two subjects for the five years of the programme and the arithmetic reaches a figure most parents have never totalled. The point is not that it is too much money. The point is that MYP spending rarely has an exit condition attached, and spending without an exit condition is the most reliable way to waste it.

The second structural reason MYP tutoring misfires is that the marks are not content marks. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, each scored out of eight, and each describing a skill rather than a body of knowledge. A science criterion asks whether the student can design a controlled investigation; a mathematics criterion asks whether they can communicate a solution clearly; an individuals and societies criterion asks whether sources were evaluated for bias. A tutor who spends an hour revising the content of the unit may leave every one of those strands untouched.

This is why a middling MYP report so often coexists with a child who clearly knows the material. The grade is held down by one criterion, usually the same one term after term, and nobody has named it. Diagnosing which letter is the problem takes a single session with the marked task sheet in hand. It is also, in our experience of Al Warqa families, the cheapest intervention available in the entire programme, because once a student understands what criterion C is asking for, they can usually supply it.

Al Warqa sits among large eastern-suburb cohorts, and that shapes the specific gap here. In a subject group where a teacher writes criterion-level feedback for well over a hundred students, the feedback that arrives is necessarily brief. Parents read a row of numbers out of eight and a sentence of comment. What is missing is somebody translating that into an instruction the student can act on this week. That translation is a short job, not a five-year subscription.

Everything below is priced, with the source for each band, and written for the Middle Years Programme specifically rather than borrowed from a Diploma page. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; visiting tutors are a service we operate only in India, and the in-home comparison further down shows what the Dubai market charges for that and what it buys.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-warqa.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme runs five years and changes character twice inside them. What a tutor should be doing in MYP 2 bears little resemblance to MYP 5, and paying the same rate for the same shape of lesson throughout is the commonest budgeting error we see in the eastern suburbs.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, early years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, interdisciplinary units, and the first exposure to criterion-based marking. Tutoring here should be rare and short. The useful purchase is not weekly subject support but two or three sessions teaching a student how to read a criterion descriptor and write to it, because that skill transfers across all eight groups and lasts the full five years. Families who buy weekly content tutoring at this stage are usually paying to fix something that is not broken.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary widely in how much criterion-level feedback they return at this stage, and in the largest Al Warqa and Al Qusais cohorts it is necessarily brief. Ask to see a marked task sheet with the strand descriptors attached before deciding any tutoring is needed at all.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, upper years
programmes.description: Subject choice narrows, the mathematics splits into standard and extended pathways in most schools, and grades start to carry weight for Diploma Programme course selection. This is where tutoring money earns its keep, particularly in mathematics and sciences, because the criteria now demand sustained independent work. A weekly slot in one or two subjects is defensible here in a way it is not three years earlier.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, upper-MYP grades feed directly into whether a student is accepted onto Higher Level courses in DP1 at their own school. Al Warqa families moving a child between an IB continuum school and a British-curriculum school at this point should expect the entire assessment logic to change, not just the timetable.

programmes.name: The MYP Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent project completed in the final MYP year, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. Students lose marks on the process documentation rather than on the product, because the process journal is written retrospectively in a weekend. A defined block of four to six supervision sessions, spread across the year rather than clustered at the end, is the single most cost-effective MYP purchase.
programmes.countryNote: The project is supervised by a member of staff at the school, and an outside tutor works alongside that supervision rather than replacing it. A tutor may question, challenge and give feedback on the student's own work. Writing any part of the project or the journal would breach IB academic-honesty rules and put the student at risk.

programmes.name: The step into the Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The transition is the point where MYP spending either pays off or reveals what was skipped. Students arrive in DP1 from the MYP with strong research and communication habits and, frequently, a gap in procedural fluency because the MYP rewarded explanation over drill. The fix is a short bridging block in the summer before DP1, which costs a fraction of a remedial term in the autumn.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students entering the Diploma also pick up Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies obligations that KHDA requires of all private schools in the emirate regardless of curriculum, so the DP1 week is tighter than the course list suggests.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-warqa.subjectsIntro: The Middle Years Programme organises learning into eight subject groups rather than discrete examined subjects. Below is each group with the criterion that most often holds an Al Warqa student's grade down, because that is where tutoring money should go.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing is the criterion that stalls. Students summarise the text and then offer an opinion, where the strand asks for the effect of a specific choice by the writer on a specific reader. Producing text and using language are usually sound; the analytical strand is the one costing marks, and it responds quickly to marked paragraphs.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Phase placement matters more than effort. A student working hard in a phase above their comfort will score low on comprehension strands regardless of input. Tutoring is worth buying only after the phase has been checked with the school, which is a free conversation that families skip.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigating and the evaluation of sources carry the losses. Students describe what a source says rather than what it is worth, and never state provenance, purpose or limitation. This is a technique gap, fixable in a handful of marked tasks, and expensive to leave until MYP 5.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Inquiring and designing is the criterion that sinks otherwise capable students. A hypothesis with no reasoning behind it, variables unnamed, and a method nobody could repeat will score poorly even where the practical work was executed well. The strand rewards planning documentation, which is teachable.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Communicating is where marks vanish. Correct answers presented without working, notation, units or a line of reasoning cannot earn the upper bands of the criterion. The content is rarely the issue in Al Warqa cohorts; the presentation of reasoning almost always is.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The design cycle is the whole assessment: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. Students build the product and neglect the documentation, which is where most of the available marks sit. A short block on the cycle is better value than ongoing weekly support.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Developing skills and thinking creatively are assessed through the process portfolio rather than the finished piece. Students who perform or paint well and document nothing score in the middle bands, which surprises families every single year.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Planning for performance and reflecting on performance are written criteria in a practical subject, and a capable athlete can be marked down for not evidencing either. Worth knowing before a parent concludes the grade reflects ability on the field.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed separately against their own criteria, requiring students to synthesise two subject groups. Marks are lost where the work stays inside one discipline and the synthesis is asserted rather than demonstrated.

subjects.name: Approaches to Learning
subjects.description: Not graded directly but embedded in every criterion: research skills, self-management, thinking, communication, social skills. Most of what a good MYP tutor actually teaches sits here, which is why the gains show up across several subjects at once rather than in the one you paid for.

sections.heading: What an MYP tutor in Al Warqa costs, and why the bill behaves differently
paragraphs: The hourly rates in Dubai do not change because a programme is called the Middle Years Programme. Reading across the providers that publish figures, in October 2026 the market ran from AED 45 at the budget end to AED 650 for premium named tutors, with qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. What changes is the duration of the commitment. An IGCSE arrangement ends with the June series. An MYP arrangement has no natural end at all.

That is the hidden cost. Two subjects supported weekly at mid-market rates is roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400 a month, and across five years of the programme the total is a figure most families have never written down. We are not arguing that the money is badly spent in every case; we are arguing that it should be spent against a stated condition. Before you begin, write down what has to change for the sessions to stop. If you cannot write it, the diagnosis is not finished.

The second difference is what the hour should contain. In the MYP, a session spent revising the content of the current unit frequently leaves all four assessment criteria untouched, because the criteria measure skills. A session spent on one criterion with the marked task sheet open can move a grade without covering any new content at all. The rate card is the same. The value is entirely in which of those two sessions you bought.

sections.heading: Five years priced out: where MYP money repays and where it does not
paragraphs: Treating the Middle Years Programme as one undifferentiated block of tutoring years is how households end up with the figures in the table below. The programme changes shape twice, and the right spend in MYP 2 is close to zero while the right spend in MYP 5 is concentrated and specific. Mapping it year by year turns a vague monthly outgoing into a plan with start and end points.

The early years repay short, skill-focused intervention and punish standing weekly slots. An eleven-year-old who has just met criterion marking for the first time needs somebody to explain what a descriptor is and how to write to one. That is two or three sessions. What they do not need is a tutor re-teaching the content of units their school is teaching perfectly well, which is the arrangement most families drift into because it is the one that is easy to buy.

The upper years invert that. By MYP 4 the criteria demand independent investigation, sustained written reasoning and documented process, and the grades begin to decide which Diploma courses a student can access at their own school. A weekly slot in one or two subjects is defensible here. So is a Personal Project block in MYP 5 and a bridging block in the summer before DP1, which is the cheapest insurance available against a remedial autumn term.

The arithmetic in the table uses the published mid-market band of AED 150 to 300 an hour throughout, so you can substitute your own rate and recalculate. What it is intended to show is not a recommended total but the difference between a planned five years and an unplanned one.

sections.heading: Why content tutoring is usually the wrong purchase in the MYP
paragraphs: A Middle Years Programme grade is built from four criterion marks, each out of eight, each describing a skill. In sciences the strands cover inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In mathematics they cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. None of those is a list of facts. A student can know everything in the unit and score in the middle bands on three of the four.

This is why the familiar Dubai tutoring product — an hour re-explaining the current topic — so often produces a confident child and an unchanged report. The hour was spent on knowing and understanding, which was already the student's strongest strand. The grade was being held down by communicating, which nobody looked at. Parents then conclude that more hours are needed, and the spending escalates in exactly the wrong direction.

The fix is cheap and begins with a document. Every MYP task comes with the criterion strands and the band descriptors the teacher marked against. Put that sheet in front of a tutor who knows the programme and the diagnosis takes most of one session. In the large eastern-suburb cohorts, where written feedback per student is necessarily short, that translation step is the whole of what an outside tutor usefully adds.

There is a second-order benefit worth paying for. Criterion skills transfer. A student who learns to evidence a method in sciences will evidence a method in design, and a student who learns to communicate reasoning in mathematics will communicate it in individuals and societies. One strand properly fixed tends to move several reports, which is not something content tutoring can claim.

sections.heading: What each criterion is worth, and what a low one looks like
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, each marked from zero to eight, giving thirty-two marks that the school converts to a one-to-seven grade using published boundaries. The letters mean different things in different subject groups, which is why a parent cannot read across from one report line to another, and why a tutor needs the subject's own descriptors rather than a general sense of the programme.

The practical value of knowing this is diagnostic. A student scoring sixes and sevens on criterion A and threes on criterion C is not a weak student; they are a student with one unaddressed skill. In our experience of eastern-suburb cohorts the recurring culprits are narrow: evidencing a method in sciences, communicating reasoning in mathematics, evaluating sources in individuals and societies, and analysing effect rather than summarising content in language and literature. Ask for the criterion marks themselves at every reporting cycle, not only the converted one-to-seven grade. Some Dubai schools publish the A to D breakdown only when a parent requests it, and without it a family is negotiating about a single number that hides the four marks behind it.

The table below sets out, for the subject groups we are asked about most from Al Warqa, the strand that most commonly holds a grade down and what a tutor should actually be doing about it. It is deliberately specific. A plan that says more practice is not a plan, and at AED 150 to 300 an hour it is not a plan worth paying for either.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: the MYP 5 block worth paying for
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the one place in the Middle Years Programme where a defined block of paid supervision reliably returns more than it costs. The reason is structural: the project is assessed on process rather than on the finished product, and the process evidence is the part students neglect. A beautifully built outcome with a journal written in one weekend scores poorly, and students are genuinely surprised by that every year.

What the assessment rewards is a clear goal with criteria for success stated at the outset, a research record that shows how decisions were made, evidence of the skills applied along the way, and a reflection that measures the outcome against the criteria the student set. All four of those are documentation habits. They cost almost nothing to build if the support is spread across the year and a great deal to reconstruct if it is not.

The academic-honesty line here is absolute and we state it to the student in the first session. A tutor may ask questions, challenge a weak goal, point out that a journal entry asserts something it does not evidence, and give feedback on the student's own writing. A tutor may not write the project, draft the journal, or edit the reflection to completion. Under IB rules that is malpractice and the consequences fall on the student, not on the tutor. Any provider offering to produce the work should be declined on that basis alone.

Practically, four to six sessions placed at the school's own milestones — goal setting, mid-project review, draft reflection, final check — is the shape that works. Spread that way it is a modest one-off cost against a component that appears on the MYP record and, more usefully, teaches the independent-project habits the Diploma Programme will demand twice over in the Extended Essay.

sections.heading: Where Al Warqa families overspend on the Middle Years Programme
paragraphs: The first overspend is the standing slot nobody reviews. An arrangement begun in MYP 2 because a report looked disappointing can still be running in MYP 5, at AED 600 to 1,200 a month, with no mechanism for deciding whether it is working. The remedy is a date in the calendar every six weeks and a marked piece of work to look at. If the strand that prompted the arrangement is no longer the low one, the arrangement has done its job.

The second is buying for the wrong child in the house. MYP reports are harder to read than percentage reports, and anxiety transfers easily from one sibling to another. We see households supporting three children weekly when the marked evidence justified it for one. Ask for the diagnostic on each child separately, and be prepared for the answer that two of them do not need anything.

The third is paying premium rates for a programme with no external examination. An examiner-led tutor at AED 650 an hour has expertise in marking external papers. The MYP, for most Dubai students, is marked internally by their own teachers against published criteria. The expertise that matters is familiarity with those criteria and with how the school applies them, which sits comfortably in the AED 150 to 300 band.

The fourth is leaving the Diploma transition to chance and then paying for a remedial autumn. Students arriving in DP1 from the MYP typically bring strong research and communication habits and thinner procedural fluency, because the programme rewarded explanation over repetition. Six to ten sessions in the summer on the algebra, calculation or essay-timing demands of their intended Higher Level subjects costs a fraction of catching up once DP1 has started.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group support compared for Al Warqa
paragraphs: Parents searching for an MYP tutor in Al Warqa generally picture someone arriving at the villa, so the market position deserves a direct answer. Dubai prices in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for an equivalent qualified tutor working online, and advertised in-home monthly packages of four two-hour sessions have run at AED 1,599 to 1,799. The difference is travel time converted into fee.

For the Middle Years Programme that premium buys less than it does elsewhere, because the tutor pool it restricts you to is already thin. MYP provision in the eastern suburbs is sparser than British-curriculum provision, so the number of tutors who both know criterion marking in a specific subject group and will drive to Al Warqa on a weekday evening is small. Choosing on geography in a thin market means choosing on the wrong variable.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors operate only in India. Sessions for Al Warqa families run one-to-one over live video to Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own marked task sheets shared on screen, which is the format that actually suits criterion work: the descriptor, the marked task and the student's redraft all visible at once. Group classes, meanwhile, suit content revision and cannot do criterion diagnosis at all, so they are a poor substitute for the two-session purchase this page recommends most often.

sections.heading: eAssessment, the MYP record and what any of it is worth
paragraphs: Some Dubai schools enter MYP 5 students for IB eAssessment, producing an externally validated MYP Certificate; many do not, and run the programme to its final year assessed entirely internally. Which of those your child's school does changes the shape of MYP 5 completely, and it is worth asking the coordinator directly rather than inferring it. Families who assume there is an external examination and then discover there is not have usually bought tutoring on a false premise. Whichever route the school has taken, get the answer in writing at the start of MYP 4, because the entry decision is made for a whole cohort and is rarely revisited for one student.

Where eAssessment is in play, the preparation resembles conventional examination preparation and the usual rules apply: past material, timing, command language, and the discipline of answering the question asked. Where it is not, the only marks that exist are the ones your child's own teachers award against the published criteria, and the tutoring brief is entirely about meeting those descriptors in the work the school sets.

Either way, the MYP record is not what a university will read. Its value is internal and immediate: it decides which Diploma courses the school will let a student take, and it builds or fails to build the habits the Diploma then tests. That is the honest frame for any spending decision in these five years. Money spent on a habit that carries into DP1 is money that works twice. Money spent to move a single internal grade from a five to a six, with nothing structural changed, works once and then stops.

process.title: Send the marked task, not the report card
process.description: The report tells us a grade. The marked task sheet, with the criterion strands and band descriptors the teacher used, tells us why. Send one or two of those along with your child's subject group and year, and the diagnosis can start in the first session rather than the third.

process.title: A diagnostic session at no cost
process.description: The first session is free and is spent naming the strand that is holding the grade down. You receive that in writing. For a meaningful number of Al Warqa families this is also the last session, because the instruction the student needed was a short one and the school is already doing the rest.

process.title: Decide the shape before the schedule
process.description: A two-session criterion diagnostic, a Personal Project supervision block, and a standing weekly slot in upper MYP are three different purchases at three different prices. We say which one the evidence supports, including when the answer is none of them, and the indicative cost at published market rates.

process.title: Write down the condition for stopping
process.description: Before the first paid session we agree what has to change for the arrangement to end: a specific criterion mark on a specific kind of task. This is the step that separates a plan from a subscription, and it is the single most useful thing on this page for a family at the start of a five-year programme.

process.title: Review every six weeks on marked evidence
process.description: At each review we look at marked work and recommend continuing, moving to another subject, or stopping. A tutor who never recommends stopping is not advising you. If the strand that prompted the arrangement is no longer the low one, we will say the work is done.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-first, not content-first
whyPoints.description: Sessions work from your child's marked tasks and the subject group's published strand descriptors, because that is what the grade is actually built from. An hour of content revision in the MYP frequently leaves all four assessed skills untouched, which is how families end up paying more for less movement.

whyPoints.title: A stated exit condition on every arrangement
whyPoints.description: The Middle Years Programme has no external examination date to end a tutoring arrangement, so we write the ending into the beginning. You will know before the first invoice what has to change for the sessions to stop, which is the discipline this programme lacks by design.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project line is drawn out loud
whyPoints.description: A tutor questions, challenges and gives feedback on your child's own work. We do not write, draft or edit to completion any project, journal or reflection submitted for assessment. Under IB academic-honesty rules the consequences of that fall on the student, and any provider offering it should be refused.

whyPoints.title: No published syllabus material supplied
whyPoints.description: Subject guides, criterion documents and assessment material are published by the International Baccalaureate and should be obtained from the organisation or from your child's coordinator. We reference and explain them; we do not reproduce or distribute them.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered without evasion
whyPoints.description: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Ask any tutor to show theirs. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK or Ministry of Education approval and makes no claim to any.

whyPoints.title: Advice that reduces the invoice
whyPoints.description: On a page about five years of spending it would be inconsistent to recommend weekly sessions for every child who arrives with a middling report. Where the marked evidence does not support paid support, we say so, and we have ended arrangements on that basis.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for MYP tutoring in Al Warqa over the whole programme?
faqs.answer: Less than most families end up spending, if it is planned. At published Dubai rates of AED 150 to 300 an hour, a weekly slot is AED 600 to 1,200 a month per subject. Our recommendation for the eastern suburbs is near-zero standing spend in MYP 1 to 3 beyond a one-off criterion diagnostic, a single weekly subject in MYP 4 and 5 chosen on marked evidence, a Personal Project block of four to six sessions, and a short bridging block before DP1. That shape typically totals a fraction of five unplanned years.

faqs.question: Why did a term of weekly tutoring not change my child's MYP grade?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the hour was spent on the wrong criterion. MYP subjects are marked against four strands, each out of eight, and each one measures a skill rather than a body of knowledge. If the sessions covered content and the grade was being held down by communicating or by inquiring and designing, the report will not move however many hours you buy. Ask what strand each session addressed. If the tutor cannot name one, the diagnosis never happened and you were paying for revision your school had already delivered.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for MYP support in Year 7 or Year 8?
faqs.answer: Rarely as a standing arrangement. What is worth buying at that age is two or three sessions teaching the student how to read a criterion descriptor and write to it, because that skill applies to all eight subject groups and lasts the full five years. Weekly content tutoring for an eleven-year-old whose school is covering the units competently is the clearest example of MYP overspending we see in Al Warqa households. Keep the money for MYP 4 and 5, where the criteria demand sustained independent work and the grades start to matter.

faqs.question: What does Personal Project supervision cost, and is it a good buy?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions spread across MYP 5 at mid-market rates comes to roughly AED 600 to 1,800 in total, and it is one of the few MYP purchases we recommend without hesitation. The project is assessed on process, and students lose marks on documentation rather than on the outcome they built. Support spaced across the year builds the journal and the research record as they happen, which costs very little. Reconstructing them in the final fortnight costs a great deal and still scores poorly.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my child's Personal Project?
faqs.answer: No, and you should not accept an offer to. A tutor may question a weak goal, point out where a journal entry asserts something it does not evidence, and give feedback on writing the student has produced. Writing, drafting or editing the project to completion is malpractice under IB academic-honesty rules and the consequences fall on the student. Any provider advertising a completed project should be declined on that basis. We state this line to the student directly in the first supervision session so there is no ambiguity later.

faqs.question: Do we need separate tutors for the eight MYP subject groups?
faqs.answer: No, and the question points at the overspending risk in this programme. Much of what a good MYP tutor teaches sits in the approaches-to-learning skills shared across every group: research records, self-management, structuring written reasoning, documenting a process. One tutor working on the recurring low strand will usually move several reports at once. Buy a second subject specialist only where the marked evidence names a specific content gap, not because four of the eight report lines look average.

faqs.question: What is MYP eAssessment and does it change what we should pay for?
faqs.answer: It is the optional externally validated route at the end of MYP 5, leading to an IB MYP Certificate. Some Dubai schools enter candidates and many do not. It changes the brief completely: where eAssessment applies, preparation looks like conventional examination work with timing and command language mattering; where it does not, the only marks that exist are internal ones awarded against published criteria. Ask your child's coordinator which applies before buying anything for MYP 5, because families regularly plan for an examination that is not happening.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject most often needs paid support in the upper years?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, followed by sciences. In mathematics the recurring loss is the communicating criterion: correct answers with no notation, no units and no visible reasoning cannot reach the upper bands. In sciences it is inquiring and designing, where hypotheses arrive without reasoning and variables go unnamed. Both are presentation-of-thinking problems rather than content problems, which is good news for a budget because they respond to a handful of properly marked tasks rather than to a year of lessons.

faqs.question: Is an in-home MYP tutor in Al Warqa worth the extra money?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market charges roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for in-home visits against AED 150 to 300 for an equivalent qualified tutor online, and the gap is travel priced into the hour. For the Middle Years Programme the premium buys less than usual, because provision in the eastern suburbs is thin and insisting on someone who will drive to Al Warqa narrows an already small pool of tutors who know criterion marking in your child's subject group. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; sessions run over live video to Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: How do we know when to stop paying for MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: Write the condition down before you start. A usable one names a strand and a task type: criterion C at six or above on two consecutive mathematics investigations, for instance. Then review marked work every six weeks against it. Because the MYP has no external examination date, nothing else will end the arrangement for you, and an unreviewed weekly slot can run for years. A tutor who never recommends stopping is selling rather than advising, and that is worth noticing early.

faqs.question: Our two children are in MYP 3 and MYP 5. Should we support both?
faqs.answer: Diagnose them separately and expect different answers. MYP 5 with a Personal Project and Diploma course selection ahead is a reasonable place to spend; MYP 3 with a competent school and no repeated low strand usually is not. Anxiety about one child's report transfers easily to a sibling, and we regularly meet Al Warqa households paying for three weekly slots where the marked evidence supported one. One tutor can cover both children in consecutive sessions if the subject groups are compatible, which reduces switching cost without pretending two children fit in one hour.

faqs.question: Why does my child score highly on criterion A and poorly on criterion C?
faqs.answer: Because those letters measure different things, and your child has one skill and not the other. Criterion A in most subject groups rewards knowing and understanding, which is what traditional schooling trains. The later criteria reward investigation, communication of reasoning, evaluation and reflection, which are taught less explicitly and assessed heavily. A gap of that shape is a good outcome diagnostically: it is narrow, it is nameable, and it is usually fixed by a small number of marked tasks rather than by a change of school or a year of lessons.

faqs.question: Does the MYP record matter to universities later?
faqs.answer: Not directly. What it decides is internal and immediate: which Diploma Programme courses your child's own school will permit them to take, particularly at Higher Level, and how well prepared they are for the independent work the Diploma demands. That is the honest frame for spending in these five years. Money that buys a habit carrying into DP1 — documented research, reasoned written method, a project managed over months — works twice. Money that lifts one internal grade with nothing structural changed works once.

faqs.question: How does the Dubai mandatory-subject requirement affect an MYP week?
faqs.answer: It fills more of it than the subject list suggests. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students. An MYP student in Al Warqa therefore carries eight subject groups plus those obligations, and the realistic amount of discretionary evening study time is smaller than parents assume. Plan the week before adding a tutoring slot to it.

faqs.question: What if no MYP specialist is available in our child's subject group?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting a general tutor and hoping. MYP criterion marking in a specific subject group is a narrower skill than it sounds, and a tutor who does not know the strands will spend the hour on content. If no UAE-based tutor matches, we look across our wider pool, including tutors in India teaching the same programme to Gulf Standard Time. If that still does not produce a match, we say the need is unmet and suggest asking the school coordinator what internal support exists.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-warqa.closingHeading: Buy the diagnosis, then decide whether to buy anything else
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-warqa.closingBody: If your child is in the Middle Years Programme at a school near Al Warqa and the reports are not what you hoped, the useful first purchase is not a weekly slot. It is one session with the marked task sheet open, naming the criterion that is holding the grade down and what to do about it this week. Send the subject group, the year and one marked task, and the trial session is at no cost. A meaningful number of families get an answer that costs them nothing further, and on a page about five years of spending that outcome is the point rather than an embarrassment.

intro.heading: MYP marks are letters and eights, and that changes what tutoring is for
paragraphs: The first thing to understand about the Middle Years Programme is that it does not mark the way the school report implies. There is no running percentage. Each subject is assessed against four lettered criteria, each one scored from 0 to 8, and the four scores are added and converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. A student can be strong on two criteria and weak on two and come out looking mediocre, with nobody in the household able to say which half was the problem.

That is the gap an IB MYP tutor in Al Wasl is genuinely useful for. The criteria are published, they are specific, and they are different in each subject group. In MYP Mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In MYP Sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Those are not the same skill asked four ways; they are four separate things, and a student who has only ever been taught the first one will plateau at the same grade indefinitely.

Al Wasl families meet this most often in two places. The first is MYP 4, when tasks get longer and the criteria that reward process rather than recall start to dominate. The second is MYP 5, where eAssessment and the Personal Project arrive together and the student discovers that the thing being judged is their documentation of their thinking, not only the output. Both are coachable, and both are badly served by generic homework help.

The subject-level detail is where this page spends its time, because that is what the brief for this page asks for and because it is the thing the Al Wasl market does not publish. Competitor pages for Dubai MYP tutoring treat the programme as a label. None of the pages we examined names a single criterion letter, and none explains that a criterion is marked against a descriptor with specific verbs in it. A parent who reads the descriptor for criterion C in their child's subject learns more in five minutes than a term of parents' evenings provides.

On delivery, be clear from the start: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we run only in India. MYP tuition for Al Wasl runs online, one-to-one, over live video. For criterion work this is not a compromise but an advantage, because the task sheet, the descriptor table and the student's own draft can all sit on a shared screen while the tutor points at the exact sentence that is not earning the mark.

The pages next to this one take different routes through the same neighbourhood. The Al Wasl science and physics pages work from the exam calendar and the paper structure; the home-tutor pages compare Al Wasl with the communities either side of it. This page works from the assessment model, because for a Middle Years student the assessment model is the thing nobody has explained.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-wasl.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme spans five years in most Dubai schools, and the tutoring question changes sharply between the start and the end of it. Naming the year your child is actually in prevents a lot of wasted money.

programmes.name: MYP 1 to 3, the early years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, criterion-referenced from the first term, with shorter tasks and more scaffolding. Students at this stage usually understand the content and lose marks on the shape of the response: no statement of inquiry referenced, no reflection, no evaluation of method. These are habits of writing rather than gaps in knowledge, which is why they are cheap to fix here and expensive to fix later.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Wasl most MYP 1 to 3 students are in an IB continuum school a short drive away, which means the school day ends early enough for a weekly session without a long commute. This is the stage at which families almost never book a tutor, and the stage at which a single term of criterion work pays for itself most clearly.

programmes.name: MYP 4, where the criteria start to bite
programmes.description: Tasks lengthen, the process criteria carry more weight, and subject choices begin narrowing towards the Diploma. Mathematics splits into standard and extended routes in many schools, and sciences begin to separate. The student who has coasted on recall meets criterion B in sciences or criterion D in mathematics and discovers that nobody ever taught them how to design an investigation or justify a real-world application.
programmes.countryNote: This is the most common point at which an Al Wasl household first asks for MYP help. The usual presentation is a grade that has slipped from a 6 to a 5 with no obvious cause, and the usual finding is two criteria carrying the whole loss. One session with the mark breakdown in front of us normally identifies which two.

programmes.name: MYP 5, eAssessment and the Personal Project
programmes.description: The final year carries the Personal Project plus, in schools that offer it, MYP eAssessment through on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate. Deadlines cluster, and the Personal Project process journal has to be maintained across months rather than produced at the end. The commonest failure is a good project with thin documentation of planning and reflection.
programmes.countryNote: Al Wasl students in MYP 5 are often simultaneously deciding between the Diploma and A Levels, because several schools in the Al Safa and Jumeirah cluster run one route and not the other. That decision and the Personal Project land in the same months, which is why the autumn term of MYP 5 is the busiest slot we are asked for here.

programmes.name: The MYP to Diploma bridge
programmes.description: The Diploma asks for things the MYP deliberately does not: timed written examinations with heavy recall, Higher Level depth in three subjects, and an Internal Assessment judged against criteria that look familiar but are marked far more strictly. The gap is widest in mathematics and the sciences, where DP1 assumes algebraic fluency that criterion-referenced MYP tasks did not force.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Wasl families moving from an MYP school into a Diploma school, the useful window is the summer between MYP 5 and DP1. Six to eight sessions of algebra and examination-style practice in that window removes most of the first-term shock, and it costs less than remediation in DP1 does.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-wasl.subjectsIntro: These are the MYP subject groups, with the criterion letters that apply in each and the places Al Wasl students most often lose marks. Read the ones your child studies; the criterion names are the vocabulary the rest of this page uses.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Most lost marks sit in B and D: students who can compute will not generalise a pattern into a rule, and will not justify the degree of accuracy of a real-world answer.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B is the usual gap: a research question stated without variables, a method without a control, a hypothesis that is a prediction with no reasoning attached.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria A analysing, B organising, C producing text, D using language. Strong readers often lose criterion A marks by retelling the text instead of analysing how a choice creates an effect, and criterion B marks by writing without a visible structure the examiner can follow.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, assessed by phase rather than by year group. Students placed in the wrong phase lose marks that look like weak language and are really a placement problem, which is worth checking before booking any tutoring at all.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D is where the grade is decided: sources have to be evaluated for origin, purpose, value and limitation, and most students summarise the source instead of judging it.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Criteria A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The design cycle is the assessment, so a working product with no documented research, specification or testing against that specification scores poorly however good the product is.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Criteria A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. The process portfolio carries much of the mark, and students who make good work without recording their experimentation and their response to feedback cap themselves on A and B.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. Written criteria A, B and D carry marks that surprise sporting students and their parents, since performance alone touches only criterion C.

subjects.name: MYP Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed with its own criteria on disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. Students treat these units as a lighter task; they are marked as a separate set of criteria and can move a reported grade, so they deserve the same preparation as any single-subject assessment.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on planning, applying skills, and reflecting, with the process journal as the main evidence. The object produced is not what earns the grade; the documented thinking around it is, which is why a strong maker with a thin journal often scores below a modest maker with a full one.

regions.note: The Al Wasl Road corridor between Safa Park and the Jumeirah side. Short runs to the local IB and British secondaries mean a 4.30pm MYP session is realistic most weekdays, which suits the shorter attention span of a younger Middle Years student.

regions.name: Al Safa 1
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, sharing the same catchment. Households here often have one child in MYP and one in IGCSE, so the common booking is two different subjects in consecutive slots on the same evening.

regions.name: Al Safa 2

sections.heading: What the criterion letters actually ask for, subject by subject
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single MYP criterion. That is a strange omission, because the criteria are the assessment and they are published. A parent who reads the descriptor for the criterion their child is losing marks on usually understands the problem immediately, and often recognises it as something the child has been doing wrong for two years without anybody isolating it.

The pattern across subject groups is worth seeing whole. Criterion A is almost always knowing and understanding, which is the closest thing the MYP has to a traditional recall mark. Criterion B is typically process: inquiring and designing in sciences, investigating patterns in mathematics, investigating in individuals and societies, developing ideas in design. Criterion C is usually communication or production, and criterion D is usually evaluation, reflection or application to a real context.

That structure explains a common Al Wasl parent experience. A child who is good at school in the conventional sense scores well on A, respectably on C, and poorly on B and D, producing a middling overall grade that nobody can account for. The grade is not a verdict on ability; it is a verdict on two specific untaught skills. Teach the structure of a research question and the structure of a reflection, and two criteria move at once.

The table below sets the criteria out by subject group so a parent can find their child's subject and read the four things being judged. The descriptors themselves are in the IB's subject guides, which belong to the IB and which schools hold; ask your child's coordinator for the relevant descriptor table rather than relying on a third-party summary, including this one.

sections.heading: How four scores out of eight become a grade out of seven
paragraphs: Each criterion is marked from 0 to 8 against level descriptors, which means the maximum total for a subject is 32. That total is then converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries the IB publishes and schools apply. The arithmetic matters because it tells a family where the marginal mark is cheapest to win.

Consider a student sitting on 6, 4, 6, 4 across the four criteria. The total is 20. The two weak criteria are costing eight marks between them, and moving each by two levels adds four marks to the total. Compare that with pushing criterion A from 6 to 8, which is hard, competitive and worth two marks. Almost always the cheapest marks available are on the criterion the student scores lowest on, and almost always the student wants to practise the one they already do well.

The second consequence is that a single bad task does not sink a grade in the way a bad test does under a percentage system. Criterion scores are judged on best-fit across the body of work in the reporting period, which schools interpret according to their own assessment policy. That is a reason to ask the school how it determines the reported criterion level rather than to assume the last task decides it.

What a tutor does with this is simple and specific. We look at the marked tasks, find the criterion with the lowest level, read the descriptor for the level above, and teach exactly the difference between where the student is and where that descriptor sits. That is a narrow, finishable piece of work, and it is far more useful than general subject revision.

sections.heading: MYP 5: eAssessment, ePortfolios and the Certificate
paragraphs: In the final MYP year some schools enter students for MYP eAssessment, which combines on-screen examinations with ePortfolios and leads to the IB MYP Certificate. Other authorised MYP schools do not enter candidates at all and instead report school-based grades. Those two situations produce completely different final years, and the first useful question for any Al Wasl family in MYP 4 is which one their school runs.

Where eAssessment applies, the on-screen examinations are a genuinely different experience from the task-based assessment of earlier years. They are time-bounded, they present unfamiliar stimulus material, and they reward students who can read a prompt quickly and structure a response under pressure. A student who has produced excellent extended work across four years can still be unprepared for that, because nothing in MYP 1 to 4 necessarily practises it.

The ePortfolio route works the other way. It rewards sustained documentation: evidence of process, of experimentation, of response to feedback, gathered over months. Students lose marks here not because the work is weak but because the record of the work is thin. A tutor's job in an ePortfolio subject is mostly to keep asking whether the evidence exists yet, which is unglamorous and effective.

Either way, the practical advice for an Al Wasl household is the same. Establish in MYP 4 which route applies, ask the coordinator what the internal deadlines are, and put them in a household calendar. The commonest avoidable disaster in MYP 5 is not weak work; it is a deadline that arrived while a family assumed there was another term.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and where honest help stops
paragraphs: The Personal Project is assessed on planning, on applying skills, and on reflecting. The object the student makes is evidence, not the grade. This catches out capable students constantly: a beautifully finished product with a journal written in the last fortnight scores below a modest product with months of recorded thinking behind it.

The process journal is therefore the centre of the work. It needs to show the goal being set and refined, the research being done and judged, the obstacles being met and responded to, and the student's own assessment of what they achieved against what they intended. None of that can be reconstructed convincingly after the fact, which is why supervision across the whole window beats intensive help at the end.

Here is the boundary, stated plainly because the market around us is not always clear about it. A tutor may ask the questions a supervisor asks, point out where the journal has no evidence of a criterion, read the student's draft report and say which section does not meet the descriptor, and teach the skills the project needs. A tutor may not write any part of the project, the journal or the report, and may not dictate sentences for a student to transcribe. The work has to be the student's own, and the consequences of it not being so fall on the student.

One seller in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Treat any similar offer about a Personal Project the same way: as a reason to stop the conversation. The grade is not worth the risk, and a student who has outsourced the project enters the Diploma without the skills the project exists to build.
