sections.heading: The MYP to Diploma gap, named subject by subject
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme and the Diploma are both IB programmes and they assess almost opposite things. The MYP asks for process, documentation, reflection and application, assessed over extended tasks. The Diploma asks for recall under time pressure, technical fluency and Higher Level depth, assessed mostly by terminal written examinations with one Internal Assessment per subject. A student who has thrived under the first model can struggle badly in the first term of the second.

The gap is widest in mathematics. MYP mathematics rewards investigation and communication; Diploma Mathematics Analysis and Approaches assumes algebraic manipulation is automatic and spends its time on calculus, functions and proof. A student who has always had time and a calculator meets Paper 1 without one, and the problem looks like weak mathematics when it is really absent fluency.

In the sciences the gap is content volume and quantitative work. Diploma Chemistry and Physics carry substantially more material than MYP sciences, examined in timed papers with command terms the MYP does not use in the same way. In the humanities and languages the gap is narrower, because extended writing transfers well, but timed essay writing still has to be practised specifically.

For an Al Wasl family the actionable version is this: identify the two subjects your child intends to take at Higher Level, and spend the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 on the specific fluency those two assume. Six to eight sessions is usually enough. It is the single best-value block in this entire page, and almost nobody books it.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs in Dubai, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Work up from the bottom of the market, because for Middle Years support the cheap end is more often adequate than it is at Diploma level. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; the budget online and university-student band overall runs AED 45 to 150. For an MYP 1 to 3 student who needs homework structure and someone to check that a reflection has actually been written, that band can genuinely be enough.

Above it, qualified online subject tutors run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is the band where criterion-level work becomes realistic, because it requires a tutor who has read the subject guide rather than one who knows the content. For MYP 4 and 5, and for anything touching eAssessment or the Personal Project, this is the honest starting point.

The specialist band, AED 200 to 450 and above, is quoted by TutorChase at AED 270 and by Bestimate at AED 200 to 450 plus; premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, sit at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching AED 500. On monthly figures, Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work; advertised packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

Each of those figures belongs to the provider named beside it. None is an IB Gram rate, and we do not put a price list on a landing page because the answer depends on the subject group, the year and the number of weeks. For context a parent can check independently, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for 2026-27, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

sections.heading: Online delivery, and the Al Wasl afternoon it has to fit into
paragraphs: IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, and MYP tuition for Al Wasl is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For criterion work that format carries a specific advantage worth spelling out, rather than being defended as an acceptable substitute.

Criterion assessment is about documents. A task sheet, a descriptor table, a marked draft, a process journal entry. All four can be on a shared screen simultaneously, with the tutor's cursor on the exact sentence that fails the descriptor and the student's own typing visible as they revise it. In a room with a single sheet of paper, that comparison is much harder to hold. Screen sharing is the right tool for this particular job.

The Al Wasl timing picture is favourable. The neighbourhood sits close to its main IB and British secondaries, so arrival home is earlier than in most Dubai communities and a 4.30pm start is usually workable, with 4pm possible from the Safa Park end. Middle Years students have shorter concentration spans than Diploma students, so a focused 60 minutes early in the afternoon beats a 90-minute session at 7pm. Avoiding a commute at both ends is most of what makes that possible.

The trade-offs should be stated rather than glossed. A younger MYP student may need a parent in the room for the first sessions to stay on task. Handwritten mathematics working needs a visible writing surface, so a tilted phone or a document camera is worth setting up before the first paid lesson. And a household with a weak connection should find that out on the free trial. None of those is fatal and all are easier to solve in advance than in week three.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects, and the shape of an MYP week in Dubai
paragraphs: KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it inspects private schools annually on a six-band scale. Elsewhere in the country the map differs: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

For a Middle Years student in Dubai the mandatory subject rules shape the week directly. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited.

KHDA also sets the language of instruction: Standard Arabic for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length if total weekly time is met, and any mandatory subject lesson is advised to run at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited.

Put together with eight MYP subject groups, this is a full week. Dubai's private sector is also expanding: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. For a parent planning tutoring, the operational conclusion is modest and reliable: one protected hour a week on a named criterion outperforms an ambitious schedule the household cannot keep.

sections.heading: Permits, and what an Al Wasl parent is entitled to ask
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and asking about it is reasonable rather than rude. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. It lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified until a parent can find it on an official source.

A related point applies specifically to Middle Years families, who are often tempted by the idea of their child's own subject teacher. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy, but it is a clear enough signal to avoid the arrangement.

Finally, the distinction between an individual tutor and an institution. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps. IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no UAE premises. We are an online matching platform, and describing ourselves as anything else would be a misrepresentation rather than marketing.

process.description: The two things that make a plan possible are which MYP subject group your child studies and a recent marked task with the criterion levels on it. Year group alone tells us almost nothing, because the same year contains students with completely different criterion profiles.

process.description: The first session produces a short written note naming which criterion letters are low, what the descriptor one level above asks for, and which skill will be taught first. That note is the plan, and it makes progress checkable rather than a matter of impression.

process.title: Fixed slots on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are booked on GST around the Al Wasl school run, typically from 4.30pm on weekdays with weekend mornings available for Personal Project work. During Ramadan slots shift later, including post-Iftar timings, and that is agreed in advance rather than improvised.

process.title: Progress measured on the next marked task
process.description: The test of a block is whether the targeted criterion level moved on a real school assessment. We ask to see the next marked task and compare. If the level has not moved, the plan changes or the tutor does, rather than the block simply continuing.

process.description: Some MYP combinations are narrow, particularly in language acquisition phases and specific arts disciplines. If nobody suitable is free in your window we will say so rather than putting a generalist in the slot, and we will tell you where the tutor is based.

whyPoints.title: We work in criterion letters, not in topic lists
whyPoints.description: Every session names the criterion it is about. That is the vocabulary the MYP marks in, and it is the reason a block of tutoring can be judged as successful or not rather than merely felt to be useful.

whyPoints.title: The subject guide is the reference, not a textbook
whyPoints.description: Criterion descriptors differ by subject group, and a tutor working from a general textbook cannot target them. Our match is on whether the tutor has taught the specific subject group against its own published criteria.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project stays the student's work
whyPoints.description: Supervision means questioning, reviewing and teaching. Nobody writes a journal entry or a report section for a student. We state that explicitly because providers in this market openly sell the opposite.

faqs.question: What exactly is the MYP marked on, if there are no percentages?
faqs.answer: Each MYP subject is assessed against four lettered criteria, A to D, and each criterion is marked from 0 to 8 against published level descriptors. The four scores add to a maximum of 32, which is converted to a reported grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. The criterion names differ by subject group: in mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Ask your child's coordinator for the descriptor table for their subjects. It is the single most useful document a Middle Years parent can read.

faqs.question: My child's MYP grade dropped from a 6 to a 5 and nobody can tell me why. What do I do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the criterion-level breakdown rather than the grade. Almost every unexplained MYP grade drop turns out to be two specific criteria falling while the other two hold, and the two that fall are usually the process and evaluation criteria rather than knowledge. Once you know which letters are low, read the descriptor for the level immediately above and you will usually recognise the problem. That is a narrow and finishable piece of work for a tutor, which is why a diagnostic session on marked tasks is worth more than a term of general subject help.

faqs.question: Which MYP criteria do students in Al Wasl most often lose marks on?
faqs.answer: The process and evaluation criteria, consistently. In sciences that is criterion B, inquiring and designing, where a research question appears without variables and a method without a control. In mathematics it is criterion B, investigating patterns, and criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, where students compute correctly but will not generalise or justify. In individuals and societies it is criterion D, thinking critically, where sources are summarised instead of evaluated. All three are structural writing skills rather than content gaps, which is why they respond quickly to direct teaching.

faqs.question: How much does an IB MYP tutor in Al Wasl cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market figures in Dubai, each attributed to its publisher: budget online and student tutors run AED 45 to 150, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 budget and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range. None of these is an IB Gram price; ask for a quote after the free trial, against a stated plan.

faqs.question: Does my child's school enter students for MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Some authorised MYP schools do and some do not, and the answer changes the whole of MYP 5. Where eAssessment applies, it combines on-screen examinations with ePortfolios and leads to the IB MYP Certificate; where it does not, the school reports its own criterion-based grades. Ask the MYP coordinator directly, ideally while your child is in MYP 4 rather than MYP 5. If on-screen examinations are coming, timed response under pressure needs practising specifically, because nothing in the earlier MYP years necessarily builds it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP Personal Project without doing it for my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction is sharp. A tutor can ask the questions a supervisor asks, point out where the process journal holds no evidence of a required criterion, read your child's own draft report and say which section falls short of the descriptor, and teach the research or technical skills the project needs. A tutor cannot write any part of the journal, the report or the project, and must not dictate sentences for a student to transcribe. Any provider offering to produce the project is offering an academic-integrity breach whose consequences fall on your child.

faqs.question: What is the Personal Project actually assessed on?
faqs.answer: Planning, applying skills, and reflecting. The object your child makes is evidence, not the grade. That is why a beautifully finished product with a journal written in the final fortnight can score below a modest product with months of recorded thinking behind it. The journal needs to show the goal being set and refined, research being judged rather than collected, obstacles being met, and the student assessing what they achieved against what they intended. None of that reconstructs convincingly after the fact, so supervision across the whole window matters more than help at the end.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from MYP 5 to the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Larger than the shared IB branding suggests, because the two programmes assess nearly opposite things. The MYP rewards process, documentation and application over extended tasks; the Diploma rewards recall and technical fluency under timed examination conditions. The gap is widest in mathematics, where Analysis and Approaches assumes automatic algebraic manipulation and includes non-calculator papers, and in the sciences, where content volume rises sharply. Six to eight sessions in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1, aimed at the two intended Higher Level subjects, removes most of the first-term shock.

faqs.question: What time can an MYP session start for a family in Al Wasl?
faqs.answer: Al Wasl sits close to its main IB and British secondaries, so arrival home is earlier than in most Dubai communities and a 4.30pm start works on most weekdays, with 4pm possible from the Safa Park end. From Jumeirah 3 and Umm Suqeim the first realistic slot drifts to 5pm. Middle Years students concentrate better earlier, so one focused hour in the late afternoon beats a longer evening session. Slots are booked on Gulf Standard Time and shift later during Ramadan, including post-Iftar timings, agreed in advance.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover several MYP subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Often the better answer is one tutor working on one criterion across several subjects. Students frequently lose marks on the same underlying skill in three places: inquiring and designing in sciences, investigating in individuals and societies, and investigating patterns in mathematics all ask for a researchable question and a structured method. A short block on that single skill can move several reported grades together. Where the problem is genuinely subject-specific content, a specialist in that subject group is the right choice instead.

faqs.question: Is my child in the right MYP language acquisition phase?
faqs.answer: It is worth checking before buying any tutoring, because a placement problem looks exactly like weak language. Language acquisition is assessed in phases rather than by year group, with criteria A listening, B reading, C speaking and D writing. A student placed above their actual level loses marks across all four criteria and reads the result as personal failure; one placed below plateaus. Ask the coordinator which phase your child is in and on what evidence. If the placement looks wrong, that conversation is more valuable than a term of lessons.

faqs.question: Why would an Al Wasl family choose online MYP tutoring over someone local?
faqs.answer: Criterion work is document work, and documents live better on a shared screen than on a single sheet of paper between two people. The task sheet, the descriptor table, the marked draft and the journal entry can all be visible at once, with the tutor's cursor on the sentence that is not earning the mark. The pool argument matters too: accepting live video means choosing from everyone who has taught that specific MYP subject group against its own criteria, not only from those willing to drive to Al Wasl at 4.30pm.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send an MYP tutor to our home in Al Wasl?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing, a shared whiteboard and a session recording your child can revisit. We target the home-tutor phrasing because that is what parents search for, and then answer it honestly instead of implying a service we do not sell. The in-home market does exist in Dubai and is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour if you prefer that format.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory UAE subjects fit alongside eight MYP subject groups?
faqs.answer: They sit on top of them. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and calculating instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. With eight MYP subject groups already in the timetable, the week is genuinely full. That is the practical reason one protected weekly hour on a named criterion works better than an ambitious multi-session plan.

faqs.question: Do MYP interdisciplinary units really affect my child's grade?
faqs.answer: They are assessed against their own separate criteria on disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting, and they are reported. Students routinely treat them as a lighter task because they do not belong to a single subject, then lose marks on exactly the reflective and synthesising elements the unit exists to test. Prepare them the way you would prepare any assessed task: read the criteria, check what evidence each one needs, and make sure the written response addresses all of them rather than describing the activity that was done.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to tutor my child if they teach at their school?
faqs.answer: Treat it as an arrangement to avoid. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document, but the direction is unambiguous. Separately, any private tutor needs the MoHRE permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-wasl.closingHeading: Find the criterion letter, then book the trial
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-wasl.closingBody: The useful first step costs nothing. Find a recent marked MYP task and look for the criterion levels on it, A to D, each out of 8. Identify the lowest one. Then ask your child's coordinator for the descriptor table and read the level immediately above where your child sits. That paragraph is the whole of the work in front of you, and it is usually narrower than a parent expects. Book a free trial lesson on that same task sheet and watch whether the tutor can explain the difference in a way your child recognises. Lessons run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, around the Al Wasl school run.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Middle Years Programme subjects from MYP 1 to MYP 5, by criterion rather than by topic. Each works from the student's own marked task sheets and task-specific clarifications, and can show a student exactly what moves a criterion level from a four to a six in their subject group.

intro.heading: Reading the report card is the first piece of teaching
paragraphs: An MYP report from a Dubai school does not look like a British or American one. There is no percentage. There is a set of criterion levels, usually four per subject, each awarded on a scale of nought to eight, and a final grade from one to seven that is derived from them. A parent in Arabian Ranches looking at sciences with a six on criterion A and a three on criterion C has been given a precise diagnosis and almost no help interpreting it. That gap is where most MYP tutoring enquiries start.

The criteria are not arbitrary. Each subject group has four of them, and they measure genuinely different things. In sciences, criterion A is knowing and understanding, criterion B is inquiring and designing, criterion C is processing and evaluating, and criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science. A student scoring well on A and badly on B does not have a science problem; they have an experimental design problem. The content revision that an anxious family buys first will not move criterion B at all, because criterion B is not about content.

Mathematics works the same way with different labels. Criterion A is knowing and understanding, criterion B is investigating patterns, criterion C is communicating, and criterion D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student who can do the exercises and cannot write up an investigation is losing criterion B and C marks while being entirely competent at the mathematics. Again, more practice questions will not help. What helps is being shown what an investigation that scores six or seven on criterion B actually contains.

Families around the Ranches reach the Middle Years Programme at a handful of campuses: Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Emirates International School Meadows, GEMS International School Al Khail in Dubai Hills Estate, Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Nord Anglia International School Dubai. JESS Arabian Ranches, inside the community, runs the English National Curriculum through IGCSE instead and then moves to the IB Diploma, so a Ranches household can contain one child on criterion-based marking and one on percentages in the same week.

IB Gram teaches the Middle Years Programme live over video, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For MYP work the online format fits the task well, because almost everything being assessed is a piece of written or designed work that can be opened, annotated and rebuilt on a shared screen while the task-specific clarifications sit beside it. The practical effect is that a session is spent on the student's actual task rather than on a textbook example of a similar one, which is the difference between understanding a criterion and being able to satisfy it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme sits between two other IB programmes and ends with a choice. Each stage below is described by what it assesses, because the assessment model is the thing that changes when a child moves between them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria on a scale of nought to eight, giving a maximum total of 32 criterion levels per subject. That total converts to a grade from one to seven against published boundaries. Units are framed by a statement of inquiry built from a key concept, related concepts and one of six global contexts, with approaches to learning skills taught alongside the content.
programmes.countryNote: In the Ranches belt the Middle Years Programme is run at Fairgreen International School, Emirates International School Meadows, GEMS International School Al Khail, Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Nord Anglia International School Dubai. Each school sets its own task calendar and writes its own task-specific clarifications, which is why a tutor needs the actual task sheet rather than a general syllabus.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, finishing with the PYP exhibition. There are no criterion levels in the MYP sense, so the first MYP report a family receives is usually their first encounter with the four-criteria model. The transferable skill from the PYP is inquiry habit; the new demand in MYP 1 is written communication against published descriptors.
programmes.countryNote: Several Ranches-belt campuses run the full continuum, so a child can move from PYP into MYP without changing school. Families transferring in from a British primary, including Ranches Primary School in Arabian Ranches 2, meet both the criteria and the inquiry framing at the same time, which is the harder of the two transitions.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Assessment moves to externally marked examinations with an internal assessment component, so the science and mathematics courses are weighted at Paper 1, Paper 2 and an internal task rather than at four criteria.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 students in the Ranches belt usually continue into the Diploma at the same school or move to a Diploma campus nearby. The step is smaller than it looks for students who have taken criterion C in mathematics and criteria B and C in sciences seriously, because those are the direct ancestors of Diploma internal assessment.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with a career-related study and a reflective project. Rare in Dubai compared with the full Diploma. For an MYP 5 student weighing it up, the relevant point is that it uses the same Diploma subject assessment for the courses taken, so MYP preparation carries across identically.
programmes.countryNote: No campus inside Arabian Ranches runs the Career-related Programme, so families exploring it look across the city. The MYP exit requirements and the Personal Project are unaffected by which post-16 route is chosen, which means nothing in MYP 5 needs to be decided differently on account of it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.subjectsIntro: Below are the eight MYP subject groups with their four criteria named, plus the two project components. Find the subject where your child's criterion levels are uneven; that is where the teaching should start.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B and C are the ones that transfer directly into the Diploma scientific investigation, and the ones most Ranches students score lowest on, because experimental design is rarely practised outside the task itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is the investigation: finding a pattern, describing it as a general rule, and justifying it. A student who is strong at exercises and weak at criterion B is extremely common and entirely fixable.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criterion A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language. Criterion A rewards analysis of how a text achieves its effect rather than what it says, which is the distinction most students miss. Criterion D is about control of register, vocabulary and syntax, assessed separately from the quality of the ideas.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Criterion A comprehending spoken and visual text, B comprehending written and visual text, C communicating, D using language. Students are placed in a phase rather than a year group, so two children in the same MYP class can be assessed against different descriptors in the same subject.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D is where most marks are lost: evaluating sources, recognising perspective and bias, and weighing competing interpretations rather than reporting them. It is also the criterion that most resembles Diploma history and geography work.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criterion A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The design cycle is assessed as a process, so documentation matters as much as the artefact. Students who build something good and record nothing score poorly, which feels unfair until the criteria are read.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B developing skills, C thinking creatively, D responding. The process journal carries a large share of the available marks, and it is the component students most often leave until the work is finished, at which point criterion B cannot be evidenced properly.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. Two of the four criteria are written rather than physical, which regularly surprises families whose child is a strong athlete with a middling grade.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.levels: MYP 5, assessed against its own criteria
subjects.description: An independent project in the final year, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each worth up to eight marks and 24 in total. The process journal is the evidence base. A tutor may teach project management, discuss goals and give feedback on the student's own writing, and nothing more than that.

subjects.name: Community Project
subjects.description: A service-focused project run in MYP 3 or MYP 4 depending on the school, assessed against its own criteria on the same nought-to-eight scale. The recurring difficulty is scope: students choose an action too large to complete and then have nothing specific to reflect on, which costs marks in the final criterion.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units that draw on two or more subject groups and are assessed against interdisciplinary criteria rather than the subject ones. They are reported separately at many schools, and a low interdisciplinary result in an otherwise strong report usually means the synthesis, not the subject knowledge, was the problem.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Five skill categories, communication, social, self-management, research and thinking, taught through subject content rather than separately. They are commented on in reports and underpin every criterion, which is why a self-management problem shows up as four low criterion levels in four different subjects.

sections.heading: What an MYP report card is actually telling you
paragraphs: An MYP report gives a parent more diagnostic information than a percentage ever could, and almost no explanation of how to use it. Each subject shows four criterion levels, each awarded from nought to eight, and a final grade from one to seven. The criterion levels are the useful part. They say which of four distinct abilities is weak in each subject, and because the four criteria measure different things, a pattern across subjects usually points at one underlying cause rather than four separate ones.

Read across the report rather than down it. A student with low criterion C in mathematics, low criterion C in sciences and low criterion B in language and literature does not have three subject problems; they have a written-communication problem appearing three times, because those three criteria all assess organising and expressing work. A student with low criterion B in sciences and low criterion A in individuals and societies does have two separate problems, because inquiring and designing has nothing in common with knowing and understanding.

Read the levels rather than the final grade too. Two students can both receive a five in sciences with completely different profiles: one steady at five across all four criteria, one scoring seven, seven, two and four. The second student is in more trouble and the grade conceals it. This is the single most useful thing a parent in Arabian Ranches can learn from an MYP report, and it takes ten minutes rather than a term of tutoring.

The table below sets out the four criteria for each subject group side by side. Finding the repeated low criterion is the diagnosis. Everything else on this page follows from it, because the teaching that moves criterion B in sciences looks nothing like the teaching that moves criterion D in individuals and societies, and buying the wrong one is the most common way MYP tutoring money is wasted.

sections.heading: How four levels out of eight become a grade out of seven
paragraphs: This is the arithmetic that MYP reports never show. The four criterion levels in a subject are added to give a total out of 32, and that total is converted to a grade from one to seven against published boundaries. The boundaries are not evenly spaced, which has consequences a family can act on. The step from grade four to grade five is narrower than the step from grade six to grade seven, so a student sitting at the top of one band is closer to the next grade than they feel.

Work an example. A student scoring five, five, four and four has a total of eighteen, which lands at grade four, near the top of its band. One extra level on any single criterion takes the total to nineteen and the grade to five. That is a genuinely small change: one criterion, one task, one specific improvement. A family told only that their child has a four in sciences has no way of knowing how close the five is, and the answer is often very close indeed.

The same arithmetic explains why chasing content revision across a whole subject is inefficient. Raising criterion A by two levels when criterion A is already at seven is impossible. Raising criterion C from two to four is usually a matter of being shown what a well-organised write-up looks like, and it moves the total by the same amount. A parent who knows the four levels can work out where the cheapest two points are without any help at all.

The boundaries below are the general MYP grade boundaries applied to a total out of 32. Schools in the Ranches belt apply them as published, and most report the total alongside the grade if asked. Ask for the four levels and the total at the next parents' evening; a school running the programme properly will give them without hesitation, and the conversation changes immediately once they are on the table.

sections.heading: Task-specific clarifications, and why the generic descriptor is not enough
paragraphs: Every MYP task comes with two documents: the published criterion descriptors, which are the same across all schools, and the task-specific clarification, which the teacher writes for that particular task. The clarification translates the general descriptor into what this piece of work needs in order to score in a given band. It is the single most important document in the programme and the one students most reliably ignore until after the task has been handed in.

A generic descriptor for sciences criterion B talks about explaining a problem, formulating a testable hypothesis, explaining how to manipulate variables and designing a logical method. The task-specific clarification for a particular experiment names which variables, which equipment, what the hypothesis has to predict and how many trials the method needs. Working from the descriptor alone leaves the student guessing at all of that. Working from the clarification makes the task far more tractable and is entirely legitimate, because the teacher provided it on purpose.

A productive MYP tutoring session therefore starts with the task sheet rather than with the topic. The tutor reads the clarification with the student, identifies which band the work is currently aimed at, and shows what the next band requires in that specific task. Over a term the student stops needing the tutor for this, because they start reading the clarification before beginning the task, which is the habit the programme is trying to build in the first place.

Command terms work the same way and are published for each subject group. Analyse, evaluate, describe, explain, justify, outline and state ask for different things, and a criterion descriptor that says evaluate is not satisfied by a description however accurate. Ranches students transferring in from a British curriculum are the most likely to be caught by this, because they are used to being rewarded for content rather than for the specific intellectual operation named in the task.

sections.heading: Where MYP marks are actually lost, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Across the Ranches-belt MYP campuses the same losses recur. In sciences, criterion B fails because the hypothesis is a prediction without a reason and the method does not say how variables are controlled. Criterion C fails because the data is presented and not processed: a table and a graph with no analysis of trend, no uncertainty acknowledged, no anomaly addressed. Criterion D fails because the reflection is about the experiment rather than about the impacts of science, which is what the criterion actually names.

In mathematics, criterion B fails because the student finds the pattern and stops, without expressing it as a general rule and without justifying why it holds. Criterion C fails on notation, labelling and structure rather than on mathematics. Criterion D fails because the real-life context is described rather than used: the model is built and never evaluated against the situation it was supposed to represent.

In language and literature, criterion A fails because the student writes about what the text says rather than how it achieves its effect. In individuals and societies, criterion D fails because sources are reported rather than evaluated for perspective, reliability and purpose. In design, criteria A and D fail because the process is undocumented, and the artefact alone cannot evidence inquiry or evaluation. In arts, criterion B fails for the same reason: an incomplete process journal.

The pattern across all of these is consistent and worth stating plainly. MYP marks are lost in the parts of the work that surround the content rather than in the content itself. That is why a student can be genuinely good at a subject and sit at a four, and why content revision is the wrong purchase. The teaching that moves these levels is explicit instruction in the operation the criterion names, practised on the student's own tasks.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the culminating piece of the Middle Years Programme, completed in MYP 5 and assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each worth up to eight marks for 24 in total. The evidence base is the process journal, kept throughout, and the final report. Schools in the Ranches belt set their own internal deadlines, usually with a goal statement in the autumn and a report in the spring, so the calendar is the school's rather than the IB's.

Two failure modes account for most lost marks. The first is scope. A goal that is too large cannot be completed, which starves the applying-skills criterion of evidence and leaves the reflection abstract. A goal that is too small produces a finished product and nothing to say about the process. The second is the journal. A student who writes the journal retrospectively, in the week before submission, cannot evidence planning or skill development, and the marks for both are effectively gone before the report is written.

The boundary on tutoring here is strict and it exists to protect your child. A tutor may teach project management, discuss whether a goal is appropriately scoped, explain what each criterion rewards, teach a skill the project requires, and give feedback on journal entries and report drafts the student has written. A tutor may not write or rewrite the report, construct the journal, choose the goal on the student's behalf or produce any part of the product. IB Gram works only on the first side of that line.

The same applies to the Community Project in MYP 3 or MYP 4, and to the Diploma work that comes later. There are providers in this market selling completed Internal Assessments with a published price, and the malpractice consequence of using one falls on the student rather than the seller. For a Ranches family the practical safeguard is simple: ask any tutor, in writing, what they will and will not do with a project, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

sections.heading: Service as action, the community project and interdisciplinary units
paragraphs: Three parts of the Middle Years Programme sit outside the eight subject groups and account for a surprising share of family confusion. Service as action runs through all five years and is not graded like a subject, but schools require evidence of it and some make it a condition of progression. Families in the Ranches belt sometimes discover this late, which is avoidable: ask the school in MYP 1 what evidence it expects and in what form, and keep it from the start.

The community project, run in MYP 3 or MYP 4 depending on the school, is a service-focused project assessed on the same nought-to-eight scale as subject criteria. It is the rehearsal for the Personal Project and it suffers from the same scope problem. Students choose an action that cannot be completed in the time, and the reflection criterion has nothing concrete to work with. A short conversation about scope at the start is worth more than any amount of help later.

Interdisciplinary units draw on two or more subject groups and are assessed against interdisciplinary criteria rather than the subject criteria. Many schools report them separately, which is why a report can show strong subject grades and a weak interdisciplinary result. That combination almost always means the student handled each subject's content competently and did not synthesise them, which is exactly what the interdisciplinary criteria are designed to detect.

For a tutor, these three components are mostly a matter of making the requirements visible. Students rarely fail them through inability; they fail them through not knowing what was being asked, or through leaving the documentation until the work was over. A session spent reading the school's own requirements with the student at the start of a year is worth several spent rescuing a project at the end of one.

sections.heading: From MYP 5 into DP1: the step measured honestly
paragraphs: The move from the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma changes the assessment model completely, and the size of the change depends on which criteria the student took seriously. Diploma sciences assess Paper 1 at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44 per cent and an individual scientific investigation at 20 per cent. That investigation is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, which is recognisably MYP sciences criteria B and C at greater depth. A student who scored well on those arrives prepared.

A student who did not has a genuine gap, and it is specific rather than general. Diploma internal assessment demands uncertainty handling, repeated trials, graphing with error treatment and evaluation of a named limitation. MYP criterion C asks for the same operations in simpler form. Where a student has been scoring three or four on criterion C for two years, the Diploma investigation is going to be the hardest single piece of work in DP1, and it is worth a summer block rather than a panic in the spring.

Content depth is the second change. MYP subject groups cover breadth; Diploma courses cover depth in six chosen subjects, two or three at Higher Level with 240 taught hours each. Mathematics is the sharpest step: Diploma Analysis and Approaches assumes algebraic fluency that MYP mathematics does not require, which is why Ranches-belt students who move from MYP 5 into Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level most often need support in the first term rather than the last.

The table sets out the main transitions with an honest note on each. The timings are drawn from the pattern of enquiries rather than from a study, so treat them as planning estimates and not as findings. The general rule holds in every case: a gap addressed in the summer before DP1 costs a fraction of what the same gap costs in the spring of DP2, and the student spends two years feeling competent rather than behind.

sections.heading: What MYP tuition costs for an Arabian Ranches family
paragraphs: Take the part a parent can verify independently first. Every figure in this section was published by the company or research service that charges it, on a page a family can open and read for itself, and that is the test to apply to any tutoring price anywhere. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table is public. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. BartyED's examiner-led tier is AED 650. EdFlik advertises online from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. None of those are our numbers, and all of them can be checked.

Mapped onto the Middle Years Programme the picture is slightly different from the Diploma. MYP work is rarely the premium tier, because what moves a criterion level is explicit instruction in an operation rather than examiner-level subject depth. Bestimate's band for qualified online subject tutors, AED 150 to 300 an hour, is where most productive MYP teaching sits. In monthly terms the same research estimates AED 600 to 1,200 for a weekly one-hour session at that level, against AED 240 to 600 at the budget end.

In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions against AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. The gap between those two package prices is the clearest published statement of what travel costs in Dubai. IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE in any case, so the in-home figures appear here only as the comparison that makes the point.

Two practical conclusions for a Ranches household. First, MYP tutoring is usually short and targeted rather than continuous: a block aimed at one criterion, or at a transferring student's induction into the model, finishes. Second, the thing worth paying for is a tutor who asks for the task sheet and the task-specific clarification before the first session. For context on the wider budget, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27, so tuition is the line that still moves.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page. The free trial lesson and a short conversation establish what the work actually is first, because quoting a price before knowing whether the problem is one criterion or the whole assessment model would be guessing.

process.title: Send the report and one marked task
process.description: The report gives the four criterion levels per subject, which is the diagnosis. One marked task with the teacher's task-specific clarification attached shows what the student actually did against what was asked. Those two documents together are worth more than any description of the problem, and they take a minute to send.

process.title: We find the repeated low criterion
process.description: Reading across the report rather than down it usually reveals one underlying cause behind several low subject grades. A tutor will tell you which criterion to target and which subjects it is costing marks in, and will say if the answer is a written-communication problem rather than a subject problem.

process.title: Match a tutor to the subject group and the criterion
process.description: Matching is on the subject group and the specific criterion rather than on the year group. If no suitable tutor is free in your preferred slot we say so and offer another time, rather than putting a general tutor in front of a student who needs to be shown what criterion B rewards.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session before anything is paid, worked on the student's own task rather than on an exemplar. The tutor reports what they found. If the match is wrong, say so and we try another tutor; nothing is owed either way and no card details are needed to start.

process.title: Work in a finite block, then review
process.description: MYP support is usually short. A block aimed at one criterion, or at inducting a transferring student into the model, has an end point. At the halfway mark you get a written note on what has moved, and we will tell you when the work is done rather than letting a weekly slot run on.

whyPoints.title: Taught by criterion, not by topic
whyPoints.description: MYP marks are lost in the operation the criterion names rather than in the content, which is why content revision so often fails to move a grade. Every block here starts from the student's criterion levels and works on the specific ability the low one measures.

whyPoints.title: The task-specific clarification is the working document
whyPoints.description: The generic descriptor is identical across every MYP school in the world; the clarification your child's teacher wrote is what the task is actually marked against. A tutor who asks for it before the first session is doing the job properly, and that is how we work.

whyPoints.title: The boundary arithmetic explained
whyPoints.description: Four levels out of eight add to a total out of 32 which converts to a grade out of seven against published boundaries. Knowing where your child sits inside a band tells you whether one level on one criterion crosses it. Most families are never shown this, and it changes the conversation.

whyPoints.title: Project support that keeps your child safe
whyPoints.description: The Personal Project and the community project are the student's own work. We teach project management, test scope, explain the criteria and comment on drafts the student has written, and we do not touch the text or the journal. The line is stated in writing because the consequence of crossing it falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the MYP 5 to DP1 step
whyPoints.description: The transition is real but specific: the scientific investigation, timed assessment and algebraic fluency. We name those three rather than selling a general bridging course, and the work is cheapest in the summer before DP1 rather than in the spring of DP2.

whyPoints.title: No claimed accreditation and no supplied materials
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or endorsed by the IB, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, holds no UAE office or centre, and does not host or distribute IB subject guides or assessment material. All of that is checkable.

faqs.question: How are MYP subjects graded if there are no percentages on the report?
faqs.answer: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, and each criterion is awarded a level from nought to eight. The four levels are added to give a total out of 32, and that total converts to a final grade from one to seven against published boundaries. There is no percentage behind it because the criteria measure different abilities rather than the same ability repeatedly. The useful information for a parent is the four separate levels, not the single grade, because the levels say which ability is weak and the grade conceals it.

faqs.question: What do MYP criteria A to D actually measure in sciences?
faqs.answer: Criterion A is knowing and understanding, which is content and its application. Criterion B is inquiring and designing: formulating a testable hypothesis with a reason, identifying and controlling variables, and designing a logical method. Criterion C is processing and evaluating: handling the data, presenting it properly, analysing the trend and addressing anomalies. Criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science, which is about science in context rather than about the experiment. Criteria B and C are the ones that lead directly into the Diploma scientific investigation.

faqs.question: How does an MYP 1 to 7 grade convert from criterion marks out of eight?
faqs.answer: The four criterion levels are summed to a total out of 32 and read against published grade boundaries. A total of 15 to 18 is a grade four, 19 to 23 is a five, 24 to 27 is a six and 28 to 32 is a seven, with the lower bands covering totals below 15. The bands are not evenly spaced, so a student near the top of a band can cross into the next grade on a single extra level in a single criterion. Ask the school for the total alongside the grade.

faqs.question: What is the MYP Personal Project and how is it assessed?
faqs.answer: It is an independent project completed in MYP 5, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each worth up to eight marks for 24 in total. The evidence is a process journal kept throughout the project plus a final report. Most lost marks come from two causes: a goal scoped too broadly to complete, and a journal written retrospectively in the final week, which cannot evidence planning or skill development. Schools set their own internal deadlines, so the calendar comes from your child's campus rather than from the IB.

faqs.question: Which MYP year group do Arabian Ranches families ask for help with most?
faqs.answer: MYP 4 and MYP 5, for two different reasons. MYP 4 is where the subject content deepens and where a criterion that has been quietly weak for two years starts costing visible grades. MYP 5 brings the Personal Project alongside subject work and the Diploma options decision, which is the heaviest single year in the programme. Enquiries from MYP 1 and MYP 2 are usually about the assessment model rather than content, and they come from families who have just transferred into an IB school.

faqs.question: Does MYP eAssessment matter for a child who will move into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the school enters candidates for it. Some MYP schools use external eAssessment in the final year, leading to the IB MYP Certificate, and some do not, relying on internally moderated assessment instead. Diploma admission at the same school generally rests on internal results and teacher recommendation rather than on an eAssessment outcome. Ask your child's campus directly whether it enters candidates, because the answer changes how MYP 5 should be planned and it varies between schools in the Ranches belt.

faqs.question: What is a statement of inquiry and why does it appear in every unit?
faqs.answer: It is one sentence that ties the unit together, built from a key concept, one or more related concepts and one of six global contexts. The global contexts are identities and relationships, orientation in space and time, personal and cultural expression, scientific and technical innovation, globalization and sustainability, and fairness and development. Its purpose is to give the content a reason to exist beyond itself, and its practical use for a student is that assessment tasks are usually written against it, so reading it tells you what the task is really asking.

faqs.question: How do Approaches to Learning skills get taught in a tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Through the subject work rather than separately, which is how the programme intends it. The five categories are communication, social, self-management, research and thinking. In practice a tutor who notices that a student cannot plan a long task is working on self-management, and one who shows a student how to evaluate a source is working on research. These skills are why one weak criterion often appears in four subjects at once: the cause is a skill rather than four separate knowledge gaps.

faqs.question: Can an MYP tutor help with the community project in Year 3 or Year 4?
faqs.answer: Within the same limits that apply to the Personal Project. A tutor may discuss whether the goal is scoped so that it can actually be completed, explain what each criterion rewards, teach a skill the project needs, and give feedback on journal entries and writing the student has produced. A tutor may not choose the goal, write or rewrite any part of it, or construct the journal. The scope conversation at the start is the most valuable part, because an over-large action leaves the reflection criterion with nothing specific to work on.

faqs.question: My child moved from a British Year 8 into MYP 3. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Usually not content. The gap is the assessment model: four criteria measuring different abilities, task-specific clarifications that have to be read before starting, command terms that are not interchangeable, and written components in subjects where a British curriculum would have tested recall. Students who were rewarded for knowing things find themselves marked on operations instead. A short induction block of a few sessions fixes most of it, and is far more effective than subject tutoring in the first term after a transfer.

faqs.question: What does MYP tuition cost for an Arabian Ranches family per month?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai research estimates AED 600 to 1,200 a month for a weekly one-hour session with a qualified online subject tutor, against AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. An advertised online package runs at AED 799 a month for eight sessions, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Most MYP work sits in the middle band and is bought as a finite block rather than continuously. Those are published figures, not IB Gram rates.

faqs.question: Is the MYP Interdisciplinary unit assessed separately from subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes. Interdisciplinary units draw on two or more subject groups and are assessed against interdisciplinary criteria rather than the criteria of either subject, and many schools report the result separately. That is why a report can show solid subject grades beside a weaker interdisciplinary outcome. When that happens it almost always means the student handled each subject's content competently and did not synthesise the two, which is exactly the ability the interdisciplinary criteria are designed to assess.

faqs.question: How do I read an MYP report card that shows four criterion scores?
faqs.answer: Read across the subjects rather than down them. If the same criterion is low in several subjects, there is one underlying cause: low criterion C in mathematics and sciences alongside low criterion B in language and literature usually means written organisation rather than three subject problems. Then look at the spread within a subject. A five made of five, five, four, four is a different situation from a five made of seven, seven, two, four, and only the second one is urgent. Ask the school for the totals.

faqs.question: Which schools near Arabian Ranches run the MYP rather than IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Emirates International School Meadows, GEMS International School Al Khail in Dubai Hills Estate, Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Nord Anglia International School Dubai all run the Middle Years Programme, several as part of a continuum from the primary years. JESS Arabian Ranches, inside the community, runs the English National Curriculum to IGCSE before the Diploma, as do Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills and GEMS Metropole School in Motor City. Check the current KHDA report for any campus you are considering.

faqs.question: Does the MYP prepare a child adequately for Diploma mathematics?
faqs.answer: For Applications and Interpretation, usually yes. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the honest answer is that it prepares the thinking and not always the fluency. MYP mathematics criterion B rewards investigating patterns and criterion D rewards applying mathematics to real contexts, both of which matter in the Diploma. What it does not demand is fast, accurate algebraic manipulation under time pressure, which Analysis and Approaches assumes from the first week. That is the specific gap, and the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 is the cheap time to close it.

intro.heading: Why almost nobody near you teaches this programme privately
paragraphs: The honest answer to the question behind this search is that the pool of people who can genuinely teach the Middle Years Programme in Dubai is small, and the pool within driving distance of Arabian Ranches 2 is smaller still. This is not a marketing position. It is arithmetic. International Baccalaureate programmes account for around seven per cent of private enrolment in Dubai, against thirty-seven per cent for UK curricula, and only a fraction of IB schools run the full continuum including the MYP. The teachers who know it are mostly employed teaching it.

The second reason is structural. Most private tutors sell subject knowledge, and the MYP is not assessed on subject knowledge in the way a parent expects. Each subject is marked against four criteria, each on a scale of one to eight, giving a total out of thirty-two that is then converted into a grade from one to seven. A mathematics tutor who can teach quadratics brilliantly may have no idea what criterion B, investigating patterns, actually asks a student to produce, or why a student who can factorise perfectly is scoring a four on it.

The third reason is that there is no past-paper industry. A British-curriculum tutor can prepare for Cambridge 0580 by working through fifteen years of papers. MYP assessment is largely internal, task-based and moderated within the school, with task sheets, rubrics and command verbs that vary by unit. A tutor cannot bluff their way into that from a syllabus document, and the ones who have not taught it generally do not realise how much they are missing.

Arabian Ranches 2 sharpens the problem geographically. There is no secondary school inside the community, so students from Casa, Rosa, Palma, Lila, Camelia, Azalea, Reem, Yasmin and Rasha travel out to Motor City, Al Barsha South, Nad Al Sheba, the Sustainable City or Dubai Hills. The MYP schools they attend are spread across the city. The chance that a genuine MYP teacher in your child's subject group also happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of your villa is low, and searching by distance actively selects against the people who can help.

So this page is written to make you a better buyer rather than to claim a stock we do not hold. It sets out what the programme actually assesses, gives you ten questions that distinguish an MYP teacher from a subject graduate in the first ten minutes of a conversation, and is honest about what happens when nobody suitable is free. IB Gram delivers MYP support to this community one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is also what makes the subject-group filter possible at all, because it stops competing with a map.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-2.programmesIntro: The MYP sits between two other programmes and feeds into choices made at fifteen. Where your child is in that sequence changes which kind of tutor is useful and whether one is useful at all.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked one to eight, organised around key and related concepts, global contexts and statements of inquiry. Assessment is largely internal and task-based, with teachers applying published criteria and moderating within the school rather than marking a national paper.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP runs in the schools operating the full IB continuum, which is a minority of the private sector. For families in Arabian Ranches 2 this means a longer school run and a thinner private tutoring market than a British-curriculum family faces. It also means the school's own task sheets are the single most useful document a tutor can be given.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary, inquiry-led and without the criterion scales that arrive in the MYP. A child moving from PYP into MYP 1 meets formal criterion marking for the first time, and the shock is usually about the form of the feedback rather than the difficulty of the work.
programmes.countryNote: Families in this community whose children attended Ranches Primary School or another British-curriculum primary before moving into an MYP school face a different adjustment again: from percentage marks and levels to a four-criterion profile that looks like a judgement on the child rather than on a task.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where the MYP leads for most students in continuum schools, and the reason MYP 4 and MYP 5 choices matter. Diploma assessment is largely external, heavily time-pressured and marked against mark schemes rather than criteria scales, which is a genuinely different skill.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma transition is where a specific weakness surfaces: students who have never been examined under time now are. The MYP rewards process, reflection and extended production; the Diploma rewards precise performance in two hours. A student with strong criterion marks and no exam stamina can lose a grade in DP1 term one for that reason alone.

programmes.name: The IGCSE alternative at 14
programmes.description: Some Dubai families move out of the MYP at fourteen into IGCSE, either by changing school or because their school offers both. It trades the MYP's breadth and interdisciplinary work for external examinations and a familiar grade scale, and it is a real decision rather than a formality.
programmes.countryNote: Worth deciding on the destination rather than the comfort. A student heading for the IB Diploma in the same school usually benefits from staying in the MYP through MYP 5, because the inquiry and extended-production skills carry forward. A student who finds criterion-referenced feedback demoralising may do better on a route with a clearer mark.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-2.subjectsIntro: The MYP's eight subject groups each have their own four criteria, and the criterion that drags is rarely the one a parent expects. The entries below name what each group actually asks a student to produce.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the usual drag: it asks a student to find a rule, test it, generalise it and justify the generalisation, which is a different activity from solving an exercise correctly.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Inquiring and designing asks for a researchable question and a method with controlled variables, written by the student before any data exists, which is the skill that later carries the Diploma investigation.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students frequently lose marks on analysing while writing fluently, because analysis asks for interpretation supported by evidence rather than for an account of what happened in the text.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Organised into phases rather than years, with criteria covering comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. The phase a child is working in matters more than their MYP year, and a tutor who does not ask which phase has missed the first question.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is where able students lose marks: it asks for evaluation of sources and recognition of different perspectives, not a more confident version of the same narrative.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The subject most often misread by parents as an art class. It is a documented design cycle in which the process evidence carries as many marks as the product, and the documentation is what students neglect.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. A student can produce excellent work and score poorly because the process journal is thin. Supporting arts in the MYP is largely about helping a student record their thinking, which is a teachable habit.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Written and reflective components carry real weight, which surprises families who assume the grade follows athletic ability.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units that join two or more subject groups and are assessed against their own criteria: disciplinary grounding, synthesising, and reflecting on interdisciplinary learning. Almost no private tutor has encountered these, and they appear on reports, which is why a parent sees a mark nobody can explain.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. A supervisor is appointed by the school. A tutor may teach skills, discuss the process and respond to the student's own writing; no tutor may write the Personal Project or any part of what is submitted.

sections.heading: Ten questions that tell you whether a tutor knows the MYP
paragraphs: Use the first ten minutes of any conversation to test the thing that actually matters, rather than qualifications. A tutor who has taught the Middle Years Programme answers these without hesitation. A subject graduate who has read a syllabus summary will answer three or four and then generalise. The difference is worth more than any credential, and it costs you nothing to find out.

The questions are deliberately specific, because specificity is what cannot be bluffed. Asking whether somebody is familiar with the MYP produces a yes from everybody. Asking which four criteria apply in your child's subject group, and what a seven in criterion B looks like compared with a five, produces an answer that is either detailed or evasive within a sentence.

Two of the questions are about things that barely exist in other systems. Interdisciplinary units appear on MYP reports and are assessed against their own criteria, and almost no private tutor in Dubai has seen one. Approaches-to-learning skills, grouped into thinking, communication, social, self-management and research, are explicitly taught and referenced in feedback, and a tutor who has never had to teach them will treat a self-management problem as laziness.

The last question is the most useful. Ask what they would want to see before the first session. The right answer is the school's task sheet, the published criteria for that unit, and the student's last marked task with the teacher's comments. Anything else - a topic list, a textbook, a description of how the child is finding it - tells you the tutor is planning to teach a subject rather than to raise a criterion mark.

sections.heading: Criterion-referenced marking, and why a 5 is not a percentage
paragraphs: The single largest source of confusion for families in this community is the mark itself. In the MYP each subject is assessed against four criteria, each on a one-to-eight scale, giving a total out of thirty-two. That total is then converted into a grade from one to seven using published general boundaries. It is not an average, it is not a percentage, and a five does not mean sixty-two per cent of anything.

What follows from this is that the same child can look inconsistent across subjects for reasons that have nothing to do with effort. A student who is strong at criterion A, knowing and understanding, and weak at the criterion that asks them to investigate or design is averaging out at a four while being genuinely good at half the subject. A report that shows this looks like underachievement; read properly, it is a precise instruction about what to work on.

It also explains why generic tutoring produces so little movement in the MYP. More content teaching improves criterion A and leaves the others untouched, so the total barely shifts and the grade does not move at all. A parent who has paid for a term of weekly sessions and seen no change on the report has usually bought the wrong criterion, not a bad tutor. The fix is to identify the criterion that is dragging and work only on that.

The practical step for a family in Arabian Ranches 2 is to ask the school for the criterion breakdown rather than the grade, if the report does not already show it. Four numbers out of eight tell you where the work is. One number out of seven tells you nothing actionable, and it is the number most conversations about MYP tutoring begin and end with.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units: the mark nobody can explain
paragraphs: At least once a year an MYP student works on a unit that joins two or more subject groups, and that unit is assessed against its own criteria rather than the criteria of either subject. It appears on the report. Parents in this community routinely see that line, do not understand it, ask a tutor about it, and discover that the tutor has never heard of it either. That is the clearest single illustration of why subject expertise alone does not cover this programme.

What the unit asks for is specific. A student has to bring disciplinary grounding from each subject involved, synthesise it into something neither subject would produce alone, and then reflect on what the combination made possible. A history-and-science unit on water scarcity is not a history essay with some science in it, and a student who writes one scores poorly while believing they worked hard.

Supporting it well does not require a tutor who teaches both subjects. It requires somebody who understands the criteria and can hold a student to them: has each discipline genuinely contributed, is the synthesis doing work, and does the reflection discuss the interdisciplinary learning rather than the topic. Those are process questions, and they are answerable by one tutor who knows the programme.

For families weighing whether MYP support is worth buying at all, this is a useful test of the market. A tutor who asks about interdisciplinary units unprompted has taught the programme. A tutor who waits for you to raise it and then says they can look into it has not, and that is worth knowing before rather than after a term of sessions.
