sections.heading: eAssessment at the end of MYP 5, and whether your child is sitting it
paragraphs: The first thing to establish is whether your child's school uses it at all. MYP 5 eAssessment is an option schools choose, leading to the IB MYP Certificate, and plenty of Dubai schools do not take it up. A family planning tutoring around on-screen examinations that their school does not enter students for is planning for the wrong thing entirely, and a single email to the MYP coordinator settles it.

Where a school does use it, the format is a mix. Some subject groups are assessed through on-screen examinations and others through ePortfolios of the student's own work, with an interdisciplinary on-screen examination and the Personal Project also forming part of the certificate requirements. That mix matters for tutoring because an on-screen examination rewards timed performance while an ePortfolio rewards curated process evidence, and those are different kinds of preparation.

For students sitting on-screen examinations, the useful work is familiarity rather than content: what the question types look like, how long there is, how to handle an unfamiliar stimulus under time. This is the first genuinely external, timed assessment many MYP students have faced, and the shock of it accounts for more lost marks than any gap in knowledge. Short timed practice, several weeks out, is the whole intervention.

For students assessed through ePortfolios, the work is documentation discipline: selecting the right evidence, showing the process rather than the outcome, and writing the reflective commentary that the criteria actually reward. Students who have strong practical ability and thin records lose marks here consistently, and it is fixable in a handful of sessions because the problem is a habit rather than an ability.

sections.heading: MYP 4, the narrowing, and the decision families make at fourteen
paragraphs: MYP 4 is where the programme changes character for most students. Subject choices narrow, work lengthens, and the gap between students who have internalised the criteria and those who have been producing content widens quickly. It is also the point at which families in this community start asking whether to stay in the MYP through MYP 5 or move to IGCSE, either within a school that offers both or by changing school entirely.

There is no general right answer, and anybody who offers one is not paying attention to your child. The argument for staying is continuity: a student heading for the IB Diploma in the same school carries forward the inquiry habits, extended production and reflective writing that the Diploma rewards, and avoids a disruptive change at fourteen. The argument for moving is clarity: external examinations, a familiar grade scale and a smaller gap between effort and visible mark.

What should drive the decision is the destination and the child's response to criterion-referenced feedback. A student who finds four numbers out of eight demoralising, and who works better towards a single clear mark, may genuinely do better on an IGCSE route. A student who thrives on open tasks and reflection will lose something real by leaving. Those are observations about your child rather than claims about either curriculum.

One thing not to let drive it is the availability of tutoring. The MYP is harder to support privately, and that is a real cost, but choosing a curriculum because help is easier to buy is the wrong order of priorities. A better response is to use the ten questions earlier on this page to find somebody who genuinely knows the programme, and to accept that it may be somebody who does not live anywhere near Arabian Ranches 2.

sections.heading: Service as action, the Community Project and the Personal Project line
paragraphs: Three strands of the programme sit outside subject teaching and produce most of the questions we get from families in this catchment. Service as action runs throughout the MYP as an expectation that students act on what they learn. The Community Project sits in MYP 3 or MYP 4 depending on the school's model. The Personal Project sits at the end of MYP 5 and is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting.

None of these needs a tutor in the ordinary sense, and families who hire one for them are usually buying the wrong thing. What students struggle with is process management: choosing a goal that is achievable, keeping a usable record while the work happens rather than reconstructing it afterwards, and writing reflection that discusses decisions rather than summarising activity. That is coachable in a small number of sessions and does not require subject expertise at all.

The boundary here is strict and worth stating plainly before any booking. A school-appointed supervisor oversees the Personal Project. A tutor may teach a skill the student needs, discuss how to plan, ask whether a claim is supported, and give feedback on writing the student has produced. No tutor may write the Personal Project, draft any section of it, or supply text that ends up in the submission. The same applies to the Community Project and to any assessed task.

This matters more in the MYP than parents expect, because so much of the assessment is coursework produced at home. An IB academic-honesty breach falls on the student, not on the tutor who offered to help, and the programme's whole point is that the thinking is the student's. Any tutor who offers to tidy a project into shape is offering something that puts your child at risk, and the correct response is to decline and find somebody else.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs, and what happens when nobody suitable is free
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates do not have an MYP tier, which tells you something in itself. The bands in this market are organised around examined curricula: budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; IB specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270; and premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

For MYP work the honest guidance is that the specialist band is where genuine programme expertise sits, for the supply reasons set out at the top of this page, and that the budget band buys subject help that will improve criterion A and leave the others where they were. In-home visits are published at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table at AED 180 to 350, and the increment over the online band is travel into Dubailand rather than better teaching. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all.

On availability, we would rather disclose a limit than fill a slot. MYP expertise in a specific subject group at a specific time is a narrow intersection, and there are weeks when we cannot cover a request from this community. When that happens we say so and set out the alternatives with rates attached: a different time with the right person, a weekend slot, a tutor outside the Gulf evening peak, or - genuinely - the advice that the school's own MYP coordinator is the better first call for this particular problem.

Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work and the permit is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct does the same, so your child's own teacher privately is not an arrangement we will make.

sections.heading: What an MYP tutor cannot fix
paragraphs: Three problems get brought to MYP tutors regularly and none of them is solved by paid teaching. The first is a report a family cannot interpret. Four criterion scores out of eight, converted into a grade out of seven, with a comment about approaches-to-learning skills, is genuinely hard to read if nobody has explained the system. The answer is a conversation with the school, which costs nothing, and this page rather than a term of sessions.

The second is a mismatch between a child and criterion-referenced assessment. Some students find a four-part profile demoralising in a way that a single percentage would not be, and no amount of tutoring changes the assessment model. That is a real consideration in the decision at fourteen about whether to continue in the MYP or move to an examined route, and it belongs in a conversation with the school rather than in a purchase.

The third is organisation presented as ability. The MYP produces a lot of coursework at home, over long deadlines, with process evidence expected throughout. A student who cannot manage that will have low criterion marks across every subject at once, and more subject teaching does not touch it. Approaches-to-learning skills, particularly self-management and research, are the actual target, and they are coachable - but as a habit over a term, not as content in a session.

What MYP support genuinely does is narrower and more useful than the general version. It raises a specific criterion in a specific subject by working from the school's own task sheet and the student's last marked task. It closes the gap between criterion-assessed coursework and timed external assessment before the Diploma. And it teaches the documentation habits that the design cycle, the arts process journal and the science method all reward. Those are worth buying. A general sense that someone should help with the MYP is not.

faqs.question: Why can I not find an MYP tutor anywhere near Arabian Ranches 2?
faqs.answer: Because the pool is genuinely small. International Baccalaureate programmes account for around seven per cent of Dubai's private enrolment against thirty-seven per cent for UK curricula, only some IB schools run the full continuum including the MYP, and the teachers who know the programme are mostly employed teaching it. Add that there is no secondary school inside this community and the continuum schools are spread across the city, and the chance of a genuine MYP teacher living twenty minutes from your villa is low.

faqs.question: Is a good subject tutor enough for MYP, or do they need programme experience?
faqs.answer: Programme experience, for a specific reason. MYP subjects are assessed against four criteria, each marked one to eight, and a subject tutor improves criterion A, knowing and understanding, while leaving the other three where they were. The criterion total barely shifts and the report grade does not move, which is why families pay for a term and see nothing change. The tutor needs to have seen a marked task against the criteria, not just to know the subject.

faqs.question: How do four criterion scores turn into the grade on the report?
faqs.answer: Each of the four criteria is marked out of eight, giving a total out of thirty-two, and that total is converted into a grade from one to seven using published general boundaries. It is not an average and not a percentage. The practical consequence is that a child strong in two criteria and weak in two can look like a middling student while being genuinely good at half the subject, which is why the criterion breakdown is more useful than the grade.

faqs.question: What exactly does criterion B in MYP mathematics ask for?
faqs.answer: Investigating patterns asks a student to find a rule in an unfamiliar situation, test it against further cases, generalise it and justify the generalisation. That is a different activity from solving an exercise correctly, which is why students who are fluent at procedures often score a four or five on it. Supporting it means working through open investigations rather than more practice questions, and it needs a tutor who has marked one against the descriptors.

faqs.question: My child's report has a mark for something that is not a subject. What is it?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly an interdisciplinary unit. MYP students work on at least one a year, joining two or more subject groups, assessed against its own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting on interdisciplinary learning. It is not one subject's essay with material from another added. Very few private tutors in Dubai have seen one, which is why a tutor who raises interdisciplinary units unprompted has almost certainly taught the programme.

faqs.question: What are approaches-to-learning skills and can a tutor actually teach them?
faqs.answer: They are five categories of skill the programme teaches explicitly: thinking, communication, social, self-management and research. They appear in feedback, and a weakness in self-management or research shows up as low criterion marks across every subject at once. They are coachable, but as habits built over a term rather than content delivered in a session, and a tutor who has not taught the programme will usually read a self-management problem as laziness.

faqs.question: Which questions should I ask before hiring an MYP tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask which four criteria apply in your child's subject group, what each is marked out of, how the total becomes a report grade, what a statement of inquiry is, what the five approaches-to-learning categories are, what an interdisciplinary unit is assessed on, and what they want to see before the first session. The right answer to the last one is the school's task sheet, the published criteria and the last marked task. A topic list is the wrong answer.

faqs.question: Does my child's school even use MYP eAssessment at the end of MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Many Dubai schools do not, and you should establish this before planning anything around it. MYP 5 eAssessment is an option a school chooses, leading to the IB MYP Certificate, combining on-screen examinations in some subject groups with ePortfolios in others, plus an interdisciplinary on-screen examination and the Personal Project. One email to the MYP coordinator settles whether your child is being entered, and a plan built on the wrong assumption wastes a term.

faqs.question: How should we prepare for on-screen MYP examinations if the school does use them?
faqs.answer: With timed familiarity rather than more content. For many MYP students this is their first external, timed assessment, and the shock of working to a clock against unfamiliar stimulus material accounts for more lost marks than any knowledge gap. Short timed practice several weeks out, with the question types and the time pressure made familiar, is the whole intervention. Students assessed through ePortfolios instead need documentation discipline, which is a different and equally short piece of work.

faqs.question: Should my child leave the MYP for IGCSE at fourteen?
faqs.answer: It depends on the destination and on how your child responds to criterion-referenced feedback. Staying through MYP 5 preserves continuity into the IB Diploma and the inquiry and extended-production habits it rewards. Moving to IGCSE gives external examinations, a familiar grade scale and a smaller gap between effort and visible mark. What should not drive the decision is that MYP tutoring is harder to buy, which is a real cost but the wrong priority.

faqs.question: Why does a strong MYP student sometimes struggle in the first term of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Because the assessment changes character. The MYP rewards process, reflection and extended production assessed against criteria over long deadlines. The Diploma rewards precise performance against mark schemes in two-hour papers. A student with excellent criterion marks and no exam stamina can lose a grade in DP1 term one for that reason alone, and it is why a short block of timed practice in MYP 5 or the summer afterwards is worth more than it looks.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do on my child's Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Teach a skill the student needs, discuss how to plan the work, ask whether a claim is supported, and give feedback on writing the student has produced themselves. A school-appointed supervisor oversees the project and a tutor is not a substitute for one. What no tutor may do is write the Personal Project, draft any section of it or supply text that ends up in the submission. An academic-honesty breach falls on the student rather than on the tutor who offered.

faqs.question: My son is good at design but his mark is low. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the documentation rather than the product. MYP Design is assessed on inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating, so the process evidence carries as many marks as the finished object. Students who build something good and record almost nothing lose marks in two or three criteria at once. The same pattern appears in Arts, where a thin process journal undermines strong practical work. It is a habit problem and fixable in a few sessions.

faqs.question: What does MYP support cost, and is there an MYP rate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: There is no published MYP tier, which is itself informative. The market bands are built around examined curricula: budget online tutors from roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200; IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Genuine programme expertise sits in the specialist band. The budget band buys subject help that moves one criterion.

faqs.question: What if no tutor who knows my child's MYP subject group is available?
faqs.answer: We will tell you, with the alternatives and their rates: a different time with the right person, a weekend slot, a tutor whose hours sit outside the Gulf evening peak, or sometimes the honest advice that your school's MYP coordinator is the better first call for that particular problem. Programme expertise in a named subject group at a named hour is a narrow intersection, and there are weeks when we cannot cover a request from this community.

faqs.question: Is there any point tutoring an MYP 1 or MYP 2 student?
faqs.answer: Rarely for content, often for the system. The real adjustment in the early MYP years is to criterion-referenced assessment itself, particularly for a child arriving from a British-curriculum primary or from the Primary Years Programme where no such scales existed. Teaching a student to read the descriptors and self-assess against them is worth a handful of sessions and pays back across every subject for five years. Weekly subject tutoring at that age usually is not worth buying.

Each works from the descriptors the school publishes, marks the student's own writing against them, and shows where a mark of 5 falls short of a 6.

intro.heading: Where you are in the MYP year decides what help is worth buying
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme has no public exam for most students, which is why it confuses parents who have come from a British or an Indian system. There is no June paper to count down to and no grade boundary published in a newspaper. Instead there is a report cycle, four criteria per subject marked out of eight, a Personal Project in MYP 5, and a quiet accumulation of habits that either prepares a child for the Diploma Programme or does not. The absence of an exam date makes the year feel shapeless, and that is the main reason support gets bought too late.

So this page is built as a calendar. Families in Arabian Ranches 3 asking about MYP support are almost always asking in one of four situations: a first report in October that made no sense, a mid-year review in January that showed a subject sliding, an MYP 5 Personal Project that has stalled, or the February conversation about whether to move to IGCSE or stay in the programme. Each of those has a different useful answer, and the answers do not substitute for each other.

Arabian Ranches 3 sits in the Dubailand belt, surrounded by Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2, Mudon, Remraam, Town Square, Motor City, Dubai Sports City and the DAMAC Hills communities. The IB schools that serve this belt are not all inside it. Several families drive north and east towards Al Khail, Nad Al Sheba and Al Barsha for an IB place, which means the school calendar that governs your child's deadlines may belong to a campus twenty minutes away. Knowing which calendar applies matters more than knowing which community a tutor lives in.

The structural point about the MYP is that criterion marks are not percentages and do not average the way parents assume. A child can hold a 6 in criterion A and a 3 in criterion D in the same subject, and the report shows one number that hides both. A tutor's first job is usually to split that number back apart, because the work needed for a weak criterion D is almost never the work that moves criterion A. Reading the report properly is the cheapest intervention available and most families have never been shown how.

The second structural point is the Personal Project in MYP 5. It is assessed against its own criteria, moderated, and it is the student's own work from the first line to the last. A tutor can coach process: how to narrow a goal, how to keep a process journal that actually earns marks, how to write a report that references the criteria. A tutor cannot supply content, and any provider offering to is offering your child an academic-honesty problem rather than a service.

Everything below is written for a family deciding what to do this term. There is a milestone table counted backwards from the report cycle, a criterion-by-criterion breakdown for each subject group, the conversion table from criterion totals to a grade out of 7, an honest section on what eight weeks changes, and the market rates in AED with attribution. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, with a shared whiteboard and a recording.
bullets: Four criteria per subject, each marked 1-8, totalling 32 before conversion
The reported grade out of 7 comes from published boundary bands, not an average
Personal Project support is process coaching only
MYP eAssessment is optional and school-dependent; confirm with the IB coordinator
No home visits in Dubai; delivery is live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.programmesIntro: Four programmes bear on an MYP family in this part of Dubai: the programme itself, the primary years that feed it, and the two routes a child takes at 16. The MYP decision in February is really a decision about which of those last two is coming.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked from 1 to 8, with interdisciplinary units, Approaches to Learning skills and Service as Action running alongside. MYP 3 or 4 carries a Community Project in most schools and MYP 5 carries the Personal Project. Assessment is internal and criterion-referenced, with optional on-screen eAssessment and ePortfolios available at the end of MYP 5 for schools that register for them.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB schools run the MYP on a UAE academic year that starts in late August or early September and ends in June or early July, with mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons sitting inside the same timetable. The practical effect for a family in Arabian Ranches 3 is a denser week than the programme's documentation implies, and a narrower window for catch-up work.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, transdisciplinary, and ending with the Exhibition. Children arriving in MYP 1 from the PYP are usually strong at framing questions and weaker at the formal writing conventions the MYP criteria start to reward. That is a predictable and short-lived gap, and it is worth naming in MYP 1 rather than discovering in MYP 3 when criterion C and D marks start to matter.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the full IB continuum on one campus, so a child may move PYP to MYP without changing building. Others do not, and a PYP child in the Dubailand belt may transfer into an MYP school further north. A transfer in the same term as a programme change is the combination most likely to produce a confusing first report.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The MYP is designed to feed it, and in the subjects where it does so well, the handover is almost invisible. Where it does not, the gap is usually mathematical fluency and the volume of independent writing, both of which can be built during MYP 4 and 5 rather than repaired in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools sit the May DP session. The IB's own published dates should be confirmed with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from any tutoring site, including this one. What matters for an MYP family is earlier: subject choices are made in MYP 5, and a Higher Level science or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches choice assumes a level of MYP performance that is worth checking honestly.

programmes.name: IGCSE at 16, the other route
programmes.description: Many Dubai families leave the MYP at 14 or 15 for Cambridge or Pearson IGCSEs, because the British-curriculum sector in this emirate is large and the qualification is externally examined. The switch is not neutral: IGCSE rewards exam technique and timed recall, where the MYP rewards process and sustained work. A child who thrives under one does not automatically thrive under the other.
programmes.countryNote: Around Arabian Ranches 3 the British-curriculum schools outnumber the IB ones, so the MYP-to-IGCSE move often comes with a school change as well as a curriculum change. That makes February of MYP 4 or MYP 5 the decision point, and it makes an honest read of criterion marks the most useful input into the decision.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.subjectsIntro: The MYP is organised into eight subject groups rather than a list of subjects, and each group has its own four criteria. Knowing which criterion is weak is more useful than knowing which subject is weak, because the remedy follows the criterion.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria A Analysing, B Organising, C Producing text, D Using language. Marks are lost in A when a student retells a text rather than analysing how it works, and in D when register and syntax are inconsistent. Both are teachable through annotated redrafting of the student's own essays rather than through reading more texts.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria A Listening, B Reading, C Speaking, D Writing, with phase bands that matter more than the year group. A child placed in phase 3 is assessed against phase 3 descriptors whatever their age. Families are often unaware of the phase, and it changes what a grade of 5 means entirely.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating, C Communicating, D Thinking critically. Criterion D is where most marks go missing: students describe a source rather than evaluating its origin, purpose, value and limitation. That is a formula and it can be learned in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Inquiring and designing, C Processing and evaluating, D Reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B rewards a precisely worded hypothesis and controlled variables, and criterion C rewards correct processing plus a genuine evaluation of method. Both are written skills, not laboratory skills.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating patterns, C Communicating, D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B surprises families: it asks a student to find a pattern, describe it as a general rule and then justify why the rule holds. Strong calculators often score poorly on it.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria A Inquiring and analysing, B Developing ideas, C Creating the solution, D Evaluating. The marks live in the documentation as much as in the artefact: a specification with testable criteria, a planned sequence, and an evaluation against the original specification rather than against how the student feels it went.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria A Investigating, B Developing, C Creating or performing, D Evaluating. The process journal carries real weight, and students who produce strong work with no recorded development lose marks they cannot recover. Support here is largely about documentation discipline.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Planning for performance, C Applying and performing, D Reflecting and improving performance. The written criteria are assessed as seriously as the practical ones, which catches out capable athletes who treat the subject as purely physical.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria, usually once or twice a year, and typically the lowest marks on a report because students treat them as a side project. Understanding that an interdisciplinary unit asks for genuine synthesis between two subject groups, not two separate answers stapled together, is most of the work.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed against its own criteria and externally moderated. The marks come from a clear goal, a sustained process journal, evidence of applied Approaches to Learning skills and a report that addresses each criterion. It is the student's own work throughout; a tutor's role is coaching the process and reviewing their drafts.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.regionsIntro: These are the communities around Arabian Ranches 3 whose families share the same IB school options and the same weekly logistics. The notes below describe what each one changes about scheduling MYP support rather than repeating a description of the villas.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 3
regions.note: A young population, which in MYP terms means a concentration in MYP 1 to MYP 3 rather than in MYP 5. That is the useful half of the programme to get help in, because criterion habits formed in MYP 2 are still cheap to change.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: More families with children at both ends of the programme at once. A common arrangement here is one weekly slot for an MYP 5 Personal Project and a shorter fortnightly slot for a younger sibling's maths criterion B.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: The established centre of the cluster, with the longest-standing school relationships. Parents here are often the ones who already know how the report cycle works, and the request tends to be subject-specific rather than a general decoding of criterion marks.

regions.name: Mudon
regions.note: South along the Al Qudra corridor, and a community where the IB school run is genuinely long. The strongest argument for online MYP support in Mudon is that the family car is already committed twice a day.

regions.name: Town Square
regions.note: A commute shaped towards Al Barsha and Dubai Hills, where several of the IB schools used by this belt actually sit. MYP deadlines here belong to a campus a district away, so the household calendar and the school calendar diverge.

regions.name: Motor City
regions.note: Short school runs and a dense club schedule. Mid-week late afternoon slots are workable, but MYP 5 Personal Project sessions tend to land on the weekend because they need an uninterrupted hour rather than a convenient one.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Training timetables dominate weekday evenings, and students here frequently use Physical and Health Education as a strength. The criterion B and D written components are the part that still needs attention, and it is the part most often ignored.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills
regions.note: Longer journeys to every IB campus in the belt. Families here are the clearest case for a fixed online slot, since an in-person arrangement would spend its first twenty minutes on the Umm Suqeim Road.

regions.name: Remraam
regions.note: The furthest south of the group and the least served locally, which makes schedule reliability the deciding factor rather than tutor location. A slot that never gets cancelled is worth more than one that is theoretically closer.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: North-east of the belt and the destination for a share of secondary-age children from Arabian Ranches 3. Worth listing because the MYP calendar a family follows is set by the campus, not the community.

schoolClusters.city: IB schools used by Dubailand families
schoolClusters.note: The MYP is taught in a smaller set of Dubai schools than the British curriculum is, and few of them sit inside the Arabian Ranches communities. These are the campuses families from this belt most often travel to, which is why MYP deadlines here frequently belong to a different district from the home address.

schoolClusters.city: Schools in the belt that run the British route instead
schoolClusters.note: These are the schools that make the February decision a live one. A family in Arabian Ranches 3 weighing MYP 5 against a move to IGCSE is usually weighing a specific local British-curriculum place against a longer drive to an IB campus, and the academic question and the logistical question arrive together.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School (JESS) Arabian Ranches

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.modesIntro: Three patterns cover almost every MYP request from this belt, and the right one depends entirely on where the school year has got to. All are one-to-one and all run live over video, with screen sharing for drafts and a recording kept for the student.

modes.title: Fixed weekly criterion slot
modes.description: One hour a week on one subject group, aimed at a named criterion rather than at the subject in general. The session ends with the student's own work marked against the descriptor and a short note saying which band it currently sits in. This is the pattern for MYP 1 to MYP 4, where there is time for habits to form.
bullets: One subject group, one criterion focus at a time
The student's own assignments marked against descriptors
A running record of which band each criterion sits in
Same slot weekly, Gulf Standard Time

modes.title: Personal Project process coaching
modes.description: A fortnightly or weekly slot through MYP 5 covering goal setting, the process journal, Approaches to Learning evidence and report structure. The student produces everything; the tutor reviews it, asks the questions a moderator would ask, and says when a journal entry would earn nothing. The work remains entirely the student's own.
bullets: Goal narrowed until it is actually assessable
Process journal reviewed for criterion evidence
Report structure mapped against each criterion
No text supplied, drafted or dictated by the tutor

modes.title: Eight-week report-cycle block
modes.description: A short, dated run of sessions between one report and the next, built from the previous report's weakest criteria. It suits the family who has just read a confusing set of marks and wants a measurable answer by the following cycle rather than an open-ended arrangement.
bullets: Starts from the marked report, not from a general assessment
Two or three criteria targeted, never all eight
Progress judged against the next report cycle
Reviewed and stopped or renewed at the end

sections.heading: What an IB MYP tutor is for, and what the school already does
paragraphs: An MYP tutor is not a second teacher. The school teaches the units, sets the summative tasks and applies the criteria, and a tutor who tries to run a parallel curriculum simply adds hours. The useful role is narrower and more specific: translating criterion marks into a plan, drilling the written skills the criteria reward, and giving a student the experience of having their own work marked honestly against a descriptor before the teacher does it for real.

That translation work is genuinely necessary because MYP reporting is opaque to anyone who has not taught it. A report that says Sciences 5 hides four separate marks out of eight. The child may be a 7 on knowing and understanding and a 3 on reflecting on the impacts of science, and the single number averages a strength and a gap into a result that looks merely adequate. Buying general science tuition for that child wastes most of the money, because three quarters of the subject is fine.

The second thing a tutor adds is pace discipline in MYP 5. The Personal Project is the first piece of sustained independent work most students have ever attempted, and it fails on scheduling far more often than on ability. A student who has set a goal by the end of the first term, kept a journal weekly rather than retrospectively, and drafted a report section by section will almost always land a better mark than a more capable student working in a panic in the final fortnight.

Delivery is online, one-to-one and live over video, with screen sharing so a draft can be annotated while the student watches. There are no home visits in Dubai; that is an India-only service. For MYP work the online format is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise, because the material being discussed is almost always a document on a screen.

sections.heading: The MYP year counted backwards from the report cycle
paragraphs: Nobody publishes this and every MYP parent needs it. The programme has no external exam date for most students, so the calendar that governs everything is the school's own: the report cycle, the summative task schedule and the internal Personal Project deadlines. Those dates are set by the campus and they differ between schools, which is why the table below describes windows rather than dates and tells you who to ask.

Work backwards from the report rather than forwards from today. If the next report lands in early December, a criterion that needs to move has roughly eight teaching weeks to move in, and summative tasks inside that window are the only evidence that will count. A session plan that ignores the summative schedule is working on the right criterion at the wrong time, and the mark on the report will not reflect the effort.

For MYP 5, two additional sequences run alongside. The Personal Project has internal checkpoints from the first term, and in schools that register for it the optional on-screen eAssessment and ePortfolio route adds registration and submission deadlines of its own. Both sit outside the ordinary report rhythm, and both are set by the IB and the school rather than by anything a tutoring site can confirm. Ask the IB coordinator for the current dates in writing and build the plan on those.

The last column of the table is the one worth reading twice. It names what a student should already have finished at each point, which is a more useful planning tool than a date, because it still works if the school's calendar is a fortnight different from the typical one.

sections.heading: Criterion letters: what A, B, C and D actually ask for
paragraphs: This is the gap in every competing page about IB tutoring in Dubai, and it is the most practical thing a parent can be handed. Every MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria, each marked from 1 to 8 against published descriptors, and the criteria are not interchangeable between subjects. Criterion B in Mathematics asks for pattern investigation. Criterion B in Sciences asks for experimental design. Criterion B in Language Acquisition is reading comprehension. A tutor who talks about criteria generically is not teaching to them.

The pattern across the groups is that criteria A and C tend to reward knowledge and clear communication, which schools teach well and students usually manage. Criteria B and D tend to reward investigation, evaluation and reflection, which are the skills that get squeezed when a unit runs out of time. That is why so many MYP reports show a profile with two solid marks and two weaker ones, and it is why the weaker ones are often the cheapest to fix: they are formulaic skills that nobody has yet been shown explicitly.

Use the table to read your child's last report properly. Find the subject group, find the criterion with the lowest mark, and read what that criterion actually asks for. In most cases the description makes the problem obvious: a child who writes beautifully but scores 3 on Individuals and Societies criterion D is describing sources instead of evaluating their origin, purpose, value and limitation, and that is a fortnight's work rather than a term's.

One caveat. Descriptors are revised and schools publish the current version in the subject guide or the task sheet. Treat the table as a map of what each criterion is about, then work from the exact wording your child's teacher is marking against, which the task sheet will carry.

sections.heading: From four marks out of eight to one grade out of seven
paragraphs: Here is the arithmetic that explains most confused conversations at parents' evening. Four criteria, each marked from 1 to 8, give a maximum total of 32. That total is then converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using boundary bands published in the MYP documentation. It is not a percentage and it is not an average, and the bands are not evenly spaced, which has consequences a parent can use.

The consequence is that marks are worth different amounts depending on where a student sits. Moving a total from 18 to 19 crosses a boundary and changes the reported grade. Moving from 19 to 22 does not change the grade at all. A child on 18 who gains a single mark on one criterion gets a visibly better report; a child on 20 who gains two marks gets the same number as before and looks static to everyone who only reads the grade. That is not a flaw in the system but it is the reason to look at criterion marks rather than grades when judging whether support is working.

It also tells you where to aim. If your child is on a total of 17 with a weak criterion D, the highest-yield work is a two-mark improvement on criterion D, not a one-mark improvement spread across three. Tutors who ask to see the criterion breakdown before planning are doing this calculation; tutors who ask only for the grade cannot.

The bands below are the general conversion published in the MYP subject guides. Schools apply them, and some schools report with additional internal detail. Confirm the current version with your child's coordinator before planning around a single boundary, and treat any figure on a tutoring site, including this one, as something to check rather than something to rely on.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project is assessed against its own criteria and moderated by the IB, and it is the single most common reason a Dubai family looks for an MYP tutor in MYP 5. It is also the place where the academic-honesty line sits closest to the service being bought, so it is worth stating exactly where that line is before describing any help at all.

A tutor may ask the questions a moderator would ask. Is the goal specific enough to be assessed, or is it an ambition rather than a project? Does the process journal show decisions being made and revised, or is it a diary written in one sitting at the end? Which Approaches to Learning skills does the student actually have evidence for? Does the report address each criterion explicitly, or does it describe the product and hope? Those questions are coaching, and they are the most valuable hour a tutor can give an MYP 5 student.

A tutor may not supply text, dictate sentences, restructure a draft into their own prose, or contribute any part of the product itself. The project must be the student's own work from the first entry in the journal to the final submission. Any provider offering otherwise is offering an academic-honesty breach, and the consequence falls on your child rather than on the provider. If something sounds unusually convenient, that is what it is.

In practice the useful rhythm is fortnightly. Sessions come after the student has produced something, not before: a journal entry, a draft section, a revised goal statement. The tutor reads what exists, marks it against the criteria, and names the next piece. A student who keeps that rhythm from the first term of MYP 5 rarely needs the emergency sessions in the final fortnight, which is the version of this work nobody enjoys and nobody does well.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of MYP support can and cannot change
paragraphs: Families ask for a timeline and deserve a straight one. Eight weeks is roughly the gap between report cycles in a Dubai school, which makes it the natural unit for judging whether support is working. Within eight weeks some things move reliably, some move partly, and some do not move at all, and knowing which is which prevents both disappointment and wasted terms.

What moves reliably: criterion-specific written formulas. Source evaluation in Individuals and Societies. Hypothesis wording and variable control in Sciences criterion B. Communicating mathematics with correct notation and a justified general rule. Report structure for Design criterion D. These are procedures, they can be taught explicitly, and a student who has never been shown the procedure usually gains two marks within four or five sessions of focused practice on their own work.

What moves partly: subject knowledge gaps. A student who missed a unit, or who changed schools mid-year, has real content to rebuild, and eight weeks covers one unit properly rather than three. What moves slowly: reading stamina, mathematical fluency and the habit of independent work. Those are built over a year, they are the right thing to work on in MYP 2 and MYP 3, and they are the wrong thing to start in the term before a decision has to be made.

What does not move on command is the grade on the report, for the boundary-band reason set out above. A child whose criterion total goes from 20 to 23 has made genuine progress and will show the same 5 as before. Judge the work by the criterion marks and the quality of the student's drafts, agree in advance what success looks like, and review at the report cycle rather than week by week. Nobody can promise a grade, and the structure of MYP reporting makes that promise even emptier than usual.
bullets: Criterion procedures: two marks in four to five sessions is realistic
Content gaps: one unit per eight weeks, not three
Fluency and stamina: a year's work, best started early in the programme
The reported grade may not move even when the criterion total does

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar and when the work actually happens
paragraphs: A Dubai school year has a shape that MYP planning documents do not describe, and families new to the Emirates consistently miscount the available weeks. Term dates fall in late August or early September and run to late June or early July. There are breaks in the autumn and at the winter holidays. And there is Ramadan, during which school days are shortened across the emirate and the rhythm of the household changes completely for a month.

The practical consequence for MYP support is that the weeks between the mid-year report and the final one are fewer than they look. If Ramadan falls inside that window, a family that had planned twelve sessions will realistically get eight or nine, and the ones during the month work far better in the evening after Iftar than in the shortened afternoon. Saying this in advance and building the plan around it is better than discovering it in week three and losing momentum.

The same calendar awareness applies to the Personal Project. An internal submission deadline in Term 2 that sits a fortnight after a shortened-hours month is a deadline that needs the journal substantially finished before the month starts. Students who plan around that comfortably outperform equally capable students who do not, and this is one of the few pieces of advice in MYP support that costs nothing to follow.

Scheduling here is deliberately flexible for that reason. Slots move to post-Iftar timings during Ramadan, pause for school study leave and the long summer break, and resume on a fixed weekday evening in Gulf Standard Time once term restarts. For a family in Arabian Ranches 3 juggling a long school run and a club calendar, that predictability is usually worth more than any particular hour of the day.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs in Dubai, and who publishes what
paragraphs: Market rates first, with attribution, because most pages competing for this search publish no figure at all and two of the ones that do quote in US dollars. As of October 2026, published Dubai rates put budget online tuition at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit runs AED 180 to 500 with travel included, on Bestimate's Dubai rate table and independent home-tutor advertising. Specialist IB tuition sits at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270.

Those are market bands, not an IB Gram price list, and they are the market for one hour of teaching. MYP support is usually bought in a different shape from exam-year tuition: a fortnightly Personal Project slot across two terms, or an eight-week criterion block, rather than a weekly hour for a year. Comparing a monthly package price against an hourly rate without adjusting for that is how families end up surprised, and monthly packages advertised in this market have been seen at around AED 799 for eight online sessions.

For context on where tutoring sits in a Dubai family's education spending, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. The fee line is flat; the discretionary line is not. A sensible MYP plan is explicit about how many sessions it is buying and what the review point is, rather than open-ended.

Our own route is the introductory lesson and a conversation. Quoting a figure before anyone has read the criterion breakdown on your child's report would be a number invented to fill a form, and the thing this market is short of is not prices but honest ones with their sources attached.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the questions worth asking a tutor
paragraphs: KHDA is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and it is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. It inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the published report for your child's IB school is free, specific and usually honest about the middle years. If you are weighing an MYP campus against a British-curriculum one in the Dubailand belt, those two reports are a better input than any prospectus.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately and federally. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule has been published, any specific amount quoted to you is unverified. And no tutor or platform, including this one, can describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board on the strength of a tutoring permit. The permit is a permit. KHDA's Educational Services Permit is a separate thing, issued to training institutes that hold premises.

The questions worth asking, then, are concrete. Does the tutor hold the MoHRE permit and under which eligibility category? Which MYP subject groups have they taught, and to which year groups? Can they describe what criterion D asks for in the subject you care about, without looking it up? And will they mark your child's own work in front of them? A tutor who answers all four clearly is a better bet than one with a longer list of adjectives.

process.title: Send the report with the criterion marks
process.description: Not the summary grade, the breakdown. Four marks out of eight per subject group is the information that decides what to work on, and most schools publish it in the full report or on the learning platform. If you only have the grade, ask the tutor for help reading the detailed version rather than starting without it.

process.title: Name the next deadline
process.description: The next summative task, the next report date, or the Personal Project checkpoint. MYP support that is not anchored to a dated piece of assessed work tends to drift, because there is no external exam to pull it forward. One date on the first email changes the shape of the whole plan.

process.title: Agree which two criteria
process.description: Never all four, and never all eight subject groups. Two criteria in one or two subject groups is the amount of change an eight-week block can carry, and choosing them deliberately is the difference between measurable progress and a general feeling that things are a bit better.

process.title: Take the introductory lesson
process.description: One session with the matched tutor before committing. The test afterwards is simple: did the tutor mark something your child had written, and could they explain why it sat in one band rather than the next. A session that only discussed the subject in general has not demonstrated anything.

process.title: Review at the report, not weekly
process.description: Compare criterion marks across the two cycles either side of the block. If the targeted criteria have moved and the others are stable, the plan worked even where the reported grade did not change. If nothing has moved, change the plan or the tutor; both are normal.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-first, not subject-first
whyPoints.description: Support is planned from the four marks on the report rather than from a subject name, because the work that moves criterion B is not the work that moves criterion D. It is a narrower promise than general tuition and a considerably more useful one for a programme assessed this way.

whyPoints.title: The student's own work gets marked
whyPoints.description: Every session works on something your child produced: a draft, a lab write-up, a journal entry, a set of solutions. Marking their own text against the descriptor is what teaches the descriptor. Generic worksheets teach the subject and leave the assessment untouched.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on the Personal Project
whyPoints.description: Process coaching, questioning and review of the student's own drafts. No text supplied, no sections drafted, no product contributed. The project is moderated by the IB and the consequence of a breach lands on the student, which is reason enough to be explicit about it.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built on the UAE calendar
whyPoints.description: Slots account for the Dubai term shape, shortened school hours during Ramadan, study leave and the long summer. Sessions move to post-Iftar timings when that works better, and the plan counts the weeks that actually exist rather than the ones on a generic planner.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted as the market, with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the date. There is no invented price list, no dollar pricing for a family that pays in dirhams, and no claim about value that a parent cannot check.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated up front
whyPoints.description: Some MYP subject groups have thinner UAE-based specialist cover than others, Design and Arts in particular. If your slot cannot be filled locally you are told, and offered either a different time or a tutor teaching into Gulf Standard Time from elsewhere, disclosed before booking.

faqs.question: What does a 5 in MYP Sciences actually mean when the criteria are marked out of 8?
faqs.answer: It means a criterion total somewhere between 19 and 23 out of 32, converted using the published boundary bands. The grade hides four separate marks: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A child can be a 7 on the first and a 3 on the last and still report a 5. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown rather than the grade, because the remedy for a weak criterion B is experimental design practice and the remedy for a weak criterion D is structured reflection writing. They are different work.

faqs.question: Is MYP eAssessment compulsory for a child finishing MYP 5 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. The on-screen examinations and ePortfolios at the end of MYP 5 are an optional route that individual schools choose to register for, and many Dubai schools do not. Whether your child sits them, and in which subjects, is a question for the school's IB coordinator rather than for a tutoring provider, and the registration and submission deadlines come from the IB and the school. Ask for the current dates in writing. If the school does not offer the route, the MYP concludes on internal criterion-based assessment and the Personal Project, which is entirely normal.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without breaching academic honesty?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can ask whether the goal is specific enough to be assessed, whether the process journal shows decisions being made rather than a diary written at the end, which Approaches to Learning skills have evidence behind them, and whether the report addresses each criterion explicitly. That is coaching and it is genuinely valuable. What a tutor must not do is supply text, dictate sentences, rewrite a draft in their own prose or contribute to the product. The project is moderated by the IB and the consequence of a breach falls on the student.

faqs.question: My child moved from a British school into MYP 3 — what is the gap we should expect?
faqs.answer: Rarely content, usually assessment grammar. A student arriving from Year 8 or Year 9 in a British school has met topics in a different order and has been marked on percentages and levels rather than on four criteria out of eight. The specific gaps that show up are criterion B and D skills: designing an investigation, evaluating sources, justifying a general rule, reflecting against a specification. None is hard but none has been taught, so the first reports look worse than the child's actual ability. Four to six sessions on criterion procedures usually closes most of it.

faqs.question: How are four MYP criterion marks turned into one grade out of 7?
faqs.answer: They are added, not averaged. Four criteria marked 1 to 8 give a total out of 32, and that total converts to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundary bands: roughly 1 to 5 for a grade 1, 6 to 9 for a 2, 10 to 14 for a 3, 15 to 18 for a 4, 19 to 23 for a 5, 24 to 27 for a 6 and 28 to 32 for a 7. The bands are uneven, so a single mark can change the grade at one point and three marks can change nothing at another. Confirm the current bands with your child's coordinator.

faqs.question: What are ATL skills and can they actually be taught in a tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Approaches to Learning skills are the thinking, research, communication, social and self-management skills the MYP teaches alongside subject content, and they carry real weight in the Personal Project where a student has to evidence them. They can be taught, but only through subject work rather than in the abstract. A session that builds a research plan for an actual Individuals and Societies investigation teaches research skills; a session that discusses research skills teaches nothing. Ask any tutor to demonstrate the skill inside a task your child is genuinely doing this fortnight.

faqs.question: Should my child leave for IGCSE at 14 or stay in the MYP through to MYP 5?
faqs.answer: It depends on how your child is actually assessed well, and the criterion marks are the honest evidence. Students who score strongly on criteria that reward sustained process and investigation usually do better staying in the programme and moving to the Diploma. Students whose strength is timed recall and whose process marks lag often do better on externally examined IGCSEs. Around Arabian Ranches 3 the decision usually comes with a school change as well, because the British-curriculum schools outnumber the IB ones in this belt, so the logistics and the academics arrive together.

faqs.question: How long does it take to move an MYP criterion mark from a 4 to a 6?
faqs.answer: For procedural criteria, four to five focused sessions on the student's own work is a realistic expectation, because the gain comes from learning an explicit formula nobody has shown them: how a source evaluation is structured, how a hypothesis is worded, how a general rule is justified. For criteria that depend on underlying content or writing fluency, plan a term rather than a half-term. And remember that a two-mark gain inside a wide boundary band may not change the reported grade at all, which is a reason to judge progress on criterion marks rather than on the report headline.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change when MYP tutoring should happen in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially. School days are shortened across the emirate for the month, household routines change, and an afternoon session that worked in February stops working. Sessions during the month generally work far better in the evening after Iftar. The planning consequence matters more than the timing one: if Ramadan falls between the mid-year and final report cycles, a family expecting twelve sessions will realistically get eight or nine, and any Personal Project journal work should be substantially finished before the month begins rather than after it.

faqs.question: What does MYP Mathematics criterion B, investigating patterns, actually ask for?
faqs.answer: It asks a student to find a pattern in given or generated data, describe it as a general rule in correct notation, test the rule on further cases and then justify why it holds. That final step is where marks go missing. Strong calculators often score poorly here because they produce the right answer without articulating the rule or defending it, and the descriptor rewards the articulation. It is a learnable procedure: generate, tabulate, conjecture, verify, justify. Four or five pattern investigations marked against the descriptor usually move the mark.

faqs.question: Is the MYP good preparation for the IB Diploma or does it leave gaps?
faqs.answer: It prepares students well for the parts of the Diploma that reward independent work, research and sustained writing, which is most of the internal assessment and all of the Extended Essay. The gaps that appear most often are mathematical fluency and the volume of timed written work, because the MYP assesses process more than speed. Both can be built during MYP 4 and MYP 5 rather than repaired in DP1, and a child aiming at a Higher Level science or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches should be building them deliberately from the February of MYP 5 onwards.

faqs.question: What does MYP tuition cost in Dubai, in dirhams?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates as of October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tuition, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB specialist. Those bands come from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate's Dubai rate table, and they are the market rather than our price list. MYP work is often bought as a fortnightly Personal Project slot or an eight-week criterion block rather than a weekly hour across a year.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report shows a different grade for the same subject each term — why?
faqs.answer: Because different units assess different criteria. A term whose summative tasks happened to weight criterion A and C can produce a higher grade than a term weighted towards B and D, with no change in the child's ability at all. That is why direction matters more than level in MYP reporting, and why comparing two cycles criterion by criterion is the only sensible reading. Ask which criteria each cycle actually assessed; schools will tell you, and the answer usually explains a swing that looked alarming on the summary page.

faqs.question: Does the Community Project in MYP 3 or MYP 4 need tutoring support?
faqs.answer: Usually not in the way the Personal Project does. The Community Project is shorter, often done in pairs or groups, and schools scaffold it heavily. Where support helps is the same place it helps later: keeping a process journal that records decisions as they are made, and writing a report that addresses the criteria rather than narrating the activity. A single session early on, teaching a student what a useful journal entry looks like, tends to be worth more than several sessions near the deadline.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do families in Arabian Ranches 3 typically use for the MYP?
faqs.answer: Few of the MYP campuses sit inside the Arabian Ranches communities, so families travel. The schools used most often from this belt include Fairgreen International School, GEMS International School Al Khail, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai. Those names are listed as market context only and imply no relationship with us. The practical point is that your child's MYP calendar is set by a campus that may be twenty minutes away, so the deadlines that matter are the school's, not the community's.

faqs.question: Can MYP support really work online for a family in Arabian Ranches 3?
faqs.answer: For this programme it suits the work particularly well, because almost everything being discussed is a document on a screen: a draft, a journal entry, a lab write-up, a set of annotated solutions. Sessions run one-to-one and live over video with screen sharing and a recording. There are no home visits in Dubai, and that service exists only in India. The real gain is selection: an online slot can be filled by a tutor who has taught the specific subject group, where a visit can only be filled by someone willing to drive out to the Dubailand belt at five in the afternoon.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.closingHeading: Start from the report and the next deadline
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.closingBody: Two pieces of information make an MYP conversation productive: the criterion breakdown from your child's most recent report, and the date of the next summative task, report cycle or Personal Project checkpoint. With those, a tutor can name which two criteria are worth eight weeks of work, say honestly whether the reported grade is likely to move inside that window, and show you what the descriptor actually asks for. The introductory lesson is one session with the matched tutor, and the question afterwards is whether they marked your child's own writing. Sessions run live over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, for Arabian Ranches 3 and the communities around it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bluewaters-island.tutorsIntro: These are MYP specialists matched to the subject group, teaching Bluewaters students online. Session length and time are set from the year group and the bus, because at this age a plan that ignores either is a plan that stops in October.

intro.heading: Eleven and sixteen are not the same commute
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme spans five years and ages eleven to sixteen, which in practice means two completely different students under one heading. A Year 7 child and a Year 11 student living in the same Bluewaters building travel to school across the same bridge and come home in states that have almost nothing in common. Scheduling both the same way, which is what a household rota naturally does, is the most common reason MYP tutoring here fails.

Bluewaters Island is a compact residential community on reclaimed land off JBR, joined to the mainland by one road bridge and a pedestrian link, with no school on it. Children here commute inland to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim, The Greens or Emirates Hills. Younger students are often on earlier buses and home sooner, but they have less attention left when they arrive. Older ones arrive later with more stamina and more homework competing for it.

So the right session for a Year 7 child is twenty-five or thirty minutes, early, with a parent nearby for the first few minutes. The right session for a Year 11 student in the final MYP year is longer, later, and probably involves the Personal Project. Treating those as the same product, at the same hour, in the same length, is why one of the two children usually ends up disengaged within a month.

This page is built around that. Session length and timing by year group, which MYP criteria work survives a tired slot and which needs a fresh student, how a household with two children at two campuses schedules both, and where the Personal Project fits in a final MYP year that already contains a long bus day.

The criteria content is here too, because it is what the work actually consists of. Four criteria per subject, each scored out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries, with the criterion letters meaning different things in different subject groups. Most lost marks in this cluster are communication marks rather than content marks, and reading the published descriptor for the band above is the intervention that moves them.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run in India only, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. For MYP work the relevant consequence is session length: because nobody travels, a twenty-five minute session is possible, and no tutor crosses a bridge in evening traffic for twenty-five minutes. Reviewed October 2026.

One qualification about who this page is for. It assumes a student who is coping and underperforming against the descriptors, which describes most MYP students whose families search for a tutor. A child who is genuinely struggling with the content, or who may have an unidentified learning need, is a different conversation and the first call belongs to the school rather than to us. We will say so rather than selling sessions, because criterion work on top of an unaddressed difficulty is an expensive way to make no progress.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bluewaters-island.programmesIntro: Three stages inside and around the MYP, each with a different scheduling shape. The middle years are the forgiving part; the first year and the last year are the ones that need planning.

programmes.name: Early Middle Years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, with interdisciplinary units and approaches to learning running alongside. At this stage criterion familiarity is the whole game: a student who understands what each criterion rewards will outperform one with better content knowledge and no descriptor literacy, and the habit transfers across every subject.
programmes.countryNote: This is the age group most often scheduled badly on Bluewaters. A Year 7 child home at three or four is tired rather than free, and an hour-long session at five produces twenty useful minutes. Twenty-five or thirty minutes twice a week, with a parent nearby at the start, achieves considerably more and costs less.

programmes.name: Penultimate MYP year
programmes.description: Subject criteria continue with increasing demand, and the Personal Project usually begins to be discussed. Students start to feel the gap between what they know and what the descriptors reward, which makes this the year criterion literacy work pays most, before the final year adds a major independent piece on top.
programmes.countryNote: A Year 10 student from Bluewaters is typically home between four and half past five depending on the campus, with a real homework load. One session a week of forty to forty-five minutes on criterion work, plus occasional weekend time, is the pattern that fits. Two weekday hours is the arrangement that collapses.

programmes.name: Final MYP year and the Personal Project
programmes.description: The final year carries the Personal Project, an extended independent piece with a goal, an inquiry, a process journal, a product and a report assessed against its own criteria. Subject criteria continue alongside it, and some schools also enter students for MYP eAssessment. The project is the part that slips.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project is where the commute bites hardest, because the work needs sustained blocks and the weekday evening does not supply them. On this island it belongs on weekend mornings almost entirely, with the weekday slot used for short journal checks rather than for the writing itself.

programmes.name: Transition into the Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma replaces continuous criterion-based judgement with externally examined papers plus one internally assessed component per subject. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with a maximum of 45 points.
programmes.countryNote: Because the MYP sets no external examination, a Bluewaters student entering DP1 has usually never sat a three-hour paper. The final MYP term and the summer after it are the highest-value tutoring window in the programme, and on this island the weekend morning is where that bridging work has to sit.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bluewaters-island.subjectsIntro: The eight MYP subject groups, with what the criteria measure and whether the work survives a tired weekday slot. That last judgement is what makes a schedule hold on an island with a long commute.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Communication marks are lost through unexplained working, which is habit work and survives a tired slot well. Investigating patterns needs a fresher student.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Processing and evaluating involves graph work that drills well late in the day; inquiring and designing needs sustained thought.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is where the top band sits and where students stop short, offering description where the descriptor asks for evaluation. Needs a fresh student.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Analysing marks are lost when a student summarises content instead of examining how the text produces its effect. Extended writing needs a weekend slot rather than a weekday evening.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Vocabulary and structure drill suits short tired sessions very well, which makes this the most schedule-friendly group in the programme.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than students expect, and responding marks are lost when reflection describes what was made rather than evaluating the choices.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Students over-invest in the product and under-invest in the design cycle documentation, which is where most of the available marks sit.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and reflective components surprise families who assumed the subject was practical only, and they are straightforwardly teachable in short sessions.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, supported by a process journal maintained throughout. Needs sustained weekend blocks on this island, with weekday slots used only for short journal checks.

sections.heading: Session length by year group, not by household
paragraphs: The instinct in a household with two or three children is to standardise: everybody gets an hour, on a rota, and the week is tidy. For the MYP that is the wrong design, because an eleven-year-old and a sixteen-year-old have different attention spans, different arrival times and different homework loads, and the gap between them is five years of development rather than a scheduling preference.

For Years 7 to 9, twenty-five to thirty minutes is the honest figure. A child home at three or four after a bus from Al Barsha is tired rather than available, and the last half of an hour-long session at five is usually spent watching them lose focus. Two short sessions a week achieve more than one long one, cost less, and are short enough that a difficult day does not end the arrangement.

For Year 10, forty to forty-five minutes on a weekday works, with anything demanding moved to the weekend. Homework has become a serious competitor for the evening by this point, and a session that displaces homework rather than supporting it creates a problem rather than solving one.

For the final MYP year, the weekday slot stays short and the weight moves to weekend mornings, because the Personal Project needs blocks of sustained attention that a Bluewaters weekday evening cannot provide. A family that plans for this at the start of the year, rather than discovering it in February, usually gets the project finished without a crisis.
