sections.heading: Which criteria work survives a tired slot
paragraphs: MYP criteria are skills rather than topics, and they differ in how much mental energy they require. Planning the week around that distinction is what allows a short weekday session to be genuinely productive rather than nominally attended.

Communication criteria survive tiredness best, which is convenient because they are also where most students in this cluster leave the largest share of marks. Laying out working so a reader can follow it, defining terms, labelling a diagram, structuring a paragraph so the point comes first: all of that is presentational, all of it is teachable by example, and a tired student can apply it to a piece of work they have already written.

Investigation and inquiry criteria do not survive tiredness. Criterion B in the sciences, inquiring and designing, asks a student to frame a question and plan a method, which requires holding several possibilities in mind at once. Investigating patterns in mathematics is the same. Thinking critically in Individuals and Societies is the same again. These belong in a fresh slot, which on this island means a weekend morning for most families.

Language Acquisition is the exception that makes scheduling easier. Vocabulary, structures and comprehension drill suit short tired sessions unusually well, because the work is repetitive and immediately checkable. A household juggling two children can often put the Language Acquisition session in the least promising slot in the week and still get value from it, which is a useful piece of flexibility when two campuses produce two awkward arrival times.

sections.heading: Reading the descriptor, which is the whole method
paragraphs: The most useful session we run with a new MYP student takes a returned piece of work with its criterion score, opens the published descriptor for that band and the band above, and asks the student to find the difference in words. Students are routinely assessed against criteria they have never read, which is like being marked against a rubric kept in another room.

The letters mean different things in different subject groups, which compounds the confusion. In the sciences, Criterion B is inquiring and designing and Criterion C is processing and evaluating. In mathematics, Criterion B is investigating patterns and Criterion C is communicating. In Individuals and Societies, Criterion D is thinking critically. A student who has learned what Criterion C means in mathematics and assumes the same in science is answering the wrong instruction.

The pattern across this cluster is consistent. Communication and the critical or evaluative criterion carry most of the lost marks, and both are presentation and reasoning skills rather than knowledge. A student who knows the material and cannot lay out reasoning in the form a descriptor rewards will sit a band or two below their understanding, in every subject, every term.

Once the student has read the descriptor and redrafted one piece to meet the higher band, they generally start applying it without being told. That is why this work suits short sessions: the insight is quick, and what follows is repetition on their own tasks rather than new teaching. It is also why the work does not need an expensive tutor, only one who will use the published wording rather than a paraphrase.

sections.heading: Two children, two campuses, one bridge
paragraphs: Many Bluewaters households have children at two different schools, because provision for different ages sits in different places and nothing on the island is walkable. That produces two arrival times, two homework loads, two reporting calendars and often two assessment systems, since one child may be on the MYP and another on IGCSE or an American curriculum.

The arrangement that works is consecutive short slots rather than parallel long ones. The younger child goes first, soon after arriving, for twenty-five or thirty minutes while the older one eats and settles. The older child follows for forty-five. Both at the same times every week, with different subject specialists working to one shared written schedule.

That requires some administration, and it is worth it. The alternative, which is improvising around whoever seems to need help most this week, produces an arrangement that survives the easy weeks and collapses in the busy ones, which are the weeks it was bought for. Fixed times also mean the children stop negotiating about it, which removes a daily argument from the household.

Where the children are on different systems the schedules also have to respect two reporting calendars and two holiday patterns, which do not always align even between schools in the same emirate. A plan written against one child's term dates will collide with the other's, usually in the week of a report. Put both calendars on the table at the first conversation and the collision is avoidable.

Same times every week so the household stops negotiating about it

sections.heading: The Personal Project against a long commute
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the largest independent piece a student has produced by that point, assessed on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, supported by a process journal maintained throughout. On an island with a long bus day it is also the piece of work least compatible with a weekday evening, and families who do not plan for that end up compressing it.

The process journal is the specific trap and also the solution. It is meant to be kept as the work happens, recording decisions, setbacks and changes of direction, and it cannot be reconstructed at the end: a journal assembled in the final fortnight reads exactly like one assembled in the final fortnight, and the reflection criterion suffers. But journal entries are short, which means they fit the weekday slot perfectly while the substantive work waits for the weekend.

Goal feasibility is the second trap, and on this island it has a local dimension. A goal requiring materials, a venue or repeated travel to the mainland is more expensive in time here than it would be in a villa community with a garage and a garden. Counting the real hours in week one, including the crossings, prevents a project that would have needed a term it does not have.

Our role is bounded and we state it plainly. We teach what each criterion requires, question whether the goal is achievable in the time available, check the journal is being maintained, and give feedback on report drafts the student wrote. We do not produce the product, write any part of the report, or contribute content to either. The consequence of crossing that line falls on the student's record.

sections.heading: What an MYP report means, and the three questions to ask
paragraphs: Parents moving from a British or Indian system frequently find the first MYP report unreadable, and that reaction is reasonable. There are criterion scores out of eight, a converted grade out of seven, no percentages, and a best-fit judgement rather than an average. None of it maps onto what they are used to.

The mechanics: each criterion is scored out of eight against published descriptors, the four scores are totalled, and the total converts to a 1-7 grade using boundaries published in the MYP documentation. Teachers apply a best-fit judgement across the evidence rather than averaging every mark recorded, which means a single weak task does not sink a grade and a single strong one does not rescue it. Consistency matters more than peaks.

So the questions to ask at a parents' evening are not about percentages. Which criterion is lowest? What does the descriptor for the next band up say, in its actual wording? And which upcoming task will assess that criterion again? Those three are all answerable and together they give a family something to act on.

In the final MYP year, add a fourth: what timed assessment will the school run before DP1 begins? The MYP sets no external examination, so a student can hold strong criterion scores and still be unprepared for a three-hour paper. The answer tells you whether a bridging block is needed, and on this island that block belongs on weekend mornings in the final term.
bullets: Criterion scores are out of eight; the reported grade is 1-7, converted from the total
Teachers apply a best-fit judgement rather than averaging every mark
Ask which criterion is lowest and what the next band's descriptor says

sections.heading: Ramadan, travel and the slot that moves
paragraphs: During Ramadan, school hours in Dubai shorten and household routines move later. For MYP students that changes the slot rather than ending it, and in some ways improves it: a younger child who was tired at five may be more alert at a later hour once the household is awake, and older students often work well after Iftar.

The planning complication is that Ramadan shifts earlier by roughly eleven days each Gregorian year, so the school weeks it overlaps with change annually. A schedule copied from a previous year will be wrong about which term is affected, which matters when it lands near a reporting point or a Personal Project deadline.

Travel is the other predictable disruption, and on Bluewaters it is frequent. Because sessions are online they follow the laptop, so a fortnight abroad usually means a different clock time rather than a gap. That matters more at MYP level than families expect, because criterion work is cumulative in a quiet way: the student is building a habit of reading descriptors, and a month off resets more of it than a month of content teaching would.

The practical step is to put the dates on the table at the first conversation: school term dates for each child, travel plans, and the Ramadan window for the year ahead. A schedule built around those still exists in week nine, and both children's slots move together rather than separately. The alternative, which is renegotiating each disruption as it arrives, is how a sensible plan turns into a series of cancellations by the second term.
bullets: Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each Gregorian year
Post-Iftar sessions are a normal request and the slot is held
A later slot sometimes suits a younger child better than a tired five o'clock
Online sessions follow the laptop, so travel changes the clock time not the plan

sections.heading: Cost, permits and starting
paragraphs: MYP support should cost less than Diploma support, because the work is criterion literacy and redrafting rather than examination decoding. That sits in the qualified subject tutor band of roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Budget and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which is adequate for Language Acquisition drill and younger-years practice.

At the session lengths this page recommends, the arithmetic is modest. Two twenty-five minute sessions a week across a twelve-week term is ten hours, or AED 1,500 to AED 3,000 at the qualified band. A weekly forty-five minute session is nine hours, or AED 1,350 to AED 2,700. The specialist band of AED 200-450 is worth paying for Personal Project criterion feedback and for the bridging block before DP1, and not for Year 8 descriptor work.

On permits: individual tutors need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. u.ae states that tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which inspects annually and publishes ratings. IB Gram is not IB authorised, KHDA approved or ADEK approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and has no UAE office.

To start, send the year group, the subject, the real arrival time, and a returned piece of assessed work with its criterion scores on it. That last item is the one families leave out and the one that makes the first session useful. Then take the free trial lesson, run at the day, time and length intended for the weekly session, with a short written note afterwards naming the criterion and the gap.

process.title: Tell us the year group and the real arrival time
process.description: Not the school finish time. A Year 7 child home at three after a bus from Al Barsha is tired rather than available, and a Year 11 student arriving at half past five has more stamina and more homework. Those two need different lengths at different hours, and the household rota is the wrong unit.

process.title: Send returned work with its criterion scores
process.description: A marked task with its criterion score is the whole diagnosis, because the score plus the published descriptor for the band above shows the gap in words. Families routinely send a report summary instead, which confirms that something is wrong without saying what to do about it.

process.title: Set the length by age, not by convention
process.description: Twenty-five to thirty minutes for Years 7 to 9, forty to forty-five for Year 10 and the final year, with sustained work moved to weekend mornings. Short sessions survive a bad day, cost less and fit a week where everything structured is across a bridge.

process.title: Free trial at the intended day and length
process.description: We run the trial at the time and length we intend the weekly session to be, so you find out whether it works before committing. A short written note follows, naming the criterion and the specific gap. No card held, nothing renews, one free rematch if the fit is wrong.

process.title: Plan the Personal Project in the first weeks
process.description: Goal feasibility counting real travel time, the criteria read before anything is chosen, and the journal started immediately with weekly short checks. On this island the substantive project work belongs at weekends, and planning that in September prevents a February crisis.

whyPoints.title: Length set by year group
whyPoints.description: Twenty-five minutes for a Year 7 child and forty-five for a final-year student are different products, not the same product in different sizes. Standardising on an hour across a household is why one of two children usually disengages within a month of starting.

whyPoints.title: Short sessions genuinely available
whyPoints.description: Because nobody travels, a twenty-five minute session is economic. No tutor crosses the bridge in evening traffic for twenty-five minutes, which means in-home arrangements cannot offer the length that actually suits a tired eleven-year-old at this age.

whyPoints.title: Criteria work matched to energy
whyPoints.description: Communication criteria and Language Acquisition drill survive a tired slot, and they are where most marks in this cluster are lost. Inquiring and designing, investigating patterns and thinking critically do not, so they go to weekend mornings rather than into a six o'clock session.

whyPoints.title: Descriptors read, not paraphrased
whyPoints.description: We work from the published subject-guide wording with the student reading the band above their own score. Students are routinely assessed against criteria they have never read, and simply reading them changes output within a session in most cases.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project planned around the bridge
whyPoints.description: Substantive work at weekends, short journal checks on weekdays, and goal feasibility counted in week one including the travel a mainland-dependent project would need. Almost every project failure we see is a scheduling failure rather than an ambition failure.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the band you need
whyPoints.description: Year 8 descriptor work does not require a specialist at AED 200-450 an hour and we will say so. The specialist band is worth paying for Personal Project criterion feedback and for the bridging block before DP1, which is a much smaller purchase than a weekly specialist arrangement.

faqs.question: How long should an MYP session be for a Year 7 child?
faqs.answer: Twenty-five to thirty minutes, twice a week, soon after they get home and have eaten something. A child returning to Bluewaters at three or four after a bus from Al Barsha is tired rather than available, and the second half of an hour-long session at five is usually spent watching attention drain away. Two short sessions achieve more than one long one, cost less, and are short enough that a difficult day does not end the arrangement. A parent nearby for the first few minutes helps measurably at this age.

faqs.question: Why schedule our two children differently when it complicates the week?
faqs.answer: Because an eleven-year-old and a sixteen-year-old differ by five years of development, not by preference. The younger child needs a short early session and the older one needs a longer later slot, probably involving the Personal Project. Standardising on an hour each on a rota is tidy and it is why one of the two usually disengages within a month. Consecutive slots work well: the younger child goes first while the older eats and settles, both at the same times every week.

faqs.question: Which MYP work can our daughter do when she is tired?
faqs.answer: Communication criteria and Language Acquisition drill, which is fortunate because communication is where most students in this cluster lose the largest share of marks. Laying out working so a reader can follow it, defining terms, labelling a diagram, structuring a paragraph so the point comes first: all presentational, all teachable by example, and all applicable to work she has already written. What does not survive a tired slot is inquiring and designing, investigating patterns, thinking critically, and any extended writing.

faqs.question: Criterion C means one thing in maths and another in science. Why?
faqs.answer: They label skills, and they mean different things in different subject groups, which is the main source of confusion. In the sciences, Criterion B is inquiring and designing and Criterion C is processing and evaluating. In mathematics, Criterion B is investigating patterns and Criterion C is communicating. In Individuals and Societies, Criterion D is thinking critically. Each is scored out of eight against descriptors published in the subject guide your child's school holds, and a student who assumes the letters mean the same everywhere is answering the wrong instruction.

faqs.question: Our report shows 24 out of 32 and a grade 6. How is that worked out?
faqs.answer: The four criterion scores are totalled, giving a figure out of thirty-two, and that total converts to a 1-7 grade using boundaries published in the MYP documentation. Teachers apply a best-fit judgement across the evidence rather than averaging every mark ever recorded, so a single weak task does not sink a grade and a single excellent one does not rescue it. The practical consequence is that consistency matters more than peaks, and a persistently weak criterion is the thing worth attacking.

faqs.question: With no percentages anywhere, what is worth asking the subject teacher?
faqs.answer: Three questions. Which criterion is lowest? What does the descriptor for the next band up say, in its actual wording? And which upcoming task will assess that criterion again? Those three are all answerable and give you something concrete to act on, whereas asking what percentage your child is on gets an answer that does not exist in this system. In the final MYP year add a fourth: what timed assessment will the school run before DP1 begins, since the MYP sets none.

faqs.question: When should the Personal Project happen in a Bluewaters week?
faqs.answer: Substantive work at weekends, almost entirely, with the weekday slot used for a ten to fifteen minute journal check. The project needs sustained blocks that a weekday evening after a bridge crossing does not supply, and families who do not plan for that compress the work into a final fortnight. Journal entries are short, which is why they fit the weekday slot perfectly while the writing and the product wait for a weekend morning when the student is actually capable of sustained thought.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether a Personal Project goal is realistic here?
faqs.answer: Count the hours honestly, including the travel. Take the weeks between the goal being agreed and the school's report deadline, subtract exam weeks, holidays and the time the report itself will take, then ask whether the product could be completed in what remains by a student also doing eight subjects. On this island add a local check: a goal needing materials, a venue or repeated trips to the mainland costs more in time than it would in a villa community, and each crossing is most of an evening.

faqs.question: Why does the process journal matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because it is assessed and it cannot be reconstructed. The journal is meant to record decisions, setbacks and changes of direction as they happen, and one assembled in the final fortnight reads exactly like one assembled in the final fortnight, with the reflection criterion suffering accordingly. Students who keep it weekly, even briefly, score better on reflection without doing any additional work. Entries are short enough to fit a ten-minute weekday check, which is the cheapest mark available in the whole project.

faqs.question: Is MYP tutoring cheaper than Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: It should be, because the work is different. Criterion literacy and redrafting need a tutor who will read the published descriptors with the student and hold them to the band above, which sits in the qualified band of roughly AED 150-300 an hour rather than the specialist band of AED 200-450. Two twenty-five minute sessions a week across a twelve-week term is ten hours, or AED 1,500 to AED 3,000. The specialist band is worth paying for Personal Project criterion feedback and the DP bridging block only.

faqs.question: Our son is in the wrong Language Acquisition phase. Can tutoring fix it?
faqs.answer: Tutoring can help him cope, but the fix is a conversation with the school rather than extra hours. Language Acquisition runs in phases, and a student placed too low is unchallenged while one placed too high is assessed against descriptors he cannot yet reach, producing low scores that look like a learning problem and are really a placement problem. Ask which phase he is in, what evidence placed him there, and what the review process is. Then decide whether paid support is needed at all.

faqs.question: How do we use the last MYP term before DP1 starts in September?
faqs.answer: Bridging work for the Diploma, on weekend mornings. The MYP sets no external examination, so a student may never have sat a paper longer than an hour while the Diploma asks for two and three-hour papers using command terms the MYP does not use. Eight to twelve sessions introducing timed questions, answer structure against mark bands, and the content prerequisites of the chosen Higher Level subjects consistently achieves more than the same hours spent in DP1 recovering from the first mock.

faqs.question: Will sessions continue through Ramadan and travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, by moving rather than cancelling. During Ramadan school hours shorten and routines move later, and a later slot sometimes suits a younger child better than a tired five o'clock, so we shift to post-Iftar times and hold the tutor. Note that Ramadan moves about eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, so last year's schedule will be wrong about which term is affected. Because sessions are online they also follow the laptop, so a fortnight abroad means a different clock time rather than a gap.

faqs.question: May a tutor read my son's project report draft before he submits it?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor can teach what each criterion requires, question whether the goal is achievable in the time available, check that the process journal is being maintained, and give feedback on report drafts the student wrote. A tutor cannot produce the product, write any part of the report, contribute content to either, or make the design decisions. The test is authorship, and the consequence of crossing it is an academic honesty finding carried by the student rather than by anyone else.

faqs.question: Do you come to our apartment on Bluewaters for MYP sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. At MYP age the length point matters most: because nobody travels, a twenty-five minute session is economic, and no tutor crosses the bridge in evening traffic for twenty-five minutes, so in-home arrangements cannot offer the length that suits a tired eleven-year-old. Independent local tutors do work across the Marina and JBR and can suit a younger child who needs an adult physically present.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bluewaters-island.closingHeading: Schedule the child, not the household
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bluewaters-island.closingBody: The Middle Years Programme covers five years of development, so the useful questions are about age rather than subject. When does this particular child actually walk through the door, and how much attention is left? Twenty-five minutes twice a week for a Year 7 student, forty-five for a final-year one, with inquiry work, extended writing and the Personal Project moved to weekend mornings when they are capable of sustained thought. Send a returned task with its criterion scores and take a free trial at the length you intend to use.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bur-dubai.tutorsIntro: These are tutors who ask for the unit planner and the assessment map before they ask what the student finds hard. In the MYP, timing a block of work to land before a task is most of the value.

intro.heading: The MYP runs on a calendar, and the calendar is published
paragraphs: Middle Years Programme tutoring in Dubai is bought, almost universally, at the wrong moment. A task comes home with a disappointing criterion score, the family reacts, and a tutor is engaged to repair something that has already been graded. The repair is not worthless - criterion judgements accumulate over a reporting period and a later, stronger piece of evidence carries weight - but it is a fraction as effective as the same hours spent two weeks earlier, before the task was set.

What makes that avoidable is that the calendar is not secret. MYP schools build units against the programme framework and publish, in some form, which units run when and which criteria each unit assesses. Not every criterion is assessed in every unit: a Sciences unit might assess Criterion A and Criterion C only, with B and D coming in the next one. That means a parent who asks for the assessment map knows in September which letters are being judged in which term, across all eight subject groups, and can time any paid help to arrive before the judgement rather than after it.

The second calendar feature families in Bur Dubai miss is the long run-up to the Personal Project. In MYP 5 the Personal Project is assessed on three criteria - Planning, Applying skills and Reflecting - worth 24 marks between them, and most of those marks live in a process journal kept over months. A project supported from the first term of MYP 5 costs a handful of sessions and runs calmly. The same project supported three weeks before the deadline costs more, delivers less, and pushes everyone towards a line that must not be crossed.

The third is the handover into the Diploma, which has a window nobody uses. The weeks between the end of MYP 5 and the start of DP1 are the single cheapest opportunity in five years to close the three gaps that actually cause trouble - examination stamina, algebraic fluency and command terms - and almost every family discovers those gaps halfway through the first DP1 report cycle instead. That is a scheduling failure rather than an academic one.

On how we work: IB Gram is an online platform and for every family in the UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India. For MYP work that suits the subject, because almost everything assessed is a document. The task sheet, the task-specific clarification and the student's own draft sit side by side on a shared screen, annotated together and saved, which is more useful than paper read across a Bur Dubai dining table and taken away afterwards.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bur-dubai.programmesIntro: Four points on the MYP path through a Bur Dubai school. What a tutoring hour should be doing differs at each, and the difference is almost entirely about when in the year it falls.

programmes.name: The early Middle Years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups running in parallel, each assessed against four criteria on a 0 to 8 band. The characteristic difficulty is not content but organisation: a student holding eight sets of unit requirements, five Approaches to Learning skill categories and a service record at once. Tutoring here is most useful as targeted work before a known assessment window rather than as a standing weekly commitment.
programmes.countryNote: In a Dubai school these three years also carry mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies alongside the eight subject groups, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. A student who looks weak across several criteria is quite often weak on load management rather than on any subject.

programmes.name: The upper Middle Years
programmes.description: The two years where the criterion descriptors tighten noticeably and where the Personal Project arrives. Subject choices narrow in some schools, interdisciplinary units continue, and reporting starts to be read by families as a predictor of Diploma readiness. The calendar here is dense and the Personal Project timeline is the single most plannable thing in it.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP 4 and 5 as the route into DP1 without IGCSE. That route is legitimate and means the student will never have sat a two-hour externally marked paper before DP1 mocks, which is a known, fixable gap if it is addressed in the handover window.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: Three criteria - Planning, Applying skills, Reflecting - at 8 marks each for a total of 24. The process journal is the evidence base for Planning and Reflecting, which means two-thirds of the marks sit in a document most students treat as an afterthought. The product itself feeds mainly one criterion. Starting in term one rather than term three is the whole game.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Personal Project seasons collide with a dense social calendar and, in some years, with Ramadan and a shortened school day. Families who front-load the planning and journal habit in the first term keep the spring calm; those who leave it find the deadline landing in the worst possible weeks.

programmes.name: The handover into the Diploma
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The three gaps that bite coming from MYP 5 are examination stamina, algebraic fluency and command terms, and none of them are visible on an MYP report. All three are closeable in the weeks between the two programmes, which is the cheapest tutoring window in the whole five years.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai IB schools generally run DP1 mocks in the first year, and for an MYP 5 graduate that is often the first timed paper of their life. Preparing for that mechanically - starting at thirty minutes and building - is far more useful than revising content they already know.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bur-dubai.subjectsIntro: The eight subject groups plus the components that sit outside them, each with the point in the year at which help is actually worth buying.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Four criteria: Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, Reflecting on the impacts of science. The investigation criteria are assessed in specific units rather than continuously, so the useful fortnight is the one before the investigation unit begins - once the method has been submitted, the design marks are settled.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The investigation task that carries Criterion B usually lands once or twice a year and is flagged in advance. A student who has never written a general rule with justification before that task will not learn to during it.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Analysing, Organizing, Producing text, Using language. Assessment is spread across the year in different text types, which means the criterion weaknesses recur rather than resolve. Work on analysis of writer's choices, as opposed to plot summary, transfers to every subsequent task in the year.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, Reading, Speaking, Writing - four skills marked separately. Phase placement is reviewed at particular points in a school's year, which makes the review a date to plan around rather than a decision to accept passively. Ask when your school next reviews placement.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, Investigating, Communicating, Thinking critically. The research task carrying Criterion B and the source-evaluation work carrying Criterion D usually sit in the same unit, so one well-timed block before that unit affects half the subject's marks for the year.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, Developing ideas, Creating the solution, Evaluating. Design runs on the design cycle and the documentation is where the marks are, which means the moment to intervene is at the brief and specification stage - before the student has built anything that the specification then has to be retrofitted to.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Investigating, Developing, Creating or performing, Evaluating. Three of four criteria are evidenced through the process journal, which accrues over the whole unit. A journal habit established in week one of a unit cannot be reconstructed in the last week, and reconstruction is visible to a marker.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, Planning for performance, Applying and performing, Reflecting and improving performance. Three of the four are written: physiology knowledge, a training plan with measurable goals, and reflection against those goals. The plan has to exist before the performance block for the reflection to have anything to measure.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed on its own criteria - Evaluating, Synthesising, Reflecting - and reported separately. These units are scheduled in advance and often ambush students because the task asks for synthesis of two disciplines rather than two parallel essays. Knowing the unit is coming is most of the preparation.

subjects.name: Service as action
subjects.description: Required, recorded and reported rather than criterion-graded, with documented reflection against learning outcomes expected across all five years. A student who has recorded nothing until MYP 5 has a reconstruction problem. Ten minutes a term is the whole task, and almost nobody does it on time.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Five skill categories - communication, social, self-management, research and thinking - taught through subject units. Self-management and research are the two that show up as criterion losses in other subjects. A student who cannot cite a source loses Individuals and societies marks for a reason nobody has named for them.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Planning, Applying skills, Reflecting - 24 marks, two-thirds of them journal and report. The timeline is long and entirely visible from term one. A tutor coaches goal-setting, testable success criteria, journal habit and question-led reflection, and produces no part of the submitted work.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bur-dubai.regionsTitle: Bur Dubai and the districts around it
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bur-dubai.regionsIntro: Bur Dubai sits on the creek's south bank in the oldest part of the city. The MYP calendar is the same everywhere; what varies by neighbourhood is which hour of the afternoon a session can actually hold.

regions.name: Bur Dubai
regions.note: Apartments, several large schools within reach, and a busy early evening. Most MYP students living here travel out of the district to an IB school, so the session hour has to survive someone else's journey.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: Immediately west with its own school cluster, often a walk or a five-minute drive. Households here can hold a 4pm slot, which is unusual in Old Dubai and worth booking in the first week of term.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: Dense flats a few minutes inland, with shared study space the norm. For document-based MYP work a quiet surface and a single screen matter more than how close the tutor is.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: Inside the school belt, with schools walking distance away and the shortest commutes here. The earliest evening slots are usable, which is a real advantage when a task deadline is close.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Across the creek near the airport, and the nearest concentrated IB provision to Bur Dubai. Most MYP students in this part of the city attend a school in or near this cluster.

regions.name: Deira
regions.note: The north bank, with an unpredictable five o'clock crossing. Deira and Bur Dubai MYP families reach the same conclusion about scheduling, because travel is the unreliable variable rather than the teaching.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: A large British and Indian curriculum belt towards Sharjah where MYP is a minority route. Students here commute furthest to an IB school and generally need a session after six.

regions.name: Al Jaffiliya and Satwa
regions.note: Between Bur Dubai and Jumeirah, short runs to two clusters, and frequently two curricula inside one household. The family timetable rather than the tutor's address is what constrains the week.

schoolClusters.city: Bur Dubai, Al Mankhool and Oud Metha
schoolClusters.note: Mostly British and Indian curriculum, which means MYP students from these streets usually commute to an IB school elsewhere in the city. That daily journey is the practical reason a fixed online hour holds where a travel-based arrangement does not.

schoolClusters.city: Al Garhoud, Deira and Al Mamzar
schoolClusters.note: The nearest IB provision to Bur Dubai and where most MYP students in this part of the city actually study. Shorter school runs than the Al Qusais belt and the only group for whom a 4.30pm MYP session is routinely realistic.

sections.heading: The MYP year has a published shape - ask for the assessment map
paragraphs: The most useful document in Middle Years Programme tutoring is not a textbook. It is the school's assessment map: which units run in which term, and which of the four criteria each unit assesses, across all eight subject groups. Schools build this to plan teaching, and in most cases a parent can simply ask for it. Almost nobody does, which is why so much MYP tuition in Dubai is bought reactively.

The reason it matters is structural. Not every criterion is assessed in every unit. A Sciences unit may judge Criterion A and Criterion C and leave B and D for the next one. So a criterion that appears absent from a report is frequently just not yet assessed that period, and a family reading a report as a complete picture is reading an incomplete one. Conversely, a criterion that is about to be assessed is a known, dated target, and preparation can be aimed at it specifically.

That turns tutoring from a reaction into a plan. If Individuals and societies will assess Criterion D - Thinking critically, which rewards evaluating sources for origin, purpose, value and limitation - in a unit starting in six weeks, then a two-session block in week four is worth several times the same two sessions after the task comes back. The student arrives at the task already knowing what the descriptor rewards rather than discovering it from a mark.

A second practical use of the map is load. Eight subject groups each running units with assessment points produces weeks in which four criterion-marked tasks are due together, and those weeks are visible in advance. A family looking at the map in September can see the crunch weeks, and a student struggling in a crunch week is not necessarily struggling with any subject. We would rather tell a family to look at the calendar than sell them hours against a problem the calendar created.

sections.heading: The Personal Project counted backwards from the deadline
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the most plannable piece of work in the Middle Years Programme and the one most often left latest. It is assessed on Planning, Applying skills and Reflecting - three criteria at 8 marks each, 24 in total - and the process journal is the evidence for two of those three. That is the fact that should change behaviour: the thing a student makes feeds mainly one criterion, and sixteen of the twenty-four marks live in a record kept over months.

Counted backwards, the timeline is generous. A final deadline in the second half of MYP 5 implies a report written in the weeks before it, a product substantially finished before that, data or evidence of the making gathered throughout, success criteria agreed near the start, and a goal narrowed in the first term. Every one of those steps has months of slack if the first step happens on time. None of them do if the first step happens in the final term.

The characteristic Dubai failure has a specific shape. A student picks an ambitious goal - a short film, an app, a community event - works hard on it through the spring, and arrives at the report with nothing to evidence Planning or Reflecting because no journal exists. A reconstructed journal is visible to a marker and scores poorly. The opposite case is also instructive: a modest product with a rigorous journal and honest, specific reflection scores far better than parents expect, and students find that counter-intuitive until somebody explains the mark allocation to them.

On the boundary, clearly, because the Personal Project is where pressure concentrates. A tutor can help narrow a goal until it is achievable, help write success criteria that can actually be tested, set up a journal habit that takes ten minutes a week, and ask the questions that produce reflection rather than description. A tutor does not choose the project, make any part of the product, write or edit any part of the report, or supply material to be submitted. Crossing that line is an academic honesty breach under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units, and why they ambush good students
paragraphs: Interdisciplinary units are scheduled, assessed on their own criteria - Evaluating, Synthesising and Reflecting - and reported separately from the eight subject groups. They are also the single most reliable source of an unexpectedly low grade for a student who is doing well everywhere else, and the reason is structural rather than academic.

The task asks a student to combine two disciplines to produce something neither could produce alone. What most students produce instead is two parallel pieces of work stapled together: a science section and a history section, each competent, with a sentence in between. That is not synthesis, and the Synthesising criterion marks it as what it is. The failure is invisible to the student, who has worked hard and written a lot, and often invisible to the parent too until a separate interdisciplinary grade appears on a report nobody was expecting.

Knowing the unit is coming is most of the preparation, which is why it belongs in a section about the calendar. A student who is told in advance that the task will be marked on whether the two disciplines genuinely inform each other will plan differently from the outset. The practical exercise is short: before writing anything, state in one sentence what the second discipline lets you say that the first could not. If that sentence does not exist, the plan is two essays and needs rethinking.

The Reflecting criterion in these units has its own trap, shared with much of the MYP. It asks what the student learned about combining disciplines, not what the student did. Students write process narratives - first we researched, then we wrote - where the descriptor wants an account of what the combination made possible and what its limits were. That distinction takes one session to teach and recurs in the Personal Project, in the Arts journals and in Sciences Criterion D.

sections.heading: Service as action and the five-year record nobody keeps
paragraphs: Service as action is not graded on criteria, which is exactly why it gets ignored, and it is required, recorded and reported across all five MYP years. Schools expect documented reflection against learning outcomes. A student who has recorded nothing by MYP 5 faces a reconstruction task at the worst possible moment, competing with the Personal Project for the same weeks.

The work itself is trivial in volume. A short entry per activity naming what was done, what was learned and which outcome it addresses, written at the time, takes a few minutes. Done once a term across five years it produces a complete record with no effort worth mentioning. Left until the end, it produces either a thin record or an invented one, and an invented one is both obvious and dishonest.

Where tutoring has a legitimate and narrow role is in helping a student articulate learning rather than activity. Students write lists of what they did; the expectation is reflection on what changed in them and what the experience showed about the issue. That is a writing skill, it is the same skill the Personal Project's Reflecting criterion rewards, and it is the same skill Sciences Criterion D rewards. Teaching it once pays in three places, which is the most efficient thing available in MYP tutoring.

A practical suggestion for Bur Dubai families, because the calendar is the theme of this page: put one calendar reminder a term, in the same week as the school's reporting date, to write the service entries. It costs nothing, it removes a reconstruction crisis from MYP 5, and it is the sort of intervention that makes tutoring unnecessary rather than necessary. We would rather say that than sell hours against a problem a reminder would have prevented.

sections.heading: eAssessment, and the fork in the final MYP year
paragraphs: There is a question every MYP 5 parent should ask and most never do: does this school run IB eAssessment? The answer changes the whole shape of the final year, and it is a school-level choice rather than a programme requirement, so two schools five minutes apart in Bur Dubai can be doing different things.

Where a school opts in, the final MYP Certificate grade comes from on-screen examinations and ePortfolios marked by the IB rather than from the school's own criterion judgements. That means the final year contains externally assessed components with their own registration and submission dates, and the student needs preparation for a timed on-screen examination environment they may never have met. It is, in that respect, a rehearsal for the Diploma, which is one of its genuine advantages.

Where a school does not opt in, the MYP record remains school-assessed against the criteria throughout, and the final year looks much like the preceding ones with the Personal Project added. Neither route is better, and no family needs to choose because the school already has. What families need is to know which one applies, because the preparation, the deadlines and the timing of any tuition differ substantially between them.

This is a one-question conversation with the MYP coordinator and it should happen before the final year begins rather than during it. If the answer is eAssessment, plan for timed on-screen practice and for the portfolio deadlines. If it is school-assessed, the assessment map remains the planning document and the Personal Project timeline is the main fixed structure in the year. Either way the conversation costs nothing and prevents the most common form of MYP 5 surprise.

sections.heading: The weeks between MYP 5 and DP1: the window nobody uses
paragraphs: Here is the calendar observation that saves families the most money over five years, and it concerns a period in which nothing has gone wrong. The gap between the end of MYP 5 and the start of DP1 is the cheapest, highest-return tutoring window in the programme, and it is almost entirely unused because there is no bad report to react to.

Three gaps reliably cause trouble in the first Diploma year, and none of them appear on an MYP report. Examination stamina: MYP assessment is coursework-shaped, with tasks, investigations and projects, and the Diploma ends in timed papers. A student who has never written for ninety minutes without a break finds the first DP1 mock brutal regardless of what they know. The fix is mechanical - start at thirty minutes and build - and it does not require any content teaching at all.

Algebraic fluency: MYP Mathematics is assessed on criteria that reward investigation and real-world application, while Diploma Mathematics rewards accurate manipulation and correct calculator use under time pressure. A student with strong Criterion B investigation marks and shaky algebra has a gap that MYP reporting cannot show and DP1 exposes within a term. Students moving from standard MYP Mathematics into Higher Level Analysis and Approaches have the widest version of this gap.

Command terms: the Diploma publishes a defined list per subject - state, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss - each with a specific expected response and a specific mark allocation. MYP students are fluent in criterion descriptors, which are related but not the same vocabulary. Two sessions on command terms before DP1 begins pays back across all six subjects rather than one, which makes it the single best-value pair of hours in the handover. A block of six to ten sessions in this window typically covers all three gaps, and it ends on a fixed date.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs in Dubai, timed to the calendar
paragraphs: Because MYP help is most effective in short, well-placed blocks, the cost question is better answered per block than per month. A pre-task block is two or three sessions. Personal Project process support across MYP 5 is four to six spread thinly. The DP1 handover is six to ten in a fixed window. Added up over five years, a family that times its purchases well spends a fraction of what a standing weekly hour would cost and gets more for it.

The market rates, each attributed and read in October 2026: at the budget end Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which buys homework supervision. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270; BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work, with packages advertised around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Applying that to the MYP: a three-session pre-task block at the mid band is a small, bounded purchase with a measurable outcome - the next criterion score. The specialist band is worth it for Personal Project process coaching and for the DP1 handover, because both involve judgement about what a descriptor rewards rather than content delivery. Nothing in the market justifies a premium for homework supervision, which is what the budget band actually sells.

None of the figures above are IB Gram prices; we publish no rate card on a landing page. We hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We are not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and we publish no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor headcount, because none of those could be given a sample size, a date and a method.

sections.heading: An MYP tutor in a Bur Dubai flat against one-to-one online
paragraphs: The in-home instinct here is understandable. A tutor in the room is visible, a parent can judge whether the hour was used, and in an apartment with younger children it removes a journey. Those are fair arguments and we are not dismissing them.

The position, stated before payment: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a family in Bur Dubai, Karama or Al Mankhool is one-to-one over live video. We put that on the page because two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without disclosing where the tutor actually sits.

For MYP work the format is unusually well matched to the task, because nearly everything assessed is a document. A unit planner, a task sheet, a task-specific clarification and the student's own draft can all be open on one shared screen, annotated in the tutor's hand against each descriptor, and saved for the student to use when the next task in that subject group arrives. Paper across a table cannot do any of that, and it leaves with the tutor.

The supply argument is the decisive one in this district, though, and it is specifically a calendar argument. A pre-task block has to land in a particular fortnight, not whenever a nearby tutor happens to be free. The pool of people who understand what Design Criterion A rewards, or how a Personal Project journal evidences Reflecting, is small; the subset of that pool living within a twenty-minute drive of Al Mankhool and free in the right fortnight is smaller still. Online removes the geography from the problem and leaves only the timing, which is the thing that actually matters.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the hours the MYP week has left
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. In 2024-25 the sector was 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of pupils, Indian at 26 per cent and US at 14 per cent. The International Baccalaureate accounts for a small share of enrolment, which is the plain reason MYP specialists are thin on the ground in a district like Bur Dubai.

The timetable facts matter directly to a calendar-led plan. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which constrains how tutoring in them can be described.

Put those hours next to eight MYP subject groups, interdisciplinary units, service as action and, in MYP 5, the Personal Project, and the week is tight. A student whose criterion scores dip in a particular term may be in a crunch week visible on the assessment map rather than struggling with a subject. That is a reason to look at the calendar before buying hours, and we would rather point a family at the calendar than at a booking page.

KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places. Useful context for a family weighing school fees against tutoring spend in this district.

sections.heading: Permits, claims and the lines we hold
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit and a Bur Dubai parent can check it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and states a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published officially, no amount should be quoted to you.

A related rule is worth knowing. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct likewise bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. If someone offers you your child's own subject teacher privately, neither of them should be making that arrangement.

On IB Gram, three plain statements. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry; we do not hold one and do not describe ourselves as KHDA approved. We have no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE.

And the academic honesty line, which in the MYP concentrates on the Personal Project. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write, co-write, edit to completion or supply any part of a Personal Project, a process journal, an interdisciplinary task or any other submitted assessment. We also do not publish or redistribute IB subject guides, assessment criteria documents or school material as downloads; we reference them and cite the source. One provider ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright, which is an IB malpractice trigger for the student who submits one.

That boundary is written down before work starts, because under IB rules the consequence of crossing it falls on the student.

whyPoints.description: Each AED range here names the provider that published it and the month it was read. We publish no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor count, hold no UAE premises, and claim no approval from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education.

whyPoints.title: Sometimes the answer is a calendar reminder
whyPoints.description: Service as action needs ten minutes a term. A crunch week explains a dip better than a subject weakness does. Where a free fix exists we will name it rather than sell hours against a problem that scheduling would have prevented.

faqs.question: When in the MYP year is tutoring actually worth buying?
faqs.answer: In the fortnight before a criterion is assessed. Not every criterion is judged in every unit, so the school's assessment map tells you which letters are being marked in which term across all eight subject groups. Two or three sessions landing before the task is set are worth several times the same sessions after the mark comes home, because the student arrives already knowing what the descriptor rewards rather than learning it from a score. Ask the MYP coordinator for the map; most schools will share it.

faqs.question: What is an MYP assessment map and why should we ask for it?
faqs.answer: It is the school's plan of which units run in which term and which of the four criteria each unit assesses, across the subject groups. Schools build it to plan teaching rather than to hand to parents, which is why so few families have seen one. With it you can time paid help to land before a judgement, understand why a criterion is missing from a report - often it simply has not been assessed yet - and spot the weeks where four criterion-marked tasks fall together.

faqs.question: How early should the MYP Personal Project really start?
faqs.answer: Term one of MYP 5. The project is assessed on Planning, Applying skills and Reflecting - 24 marks - and sixteen of those rest on the process journal and the report rather than on the product. A goal narrowed early leaves months of slack; the same goal set in the final term produces a panic. Counted backwards, the report needs weeks, the product needs months, and the journal needs the whole period, because a reconstructed journal is visible to a marker and scores poorly.

faqs.question: Why did my child get a separate low grade for an interdisciplinary unit?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because the work was two parallel pieces rather than one synthesised argument. Interdisciplinary units are assessed on Evaluating, Synthesising and Reflecting, and the Synthesising criterion marks whether two disciplines genuinely inform each other. A competent science section and a competent history section with a joining sentence is the commonest and most invisible failure. The test before writing is one sentence: what does the second discipline let you say that the first could not?

faqs.question: Does our school use IB eAssessment for MYP 5?
faqs.answer: That is a question for your MYP coordinator, and it should be asked before the final year begins. Where a school opts in, the final MYP Certificate grade comes from on-screen examinations and ePortfolios marked by the IB rather than from the school's own criterion judgements, which introduces external deadlines and the need for timed on-screen practice. Where a school does not, the record stays school-assessed and the Personal Project is the main fixed structure. Two schools five minutes apart can differ.

faqs.question: What should we do in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1?
faqs.answer: Close the three gaps MYP reporting cannot show. Examination stamina, because MYP assessment is coursework-shaped and the Diploma ends in timed papers - build from thirty minutes upward. Algebraic fluency, because MYP Mathematics rewards investigation while Diploma Mathematics rewards manipulation under time pressure. And command terms, because the Diploma publishes a defined list per subject with specific expected responses. Six to ten sessions in that window is the best-value purchase in the whole programme and almost nobody makes it.

faqs.question: Why is service as action a problem by MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Because it is required and reported across all five years but not graded on criteria, so it gets ignored until it cannot be. A student who has recorded nothing faces reconstructing five years of reflection in the same weeks as the Personal Project. The task itself is tiny - a short entry per activity naming what was done, what was learned and which outcome it addresses. One calendar reminder a term, set in the same week as the school's reporting date, removes the whole problem for free.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project journal?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the help is process rather than content. A tutor can establish a journal habit that takes ten minutes a week, show what an entry needs to evidence against the Planning and Reflecting descriptors, and ask the questions that produce reflection instead of a process narrative. A tutor cannot write entries, supply material to be submitted, or edit the report to completion. We put that boundary in writing before any Personal Project work begins, because the consequence of crossing it falls on the student.

faqs.question: My child's MYP grade dropped a point this term. Should we be worried?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and the assessment map usually explains it. Different units assess different criteria, so a grade built from Criterion A and C in one period and Criterion B and D in the next is not measuring the same thing twice. A drop can mean a harder criterion was assessed rather than that the student got worse at the subject. Ask which criteria were judged in each period before reacting. If the same criterion dropped twice, that is a real signal and worth two or three sessions.

faqs.question: Do you send an MYP tutor to our flat in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Bur Dubai family is one-to-one over live video, stated before payment. For MYP work the format fits, because almost everything assessed is a document: the unit planner, the task sheet, the clarification and the student's own draft sit on one shared screen, annotated against each descriptor and saved for the next task. The stronger argument is timing - a pre-task block has to land in a particular fortnight.

faqs.question: How much should a Bur Dubai family expect to spend on MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: Less than most do, if the purchases are timed. A pre-task block is two or three sessions; Personal Project support is four to six spread across MYP 5; the DP1 handover is six to ten in a fixed window. Market rates read in October 2026 put qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, Bestimate placing specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and TutorChase at AED 270. A standing weekly hour, by Bestimate's monthly estimates, runs AED 240 to 1,200.

faqs.question: Does the MYP prepare a student for Diploma examinations?
faqs.answer: For the content and the thinking, yes. For the examination itself, less so, and that is the gap worth planning for. MYP assessment is coursework-shaped throughout - tasks, investigations, projects, with feedback cycles - while the Diploma ends in externally marked timed papers. A student arriving in DP1 from MYP 5 without IGCSE has often never written for ninety minutes under timed conditions, and the first DP1 mock reflects that rather than their understanding. Timed practice built up progressively solves it mechanically.

faqs.question: How many MYP subject groups should we buy tutoring in at once?
faqs.answer: Usually one, and sometimes none. If the same criterion letter is weak across several subject groups - Criterion B, say, which asks for a plan or a line of inquiry in Sciences, Mathematics, Individuals and societies and Design - that is one transferable skill and one tutor can move several reported grades. If the weakness is genuinely different in each, buying three standing hours against eight subject groups is not a plan. We will say which case you are in during the free trial.

faqs.question: Does my child have to study Arabic alongside the MYP in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Those hours sit in the same week as eight MYP subject groups, which is part of why MYP weeks in Dubai are tighter than families expect.

faqs.question: Is a mid-term start a problem for MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and in the MYP it is less costly than in an examined course. Criterion judgements are gathered over a reporting period and a later, stronger piece of evidence carries weight, so an early weak task is recoverable in a way an early low examination mark is not. What matters more is whether the start lands before or after the next assessment of the criterion in question. Ask for the assessment map and place the block accordingly rather than starting on the first available week.

faqs.question: Does an MYP tutor working with a Bur Dubai family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and states a two-working-day completion time. Ask any prospective tutor directly. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no official fine schedule is published.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bur-dubai.closingHeading: Ask for the map, then pick the fortnight
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-bur-dubai.closingBody: One request to the MYP coordinator - the assessment map for the year - changes what MYP tutoring is for. With it you can place two or three sessions before a criterion is judged instead of after, see the crunch weeks coming, start the Personal Project journal in term one, and use the handover weeks into DP1 that almost nobody uses. If you want help reading it, book the free trial lesson: one hour, no cost, with the tutor you would continue with, spent on a task read against its actual descriptor and a written note of where the gap sits. All lessons for Bur Dubai families are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-business-bay.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work with Middle Years Programme students across Dubai's central corridor, in maths, the sciences, language and literature and individuals and societies. Each reads the school's own criterion feedback before teaching anything.

intro.heading: The report is in letters, and that is the whole problem
paragraphs: Middle Years Programme reports arrive looking nothing like the reports a parent grew up with. Instead of a percentage and a rank there are four criterion letters per subject, each marked out of eight, and a converted grade from 1 to 7. A child can hold a 6 and a 3 in the same subject. The 3 is the thing to act on and it is frequently the thing nobody discusses, because the converted grade looks respectable and the conversation stops there.

That is what an MYP tutor is for in practice. The subject content in MYP 3 or MYP 4 is rarely the difficulty. The difficulty is that each subject group is assessed against four published criteria which reward different behaviours, and students are strong at two of them and weak at two of them in a pattern that repeats across every piece of work for years. A tutor who reads the criterion marks rather than the converted grade can name that pattern in one session. A tutor who teaches generic maths or generic science will improve the criterion the student was already good at.

This page is written as a comparison, because Business Bay parents ask a comparison question. They want to know whether living here, rather than in Downtown Dubai or DIFC or Sobha Hartland, puts their child at any disadvantage in finding help. The answer is no, and it is worth spelling out why: the MYP criteria are set internationally, the same descriptors are used in every IB school in the city, and the people who know how to read them are scattered across the world rather than concentrated in any Dubai district. What the district changes is the hour a session can start.

Business Bay in particular has no secondary campus inside it. Children here are driven or bussed out towards Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf, Al Barsha or Jumeirah and come home in the late afternoon. Lessons are delivered live online, one-to-one, over video, which removes travel from both ends of the evening. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai — home visits are a service we offer only in India — and this page makes the comparison openly rather than implying something different.

What follows is the machinery. The eight subject groups and the criteria attached to each. How a total out of 32 becomes a grade out of 7, and why a child two marks below a boundary looks identical to one five marks below it. Where MYP marks genuinely go missing, which is almost always the same two criteria. The Personal Project in MYP 5 and the exact line a tutor may not cross on it. What happens in September of DP1 or Year 10 to a student who has only ever been assessed this way. And what the Dubai market charges, with each figure attributed to whoever published it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-business-bay.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes bear on an MYP family's decisions in this corridor: the Primary Years Programme behind it, the Middle Years Programme itself, and the Diploma that most MYP 5 students move into.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, ending in the Exhibition. Students arrive in MYP 1 fluent in asking questions and presenting findings, and frequently short of the written fluency and arithmetic speed that MYP subject criteria start to reward from MYP 2 onwards. That mismatch is normal and is cheapest to address in MYP 1 and 2.
programmes.countryNote: Several central Dubai schools run the full IB continuum, so a Business Bay child may move from PYP to MYP without changing building. Families transferring in from a British or Indian primary meet the criterion system for the first time in MYP, which is where most of the early confusion in this corridor comes from.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project, and some schools enter students for the optional on-screen examinations and ePortfolios that lead to the IB MYP Certificate. Interdisciplinary units and service as action run throughout.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the programme runs alongside the emirate's mandatory subjects — Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies — which are taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Those hours are part of the week, so an MYP 4 student in Business Bay has less discretionary study time than the subject list alone suggests.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where MYP 5 students usually arrive next. Assessment changes shape entirely: externally marked papers, command terms with fixed meanings, and an internal assessment in each science. Students who have been assessed only against criteria for five years meet timed written examinations for the first time, which is the single predictable difficulty of DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Business Bay family continues in the IB. Some schools in the corridor move students from MYP 5 into International A Levels, and some transfer into a British school for IGCSE at Year 10. Each route produces a different September gap, and knowing which one is coming decides what MYP 5 support should concentrate on.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-business-bay.subjectsIntro: These are the MYP subject groups and courses Business Bay families most often ask for, with the criterion that usually causes the trouble in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria A to D: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where most marks are lost, because it asks a student to find and justify a general rule rather than complete a calculation.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A to D: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion D is routinely under-marked because students describe an impact without evaluating the science behind it.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criteria A to D: analysing, organizing, producing text, and using language. Students who write fluently often score well on D and poorly on A, because analysis means explaining the effect of a choice rather than identifying that a choice was made.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criteria A to D: knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Criterion D rewards evaluation of sources and of competing interpretations, which is a different skill from knowing the content well.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Assessed on listening, reading, speaking and writing, with the phase rather than the year group setting the standard. Parents are often surprised that a child can move year group without moving phase, and that the phase is what determines the descriptors used.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria A to D: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The most process-heavy subject in the programme, and the one where documentation rather than the finished product carries the marks.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria covering knowledge, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. The process journal is assessed, which means a strong performer with a thin journal scores below a careful one, and that is a correctable problem.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Assessed on knowledge, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on performance. Written reflection carries real weight, which surprises families who assume the subject is judged only on the field.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Three criteria — planning, applying skills, reflecting — totalling 24 marks, with a process journal and a report. The product itself is not what is marked, and students who understand that early score noticeably better than those who do not.

subjects.name: Arabic and the Dubai mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are required in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and the language of instruction set accordingly.
