sections.heading: The five-year arc: which criteria to fix in which year
paragraphs: Because the Middle Years Programme runs for five years, support has a longer arc available than in a two-year examined course, and the useful work differs by year. Treating MYP 1 the same as MYP 5 wastes both. The general shape is that the early years are for criteria literacy, the middle years are for the process criteria that transfer forward, and the final year is for the Personal Project and the transition.

In MYP 1 to 3 the highest-value work is teaching a student to read a task sheet and identify which criterion it assesses before starting. That sounds administrative and is transformative, because a student who knows the task is assessing communicating rather than knowledge will write differently. It is also the cheapest intervention available in the programme, it applies across all eight subject groups at once, and it keeps paying for five years.

In MYP 4 the criteria sharpen and the process criteria become the ones worth strengthening deliberately, because they transfer. Investigating patterns in mathematics maps onto the Diploma's Exploration. Inquiring and designing, and processing and evaluating, in sciences map onto the Diploma's scientific investigation. Organising in language and literature maps onto every extended piece of writing the student will ever be assessed on. Strengthening those is preparation for a component worth twenty per cent two years later.

In MYP 5 the Personal Project dominates and the transition conversation arrives. The honest advice for this year is to protect the Personal Project early and then shift attention to the written-paper technique that neither the MYP nor a strong report has given the student. Most MYP students have never sat a ninety-minute timed paper marked by someone who has never met them, and that is the gap that bites in the first term of whatever comes next.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units and the calendar nobody plans for
paragraphs: Interdisciplinary units draw on two or more subject groups and are assessed against their own criteria. On a report they frequently produce one of the lowest marks, and the reason is almost always that the student treated the unit as an add-on rather than as an assessed task with its own requirements. Nobody told them otherwise, and the unit sat outside the mental map they had built of their subjects.

The fix is calendar awareness rather than content work. Ask the school when interdisciplinary units run and what they are assessed against. With that information, a student can approach the unit as an assessed task, which usually raises the mark substantially without any additional teaching, because the content was never the problem. It is the clearest example in the programme of a mark lost to not knowing something administrative.

Service as action belongs in the same category. It is a requirement rather than a graded component, and it carries school-scheduled expectations and reflection points. Tutoring does not touch it and we will not pretend otherwise. The planning point is to keep its dates visible, so that a term already carrying several assessed tasks does not also acquire a service catch-up nobody scheduled.

Approaches to learning skills sit across everything and are worth one paragraph for the same reason. They are taught and referenced throughout the programme and they underpin several criteria, particularly the process ones. A student who has been taught to plan, to self-manage and to reflect explicitly performs better against criteria that reward exactly those behaviours, which is why criteria literacy work tends to raise marks in subjects nobody bought support for.

sections.heading: The handover year, and the paper nobody has sat
paragraphs: The most consequential calendar fact about the Middle Years Programme is what happens the year after it ends. Most MYP years have no external examination, so a student can leave with a strong record and no experience of a ninety-minute written paper marked by someone who has never met them, with no opportunity to resubmit. Whether the destination is the IB Diploma or a post-16 route via IGCSE, that is the gap that shows up in the first term.

The specific difficulties are predictable. Pace under timed conditions, because MYP tasks are usually completed over days rather than in a fixed hour. Writing method and reasoning for an unknown marker rather than for a teacher who already understands the student. And the absence of a second attempt, which changes how a student should approach a first assessment entirely. None of those is a content gap and none is addressed by covering more syllabus.

Two MYP components prepare a student directly, and both are cheap to strengthen in MYP 4 rather than MYP 5. Investigating patterns in mathematics maps almost exactly onto the Diploma's Exploration, worth twenty per cent of the final maths grade. Inquiring and designing, with processing and evaluating, in sciences maps onto the Diploma's scientific investigation, also twenty per cent. A student competent in those arrives at a fifth of two grades already prepared.

The practical recommendation for a Culture Village family in MYP 5 is unglamorous. In the second half of the final year, once the Personal Project is under control, buy a short block of timed written paper practice in the subjects the student will carry forward. Three or four papers sat under proper conditions, marked strictly, is enough to remove the shock, and it is considerably cheaper than the emergency support that follows a poor first Year 12 assessment.

sections.heading: Fitting MYP support into a Culture Village week
paragraphs: MYP students are younger than Diploma students and their concentration fades earlier in the evening, which makes the session slot more consequential rather than less. Culture Village helps here: the district is compact, sits on the Creek beside Al Jaddaf, and a student at a school in Al Jaddaf or across the water in Dubai Festival City is frequently home in time for a 16:30 start. For a Year 8 student that is the difference between a productive hour and a tolerated one.

The week is also fuller than families expect. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA calculating instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit and requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Those periods are in the timetable before eight subject groups are counted.

The practical consequence is that adding a fourth evening commitment to an MYP student's week produces diminishing returns quickly, and we will say so rather than selling it. One well-placed session a week, timed before a criterion reassessment, does more than three sessions spread across subjects in a week that already has no spare capacity. For younger students in particular, less and earlier beats more and later.

For students commuting from Nad Al Sheba or beyond Al Khail Road, the geographic advantage reverses and a weekend morning is the better instrument, especially for Personal Project work and longer written tasks that need an uninterrupted stretch. It also widens the choice of tutor, because the weekday window between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf Standard Time is the busiest hour in the UAE tutoring day.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and getting started
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. An inspection rating judges a school. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises and staff, which we are not.

Tutoring is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, with no fee and a stated two-working-day completion time. No fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted is unverified.

One boundary specific to the Middle Years Programme. Because the programme is internally assessed, the person marking your child's criteria is their own subject teacher, and the pressure to engage them privately can be real. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The person assessing the work should not be separately paid by one family in the class.

To start, send the subject group, the MYP year, the criterion marks out of eight if the school has shared them, and when the next assessed task in that subject falls. Add two evening windows that genuinely work from Jaddaf Waterfront. We match a subject-group specialist and run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep, with one trial per student, nothing charged beforehand and no card details required. Nobody can promise a grade and this page does not.

faqs.question: How should MYP tutoring be timed when there is no exam to work towards?
faqs.answer: To the reporting cycle rather than to a date. Each criterion in each subject is assessed more than once across a year, so there are recurring moments when a recorded mark is still live. A short block of work landing in the fortnight before a criterion is assessed again changes a mark that will count. That requires the school's assessment schedule, showing which criteria the next task covers, rather than only the report dates that most families work from.

faqs.question: Can an MYP criterion mark actually be improved after a poor report?
faqs.answer: The recorded mark cannot be changed, but the criterion is usually assessed again. Because each criterion is judged through several tasks across the year, and later evidence typically carries more weight in the year-end judgement, a weakness identified in November can still be addressed before the February and April tasks that assess the same criterion. Ask the school two things: will this criterion be assessed again this year, and how is the year-end judgement formed.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school for before buying MYP support?
faqs.answer: Three things, all free. The criterion marks out of eight for each subject, A through D, which most MYP schools record. The boundary table used to convert the thirty-two-mark total into a grade from one to seven. And the assessment schedule showing which criteria the next assessed tasks cover and when they fall. The first two name the target and the third lets you place the work where it changes a mark that counts rather than after the fact.

faqs.question: Why do interdisciplinary units produce such low marks on reports?
faqs.answer: Because students treat them as an add-on rather than as an assessed task with its own criteria, and nobody usually tells them otherwise. The unit sits outside the mental map the student has built of their subjects. The fix is administrative rather than academic: ask the school when interdisciplinary units run and what they are assessed against, and the mark usually rises substantially without additional teaching, because the content was never the problem.

faqs.question: When should Personal Project support be bought in MYP 5?
faqs.answer: At the start, when the project is introduced, not when the deadline approaches. Almost every project that goes wrong does so at the goal stage, because a goal too ambitious to finish and document produces an incomplete product and thin process evidence. The criteria reward documented process substantially, so a completed modest project outscores an unfinished ambitious one. Two hours of scope conversation at the start prevents an outcome twelve hours at the end cannot repair.

faqs.question: Does the Personal Project process journal really carry marks?
faqs.answer: It is an assessed artefact rather than a formality, and it is meant to record decisions and reflections as they happen. A student who writes in it weekly produces exactly the evidence the reflection criteria can reward. A student who assembles it in the final fortnight produces a retrospective narrative that reads as one, and the marks follow accordingly. Establishing the weekly habit in the first weeks of the project is a single conversation with a disproportionate effect.

faqs.question: Which MYP criteria are worth strengthening for the Diploma specifically?
faqs.answer: The process criteria, and two in particular. Investigating patterns in mathematics maps almost exactly onto the Diploma's Exploration, which is worth twenty per cent of the final maths grade. Inquiring and designing, with processing and evaluating, in sciences maps onto the Diploma's scientific investigation, also twenty per cent. A student competent in those arrives at a fifth of two separate grades already prepared, and strengthening them in MYP 4 costs a fraction of addressing them in Year 13.

faqs.question: What catches MYP students out in their first year after the programme?
faqs.answer: The timed written paper, because most MYP years have no external examination. The specific difficulties are pace under timed conditions, writing method and reasoning for a marker who has never met them, and the absence of a second attempt, since MYP tasks are often revisited. None of those is a content gap. Three or four papers sat under proper conditions in the second half of MYP 5 removes most of the shock, and it is far cheaper than post-hoc rescue work.

faqs.question: Is it worth buying support in several MYP subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Rarely, because the criteria repeat across subject groups as recognisable forms of the same skill. Organising in language and literature, communicating in mathematics and documenting process in design are all structured communication. A student who learns to plan and structure written work in one subject frequently gains marks in two others without an hour being bought for them. Start with the lowest criterion letter across subjects rather than the lowest grade, and reassess after one reporting point.

faqs.question: How much evening capacity does an MYP student in Dubai actually have?
faqs.answer: Less than families assume. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA calculating instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit and requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Those periods sit in the timetable before eight subject groups are counted, so a fourth evening commitment produces diminishing returns quickly.

faqs.question: What time should an MYP session start from Culture Village?
faqs.answer: As early as the commute allows, and earlier matters more for younger students than for Diploma candidates because concentration fades sooner. Culture Village is compact and sits on the Creek beside Al Jaddaf, so a student at a school in Al Jaddaf or across the water in Dubai Festival City is frequently home for a 16:30 start. Pupils travelling to Sobha Hartland sit better at 17:00 and those commuting to Nad Al Sheba at 17:15 or later.

faqs.question: Does eAssessment change how the final MYP year should be planned?
faqs.answer: Substantially, where a school offers it. On-screen eAssessment and ePortfolios leading to the MYP Certificate introduce the only genuinely external deadlines most MYP students meet, and they change the shape of a year that otherwise has none. Confirm with the school early whether your child's cohort is entered, because a plan built for an internally assessed year will be wrong if external dates exist. Where a school does not offer it, the Personal Project stages remain the fixed points.

faqs.question: Where is the line on Personal Project help that a school would accept?
faqs.answer: A tutor may discuss scope, ask questions about the plan, explain what a criterion is asking for in plain language, and give feedback on the student's own draft and process journal. A tutor may not write the report, restructure it to a standard, or supply the product. The supervisor remains a member of school staff and the work must be the student's own. Providers in this market sell completed internal assessments, and the consequence of that falls on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Which schools near Culture Village run the Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: No private school sits inside Culture Village itself. Swiss International Scientific School Dubai is next door in Al Jaddaf and runs IB programmes including the Middle Years Programme, making it the closest provision. South along Al Khail Road, North London Collegiate School Dubai and Hartland International School serve Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City, with GEMS Modern Academy in Nad Al Sheba. Schools are named as market context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: Can we pay our child's own MYP teacher for private sessions instead?
faqs.answer: You should not, and the conflict is sharper in the MYP than elsewhere because the programme is internally assessed. The person marking your child's criteria is their subject teacher. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. An independent specialist avoids the problem entirely.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-damac-hills.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Middle Years Programme subjects to students across DAMAC Hills and the Dubailand communities. Matching is by subject group and year, because a criterion-led task in Sciences is a different piece of writing from one in Individuals and Societies.

intro.heading: The rubric is the subject
paragraphs: In the Middle Years Programme the rubric is not a guide to the assessment; it is the assessment. Every subject is marked against four criteria, each out of eight, with published boundaries converting the combination into a grade from one to seven. The wording of each criterion is what is being measured, and an answer that is accurate but does not do what the strand asks for will score in the middle band regardless of how much the student knows.

That is the single most important thing for a parent in DAMAC Hills to understand before buying any support, because it determines what good support looks like. A tutor who teaches the subject well and ignores the rubric produces a better-informed student with the same criterion marks. A tutor who teaches the strand — what evidence it wants, in what form, with what reasoning attached — changes the mark on the next assessed task.

The second thing is that the criteria differ by subject group. In Mathematics the four cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences they cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In Language and Literature they cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Those are not variations on a theme; they ask for different things.

The third is that one weak strand can sit inside an acceptable grade for years. Three strong criterion marks and one weak one still produce a respectable number, so nothing in the reporting forces a conversation. The strands that go unnoticed are consistent: investigating patterns in Mathematics, processing and evaluating in Sciences, organising in Language and Literature, thinking critically in Individuals and Societies.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For this age group sessions run forty-five to sixty minutes, because concentration rather than content is the limit, and a written note goes home after each one, because a thirteen-year-old will not relay accurately what was covered.

The scheduling point matters here. Secondary students in DAMAC Hills generally travel out of the community to school and arrive home after five, which for a younger student means a shorter session later in the evening or, better, a weekend morning. Two short sessions a week beat one long one, and because lessons are online the second adds no journey for anybody.

What follows is the programme itself: what an assessed task looks like, the criteria strand by strand across the main subject groups, the command terms MYP uses, and how the Personal Project is actually marked.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-damac-hills.subjectsIntro: Each entry names the subject group's four criteria and the strand that most often goes unnoticed, because that strand is usually the block.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding; investigating patterns; communicating; applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the usual weak strand, because it asks for a generalised rule with justification rather than correct answers to set questions.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding; inquiring and designing; processing and evaluating; reflecting on the impacts of science. Processing and evaluating is where marks disappear: data handled correctly and then evaluated in two sentences lands in the middle band.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing; organising; producing text; using language. Fluent writers often score lower on organising than on producing text, because structure is marked separately from expression and is rarely taught as a skill in its own right.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding; investigating; communicating; thinking critically. Thinking critically separates the grades and requires evaluating sources and perspectives rather than describing events accurately and at length.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehending spoken text; comprehending written text; communicating; using language. Organised by phase rather than by year, so a student can sit in a phase that does not match their year group, which parents frequently misread as being behind.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing; developing ideas; creating the solution; evaluating. Documentation of the process carries as much weight as the product, which surprises students who build something good and write little about how they arrived at it.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding; developing skills; thinking creatively; responding. The process journal is assessed rather than preparatory, so consistent documentation across the unit matters as much as the final piece.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding; planning for performance; applying and performing; reflecting and improving performance. The written strands are frequently the weak ones for students who perform strongly in the practical element.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An extended independent project with a process journal and a report, assessed against published criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. The journal forms part of the assessment, which is the most common misunderstanding about this component.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed tasks crossing subject groups, with their own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. Students treat them as a double dose of two subjects rather than as a separate assessment with its own requirements.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP tutor in DAMAC Hills actually does
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in DAMAC Hills means one-to-one Middle Years Programme teaching arranged outside school for a student in the community, and IB Gram provides it live online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India, which is stated here rather than discovered during a scheduling conversation.

The work divides into two kinds and families usually want the first while needing the second. The first is criterion work: reading the four marks on a report, identifying the weak strand, and teaching what that strand rewards. It is fast, satisfying and produces a visible change on the next assessed task. The second is fluency work on the skills the programme assumes but rarely teaches directly — manipulation, structured writing, reading for argument — which shows up two years later in the Diploma.

For a student in MYP 1 to 3, the second is usually the better purchase. There is time, the content pressure is low, and the skills built there set what the final two years can be. For a student in MYP 5 with a Diploma place waiting, criterion work is more urgent, with bridging work in the summer that follows.

There is a third piece of work that costs almost nothing and almost nobody does: teaching a student to read the task sheet. Every MYP assessed task names the criteria it is marked against. Students start writing without reading that line, answer the question they imagined, and lose marks on strands they could have addressed. One session on task literacy changes marks across every subject simultaneously.

sections.heading: What an assessed task rewards
paragraphs: An MYP assessed task is not a test in the ordinary sense. It states the criteria it will be marked against, often two of the four, and the descriptors for those criteria state what evidence earns each band. A student who reads the task statement and the descriptors before beginning is working from the same document as the teacher who will mark it. A student who does not is guessing.

The descriptors are specific in a way students find surprising. They ask for things like a justified general rule, a method with controlled variables identified, a structure that supports an argument, or an evaluation of a source's reliability with reference to its origin. Each of those is a form of writing as much as a piece of knowledge, and each can be practised in isolation.

That is why a strong answer can score in the middle band. A student who writes everything they know about photosynthesis on a task marked against processing and evaluating has produced accurate work that does not supply the evidence the strand requires. The teacher is not being harsh; they are marking the task that was set.

The practical routine for a DAMAC Hills student takes five minutes per task and costs nothing. Underline the criteria the task names. Find those descriptors. Write down, in the student's own words, what evidence the top band asks for. Then plan the answer to produce that evidence. Students who adopt that routine see criterion marks move within a term without any additional teaching.

sections.heading: Mathematics and Sciences, strand by strand
paragraphs: In Mathematics the four criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The strand that most often sits two or three points below the others is investigating patterns, because it asks for a generalisation and a justification rather than for correct answers to set questions. A student who computes well and never writes a general rule will not score in the upper bands.

Communicating in Mathematics is the second commonly underestimated strand. It asks for appropriate mathematical language, notation and forms of representation, which means working set out so a reader can follow the reasoning. Students who arrive at correct answers with no visible structure lose marks that have nothing to do with the mathematics itself, and the fix is identical to the one Diploma students need later.

In Sciences the criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Processing and evaluating is the usual weak strand. It asks for data handled correctly, results interpreted against the hypothesis, and the method evaluated with specific improvements suggested. Students write two sentences of evaluation and lose most of the available marks.

Inquiring and designing is the other one worth naming, because it rewards a method in which variables are explicitly identified and controlled. A student who describes an experiment they could run, without naming the independent, dependent and controlled variables, has produced something that reads sensibly and does not supply the evidence the descriptor asks for. The table sets both subject groups out strand by strand.

sections.heading: Language and Literature, and Individuals and Societies
paragraphs: In Language and Literature the criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. The strand that catches out strong writers is organising, because structure is marked separately from expression. A student who writes beautifully in a sequence that does not build an argument scores well on using language and poorly on organising, which feels arbitrary until the descriptors are read.

Analysing is the strand most often confused with summarising. It asks for interpretation of content, context, language, structure and technique, and for connections between them. A student who identifies a metaphor without saying what it does to a reader has spotted a feature rather than analysed it, and feature-spotting is the single most common weakness in this subject group across every year of the programme.

In Individuals and Societies the criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the strand that separates grades and the one least often taught explicitly. It asks for analysis of concepts and issues, synthesis of information, and evaluation of sources and of different perspectives with reasons attached.

Investigating is the companion strand and rewards a research question that can actually be answered, a method for finding information, and a record of what was found and where. Students produce a question too broad to answer and a bibliography assembled at the end, both of which are visible in the work. Four to six sessions on either strand moves a criterion mark, and both transfer directly into Diploma coursework two years later.

sections.heading: Command terms, taken literally
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme uses command terms in the same disciplined way the Diploma does, and in both the terms are defined and the definitions are enforced in marking. Describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, justify, outline, compare and contrast each ask for something specific, and answering one with the behaviour of another costs marks regardless of accuracy.

The pattern across subject groups is consistent. 'Describe' wants an account without reasons, so adding reasons wastes time that was needed elsewhere. 'Explain' wants reasons or causes, so a correct description earns little. 'Analyse' wants the parts identified and their relationship examined. 'Evaluate' wants a judgement supported by evidence, and an answer that lists strengths and weaknesses without deciding has not completed the task. 'Justify' wants reasons for a position already taken.

Students in MYP meet these terms in every subject and are rarely taught them as a set. Learning the eight or ten that recur in their own task sheets takes two sessions and pays in Mathematics, Sciences, Language and Literature and Individuals and Societies simultaneously. It is the highest-leverage piece of cross-subject work available in the programme.

There is a second-order benefit worth mentioning. A student who understands command terms also understands the criterion descriptors better, because the descriptors are written in the same vocabulary. Teaching the terms is therefore partly teaching the rubric, which is why it belongs near the start of any MYP block rather than as an afterthought in the last session.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The Personal Project is completed in MYP 5 and assessed against published criteria covering the planning of a goal, the application of skills to achieve it, and reflection on the process and the outcome. The process journal is part of the assessment rather than preparation for it, and that single fact resolves most of the difficulty students have with the component.

It means a strong product documented thinly scores below a modest product documented well, which feels wrong to a fifteen-year-old and is exactly what the criteria say. The journal is evidence of planning, of skills applied, and of reflection as the work proceeded. A journal reconstructed in the final fortnight reads like one, because the reflections are all retrospective and none of them changed anything.

What support can usefully do is explain each criterion, question whether the stated goal can be achieved and documented in the time available, check that the journal is being kept weekly, and give feedback on what the student has written. Choosing a feasible goal is the highest-value conversation and belongs at the start, because an overambitious goal discovered halfway through cannot be rescued by effort.

What support must not do is produce any part of the project, the artefact or the report. That is an academic-honesty requirement rather than a preference, and work a student did not produce becomes a finding against the student. The table sets out the criteria with what each one rewards and the failure that costs it.

sections.heading: Session length, frequency and what it costs
paragraphs: MYP blocks are shorter than Diploma blocks and should be, because the targets are narrower and the students are younger. Forty-five to sixty minutes is the useful ceiling for most students at this stage, and twice weekly beats one long session. Because lessons are online, the second short session adds no travel for anybody, which makes the better pattern practical rather than theoretical.

The published rates in this market are these. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors once travel is counted.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with local packages advertised at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. All of those figures are provider-published and were read in October 2026; none is IB Gram's price list.

For MYP the budget band fits one specific job: homework supervision and company for a younger student who is coping but disorganised. It does not fit criterion work, because reading a rubric and teaching what a strand rewards is a specialist skill the band does not buy. Families frequently pay the low rate for the high-skill task, conclude that tutoring does not work, and are reasonable to do so given what they bought.

sections.heading: The mandatory subjects, the regulator and the permit
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and using different or additional content for the mandatory subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited. For an MYP student in DAMAC Hills the practical effect is a fuller week than the eight subject groups imply, which matters when planning how much homework time actually exists.

Private tuition is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

sections.heading: What is not claimed on this page
paragraphs: IB Gram holds no International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. It is an independent matching platform. The regulators and the programme are described here because a parent needs to know who does what, not because any of them endorses this service, and 'IB-approved tutors' is a phrase no honest provider in this market can use.

No grade, criterion mark or admission outcome is promised. What is offered instead is a target per block taken from the criterion breakdown, a written note after each session, and an honest answer when the target has not moved by the review point. For MYP that review is unusually concrete, because the next assessed task carries the same criterion and produces a comparable number.

No part of a Personal Project, an interdisciplinary unit or any other assessed task is written, completed or produced for a student. Tutors explain criteria, question feasibility, and give feedback on the student's own writing. The process journal remains the student's own record throughout, which is both an honesty requirement and the reason the journal is worth anything as evidence.

Finally, no statistic appears anywhere on this page. A percentage without a sample size, a date and a method cannot be checked by a reader and therefore proves nothing, however good it looks. Programme facts stated here come from the structure of the Middle Years Programme itself and from the KHDA and u.ae publications named, and anything that could not be verified has been left out rather than estimated.

process.title: Send the criterion breakdown
process.description: Four marks out of eight per subject contains the diagnosis already. 'Sciences: A six, B five, C two, D five' names the block immediately, where the overall grade hides exactly the information that would make a first session useful.

process.title: Bring a recent task sheet as well
process.description: The task sheet names the criteria it was marked against, and reading it alongside the student's answer shows whether the problem was knowledge or whether the answer addressed a different strand. That distinction decides whether the block is content work or rubric work.

process.title: Short diagnostic trial session
process.description: Forty-five to sixty minutes with the proposed tutor, spent on that task and the descriptors it was marked against. It ends with a written note naming the strand to target and what evidence it asks for. No card is required and nothing is committed.

process.title: Two short sessions a week
process.description: Forty-five to sixty minutes twice rather than ninety minutes once, because concentration rather than content is the limit at this age. One of the two is often best placed on a weekend morning for students travelling out of DAMAC Hills to school.

process.title: Review against the next assessed task
process.description: The target is measured on the next task carrying the same criterion, in writing. If the mark has not moved, the strand may have been misread or the task may not have assessed it, and both are fixable. Catching that at four sessions avoids a term of polishing the wrong thing.

whyPoints.title: The rubric treated as the subject
whyPoints.description: Every MYP task names the criteria it is marked against and the descriptors state what evidence earns each band. A tutor who teaches the subject and ignores the rubric produces a better-informed student with unchanged criterion marks, which is the most common disappointment in MYP tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Criterion marks read before the grade
whyPoints.description: Three strong strands and one weak one still produce a respectable grade, so a weak strand can persist for years with nothing in the reporting forcing a conversation. Starting from the four numbers is what makes an MYP block short and targeted rather than general.

whyPoints.title: Task literacy taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Students begin writing without reading the line that says which criteria the task is marked against, then answer the question they imagined. Five minutes of routine per task — underline, find descriptors, note the evidence — moves marks across every subject group with no additional teaching.

whyPoints.title: Command terms as cross-subject work
whyPoints.description: Describe, explain, analyse, evaluate and justify are defined and enforced, and students meet them in every subject group without ever being taught them as a set. Two sessions pays in Mathematics, Sciences, Language and Literature and Individuals and Societies at once.

whyPoints.title: Sessions sized for the age group
whyPoints.description: Forty-five to sixty minutes, twice a week, with a written note home because a thirteen-year-old will not relay accurately what was covered. For DAMAC Hills students travelling out to school, one of the two sessions is usually better placed on a weekend morning.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: No part of a Personal Project, interdisciplinary unit or assessed task is written, completed or produced for a student. The process journal stays the student's own record, which is both an honesty requirement and the reason it counts as evidence at all.

faqs.question: What does a strong MYP answer need that an accurate one does not?
faqs.answer: The evidence the named strand asks for. Every assessed task states the criteria it is marked against, and the descriptors specify what earns each band: a justified general rule, a method with controlled variables identified, a structure that supports an argument, an evaluation of a source's reliability. A student who writes everything they know about the topic has produced accurate work that does not supply that evidence, and will land in the middle band however sound the knowledge.

faqs.question: Can an MYP tutor come to a villa in DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. All UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For this age group the online format also makes the better pattern practical: two sessions of forty-five to sixty minutes a week rather than one long one, with no travel on either side. Published in-home rates in this market run AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted.

faqs.question: What exactly does the investigating patterns criterion want in MYP maths?
faqs.answer: A general rule, described and justified, rather than correct answers to set questions. A student who finds the pattern in a sequence, states the next three terms and stops has addressed part of the strand. The upper bands want the rule expressed generally, tested, and justified with reasoning about why it holds. That is a specific form of mathematical writing, it is rarely taught in isolation, and four to six short sessions will move the mark.

faqs.question: Why is processing and evaluating the weak strand in MYP sciences?
faqs.answer: Because it asks for three things and students usually supply one. Data handled and presented correctly, results interpreted against the hypothesis, and the method evaluated with specific improvements suggested. Most students handle the data well, interpret briefly and write two general sentences of evaluation, which loses the majority of the available marks. Naming specific weaknesses in the method and specific improvements is a teachable form of writing rather than a matter of scientific insight.

faqs.question: My child writes well but scores badly on organising. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Structure is marked separately from expression in Language and Literature, so fluent prose earns credit under using language and nothing under organising. A piece that reads beautifully but does not build towards a point will be marked accordingly, which most students find genuinely surprising. The fix is four to six sessions: plan before writing, give each paragraph one job, signpost the argument, and check at the end that the sequence serves the point being made.

faqs.question: How are command terms used in MYP tasks?
faqs.answer: The same disciplined way as in the Diploma, and they are enforced in marking. 'Describe' wants an account without reasons, so adding reasons wastes time. 'Explain' wants reasons or causes, so a description earns little. 'Analyse' wants parts identified and their relationship examined. 'Evaluate' wants a judgement supported by evidence rather than a balanced list. Learning the eight or ten that recur in a student's own task sheets takes two sessions and pays in every subject group.

faqs.question: Is the Personal Project journal really part of the mark?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the most common misunderstanding about the component. The journal is evidence of planning, of skills applied and of reflection as the work proceeded, so a strong product documented thinly scores below a modest product documented well. A journal reconstructed in the final fortnight reads like one, because every reflection is retrospective and none of them changed a decision. Keeping it weekly from the start is the whole discipline.

faqs.question: What makes a Personal Project goal a good one?
faqs.answer: That it can be both completed and documented in the time available, and that success can be judged against criteria the student sets at the start. Goals fail by being too broad to judge, by depending on resources the student cannot get, or by being achievable without applying any skill worth documenting. That judgement takes a single conversation at the beginning and cannot be made up for later, which is why the first checkpoint earns more than any session afterwards.

faqs.question: Should a student in MYP 2 have criterion tutoring?
faqs.answer: Usually not. At that stage the better purchase is fluency — algebraic manipulation, written explanation structure, reading for argument — because there is time and those skills determine what the final two years can be. Criterion work matters more in MYP 4 and 5, where a weak strand has a direct effect on the grade and on the move at sixteen. Task literacy, however, is worth teaching at any age and takes two or three sessions.

faqs.question: Why is criterion-literate MYP support hard to find in Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Because fewer schools in this belt run the programme than run the British curriculum, cohorts are small within each subject group, and reading a rubric is a separate qualification from knowing a subject. Plenty of tutors can teach science to a fourteen-year-old; rather fewer can read a Sciences criterion breakdown and teach what the processing and evaluating strand rewards. That scarcity is the same in DAMAC Hills, Mudon and the Ranches.

faqs.question: How long should a session be for a student who gets home at five?
faqs.answer: Forty-five to sixty minutes, and ideally one of two shorter sessions in the week rather than a single long one. Concentration rather than content is the limit at this age, and a ninety-minute session after a commute from Al Barsha or the Ranches produces perhaps half an hour of usable work plus fatigue that damages willingness to attend the next one. A weekend morning slot often works better than any weekday evening.

faqs.question: What does an MYP block cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: A four to six session single-strand block at the qualified or specialist band is the usual shape, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle. All figures are provider-published and were read in October 2026, and none is IB Gram's price list.

faqs.question: What are interdisciplinary units marked against, and why do students misread them?
faqs.answer: A tutor can explain the criteria, which cover disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting, and can give feedback on what the student has written. A tutor cannot write, complete or produce any part of the task. Students usually treat these units as a double dose of two subjects rather than as a separate assessment with its own requirements, and simply reading the criteria at the start resolves most of the difficulty with no teaching at all.

faqs.question: How will I know whether the criterion block has worked?
faqs.answer: By the mark on the next assessed task carrying the same criterion. MYP makes this unusually concrete: the strand has a number, the next task produces a comparable number, and the two can be put side by side in writing. If it has not moved, either the strand was misread or the task did not actually assess it, and both are fixable. Reviewing at four sessions avoids a term spent polishing something that was never the problem.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.tutorsIntro: MYP tutors matched to DAMAC Hills 2 students work from the subject-group criteria your child is marked against, which is a different skill from teaching Diploma content at a lower level.

intro.heading: Reading an MYP report, and what it is actually telling you
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme is the stage at which Dubai parents most often lose the thread. A primary report said their child was doing well. A Diploma report will carry a familiar number out of seven. In between sit five years of reports showing four letters per subject, each scored out of eight, with no overall grade and no obvious instruction about what to do. Families in DAMAC Hills 2 come to us at this point more than at any other, and the first job is usually translation rather than teaching.

Here is the key. The MYP marks every subject against four criteria, each on a 0-8 scale, and the criteria differ by subject group. In Mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The criteria are not four attempts to measure the same thing. They measure genuinely different capabilities, which is why a profile of 7, 4, 5, 3 is informative and an average of those four numbers is not.

So a report showing a strong criterion A and a weak criterion D is not telling you that your child is a middling student. It is telling you something precise: they know the content and they cannot apply it to an unfamiliar real-world context, or they can investigate but cannot communicate the result. Those are different problems with different remedies, and a tutor who teaches more content to a student with a criterion D problem will spend a term on the wrong thing.

The second thing worth knowing is that the MYP is the honest preparation for whichever Diploma route follows, and the criteria predict it. A student strong in investigating patterns is being told something about Analysis and Approaches maths. A student strong in applying mathematics in real-life contexts is being told something about Applications and Interpretation. A student weak in the sciences' processing and evaluating criterion will struggle with the Diploma individual investigation two years before anyone mentions it.

The practical side out here is the Al Qudra corridor. DAMAC Hills 2 students mostly travel to school in Motor City, Dubai Sports City or further, and a half three finish becomes a 4:30pm arrival home in afternoon traffic. MYP-age students can sustain a 5pm or 5:30pm session comfortably, which is the band most families here settle into, and a tutor who still has to drive out pushes that past six. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only.

Supply matters as well. The IB is roughly 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools, and MYP-specific tutoring is thinner still, because many tutors who advertise IB experience mean the Diploma. An MYP tutor who has not worked with the criteria will teach competently against the wrong target.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.programmesIntro: The MYP spans five years and asks for very different things at each end. These are the stages we cover for DAMAC Hills 2 families, with what each actually demands.

programmes.name: MYP Years 1 to 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The years in which criterion-based working becomes a habit or does not. Students meet tasks that ask them to investigate, communicate and reflect rather than simply answer, and the ones who treat every task as a test of recall score below what they know. Reports begin to show the four-letter profile that parents find hard to read.
programmes.countryNote: DAMAC Hills 2 sees many arrivals from other systems at this stage, and a child moving in from CBSE or an American school meets criterion-based assessment for the first time. They are frequently quick and accurate and still marked down, because the task asked for a justified generalisation and they produced an answer. That is a fixable mismatch, not a weakness.

programmes.name: MYP Years 4 and 5, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: The demand rises sharply and the stakes become real, because these are the years that decide Diploma subject and level choices. Year 11 adds the Personal Project, a substantial independent piece assessed against its own criteria, which competes with everything else for the same hours.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most of our DAMAC Hills 2 MYP work sits. The useful intervention is criterion-specific rather than general: identify which one or two criteria are consistently low across subjects, because the same underlying skill usually drives both, and work there rather than adding content hours.

programmes.name: The MYP Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent project of the student's choosing, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and communicating the process. Marks are lost on process documentation far more often than on the product itself — students build something impressive and record almost nothing about how they did it.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project is also the first serious rehearsal for the Diploma's Extended Essay and Internal Assessments, and students who learn to document a process here find the Diploma coursework dramatically less alarming. A tutor coaches the process and the reflection; the project remains entirely the student's own.

programmes.name: The step into the Diploma
programmes.description: The largest curriculum step in the IB continuum. Criterion-based internal assessment gives way to external examination plus Internal Assessments, content depth increases sharply, and Higher Level subjects demand sustained independent work. Students comfortable in MYP 5 can be struggling by November of Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: Criterion profiles are the best available predictor of this step, and nobody uses them. A student with a weak sciences processing and evaluating criterion will find the Diploma individual investigation hard; a student with weak mathematics communication will lose marks in the Exploration. Both are addressable in Year 11, cheaply, before the Diploma starts.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.subjectsIntro: These are the MYP subject groups DAMAC Hills 2 families most often ask about, with the criteria that apply and where marks are genuinely lost in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B rewards generalising from a pattern and justifying it, which no traditional maths lesson drills, and criterion C marks the quality of mathematical communication rather than the answer.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B asks for an investigation designed with controlled variables; criterion C asks for data processed and the method evaluated. These are the direct ancestors of Diploma practical work.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Students lose marks by summarising a text rather than analysing how it produces meaning, exactly as they later will in Diploma Paper 1. Organisation is marked explicitly, which rewards planning before writing.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed by phase rather than by year group. A student can be in a different phase from their year peers, which confuses parents and is entirely normal. Progress is measurable because the skills are discrete.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. The critical-thinking criterion is where most marks go missing: students describe sources rather than evaluating their reliability and usefulness, which is a teachable technique rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating. Documentation carries the marks, and students routinely produce a good outcome with almost no record of the design cycle, which caps the score regardless of the product's quality.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. The process journal is where marks sit, and students who treat it as an afterthought lose credit their practical work had already earned.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Written and reflective components surprise families who expect a purely practical subject, and they are where the marks are often lost.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and communicating. Process documentation decides the score far more than the product does, which is why the single most useful coaching intervention is establishing a documentation habit in the first fortnight.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Thinking, research, communication, social and self-management skills, assessed implicitly through the subject criteria. Weak self-management shows up as low scores across several subjects at once, which is the pattern worth spotting on a report before any subject tutoring is bought.

sections.heading: What the four criteria actually measure, by subject group
paragraphs: No competitor page publishes this, and it is the single most useful thing an MYP parent can have in front of them when reading a report. The criteria are not generic. They are specified per subject group, and knowing which is which turns an opaque profile into a to-do list.

In Mathematics the four are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In Individuals and Societies they cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. In Language and Literature they cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language.

Each is marked 0-8, and the published descriptors make it clear what moves a score. A criterion A score reflects whether the content is known and can be used. A low score on an investigation or inquiry criterion reflects whether the student can design or generalise rather than whether they know the material. A low communication criterion reflects presentation of reasoning rather than the reasoning itself. A low evaluation or critical-thinking criterion reflects whether the student can judge rather than describe.

The table below sets out the criteria across subject groups with the diagnosis each low score implies. Read your child's report against it and the next step usually becomes obvious — and frequently it is not a subject tutor at all, but work on one transferable skill that is dragging three subjects down together.

sections.heading: Why averaging the four numbers hides the answer
paragraphs: This is the mistake almost every family makes with an MYP report, and it is entirely understandable, because every other reporting system a parent has met produces a single figure. Faced with 7, 4, 5 and 3, the instinct is to conclude that the child is around a 5 and could do better. That conclusion discards the only information the report contained.

A profile of 7, 4, 5, 3 and a profile of 5, 5, 5, 4 average similarly and mean completely different things. The first describes a student who knows the material well and cannot yet investigate, communicate or transfer it — a technique problem with specific, teachable remedies. The second describes a student with a uniform, modest grasp of everything, which is a content problem and needs content teaching. Buying the same tutoring for both is how a term gets wasted.

The pattern worth looking for is a criterion that is low across several subjects at once. A student scoring poorly on communication in Mathematics, on organising in Language and Literature, and on documentation in Design is not weak in three subjects. They have one self-management and structuring problem appearing in three places, and fixing it once lifts all three. We see this constantly, and it is almost never what a family comes to us asking for.

The opposite pattern also matters: a strong criterion that nobody has noticed. A student with consistently high investigating-patterns scores in Mathematics is showing an aptitude that points towards Analysis and Approaches and, eventually, towards quantitative degrees. Reports carry that signal for five years and almost nobody reads it, which is a shame given what the Year 11 subject choice decides.

sections.heading: The Personal Project is scored on process, not product
paragraphs: Year 11 adds an independent project of the student's choosing, assessed against its own criteria, and the way it is marked catches families out every single year. Students build, make or organise something genuinely impressive and receive a moderate score, and nobody can explain why.

The explanation is that the criteria reward planning, applying skills, reflecting and communicating the process — not the quality of the object produced. A student who designs a complex outcome and documents almost nothing about how decisions were made, what went wrong, what was learned and how the goal evolved is being assessed on the thin part of their work. Meanwhile a student with a modest project and a thorough, honest process journal scores well.

That makes the single most valuable intervention a documentation habit established in the first fortnight, before there is much to document. Not a retrospective write-up assembled in the final month, which reads as reconstruction because it is. Students who keep a short, dated entry after each working session have the raw material for genuine reflection; students who do not are writing fiction about their own project.

A tutor's role here is coaching and strictly coaching. Helping scope a project achievable alongside everything else a Year 11 is carrying. Explaining what each criterion rewards. Establishing the documentation habit. Giving feedback on the student's own journal and report against the criteria. What a tutor may not do is produce, write or finish any part of the project — the student signs for their own work, and this project is also their rehearsal for the Diploma coursework where the same rule applies with higher stakes.

sections.heading: The step from MYP 5 into the Diploma
paragraphs: This is the largest curriculum step in the IB continuum and the one families are least prepared for, because MYP 5 reports do not look like a warning. Criterion-based internal assessment gives way to external examination plus Internal Assessments. Content depth rises sharply. Higher Level subjects expect sustained independent work. Students who were comfortable in MYP 5 can be genuinely struggling by November of Year 12.

What makes this frustrating is that the MYP report predicted it and nobody read it that way. The sciences processing and evaluating criterion is a direct forerunner of the Diploma individual investigation, which carries 20% of a science grade. The mathematics communicating criterion forecasts how a student will fare in the Exploration. The Individuals and Societies critical-thinking criterion forecasts the Extended Essay. A student with low scores in those specific places is being told, two years early, where the Diploma will hurt.

The second part of the step is the subject and level choice at the end of Year 11, which the criterion profile also informs. Strong investigating patterns in Mathematics points towards Analysis and Approaches; strong applying-in-context scores point towards Applications and Interpretation. Strong criterion A with weak inquiry in Sciences suggests Standard Level will be more comfortable than Higher. None of that is deterministic, and all of it is better than choosing on which subject feels nicer in Year 11.

The practical recommendation is a short block in the second half of Year 11 or over the summer, targeted at the one or two criteria that forecast trouble. It costs a fraction of a Year 12 rescue and it arrives before two years of content has been built on top of the gap.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: This is absent from almost every competitor page and it is a real part of an MYP student's week in Dubai. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The structure is specific. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with Arabic the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

There are two further details worth knowing as a parent. KHDA requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete, checkable credential point. And mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

One constraint applies directly to tutoring in these subjects: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That is a genuine limit on how any provider may describe Arabic, Islamic or Social Studies support, and it is why we describe this work as helping a student with the material their school teaches rather than as an alternative curriculum.

sections.heading: Fitting MYP sessions into a DAMAC Hills 2 week
paragraphs: MYP-age students have a narrower usable window than Diploma students, and getting that wrong wastes the money regardless of how good the tutor is. A fifteen-year-old can work at eight in the evening. A twelve-year-old cannot, and a Year 8 student who has spent fifty minutes in a car after a full school day is not going to produce their best thinking at half six.

The arithmetic out here: a half three finish in Motor City or Dubai Sports City means a 4:30pm arrival home in afternoon traffic. Because nobody is driving to you, a session can begin at 5pm after a break and some food, which for MYP students is the sweet spot — late enough to have decompressed, early enough to still concentrate. MYP 4 and 5 students can push to 6pm comfortably. Below MYP 3, earlier is better and we will say so.

Weekend mornings are the alternative and for this age group they are often better than any weekday slot. Two hours on a Friday or Saturday morning during a Personal Project term, or during a unit with a criterion-assessed task due, is more productive than scattered tired half-hours. It is also the honest answer for a household running school runs to two or three different schools.

Ramadan and the school calendar get planned rather than discovered: shortened days, evenings reorganised around Iftar, and a shift to late-morning, early-afternoon or post-Iftar slots, or a deliberate pause with a heavier block afterwards. Prayer times are built in from the start. The pattern we work to avoid is cancel, reschedule, cancel, which with younger students ends an arrangement faster than anyone admits.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs, and the mismatch to avoid
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates, read from provider pages in October 2026. Budget online tutoring advertises from AED 33-65 an hour, with Tutopiya at AED 33-52 and EdFlik at AED 45-65. Qualified online subject tutors run AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate putting the band at AED 200-450 plus. In-home visits are AED 180-500 including travel. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end.

MYP sits in an unusual place on that ladder, and it is worth understanding before you buy. The budget band is more viable here than it is for the Diploma, because a capable graduate can genuinely help an MYP 2 student with content and confidence. What the budget band cannot do is work to the criteria, and if the report shows a criterion problem rather than a content problem, that limitation is the whole issue.

The specific mismatch to avoid is the opposite one: paying Diploma specialist rates for a tutor who has never taught the MYP. Many tutors advertising IB experience mean the Diploma, and a Diploma specialist handed an MYP 3 student will teach excellent content against the wrong target — more depth, when the report was asking for justified generalisation or documented process. That is an expensive misfit and it looks entirely satisfactory for a term.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for one weekly hour at the budget band, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist work. Advertised packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. All figures belong to the providers named; none is an IB Gram price. We quote after the diagnostic, because the honest number depends on the year, the criterion and whether the Personal Project is in play.

sections.heading: What we will not claim about MYP progress
paragraphs: No guarantee of a criterion score, a grade or an improvement. Criterion scores move when a student changes how they approach a task, which takes practice and happens on the student's timeline rather than ours, and an offer that ignores that is a sales device.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which means none published. No average criterion scores achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction figure, no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish such numbers routinely, sometimes in two conflicting versions on the same page, and almost never state how any of them was produced.

No regulator or awarding-body claim. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE or IB approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, has no office or centre anywhere in the UAE, and does not claim KHDA teaching approval of any kind — which is a real credential for Arabic and Islamic Education teachers in schools, and not something a tutoring platform holds. We also host no IB material as downloads; subject guides and criteria belong to the IB and we reference them.

And no promise that a tutor will visit a DAMAC Hills 2 address, because we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE at any price. What we will do is read the report with you, say which criterion is actually driving the problem, and sometimes tell you that no tutoring is needed — that the profile describes a student who is doing fine and whose parents have been reading an unfamiliar scale as a bad result.
