faqs.question: What do the MYP criteria A to D actually mean?
faqs.answer: Four different capabilities, specified per subject group and each marked 0-8. In Mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In Individuals and Societies they cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. They are not four attempts at the same measurement, which is why the profile matters and the average does not.

faqs.question: Why does my child's MYP report have no overall grade?
faqs.answer: Because the programme deliberately reports capability by capability rather than as a single figure. Each subject carries four criterion scores out of eight, and the point is that a 7 in one and a 3 in another is an instruction about what to work on rather than a middling overall result. The absence of a single grade is disorienting if you have come from a percentage-based system, but the information content is higher: a profile tells a tutor where to start, which a single number never does.

faqs.question: Should I average my child's four criterion scores?
faqs.answer: No, and it is the commonest mistake MYP parents make. A profile of 7, 4, 5, 3 and one of 5, 5, 5, 4 average similarly and mean entirely different things: the first is a student who knows the material and cannot yet investigate, communicate or transfer it, which is a technique problem with teachable remedies; the second is a uniform modest grasp of everything, which needs content teaching. Buying the same tutoring for both wastes a term. Bring the actual scores, not an average.

faqs.question: What does a low criterion D mean in MYP maths?
faqs.answer: In Mathematics, criterion D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A low score there alongside a strong criterion A means the content is known and the student cannot transfer it to an unfamiliar practical situation — they can do the technique when told which technique it is, and not when the question is dressed as a real scenario. That is pattern-recognition and modelling practice rather than more content, and it also says something useful about the eventual Analysis and Approaches versus Applications and Interpretation choice.

faqs.question: My child's scores are low in one criterion across three subjects. What now?
faqs.answer: That is one problem in three places rather than three subject weaknesses, and it is the most efficient thing to fix. Communication low in Mathematics, organising low in Language and Literature and documentation low in Design is usually a single structuring and self-management issue surfacing wherever it is assessed. Working the underlying skill once lifts all three subjects, which is cheaper and faster than three subject tutors. This is the first thing we look for on a report, and it is almost never what a family comes asking for.

faqs.question: Why did an impressive Personal Project get a moderate score?
faqs.answer: Against criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and communicating the process — not on the quality of the object produced. Every year students build something genuinely impressive, document almost nothing about how decisions were made or what went wrong, and receive a moderate score nobody can explain. A modest project with a thorough, dated process journal outscores it. The most valuable intervention is establishing the documentation habit in the first fortnight rather than reconstructing it in the final month, which always reads as reconstruction.

faqs.question: Where does Personal Project coaching stop being allowed?
faqs.answer: With the process, substantially. A tutor can help scope a project that is achievable alongside everything else a Year 11 carries, explain what each criterion rewards, establish the documentation habit early, and give feedback on the student's own journal and report against the criteria. A tutor cannot produce, write or finish any part of the project. The student signs for their own work, and this project is also their rehearsal for Diploma coursework where the same rule applies with considerably higher stakes.

faqs.question: Why is Year 12 so much harder than MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Because it is the largest step in the continuum. Criterion-based internal assessment gives way to external examination plus Internal Assessments, content depth rises sharply, and Higher Level subjects expect sustained independent work. Students comfortable in MYP 5 can be struggling by November of Year 12. What is frustrating is that the MYP report predicted it: a weak sciences processing and evaluating criterion forecasts difficulty with the Diploma individual investigation, and weak mathematics communication forecasts the Exploration.

faqs.question: Do MYP criterion scores predict the right Diploma subject choices?
faqs.answer: They are the best available signal and almost nobody uses them. Consistently strong investigating patterns in Mathematics points towards Analysis and Approaches and, eventually, quantitative degrees. Strong applying-in-context scores point towards Applications and Interpretation. Strong criterion A with weak inquiry in Sciences suggests Standard Level will be more comfortable than Higher. None of it is deterministic and all of it beats choosing on which subject feels nicer in Year 11, which is how the decision is usually made.

faqs.question: Is an MYP tutor different from an IB Diploma tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the difference costs money when it is ignored. Many tutors advertising IB experience mean the Diploma, and a Diploma specialist handed an MYP 3 student will teach excellent content against the wrong target — more depth, when the report was asking for justified generalisation or documented process. It looks entirely satisfactory for a term. Ask directly whether a tutor has worked with the MYP criteria, by name, for the subject group in question, and treat a vague answer as a no.

faqs.question: What time should an MYP session be for a DAMAC Hills 2 family?
faqs.answer: Around 5pm for most MYP students: late enough to have decompressed after the run from Motor City or Dubai Sports City and eaten something, early enough to still concentrate. MYP 4 and 5 students can push to 6pm comfortably. Below MYP 3, earlier is genuinely better and we will say so rather than take a later booking. Weekend mornings often work better than any weekday slot for this age group, and for households running school runs to two or three schools they are frequently the only honest answer.

faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026: budget online from AED 33-65 an hour (Tutopiya, EdFlik), qualified online subject tutors AED 150-300 with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, IB specialists AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270, and in-home visits AED 180-500 including travel. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid and AED 1,000-2,000 plus for specialist work. The budget band is more viable at MYP than at Diploma for content help, but it cannot work to the criteria.

faqs.question: Do DAMAC Hills 2 MYP pupils still sit Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These subjects sit alongside the MYP, not inside it.

faqs.question: Will an MYP tutor come to our house in DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram delivers MYP tuition to DAMAC Hills 2 one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. We acknowledge that physical presence matters more at MYP age than at Diploma age, and for a younger or less self-managing child an in-home tutor genuinely has an advantage. Other Dubai providers offer that at published rates of AED 180-500 an hour including travel. The free trial lesson is how you test whether the format works for your child.

faqs.question: My child moved from another system and the MYP marking seems unfair. Is it?
faqs.answer: Usually it is unfamiliar rather than unfair, and the mismatch is specific. Students arriving from a drilled, answer-focused system are frequently quick and accurate and still marked down, because the task asked for a justified generalisation, a designed investigation or a documented process and they produced an answer. The content knowledge is often ahead of their classmates'. What is missing is the shape of response the criteria reward, which is teachable in weeks rather than years once somebody names it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.closingHeading: Send the report and we will read it with you
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.closingBody: The useful first step with an IB MYP tutor in DAMAC Hills 2 is not booking lessons. It is sending us the actual criterion scores, subject by subject, and letting a tutor who knows the MYP tell you what the profile is asking for — a content gap, an investigation-design gap, a communication gap, or one self-management problem showing up in three subjects at once. Sometimes the answer is a short block on one criterion, sometimes a weekly subject slot, and occasionally that the report is fine. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no UAE home visits.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-deira.tutorsIntro: These are tutors who have taught inside criterion-referenced assessment rather than percentage marking. For a Deira MYP student that matters more than subject breadth: the fix is usually a specific criterion descriptor the student has never read.

intro.heading: Your child is not being marked out of 100, and that changes everything
paragraphs: The single most common mistake a Deira parent makes with the Middle Years Programme is reading an MYP report as though it were a percentage. It is not. In every one of the eight MYP subject groups, a student is assessed against four criteria labelled A, B, C and D, and each criterion is scored on a band from 0 to 8. Those four scores are added to a maximum of 32, and the school then converts that total into a grade from 1 to 7 using published grade boundaries. A child can be strong on three criteria and weak on one and still come home with a 4. The report will not tell you which letter went wrong unless you ask, and most parents do not know there is a letter to ask about.

This is the whole case for a specialist IB MYP tutor in Deira rather than a general secondary tutor. A general tutor hears "my son is getting 5s in Sciences" and starts re-teaching cells and circuits. An MYP tutor asks for the four criterion scores, sees Criterion B at 3 and Criterion A at 7, and understands immediately that the problem is not knowledge of science at all. Criterion A is Knowing and understanding. Criterion B is Inquiring and designing. The student knows the content perfectly well and cannot write a method with a controlled variable in it. Re-teaching the content would have been eight wasted hours.

Deira adds a second layer that most of Dubai does not. The district's households are genuinely multilingual, and MYP Language acquisition is placed in one of six phases rather than by year group. A Grade 8 student in Deira might sit Arabic in Phase 2 and French in Phase 4, or arrive from a school in Kochi or Manila and be placed in a phase that does not match what they can actually do. Phase placement controls the command terms on the task, the length of the text they are expected to handle and the ceiling on what Criterion C and D can award. Getting the phase conversation right with the school is often worth more than a term of tuition.

We are an online tutoring platform, and for families in the UAE every lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we provide only in India. For MYP work this is not a compromise. A criterion-marked task is a document on a screen, and the useful hour is one where a tutor and a student look at the task-specific clarification side by side, annotate the student's own draft against each descriptor, and rewrite one paragraph together. That works better shared on a screen than read upside-down across a Karama dining table.

What follows is the detail a Deira parent actually needs: the four criteria for all eight subject groups in one table, how 32 raw marks become a grade, what the task-specific clarification document is and why it is the most under-used page in the programme, how the Personal Project is marked, what the market charges for MYP support in dirhams, and where the honesty line sits on a project a student must own themselves. There is no sign-up required to read any of it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-deira.programmesIntro: Deira families usually arrive at MYP tutoring from one of three directions: a child already in MYP 1-3 with uneven criterion scores, an MYP 5 student facing the Personal Project, or a family deciding whether MYP 5 or IGCSE is the better route into a Diploma.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups: Language and literature, Language acquisition, Individuals and societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and health education, and Design. Every group is assessed against four criteria scored 0-8. There is no externally set syllabus content list in the way IGCSE has one; the school builds units against the MYP framework, which is precisely why tutoring has to start from the unit planner and the task, not from a textbook.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running MYP are inspected by KHDA on the same six-band scale as every other private school in the emirate. A handful of Deira-adjacent schools run MYP as the middle-school phase before the Diploma; others run a British middle school and switch to IGCSE. Ask which your child's school does before assuming either.

programmes.name: MYP Year 5 and the Personal Project
programmes.description: The final MYP year carries the Personal Project, which is assessed on three criteria - Planning, Applying skills, and Reflecting - each scored 0-8 for a total of 24. The project is supervised, not taught. Students keep a process journal, and the journal is the evidence base for Criterion A and Criterion C. Most lost marks in the Personal Project are journal marks, not product marks, and that is fixable in a handful of sessions if it is caught early enough.
programmes.countryNote: In Deira the Personal Project season collides with the heaviest part of the Dubai social calendar and, in some years, with Ramadan. Families who schedule project supervision sessions for the first half of the MYP 5 year rather than the second consistently have a calmer spring.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma that MYP 5 feeds into: six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The jump from criterion-referenced MYP marking to Diploma mark schemes with command terms and fixed weightings is the gap most MYP 5 students feel in their first DP1 term, especially in Mathematics and the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools accept an MYP 5 student directly into DP1 without IGCSE. That route is legitimate, but it means the student has never sat a two-hour externally marked paper under exam conditions, and the first set of DP1 mocks is often a shock worth preparing for deliberately.

programmes.name: IGCSE as the alternative route
programmes.description: The British route many Deira schools take instead of MYP 4 and 5: externally examined subjects with published syllabus codes, graded 9-1 or A*-G depending on board. Content is specified; marking is on mark schemes rather than criteria. A student moving from MYP 3 into IGCSE Year 10 gains clarity and loses the inquiry-led assessment they are used to, and the first term usually needs explicit work on exam technique.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count. That rule is worth knowing before a subject is dropped in Year 10.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-deira.subjectsIntro: MYP tutoring is organised by subject group rather than by named subject, because the criteria belong to the group. Below is what each group's four criteria actually reward, and the criterion a Deira student most often loses marks on.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Inquiring and designing, C Processing and evaluating, D Reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B is the usual weak point: students write a method without naming the independent, dependent and controlled variables, and the descriptor requires all three. Criterion D asks for the implications of the science, which is a different kind of writing altogether.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating patterns, C Communicating, D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where strong calculators collapse: it wants a pattern described, a general rule stated and the rule justified, and a correct answer without a general rule scores low. Criterion C penalises missing working and unlabelled diagrams.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criteria A Analysing, B Organizing, C Producing text, D Using language. Criterion A is the hardest to fake: it asks for analysis of how the writer's choices create effect, not for what the text is about. Plot summary scores in the lowest band however fluent the writing. Criterion D covers register, grammar and vocabulary range.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria A Listening, B Reading, C Speaking, D Writing - four separate skills, each 0-8. Phase placement sets the difficulty of the text and the task. A Deira student placed too high loses marks on B and D for reasons that have nothing to do with effort. Arabic as an additional language is the most common case in this district.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating, C Communicating, D Thinking critically. Criterion D is the grade-mover: it wants sources evaluated for origin, purpose, value and limitation, and interpretations weighed against each other. Most students describe sources instead of evaluating them, which caps the criterion in the middle bands.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria A Inquiring and analysing, B Developing ideas, C Creating the solution, D Evaluating. This is the group parents most often dismiss and the one that most often drags a grade. The design cycle has to be documented: a research plan, a design brief, specifications written as testable criteria, and a test of the solution against those exact specifications.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria A Investigating, B Developing, C Creating or performing, D Evaluating. The process journal carries A, B and D, which means three of the four criteria are won or lost in a document most students treat as an afterthought. A technically accomplished final piece with a thin journal scores far lower than parents expect.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Planning for performance, C Applying and performing, D Reflecting and improving performance. Criteria A, B and D are written work: anatomy and physiology knowledge, a training plan with measurable goals, and reflection against those goals. A fit student can score poorly here, and often does.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed on its own criteria - Evaluating, Synthesising and Reflecting - and reported separately from the eight subject groups. Students are asked to combine two disciplines to produce something neither could produce alone. The common failure is writing two parallel essays rather than one synthesised argument, which is a structural fix rather than a content one.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Criteria A Planning, B Applying skills, C Reflecting - three criteria, 24 marks. The process journal is the evidence for A and C. The product is only one part of B. Students who build something impressive and journal nothing lose two-thirds of the available marks, and that is the single most predictable grade loss in the whole programme.

subjects.name: Service as action
subjects.description: Not graded on criteria, but required, recorded and reported. Schools expect documented reflection against learning outcomes. Tutoring here is limited to helping a student articulate what they actually learned rather than listing what they did, which is a short piece of work with a real effect on a report comment.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Five ATL skill categories - communication, social, self-management, research and thinking - taught through subject units rather than separately. Self-management and research are the two that show up as criterion losses elsewhere: a student who cannot cite a source loses Individuals and societies Criterion D marks for a reason nobody has told them about.

sections.heading: All eight MYP subject groups and their four criteria, in one place
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group has exactly four assessment criteria, labelled A to D, and every criterion is marked 0 to 8. What changes between groups is what those letters mean, and no school hands parents a single sheet listing all thirty-two of them. That omission is why so much MYP tutoring in Dubai is aimed at the wrong thing. If you know only one fact from this page, make it this: ask your child's teacher which letter the marks were lost on, then look it up in the table below.

Read down the Criterion B column and a pattern appears. In Sciences it is Inquiring and designing. In Mathematics it is Investigating patterns. In Individuals and societies it is Investigating. In Design it is Developing ideas. Across half the programme, Criterion B is the criterion that asks a student to produce a plan or a line of inquiry rather than an answer. That is a single transferable skill, and a student weak on Criterion B in one group is very often weak on it in three. One tutor working on that skill can move several reported grades at once, which is the most efficient thing MYP tuition ever does.

Criterion D is the other recurring theme, and it is almost always the reflective or evaluative one: Reflecting on the impacts of science, Applying mathematics in real-life contexts, Thinking critically, Evaluating. Students who are confident and quick tend to score well on A and C and badly on D, because D rewards slowing down and weighing something. Students who are thoughtful but disorganised show the opposite shape. Either pattern is visible the moment you have the four numbers, and invisible if all you have is a grade from 1 to 7.

A practical note for Deira households with more than one child in MYP: the criteria are the same across year groups, so the vocabulary you learn for a Grade 7 student still applies to a Grade 10 one. The descriptors get harder, the letters do not change. That makes this table worth keeping.

sections.heading: How 32 raw marks become a grade from 1 to 7
paragraphs: Four criteria at 8 marks each gives a maximum of 32. The school then applies MYP grade boundaries to convert that total into a reported grade of 1 to 7. The conversion is not linear and it is not a percentage, which is why parents who do the arithmetic themselves get confused. A total in the low twenties out of 32 is a solid grade 5 or 6 in most conversions, not the 70 per cent that a percentage mindset would read as mediocre.

The second thing to understand is that a criterion is not marked once and averaged. Over a unit or a reporting period the teacher gathers several judgements on each criterion and applies a best-fit, most-recent-evidence approach rather than a mean. That has a direct consequence for tutoring: an early weak task is recoverable in a way an early low exam mark is not. If Criterion C was a 3 in September and a 6 in November, the November judgement is what counts. Starting tuition in the middle of a reporting period is therefore less wasteful in MYP than it would be in an examined course.

Third, not every criterion is assessed in every unit. A unit might assess Sciences A and C only, with B and D coming in the next unit. So a criterion that looks absent from a report is often just not yet assessed that period. Ask for the assessment map for the year if the school publishes one; it tells you when each letter is coming and lets you time a block of tuition to land before the task rather than after it.

For MYP 5 students whose school uses IB eAssessment, the final MYP Certificate grade comes from on-screen examinations and ePortfolios marked by the IB rather than from the school's own criterion judgements. Not every school opts in. The route your school uses changes the whole plan for the final year, and it is a one-question conversation with the MYP coordinator.

sections.heading: The task-specific clarification: the page that tells you the answer
paragraphs: For every assessed MYP task, a teacher is expected to produce a task-specific clarification: the generic criterion descriptors rewritten in the language of that particular task. Where the generic Sciences Criterion B descriptor says the student "designs a logical, complete and safe method", the clarification for a specific investigation will say what a complete method looks like for that investigation. It is, in effect, the mark scheme written in advance and handed to the student.

Most students do not read it. A substantial share of the MYP tutoring hours bought in Dubai are spent explaining something the clarification already said. When a Deira family starts with us, the first request is always the same: send the task sheet and the clarification, not the textbook. Fifteen minutes reading those two documents with a student usually locates the problem precisely, and sometimes removes the need for most of the block that was about to be booked.

There is a useful exercise here that costs nothing. Before the student writes anything, have them highlight every verb in the clarification for the band they are aiming at - describe, explain, justify, evaluate, outline - and then write a one-line plan that uses each of those verbs once. The gap between what the student planned to write and what the clarification asked for is the grade, nearly every time. For a student who is strong on content and middling on marks, this single habit tends to move two criteria at once.

If a task comes home without a clarification, that is a fair thing to ask about. It is a normal part of MYP assessment practice, not an unusual request, and asking for it signals to the school that the household is reading the criteria rather than the grade.

sections.heading: Language acquisition phases, and the Deira household with three languages in it
paragraphs: MYP Language acquisition does not run by year group. It runs in six phases, and a student is placed in the phase that matches their current proficiency in that language regardless of age. Phases 1 and 2 are emergent, 3 and 4 are capable, 5 and 6 are proficient. A Grade 9 student can legitimately be in Phase 2 Arabic and Phase 5 French at the same time. The four criteria stay the same - Listening, Reading, Speaking, Writing - but the texts, the task length and the expected register all scale with the phase.

This matters more in Deira than in most Dubai districts because the households here are genuinely multilingual, and because a child's home language is frequently not the language of instruction nor the additional language they are placed in. Three recurring situations: a student with strong conversational Arabic from the neighbourhood placed in a low phase and bored; a student with no Arabic at all placed by year group rather than by proficiency and drowning; and a student who moved mid-year from a school using a different phase scale and whose placement was never re-examined.

Placement is a school decision and we do not make it. What a tutor can usefully do is diagnose honestly. Give a student a Phase 3 reading task and a Phase 5 reading task in the same hour and the right phase becomes obvious very quickly. That evidence, written down, is a far better basis for a conversation with the MYP coordinator than a parent's impression, and the conversation is often worth more than the tuition that follows it.

There is also a KHDA layer sitting on top. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies - combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. For an MYP family, that means Arabic may appear twice in the week in two different forms, and it is worth being clear which one a report comment refers to.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and why the journal is two-thirds of the mark
paragraphs: The MYP Personal Project is assessed on three criteria - A Planning, B Applying skills, C Reflecting - each marked 0 to 8 for a total of 24. Read that again, because it is the fact that changes behaviour: only one of those three criteria is about the thing the student makes. Planning and Reflecting together are 16 of the 24 marks, and both are evidenced primarily through the process journal and the report.

The predictable failure is a student who spends four months building something genuinely impressive - a short film, an app, a community event - and keeps no usable record of how they did it. The product earns well on Criterion B and the other sixteen marks have almost nothing to point at. The reverse also happens: a modest product with a rigorous journal and honest reflection scores far better than parents expect, and students find that counter-intuitive until it is explained.

What a tutor can legitimately do here is narrow. We help a student sharpen a goal so it is specific enough to be achievable, write success criteria that can actually be tested rather than admired, set up a journal habit that takes ten minutes a week, and ask the questions that produce reflection rather than description. We do not choose the project, make any part of the product, write any part of the report, or edit a draft into a finished piece. The report must be the student's own work, and under IB academic honesty rules anything else puts the student at risk, not us.

Timing is the other lever. A Personal Project supported in the first term of MYP 5 costs a handful of sessions and runs calmly. The same project supported three weeks before the deadline costs more, achieves less, and pushes a tutor towards a line we will not cross. Deira families who book this early are consistently the ones who need the fewest hours.

sections.heading: MYP 5 into DP1: the three gaps that actually cause trouble
paragraphs: Most Deira MYP students are heading for the Diploma, and the transition has a reputation for being smooth because both are IB programmes. In practice three specific things bite, and all three are addressable in the final MYP term rather than discovered in the first DP1 report.

The first is examination stamina. MYP assessment is coursework-shaped: tasks, investigations, projects, with feedback cycles. The Diploma ends in externally marked papers written under timed conditions, and a student who has never written for ninety minutes without a break finds the first mock brutal regardless of how well they know the content. The fix is mechanical and unglamorous: timed practice, starting with thirty minutes.

The second is mathematics. MYP Mathematics is assessed on criteria that reward investigation and real-world application. Diploma Mathematics, in either Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, is assessed on papers that reward accurate algebraic manipulation and correct calculator use under time pressure. A student with strong Criterion B investigation marks and shaky algebraic fluency has a gap that is invisible in MYP reporting and very visible in DP1. Extended MYP Mathematics narrows it; standard MYP Mathematics into Higher Level Analysis and Approaches widens it considerably.

The third is command terms. The Diploma publishes a defined list of command terms per subject - state, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss - each with a specific expected response. MYP students are used to criterion descriptors, which are related but not the same vocabulary. Spending two sessions explicitly on command terms before DP1 starts is one of the cheapest interventions available, and it pays back across all six subjects rather than one.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs around Deira, and what each band actually buys
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest thing in the market and work up, because that is the order a Deira household actually shops in. Platform tutoring with university-student tutors is advertised from around AED 33 to 52 an hour by Tutopiya and from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik. At that level you are buying homework supervision and a second explanation of something a teacher already taught. For a student whose Criterion A is fine and whose Criterion B is a 3, that is not the purchase that helps.

The next band up is a qualified subject tutor working online, which Unitors publishes from AED 150 an hour for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one visits, which include the tutor's travel, are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors; TutorChase publishes AED 270, and BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. Monthly packages seen across the market run from around AED 799 for eight online sessions to AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What those figures mean for MYP specifically is a bit different from the examined courses, because the useful purchase is often small. A single-criterion repair block is two to four sessions. Personal Project process support, started early, is four to six. You are not usually buying a two-year programme. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session - AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work - describe the recurring commitment, and most MYP families should be at the lower end of that range for a shorter period.

None of these are IB Gram prices and we do not publish a rate card on a landing page. They are what the market charges, taken from each provider's own published figures as read in October 2026, so that you can judge any quote you receive, including ours, against something real. Two things worth knowing before you pay anyone: ask whether the rate is per hour or per lesson, and ask what happens if you stop after one session. Those two answers separate the providers quickly.

sections.heading: The in-home question, answered honestly for a Deira flat
paragraphs: Parents in Deira search for a home tutor for sensible reasons. A flat is quieter to supervise than a drive across the creek, a younger sibling cannot be left alone, and a tutor in the room is visible in a way a tutor on a screen is not. Those are real arguments and we are not going to pretend otherwise.

Here is the position stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. For Deira, and for every other UAE address, lessons are one-to-one over live video. We say that before anyone pays rather than after, because two competitors in this market route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without disclosing where the tutor actually sits.

The case for online in this specific district is not a cost argument, although the travel premium in the market data above is real. It is a supply argument. MYP is a minority curriculum in the Deira, Al Qusais and Al Nahda belt, and a specialist in MYP Design criteria or MYP 5 Personal Project supervision who happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of Al Muteena may simply not exist. Insisting on physical proximity narrows the pool to whoever is nearby, which for a niche MYP requirement often means accepting a generalist. Online removes the constraint and lets you pick on criterion expertise instead of on postcode.

The practical gains are smaller and still worth naming. A fixed hour that does not move because of traffic on Al Ittihad Road. A screen where the task sheet, the clarification and the student's draft sit side by side, annotated and saved. A recording or a set of notes a parent can read later. For criterion-marked work, which is almost entirely document work, these are not consolation prizes.

sections.heading: KHDA, mandatory UAE subjects, and the hours they take from the MYP week
paragraphs: In Dubai, private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Dubai's private sector was 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. That last figure explains a lot about why MYP specialists are thin on the ground in a district like Deira: IB is a minority curriculum, and MYP is a subset of it.

The mandatory subject rules are the part that affects an MYP timetable directly. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Two consequences for planning. First, those lessons occupy real hours in a week that also has to carry eight MYP subject groups, and a student struggling across several criteria may be struggling with load rather than with any single subject. Looking at the actual timetable before booking tuition sometimes produces a better answer than tuition. Second, for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is a genuine constraint on how any tutoring in those subjects can be described.

One more thing on inspection bands, because Deira parents read them closely when choosing a school. A band describes a whole school across many measures. It does not tell you whether that school's MYP Design teaching is strong or whether its Language acquisition phase placement is careful. For those questions the useful source is other parents in the same year group, and the MYP coordinator.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and the things we will not do
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

A Deira parent can therefore ask any prospective tutor a direct question - do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit - and the answer is checkable. One further point worth knowing: in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct likewise bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Anyone offering you your child's own class teacher privately is offering something they should not.

On our own position, three statements. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson, and anybody in this market claiming otherwise should be asked for a permit number. We hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE. And we do not publish a satisfaction percentage or a star rating, because we cannot produce the underlying data with a sample size and a method attached, and a number without those things is decoration.

The academic honesty line is the one that matters most in MYP, because the Personal Project is the obvious pressure point. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write, co-write, edit to completion or produce any part of a Personal Project, an interdisciplinary task, a process journal or any other submitted assessment. We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or subject guides as downloads; we cite them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is somebody else's copyright.

process.title: Send the task, not the textbook
process.description: Share the marked MYP task, the task-specific clarification and the four criterion scores if you have them. Fifteen minutes with those three documents locates the problem more precisely than an hour of conversation. If the clarification was not sent home, ask the school for it - it is a normal request.

process.title: A free trial lesson, criterion-first
process.description: One session at no cost, with the tutor you would continue with. The hour is spent diagnosing which lettered criterion is costing the grade and showing the student what the descriptor actually asks for. You get a written note of what was found, whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Agree a short block, not a year
process.description: Most MYP problems are two to six sessions. We say so, and we would rather you bought four sessions that fix Criterion B than a standing year that fixes nothing in particular. Weekly support makes sense when criterion scores are evenly low across a subject group.

process.title: Fix the hour to the Deira afternoon
process.description: Pick a slot that survives the real commute from your child's school, not an optimistic one. Families in Al Muteena and Al Garhoud can often hold 4.30pm; Al Nahda and Al Mamzar households are usually better served after six. The hour is in Gulf Standard Time and does not move for traffic.

process.title: Check it against the next school task
process.description: The test of MYP tutoring is the next criterion judgement from the school, not the tutor's opinion. We tell you which criterion we worked on and what to look for on the next returned task. If it did not move, say so and we will change the tutor or the approach.

process.title: Stop when it is fixed
process.description: A criterion repair block ends. If the MYP 5 Personal Project is coming, that is a separate short piece of work with its own timing, best started in the first term. Nobody here benefits from an open-ended booking that nobody is measuring.

whyPoints.title: We start from the criterion, not the topic
whyPoints.description: The first question is which lettered criterion lost the marks. For a Deira family who has only ever seen a grade from 1 to 7, that reframing alone often changes what they buy. Re-teaching content when Criterion B is the problem is the most common waste of money in MYP tutoring.

whyPoints.title: All eight subject groups, including the ones parents dismiss
whyPoints.description: Design and Physical and health education are criterion-marked written subjects for three of their four criteria, and they drag reported grades more often than families expect. We cover the groups that general tutors do not touch, because a 3 in Design Criterion A costs exactly as much as a 3 in Sciences.

whyPoints.title: Honest about where the tutor sits
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson is online, one-to-one, over live video, and we say it before payment. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE. Two providers in this market route UAE parents to overseas numbers without disclosing delivery; we would rather lose the booking than do that.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We coach the process on a Personal Project and we do not produce any part of it. That is a boundary, written down, and it protects the student: under IB academic honesty rules the consequence of crossing it falls on them. One competitor in this SERP sells completed Internal Assessments outright.

whyPoints.description: Every AED range on this page carries the provider who published it and the month it was read. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no star rating and no tutor headcount, because we cannot attach a sample size and a method to any of them.

whyPoints.title: A schedule built for this side of the creek
whyPoints.description: Session times are set against the actual Deira and Al Nahda afternoon rather than a generic 4pm slot. A fixed hour that holds every week is worth more over a term than a nominally convenient one that moves twice a month.

faqs.question: What exactly do the four MYP criteria mean in my child's subject?
faqs.answer: Every MYP subject group has four criteria labelled A to D, each marked 0 to 8, but the letters mean different things in different groups. In Sciences they are Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science. In Mathematics they are Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The table earlier on this page lists all eight groups. Ask your child's teacher which letter the marks were lost on; that single answer usually redirects the tutoring entirely.

faqs.question: Why does my child's MYP report show a 5 when they get most answers right?
faqs.answer: Because MYP is criterion-referenced, not percentage-based. Four criteria at 8 marks each give a total out of 32, which the school converts to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. Getting answers right mostly feeds Criterion A, Knowing and understanding. The other three criteria reward method design, communication and evaluation, and a student can be excellent on content and weak on all three. Ask for the four separate criterion scores. The shape of those four numbers tells you what to work on; the grade does not.

faqs.question: What is a task-specific clarification and should we have been given one?
faqs.answer: It is the generic criterion descriptors rewritten in the language of a particular task, which makes it effectively the mark scheme handed out in advance. Producing one is normal MYP assessment practice. If a marked task came home without it, asking the school is a reasonable request rather than a complaint. Reading it with your child before they write is the highest-value fifteen minutes available in the whole programme, and in our experience a good share of booked MYP tutoring hours are spent explaining something the clarification already said plainly.

faqs.question: How are the MYP language acquisition phases decided for a child in Deira?
faqs.answer: By proficiency in that language, not by year group. There are six phases: 1 and 2 emergent, 3 and 4 capable, 5 and 6 proficient. A student can sit in Phase 2 for one language and Phase 5 for another at the same time. Placement is the school's decision. What a tutor can do is diagnose honestly by setting tasks from two different phases in one session, which produces written evidence you can take to the MYP coordinator. In multilingual Deira households, a misplacement is a common and fixable cause of low Reading and Writing scores.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP Personal Project without crossing the honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. The Personal Project is marked on three criteria - Planning, Applying skills, Reflecting - worth 24 marks, and sixteen of those rest on the process journal and the report. A tutor can help narrow the goal, write testable success criteria, build a journal habit and ask the questions that produce genuine reflection. A tutor cannot choose the project, make any part of the product, write or edit any part of the report. Crossing that line is an IB academic honesty breach, and the consequence lands on the student.

faqs.question: Is the MYP harder than IGCSE for a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They are hard in different ways, which is why the comparison rarely helps. IGCSE specifies content and examines it externally, so a student knows what to learn and has to perform on the day. MYP specifies skills through criteria and assesses them continuously, so a student has to understand how they are being judged across eight subject groups at once. Organised students who dislike exams often prefer MYP. Students who learn content readily but struggle with sustained coursework usually find IGCSE a cleaner fit. Your child's school decides which route it runs.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 5 and going into DP1 next year. What should we fix now?
faqs.answer: Three things, in this order. Examination stamina, because MYP assessment is coursework-shaped and the Diploma ends in timed papers - start at thirty minutes and build. Algebraic fluency, because MYP Mathematics rewards investigation while Diploma Mathematics rewards accurate manipulation under time pressure, and that gap is invisible on an MYP report. And command terms, because the Diploma publishes a defined list per subject with specific expected responses. Two sessions on command terms before DP1 begins pays back across all six subjects rather than one.

faqs.question: How many sessions does MYP tutoring usually take to show something?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect. A single-criterion repair - Sciences Criterion B, say - is typically two to four sessions, because the student usually already knows the content and has never read the descriptor. Personal Project process support started in the first term of MYP 5 is four to six. Weekly standing support makes sense only when criterion scores are evenly low across a whole subject group rather than spiky. We would rather sell you four sessions that move one criterion than a year that moves nothing measurable.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost in Dubai, and how do I judge a quote?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; Unitors publishes from AED 200 for IB; Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above and in-home visits at AED 180 to 350; BartyED sits at AED 650. Those are the market, not our prices. When you get a quote, ask two questions: is the rate per hour or per lesson, and what happens if we stop after one session. The answers separate providers fast.

faqs.question: Do you send an MYP tutor to our flat in Deira?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, and we state that before you pay rather than after. For criterion-marked work the online format is genuinely better suited: the task sheet, the clarification and the student's own draft sit side by side on a shared screen, get annotated together and can be revisited. The real argument, though, is supply - an MYP Design or Personal Project specialist within a twenty-minute drive of Deira may not exist.

faqs.question: Does my child have to take Arabic alongside the MYP in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed for, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Note that this mandatory Arabic is a different thing from MYP Language acquisition Arabic, and report comments can refer to either.

faqs.question: Does every MYP 5 student sit IB eAssessment?
faqs.answer: No - it is a school-level choice. Where a school opts in, the final MYP Certificate grade comes from on-screen examinations and ePortfolios marked by the IB rather than from the school's own criterion judgements, which changes the whole plan for the final year. Where a school does not, the MYP record is school-assessed against the criteria. This is a one-question conversation with your MYP coordinator and it should happen before the final year starts, because the two routes need different preparation and different timing for any tuition.

faqs.question: Does an MYP tutor working with a Deira family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted.

faqs.question: Why is Design dragging my child's MYP grades when the project looked good?
faqs.answer: Because three of Design's four criteria are documentation rather than making. Criterion A is Inquiring and analysing, B is Developing ideas, C is Creating the solution and D is Evaluating. The design cycle has to be evidenced: a research plan, a design brief, specifications written so they can actually be tested, and a test of the finished solution against those exact specifications. A beautiful outcome with no documented specification scores badly on A, B and D. This is one of the quickest MYP fixes available and usually needs two or three sessions.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover several MYP subject groups for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on whether the problem is content or criterion. If a student is weak on Criterion B across Sciences, Mathematics and Individuals and societies, that is one transferable skill - producing a plan or line of inquiry rather than an answer - and a single tutor working on it can move several reported grades. If the problem is subject content in two unrelated groups, you want two specialists. We will tell you which case you are in during the free trial rather than selling the convenient answer.

faqs.question: We are moving to Deira mid-year from an IB school abroad. What should we check first?
faqs.answer: Three things in the first fortnight. Language acquisition phase placement, because a transfer is usually placed by default rather than by assessment and the wrong phase caps Reading and Writing marks for reasons unrelated to effort. The school's assessment map, so you know which criteria are being assessed in the current reporting period and can time any tuition to land before the task. And whether the school runs MYP eAssessment in the final year. All three are questions for the MYP coordinator, and none of them cost anything.

Ask your child's teacher, get the four scores out of 8, and the right tutoring decision usually becomes obvious - often a short block rather than a standing commitment. dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-difc.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Middle Years Programme subjects against the published criteria rather than against a textbook chapter. Each one can read a criterion-marked report, say which of the four strands is actually costing the level, and work in forty-minute blocks when the student is eleven rather than sixteen.

intro.heading: Decoding a Middle Years Programme report from a DIFC address
paragraphs: Two things bring DIFC parents to this search. The first is a report that resists interpretation. A British or American system gives percentages, ranks and a comment; the Middle Years Programme gives four criterion marks out of eight per subject, an overall level from one to seven, and a set of command-term-heavy descriptors. A parent reading 'Criterion B: 4' has no way of knowing whether that is a disaster, a plateau or entirely normal for the middle of MYP 3. Schools publish the criteria, but very few explain them in a form a parent can act on, and almost nobody explains them before the first reporting cycle.

The second is the clock, and it works differently for a middle-schooler than for a Diploma student. A twelve-year-old in MYP 2 finishes school somewhere between 14:45 and 15:20, loses twenty to forty minutes to the drive back into the towers, and is genuinely finished by half past seven. The usable window is roughly 16:30 to 18:30, and inside it there is also school homework, a sport, an instrument and the collapse that every child needs after a school day. A plan built on a fifty-five-minute evening session three times a week was never going to survive, and when it fails the family concludes the child cannot focus rather than that the diary was wrong.

The programme's structure makes early intervention unusually cheap. There are five Middle Years Programme years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, covering roughly ages eleven to sixteen. Nothing in MYP 1 or MYP 2 is externally assessed and nothing is irreversible, which means a weakness identified there costs a handful of sessions. The same weakness discovered in MYP 5, with the Personal Project running and Diploma subject choices being made, costs a term. The criterion that most often turns out to be the real problem is not knowledge. It is the investigating, designing or communicating strand, which no amount of content revision touches.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring exists only in India. For a younger student that turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise: the session can be forty minutes rather than an hour because no travel has to be amortised, it can sit at 16:30 on the day the child is least tired, and it can move by a day without anybody rearranging a journey across the city.

What follows is the detail that makes the report readable: what each of the five years is for, the criteria by subject group with their maxima and the specific things parents misread, the realistic afternoon window by year group, how the Personal Project is marked and where students lose it, the Arabic and Islamic Education requirements KHDA places on every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it licenses, what MYP 5 does and does not prepare a child for in the Diploma, and the limits we will not pretend away.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-difc.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme sits in the middle of a line that starts in primary and ends with a sixth-form qualification. Each point on it asks something different of a DIFC family, and the Middle Years Programme years are the cheapest place on the line to fix anything.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than separate subjects, finishing with an exhibition in the final year. There are no external examinations and no numerical grades of the kind parents from other systems expect. The skills it builds, particularly independent inquiry and oral presentation, are exactly what the Middle Years Programme criteria will later reward.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses within reach of DIFC run the Primary Years Programme into the Middle Years Programme as a continuum, which is why families here often stay at one school for a decade. The jolt arrives for children who join in MYP 1 or MYP 2 from a British primary: they meet criterion marking, command terms and an inquiry expectation all at once, and the first report is usually worse than the child's actual ability.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, plus interdisciplinary learning, Service as Action and the Personal Project in the final year. Assessment is criterion-based: four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with the total of 32 converted to a level from one to seven using published boundaries. Optional on-screen eAssessment exists at the end of MYP 5 but many schools do not enter candidates for it.
programmes.countryNote: In the DIFC catchment the Middle Years Programme is the minority route. Dubai's private sector is British-curriculum by weight of enrolment, at 37% of pupils against 7% on IB programmes, so a DIFC family on this route will have neighbours whose children are sitting Year 9 tests while theirs are being marked against criterion descriptors. That comparison causes a great deal of unnecessary worry and is worth understanding properly rather than arguing about at the school gate.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and a service commitment. Assessment becomes external and heavily examination-weighted, which is the sharpest change a Middle Years Programme student experiences. Internal assessments carry fixed criteria and fixed weightings, usually around a fifth of each science grade.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 flows into the Diploma at most of the continuum campuses near DIFC, and the transition is where the programme's real gaps surface. Students arrive with strong inquiry and communication habits and with less drilled content recall and less examination stamina than their peers coming from a Year 11 qualification. Both are fixable in the summer between, and both are considerably harder to fix in the second term of Year 12.

programmes.name: The Year 11 alternative at 14
programmes.description: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, taken instead of MYP 4 and MYP 5 at the many Dubai schools that run a British route. Content-heavy, externally examined, tiered in several subjects, with syllabus codes a parent can look up. It is a different kind of preparation, not a better or worse one, and the choice is often made for a family by the school it is already in.
programmes.countryNote: Families in DIFC sometimes move a child from the Middle Years Programme into a Year 11 qualification at the end of MYP 3, usually for a change of school rather than a change of philosophy. The move is entirely workable, and the content gap is narrower than parents fear. The habit gap is wider: an MYP 3 student has rarely sat a long written examination under timed conditions, and that is what needs building first.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-difc.subjectsIntro: The Middle Years Programme has eight subject groups, each with its own four criteria. These are the groups, with what the criteria actually reward and where a DIFC student most often loses the level.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Most students are solid on A and lose the level on B and D, because pattern investigation and real-world modelling are rarely practised at home. Extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 is the route into Higher Level Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C is the one that predicts later Diploma trouble, because it tests data handling, graphing and evaluation rather than recall, and the Diploma's data-based examination questions test the same thing with harder numbers.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criteria A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language. Strong readers frequently score well on A and poorly on B, because organising an argument into a structure a marker can follow is a separate skill from understanding the text. Criterion D covers register and accuracy and is where second-language speakers lose marks they could recover quickly.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, with students placed in a phase rather than a year group. French, Spanish and Arabic are the common offerings near DIFC. The phase placement is the thing parents should query: a child placed too low coasts for two years, and a child placed too high loses criterion marks for reasons unconnected to effort.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D is the hardest to self-teach and the most heavily weighted in practice, because it asks for evaluation of sources and of arguments rather than recall of content. It is also the criterion that transfers most directly into Diploma history and economics.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. Students enjoy C and neglect A and D, so the folder is full of product and thin on research and testing. Because the Personal Project uses a very similar planning and evaluating structure, strong design habits in MYP 3 pay back directly in MYP 5.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. The process journal carries more of the mark than most families expect, and a student whose finished piece is strong can still sit on a level 4 because the documentation of how they got there is missing. That is a habit problem and it responds quickly to being named.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting on and improving performance. The written and reflective strands surprise sporty students, who assume the subject is assessed on the field. Criterion D in particular asks for analysis of their own performance data, which is a transferable skill worth building.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Three criteria, planning, applying skills and reflecting, each out of eight. The product matters far less than the process journal and the report, which is the opposite of what most students assume in September. A tutor may teach the criteria and ask hard questions; the research, the product, the journal and the report belong to the student alone.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.levels: KHDA requirement · all Dubai private schools
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils and prescribed languages of instruction. These subjects sit alongside the Middle Years Programme rather than inside it, and they occupy real timetable and homework time that any support plan has to account for.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-difc.regionsTitle: Which areas near DIFC actually run the Middle Years Programme
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-difc.regionsIntro: The Middle Years Programme is not offered everywhere in this catchment, and that single fact shapes where DIFC families on this route end up living and driving. These are the areas, with what each one offers a middle-school student.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: The nearest cluster of substantial campuses to DIFC, ten to eighteen minutes out. Both IB continuum and British provision here, which makes it the area where a family can change route without changing commute. Short journey means a 16:30 session is genuinely achievable for an MYP 2 student.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: A continuum campus running from the early years through the Diploma, with the Middle Years Programme in the middle of it. Families here stay for years, so weaknesses can be worked on across several terms rather than fixed in a panic. The later finish time pushes sessions to 17:15 or 17:30.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: No large secondary campus in either district, so every middle-school family commutes out. These areas generate the heaviest demand for early-evening slots in this cluster, and a family booking in October rather than September usually finds 16:30 and 17:00 already gone.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Quoz 4
regions.note: Three campuses within a quarter of an hour on a clear run, mostly British curriculum with strong middle-school provision. A family here comparing the Middle Years Programme against a Year 9 and then Year 11 route will find both options within the same drive, which makes the choice a real one.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Twenty to thirty-five minutes back at pick-up. For a younger student that journey is the binding constraint: a child who gets home at 16:05 should not start a session at 16:15. Families here do better with 17:30 sessions or weekend mornings, and with forty-minute blocks rather than hour ones.

regions.name: Al Safa and Jumeirah
regions.note: The established British-curriculum belt with one well-known IB continuum school among it. Middle-school students travelling here from DIFC face a long return leg, and the practical consequence is that weekday sessions end up later than is ideal for an eleven or twelve-year-old.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and the coast
regions.note: Twenty-five to forty minutes each way, which for a middle-school child effectively removes the weekday evening. Families from this group most often take Saturday or Sunday morning sessions, which suits the age group well because attention in the morning is markedly better than at 18:30.

schoolClusters.city: Continuum campuses near DIFC running the Middle Years Programme
schoolClusters.note: These are the schools a DIFC family on an IB route most often uses, several running the Primary Years Programme and the Middle Years Programme into a Diploma sixth form. Programme offerings change, so confirm the current position with the school and against the regulator's own listing rather than with any tutoring site.
schools: Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, Al Jaddaf
North London Collegiate School Dubai, Sobha Hartland
GEMS Wellington International School, Al Sufouh

schoolClusters.city: British-curriculum campuses offering the Year 9 and Year 11 route instead
schoolClusters.note: The alternative within the same commute. Families comparing routes should know that these campuses take students into a Year 11 qualification at sixteen and then into A Levels or a Diploma sixth form, which is a different kind of middle school rather than a weaker one.
schools: Kent College Dubai, Nad Al Sheba

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-difc.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are listed as context for the programmes available within the DIFC catchment. IB Gram has no affiliation with, endorsement from or partnership with any of them, and programme offerings should be confirmed with the school directly.
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-difc.modesIntro: Three shapes of Middle Years Programme support, chosen mainly by the student's age rather than by subject. All of them run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, in blocks short enough for the age group.

modes.title: Forty-minute weekly sessions, MYP 1 to MYP 3
modes.description: Shorter than a Diploma session and deliberately so. An eleven or twelve-year-old arriving home at four o'clock has roughly one good block of concentration left, and forty focused minutes at 16:30 produce more than an hour at 18:00. The session takes one criterion at a time rather than a whole subject, and finishes with something small enough to be done before the next one.
bullets: 16:30 or 17:00 start in Gulf Standard Time, one fixed day
One criterion as the focus, not a whole subject
A short task set that genuinely fits in twenty minutes

modes.title: Fifty-five-minute sessions, MYP 4 and MYP 5
modes.description: Full-length sessions for the years where work starts to count towards choices. These track the school's own units and assessment calendar, so the hour prepares the criterion-marked task that is actually coming rather than a generic topic. In MYP 5 the Personal Project and Diploma subject selection both land in the same year, and the session plan has to acknowledge that.
bullets: Planned against the school's unit and assessment calendar
Criterion-marked task preparation rather than topic revision
Written note after each session naming the next two priorities

modes.title: Personal Project coaching in MYP 5
modes.description: A short block around the project's three criteria: planning, applying skills and reflecting. The tutor teaches what each criterion rewards, asks whether the goal is specific enough to be assessed, and presses on the process journal, which carries more of the mark than students expect. The research, the product, the journal and the report are entirely the student's.
bullets: Goal tested against criterion A before work begins
Process journal habits built early rather than reconstructed late
Questioning feedback only; nothing written, edited or supplied

modes.title: Transition blocks and holiday work
modes.description: Used at two specific points: joining the Middle Years Programme from another system, and leaving MYP 5 for the Diploma or a Year 11 route. Both are content-and-habit jobs rather than subject jobs, and both are best done in a Dubai school holiday when there is no school day to recover from and ninety minutes is possible.
bullets: Command terms and criterion language taught explicitly on entry
Examination stamina and content recall built on exit
Weekend and holiday morning slots in Gulf Standard Time

sections.heading: What a DIFC search for Middle Years Programme help usually means
paragraphs: In practice this search comes from one of three situations. A family has just moved to Dubai and the first criterion-marked report has arrived; a child in MYP 4 has dropped a level in one subject and nobody can explain why; or MYP 5 has started, the Personal Project has been announced, and Diploma subject choices are due in the same term. The three need different responses, and the thing they have in common is that the parent cannot tell from the report which criterion is actually the problem.

That is a solvable information problem rather than a teaching problem, and it is worth separating the two before spending anything. Every subject group is marked against four criteria, each out of eight, and the total out of 32 is converted to a level from one to seven using boundaries the school publishes. A student on 7, 4, 4, 5 and a student on 4, 6, 6, 4 can land on the same overall level while having entirely different problems. The first needs organisation and communication work; the second needs content. A tutor who reads the criterion breakdown rather than the level gets this right in one session.

The second half of the search is about the afternoon. DIFC is a tower district and the schools are not in it, so every middle-school family here drives, usually against the worst of the traffic. The difference between a plan that runs for thirty weeks and one that dies in October is whether it was built around the hour the child is actually alert. For an MYP 1 student that hour is 16:30, not 18:30, and it is shorter than an hour. Everything below is written with that in mind.
bullets: Two students on the same level can have opposite problems
The criterion breakdown, not the level, is the diagnostic
Younger students need shorter, earlier sessions, not more of them

sections.heading: The five Middle Years Programme years and what each one is for
paragraphs: Parents arriving from other systems reasonably ask which year matters. The honest answer is that none of the first three carry external consequences and all of them carry habit consequences, and the habits are what the Diploma later charges for. MYP 1 to MYP 3 are where command terms, inquiry structure and process documentation become automatic or do not. MYP 4 and MYP 5 are where subject choices narrow, where extended mathematics separates from standard, and where the Personal Project runs.

The table below maps the years onto the school-year labels Dubai families actually use, which is the first thing a new arrival needs, and then says what changes in each year and where support does the most. The labels vary slightly between campuses, so confirm against your own school, but the pattern holds across the continuum schools in this catchment. The useful column is the last one: it names the single intervention that pays back most at each stage.

The pattern worth noticing is that the cost of a fix rises steeply from left to right. A communication-criterion weakness named in MYP 2 is three or four sessions and a changed habit. The same weakness still present in MYP 5 shows up in the Personal Project report, in Diploma subject recommendations and in the first Year 12 essays, and now costs a term. Nothing about the programme forces that escalation; it happens because criterion reports are hard for parents to read and the first three years feel consequence-free.

columns: The intervention that pays back most
rows: Criterion marking and command terms arrive
Teach the criterion language explicitly, once
Fix the communication and organising strands
