sections.heading: Reading an MYP report properly: the four letters and what they mean
paragraphs: An MYP report gives a grade from 1 to 7 per subject, and underneath it, if the school publishes them, four criterion marks out of eight. The grade is derived from the sum of those four, through a published boundary table. The sum is what matters, and the distribution inside it matters more. Two students can both come out with a 5 while having entirely different problems, and the overall grade conceals which is which.

The criteria are named differently in each subject group but they follow a pattern. Criterion A is almost always knowledge and understanding, which rewards recall and application. Criterion B is the inquiry or investigation criterion, which rewards designing, planning or pattern-finding. Criterion C is usually communication or production. Criterion D is usually the critical, evaluative or reflective one. A student who is strong on A and weak on B is a good learner who has never been taught to plan, which is a specific and very fixable thing.

The practical move for a parent is to stop looking at the grade and start looking at the shape. If criterion A is the highest and D the lowest across several subjects, the issue is evaluation and critical thinking, and it will limit DP assessment in every subject later. If B is the outlier, the issue is investigation design. If C is the outlier, the issue is written structure. In each case the tuition is a short block aimed at that one thing, not a general programme in the subject.
The table below sets out the four criteria for the subject groups Downtown families ask about most. Hold your child's report against it and the pattern usually appears within a minute.

sections.heading: From 32 criterion marks to a single grade, and why one band matters
paragraphs: Four criteria at eight marks each gives a maximum of 32, and that total converts to the familiar 1 to 7 grade through the published MYP boundary table. The bands are not evenly spaced, which has a consequence most parents never see: a two-mark gain in the right place can move a grade, while a four-mark gain in the wrong place moves nothing. Knowing where your child sits inside a band is worth more than knowing which band they are in.

Take a student on 18 out of 32. That sits at the top of the grade 4 band, one mark short of grade 5. If their weakest criterion is a 3, lifting that single criterion to a 5 moves the total to 20 and the grade to 5. If instead they spend a term improving their strongest criterion from a 6 to a 7, the total reaches 19 and the grade still moves, but the work was harder and the room left for improvement is now gone. Working on the weakest criterion is almost always the better investment, and it is also the easier one, because the lowest band descriptors are the least demanding to satisfy.

Schools do not usually explain this and are not obliged to. Reporting conventions vary across Dubai, with some schools publishing all four criterion marks and others publishing only the grade. If yours publishes only the grade, ask the subject teacher for the criterion breakdown; they will have it, because they generated it. That one email converts a vague report into an actionable plan.

sections.heading: Where the Downtown day leaves room for an MYP student
paragraphs: MYP students are younger than Diploma students and tire earlier, which changes the scheduling problem rather than simplifying it. A thirteen-year-old who left a Boulevard lobby at 6.50am and reached home at 4.30pm has a usable window that closes around 7.30pm, not 9pm. Pushing a session later to suit a parent's working day produces an hour that looks like tuition and achieves very little, and most families only learn this after paying for a term of it.

The corridor matters here as much as it does for older students. Children bussed north to Al Safa, Al Satwa or Jumeirah are generally home between 3.45pm and 4.15pm, which makes a 5pm start comfortable and a 5.30pm start ideal. Children bussed south-east to Nad Al Sheba or across to Al Quoz are often not home until closer to 5pm, which means 6pm is the honest earliest start and the session should probably be sixty minutes rather than ninety. Co-curricular days add an hour to all of it.

There is a second constraint specific to this age group. MYP students carry homework from up to eight subject groups, and the assessment load clusters: schools commonly schedule several criterion assessments in the same fortnight. A session that is useful in a quiet week is a burden in an assessment week, so the sensible pattern is one fixed weekly hour with the content flexed to whatever is actually due, rather than a rigid syllabus march that ignores the school calendar.

Online delivery is what makes the narrow window usable at all, because no part of it is spent on travel at either end. It also means a session can move from Tuesday to Thursday in an assessment-heavy week without anybody writing off a journey, and that flexibility is worth more to an MYP family than to a DP family.

sections.heading: MYP 5, the Personal Project and the honesty line
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the piece of MYP work parents in Dubai worry about most, and with some reason: it is substantial, largely unsupervised, and documented through a process journal that students find unnatural. It is also the clearest ancestor of the Extended Essay, and a student who learns to record decisions as they make them in MYP 5 is a student who will not be reconstructing a researcher's reflection space from memory in DP2.

The marks are lost in a predictable place. Students choose an ambitious goal, build something genuinely good, and then discover that the report asks for evidence of a process they did not document. A product that works and a journal with four entries scores poorly. A modest product with a thorough record of decisions, dead ends and revisions scores well. Explaining that in month one, rather than in the week before submission, is most of the available value a tutor can add.

The honesty line has to be drawn firmly here, because the Dubai market includes businesses that sell completed coursework. A tutor may help a student narrow a goal until it is achievable, establish a journalling routine, read the published criteria with them, ask the questions that produce a usable reflection, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not design the project, build the product, write the journal, or draft any part of the report. The work must be the student's own, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student.

We also do not supply IB documents as downloads. Subject guides, project guides and assessment criteria are published by the IB and we point to the official source or to the version your child's school has issued, rather than reproducing material we do not own.

sections.heading: The MYP to DP transition, subject by subject
paragraphs: Families in Downtown making the post-16 decision usually ask whether MYP prepares a child for the Diploma, and the answer is yes in skills and no in format. The skills map almost one to one. What does not transfer is the assessment mechanism: MYP adds criterion marks from internally assessed tasks, while the Diploma weights externally examined papers with one internally assessed component. A student who has never sat a three-hour paper arrives in DP1 with excellent inquiry skills and no examination stamina.

The specific transitions are worth naming because each has a different gap. In sciences, MYP criterion B and C become the DP Scientific Investigation's Research design and Data analysis almost directly, but DP adds two written papers with a data booklet and command-term conventions the MYP never used. In mathematics, MYP criterion B becomes the heart of the DP mathematical exploration, while DP Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches is sat without a calculator, which exposes any arithmetic the MYP permitted a device to do.

In language and literature, the MYP's analysing criterion becomes DP Paper 1 guided analysis, and the gap is timed writing rather than analytical ability. In individuals and societies, the thinking critically criterion becomes most of what a DP history or economics paper rewards, and the gap is content volume. Across all subjects, the Diploma core adds Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS on top, which is a workload change rather than a skills change.

The table maps each transition with the gap and roughly how much bridging work it takes. A student who does that bridging in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 starts the Diploma differently from one who discovers the gap in October.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies inside an MYP timetable
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches these subjects regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed to deliver, and MYP families are frequently surprised by how the requirements work in practice. KHDA's published guidance makes Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies mandatory across all Dubai private schools, with the requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisational rules are specific and they explain things parents notice but cannot account for. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and KHDA states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. That is why your child may be in a different Arabic set from a classmate in the same form group, and it is a regulatory requirement rather than a setting decision.

Language of instruction is also set. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the language of the school's licensed curriculum. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

One constraint affects tutoring directly. For these mandatory subjects, KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Practically, that means support in Arabic or Islamic Education should work from the material the school uses rather than from an alternative syllabus, and any tutor offering a parallel curriculum in these subjects is offering something that does not fit the rules. KHDA also requires schools to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from KHDA to teach them, which applies to school staff rather than to private tutors.

sections.heading: What MYP tuition costs, and why families spend too little too late
paragraphs: The pattern across the central corridor is consistent and expensive. Families notice a criterion problem in MYP 3, decide it is early and probably nothing, and then buy a great deal of tuition in DP1 to repair a skill that would have taken five sessions to fix at thirteen. Pricing the two options against each other makes the case better than any argument: five sessions at mid-market rates against a year of Diploma-level support is not a close comparison.

The published market rates give the arithmetic. Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts weekly one-hour tutoring at AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. At the lower end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52; at the upper end TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for named or examiner-linked tutors. In-home delivery sits across those bands with travel loaded in, at AED 180 to AED 350 per Bestimate and AED 200 to AED 500 for independent home tutors.

An MYP criterion block, four to six sessions in the mid-market band, costs in the region of AED 600 to AED 1,800 in total depending on the tier chosen. The DP-year equivalent for the same unaddressed skill is a specialist rate across two or three terms. The MYP intervention is also easier to buy well, because the success condition is explicit: the next criterion mark either moves or it does not, and you find out within a few weeks.

For context on household budgeting, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Fees are flat; tutoring is the discretionary line. Every figure quoted in this section belongs to the provider named beside it and none is an IB Gram price. sections.heading: Getting started with an MYP tutor, and what to do if the hour is full
paragraphs: The useful first step is not booking anything. It is getting the four criterion marks for the subject you are worried about, which the subject teacher holds whether or not the report prints them. One email produces a breakdown that turns a vague worry into a specific job, and it also tells you whether the problem sits in one subject or in a skill shared across several.

With that in hand, the match is straightforward. Tell us the subject group, the MYP year, the criterion in question and the hour your child is realistically home from the bus, and we will shortlist tutors who teach that subject group at that level and are free then. The first lesson is free and is a real lesson: the tutor reads the descriptor with your child and re-marks a piece of their past work against it, which is usually the moment a twelve-year-old understands what they have been losing marks for.

Availability is honest rather than assumed. Demand across Downtown, Business Bay and DIFC concentrates between roughly 5pm and 7pm on weekdays because every family is working around the same bus returns, and the MYP window is narrower than the Diploma one because younger students cannot take a late slot. When an hour is full we offer a different hour, a different day, or a named wait. We do not substitute a Diploma tutor onto an MYP 2 request and hope the age difference does not show, because it does.

Two closing disclosures. Some of our MYP tutors are UAE residents and others teach from India, where our in-home service operates, working with Dubai students over live video in Gulf Standard Time. And IB Gram runs no office, centre or branch in the UAE and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the country, so there is nothing to arrange at your end beyond a quiet room and a charged laptop.

faqs.question: What do the MYP criterion marks on my child's report actually mean?
faqs.answer: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each marked out of eight. The four marks are added, giving a total out of 32, and that total converts through a published boundary table into the grade from 1 to 7 you see on the report. The pattern inside the four is what tells you something: a high A with a low B means a child who knows the content but has never been taught to plan an investigation. Ask the subject teacher for the breakdown if the report prints only the grade.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well on criterion A but badly on criterion B?
faqs.answer: Because the two reward different things and schools teach the first more than the second. Criterion A is knowledge and understanding, which rewards recall and application and responds to revision. Criterion B is the inquiry or investigation criterion, which rewards designing a method, choosing a sensible range of values, or finding and generalising a pattern. That is a taught skill rather than a learned body of content, and a student who has never had it explicitly taught will underperform on it indefinitely. It typically takes four to six focused sessions to shift.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion should we work on first to move the grade?
faqs.answer: Almost always the lowest one. The boundary bands between grades are unevenly spaced, so a two-mark gain on a weak criterion often moves the grade while a two-mark gain on a strong one does not. The low bands are also easier to satisfy, because their descriptors are less demanding, so the same effort produces more marks there. A student sitting on 18 out of 32 with a weakest criterion of 3 can usually reach the next grade by lifting that single criterion rather than by improving everything.

faqs.question: Is MYP good preparation for the IB Diploma, or does it leave students behind?
faqs.answer: It prepares the skills well and the format badly. MYP criterion B in sciences becomes Research design in the DP Scientific Investigation; criterion B in mathematics becomes the core of the mathematical exploration; the Personal Project's process journal is the direct ancestor of the Extended Essay's reflection space. What MYP does not provide is experience of long externally examined papers, command-term conventions, or the sheer content volume a Diploma subject carries. A short bridging block in the summer before DP1 is the efficient answer.

faqs.question: Why did my child build a good Personal Project and still get a mediocre mark?
faqs.answer: It is reported against published criteria and documented through a process journal, and the marks are lost on evidence of process rather than on the product. The common pattern is an ambitious goal, a genuinely good finished product, and a journal with four entries written retrospectively. A modest product with a thorough record of decisions, dead ends and revisions scores better than an impressive product with no record. Establishing a journalling routine in the first month is the single highest-value intervention available.

faqs.question: What is a Personal Project tutor allowed to do, and what must my child do alone?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a clear boundary. A tutor may help narrow a goal until it is achievable in the time available, set up a journalling routine, read the published criteria with the student, ask the questions that produce a usable reflection, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not choose the project, build the product, write journal entries or draft any part of the report. The work must be the student's own, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student rather than the tutor.

faqs.question: What time should an MYP session start if my child is bussed from Downtown Dubai?
faqs.answer: Earlier than you might schedule a Diploma student. A thirteen-year-old who left the building at 6.50am has a usable window that closes around 7.30pm. Children bussed north to Al Safa or Al Satwa are usually home by 4.15pm, so 5pm to 5.30pm works well. Children bussed to Nad Al Sheba or Al Quoz are often not home until closer to 5pm, which makes 6.15pm the honest earliest start. Sixty minutes suits this age better than ninety, and co-curricular days need the slot moved rather than squeezed.

faqs.question: My child's grades dropped by one across several subjects at once. What causes that?
faqs.answer: Usually a shared skill rather than several separate content problems. Criterion C in most subject groups concerns communicating or producing text, and criterion D concerns critical or evaluative thinking, so a student who cannot structure an extended written response or evaluate a source is marked down in every subject that assesses it. The diagnostic move is to compare which criterion letter is lowest across subjects. If it is the same letter each time, one tutor fixing one skill produces a gain that appears everywhere.

faqs.question: Does my child have to study Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the MYP in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA's published guidance makes Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and KHDA states combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with any mandatory subject lesson advised to run at least 25 minutes.

faqs.question: Can we get Arabic support that follows the school's own material?
faqs.answer: That is the only form of support that fits the rules properly. For the mandatory UAE subjects, KHDA states that use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so tutoring in Arabic, Islamic Education or Social Studies should work from the material the school uses rather than from an alternative syllabus. A tutor offering a parallel Arabic curriculum is offering something that does not align with the requirement. Ask the school which textbook and scheme they follow before any session is planned.

faqs.question: How many sessions does an MYP criterion block usually take?
faqs.answer: Four to six for a single criterion in a single subject, with the next criterion assessment as the test of whether it worked. The sequence is short because the job is specific: read the descriptor band by band, re-mark the student's own past work against it, then have the student produce a response that satisfies the higher band and check it. Six to eight sessions is more realistic where the same criterion is weak across several subjects, because transfer has to be checked in each one separately rather than assumed.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost in Dubai compared with waiting until the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Considerably less, which is the strongest argument for acting early. Using published market figures, Unitors lists tuition from AED 150 an hour at IGCSE level, so a four-to-six session criterion block costs roughly AED 600 to AED 900. Repairing the same skill in DP1 means two terms of weekly support, which at Unitors' IB rate from AED 200 an hour is from around AED 4,800. Bestimate's exam-year specialist band runs AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more a month. These are published provider figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is my child in the right language acquisition phase?
faqs.answer: It is worth checking, because phase placement often happens on arrival and is rarely revisited. Language acquisition is assessed in phases rather than year groups, across listening, reading, speaking and writing, and a student placed in a phase on the basis of a first-week assessment may have moved well beyond it or may be struggling in one that was set too high. Ask the language teacher which phase your child is assessed in and whether the placement has been reviewed this year. A mismatch explains more reports than parents expect.

faqs.question: Do you tutor MYP students in Business Bay and DIFC as well as Downtown?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the scheduling logic is close to identical because the three districts share schools and roads. Business Bay pickups run slightly later than Downtown for the same campuses, which pushes the workable session start back by around half an hour. DIFC parents more often ask for late slots because they work in the towers above, and for MYP students we will usually push back on anything after 7.45pm on a school night and suggest a weekend morning instead. All sessions run live online in Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free in our MYP time slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you and give you options rather than filling the hour badly. Demand across the central corridor concentrates between roughly 5pm and 7pm on weekdays, and the MYP window is narrower than the Diploma one because younger students cannot usefully take a late session. The alternatives are a different hour, a different day, a weekend morning, or a named wait. We will not put a Diploma specialist onto an MYP 2 request on the assumption that the subject knowledge covers the age difference, because it does not.

intro.heading: What an MYP report is telling you, and what it is not
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme reports differently from any system most parents in this cluster grew up with, and that is the root of most MYP tutoring enquiries. There are no percentages. Each subject is assessed against four published criteria, each marked out of eight, and the four criterion marks are converted to a single grade from 1 to 8 using published boundaries. A grade 5 in science and a grade 5 in English can mean completely different things about a child's skills.

The useful information is therefore underneath the grade rather than in it. In the sciences the criteria are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student scoring 7 on criterion A and 3 on criterion B does not have a science problem; they have an investigation-design problem, and that is a specific, teachable thing. The overall grade of 5 hides exactly the information a parent needs.

The same pattern repeats across subjects with different criterion names. In mathematics the criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, and the weak one is almost always investigating patterns, because generalising a rule and then justifying it is a skill rarely taught directly. In individuals and societies it is usually the criterion on evaluating sources. In language and literature it is producing text or using language.

So the first thing to ask the school for is the criterion-level breakdown, not just the report. Most schools hold it and many will share it when asked directly. With four criterion marks per subject in hand, a tutor can say in one session what the next eight should contain, and a parent can stop guessing whether their child is doing well.

Geography is the other half of the question. Dubai International Academic City is an education free zone off Al Ain Road, built around university branch campuses; its own secondary, Dubai English Speaking College, runs the British curriculum. The MYP schools this cluster uses are elsewhere - Uptown International School in Mirdif and Universal American School in Al Warqa most often, with the Nad Al Sheba and Garhoud schools beyond that. So MYP families here already commute.

One more thing worth knowing before you buy anything. MYP tutoring rewards small targeted purchases far more than open weekly arrangements across several subjects. A term aimed at one named criterion usually achieves more, and costs considerably less, than a year of general support, because the criterion descriptors are specific enough to teach against directly.

IB Gram delivers this online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For the MYP that matters less than it does at Diploma level, because the local pool of competent MYP tutors is deeper than the pool of Higher Level specialists. It still matters, because criterion-literate MYP tutoring is a narrower skill than general secondary tutoring.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-academic-cit.programmesIntro: MYP tutoring requests from this cluster arrive at three distinct stages, and the right work differs sharply at each.

programmes.name: MYP years 1 to 3
programmes.description: The early years, where criteria are applied more gently and the reporting is hardest for parents to read. Tutoring at this stage is most useful for the two things the programme does not drill: arithmetic fluency and written fluency. Both become expensive to fix later and both are cheap to fix now, because nothing is at stake yet.
programmes.countryNote: Families arriving in this cluster from a British or Indian primary often ask whether their child is behind, and the MYP report cannot answer it. The criterion breakdown can. A child scoring well on knowing and understanding and poorly on communicating is not behind in content; they cannot yet write what they know, which is a different six weeks of work.

programmes.name: MYP years 4 and 5
programmes.description: The years that decide Diploma readiness. Many schools split mathematics into standard and extended at this point, and that split influences whether Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is realistic later. Criteria are applied at full strength and the Personal Project runs alongside, which makes this the busiest stretch of the programme.
programmes.countryNote: In this cluster the schools running MYP 4 and 5 are mostly in Mirdif and Al Warqa, and their mathematics route decisions are made at the end of MYP 3. If Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is a possibility, ask which route the school intends and what evidence would change that view, because the extended route builds the algebraic fluency the Diploma then assumes.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent, long-term project with a supervisor, assessed against published criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and the product itself. It is the MYP's largest single piece of independent work and the clearest rehearsal for the Diploma's Extended Essay. It also collides with everything else in MYP 5.
programmes.countryNote: The commonest Personal Project failure in this cluster is a goal too large to complete and too vague to assess - and the second commonest is a process journal kept retrospectively in the last fortnight. A tutor's job here is to interrogate the goal and the criteria and to question the journal entries. The student plans, makes and writes everything.

programmes.name: MYP 5 into the Diploma
programmes.description: The transition that catches most students in this cluster. The MYP assesses skills against criteria with generous time; the Diploma assumes fluency and examines under time pressure. The gap is specific rather than general: algebraic automaticity, essay structure under timed conditions, and the habit of answering the command term asked rather than the question remembered.
programmes.countryNote: Six to eight sessions in the summer between MYP 5 and the first Diploma year is the best-value tutoring available to a family in this cluster, and almost nobody buys it, because the subject it helps has not started yet. Families who do report a quieter first term and buy fewer hours across the two Diploma years in total.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-academic-cit.subjectsIntro: Each entry names the criteria that actually cost marks in that subject, because that is the level at which MYP tutoring is either useful or decorative.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics, standard and extended
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the weak one for most students: finding a rule is manageable, generalising it in correct notation and then justifying it is rarely taught directly and is heavily assessed.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Marks go on criteria B and C rather than A: students who know the content still design weak investigations and process data without evaluating method or reliability.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. The criterion on critical thinking carries the marks students lose, because it requires source evaluation on provenance and perspective rather than a summary of what the source says.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students strong on analysis frequently score poorly on using language, where accuracy, register and range are assessed separately from ideas. That split is invisible in a single grade and obvious in the criterion marks.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Assessed by phase rather than by year group, so two students in the same class can be working at different phases, which parents are rarely told explicitly.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The process documentation carries more marks than the finished product, which surprises students every time and is the main reason good makers score moderately.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. As with design, the developmental workbook and the reflective responses carry substantial weight beside the final piece, and students who only produce work lose the criteria that reward process.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Written and reflective components matter, which regularly startles families who assume the subject is assessed on sport alone.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units and ATL skills
subjects.description: Approaches to learning skills run across every subject: research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills. Tutoring that targets self-management and research skills often raises grades across several subjects at once, which is unusual value.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed against published criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and the product. Coaching covers goal scoping, criteria interpretation and process-journal discipline. The student sets the goal, does the work, keeps the journal and writes the report.

subjects.name: Diploma bridging in mathematics
subjects.description: Indices, surds, algebraic fractions, rearranging with the unknown appearing twice, function notation and expanding without hesitation. The Diploma assumes all of it from the first week. Six to eight sessions over a summer removes most of the first-term shock.

subjects.name: Diploma bridging in writing
subjects.description: Essay structure under timed conditions, command-term discipline, and building an argument with evidence rather than with assertion. The MYP gives time and process credit; the Diploma marks the product written in two hours, and that shift catches strong MYP writers.

sections.heading: The four criteria, subject by subject, and which one usually fails
paragraphs: Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, giving thirty-two raw marks per subject before conversion to the 1 to 8 grade. The criteria are published, they have strands with descriptors, and they are the same across every IB World School running the programme. A parent who knows the four names for their child's subject can read a report properly for the first time.

They are also predictable in where they fail. In the sciences, criterion A - knowing and understanding - is usually the strongest, because it is closest to conventional content teaching. Criteria B and C, inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating, are usually the weakest, because investigation design and data evaluation are skills most schemes of work assume rather than teach. The result is a student who knows the science and scores moderately.

In mathematics the weak criterion is almost always investigating patterns, which asks a student to find a rule, express it in correct general notation and justify it. Finding the rule is the part students can do. Expressing and justifying it is the part that scores, and it responds very quickly to teaching because the structure of a good answer is consistent.

The table below sets out the criteria for the subjects families in this cluster ask about most, with the criterion that usually costs marks and what the work on it actually looks like. Ask your school for the criterion-level breakdown and read it against this table; the two together usually make the next eight sessions obvious.

sections.heading: Reading a 1 to 8 grade without guessing
paragraphs: Parents in this cluster routinely ask whether a 5 is good. The honest answer is that it depends entirely on which criteria produced it, and that is why the grade alone is close to useless for planning. Four marks out of eight across all four criteria and a pattern of 7, 7, 3, 2 can produce similar overall grades while describing entirely different students with entirely different needs.

The conversion from criterion marks to the final grade uses published boundaries, and schools apply them consistently. What varies is how many assessment tasks have contributed to each criterion by the time a report is written - some criteria may have been assessed once and others three times, which makes early-year reports noisier than later ones. Ask how many times each criterion has been assessed when a mark looks surprising.

The second thing worth asking is whether the mark reflects the most recent evidence or an average across the term. MYP practice generally favours the most recent and most consistent evidence over a simple mean, because the programme is trying to report what a student can do now. A single poor task early in a term should not still be dragging a criterion mark in May, and if it appears to be, that is a reasonable question for a parents' evening.

For families new to the programme, one reassurance and one warning. The reassurance: MYP grades are not percentages and a 5 is not 50 per cent of anything. The warning: a comfortable MYP profile does not guarantee a comfortable Diploma, because the Diploma assesses a product written under time pressure rather than a skill demonstrated over a unit. That gap is the subject of the bridging section further down.

sections.heading: Investigation design: the criterion that costs science marks
paragraphs: If a science report shows a strong criterion A and a weak criterion B, the work is investigation design, and it is some of the most satisfying tutoring in the programme because the improvement is fast and visible. Criterion B asks a student to formulate a testable research question, identify and explain the variables, design a method that controls what needs controlling, and justify the choices made.

Students fail it in consistent ways. The research question is not testable with the apparatus available. The independent and dependent variables are named and then the controlled variables are listed without any mention of how they will be held constant. The method has no range and interval justification, no repeats, or repeats with no stated reason. None of these is a content problem and all of them are correctable in a handful of sessions.

Criterion C, processing and evaluating, fails in a matching pattern. Data is presented without processing, or processed without uncertainty or spread, or graphed without a line of best fit. The evaluation section says that more repeats would have helped, which earns nothing, instead of identifying the largest source of error and proposing a specific change. Teaching that distinction once usually fixes it permanently.

This is also the clearest investment in Diploma readiness available in MYP 4 and 5. The Diploma's scientific investigation is assessed against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, worth twenty-four marks in total, and it asks for precisely the skills criteria B and C are building. A student who has been taught investigation design properly in MYP 5 starts the Diploma investigation ahead.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, scoped properly
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the MYP's largest independent undertaking and the one most likely to go wrong in a way that is visible from the outside. It is assessed against published criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and the product itself, with a process journal running throughout and a report at the end. It is also the clearest rehearsal available for the Diploma's Extended Essay.

Two failures dominate. The first is a goal too large and too vague: a student who intends to build an application, compose an album or run an event discovers in the final month that the product cannot be finished and the criteria cannot be evidenced. The remedy is a scoping conversation at the start, where the goal is tested against both assessability and the available weeks.

The second is a process journal written retrospectively. The journal is meant to be contemporaneous evidence of planning, decision-making and reflection, and a fortnight of reconstructed entries written the night before submission reads exactly like what it is. Establishing a weekly journal habit in the first month costs nothing and protects two criteria.

Our boundary here is the same as at Diploma level and worth stating plainly, because the search results this page sits in include operators who sell completed coursework. The student chooses the goal, does the work, keeps the journal and writes the report. A tutor interrogates the goal, explains what each criterion rewards, asks the questions a supervisor would ask, and comments on the student's own drafts. Nothing is supplied.

sections.heading: The MYP 5 to Diploma step, as a list rather than a warning
paragraphs: Every family in this cluster hears that the Diploma is a step up, and the statement is useless because it names nothing. The step is specific, and once it is listed it can be worked on over a summer. The MYP assesses skills against criteria with process credit and generous time; the Diploma assesses a product written in two hours against a mark scheme, which is a different activity using the same knowledge.

In mathematics the list is indices, surds, algebraic fractions, rearranging formulae with the unknown appearing twice, function notation and expanding and factorising without hesitation. The Diploma assumes all of these are automatic from the first week and then builds quickly on top of them. A student who can do them slowly will find the first Diploma term exhausting, regardless of a strong MYP 5 grade.

In writing subjects the list is essay structure under timed conditions, command-term discipline, and making an argument with evidence rather than assertion. MYP tasks reward drafting and reflection; a Diploma paper rewards a well-structured answer produced once, to time, answering precisely the command term printed on the page. Strong MYP writers are frequently caught by this, which surprises everyone including them.

In the sciences the list is the investigation skills of criteria B and C plus uncertainty handling, which the Diploma examines directly and the MYP mostly does not. Six to eight sessions across a summer covering the mathematics list and the writing list is the highest-value tutoring in this programme, and it is bought by almost nobody because the subject it helps has not started.

sections.heading: Mathematics route choice in MYP 4 and 5
paragraphs: Many MYP schools split mathematics into standard and extended routes in MYP 4, and the decision is usually made by the school at the end of MYP 3 on the basis of performance against criterion A and criterion B. It is a quiet decision with a long tail, because the extended route builds the algebraic fluency that Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level later assumes.

This is not a hard gate in the way an IGCSE tier is - a student on the standard route can still take Diploma mathematics - but the practical effect is real. The extended route spends more time on the manipulation that the Diploma treats as given, so a standard-route student aiming at Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level has more bridging to do in less time, usually in the same summer as everything else.

The question to ask the school, in MYP 3 or early MYP 4, is which route they intend, what evidence informed it, and what would change their view. Schools generally respond well to the question when it is specific. Where a move upwards is worth arguing for, the evidence is marked work at the extended route under timed conditions, and a targeted term of tutoring can produce it.

For families in this cluster the practical geography matters here too. Uptown International School in Mirdif and Universal American School in Al Warqa run the MYP, and both lead into Diploma provision - Uptown within the same school. If your child may want Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, ask the Diploma coordinator at the intended sixth form what MYP mathematics route and profile they expect, and ask while there is still time to act on the answer.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: MYP students in Dubai also carry the mandatory UAE subjects, and this catches new arrivals in this cluster more than any other part of the timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states the requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

The rules are specific. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with Arabic primary for Social Studies for Arab students and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete credential point a parent can ask about directly.

What constrains tutoring is a content rule: for these subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support for Arabic as an additional language is ordinary language teaching and freely available, and in the MYP it maps onto language acquisition phases. Help with the mandatory Islamic Education and Social Studies content needs a conversation with the school about acceptable material first.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Market rates in this emirate, each attributed to the provider publishing it and read in October 2026, with none of them an IB Gram rate. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For MYP content support that band genuinely contains usable help, which is less true at Diploma Higher Level. What it less often contains is criterion literacy.

Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one with travel runs AED 180 to 500, per Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. Published monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range.

For the MYP specifically, the sensible purchase is usually small and targeted: a term of criterion-focused sessions in one subject, or a summer bridging block, rather than an open weekly arrangement across several subjects. A tutor who cannot name the four criteria for your child's subject is selling general secondary tutoring, which may be fine and should be priced accordingly.

What we do not claim: no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE; no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is issued to training institutes with premises; no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or the IB; no guaranteed grades; and no star ratings we cannot evidence. On regulation, the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no fine schedule published.

process.title: Ask the school for the criterion breakdown
process.description: Not the report: the four criterion marks per subject. Most schools hold them and many will share them when asked directly. With those numbers a tutor can say in one session what the next eight should contain, and you can stop guessing what the overall grade means.

process.title: Name the subject and the weak criterion
process.description: A science student weak on criterion B needs investigation design; a mathematics student weak on investigating patterns needs generalisation and justification. Those are different tutors' sessions, and the breakdown makes the choice obvious instead of approximate.

process.title: Free trial lesson and a written note
process.description: A real lesson on the actual criterion in question, with the student working. Afterwards a plain written summary of what the tutor found and what a term would target. Say no and nothing further is owed.

process.title: Short, targeted blocks rather than open arrangements
process.description: A term on one criterion, a coaching block for the Personal Project, or a summer bridging block before the Diploma. The MYP rewards targeted work, and an open weekly arrangement across three subjects usually costs more and achieves less.

whyPoints.title: We work from criteria, not from the overall grade
whyPoints.description: A grade 5 built on 7, 7, 3, 2 describes a completely different student from one built on four fives. The criterion breakdown is where the actionable information sits, and asking the school for it is the first thing we suggest.

whyPoints.title: Investigation design taught, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Criteria B and C in the sciences cost more marks than criterion A, because designing an investigation and evaluating data are skills most schemes of work assume. They are also the direct rehearsal for the Diploma's twenty-four-mark investigation.

whyPoints.title: The Diploma gap named as a list
whyPoints.description: Indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation, timed essay structure, command-term discipline. 'The Diploma is a step up' is not actionable; a list that can be worked through in six to eight summer sessions is.

whyPoints.title: Personal Project scoped before it is started
whyPoints.description: The two failures are a goal too large to finish and a process journal written retrospectively. Both are prevented in the first month and neither can be fixed in the last. We question the goal and the journal; the student does all the work.

whyPoints.title: Small targeted purchases over open arrangements
whyPoints.description: A term on one criterion usually achieves more than a year of general weekly support across three subjects, and costs considerably less. We would rather say that than sell the larger arrangement.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed, claims limited
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider who published it and the month it was read. We hold no regulator approval, have no UAE premises, publish no guaranteed grades, and do not supply IB material as downloads.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB MYP tutor in Dubai International Academic City?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one-to-one online tuition rather than a tutor coming to your address, since IB Gram offers home visits only in India. Academic City itself has no MYP provision - its secondary runs the British curriculum - so families here already travel to Mirdif or Al Warqa for the programme. The relevant scarcity for MYP tutoring is not subject knowledge but criterion literacy: a tutor who cannot name the four criteria for your child's subject is offering general secondary tutoring.

faqs.question: What do the four MYP criteria mean on my child's report?
faqs.answer: Each MYP subject is assessed against four published criteria, each marked out of eight, and those four marks convert to the single grade from 1 to 8 using published boundaries. In the sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In mathematics they cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The weak criterion, not the overall grade, tells you what to work on.

faqs.question: Is a grade 5 in the MYP a good result?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which criteria produced it, which is why the grade alone is close to useless for planning. A profile of 7, 7, 3, 2 and a flat profile of fives can produce similar overall grades while describing very different students with very different needs. Ask the school for the criterion-level breakdown, and ask how many times each criterion has been assessed, because early-year reports are noisier when some criteria have been assessed once and others three times.

faqs.question: Why does my son score well on content and badly overall in science?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly criteria B and C. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is closest to conventional content teaching and is usually the strongest. Inquiring and designing asks him to formulate a testable question, identify variables and justify a method; processing and evaluating asks him to process data and evaluate method and reliability. Most schemes of work assume rather than teach those skills, so a student who knows the science scores moderately. Both respond quickly to targeted sessions.

faqs.question: Which MYP mathematics criterion do students lose most marks on?
faqs.answer: Investigating patterns, consistently. It asks a student to find a rule, express it in correct general notation and then justify it. Finding the rule is the part most students manage; expressing and justifying it is the part that scores, and it is rarely taught directly. The structure of a strong response is consistent enough that a handful of sessions produces a visible change in the criterion mark, which makes it one of the most efficient things to target in the whole programme.

faqs.question: How should the Personal Project goal be chosen?
faqs.answer: Small enough to finish and specific enough to assess, which rules out most first ideas. The two dominant failures in this cluster are a goal too large - an application, an album, an event - that cannot be completed or evidenced, and a process journal written retrospectively in the last fortnight. Both are prevented in the first month and neither can be fixed at the end. Test the goal against the published criteria and the available weeks before any work starts.

faqs.question: How far may a tutor go with a Personal Project draft and journal?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary. A tutor can interrogate the goal, explain what each criterion rewards, ask the questions a supervisor would ask, and read and comment on your child's own drafts and journal entries. A tutor cannot choose the goal, make the product, write journal entries or supply text for the report. The search results this page sits in include operators who sell completed coursework outright, and a malpractice finding from that falls on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.question: What exactly is the gap between MYP 5 and the Diploma?
faqs.answer: A list rather than a general standard. In mathematics: indices, surds, algebraic fractions, rearranging with the unknown appearing twice, function notation, and expanding without hesitation - all assumed automatic from the first Diploma week. In writing subjects: essay structure under timed conditions, command-term discipline, and argument built on specific evidence. In the sciences: investigation design and uncertainty handling. Six to eight sessions over a summer covers most of it.

faqs.question: My daughter has a strong MYP profile. Will the Diploma be fine?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and this catches confident families. The MYP assesses skills against criteria with process credit and generous time; the Diploma assesses a product written in two hours against a mark scheme. Strong MYP writers in particular are caught by the shift, because drafting and reflection earn nothing in a timed paper. The content knowledge transfers; the working conditions do not. Timed practice in the summer before the first Diploma year is the cheapest insurance available.

faqs.question: Should my child take extended rather than standard MYP mathematics?
faqs.answer: If Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is a possibility later, it is worth asking about. The extended route spends more time on the manipulation the Diploma treats as given, so a standard-route student aiming at Higher Level has more bridging to do in less time. It is not a hard gate like an IGCSE tier. Ask the school in MYP 3 or early MYP 4 which route they intend and what evidence would change their view, because marked work at the extended route is what they respond to.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic and Islamic Education in an MYP school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's guidance requiring implementation from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on 40-minute lesson units, with any mandatory-subject lesson advised to run at least 25 minutes.

faqs.question: Can we get help with Arabic as an additional language for the MYP?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it maps onto the language acquisition phases the MYP uses, which is worth knowing because students are assessed by phase rather than by year group. Two children in the same class can be working at different phases, and parents are rarely told so explicitly. Note the constraint on the mandatory subjects: for Islamic Education and Social Studies, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so ask the school what material it will accept first.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to spend on MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: Less than at Diploma level, and the sensible purchase is small and targeted. Market rates read in October 2026: budget and university-student online tutors from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from 33 to 52; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300. For MYP content the lower band genuinely contains usable help. What it less often contains is criterion literacy, which is the thing worth paying for in this programme.

faqs.question: What time can an MYP session start from Academic City on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Around 5pm, because Academic City has no MYP provision and children travel to Mirdif or Al Warqa. From Mirdif itself, where Uptown International School sits inside the district, 4.45pm works. From International City, where there is no international school at all, 6pm is the honest answer and a weekend morning is usually the better slot. Because no tutor is travelling, the only constraint is the school run, so book against the worst-case journey rather than the average one.

faqs.question: Is a permit required for someone tutoring MYP subjects privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it applies regardless of the programme or the age of the student. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Ask the person teaching your child whether they hold a current permit.

The trial lesson is free; lessons are one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-creek-harbou.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering the Middle Years Programme for families around Dubai Creek Harbour: subject-group specialists who mark against MYP criteria rather than against percentages, and who can name which criterion a student is losing marks on.

intro.heading: Why MYP tutoring money goes astray
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme is assessed by criteria, not by percentages. Each subject carries four criteria, labelled A to D, and each is marked out of eight. The four add to thirty-two, and the school converts that total into a grade from one to seven using published boundaries. A student can know the content thoroughly and still sit at a four, because the marks are leaking from a criterion that has nothing to do with recall. In mathematics that criterion is often investigating patterns or communicating. In sciences it is frequently processing and evaluating. In language and literature it is usually organising.

That is why MYP tutoring budgets leak. A Creek Harbour family sees a four on a report, buys weekly content revision, and the grade does not move, because nobody identified which of the four criteria was costing the marks. Twelve hours of competent teaching gets spent on criterion A when the problem sat in criterion C the whole time. The spend was not wasted through incompetence; it was aimed at the wrong target because the report did not make the target visible and nobody asked the school for the criterion breakdown.

So the first thing worth paying for is diagnosis, and it costs almost nothing. Ask the school for the most recent criterion-level marks: A out of eight, B out of eight, C out of eight, D out of eight, per subject. Most MYP schools record exactly that and will share it. With those four numbers in front of a tutor, the first session becomes targeted rather than exploratory, and the number of hours needed drops rather than rises. Without them, any tutor is guessing for the first month, and you are paying for the guess.

Geography is the second cost factor, and in Dubai Creek Harbour it is a sharp one. The community contains no private school, so every secondary pupil commutes out: across the Ras Al Khor crossing to Dubai Festival City, down Al Khail Road into Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba, or over the Creek to Al Jaddaf. A visiting tutor must be paid for that travel. Published in-home rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online. A real share of the gap is time in a car.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai Creek Harbour or anywhere else in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. That removes the travel line from the cost and widens the pool of tutors who have actually taught your child's subject group in the Middle Years Programme, which for MYP specifically matters more than it does for a linear examined course.

What follows is the cost case in detail: the published market rates with their sources, the four criteria per subject group and what each one actually rewards, why an MYP five is not a percentage, what the Personal Project is worth paying for early, and the honest arithmetic of paying for MYP support now against paying more in Year 12.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-creek-harbou.programmesIntro: Creek Harbour families need MYP support at three distinct stages, and the money behaves differently at each. These are the stages we cover.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, the early years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups taught with an inquiry framework, criterion-assessed internally. There is no external examination, so the grade is built entirely from classroom tasks. The habits that matter most are stated criteria awareness and the ability to read a task sheet and work out which criterion it is assessing before starting.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai these years also carry the mandatory UAE subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in all Dubai private schools alongside the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Families budgeting for tutoring should count those periods into the week first; adding a fourth evening commitment to an already full schedule is a common way to spend money without result.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: The two years where the criteria sharpen and the Personal Project arrives. Subject criteria become more demanding in the higher achievement bands, and the gap between a five and a six is usually about independence and critical thinking rather than about coverage. Some schools offer optional on-screen eAssessment and ePortfolios leading to the MYP Certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Around Dubai Creek Harbour, several schools run the Middle Years Programme to Year 11 before entering the Diploma, while neighbouring schools run IGCSE instead. That matters for a family comparing notes with friends in the same tower: a Year 11 at one school is working towards criterion-assessed tasks, and a Year 11 at another is sitting Cambridge or Pearson written papers. The tutoring is not the same job.

programmes.name: The MYP Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent project with a product and a written report, supervised in school and assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It is the closest thing the Middle Years Programme has to the Diploma's Extended Essay, and it is the component where early support is worth most and late support is worth least.
programmes.countryNote: The supervisor is a member of school staff and the work must be the student's own. A tutor may discuss scope, ask questions about the plan, explain what a criterion is asking for and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write it, restructure it to a standard, or supply the product. Providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequence lands on the candidate.

programmes.name: Looking ahead to the Diploma
programmes.description: The Diploma is examined by timed written papers plus internally assessed components. A student arriving from the Middle Years Programme has rarely sat a ninety-minute written paper, because most MYP years have no external examination. The gap that opens in Year 12 is about pace, method-writing for an unknown marker, and the absence of a resubmission.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single strongest financial argument for MYP support. Closing a criterion-level gap in MYP Year 4 costs a handful of hours. Discovering the same gap in the first term of the Diploma, with twenty per cent of a grade sitting on an Internal Assessment and a May session approaching, costs considerably more. We do not publish IB session dates on this page; the IB's own site blocks automated checking and your school's coordinator holds the authoritative calendar.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-creek-harbou.subjectsIntro: The Middle Years Programme has eight subject groups. These are the ones Creek Harbour families most often buy support for, with the criterion that most commonly costs the marks in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where the marks go, because generalising a rule and justifying it is a different skill from computing correctly, and it is rarely taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.levels: Integrated, then biology, chemistry and physics · MYP 1-5
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Processing and evaluating is the usual leak: a student collects data correctly and then does not discuss validity, anomalies or improvement.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Organising is the common loss, because a strong argument delivered in a structure the reader cannot follow caps the band. Essay planning is the cheapest intervention available in this subject.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is where a six becomes a seven: using sources to build an argument rather than to illustrate a narrative, and recognising a source's limitations.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover listening, reading, speaking and writing. The phase placement matters more than the year group, and a student moved up a phase mid-year frequently loses marks in speaking before the other three catch up.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Design is the subject where documentation carries the marks: a good product with thin process evidence scores below a modest product fully documented.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal is the assessed artefact as much as the work itself, and students who keep it weekly outperform those who assemble it at the end.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and reflective components are where marks are available to students who are not the strongest performers.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project with a product and a report, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. Scope control decides the outcome: a project narrow enough to finish and document beats an ambitious one abandoned halfway.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs in Dubai, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because for the Middle Years Programme the bottom is more often adequate than it is for an examined course. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is advertised from AED 33 to AED 52 by Tutopiya and from AED 45 to AED 65 by EdFlik, which usually means a tutor who studied the subject recently. For a Year 7 or Year 8 student who needs a concept unblocked, that can be entirely sufficient, and buying a specialist at four times the rate would be waste.

The tier above is where MYP support usually belongs. A qualified subject tutor online in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. What the extra money buys in an MYP context is specific and checkable: a tutor who can read a criterion descriptor, say which band a piece of work currently sits in, and explain the difference between that band and the one above. A tutor who cannot do that is being paid a specialist rate for general teaching.

Above that sit specialist rates of roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's specialist band at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, and a premium tier where BartyED publishes AED 650. For the Middle Years Programme, those rates are rarely the right purchase, with one exception: Personal Project supervision support in Year 5, where experience of the criteria genuinely matters. Every figure here belongs to the provider named and was read in October 2026. None of it is IB Gram's price list.

The in-home line is the one Creek Harbour geography makes expensive. Visiting rates run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, and a real portion of the premium is travel across Ras Al Khor or down Al Khail Road at the school-run hour. IB Gram does not visit UAE addresses at all, so that line does not exist in our model. We publish no hourly figure here, because the right number depends on subject group, criterion and stage, and one printed rate would mislead most readers. The free trial lesson comes first.

sections.heading: Where the money actually leaks
paragraphs: The commonest waste in MYP tutoring is buying content revision for a criterion problem. A report shows a four in sciences. The family buys weekly science support. The tutor teaches the unit content competently for a term. The grade stays at four, because the marks were leaking from processing and evaluating, where the student collects data correctly and then writes nothing about anomalies, validity or improvement. No amount of content teaching reaches that. One session on how to write an evaluation paragraph does.

The second leak is buying hours before asking the school for the criterion breakdown. Most MYP schools record each criterion out of eight and will share it on request. Those four numbers per subject convert a vague worry into a specific target, and they are free. A family that buys twelve hours first and asks for the marks later has paid for a month of exploration that a single email would have made unnecessary.

The third is session timing, which is a cost question rather than a convenience one. A Creek Harbour student commuting from Nad Al Sheba is not home until well after 16:30, and a session at 18:30 after homework delivers materially fewer useful minutes than the same hour at 17:00. If you are paying a fixed rate per hour, the usable fraction of that hour is the real unit price. A weekend morning session at the same rate is cheaper in those terms than any weekday evening.

The fourth is buying support in three subjects at once because the report showed three fours. In the Middle Years Programme the criteria repeat across subject groups in recognisable forms: organising in language and literature, communicating in mathematics, and documenting process in design are all versions of the same underlying skill. Fixing it in one subject frequently moves the other two without a single hour being bought for them, and that is the most reliable saving available in this market.

sections.heading: The four criteria, out of eight, and what each one rewards
paragraphs: Here is the thing no competitor in this market publishes: the criteria by letter, per subject group, with what each one actually rewards. It is the specification for the entire grade, and a parent who has read it can hold a useful conversation with both the school and a tutor. Every subject group has four criteria, each marked from zero to eight, summing to thirty-two before the school converts to a one-to-seven grade.

Read across the table and the pattern becomes obvious. Criterion A is almost always knowledge and understanding, and it is the one most families assume is the problem. Criteria B, C and D are process, communication and evaluation in various forms, and together they carry twenty-four of the thirty-two marks. Three quarters of the available marks are therefore for things that are not recall, which is the single most useful fact a parent can hold when deciding what to buy.

It also explains why the same student can score differently across subjects that feel equally hard. A student strong on recall and weak on written structure will sit higher in mathematics criterion A than in language and literature criterion B, and the report will show two different grades for what is really one skill gap. Identifying the shared skill is what turns three tutoring purchases into one.

The practical move is to ask the school for the criterion marks, find the lowest letter across subjects, and start there. Not the lowest grade, the lowest letter. That is where the marks are, and it is usually cheaper to address than a content gap because the skill is teachable in a handful of sessions rather than a term.

sections.heading: Why an MYP five is not sixty-two per cent
paragraphs: Parents arriving in the Middle Years Programme from a percentage-based system frequently try to convert, and the conversion does not exist in a useful form. The grade comes from the sum of four criteria out of eight, converted through boundaries the school publishes, and the boundaries are not evenly spaced. Moving from a five to a six can require two extra marks in one place and four in another depending on where the current marks sit, which is why a single criterion can be worth a whole grade.

The practical consequence for a tutoring budget is large. If a student sits at seven out of eight on criteria A, B and D and at three on criterion C, the whole grade is being held down by one letter, and two marks on that letter may lift the grade. That is a short block of work with a clear finish line. If the same student sits at five across all four criteria, there is no single lever, and the honest answer is a longer and more expensive programme or a decision to accept the grade and spend the money elsewhere.

This is also why comparing a child's MYP grade with a neighbour's IGCSE grade is not informative, even for two Year 11 students living in the same Creek Harbour tower. One is a criterion sum converted through internal boundaries; the other is a written paper against a published mark scheme and national grade boundaries. Families compare them constantly and draw conclusions from a comparison that does not hold.

Ask the school two questions and the picture clears. First, the criterion marks out of eight for each subject. Second, the boundary table used for conversion. With both in hand, a tutor can say what two marks on a named criterion are worth in grade terms, and you can decide whether that is worth buying. Without them, nobody in the conversation knows what the money would buy.
