sections.heading: The Personal Project: buy early, and know where the line is
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP Year 5 is an independent project with a product and a written report, supervised by a member of school staff and assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It is the closest the Middle Years Programme comes to the Diploma's Extended Essay, and the economics of supporting it are unusually clear: bought early it is a handful of hours, bought late it becomes an expensive salvage operation.

The reason is scope. Almost every Personal Project that goes wrong goes wrong because it was too ambitious to finish and document in the time available. A student who wanted to build something substantial arrives in the final weeks with an incomplete product and no process evidence, and the criteria reward documented process heavily. Two hours of scope conversation before the project begins prevents the outcome that twelve hours at the end cannot repair.

This is also the component where the academic honesty line gets tested, so we put it in writing before starting. A tutor may discuss scope, ask questions about a plan, explain what a criterion is asking for in plain language, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write the report, restructure it to a standard, or supply the product. There are providers in this market selling completed Internal Assessments outright; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than the seller. We keep a session note recording whose work was in front of us.

For a Creek Harbour family the practical advice is to buy two or three sessions in the term the project is introduced, not in the term it is due. It is the single best value purchase in the whole programme, and it is almost always bought at the wrong time.

sections.heading: Paying now or paying more in Year 12
paragraphs: The strongest financial argument for MYP support has nothing to do with the MYP grade. It is that the Middle Years Programme is internally assessed with revisable tasks and the Diploma is not. Most MYP years have no external examination at all, so a student can reach Year 12 with a strong record and no experience of a ninety-minute written paper marked by someone who has never met them, with no opportunity to resubmit.

What then happens in the first term of the Diploma is predictable. The content is manageable; the pace under timed conditions is not. Method is written for a teacher who already understands the student rather than for an unknown marker. A first assessment comes back well below expectation, the family buys emergency support at specialist rates with a May session approaching, and the cost of the same gap is several times what it would have been in MYP Year 4.

Two MYP components prepare a student directly for this, and both are cheap to strengthen. Investigating patterns in mathematics maps almost exactly onto the Diploma's mathematical Exploration, which is worth twenty per cent of the final maths grade. Processing and evaluating in sciences maps onto the science Internal Assessment. A student who learned to generalise, justify and reflect in Year 10 meets those components already competent. A student whose MYP investigations were completed quickly to a template meets them for the first time with a fifth of a grade attached.
The table sets the two programmes against each other on the things that cost money, which is a comparison families in Creek Harbour make informally all the time and rarely see written down.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits, and what a Creek Harbour parent should check before paying
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with the International Baccalaureate at seven per cent of enrolment, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. Seven new private schools join for the 2026-27 intake, three of them IB.

None of that is an endorsement of any tutoring provider. A KHDA inspection rating judges a school. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises and staff, and we do not hold one. If a provider implies regulator endorsement before taking your money, treat that as a reason to check their other claims.

Tutoring is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The route is MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, with no fee and a stated two working days. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

One boundary specific to the Middle Years Programme. A Creek Harbour parent may consider paying their child's own subject teacher, who also marks the criteria and supervises the Personal Project. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The person assessing the work should not be separately paid by one family in the class.

sections.heading: Getting started, and the cheapest honest starting point
paragraphs: The cheapest first step costs nothing. Email the school and ask for the criterion-level marks, A to D out of eight, for the subjects you are worried about, plus the boundary table used to convert them into a grade. Send those to us with the subject group, the MYP year, and two evening windows that survive a normal school run from Creek Harbour. With those numbers the first session is targeted rather than exploratory, and the number of hours needed usually goes down.

Then we match a subject-group specialist and run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep. One trial per student, nothing charged beforehand, no card details required to book it. The tutor writes a short note naming which criterion they would address first and what evidence would show it has moved. That note is the thing to judge the arrangement by, more than the lesson itself.

If no specialist is free in your window we will say so, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing whoever is available. The thinnest coverage is in design, arts and language acquisition at specific phases, and in the weeks when Personal Project deadlines cluster. Weekend mornings widen the choice considerably, because the weekday window from 17:00 to 19:00 Gulf Standard Time is the busiest hour in the UAE tutoring day.

Two limits stated plainly. Nobody can promise a grade and this page does not. And nothing here implies that tutoring is required for progression, for the MYP Certificate, for Diploma entry or for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency; those are school and regulatory processes with their own published rules, and the authority rather than a tutoring provider is where to verify them.

faqs.question: How much does MYP tutoring cost for a family in Dubai Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: The published market spread is wide. Budget online tutoring is advertised from AED 33 to AED 52 by Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 by EdFlik; a qualified subject tutor online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200; specialist rates run from AED 200 to AED 450 or more. Those figures belong to the providers named and were read in October 2026. For most Middle Years Programme work the qualified tier is the right purchase, and the specialist tier is justified mainly for Personal Project support.

faqs.question: Why has weekly MYP revision not moved my child's grade at all?
faqs.answer: Most likely because the marks are leaking from a criterion that content revision cannot reach. Every MYP subject has four criteria marked out of eight, and criteria B, C and D carry twenty-four of the thirty-two marks between them. Those are process, communication and evaluation skills rather than recall. A student can know the unit thoroughly and still sit at a four because no evaluation paragraph was written. Ask the school for the criterion marks, find the low letter, and target that instead.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's MYP school for before I pay for any tutoring?
faqs.answer: Two things, both free. First, the criterion-level marks for each subject: A out of eight, B out of eight, C out of eight, D out of eight. Most MYP schools record exactly that. Second, the boundary table the school uses to convert the thirty-two-mark total into a grade from one to seven. With both in hand, a tutor can tell you what two marks on a named criterion are worth in grade terms, and you can judge whether that is worth buying before committing any money.

faqs.question: Does an MYP grade of five convert into a percentage I can compare?
faqs.answer: Not usefully. The grade is the sum of four criteria out of eight, converted through boundaries the school publishes, and those boundaries are not evenly spaced. Moving from a five to a six might need two extra marks in one position and four in another. That is also why comparing an MYP grade with a neighbour's IGCSE grade is uninformative, even between two Year 11 students in the same Creek Harbour tower: one is a converted criterion sum, the other a written paper against national boundaries.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion is most often the one costing marks?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject group in a consistent way. In mathematics it is usually investigating patterns, because generalising and justifying a rule is a different skill from computing correctly and is rarely taught explicitly. In sciences it is processing and evaluating, where data is collected well and then discussed thinly. In language and literature it is organising, where a sound argument in an unfollowable structure caps the band. Those three are versions of the same underlying skill, which is why fixing one often moves the others.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to buy support in one subject or in all the weak ones?
faqs.answer: One, almost always, and then reassess. MYP criteria repeat across subject groups as recognisable forms of the same skill: organising in language and literature, communicating in mathematics, and documenting process in design are all structured communication. A student who learns to plan and structure written work in one subject frequently gains marks in two others without an hour being bought for them. Buying three subjects at once because the report showed three fours is the most common avoidable cost in this market.

faqs.question: When is the right time to pay for Personal Project help?
faqs.answer: In the term the project is introduced, not the term it is due. Almost every Personal Project that goes wrong does so because the scope was too ambitious to finish and document, and the criteria reward documented process heavily. Two or three hours of scope and planning conversation at the start prevents an outcome that twelve hours at the end cannot repair. It is the best value purchase in the whole programme and it is usually bought several months too late.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line on Personal Project support that a Dubai school would accept?
faqs.answer: No, and you should decline any offer. A tutor may discuss scope, ask questions about the plan, explain what a criterion is asking for in plain language, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write the report, restructure it to a standard, or supply the product. Providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the candidate. We keep a session note recording whose work was in front of us at each session.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our Creek Harbour apartment for MYP sessions?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one tuition for UAE families online over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to any UAE address; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. Dubai agencies that do visit publish rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, and a real share of that premium is travel. Removing it also widens the pool of tutors who have taught your child's actual subject group.

faqs.question: What time should an MYP session start from Dubai Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: As early as the commute allows, because a late session delivers fewer usable minutes at the same hourly price. A student at a Dubai Festival City school is generally home by 16:00 if the Ras Al Khor crossing is clear, making 16:45 workable. Sobha Hartland sits better at 17:00 and Nad Al Sheba at 17:15 or later. Choose the slot for the worst normal weekday rather than the best, and take a weekend morning if one is available, because it is the cheapest hour in real terms.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP into the Diploma next year. Is support worth buying now?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and for a specific reason. Most MYP years have no external examination, so a student can reach Year 12 with a strong record and no experience of a timed written paper marked by someone who has never met them, with no resubmission available. Two MYP components prepare them directly: investigating patterns in mathematics maps onto the Diploma's Exploration, worth twenty per cent of the maths grade, and processing and evaluating in sciences maps onto the science Internal Assessment. Both are cheap to strengthen now.

faqs.question: Which schools near Dubai Creek Harbour run the Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: No private school sits inside Dubai Creek Harbour itself. Swiss International Scientific School Dubai is immediately across the Creek in Al Jaddaf, and Universal American School Dubai is in Dubai Festival City. South along Al Khail Road, North London Collegiate School Dubai in Sobha Hartland and GEMS Modern Academy in Nad Al Sheba both run IB programmes. KHDA reported the International Baccalaureate at seven per cent of Dubai private enrolment in 2024-25. Schools are named here as market context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: Do we also need to budget for Arabic and Islamic Education alongside MYP?
faqs.answer: Count them into the week before adding anything. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. KHDA also calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. A student already carrying those periods plus MYP subjects has limited evening capacity, and overloading it is a reliable way to spend money without result.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram accredited by the International Baccalaureate or by KHDA?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. KHDA is Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority and is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; it regulates and inspects schools. A KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises and staff. Any provider implying regulator endorsement before taking payment is giving you a reason to check their other claims.

faqs.question: What happens if no MYP specialist is free in our evening slot?
faqs.answer: We say so, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing whoever is available. Coverage is thinnest in design, arts and language acquisition at particular phases, and in the weeks when Personal Project deadlines cluster across schools. The alternatives are a different time slot, a shorter block with a specialist whose availability is limited, or starting on the shared skill in a subject where a tutor is free. Weekend mornings widen the choice more than any other scheduling change.

intro.heading: Why MYP tutoring goes wrong, and what to ask instead
paragraphs: An MYP report arrives with a 1 to 7 grade and four letters beside it, and most parents read the grade and ignore the letters. The letters are the useful part. Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each marked on a scale from 1 to 8, and the totals are converted to the reported grade using boundaries published in the subject guide. A student can be strong on two criteria and weak on two and come out with a middling grade that explains nothing.

This is where tutoring in Dubai routinely misfires. A parent sees a grade 4 in sciences and books a science tutor, who teaches the current unit thoroughly. The student's knowledge improves and the grade does not move, because the marks were being lost on the criterion covering inquiry and design, or on the one covering reflection on the impact of science, and nobody looked. Three months of competent teaching aimed at the wrong criterion is a real and common outcome.

So the question to ask a prospective tutor is not whether they know the subject. It is whether they can name the four criteria for that subject and say what each one assesses. A tutor who has taught MYP answers in a sentence. A tutor who has taught middle school generally will talk about the subject instead, which is the tell. You do not need any knowledge of the programme yourself to hear the difference, which is why this page is built around questions.

There is also a scarcity point worth being honest about. The International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of private school enrolment in Dubai in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum and 26 per cent Indian, so the MYP teaching pool is a small slice of a large market. Applying a driving radius to that slice, and then an available after-school hour, leaves very few people in the eastern suburbs who have actually marked against these criteria.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Al Badia, Festival Boulevard, Nad Al Hamar and Mirdif the delivery is live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason that matters for MYP specifically is that the useful session involves reading the student's own marked work against a criterion descriptor, and a shared screen puts the task sheet, the rubric and the student's attempt side by side for both people.

What follows is the detail: the eight subject groups and the criteria each uses, how the 1 to 8 marks become a 1 to 7 grade, how the Community Project and Personal Project timelines work, what MYP eAssessment is, and where the real gap sits when a student moves from MYP into the Diploma.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-festival-cit.programmesIntro: MYP spans five years and changes substantially across them, and what tutoring should do differs at each end. These are the stages that matter for a Dubai Festival City family.

programmes.name: MYP Years 1 to 3, roughly Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The years where criterion-referenced habits are formed. Students meet the four-criteria structure, learn what an inquiry question looks like, and either do or do not develop the habit of reflecting on their own work in writing. The Community Project typically sits at the end of this phase, in MYP 3 or 4 depending on the school.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest and most effective place for a Dubai Festival City family to intervene, because nothing is at stake in certificate terms and the habits built here carry into MYP 5 and then into the Diploma. A term aimed at how to write a reflection is a small purchase with a long return.

programmes.name: MYP Years 4 and 5, roughly Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Subjects become more demanding and the criteria descriptors expect more independence. The Personal Project runs through MYP 5 and is assessed against its own criteria. Schools that enter students for MYP eAssessment do so at the end of MYP 5, leading to the IB MYP Certificate for those who meet the requirements.
programmes.countryNote: This is also where the Diploma route is effectively decided, because standard and extended mathematics streams in MYP 4 and 5 feed into Applications and Interpretation and Analysis and Approaches respectively. A family thinking about Higher Level mathematics should be asking about the stream now rather than in Year 11.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, after MYP
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The step up is less about content than about external examination technique, which MYP does not emphasise, and about mathematical fluency, which MYP assesses but does not drill.
programmes.countryNote: Deira International School runs the IB continuum through to the Diploma, so a Dubai Festival City student may move from MYP 5 to DP1 within the same campus. That continuity helps, and it also means the transition gap is sometimes assumed to be smaller than it is, particularly in mathematics and in written science explanations.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside MYP
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA required these arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. Support in these subjects works from the school's approved material, because using different or additional content needs prior Ministry permission.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-festival-cit.subjectsIntro: These are the MYP subject groups, with what the criteria in each actually ask for. Pick your child's weakest two and ask any prospective tutor to talk about the criteria rather than the topic.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Students lose bands on analysing, because they summarise what a text says rather than examining how it achieves its effect. A tutor who marks against the descriptor rather than reading for general quality is what moves this.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Students are placed in phases rather than year groups, so the first useful question is which phase your child is in, not which year.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. Thinking critically is where most bands are lost: a student presents two views and does not evaluate them, which is a specific omission rather than a general weakness.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The last of those surprises parents most, and it is assessed, so a student who writes nothing about impact leaves a whole criterion scoring low.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students with strong arithmetic routinely lose bands on investigating patterns, because generalising and justifying a rule is a different skill from calculating.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Design is the subject where process documentation carries the marks, so a good final product with a thin design folder scores badly, which frustrates capable students every year.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. As in Design, the process journal is heavily weighted, and students who produce strong work without documenting how they got there lose bands they cannot recover later.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Written planning and reflection are assessed alongside performance, which is why a strong athlete can still receive a middling grade.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project with its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It runs across MYP 5 with a supervisor at the school. Support means supervision, questioning and feedback on the student's own process journal, never contributing to the product or the report.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units assessed against their own criteria covering evaluating, synthesising and reflecting across two or more subject groups. Students often treat these as a double workload rather than a distinct assessment, which costs bands in the synthesising criterion specifically.

regions.note: Closest to Deira International School, which runs the IB continuum, so local tutors here are the likeliest in the cluster to have encountered MYP criteria. That is a low bar and still the best local position available in eastern Dubai.

sections.heading: Reading an MYP report properly
paragraphs: Take the report and find the four criterion marks for the subject you are worried about. Each is on a 1 to 8 scale. Add them and you have a total, usually out of 32 in a subject with four criteria, which the school converts to the reported 1 to 7 grade using boundaries published in the subject guide. Your child's teacher holds that guide and can show you the boundary table; we do not reproduce board documents, so ask for the school's copy.

The pattern in the four marks is the whole diagnosis. A student with marks of 7, 6, 3 and 3 and a student with 5, 5, 5, 4 may receive similar grades and have entirely different problems. The first has two specific weaknesses that can be named and taught. The second is uniformly middling and needs something broader. Booking a subject tutor without looking at this distinction is how families spend a term on the wrong thing.

The criterion names are the next layer. In sciences, a low mark on the criterion covering inquiring and designing is a different problem from a low mark on the one covering reflecting on the impacts of science. The first means the student does not know how to frame a testable question or plan a method; the second means they are writing nothing at all about implications, which is often simply because nobody told them it was assessed.

This is why the first useful session in MYP tutoring is frequently a reading session rather than a teaching session. An hour spent going through the report and two or three marked tasks against the descriptors tells a parent more than a term of content coverage, and it is cheap because it is one hour. Several families go no further than that, which is a perfectly good outcome and the reason the free trial lesson exists.

sections.heading: The eight subject groups and what their criteria ask for
paragraphs: MYP organises learning into eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, physical and health education, and design. Each group has its own four criteria with its own descriptors, and the four are not variations on knowing the subject. They separate knowledge from process, from communication, and from reflection or application.

The practical consequence is that a student can be excellent at a subject and middling at the subject as MYP assesses it. The clearest example is design, where process documentation carries substantial weight: a student who builds a good solution and keeps a thin design folder scores badly, and no amount of making better things will fix it. Arts works similarly through the process journal. Capable students find this genuinely unfair until it is explained to them.

Mathematics has its own version of the mismatch. The criterion covering investigating patterns asks the student to generalise a rule and justify it, which is a different activity from calculating accurately. A student with fluent arithmetic and no experience of writing a justification will lose a band there consistently, and the repair is short and specific rather than a term of mathematics teaching.

Sciences has the criterion parents least expect, covering reflection on the impacts of science. It is assessed, it has its own descriptor, and students who write nothing about implications are leaving an entire criterion at the bottom of the scale. In most cases this is not inability; it is that nobody explained that a paragraph about impact was required. One session fixes it permanently.

sections.heading: Questions that reveal whether a tutor knows MYP
paragraphs: Because MYP is the least widely understood of the three programmes, credential claims are the least informative here. Ask about the structure instead. A tutor who has taught and marked MYP answers these quickly. One who has taught middle school generally will answer about the subject, which is the distinction you are listening for and which requires no knowledge of the programme on your part.

Start with four. Name the four criteria for this subject and say what each assesses. What is each criterion marked out of? How does a school convert those marks to the reported grade? And which criterion do students in this subject most often lose bands on, and why? A specialist produces concrete answers; a generalist produces reassurance.

Then the programme-level questions. What is the difference between the Community Project and the Personal Project, and when does each sit? What is an interdisciplinary unit assessed on? What is MYP eAssessment and does this school use it? And what would you do with my child's process journal, exactly? That last one matters, because the honest answer is read it and ask questions, never write in it.

Finally the operational ones, which apply to any tutor in the UAE. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which u.ae states is granted free of charge for two years? Will you teach every session or could it be reassigned? And what would make you tell me you are not the right tutor for this student? Write the answers down, because a week later every provider sounds alike in memory.

sections.heading: The Community Project and the Personal Project
paragraphs: MYP carries two independent projects. The Community Project usually sits in MYP 3 or MYP 4 depending on the school and is linked to service in the community. The Personal Project runs through MYP 5 and is the larger of the two, with its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, and a supervisor appointed at the school. Both are assessed, and both depend heavily on documentation rather than on the visible outcome.

That emphasis on documentation is the thing families most often discover too late. A student who builds something impressive and keeps no process journal has very little evidence to be assessed against, and the journal cannot be reconstructed convincingly at the end. Establishing the journal habit in the first weeks is therefore worth more than any amount of help later, and it costs almost nothing because it is a routine rather than a skill.

The second common failure is a goal too large to achieve or document in the time available. A Personal Project goal chosen for ambition rather than feasibility produces a thin report regardless of effort, because the criteria reward evidence of planning and reflection rather than scale. Narrowing the goal is a single conversation at the start, and it is the highest-value support available on either project.

The boundary here is strict and it is where this market most often bends. A tutor may discuss the goal, explain each criterion, ask the questions a good supervisor would ask, model a comparable project on a different topic, read what the student has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation. A tutor may not contribute to the product, draft the report, or write in the process journal. The project is the student's own work and is declared as such.

sections.heading: MYP eAssessment and the MYP Certificate
paragraphs: Some schools enter MYP 5 students for MYP eAssessment, which combines on-screen examinations with moderated ePortfolios and can lead to the IB MYP Certificate for students who meet the requirements. Others do not, and report MYP grades internally instead. Which applies to your child's school changes what MYP 5 looks like substantially, and many parents do not know which they are in.

Where eAssessment applies, MYP 5 acquires an external examination element that the rest of the programme does not have, and that is a different kind of preparation: timed, on-screen, with its own question styles. A student who has been assessed only through coursework-style tasks for four years meets a new format in the final year, and the useful tutoring there is practice with the format rather than more content.

Where eAssessment does not apply, MYP 5 remains criterion-referenced throughout and the Personal Project is the main set-piece. In that case the sensible tutoring focus is the criterion profile and the project, and there is no examination technique to build until DP1. Buying examination practice in that situation is spending on a skill that is not being assessed.

So ask the school one question: does this school enter students for MYP eAssessment and the MYP Certificate? The answer is a single line and it reshapes the whole MYP 5 plan. It is also a useful test of a prospective tutor, because somebody who has worked in MYP schools in Dubai will know that practice varies and will ask you the same question before proposing anything.

sections.heading: The MYP to Diploma gap, subject by subject
paragraphs: Students moving from MYP 5 into DP1 generally arrive with good inquiry instincts and two specific weaknesses. The first is mathematical fluency: MYP assesses mathematics against criteria including real-life application, and it does not drill algebraic manipulation to automaticity. A student who reaches the Diploma unable to rearrange formulae without hesitation will feel Analysis and Approaches as a sudden difficulty rather than a gradual one.

The second is examination technique. Unless the school uses eAssessment, an MYP student may have had very little experience of timed external papers with mark schemes behind them. The Diploma is substantially externally examined, and command terms, working-out conventions and time management are all new skills rather than improved ones. This is the gap that most often produces a disappointing first DP1 report in a capable student.

On the other side, MYP students usually arrive better prepared than their peers for internal assessment work. Four years of criterion-referenced tasks, process journals and reflection means the Diploma's internal assessments and the Extended Essay feel familiar in structure, even where the content is harder. That is a genuine advantage and worth saying, because the transition is often described as uniformly difficult when it is actually uneven.

For tutoring, the implication is about timing and target. The useful purchase is in the spring and summer between MYP 5 and DP1, aimed at mathematical fluency and at what a timed paper requires. That is a short, well-defined window and a cheap intervention relative to rescuing a Higher Level subject in DP2. It is also the window almost nobody uses, because nothing is failing yet.

sections.heading: Verifying the person, and the regulator map
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

No schedule of fine amounts is published anywhere official, so this page quotes none and you should treat any figure you read elsewhere as unverified. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time through the smart app, website and e-services system. Because the permit is free, a tutor without one has saved nothing by skipping it.

Regulation of schools sits with the emirate. In Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulate private education in those emirates, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

A provider that calls itself KHDA approved is not offering a loose compliment; it is invoking a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai and requires annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, holds no IB accreditation, and does not claim either. Ask every provider you consider the same question and compare the answers rather than the adjectives.

A tutor may question, explain criteria, model a comparable project on a different topic, read what the student has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation. faqs.question: What do the four letters on my child's MYP report in Dubai actually mean?
faqs.answer: They are the four criteria that every MYP subject is assessed against, each marked on a 1 to 8 scale. The school adds those marks and converts the total to the reported 1 to 7 grade using boundaries published in the subject guide, which your child's teacher holds. The pattern across the four is the useful information: two high and two low marks point to specific nameable weaknesses, while four middling marks usually indicate something broader, often written communication.

faqs.question: Why has content tutoring not moved my child's MYP science grade?
faqs.answer: Most likely because the lost marks sit in a criterion the tutoring never touched. MYP sciences separates knowing and understanding from inquiring and designing, from processing and evaluating, and from reflecting on the impacts of science. A student can improve their knowledge considerably and still score at the bottom of the reflecting criterion because they are writing nothing about impacts at all. Nobody had told them it was assessed, and one session usually fixes it permanently.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a Dubai Festival City tutor really knows MYP?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the four criteria for your child's subject and say what each assesses. Ask what each criterion is marked out of and how a school converts those marks to the reported grade. Ask which criterion students in that subject most often lose bands on. A tutor who has marked MYP answers in sentences with specifics; one who has taught middle school generally answers about the subject instead, which is the distinction you are listening for.

faqs.question: Is there an MYP tutor near Al Badia or Mirdif who understands the criteria?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the pool is genuinely small. IB enrolment was 7 per cent of Dubai's private school market in 2024-25, so the MYP teaching workforce is a thin slice of a large market, and applying a driving radius plus an available after-school hour reduces it further. Al Badia and Mirdif are the best-placed communities in this corridor because both sit near IB continuum schools. Elsewhere in the eastern suburbs, local supply for criterion-referenced work is sparse.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Community Project and the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: The Community Project usually sits in MYP 3 or MYP 4 depending on the school and is linked to service in the community. The Personal Project runs through MYP 5, is the larger of the two, and is assessed against its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a supervisor appointed at the school. Both depend heavily on documentation rather than on the visible outcome, which is the thing families most often discover too late to act on.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with the MYP Personal Project?
faqs.answer: With questioning and feedback, yes; with producing it, never. A tutor may help narrow the goal to something achievable and documentable, explain each criterion, ask the questions a good supervisor would ask, model a comparable project on an unrelated topic, and read what the student has written and say where it falls short. A tutor may not contribute to the product, draft the report or write in the process journal. The project is declared as the student's own work.

faqs.question: Does a tutor visit homes in Nad Al Hamar for MYP lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For MYP the online format suits the work particularly well, because the useful session involves reading the student's own marked task against the criterion descriptor. A shared screen puts the task sheet, the rubric and the attempt side by side at the same magnification for both people, which is awkward to arrange across a kitchen table.

faqs.question: My child is good at design but gets a middling MYP grade. Why?
faqs.answer: Because in MYP design the process documentation carries substantial weight alongside the solution itself. The criteria separate inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating, so a strong final product with a thin design folder scores badly. Capable students find this genuinely unfair until it is explained. The repair is establishing folder habits early in a unit rather than reconstructing documentation afterwards, which cannot be done convincingly.

faqs.question: Does our school enter students for MYP eAssessment, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because practice varies across Dubai and it reshapes the final year. Where eAssessment applies, MYP 5 gains an external on-screen examination element with moderated ePortfolios, leading to the IB MYP Certificate for students who meet the requirements, and examination technique becomes worth practising. Where it does not, MYP 5 remains criterion-referenced throughout and the Personal Project is the main set-piece, so examination practice would be spending on an unassessed skill.

faqs.question: What is the real gap between MYP 5 and DP1 for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: Two things. Algebraic fluency, because MYP assesses mathematics against criteria including real-life application but does not drill manipulation to automaticity, so a student may reach the Diploma unable to rearrange formulae without hesitation. And timed examination technique, which MYP rarely requires unless the school uses eAssessment. On the other side, MYP students usually arrive unusually well prepared for internal assessment and reflective writing, which is a real advantage.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai Festival City family buy MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do, and in smaller amounts. MYP 1 to 3 is where criterion-referenced habits form and nothing is at stake in certificate terms, so a term aimed at how to write a reflection or a justification is a small purchase with a long return. The other high-value window is the spring and summer between MYP 5 and DP1, aimed at algebraic fluency and timed papers, which almost nobody uses because nothing has failed yet.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in MYP maths despite good arithmetic?
faqs.answer: Almost always on the criterion covering investigating patterns, which asks the student to generalise a rule and justify it. That is a different activity from calculating accurately, and a student who has never been taught to write a justification will lose a band there consistently while getting the numbers right. The repair is short and specific: a four to six session block on generalising and justifying, using the student's own marked tasks as the material.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education affect an MYP timetable in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They occupy school timetable space, yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and a prohibition on combining the two groups. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Support in these subjects works from the school's approved material, because using different or additional content requires prior Ministry permission.

The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published. Since it costs nothing, ask the question directly.

faqs.question: What should one MYP tutoring session realistically achieve?
faqs.answer: Quite a lot, if it is spent reading rather than teaching. An hour going through the report and two or three marked tasks against the criterion descriptors will usually identify which strand is costing the grade and why. That is often the whole of what a family needs, and the student and the school can act on it without further paid lessons. Where more is needed, it should be a block aimed at that one criterion rather than general subject cover.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-harbour.tutorsIntro: Our MYP tutors work criterion by criterion, which is what mid-programme arrivals most often need, because the content is rarely the obstacle and the way the work is assessed almost always is.

intro.heading: Arriving in the middle of a programme that assesses differently
paragraphs: Dubai Harbour is a new district and its towers filled quickly, with families moving in from many different school systems. A large share of the Middle Years Programme students living here did not start the programme. They joined it in Year 8, or Year 9, or Year 10, from an American middle school, a national curriculum, a British Key Stage 3 or another international system, and they joined a form of assessment nobody explained to them.

That matters because the programme does not mark out of a hundred. Each subject is assessed against four published criteria, each scored from zero to eight, and the school converts the criterion profile into a grade from one to seven using a boundary table it publishes itself. A student arriving with strong content knowledge from a system that tested recall will often receive a middling grade in their first term, not because they know less but because two of the four criteria are asking for things they have never been asked to produce.

The specific demands vary by subject group. Mathematics asks students to investigate patterns and generalise them. Sciences ask them to design an inquiry and evaluate their own method. Language and literature asks for a deliberately organised response rather than a well-written one. Individuals and societies asks for a judgement supported by evidence rather than a balanced account. A student from a recall-based system can meet none of those in their first term while knowing the content perfectly well.

The practicalities are shaped by the district. Dubai Harbour is built around a cruise terminal and marina berths, approached through one corridor off King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street shared with Emaar Beachfront and the Palm Jumeirah approach. There is no school and no tuition centre inside it. Children travel to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah, leaving before 07:00 and returning after 15:30. MYP work is often project-shaped and needs longer blocks than revision does. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

What follows compares the programme with the middle-school models students here arrive from, sets out what each kind of arrival typically finds hard, explains the components that sit alongside subjects and are frequently ignored until they cost marks, describes what the final MYP year produces, and says why criterion-literate tutors are scarcer than content tutors. Confirm your own school's criterion boundaries and reporting practice, because conversion tables are set at school level rather than by the IB.

One more framing point, because it affects what is worth buying. A first set of middling MYP reports after a mid-year move is not evidence about a child's ability, and treating it as such is the most common and most expensive error families make here. It is evidence about which demands are unfamiliar, and that is a short, cheap piece of work rather than a long one. Ask for the criterion breakdown before drawing any conclusion from a grade.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-harbour.programmesIntro: Arriving mid-programme means landing at a particular point in a five-year sequence, and what the student needs depends heavily on which point. These are the stages families here write to us from.

programmes.name: Years 7 and 8
programmes.description: Criterion marking is introduced and the demands are still modest: clear explanation and accurate content satisfy most descriptors. This is the cheapest point at which to arrive, because a student has two or three years to build the investigation and reflection habits before the descriptors escalate.
programmes.countryNote: Children arriving in this district at this stage usually settle academically within a term. The difficulty tends to be social and logistical rather than academic, and a tutor should say so rather than manufacture a problem.

programmes.name: Year 9, the switching point
programmes.description: Descriptors begin asking for generalisation and justification, and accurate students who never generalise start to plateau. It is also the year in which several schools serving this district decide whether to continue the programme or switch the cohort to IGCSE at 16.
programmes.countryNote: Establish which route your school intends before investing in criterion-specific coaching, because the criteria stop applying at a switch and examination technique becomes the thing to build instead.

programmes.name: Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: The hardest point to arrive at. Extended tasks run over weeks, documentation requirements appear, and the Personal Project occupies the final year. A student joining here has to learn the assessment model and manage its most demanding version simultaneously.
programmes.countryNote: Some schools enter MYP 5 students for the IB's optional external assessment leading to the MYP certificate and others award school-based grades only. Ask which applies, because it changes what the final year prepares for.

programmes.name: The Diploma afterwards
programmes.description: Six subjects with published weightings plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Students who completed the MYP arrive comfortable with investigation and extended writing and short of procedural speed under timing, which is the one gap worth closing in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because none could be confirmed from the IB for this project; your coordinator holds the calendar.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-harbour.subjectsIntro: These are the subject groups we are asked for most in this district, each with the criterion that a mid-programme arrival most often finds unfamiliar rather than difficult.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Arrivals from procedural systems satisfy the first criterion immediately and have often never been asked to generalise a pattern or justify a generalisation at all.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Designing one's own inquiry and evaluating one's own method are the two unfamiliar demands for most arrivals, and both are teachable quickly.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students who write fluently lose marks under organising, because a response with good ideas in no deliberate order cannot reach the upper bands however well expressed it is.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed within a phase rather than a year group. A new arrival may be placed at different phases across the four skills, and support has to match the phase the school assigned rather than the age.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically separates grades from MYP 4 onwards and rewards a judgement supported by evidence rather than a balanced survey of positions.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Arrivals from systems where practical subjects were lightly assessed are surprised by the documentation requirement, and students who build first cannot reconstruct the evidence afterwards.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than students expect, so a strong final piece with no documented development will not reach the top bands.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and reflective criteria often hold marks that are available to students who are not the strongest performers.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria, asking students to integrate two subject groups and make the integration explicit. New arrivals treat them as double work rather than as a distinct task, and lose marks for not naming the connection.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project marked on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, with the process journal as assessed evidence rather than decoration. The hardest component for a student who joined the programme late.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies regardless of the licensed curriculum, with Arab and non-Arab streams taught separately. New arrivals frequently meet Arabic for the first time here.

sections.heading: The programme compared with the models students arrive from
paragraphs: Four models account for most arrivals into MYP classes in this district, and each leaves a different gap. An American middle school typically assesses through coursework, projects and tests with a percentage or letter grade, so a student arrives comfortable with projects and unfamiliar with being marked against four separate criteria that reward different things. A national curriculum with heavy content and examination emphasis produces a student strong on recall and unfamiliar with designing an inquiry or evaluating their own method.

A British Key Stage 3 produces something in between: familiarity with levelled assessment and written explanation, and little experience of the investigation and reflection criteria. Another international programme may be closest of all and still differ in how criteria are weighted and converted. In every case the content is rarely the obstacle. What the student has never been asked to produce is the obstacle, and it is identifiable in one session by reading their recent work against the descriptors.

The useful consequence is that the first month of support should be about legibility rather than about teaching. A student who can say, in their own words, what investigating patterns asks for, or what processing and evaluating rewards, will start producing work in that shape without being coached through every task. Three or four sessions usually achieve that, and it is a cheaper and more durable intervention than a year of subject tutoring that leaves the criterion profile untouched.

The comparison is also worth making with the student rather than about them, because a thirteen-year-old who understands that the standard changed is easier to help than one who believes they have become worse at school.

sections.heading: What each kind of arrival finds hard, and for how long
paragraphs: The pattern is predictable enough to plan around. A student from a recall-based system satisfies knowing and understanding in their first week and then sits in the middle bands on the other three criteria for as long as nobody explains them. That is usually two terms of unexplained middling grades, after which both student and family conclude the programme does not suit them. It is an information problem rather than an aptitude problem and it resolves in weeks once addressed.

A student from a project-led system has the opposite profile: comfortable producing extended work and sometimes weaker on content accuracy, so their knowing and understanding marks lag while their investigation marks are fine. That needs ordinary subject teaching rather than criterion orientation, and it is worth distinguishing because the two students look identical on a report that shows only a grade.

The timing of arrival changes everything. In Years 7 and 8 either gap closes comfortably within a year. In Year 9 the descriptors are escalating at the same time, so the student is chasing a moving standard. In Years 10 and 11 the student has to learn the assessment model while managing extended tasks and the Personal Project, which is the hardest version and the one where orientation work pays most. Ask for the criterion breakdown rather than the grade; most schools hold it on their reporting platform.

Ask the school, as well, how it handles a mid-year arrival's first reporting cycle. Some schools annotate the first set of criterion marks as provisional and some do not, and knowing which applies prevents a family from reading a settling-in period as a verdict.

sections.heading: The components that are not subjects
paragraphs: Alongside the eight subject groups the programme carries requirements that new arrivals routinely discover late. Interdisciplinary units ask students to integrate two subject groups and are assessed against their own criteria, which reward making the integration explicit rather than producing good work in both subjects. Students treat them as double work and lose marks for never naming the connection the unit was designed around.

Service as action runs through the programme and is a requirement rather than a graded component, with reflection expected as it happens. Students who treat it as something to document at the end of the year cannot produce the reflective record the school asks for, and a requirement is not satisfied by a retrospective summary. The Personal Project in the final year then formalises the same habit at a much higher stake, marked on criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, with the process journal as assessed evidence.

For a student who joined the programme in Year 10, all three arrive at once and none has been built up to. That is the strongest argument for orientation work in the first term rather than subject tutoring: the components reward a documented process, the documentation cannot be reconstructed afterwards, and a student who understands that in September produces evidence all year rather than discovering the requirement in March.

A practical suggestion for all three: one shared folder, dated entries, added to in the week they happen. It sounds administrative and it is the single habit that protects more MYP marks than any amount of subject revision does.

sections.heading: What the final MYP year produces
paragraphs: Families arriving late often do not know what the end of the programme looks like, and the answer depends on the school. Some schools enter MYP 5 students for the IB's optional external assessment, which leads to the MYP certificate. Others award school-based grades only, with no external component at all. Those are materially different final years: one includes external examination preparation and one does not, and planning for the wrong one wastes a term.

Ask directly and early. If there is no external assessment, the final year's time belongs to criterion work, the Personal Project and preparation for whatever comes next, and examination technique is not worth buying. If there is external assessment, then on-screen examination technique becomes a real requirement in the final terms and sits alongside everything else, which makes the arithmetic on available weeks much tighter.

Either way the final year carries the Personal Project, and either way the student is about to move into the Diploma or into a different post-16 route. The orientation question therefore inverts: a student who has adapted to criterion assessment now needs to prepare for whatever assesses differently next. For the Diploma that means timed procedural work and command-term discipline, both of which are cheap in the summer before DP1 and expensive after the first mock.
Either version also ends with the student moving on, which means the final term carries a transition requirement as well as a completion requirement, and those compete for the same hours.

sections.heading: Why criterion-literate tutors are the scarce kind
paragraphs: There are fewer people who can tutor the MYP well than there are who can tutor the Diploma or IGCSE, and the reason is not difficulty. Diploma and IGCSE content is public, specific and externally examined, so a strong subject graduate can teach either credibly after reading the specification. MYP assessment depends on band descriptors applied with judgement, and that judgement comes from having marked against them rather than from having read them once.

The result is a recognisable pattern in this district. A subject tutor is engaged, the sessions are good, the student enjoys them, the content knowledge improves and the grade holds at five. The missing marks were in investigating patterns, or in organising, or in processing and evaluating, and nothing in the sessions touched those because nobody looked at which criterion was short. The family concludes their child has reached a ceiling in a subject where the ceiling was never the problem.

The screening question is simple and worth asking every candidate, including us. Which four criteria does this subject group use, and which one do you think is costing my child marks? A tutor working in the right system names the criteria and asks to see the breakdown before answering the second part. A tutor who answers in terms of topics and chapters has not registered that the topics are not what is being marked. Removing travel from the arrangement widens the pool enough to find someone who can answer.

sections.heading: Reading the criterion profile across subjects
paragraphs: The most useful diagnostic in the whole programme costs nothing: ask the school for the criterion breakdown in each subject and read them side by side. A single low criterion appearing in three subject groups is one skill gap showing three times, not three subject problems. Communication low in mathematics, organising low in language and literature, and processing and evaluating low in sciences is a single weakness in structuring and justifying written work.

Treating that as three subject problems means three tutors and three times the cost for the same repair, which is exactly what happens when a family reads one report line at a time. Treating it as one gap means a single block of work on structure and justification that moves all three grades. The profiles make the difference visible, and most schools hold them on their reporting platform even when the printed report shows only a digit.

For a mid-programme arrival the pattern is even more pronounced, because the unfamiliar demands cluster. A student from a recall-based system will typically show the same two criteria low across every subject group they take, which is as clear a signal as this assessment model produces. Reading the profiles together converts a confusing set of middling grades into a single, specific, cheap piece of work, and it is the first thing we ask for.

Ask for them termly rather than once, because a single profile shows where the student is while three show whether the targeted criterion is actually moving, which is the only question that matters after support has started.
bullets: Ask for the criterion breakdown in every subject, not just the weak ones
One criterion low across three subjects is one gap, not three

sections.heading: Arabic and the mandatory subjects for a new arrival
paragraphs: A family moving into Dubai Harbour from outside the UAE frequently meets Arabic as a school subject for the first time. Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic language, Islamic Education and social and moral studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to teach, and KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidance set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The structure matters for support. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for Arab and non-Arab students are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students take Islamic Education and the moral, social and cultural studies strand in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two practical consequences for a new arrival. Support must be matched to the stream the school has placed the child in, because the material is not interchangeable, and a tutor working from the wrong stream's material wastes the sessions entirely. And for these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited, so support works with the school's own material rather than substituting a parallel syllabus. Instructional time is counted on a 40-minute lesson unit, with 25 minutes advised as the minimum lesson length.

sections.heading: Booking MYP support from Dubai Harbour
paragraphs: Send the year group, which system the student arrived from and when, the subject groups you are concerned about, the criterion breakdown if your school publishes it, whether the school continues the programme to Year 11 or switches to IGCSE, and the hours that genuinely exist after a bus that leaves before 07:00 and returns after 15:30. The arrival details matter as much as the subjects, because they predict which criteria are lagging and why.

We match a tutor who works criterion by criterion in that subject group and propose a slot in Gulf Standard Time, with project and extended-task work placed at weekends where ninety uninterrupted minutes exist. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, producing a criterion profile and a named target rather than a sales conversation. If the match is wrong after the trial or in week four, we change the tutor.

The limits. MYP specialists are scarcer than Diploma or IGCSE specialists in every subject group, so matching takes longer, and for the smaller subject groups there are weeks when nobody suitable is available. We will say so and offer alternatives rather than putting a content tutor into a criterion problem. We cannot promise a grade, and for the Personal Project the student does all the work, which is what the criteria require rather than a position we have adopted.

If a Personal Project deadline or a reporting cycle is close, say so in the first line, because a fixed date within a few weeks changes which block is worth starting and occasionally changes whether one is.

Those details predict which criteria are lagging more reliably than any subject report does, and they decide whether the first month should be orientation or ordinary teaching.

process.title: Ask the school for the criterion breakdown
process.description: The four criterion marks behind each grade, which most schools hold on their reporting platform even when the printed report shows only a digit. With them a tutor targets the criterion costing the grade; without them the first two sessions reconstruct the profile from the student's work.

process.title: Read the profiles across subjects together
process.description: One low criterion appearing in three subject groups is one skill gap showing three times. For a mid-programme arrival the clustering is usually obvious, and it converts a confusing set of middling grades into a single specific piece of work rather than three tutoring decisions.

process.title: Check against the school's next assessed piece
process.description: The measure is the criterion mark on the next real task, not a practice score. If the targeted criterion moves, continue. If it does not, the diagnosis or the practice format was wrong, and we change the plan in week four rather than defending it in week twelve.

whyPoints.title: Written for mid-programme arrivals
whyPoints.description: This district filled recently and most of its MYP students joined the programme partway through. The first thing they need is the assessment model made legible, which is three or four sessions rather than a year of subject tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-led rather than topic-led

whyPoints.title: The profile read across subjects

whyPoints.description: Interdisciplinary units, service as action and the Personal Project all reward documented process that cannot be reconstructed afterwards. A student who understands that in September produces evidence all year.

whyPoints.description: Some schools enter MYP 5 students for the optional external assessment and others do not. We ask which, because the two versions of the final year need different plans and planning for the wrong one wastes a term.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees and no invented statistics
