faqs.question: Our child joined the MYP in Year 9 in Dubai Harbour. Why are the grades middling?
faqs.answer: Usually because two of the four criteria in each subject are asking for something they have never been asked to produce. A student from a recall-based system satisfies knowing and understanding in their first week and then sits mid-band on investigation, communication and application until somebody explains those descriptors. It is an information problem rather than an aptitude problem, it typically costs two terms of unexplained grades, and it resolves within weeks of being addressed properly.

faqs.question: How does the MYP differ from an American middle school?
faqs.answer: Chiefly in how work is marked. An American middle school generally reports a percentage or letter derived from coursework, projects and tests, so a student arrives comfortable with continuous assessment. The MYP marks four separate criteria out of eight each, which reward different things, and the school converts the profile into a grade from one to seven. A student can be strong on two criteria and weak on two and receive a grade that reveals neither, which is what makes the first reports confusing.

faqs.question: Which criterion do new arrivals most often struggle with?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject group, and the pattern is consistent. In mathematics it is investigating patterns, because generalising and justifying a generalisation is a different skill from calculating correctly. In sciences it is processing and evaluating, specifically naming limitations of the student's own method. In language and literature it is organising, where a well-written response with no deliberate structure cannot reach the upper bands. In individuals and societies it is thinking critically.

faqs.question: Should we buy subject tutoring or something else in the first term?
faqs.answer: For a mid-programme arrival with strong content knowledge, something else. Three or four orientation sessions that make the band descriptors legible, with one piece of work produced in the shape each unfamiliar criterion expects, will usually move more criterion marks than a term of subject teaching. Where the student arrived from a project-led system with lighter content, the opposite applies and ordinary subject teaching is right. The criterion breakdown distinguishes the two cases.

faqs.question: What are interdisciplinary units and why do they cost marks?
faqs.answer: Units asking students to integrate two subject groups, assessed against their own criteria which reward making the integration explicit. Students treat them as double work, produce good material in both subjects, and never name the connection the unit was designed around, which is the thing being marked. New arrivals are particularly prone to this because nothing in their previous system looked like it. One session before the first unit is submitted usually prevents it.

faqs.question: How does service as action need to be recorded through the year?
faqs.answer: It is a requirement rather than a graded component, and it expects reflection recorded as activities happen rather than summarised at the end. Students who treat it as end-of-year documentation cannot produce the reflective record the school asks for, because a requirement is not satisfied by a retrospective account. For a student who joined in Year 10 this arrives alongside extended tasks and the Personal Project with no build-up, which is why the first term matters.

faqs.question: How early should the Personal Project be coached?
faqs.answer: In the first two sessions of the project, before the goal is fixed. The grade rests substantially on documented process rather than on the finished product, so a tutor's useful contributions are testing whether the goal is achievable in the time available, checking access to whatever the project needs, helping the student state credible success criteria, and establishing the journal habit of short dated entries. None of that can be reconstructed once the project is finished.

faqs.question: Does our school enter MYP 5 students for external examinations?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, because practice varies and the answer changes the final year. Some schools enter students for the IB's optional external assessment leading to the MYP certificate, and others award school-based grades only. With external assessment, on-screen examination technique becomes a real requirement in the final terms. Without it, the year's time belongs to criterion work, the Personal Project and preparation for whatever comes next, and examination technique is not worth buying.

faqs.question: Why did a good subject tutor not move our MYP grade?
faqs.answer: Because the missing marks were in a criterion the sessions never addressed. Diploma and IGCSE content is public and externally examined, so a strong graduate can teach either credibly from the specification. MYP assessment depends on band descriptors applied with judgement, which comes from having marked against them. A tutor who teaches topics well and has never read a descriptor improves content knowledge and leaves the criterion profile exactly as it was.

faqs.question: What two questions screen an MYP tutor quickly?
faqs.answer: Which four criteria does this subject group use, and which one do you think is costing my child marks? A tutor working in the right system names the criteria and asks to see the breakdown before answering the second part. A tutor who answers in terms of topics and chapters has not noticed that the topics are not what is being marked. Those two questions tell you more than any amount of qualification listing, and they take a minute.

faqs.question: Is a low criterion in three subjects three problems or one?
faqs.answer: Almost always one. Communication low in mathematics, organising low in language and literature, and processing and evaluating low in sciences is a single weakness in structuring and justifying written work, appearing three times. Treating it as three subject problems means three tutors and three times the cost for the same repair. For a mid-programme arrival the clustering is usually unmistakable once the profiles are read side by side rather than one report line at a time.

faqs.question: Does our child have to take Arabic as a new arrival?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic language, Islamic Education and social and moral studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to teach. KHDA requires Arab and non-Arab streams to be taught separately, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, with non-Arab students taking the moral, social and cultural studies strand in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Support must match the stream the school assigned, because the material is not interchangeable.

faqs.question: How long should an MYP session be from this district?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes for criterion work on a weekday, and ninety for project or extended-task work, which from Dubai Harbour means a weekend morning. Children here leave before 07:00 and return after 15:30, so a weekday project session that starts at 17:30 and has to stop at 18:30 achieves very little once materials are open. Splitting the week into one weekday subject slot and one weekend project slot is what holds through a term.

faqs.question: What should the first month of support produce?
faqs.answer: For a new arrival, a student who can state in their own words what each unfamiliar criterion rewards, plus at least two pieces of work produced in the shape that criterion is assessed in. Not practice questions: work shaped like the real task. The checkpoint is the school's next assessed piece in that subject, read against the targeted criterion. If the criterion mark does not move, the plan changes rather than being extended on optimism.

intro.heading: A map first, then the marking
paragraphs: Parents in this part of Dubai ask the MYP question in two halves. The first half is geographic: where, within reach of Dubai Hills Estate, does the Middle Years Programme actually run, and how does that compare with what Arabian Ranches, Motor City, DAMAC Hills or Town Square can reach? The second half is about the marking: why does a report show a 6 in mathematics with four letters next to it, and what is a parent supposed to do with that? Both halves have straightforward answers and almost nobody gives them.

Take the geography first. The Middle Years Programme is a continuum programme, and in Dubai it runs mostly at the IB campuses clustered in Al Barsha, Al Quoz and along the Al Khail Road corridor, rather than inside the Dubailand communities themselves. Which means a Dubai Hills Estate family and a Town Square family are usually choosing between the same schools, sitting in the same classes, and being marked by the same criteria. The community changes the length of the bus route. It does not change the programme, the marking or the problems.

Now the marking, because this is where MYP tutoring differs most from everything else sold in Dubai. MYP subjects are assessed against four published criteria, each marked out of eight, with the four totals summed and converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries the school applies. A child can be strong on knowledge and weak on communicating findings and come out with a mediocre grade, and a parent reading only the number has no way to see which it was. The letters on the report are the diagnosis. The number is just the summary.

That single fact changes what useful tutoring looks like. A tutor who teaches more content to a student whose marks are lost in criterion C or criterion D is treating the wrong problem, pleasantly and expensively. What moves an MYP grade is usually a specific written behaviour: justifying a conclusion with the data actually collected, evaluating a method rather than restating it, using the subject's command terms properly, structuring an investigation so the reflection has something to reflect on. These are coachable in a handful of sessions once somebody has read the descriptors.

One statement before the detail. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the emirates; home visits are a service we run only in India. For MYP that arrangement matters more than it does at Diploma level, because MYP specialists are spread across eight subject groups and five year levels, and choosing by drive time rather than by subject leaves a family with whoever happens to live nearby.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-hills-estate.programmesIntro: MYP sits in the middle of a longer sequence, and families around Dubai Hills Estate are usually deciding about more than one stage at a time. These are the programmes we support and how each connects to the next.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, physical and health education, and design. Each subject is assessed against four criteria marked out of eight. Students also complete service as action, interdisciplinary units, a community project in the middle years and the Personal Project in MYP 5. Confirm criterion wording and grade boundaries against your school's own assessment policy, as schools publish their conversion tables locally.
programmes.countryNote: Around Dubai Hills Estate, MYP is offered at the Al Barsha and Sobha Hartland IB campuses rather than within the Dubailand communities. Three of the seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 run International Baccalaureate programmes, which will widen the MYP choice for children currently in primary but does nothing for a student already in MYP 4.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The programme that feeds MYP in a continuum school, built on transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects. Children arriving in MYP 1 from PYP are usually comfortable with inquiry and less comfortable with the sudden visibility of subject-specific criteria. The adjustment is a presentation problem more often than a knowledge problem, and it responds quickly to being named.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses within reach of Dubai Hills Estate run PYP into MYP as one school, which removes the transfer at eleven. Families choosing a primary school in these communities are, in practice, choosing the shape of Years 7 to 11 as well, and it is worth asking each campus what proportion of its PYP cohort stays through MYP.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where most MYP students go next. The Diploma introduces external examinations, Higher and Standard Level distinctions, and internal assessments with published criteria of their own. The step that catches MYP students is quantitative: mathematics and the sciences assume fluency that MYP touched without drilling. Students who close that gap in the first term of DP1 are fine; students who discover it after the January mocks are not.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma Chemistry, Physics and the Analysis and Approaches mathematics route are the courses where MYP graduates from these campuses most often ask for help in the first DP1 term. A short bridging block in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 is the cheapest intervention available and almost nobody buys it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The alternative at fourteen, and sometimes a companion to MYP rather than a replacement. Some campuses enter MYP students for a small number of IGCSEs alongside the programme; others run MYP 5 alone. IGCSE is examined externally with mark schemes rather than criterion descriptors, which is a genuinely different skill, and students moving between the two systems need the difference explained rather than discovered.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai by enrolment, and the communities around Dubai Hills Estate are no exception, so an MYP student here has British-curriculum friends sitting IGCSEs at the same age. That comparison causes more family anxiety than it should, and the honest answer depends entirely on the sixth-form route intended.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-hills-estate.subjectsIntro: MYP runs across eight subject groups, and we support all of them plus the companions families ask for. What follows is what each group is actually assessed on, because that is where tutoring hours have to be aimed.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Analysing texts and producing them. Marks are lost on analysis that summarises, on comparison that describes two things separately, and on written work that ignores the audience and purpose the task specified. Close reading of unseen extracts with the criterion wording visible is the highest-return practice.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Assessed by phase rather than by year group, which confuses families comparing siblings. Listening and speaking carry as much weight as reading and writing, so a student who can write well in the language can still score moderately. Oral practice is the component most often neglected and the easiest to schedule.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Knowledge, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. The criterion that costs most marks is the critical-thinking one, because students present information instead of evaluating sources. Teaching a student to say who produced a source and why is worth more than another set of dates.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Investigation design and evaluation are where the grade is decided, not recall. Students lose marks for method descriptions with uncontrolled variables, conclusions that do not refer to the data collected, and evaluations that list improvements without explaining what each one fixes.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics to real-life contexts. The investigation criterion is unfamiliar to students arriving from a British curriculum, and the real-life application criterion rewards written justification that most students have never been asked for.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A full design cycle: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. Marks are lost almost entirely in documentation rather than in the artefact produced. Students who photograph and annotate as they go score well; students who build first and write up afterwards do not.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: The process journal carries as much assessed weight as the finished piece. Students are credited for investigating a context, developing skills deliberately, and reflecting honestly on what did not work, which is a habit rather than a talent and can be taught.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Includes written components on planning for performance and reflecting on it. Academically strong students sometimes score poorly here because they treat the written work as an afterthought, and the fix is simply taking the criteria seriously.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed separately against their own criteria, and frequently the lowest grade on an otherwise strong report. Students are asked to integrate two subject perspectives and usually answer from one. Knowing that is half the problem solved.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project with a written report assessed against published criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. The commonest failure is a goal too large to evidence. Scope it narrowly in the first fortnight and the rest of the project becomes manageable.

sections.heading: Which communities here have an MYP school, and where everybody else drives
paragraphs: Set the Dubailand communities side by side and one pattern repeats: the Middle Years Programme is not usually inside them. It sits at the IB campuses in Al Barsha, Al Quoz, Al Barsha South and along the Al Khail Road corridor, plus the Sobha Hartland and Sustainable City schools at either end. A family in Dubai Hills Estate, a family in Mudon and a family in Motor City are therefore choosing from roughly the same list, and the thing that separates them is minutes in a bus, not quality of provision.

The table below compares them on the terms that actually matter when a child is eleven. Whether there is an MYP place reachable without a major commute. What the on-community alternative is, since in most of these neighbourhoods it is a British-curriculum campus within walking distance. What happens at sixteen, which is the decision the eleven-year-old choice quietly makes. And when a weekday tutoring session can realistically begin once the journey home is finished.

That last column is the one families underestimate. A child who gets home at 16:45 and needs food, a shower and twenty minutes of decompression is not ready for a subject session until 17:30, and an MYP student has eight subjects of homework behind that. Communities further from the campus ring are not disadvantaged in the programme they receive; they are disadvantaged in the hours left afterwards. Online delivery removes the tutor's travel from that equation but not the child's, so planning around a realistic start time is the single most useful scheduling decision a family makes.

One correction worth making, because it comes up constantly in these communities. Parents assume that choosing a school nearer home will make tutoring easier to find locally. It does the opposite for MYP. A criterion-marked programme across eight subject groups needs a tutor who has read the descriptors for that subject at that year level, and the local pool in any single Dubailand community contains almost nobody who has. Proximity narrows the choice; it does not improve it.

sections.heading: How MYP marking works, and why a 6 is not a percentage
paragraphs: This is the section most MYP parents in Dubai have been waiting for. Each MYP subject is assessed against four published criteria, labelled A to D, and each criterion is marked out of eight against descriptors written in bands. The four criterion marks are summed to a total out of thirty-two, and the school converts that total into a subject grade from one to seven using published boundaries. The grade is the end of the process, not the information. The four criterion marks are the information.

Read that way, a report becomes diagnostic. A science grade of five made up of seven, seven, three and four is a student who knows the material and cannot write up an investigation. A science grade of five made up of four, four, five and five is a different student with a different problem, needing content teaching rather than writing coaching. Identical grades, opposite remedies. A tutor who does not ask for the criterion breakdown before the first lesson is guessing, and a tutoring plan built on a guess costs a term.

The criteria differ by subject group, which is why MYP tutoring has to be subject-specific in a way that general tutoring is not. In sciences, criterion B is about designing an inquiry and criterion C about processing and evaluating. In mathematics, one criterion is about investigating patterns and another about applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In design, the whole cycle from inquiring to evaluating is assessed and the documentation carries it. A tutor who has read the right descriptors can tell a student exactly what the next band up requires.

Two cautions. First, confirm criterion wording and the conversion boundaries against your own school's assessment policy: the IB publishes subject guides and schools apply the conversion locally, so the boundary for a six is not identical everywhere. Second, do not let anybody convert an MYP grade into a percentage for you. It is not one, the arithmetic is meaningless, and the translation hides exactly the information a parent needs.

sections.heading: MYP 5 and the fork: eAssessment, IGCSE alongside, or neither
paragraphs: At the end of MYP 5 a school takes one of several routes, and families are rarely told which until it is almost upon them. Some schools enter students for MYP eAssessment, the IB's on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the MYP Certificate. Some enter students for a small number of IGCSEs alongside MYP. Some run MYP 5 with internal assessment only and no external qualification at sixteen. Each of these is a legitimate choice by the school, and each has different consequences for a student's file.

The consequence that matters is evidence. A student moving to a different school, a different country or a selective sixth form at sixteen may need an externally verified qualification, and a school-reported MYP grade is not the same artefact as an examined certificate. Families in Dubai move often - the private sector here added seven new schools and 16,846 places for 2026-27 alone - so the question is not academic. Ask the campus, in writing, what external qualification your child will hold at the end of MYP 5.

The tutoring consequences differ as well, and this is the practical reason the question belongs on this page. Preparing for eAssessment means practising on-screen under time with unfamiliar stimulus material, which is a different exercise from writing a criterion-marked task over two weeks. Preparing for IGCSE alongside MYP means learning an entirely different assessment language: mark schemes, command words and externally set papers. A student doing both is being asked to hold two systems at once, and that is worth naming rather than letting them discover it.

Our advice is unexciting and it saves money. Find out the route in MYP 4, not MYP 5. If eAssessment is the route, start timed on-screen practice in the first term. If IGCSEs are involved, get the syllabus codes and treat them as the separate qualification they are. If neither, build the strongest possible portfolio of criterion-marked work and a Personal Project the student can genuinely talk about, because those become the evidence.

sections.heading: From MYP into the Diploma: the gap that shows up in October of DP1
paragraphs: Every October we take calls from families whose child was comfortable in MYP 5 and is struggling six weeks into DP1. It is rarely a sign that the MYP was weak or that the student is not able. It is a predictable transition, it has the same shape most years, and it concentrates in two places: quantitative fluency and assessment literacy.

Quantitative fluency first. MYP mathematics assesses investigating patterns and real-life application as well as knowing and understanding, which is a broader brief than a British Year 9 scheme and a thinner one on drilled procedure. A student can score well on the investigation criteria and still be slow at algebraic manipulation, index laws and rearranging formulae. In DP1 Analysis and Approaches, and in Diploma Chemistry and Physics, that slowness becomes the bottleneck within weeks, because the new content assumes the old procedure is automatic.

Assessment literacy second. MYP work is marked against descriptors the student has usually seen, over days, with feedback cycles. Diploma work is marked against external mark schemes under time, where a precise command term governs what earns credit. Students arriving from MYP write thoughtfully and score moderately, because thoughtfulness is not the currency. Learning that the word explain requires a stated reason, that three marks means three creditable points, and that a formula written down earns a method mark, takes a few weeks of deliberate work.

The table maps the transition subject by subject so a family can see what their own child's combination implies. The right time to act on it is the summer between MYP 5 and DP1, where six to ten hours of targeted work does more than a term of catching up in October. Almost nobody books that summer block, which is why this is the single most useful paragraph on the page for a family with a child in MYP 5 now.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project is independent work completed in MYP 5, with a written report assessed against published criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting on the process. It is the first piece of genuinely self-directed academic work most students produce, and it is assessed on the process at least as much as on the product. A beautiful outcome with a thin journal scores less than a modest outcome with rigorous documentation, which surprises almost every family the first time.

The commonest failure is scope. A student chooses a goal that could occupy a professional for a year, discovers in month three that it cannot be evidenced, and writes a report full of intention. Narrowing the goal in the first fortnight is the whole trick, and it is where an outside adult is genuinely useful, because narrowing requires somebody who is not emotionally attached to the original idea. The second commonest failure is a journal written retrospectively, which reads exactly as retrospective and cannot evidence a process that was not recorded.

Now the boundary, stated so nobody has to infer it. A tutor may explain each criterion and what the next band up requires. A tutor may question whether a goal is achievable and evidenceable in the time available. A tutor may teach the research, referencing and reflection skills the project needs. A tutor may read what the student has written and give feedback on it. A tutor may not write any part of the report, redraft it into adult prose, supply the structure for the student to fill, or produce the product. The supervisor at school is the adult of record, and the school's deadlines govern.

The test a parent can apply without knowing IB rules in detail is whether the student could explain and defend every line of their own report in a conversation. If yes, the help was teaching. If no, the help has created a risk that falls on the student, not on the adult who gave it. We state this plainly because vague offers of project support are common in this market, and because an MYP student is young enough that the adults around them owe them a clear line.

sections.heading: Where MYP students actually lose marks
paragraphs: Start with the one that accounts for more lost marks than anything else: answering the task instead of the criterion. An MYP task sheet usually names which criteria are being assessed. A student who writes a good piece of work that does not address criterion D will not be credited for criterion D, however good the piece is. Teaching a student to read the criteria first, write the four letters at the top of the page, and check each one before submitting, moves grades within a term and costs almost nothing.

Second, evaluation treated as a conclusion. Across sciences, design and the arts, the final criterion asks for evaluation: what worked, what did not, what would change and why. Students write a summary instead. The difference is specific and teachable - an evaluation names a limitation, explains its effect, and proposes a change with a reason attached - and it is worth several marks in several subjects simultaneously.

Third, command terms. MYP subject guides define command terms, and the descriptors use them deliberately. Describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, justify and compare each require something different, and students who treat them as synonyms lose marks they had earned. This is the same discipline IGCSE and Diploma students need, which is a useful thing to know: work done on it in MYP 3 pays dividends for the next five years regardless of which route the student takes.

Fourth, and least discussed, evidence of process. MYP rewards documented thinking. The design cycle, the arts process journal, the science investigation plan and the Personal Project report all ask the student to show how they got somewhere. Students who photograph, annotate and date as they go score well. Students who produce the thing and then describe it afterwards cannot evidence what they did not record, and no amount of writing skill recovers that.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs across these communities, read as a monthly figure
paragraphs: Most families budget tutoring monthly rather than hourly, so start there. Bestimate's Dubai rate table estimates monthly costs for weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Market packages seen in Dubai include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour home visits. Those are the numbers a household actually plans against.

Convert to hourly and the published bands are these, all read from providers' own pages in October 2026. Budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online is published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level teaching sits at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure.

For MYP specifically there is a judgement to make about which band is appropriate, and it is not the obvious one. MYP 1 to 3 support in a single subject is often well served in the middle band, because the work is criterion coaching on a student's own tasks rather than examination technique. MYP 5, the Personal Project year and the summer bridge into DP1 justify the specialist band, because the person needs to know both the MYP descriptors and what the Diploma will assume. Paying specialist rates for MYP 2 homework help is the commonest overspend we see in these communities.

Set against the wider budget, the proportion is small and controllable. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A diagnosed block of eight to twelve hours at a sensible band, aimed at a criterion that the report has already identified, is a modest and finite line. An open monthly retainer across four subject groups is neither, and it is what families default to when nobody has read the criterion breakdown.

sections.heading: MYP or a British route at eleven: the comparison parents in these communities actually face
paragraphs: This is the decision behind a great many MYP searches from Arabian Ranches, Motor City and Dubai Hills Estate, and it deserves a straight answer rather than programme advocacy. On one side, a criterion-marked international programme at a campus fifteen to thirty minutes away. On the other, a mark-scheme-marked British curriculum at a campus often inside the community. Both produce students who do well. They produce them differently, and they close different doors at different ages.

MYP keeps the Diploma open and assesses a wider range of skills, including investigation, reflection and interdisciplinary work that a British Key Stage 3 does not formally mark. It also means no external qualification at sixteen unless the school enters students for eAssessment or IGCSEs, which matters for a family likely to move. The British route produces externally examined IGCSEs at sixteen, portable and universally recognised, with narrower formal assessment of process skills along the way.

The honest framing is this. If the family expects to stay in Dubai through to eighteen and the child is likely to want the Diploma, the continuum route is coherent and the commute is the price. If the family may move within three years, or the child is heading for a British sixth form or an A Level route, the externally examined path is simpler and the local campus is a genuine advantage. Neither choice is a mistake. Making it on drive time alone is.

What tutoring can do about either, honestly, is limited and specific. It can close a criterion gap in MYP. It can build IGCSE technique on a British route. It can bridge between the two systems when a child moves mid-stream, which is the single most common reason families in these communities contact us about MYP at all. What it cannot do is substitute for the school's programme, and any provider implying otherwise is selling you something that does not exist.

sections.heading: Starting MYP support from Dubai Hills Estate, and what we will not do
paragraphs: The first thing we ask for is the report with the criterion marks on it, not the grade summary. With four numbers per subject we can tell you within a day whether the problem is content, written expression, investigation design or documentation, and which subject is worth starting with. Without them, the first session has to be spent finding out, which is a fine use of a free trial but a poor use of a paid hour. Most Dubai schools issue the breakdown; ask the class teacher if it is not on the portal.

Then a trial lesson with a subject specialist, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time after the bus gets back. The session works on a real piece of the student's own work against the school's criterion wording, so a parent can see the diagnosis rather than hear about it. Afterwards you get a written note naming the criterion strands that are costing marks and a plausible hour count. For MYP that count is usually smaller than families expect, because criterion behaviours change faster than content gaps close.

Now the limits. MYP spans eight subject groups across five year levels, which is a wide matching problem, and in any given week the right specialist for an unusual combination may not have an evening slot in the Gulf window. When that happens we say so and offer the options: a different evening, a weekend session, or a wait. We will not put a general tutor on a criterion-marked design or arts task and let a family find out from the next report that nothing changed.

And the things we will not do at all. We will not promise a grade or a level, and a provider who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child. We will not write, redraft or structure a Personal Project, a report or any assessed task; the student's own work is the only work. We will not describe IB Gram as approved, accredited or partnered with the IB, with KHDA or with any school, because none of that is true and in this market the claim is as common as it is risky. What we will do is read the descriptors, mark the work honestly, and tell you early if the plan is not working.

process.title: Send the report with the criterion marks
process.description: Four numbers per subject are worth more than any description. They separate a content problem from a written-expression problem from an investigation-design problem, and they tell us which subject to start with. If the breakdown is not on the school portal, the class teacher will usually supply it on request.

process.title: We match a subject specialist for that year level
process.description: MYP covers eight subject groups across five years, so matching is specific. We look for somebody who teaches that subject at that level and has read the current descriptors, with an evening slot that works in Gulf Standard Time after the journey home to Dubai Hills Estate.

process.title: A free trial on the student's own work
process.description: The session takes a real task the student has written and marks it against the school's criterion wording, with the student watching each strand being met or missed. It is uncomfortable for about ten minutes and then it is the most useful hour a parent will buy that term.

process.title: A written note with the strands and an hour count
process.description: You receive a short document naming which criterion strands are costing marks, in what order to address them, and roughly how many hours each needs. For MYP the counts are usually modest, because written behaviours change faster than content gaps close.

process.title: Sessions, marked work, and a review at six weeks
process.description: Lessons run on a schedule you set, with one piece of the student's own work marked each time. At six weeks we review against the next set of school marks rather than against a feeling, and if nothing has moved we say so and change the plan or stop.

whyPoints.title: We read the criteria before the first lesson
whyPoints.description: Two students with the same MYP grade can need opposite remedies, and the criterion breakdown is the only thing that distinguishes them. Asking for it before teaching begins is the difference between a plan and a guess, and it costs nothing except the willingness to ask.

whyPoints.title: Subject-specific, because the criteria are
whyPoints.description: Criterion C in sciences and criterion C in language and literature assess different things entirely. A tutor who teaches MYP generically teaches an average of eight subject groups. We match to the subject and the year level, and we say when the right specialist is not available.

whyPoints.title: The MYP 5 fork raised in MYP 4
whyPoints.description: Whether a school enters students for eAssessment, for IGCSEs alongside, or for neither changes what preparation means and what the student holds at sixteen. Families who find out in MYP 5 lose a year of runway. We raise it early because it is the question with a deadline attached.

whyPoints.title: The summer bridge nobody books
whyPoints.description: Six to ten hours between MYP 5 and DP1, aimed at algebraic fluency, mole calculations and external mark schemes, prevents the October call we take every year. It is the cheapest intervention in the whole sequence and the least purchased, which says more about marketing than about value.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on the Personal Project
whyPoints.description: A tutor explains criteria, questions scope, teaches research and reflection skills, and gives feedback on the student's drafts. A tutor does not write, redraft or structure the report. We put that in writing because MYP students are young and the consequence of a blurred line falls on them.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims, no grade promises
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or any school, and claims none. We publish market rates with sources rather than invented statistics, and we do not promise levels or grades. In this market those absences are the differentiator.

faqs.question: Which schools near Dubai Hills Estate run the IB Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: Not schools inside the community itself in most cases. Families from Dubai Hills Estate reach MYP at the IB campuses in Al Barsha, Al Barsha South and Al Quoz, with Sobha Hartland and the Sustainable City schools at either end of the Al Khail Road corridor. Three of the seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 run International Baccalaureate programmes, so the choice will widen for younger children. Confirm current provision and the latest KHDA inspection outcome on the regulator's own site before shortlisting, because programme offers change between academic years.

faqs.question: What does a MYP level 5 actually mean, and is it a pass?
faqs.answer: It is a grade on a one-to-seven scale, produced by summing four criterion marks out of eight each and converting the total using boundaries the school applies. It is not a percentage and it does not translate into one meaningfully. Whether it counts as satisfactory depends on your school's own reporting policy, so ask. The more useful question is what the four criterion marks were, because a five built from seven, seven, three and four is a completely different student from a five built from four, four, five and five.

faqs.question: Why are MYP reports written in criteria rather than percentages?
faqs.answer: Because the programme assesses distinct capabilities separately rather than averaging them into one number. Each subject has four published criteria, each marked against banded descriptors, so a report can show that a student knows the material and cannot yet write up an investigation. That is more informative than a percentage, which hides exactly that distinction. The practical consequence for parents is that the criterion breakdown is the part worth reading, and the single grade is only a summary of it.

faqs.question: Does MYP prepare a child for IGCSE or only for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: It prepares them for both, but not identically. MYP leads naturally into the Diploma, where internal assessments and published criteria are familiar territory. Moving to IGCSE or A Level means learning a different assessment language: external mark schemes, defined command words and timed papers where precision of wording governs credit. That transition is perfectly manageable and usually needs a few weeks of deliberate work rather than a year. Some schools enter MYP students for IGCSEs alongside the programme, which makes the shift gradual.

faqs.question: Is MYP eAssessment compulsory, and what happens if the school does not offer it?
faqs.answer: It is not compulsory for schools, which is the part families find surprising. MYP eAssessment comprises on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate, and each school decides whether to offer it. If your campus does not, your child finishes MYP 5 with school-reported grades and the Personal Project rather than an externally examined certificate. That is fine if they continue at the same school into the Diploma, and worth planning around if the family may move. Ask the campus in writing during MYP 4.

faqs.question: How is the MYP Personal Project marked?
faqs.answer: Against published criteria covering planning the project, applying the skills needed to complete it, and reflecting on the process and the outcome, with a written report as the main evidence. The product matters less than the documented thinking, which is why a modest outcome with a rigorous journal outscores an impressive outcome with a thin one. Confirm the current criterion structure with the school, since the IB revises the projects guide on a cycle and the school supervises the assessment locally.

faqs.question: May a tutor help with the Personal Project without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may explain each criterion, question whether the goal is achievable and evidenceable in the time available, teach research, referencing and reflection skills, and give feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not write any part of the report, redraft it into adult prose, supply a structure to fill in, or produce the product. The test is whether the student could explain and defend every line themselves. If not, the help has created a risk that falls on the student.

faqs.question: My child moved from a British Year 8 into MYP 3. What is missing?
faqs.answer: Usually nothing in content and a great deal in presentation. Students arriving from a British curriculum are used to being marked on whether the answer is right, and MYP marks them on investigation design, communication and reflection as separate capabilities. The investigating-patterns criterion in mathematics and the evaluation criteria in sciences and design are the usual shocks. Three or four sessions reading the descriptors and marking the student's own work against them normally settles it, which is far less than families fear.

faqs.question: Is MYP maths harder or easier than Year 9 British curriculum maths?
faqs.answer: Broader rather than harder. MYP mathematics assesses knowing and understanding alongside investigating patterns, communicating and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, so a student has to write about mathematics as well as do it. That suits some children and frustrates others. The procedural drilling a British scheme does more of pays off later in Diploma Analysis and Approaches, which is why the summer bridge between MYP 5 and DP1 focuses on algebraic fluency rather than on new topics.

faqs.question: What happens to a MYP student who then switches to A Levels at 16?
faqs.answer: It works, and the adjustment is specific. A Level teaching assumes fluency with externally examined content and, in the sciences, with IGCSE Extended-level procedure. A student finishing MYP 5 without external entries has strong investigation and reflection skills and may be slower on drilled technique and timed examination writing. A short bridging block over the summer covering mark schemes, command words and subject-specific procedure closes most of it. Check with the sixth-form campus what entry evidence it requires from an MYP student, since policies differ.

faqs.question: Does MYP tutoring cost less than Diploma tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It should, for most of the five years, and families frequently overpay. MYP 1 to 3 support in a single subject is criterion coaching on the student's own tasks, well served by the published middle band of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online. MYP 5, the Personal Project year and the bridge into DP1 justify the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above, because the tutor needs to know both the descriptors and what the Diploma assumes. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not our prices.

faqs.question: Do MYP students still take Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies?
faqs.answer: Yes. Those subjects are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a tutoring plan this is timetable arithmetic: an MYP student carries eight subject groups plus these hours, so one session a week that survives beats three that collapse.

faqs.question: How many MYP subjects should we support at once?
faqs.answer: One, in almost every case, and two only when the criterion breakdown shows genuinely separate problems. An MYP student already carries eight subject groups, service as action, interdisciplinary units and, in MYP 5, the Personal Project. Adding three tutoring sessions a week produces a plan that is abandoned by the second month. One subject fixed properly also tends to lift others, because the criterion behaviours - evaluating rather than summarising, using command terms precisely, documenting process - transfer across the whole programme.

faqs.question: What are approaches to learning skills and can they be taught?
faqs.answer: They are the skill clusters the programme runs through every subject: thinking, communication, social, self-management and research. They can absolutely be taught, and self-management and research are the two where tutoring makes the most visible difference. Planning backwards from a deadline, keeping a dated process journal, taking notes that can be revised from, and evaluating a source rather than quoting it are concrete behaviours. They show up in criterion marks across several subjects at once, which makes them unusually good value to work on.

faqs.question: Would a tutor from a MYP school nearby be better than an online specialist?
faqs.answer: Only if they teach your child's subject at your child's year level and have read the current descriptors, and in any single Dubailand community that combination is rare. Choosing by distance narrows the pool to whoever lives nearby; choosing by subject and year level opens it to every MYP specialist available. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE in any case - that is a service we run only in India - so our lessons reach Dubai Hills Estate one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-hills-estate.closingHeading: Read the criteria, then choose the help
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-hills-estate.closingBody: An MYP grade tells a parent very little on its own. The four criterion marks behind it tell you almost everything: whether the problem is knowledge, investigation design, written communication or documented process. Start there, bring that breakdown to a free trial session, and watch a subject specialist mark your child's own work against the school's own wording. You will leave with a written list of strands and an hour count, usually a smaller one than you expected. Lessons for Dubai Hills Estate families run one-to-one and live online, on Gulf Standard Time, after the bus gets home.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-internet-cit.tutorsIntro: The MYP tutors here work in the language the school's reports are written in: criteria, levels, command terms and task-specific clarifications. That matters because a student can raise their understanding and see no change in their grade until somebody shows them which criterion the marks were actually lost under.

intro.heading: The Middle Years Programme does not use percentages, and that is where the confusion starts
paragraphs: Parents arriving at the Middle Years Programme from almost any other system meet the same obstacle. The report does not say sixty-eight per cent. It says a level for criterion A, a level for criterion B, a level for criterion C, a level for criterion D, and a subject grade between one and seven. Nothing on it explains which of those four is dragging the grade down, and without that the natural response is to ask the child to work harder across the whole subject, which is both exhausting and largely ineffective.

The structure itself is clear once it is explained. Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria. Each criterion is marked on a scale from zero to eight, against published descriptors that say what a level looks like. The four levels are combined and converted into the one-to-seven subject grade using boundaries published in the subject guide, which your school can show you. Two students can hold the same grade for entirely different reasons, and the useful work is always on the weakest criterion rather than on the subject as a whole.

The second obstacle is the vocabulary. MYP tasks are built around key concepts, related concepts, a statement of inquiry and a global context, and they come with task-specific clarifications that redefine what each criterion level means for that particular task. A student who has not read the clarification is guessing at what the marker wants. Reading the clarification before starting is the single most transferable habit a tutor can install, and it takes one session to teach and a term to become automatic.

Dubai Internet City is a free zone in Al Sufouh, surrounded by Dubai Knowledge Park, Dubai Media City and the residential belt of The Greens, The Views, Barsha Heights, Al Sufouh and the Marina towers. The IB continuum schools these students attend sit mostly in Al Barsha and along the coastal corridor. Enquiries from this postcode come overwhelmingly from parents at work during the day, about MYP students who will be home by five, which makes written session records part of the service rather than an extra.

IB Gram works with MYP students online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. For MYP the online format has a specific advantage: so much of the work is in interpreting a task sheet, a rubric and a set of descriptors that having both documents on screen beside each other is how the teaching actually happens. A parent who was not in the room gets a written note of what the session covered and what was set.

programmes.name: Early Middle Years, ages 11 to 14

Support at this stage is mostly about reading a task properly, structuring written responses and building the arithmetic and literacy that later years assume. It is also the cheapest point at which to fix a gap, because nothing is yet high-stakes.
programmes.countryNote: Families in this district often arrive in Dubai mid-phase because of the technology and media sectors' posting cycles. A student joining MYP 2 from a national curriculum usually has the content and not the task literacy, which looks like weakness and is not. One term of explicit work on criteria and command terms generally closes it.

programmes.name: Upper Middle Years, ages 14 to 16
programmes.description: Where grades start mattering, where subject choices narrow, and where the Personal Project lands. Support here is criterion-specific: identifying the weakest criterion in each subject, working on the skills its descriptors describe, and doing it against real task sheets rather than generic exercises.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 students in Dubai schools are typically making Diploma or A Level choices at the same time as the Personal Project falls due. That collision is predictable and usually unmanaged, and a plan that acknowledges both is worth more than extra subject teaching in either.

programmes.name: Bridging MYP 5 into the Diploma
programmes.description: The transition where MYP's strengths and its gaps both become visible. Students arrive in the Diploma strong on inquiry, research and communication, and frequently short on the sustained mathematical and technical fluency that higher level subjects assume from the first week. The bridge is specific and short if it is done deliberately.

Six to eight sessions in the summer between MYP 5 and DP 1, on algebraic fluency, standard form, uncertainty and command-term precision, removes most of the September shock and costs a fraction of repairing it in the second term.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-internet-cit.subjectsIntro: The Middle Years Programme has eight subject groups, and support is requested across most of them from this corridor. These are the eight with the criteria each one is assessed against.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B and D are where most students lose levels, because both require reasoning rather than answers.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The design and evaluation criteria reward process, which textbooks do not teach.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria: analysing, organizing, producing text, and using language. Students who write fluently often score low on analysing, because fluency is not analysis.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria across comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Phase placement matters more than year group, and parents are rarely told the phase.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Criterion D is the usual weak point, because evaluating a source is a taught skill rather than an instinct.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The documented process carries the marks, which surprises students who judge themselves on the finished product.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal is assessed, so a strong performer with thin documentation still loses levels.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on and improving performance. Two of the four are written, which students regularly discover late.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria, combining disciplines around a shared inquiry. Students often treat these as a lesser task; the levels count the same as any other.

sections.heading: The four criteria, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: Every Middle Years Programme subject is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, and the criteria are different in each subject group. That is the fact that makes MYP reports hard to read and easy to act on once you have the list. A student with a low criterion C in Language and Literature and a low criterion C in Sciences has two unrelated problems, because criterion C means producing text in one and processing and evaluating data in the other.

The table sets out the four criteria for each subject group. It is the single most useful page of information a parent new to the programme can have, and it is almost impossible to find on a tutoring site: the competitor pages examined for this project name no criterion at all. With it, a report stops being a wall of numbers and becomes a diagnosis, because each criterion points at a specific and teachable skill.

Two patterns recur across subjects. The criteria that reward process rather than product are where confident students lose levels: inquiring and designing in sciences, investigating patterns in mathematics, developing ideas in design, the process journal in arts. Students judge themselves on whether the answer was right or the piece was good, and the rubric is often marking how they got there. The second pattern is the reflective criterion, which asks for genuine evaluation rather than a polite summary and is the most commonly thin section in otherwise strong work.

The practical method with a student is simple and slightly dull. Take the actual task sheet, read the criterion descriptors for the level the student is aiming at, and turn each phrase into a concrete action. Descriptors are written in general language by design; translating them into what to do on this task is most of what a good MYP tutor does, and it is the part students cannot do alone because the language is unfamiliar.

rows: Reflecting on the impacts of science

sections.heading: How criterion levels turn into a grade from one to seven
paragraphs: Each criterion is marked on a scale from zero to eight against published descriptors, which are grouped in bands. The four criterion levels are then combined and converted into the subject grade, which runs from one to seven, using boundaries published in the subject guide. Your school can show you the conversion it uses. The important consequence is arithmetic: because the four criteria contribute together, a single weak criterion can hold a grade down even when the other three are strong, and lifting that one is the shortest route to a different number on the report.

This is also why asking a child to work harder at a subject rarely moves an MYP grade. Effort spread evenly across four criteria produces small gains in each and may not cross a boundary at all. Effort concentrated on the criterion that is three levels behind the others moves the total meaningfully. Identifying which criterion that is takes five minutes with a report in front of you, and it is the conversation we have in the first session.

A second feature confuses parents reasonably. Not every task assesses every criterion, so a report reflects the tasks that happened to be set, and a criterion assessed once carries more weight in the picture than one assessed three times. If a level looks anomalous, it is worth asking the teacher which task produced it before concluding anything. Schools are generally happy to explain this, and the answer often reframes the problem entirely.

The table below describes what each criterion type rewards in practice and the evidence a marker is looking for. It is deliberately written in plain language rather than in descriptor language, because translating between the two is exactly where students and parents get stuck.

sections.heading: Statement of inquiry, key concepts and global contexts: why the question looks strange
paragraphs: MYP task sheets are written in a framework that confuses newcomers. A unit has key concepts and related concepts, a statement of inquiry that ties them to a global context, and inquiry questions in factual, conceptual and debatable forms. A student arriving from a system where questions ask what happened or how do you calculate this will find a debatable question genuinely puzzling, because it has no single correct answer and the mark is for the reasoning.

Teaching this is less about philosophy than about orientation. The factual questions check content. The conceptual questions ask the student to connect ideas. The debatable questions ask for a position that is argued and defensible. A student who treats a debatable question as a factual one writes a correct answer that scores poorly, and the puzzle is solved once they can tell the three apart. That takes a session or two and then holds across every subject.

The global context is not decoration either. It frames why the unit matters and it often appears in the assessment criteria for the task, particularly in the reflective and critical-thinking criteria. A student who ignores the stated global context in a piece of work has left out something the rubric was looking for, which is one of the more frustrating ways to lose levels because the content was all present.

The most valuable habit in this whole area is reading the task-specific clarification before starting. Schools rewrite the general descriptors into task-specific language, which tells the student precisely what a high level looks like on this particular piece. Students routinely start writing before reading it. Installing the opposite habit is a single instruction, repeated until automatic, and it changes outcomes across every subject group simultaneously.
bullets: Factual, conceptual and debatable questions want three different kinds of answer
A debatable question is scored on the reasoning, not on a correct result

Read the task-specific clarification before writing anything
Self-assess against the rubric before submitting, every time

sections.heading: Approaches to Learning: the skills being assessed behind the subject content
paragraphs: The programme assumes a set of skills it calls Approaches to Learning, grouped around thinking, research, communication, social and self-management skills. They are assumed rather than taught in most timetables, which means a student can be perfectly capable in a subject and lose levels because they cannot find and evaluate a source, plan a long task, or structure an extended piece of writing. Those are the gaps most MYP tutoring is genuinely for, even when the enquiry names a subject.

Research skills are the most commonly weak. Finding a source, judging whether it is credible, taking notes that can be used later rather than copied, and citing properly are four separate procedures, and schools vary enormously in how explicitly they teach them. A student in MYP 4 who has never been shown how to evaluate a source will lose levels in individuals and societies, in sciences and in the Personal Project, all for the same reason, which is why fixing it is efficient.

Self-management is the second. MYP work is often set over weeks rather than days, and students who have only ever done overnight homework have no method for a three-week task. Breaking a task into stages with dates, keeping a journal as the work happens rather than reconstructing it afterwards, and leaving time for revision are learnable procedures. A tutor who installs them is affecting every subject at once rather than one.

Communication is the third and the most visible on a report. Structuring an argument, using subject-specific terminology, presenting data clearly and writing to a purpose rather than to a length. Students with strong ideas and weak structure are extremely common, and their reports usually show it as a low organizing or communicating criterion across several subjects simultaneously, which is the clearest possible signal of where the work should go.
bullets: Research: find, evaluate, note and cite, as four separate procedures
Self-management: stage a three-week task with dates and keep the journal live
Communication: structure first, terminology second, length last
Thinking: tell factual, conceptual and debatable apart before answering

sections.heading: The Personal Project in MYP 5, and the line a tutor will not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project is a student-directed piece of work completed in MYP 5, assessed against its own criteria, with a process journal that forms part of the evidence. It is the first genuinely independent project most students meet, and it arrives in the same year as subject choices for the next phase, which is why it so often becomes a household problem rather than a school one.

The most common failure is scope. Students choose a goal that is either too large to finish or too vague to evaluate, and the problem is invisible until the deadline is close. A tutor can help enormously at this stage by asking the questions that expose the scope problem early: what exactly will exist at the end, how will you know whether it worked, and what will you do in week one. Fixing scope in the first fortnight is worth more than any amount of later rescue.

The second failure is the journal. The criteria reward documented process, and students reconstruct the journal at the end from memory, which produces generic entries that read exactly like the reconstruction they are. Keeping it as the work happens, with dated entries that record decisions and the reasons for them, is the difference between a thin and a strong submission. It costs five minutes a session and almost nobody does it.

On what support is permitted, we are explicit because this is where providers in this market cross a line. A tutor may coach planning, help a student interrogate their own goal, teach research and reflection skills, and respond to the student's own journal with the questions a supervisor would ask. A tutor must never write, draft or produce the Personal Project, or any part of it, and must not supply work for the student to adapt. The project is supervised in school and the supervisor is the authority on what help is allowed in your child's case; ask them rather than assuming.
bullets: Scope settled in the first fortnight: what will exist, and how success is judged
The journal kept live, dated, and recording decisions with reasons
A tutor coaches planning and reflection and never produces the work
The school supervisor decides what support is permitted; ask them directly
Plan around the subject-choice process happening in the same year

sections.heading: MYP 5 into the Diploma: what transfers and what has to be built
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme produces students who are unusually good at inquiry, research, reflection and communication, and those strengths are real advantages in the Diploma, particularly in the Extended Essay, in internal assessments and in Theory of Knowledge. Students arriving in the Diploma from MYP are rarely the ones who struggle with an open-ended research task, and that is worth saying because the programme takes criticism it does not always deserve.

What does not transfer automatically is sustained technical fluency. Higher level mathematics and the Diploma sciences assume from the first week that algebraic manipulation is automatic, that standard form and unit handling are secure, and that an uncertainty can be carried through a calculation. MYP builds those skills in the service of inquiry rather than drilling them, so a student can hold strong MYP grades and still feel the first term of the Diploma as a sudden change of gear.

The second gap is command-term literalism. The Diploma marks state, outline, explain, deduce and determine as distinct instructions with different answer lengths, and it applies them strictly. MYP descriptors are more holistic. A student used to being rewarded for a thorough answer can lose marks in the Diploma for writing one when a short statement was wanted, and the habit takes a few weeks to change rather than a term.

The table maps the main subject routes with what MYP builds well, what the Diploma assumes, and the specific gap to close. It is written as a preparation list for the summer between the two phases, which is when this work is cheapest and most effective. Six to eight sessions, aimed only at the subjects actually chosen, is normally the whole intervention.
