sections.heading: Reading the report, and the conversation to have with the school
paragraphs: An MYP report rewards being read properly rather than quickly, and most parents are never shown how. Start by listing each subject's four criterion levels side by side and looking for the outlier. A student with levels of six, six, three and six has one problem and it is not the subject. A student with four, four, four and four has a different problem, more likely about task literacy or self-management than about any specific skill, and the plan should differ accordingly.

Then look across subjects at the same criterion type. A low communicating criterion in three subjects at once is one issue with three symptoms, and it is usually about structure rather than about content in any of them. That pattern is invisible if the report is read subject by subject, which is how everybody reads it, and spotting it is the highest-value five minutes a parent can spend each term.

The conversation with the school then becomes specific and useful. Rather than asking how your child is doing, ask which tasks produced the anomalous level, what the task-specific clarification asked for, and what a higher level would have looked like on that task. Teachers answer questions like that readily and precisely, and the answers give a tutor something concrete to work on. Vague questions get reassuring answers, which feel better and change nothing.

For families in this corridor there is a practical note: with parents working in the free zone, these conversations often have to happen by email or at a scheduled time rather than at the school gate. Sending two or three specific questions in writing usually produces a better answer than a hurried conversation would, and it leaves a record that a tutor can work from directly.
bullets: List the four criterion levels side by side and find the outlier
Compare the same criterion type across subjects to spot a single shared cause
Ask which task produced an anomalous level, and what a higher level needed
Specific written questions get specific answers; vague ones get reassurance
Keep the school's reply; it is the brief a tutor should be working from

sections.heading: Scheduling, honesty and what to verify yourself
paragraphs: Sessions here are set around the parent's working day as much as the school run. Students returning from Al Barsha or the coastal schools reach home across the same hours the free zone empties, and Marina or JBR students arrive latest. A slot at 17:30 or later holds through a term; an earlier one is usually rescheduled. Because sessions run online there is no journey, so what the household has to protect is only the hour itself, and written notes after each session cover for the parent who was not there.

Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, treat any specific amount you read as unverified.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page here will claim otherwise. We have no office or centre in the UAE and we do not provide home visits anywhere in the Emirates. We do not publish success rates, satisfaction scores or star ratings, because we could not produce the data behind them. We reference and link official documents rather than reproducing them.

What to verify independently: your school's own criterion-to-grade conversion and its assessment policy, both of which the school will share; which tasks produced which levels, from the subject teacher; and what Personal Project support is permitted, from the supervisor rather than from us. Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and inspection reports are published on its own site rather than summarised accurately anywhere else.

process.title: Send the most recent report
process.description: Not a description of how things are going, but the actual report with the criterion levels on it. Five minutes with it shows whether there is one weak criterion in one subject, one weak criterion type across several subjects, or an even picture that points at task literacy instead. Those three lead to three different plans.

process.title: Add one real task sheet
process.description: A task sheet with its task-specific clarification is the most useful document a parent can send. It shows what the school is actually asking for and in what language, and it lets the first session work on something real rather than on a generic exercise. If a marked piece of work comes with it, better still.

process.title: Free trial lesson on the weakest criterion
process.description: The first session is free and is spent translating the descriptors for that criterion into concrete actions on the student's own task. A short written note follows naming what the criterion wants, what the student is currently doing instead, and what to practise. The note is yours whether or not you continue.

process.title: Fix a slot and agree the reporting
process.description: One weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, after the return from school. Because the parent in this district is usually at work when the session runs, we confirm in advance what arrives afterwards: what was covered, what was set, and which criterion it was aimed at. That record is what makes the next report readable.

process.title: Review against the next report, not against a feeling
process.description: The measure of whether this worked is the criterion level on the next report, which is a specific and public number rather than an impression. If it has not moved, we change the approach or the tutor. If a different criterion has become the weakest, the plan follows it rather than continuing out of habit.

whyPoints.title: We work in criteria, because the school does
whyPoints.description: Progress is named by criterion rather than by subject, which is the only way an MYP grade actually moves. A student weak on investigating patterns needs pattern work, not more equations, and that distinction is invisible unless somebody reads the rubric with them.

whyPoints.title: Task-specific clarifications are read before anything is written
whyPoints.description: Schools rewrite the general descriptors into task language that says precisely what a high level looks like on that piece. Students start writing before reading it. Installing the opposite habit affects every subject group at once and takes one instruction, repeated.

whyPoints.title: Approaches to Learning taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Research, source evaluation, note-taking, citation, staging a long task and structuring an argument are procedures rather than aptitudes. They are assumed by the programme and rarely taught directly, and they are the real content of most MYP tutoring.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit on the Personal Project
whyPoints.description: We coach scope, planning, journal discipline and reflection. We do not write or produce any part of a student's project, and the school supervisor remains the authority on what help is permitted. Publishing the limit is more useful to a parent than any claim about quality.

whyPoints.title: Designed for a parent who is at a desk
whyPoints.description: Written notes after every session, a fixed slot that never needs reconfirming, and an explicit record of what was set and why. In a free-zone household the person arranging support is usually unavailable at the hour it happens, so the reporting is part of the service.

whyPoints.title: The Diploma transition treated as a known, fixable gap
whyPoints.description: MYP builds inquiry and communication well and does not drill technical fluency. We say that plainly and fix it in a short summer block aimed at the subjects actually chosen, rather than pretending the transition is effortless or that the programme has failed.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost for a family near Dubai Internet City?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with IB specialists quoted from about AED 200 to 450 or more. Monthly estimates from the Bestimate Dubai table run around AED 600-1,200 for mid-band weekly support. In-home visits are quoted higher, roughly AED 180-500 an hour, because the fee carries the journey. For MYP students the usual arrangement is one weekly session in one subject, often for a single term, because the work is criterion-specific and finite. Those are market figures with sources rather than our price list; we quote after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why does my child's MYP report have no percentages on it?
faqs.answer: Because the programme does not use them. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, each criterion is marked from zero to eight against published descriptors, and the four levels combine into a subject grade from one to seven using boundaries published in the subject guide. Your school can show you the conversion it applies. The practical consequence is that two children with the same grade can have completely different problems, and that a single weak criterion can hold a grade down while the other three are strong. Reading the four levels side by side is where any useful plan starts.

faqs.question: In MYP mathematics, which of the four criteria cost Dubai students the most levels?
faqs.answer: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion A looks familiar to parents from other systems: content applied accurately, including in unfamiliar situations. The other three are where levels are usually lost. Investigating patterns asks the student to generalise and justify rather than to calculate. Communicating assesses how the mathematics is presented, including notation and reasoning. Applying mathematics in real-life contexts asks for a model, its limitations and a judgement. A student who is fluent in calculation and weak in all three is extremely common and entirely fixable.

faqs.question: Which criterion should we concentrate on first?
faqs.answer: The one furthest behind the others in that subject, and the answer is on the report. If the levels read six, six, three and six, the single weak criterion is holding the grade down and lifting it is the shortest route to a different number. If all four sit at a similar middling level, the problem is more likely task literacy or self-management than any specific skill, and the plan should address that instead. Spreading effort evenly across four criteria produces small gains in each and often does not cross a grade boundary at all.

faqs.question: Why should a student read the task-specific clarification before starting?
faqs.answer: It is the school's rewriting of the general criterion descriptors into language specific to one task, saying what a given level looks like on that particular piece of work. It is usually printed on or attached to the task sheet. Students routinely start writing without reading it, which means they are guessing at what the marker wants when the answer was supplied in advance. Reading it first, and then planning to it rather than to a word count, is the single most transferable habit available in this programme, and it affects every subject group at the same time.

faqs.question: How much help is a tutor allowed to give on the MYP Personal Project?
faqs.answer: With the planning and the thinking, yes; with the work itself, no. A tutor can help a student interrogate their own goal, settle a realistic scope, build a staged timeline, keep the process journal properly, teach research and source evaluation, and respond to the student's own journal with the questions a supervisor would ask. A tutor must never write, draft or produce any part of the project, and must not supply material for a student to adapt. The project is supervised in school, and your child's supervisor is the authority on exactly what help is permitted in their case.

faqs.question: My child is strong in class but the MYP levels are mediocre. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because the criteria reward process and the student is being judged by themselves on product. In sciences, inquiring and designing marks the method and the reasoning behind it. In design, developing ideas marks the documented development rather than the finished solution. In arts, the process journal is assessed alongside the performance. A capable student who produces good outcomes without recording how they got there leaves half the available marks unreachable. The fix is documentation discipline rather than more subject teaching, and it is quick once the student sees the rubric.

faqs.question: How does MYP prepare a student for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Well on inquiry, research, reflection and communication, which are real advantages in the Extended Essay, in internal assessments and in Theory of Knowledge. Less well on sustained technical fluency: higher level mathematics and the Diploma sciences assume from the first week that algebra is automatic and that uncertainty can be carried through a calculation, and MYP builds those in service of inquiry rather than drilling them. The Diploma also applies command terms literally where MYP descriptors are holistic. Six to eight sessions in the summer between the phases closes most of that gap.

faqs.question: We moved to Dubai mid-phase and my child joined MYP 3. What should we expect?
faqs.answer: Typically a student who has the content and not the task literacy, which looks like weakness and is not. The unfamiliar part is the framework: criteria instead of percentages, debatable questions with no single right answer, global contexts that appear in the rubric, and tasks set over weeks rather than overnight. One term of explicit work on reading tasks, planning to descriptors and self-assessing against the rubric usually closes it. The posting cycles of the free zones make this common here, so schools in this corridor are experienced at it; ask what induction support exists.

faqs.question: What are Approaches to Learning skills, in practical terms?
faqs.answer: The skills the programme assumes and few timetables teach directly: thinking, research, communication, social and self-management. In practice that means finding a source and judging whether it is credible, taking notes that can be used rather than copied, citing properly, breaking a three-week task into dated stages, keeping a journal while the work happens, and structuring an argument before writing it. A student weak in research will lose levels in individuals and societies, in sciences and in the Personal Project for the same underlying reason, which is why addressing it directly is efficient.

faqs.question: Does the MYP phase in language acquisition matter more than the year group?
faqs.answer: Yes, and parents are often not told the phase at all. Language acquisition is organised in phases rather than by age, so two students in the same MYP year can be working at different phases with different expectations and different descriptors. Support that ignores the phase aims at the wrong target. Ask the department which phase your child is in, what moving to the next one would require, and which of the four criteria is currently weakest. Those three answers turn a vague worry about languages into a specific and short piece of work.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in Al Sufouh or the Marina for MYP sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. MYP sessions are delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For this programme the format genuinely helps: most of the teaching involves reading a task sheet, a rubric and a set of descriptors side by side, which works better on a shared screen than on paper. Sessions are recorded and a written note follows each one, which matters when the parent is still at work in the free zone.

faqs.question: How long does it take to move an MYP criterion level?
faqs.answer: For a criterion that is weak because of a missing procedure, often a single term. Documentation discipline, reading clarifications, planning to descriptors and self-assessing before submission are habits rather than knowledge, and they show up on the next report. A criterion that is weak because of a genuine content or skill gap takes longer and depends on how often it is assessed. We measure against the next report rather than against a feeling, because the criterion level is a public number and an impression is not.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school at the next parents' evening?
faqs.answer: Three specific questions rather than one general one. Which task produced the lowest criterion level, and what did its task-specific clarification ask for? What would a higher level have looked like on that task? And which criterion would the department prioritise if we could only work on one? Teachers answer questions like those precisely and willingly, and the answers give a tutor a concrete brief. Asking how my child is doing produces a reassuring reply that is pleasant and changes nothing. In this corridor, sending the questions in writing beforehand often works better than the evening itself.

intro.heading: The cheapest window in the IB, and almost nobody uses it
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park sits in the southern corridor, split between DIP 1 and DIP 2, mixing industrial and commercial plots with residential enclaves including Green Community and Ritaj, served by Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Emirates Road and its own Metro station towards Expo City. Two IB schools inside the district run the continuum, so middle-years provision here is better than the industrial land use would suggest.

MYP tutoring is the cheapest tutoring in the IB continuum and the least purchased, for an entirely understandable reason: nothing external is at stake until MYP 5, so nothing feels urgent. Families wait, quite reasonably, and then buy support in DP1 or DP2 at several times the price for problems that began in Year 8 and became expensive by accumulation.

The case for spending earlier is not about MYP grades, which matter less than the reports imply. It is about prevention arithmetic. Two sessions on criterion literacy in Year 8 prevent mid-band levels across several subject groups for the next three years. One session on mathematical generalisation in Year 9 prevents a Diploma exploration built on a pattern the student cannot justify. Two on science inquiry and design prevent a capped internal investigation in DP2 that no later spending recovers.

The first thing to fix, though, is usually free: reading the report. MYP reports carry criterion letters and levels out of eight converted to a grade from one to seven, with no percentages anywhere, and most parents cannot tell whether criterion C level 4 is a problem. That gap is the commonest reason families here seek MYP tutoring, and closing it sometimes removes the need for any.

There is a second free step before any spending, and it is about capacity rather than comprehension. The MYP carries eight subject groups, interdisciplinary units and Service as Action, and in a Dubai school it carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies on top of all of that. In this corridor several hours a week have already gone to the school run before any of it begins. A Year 10 student slipping across several subjects at once is frequently out of hours rather than out of ability, and in that case an audit of the week is the correct response rather than the purchase of a tutor.

If the audit shows there is capacity and the report still does not make sense, that is the point at which outside help earns its place. Even then the honest recommendation in the MYP is usually short, because the common deficit is a habit rather than a body of missing content, and habits transfer across subjects once they are formed.

One premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one MYP tuition into DIP homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. For a middle-years student in this corridor the practical benefit is timing: a session starts when your child gets home rather than after a second car journey, and for a tired twelve-year-old that half hour is worth more than it sounds.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-investment-p.subjectsIntro: The MYP has eight subject groups, each with four criteria. Below is what each assesses, where DIP students most often lose levels, and what the fix costs.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5, standard and extended in MYP 4-5
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where levels go, because generalising a rule and then justifying it is a distinct skill most students treat as optional. One or two sessions.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowledge and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on impacts. Inquiring and designing is the weak point: hypotheses stated without a reason and variables mentioned without being classified. Two to three sessions, and it transfers to the Diploma investigation.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Levels go on analysing, where responses summarise what a text says instead of examining how it creates meaning. Three sessions, and the same skill pays in Diploma Paper 1 unseen analysis.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed by phase rather than year group. The common frustration is a student performing well in class and scoring mid-band because the phase descriptors expect a specific range of structures and registers.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the discriminator: using sources to build an argument rather than decorate one, and naming a source's limitations explicitly rather than implying them.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Levels are lost by students who build something competent without documenting the design cycle, because the documentation is a substantial part of what is assessed.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than students expect, and a strong final piece with a thin journal scores below a developing piece with a well-documented process.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving. The written criteria matter as much as the practical ones, which surprises students who assumed the subject was assessed on the field.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria, requiring integration of knowledge from two subject groups plus reflection on the integration. The common failure is two parallel pieces of subject work presented together with no integration shown. One session.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Planning, applying skills and reflecting, supported by a process journal and a report. Scope is the decisive variable: a narrow goal with a visible process scores well, and an ambitious goal begun late cannot, however impressive the outcome looks.

sections.heading: What each MYP intervention costs, and what it prevents
paragraphs: This is the table that makes the case, because MYP tutoring cannot be justified by MYP grades alone. Each row pairs a small, specific intervention with the much larger problem it prevents two or three years later, and with the market rate so the arithmetic is checkable.

The market, attributed and dated October 2026. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour, with specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above and TutorChase at AED 270. Budget online provision starts at Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

Read the prevention column rather than the cost column. A single session translating a report costs one hour at mid-market rates and prevents years of misreading what the grades mean, which is the condition under which families buy the wrong support repeatedly. Two sessions on criterion literacy lift levels across several subject groups, because the habit of reading a descriptor before writing is subject-agnostic.

The last row is the one with the largest ratio. Four to six sessions in the summer before DP1 prevents a lost first DP1 term, which families then spend a year and considerably more money recovering from. For wider context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package, which makes tutoring the main variable line in most education budgets.

sections.heading: Reading the report, which is usually free
paragraphs: Before any money is spent, the report should be understood, and most of that work can be done at home. MYP reports carry criterion letters with levels out of eight, combined and converted to a grade from one to seven using a published scale. There are no percentages, which is why a parent reading criterion C level 4 has no intuitive sense of whether that is a problem.

The structure is consistent in shape across subjects even though the wording differs. Lower bands describe a response that states or lists. Middle bands describe one that explains or applies with partial success. Upper bands describe one that does so consistently, with justification, and addressing the full demand of the criterion. The gap between a five and a seven is almost always justification and completeness rather than quality of expression.

That is extremely useful, because it means the route upwards is additive rather than mysterious. The response needs a reason attached to the claim, the variable classified rather than mentioned, the generalisation justified rather than stated, the source's limitation named rather than implied. Ask the school for the criterion wording for your child's subjects, and compare it against one piece of marked work. The missing element is usually obvious once both documents are on the table.

Across the competitor pages researched for Dubai IB queries, not one explains how a criterion band works, which leaves families guessing about the central mechanism of the programme their children are in. If reading the report removes the need to buy anything, that is a good outcome, and it is why this section comes before the pricing.

sections.heading: Why the same problem costs more every year
paragraphs: This is the honest financial case for early MYP work, and it is an argument about accumulation rather than about urgency. A specific weakness in Year 8 is a small thing. The same weakness in DP2 has three years of work built on top of it, and the repair has to include everything that was built on the gap.

Take criterion literacy. A Year 8 student who does not read descriptors before writing scores mid-band in several subjects, which looks like general mediocrity and gets attributed to effort. Two sessions fix the habit. The same student in DP1 has three years of mid-band work behind them, a weaker academic self-image, and an assessment system that no longer publishes the descriptor before the task, so the habit now has to be rebuilt in a harder environment.

Or take mathematical generalisation. A Year 9 student who finds patterns and does not justify them loses a criterion level. The same student in DP1 chooses an exploration topic they cannot develop mathematically, which caps the heaviest criterion on a piece of coursework worth 20 marks, and that cannot be recovered after the topic is fixed.

The table below sets out the ratio. It is not an argument for buying tutoring at eleven; it is an argument for knowing which windows are cheap, so that when a family does decide to spend, the money goes somewhere it buys more. In this corridor there is a secondary benefit too: MYP work can use holiday weeks, which carry no school run and are therefore the most productive hours available.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, planned backwards
paragraphs: The Personal Project fails for one reason far more often than any other, and it is scope rather than effort. A student picks an ambitious goal, works on it intermittently, and arrives at the deadline with an impressive-sounding outcome and no evidence of a process. The criteria reward the process, so the outcome alone cannot rescue it.

Planning backwards from the school's deadline solves most of it. The report and completed outcome sit at the end; before them a process journal showing decisions made and changed; before that applied skills with evidence; before that a goal narrow enough that progress can be recorded at all. Each has a sensible date, and your coordinator holds the real deadline, which in this corridor differs between schools by as much as a term.

The process journal is the component students treat as busywork and examiners treat as evidence. It is not a diary. It records decisions, the reasons for them, what was tried and abandoned, and what the student would do differently. A journal written retrospectively in the final fortnight is visible as such and caps the criteria that depend on it.

On the boundary, which matters as much here as in the Diploma: a tutor may narrow the goal, teach what each criterion rewards, ask the questions that expose a plan with no measurable milestones, and comment on the student's own journal and report. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of the project. After each session your child should be able to explain and defend every change in their own words, and the school's academic honesty policy governs the rest.

sections.heading: The transition to DP1, and why it is the best purchase here
paragraphs: Of everything on this page, the summer block between MYP 5 and DP1 has the largest ratio between what it costs and what it prevents. It is four to six sessions. It prevents a lost first DP1 term, which families then spend a year and several times the money recovering from.

The reason it works is that the problem it addresses is specific and known in advance. The MYP asks a student to satisfy a published criterion, with the descriptor available before the task. The Diploma asks a student to answer an examination question under time, where the command term dictates the response shape and the mark scheme is not in front of them. Both are reasonable systems and they reward different behaviours.

The behaviour that transfers badly is comprehensiveness. In the MYP, covering the full demand of a criterion thoroughly tends to score well. In the Diploma, writing everything known about a topic in response to an explain question scores less than answering only what was asked, because unrequested material earns nothing and consumes time other questions needed. Strong MYP writers are therefore disproportionately affected, which is counter-intuitive enough that nobody warns them.

In this corridor the summer has an additional advantage: it carries no school run, so for the first time in the year a student has full attention available at a reasonable hour. The same block is also the right moment for the Diploma subject and level conversation, including the mathematics route, which is confirmed to a school deadline at the end of Year 11 and cannot be revisited afterwards.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: This is the part of an MYP week that no other page about tutoring in this market bothers to mention, and it lands on every single student in a Dubai private school, including the ones whose families moved to Dubai Investments Park for the commute and then chose a school by curriculum alone. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for. KHDA set the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 as the date for schools whose academic year begins in April. For an MYP student that means three subjects sitting alongside the eight subject groups, and they are timetabled, assessed and reported like everything else.

What a parent needs from the detail is the language each of those lessons is taught in, because it decides which tutor is even the right one to hire. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arab students are taught in the language of the school's licensed curriculum. That split is enforced at class level rather than left to the school to interpret. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are strictly prohibited, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction are not the same thing in each group. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must additionally hold appropriate KHDA approval, which is a requirement on the school's own staff rather than on a private tutor, and worth knowing so that nobody sells you a tutor's KHDA approval as though such a thing existed.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools able to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met and a recommendation that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Content is tightly controlled: KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so support works inside the school's own material.

For a DIP family the consequence is arithmetic, and it is sharper here than in a central district. These subjects sit on top of eight subject groups, interdisciplinary units, Service as Action and, in MYP 5, the Personal Project, in a week where several hours have already gone to the school run. A Year 10 or 11 student slipping across several subjects at once is frequently out of hours rather than out of ability, and the right first response is an audit of the week rather than the purchase of a tutor. We would rather say so than take the booking.

sections.heading: Fitting MYP sessions into a corridor week
paragraphs: Middle-years students are more affected by a long school run than Diploma students, and the reason is simply age. Concentration after a 45-minute return journey is genuinely lower at twelve than at seventeen, and a session booked at the wrong hour for a Year 7 student produces compliance rather than learning.

The practical consequence in this corridor is that MYP work often belongs at the weekend even where Diploma work could survive a weekday evening. A Saturday morning session with a rested student is worth two tired weekday ones, and for a family whose child travels to Jebel Ali or Dubai South that is not a preference but an observation.

Where a weekday session is used, keep it short and self-contained. Criterion work suits this well: reading a descriptor against a piece of marked work and identifying the missing element is a forty-minute task with a natural stopping point. Personal Project work does not, because narrowing a goal or reviewing a journal needs continuity, and that belongs in the longer slot.

Holidays are the strongest asset a corridor household has, and in the MYP nothing competes for them. The summer carries the transition block before DP1. Shorter breaks carry criterion work and Personal Project milestones. Nothing depends on a Dubai address, so sessions continue while the family travels, and during Ramadan they commonly move to post-Iftar timing for the month, which for a younger student is often a better hour than a fasting-day afternoon.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Investments Park
paragraphs: Nothing about starting from Dubai Investments Park requires a drive, a meeting, or a phone call you have to schedule around a shift. It takes three attachments: your child's last report, one piece of marked work with the criterion levels still on it, and the name of the school. The marked work does the real work here, because a criterion level on its own is only a number, while the annotated script shows which strand of that criterion the response never reached. The school name supplies the rest, including which MYP year, how the year groups are banded and how the reports are worded. From those three a specialist can say what the work contained and what it lacked in specific terms, and the free trial lesson exists to put that in front of you before any money is involved.

Expect a short recommendation. In the MYP the honest answer is frequently two to four sessions rather than a term, because criterion literacy transfers across subject groups and the fix is a habit rather than a body of content. Saying so costs us the longer booking and gives you a true answer, which is the trade we would rather make.

What will not be claimed. No grade promise, which in a criterion-referenced system is even less meaningful than usual. No suggestion that tutoring is required for progression into the Diploma, for Ministry of Education equivalency or for university admission, because those are processes we do not control. No regulator or board approval: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch. No satisfaction statistics.

A disclosed limit specific to the MYP: some subject groups and language acquisition phases are narrower specialisms than Diploma subjects, so a particular phase at a particular hour may not be coverable immediately. When that happens you are told with a realistic date rather than offered a general tutor as a specialist. And we do not supply IB subject guides or criterion documents, because they are the organisation's copyright; we work from what your school provides.

process.title: Ask what the intervention prevents
process.description: MYP tutoring cannot be justified by MYP grades alone, so the useful question is what a block prevents later: mid-band levels across subjects, a capped DP investigation, a Personal Project without a process, a lost first DP1 term.

process.title: Use the holidays
process.description: In this corridor holiday weeks carry no school run and nothing competes for them, which makes them the most productive hours available. The summer before DP1 is the single best-value block on this page and it sits entirely outside term time.

process.title: Keep the block short and end it
process.description: Criterion literacy is two to four sessions and the habit then transfers on its own. If the recommendation is short, that is the answer rather than an opening position, and stopping when the habit is in place is the correct outcome.

whyPoints.title: Priced against what it prevents
whyPoints.description: Each MYP intervention is set beside the larger problem it avoids two or three years later, with market rates attributed and dated, because MYP tutoring cannot honestly be justified by MYP grades alone.

whyPoints.title: The report explained before anything is sold
whyPoints.description: How criterion bands behave and what separates a five from a seven, with the suggestion that you ask the school for the wording and compare it yourself. If that removes the need to buy anything, it is a good outcome.

whyPoints.title: The accumulation cost made explicit
whyPoints.description: The same weakness costs two sessions in Year 8, four to six in DP1 and a rebuild under deadline pressure in DP2. That is an argument about which windows are cheap, not about urgency.

whyPoints.title: The summer transition identified as the best value
whyPoints.description: Four to six sessions preventing a lost first DP1 term, in a window that carries no school run at all. In this corridor that absence of a commute is worth as much as the content.

whyPoints.title: Age-appropriate scheduling
whyPoints.description: Middle-years concentration after a long bus journey is genuinely lower, so a rested weekend session is often worth two tired weekday ones. The plan is built around that rather than around a standard hour.

whyPoints.title: Short recommendations given honestly
whyPoints.description: In the MYP the answer is frequently two to four sessions, and saying so costs the longer booking. The mandatory UAE subjects are also counted in, because sometimes the right advice is to audit the week instead.

faqs.question: Is MYP tutoring worth buying when nothing external is at stake?
faqs.answer: The case is not about MYP grades; it is about what small interventions prevent later. Two sessions on criterion literacy in Year 8 prevent mid-band levels across several subject groups for three years. One or two on mathematical generalisation in Year 9 prevent a Diploma exploration built on a pattern the student cannot justify. Two on science inquiry and design prevent a capped internal investigation in DP2 that no later spending recovers. Those are the cheapest hours in the continuum.

faqs.question: Can an MYP tutor visit our home in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: No. MYP teaching is delivered one-to-one into DIP homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. For a middle-years student in this corridor the practical benefit is timing: the session starts when your child gets home rather than after a second car journey, and for a tired twelve-year-old that half hour matters more than it does at seventeen.

faqs.question: What does criterion C level 4 actually mean on the report?
faqs.answer: That the response met part of what that criterion asked for and not the rest, with the criterion wording stating precisely which part. Lower bands describe work that states or lists; middle bands work that explains or applies with partial success; upper bands work that does so consistently and with justification. The gap between a five and a seven is usually justification and completeness rather than expression, which means the route upwards is additive and specific rather than mysterious.

faqs.question: How much of this can we work out ourselves?
faqs.answer: A surprising amount, and we would rather you did. Ask the school for the criterion wording for the subjects causing concern and compare it against one piece of marked work. The missing element, such as a reason not attached to a claim or a variable mentioned but not classified, is usually obvious once both documents are on the table. If that removes the need to buy support, that is a good outcome rather than a lost sale.

faqs.question: Why does the same problem get more expensive each year?
faqs.answer: Because of accumulation rather than urgency. A Year 8 student who does not read descriptors before writing scores mid-band across subjects, which two sessions fix. The same student in DP1 has three years of mid-band work behind them and an assessment system that no longer publishes the descriptor before the task, so the habit has to be rebuilt in a harder environment. By DP2 the rebuild happens under deadline pressure, which is the most expensive version of all.

faqs.question: What is the single best-value MYP purchase?
faqs.answer: The summer block between MYP 5 and DP1: four to six sessions on command terms, timed writing and reading a mark scheme. It prevents a lost first DP1 term, which families then spend a year and several times the money recovering from. In this corridor it has a second advantage, because the summer carries no school run, so for the first time in the year the student has full attention available at a reasonable hour.

faqs.question: Our child writes well but keeps getting mid-band levels. Why?
faqs.answer: Because good writing that does not address every element the criterion names sits in the middle bands. MYP criteria are checklists as much as standards: a hypothesis needs a reason attached, a variable needs classifying as independent, dependent or controlled, a pattern needs generalising and then justifying, a source needs its limitation stated. Two to four sessions on reading the descriptor before writing usually moves levels across several subjects at once, because the habit is subject-agnostic.

faqs.question: Our MYP 5 child has not begun the Personal Project. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It depends how early in MYP 5 you are, and the first task is narrowing the goal rather than beginning the work. The criteria reward a visible process, so a goal that cannot show recordable progress cannot score well however impressive the outcome. Maintain the process journal continuously, because one written retrospectively in the final fortnight is visible as such and caps the criteria that depend on it. Your coordinator holds the real deadline, which in this corridor differs between schools by as much as a term.

faqs.question: Where is the line on help with the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: At writing. A tutor may narrow the goal until progress is recordable, teach what each criterion rewards, ask the questions that expose a plan with no measurable milestones, and comment on the student's own journal and report. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of it. The test after a session is whether your child could explain and defend every change in their own words; if not, the line has been crossed and the school's academic honesty policy decides what follows.

faqs.question: Should MYP sessions be at the weekend?
faqs.answer: In this corridor, often yes, and more often than for a Diploma student. Concentration after a 45-minute return journey is genuinely lower at twelve than at seventeen, so a rested Saturday morning session can be worth two tired weekday ones. Where a weekday slot is used, keep it short and self-contained: criterion work against a marked piece is a forty-minute task with a natural stopping point, while Personal Project work needs continuity and belongs in the longer slot.

faqs.question: Why did a thorough interdisciplinary piece only score mid-band?
faqs.answer: Because they are marked against their own criteria, which require integrating knowledge from two subject groups and reflecting on that integration. The commonest failure is two parallel pieces of subject work presented together with no integration demonstrated, which reads as thorough and scores mid-band. One session usually fixes it: the student learns to produce a conclusion that could not have been reached from either subject alone, and to say explicitly how the two combined to produce it.

faqs.question: Are the mandatory UAE subjects part of why our child is stretched?
faqs.answer: Very likely, through the timetable, and more sharply in this corridor than centrally. They are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. They sit on top of eight subject groups, interdisciplinary units, Service as Action and the Personal Project in a week already shortened by the school run.

faqs.question: Our child is slipping in several subjects at once. What should we do first?
faqs.answer: Audit the week before buying anything. In this corridor several hours already go to the journey, and the MYP carries eight subject groups plus the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, interdisciplinary units and Service as Action. A student slipping across several subjects simultaneously is frequently out of hours rather than out of ability. If the audit shows capacity, then compare marked work across two subjects to see whether the deficit is a shared criterion habit.

faqs.question: Is every MYP subject group something you can actually match?
faqs.answer: Not every one at every hour, and you are told when not. Some MYP subject groups and language acquisition phases are narrower specialisms than Diploma subjects, so a particular phase at a particular hour may not be coverable immediately. You will be offered the nearest workable alternative and an honest date rather than a general tutor presented as a specialist. No competitor page in this research set discloses a coverage limit, which cannot be true of any operating service.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-investment-p.closingHeading: Spend small, spend early, or spend much more later
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-investment-p.closingBody: The MYP is the cheapest window in the IB continuum and the one families almost always skip, because nothing external is at stake until MYP 5. The arithmetic is unforgiving: two sessions on criterion literacy in Year 8, or four to six in DP1 in a harder environment, or a rebuild under deadline pressure in DP2. Start by asking the school for the criterion wording and comparing it against one piece of marked work. If you still need help, send the report, that marked piece and the school, and take the free trial lesson. Lessons run live online into your DIP home on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-marina.tutorsIntro: MYP tutors are matched on subject group and on which criterion is costing your child levels, because the four criteria reward genuinely different things. A student losing levels on criterion A needs content work; a student losing them on criterion D needs to be taught how a reflection is judged.

intro.heading: A report with no percentages, and a parent with no reference points
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme produces a report that most parents cannot read on first sight, and that is the usual reason a Marina family starts looking for help. There is no percentage. There is no class rank. There are four letters, each with a number out of eight next to it, and then a grade from one to seven that bears no obvious relationship to anything. A child who was getting eighty per cent in a previous school now has a five in mathematics, and nobody has explained whether that is good.

It is worth saying clearly that the system is not vague; it is just unfamiliar. Each of the eight subject groups is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, and each criterion is scored on a scale from nought to eight against published descriptors. In mathematics, for instance, criterion A is knowing and understanding, B is investigating patterns, C is communicating, and D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In the sciences, A is knowing and understanding, B is inquiring and designing, C is processing and evaluating, and D is reflecting on the impacts of science. The criteria are different in each subject group, which is why a child can be a five in mathematics and a seven in language and literature without that being a contradiction.

This has an immediate consequence for tutoring. Because the criteria differ and because they reward different things, 'my daughter needs help with science' is not actionable. A student scoring well on criterion A and poorly on criterion C has a processing and evaluation problem, which is a skills problem, and re-teaching the content will not touch it. A student in the reverse position has a knowledge gap. The returned assessment, with the criterion levels written on it, tells you which, and it is the first thing a tutor should ask to see.

The second consequence concerns timing, which is where the Marina school run comes in. MYP students are eleven to sixteen, which means they are in school until early or mid afternoon, on a bus that returns somewhere between 3:30pm and 4:30pm, and they have activities two or three afternoons a week. Younger MYP students also tire earlier than Diploma students, so a 7pm session is genuinely less useful for an MYP 2 child than a 5pm one. The slot matters more at this stage than it does later.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send an MYP tutor to a Marina address, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. MYP tuition for UAE families is one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is that a tutor who genuinely knows how the criteria are applied in one subject group can be matched to your child even if nobody within a short drive of your building happens to be that person.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-marina.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme sits in the middle of a continuum, and what a parent should be aiming at depends on which end of it their child is near. The fourth entry covers the optional certificate route, which changes the picture for the schools that offer it.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The stage before the MYP in continuum schools, inquiry-led and without the criterion machinery that arrives in MYP 1. The transition is usually smooth socially and jarring academically, because written work suddenly starts being judged against published descriptors rather than against effort and engagement.
programmes.countryNote: In the Marina cluster this transition is the single most common reason for a first tutoring enquiry about a younger child. The support needed is rarely content; it is learning to write to a descriptor, to structure an extended piece and to proofread, which is a set of habits rather than a body of knowledge.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, each assessed against four lettered criteria scored out of eight. The criterion total out of 32 is converted to a grade from one to seven using published boundaries. The programme core includes approaches to learning, service as action, and a project: the community project in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5.
programmes.countryNote: Around the Marina the MYP runs in the continuum schools in the Meadows, Emirates Hills and Al Sufouh, while neighbouring communities feed British-curriculum schools running IGCSE at the same ages. Families often have one child in each system, and the two need different targets: a descriptor in one case, a markscheme in the other.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The stage after MYP 5 in continuum schools. Six subjects at Standard or Higher Level, externally examined, plus the extended essay, theory of knowledge and creativity, activity and service. The shift from criterion-referenced internal assessment to externally examined papers is the largest change a continuum student experiences.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP 5 to Diploma transition is where the most expensive surprises happen in this cluster. A student with strong MYP grades can meet Diploma mathematics or a Diploma science and find the obstacle is quantitative fluency and examination technique rather than understanding, and addressing that in the summer between the two is far cheaper than addressing it in November.

programmes.name: MYP eAssessment and the IB MYP Certificate
programmes.ageRange: MYP 5, where the school offers it
programmes.description: An optional external route at the end of MYP 5, combining on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios, leading to the IB MYP Certificate. Not every MYP school offers it, and whether yours does changes the final year significantly: it introduces an externally assessed component into a programme that is otherwise internally assessed.
programmes.countryNote: Ask your school directly whether it enters MYP 5 students for eAssessment, because it is the single biggest variable in what the final MYP year looks like for a Marina student. A school that does enter has students sitting on-screen examinations; a school that does not has students finishing on internal assessment and the Personal Project alone.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-marina.subjectsIntro: The eight MYP subject groups each carry their own four criteria, and knowing which letter corresponds to what is how a parent reads a report. Below is each group with its criteria and the one that generates the most enquiries from this cluster.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where capable students lose levels, because investigating patterns requires describing a general rule and justifying it, not just finding the next term. Criterion C penalises missing working and poor notation.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C is the usual weak point: tables without units in the headings, graphs with poor scales, and evaluations that list errors without ranking them. It is also the most teachable of the four.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language. Criterion A asks for analysis of how a writer achieves an effect, and the commonest loss is a response that summarises the text instead. Criterion D covers accuracy and register and is where careless proofreading shows up directly in the level.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D, by phase
subjects.description: Comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Students are placed in a phase rather than a year group, so two children of the same age can be assessed against different expectations, which parents find confusing until it is explained.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D is where the levels are won and lost: it rewards evaluating sources and recognising different perspectives, and a well-written narrative with no evaluation scores modestly however confident it reads.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. Design is the subject families most often dismiss and the one where levels are most easily recovered, because it is largely a documentation discipline: a design folder that records the process properly earns levels a better product without documentation does not.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. As in design, the process journal carries real weight. A student who produces strong work and documents nothing will be marked on what is recorded, which is a hard lesson when it arrives on a report.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. The written components surprise families who assumed this subject was practical, and criteria A, B and D are all desk work that a tutor can help with.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units that deliberately combine two subject groups and are assessed on disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. They are reported separately and they confuse parents more than any other part of the report, because the grade sits alongside the subject grades without belonging to any of them.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Research, thinking, communication, social and self-management skills. These are not separately graded but they are the mechanism by which criterion levels rise, and for a younger MYP student explicit work on note-taking, planning and proofreading often moves levels further than subject content does.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring is for when there is no examination to prepare for
paragraphs: The honest starting point is that a lot of MYP tutoring is sold without anybody defining what it is supposed to achieve. In an examined course the target is obvious. In the MYP there is no paper to practise, no tier to argue about and no boundary to cross, so a weekly hour can continue for a year producing pleasant sessions and no change in the levels on the report.

Defining the target is therefore the whole job. In the MYP the target is always a criterion in a subject group, and the evidence is always the returned assessment with the levels written on it. A child at six on criterion A and three on criterion C in sciences does not need science help; they need to learn how data is processed and evaluated to the standard the descriptor sets out. That is a few sessions of concrete work, not a year of general support.

The second legitimate target is the approaches-to-learning skills that sit underneath every subject group. For younger MYP students these move levels more reliably than content does, because the thing holding the level down is often that the piece was written without a plan, or not proofread, or produced in one evening when it was set three weeks earlier. Those are fixable habits and they improve every subject at once, which makes them the best value available in the whole programme.

The table below sets out, stage by stage, what MYP support is usually for. It is a rough guide rather than a rule, but it is a better starting point than assuming the answer is a weekly hour in the weakest subject.

sections.heading: Reading the report: four criteria, thirty-two points, one grade
paragraphs: Here is the mechanism, in the order a parent needs it. Each subject group has four criteria, lettered A to D. Each criterion is assessed against published descriptors on a scale from nought to eight. Over a reporting period, teachers judge the level that best describes the student's performance on each criterion, giving four numbers. Those four are added to a total out of 32, and the total is converted to a final grade from one to seven using published boundaries.

Two things follow that explain most parental confusion. First, the criteria are different in each subject group, so a five in mathematics and a five in individuals and societies do not represent the same achievement in any comparable sense; they represent similar totals against different descriptors. Second, because four criteria are summed, one weak criterion drags the grade more than a parent expects. A student at seven, seven, seven and three has a total of 24, which sits several points below where their subject understanding would suggest.

That second point is the practical one. It means the fastest route to a better grade is almost always the weakest criterion rather than more work on the strongest. It also means a student can improve substantially in a subject and see no movement in the grade, because the criterion that was holding them down was not the one they worked on. Reading the criterion levels rather than the grade is how a family avoids spending a term on the wrong thing.

The conversion boundaries below are the ones commonly published for the MYP. Confirm them against your own school's reporting documentation, because schools publish their own guidance and the way levels are combined over a reporting period varies in practice. What is not school-specific is the structure: four criteria, eight points each, summed, converted.

sections.heading: The Marina school run, and when an MYP hour genuinely works
paragraphs: MYP students are younger than the Diploma students most tutoring is designed around, and that changes the scheduling arithmetic in a way parents underestimate. An eleven or thirteen year old does not produce useful work at 7:30pm after a full school day, a bus journey and an activity. The quality of an MYP session depends on the slot more than on almost anything else, which makes the Marina school run a genuine constraint rather than a logistical footnote.

The pattern across this cluster is consistent. Buses from the Al Sufouh and Meadows schools return to Marina and JBR addresses somewhere between about 3:30pm and 4:30pm. Al Barsha South and Sports City routes run later, and Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens addresses later still. Activities occupy two or three afternoons. What remains, for most households, is a narrow window between about 4:30pm and 6pm on the uncommitted days, and for younger students that window is where a session has to go.

Where the window does not exist, the weekend is better than a late weekday slot. A Saturday morning session with a rested MYP 2 student is worth considerably more than a Tuesday 7:30pm session with the same child, and families often resist that conclusion because the weekend feels protected. The alternative is paying for an hour in which the student is too tired to produce the work the hour is meant to improve.
