sections.heading: The Personal Project: supervisor, tutor, and the line between them
paragraphs: In MYP 5 every student completes a Personal Project, supervised by a member of staff at the school who confirms the work is the student's own. It is the component families most often want outside help with, and the boundaries are as strict as they are for the Diploma's internally assessed work. A tutor who is vague about those boundaries is a risk rather than a resource.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. Help the student interrogate their own idea for scope, because the commonest failure is a project too large to finish. Explain what the assessment criteria reward and in what language. Teach the research and referencing skills the project assumes. Coach the process journal, which carries real weight and which students routinely treat as an afterthought to be filled in retrospectively. Read a draft the student has written and give feedback the student then implements themselves. Help with time management against the school's own deadlines.

What a tutor must not do is equally clear. A tutor does not choose the project, does not write the report, does not draft any section of it, and never edits the student's Personal Project to completion. The supervisor of record is the school. Where a provider offers to produce the work, that is academic malpractice, the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller, and in this market at least one provider sells completed assessed work as a product. Ask the direct question before booking anybody and treat a hedged answer as the answer.

The most useful intervention, in practice, is early and unglamorous. Most Personal Project difficulty is scope and sequencing rather than ability: a student picks something that cannot be completed in the time available, or leaves the journal empty for ten weeks and then cannot reconstruct the process. Thirty minutes spent on the plan in the first fortnight prevents more trouble than several hours spent on the report in the last one.
bullets: Scope is the commonest failure; the project is too large to finish, not too hard
The process journal carries weight and cannot honestly be reconstructed later
A tutor coaches the process; a tutor never writes or redrafts the report
The school supervisor remains the person who confirms the work is the student's own

sections.heading: eAssessment: the question that changes the final MYP year
paragraphs: One question changes what MYP 5 looks like more than any other, and many parents in this cluster have never been asked it: does your school enter MYP 5 students for eAssessment? The route combines on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios and leads to the IB MYP Certificate. It is optional, schools decide, and the decision is not always prominent in the information families receive.

If your school does enter, the final MYP year contains an externally assessed component in a programme that is otherwise internally assessed, and that changes the preparation materially. On-screen examinations are timed, and timed assessment is something many MYP students have had very little practice at, because criterion-referenced tasks are usually produced over days or weeks. A student who writes well over three evenings can write poorly in ninety minutes, and discovering that during the assessment itself is avoidable.

If your school does not enter, MYP 5 finishes on internal assessment and the Personal Project, and the preparation that matters is different: it is about the transition into the Diploma rather than about an examination. In that case the sensible use of the final MYP terms is building the examination technique and quantitative fluency Year 12 will assume, because nothing in the MYP will have required either.

Either way, the useful thing a parent can do is ask the question and then plan accordingly. It is a one-line email to the MYP coordinator. The answer determines whether the final year needs timed practice built into it or whether the available time is better spent bridging into the Diploma, and those are substantially different uses of the same months.

sections.heading: From MYP 5 into the Diploma: the gap nobody budgets for
paragraphs: The most expensive educational problem in this cluster is not an MYP grade. It is the first term of the Diploma, when a student with strong MYP results meets externally examined courses and finds the obstacle is not understanding. It is quantitative fluency, timed writing, and the examination technique a criterion-referenced programme never required. New Diploma content arrives weekly from the first week, so there is no quiet period in which to catch up, and families end up buying far more support in Year 12 than a short bridging block would have cost.

The gaps are specific rather than general. For mathematics: algebraic manipulation at speed and without error, and comfort with a graphic display calculator if the school expects one. For the sciences: the mole and quantitative chemistry, uncertainty handling, and the discipline of carrying units through a multi-step calculation. For every subject: writing to time, which is a skill in itself, and answering the command term that was used rather than the one the student expected.

A block across the final MYP term and the summer handles this, and it has a clear end point, which makes it easier to judge than an open commitment. Because so many families in this cluster travel for long stretches of the summer, it is worth noting that a lesson delivered over live video follows the laptop, so the block can run across time zones rather than being abandoned in July and restarted too late in August.

There is a related decision worth taking deliberately rather than by default. A continuum student is not obliged to continue into the Diploma; several British-curriculum sixth forms in this cluster take students at 16 from MYP, and the A Level route suits some students better. The question to put to both your current school and any target school is what each assumes a student arriving from MYP 5 already has, because the answers differ and they tell you what the bridging block should contain.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs, and why it sits lower in the market
paragraphs: MYP support generally sits in the lower half of the published Dubai rate bands, and it is worth understanding why before judging a quote. Examination-specialist pricing reflects knowledge of a particular paper, a particular markscheme and a particular set of grade boundaries. MYP work rewards something else: knowing how the criteria are applied and being able to teach a thirteen year old to plan, draft and proofread. That is valuable and it is not the same scarce commodity as a Higher Level examiner's knowledge, so the market prices it differently.

The published figures, each attributed and recorded in October 2026, are these. EdFlik advertises tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table places IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 with home tutors reaching AED 500, and BartyED quotes AED 650 at the named end. Monthly estimates from that table run AED 240 to 600 for a weekly budget session, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A packaged offer of AED 799 a month for eight online sessions appears in the market.

For an MYP student the practical implication is that the top of that range is usually unnecessary and the bottom is often adequate for approaches-to-learning work, while criterion-specific subject work in MYP 4 and 5 sits sensibly in the middle. The in-home premium, which published rates put at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 online, buys travel rather than better teaching, and for a younger student it has a second cost: a visiting tutor arriving at 6pm is arriving after the point at which the child could have used the hour.

Worth adding for context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees remain the dominant number in a family's education budget, and five years of MYP is a long period over which to carry an unnecessary tutoring commitment. None of the figures above is an IB Gram price and we publish no rate card on these pages; the sensible first step is a free trial lesson and an honest view of whether weekly support is needed at all.

sections.heading: What to ask before buying any MYP tutoring
paragraphs: Because the MYP has no paper to point at, this is the stage of schooling where tutoring is most easily sold on reassurance rather than on need. Four questions protect a family from that, and they are all answerable in a first conversation.

Ask the tutor to name the four criteria for the subject group in question and say what each one rewards. Somebody who works in the MYP answers immediately; somebody who teaches the subject but not the programme will describe content instead. Ask which criterion they think is holding your child's grade down, having seen the returned assessment, and listen for a specific letter rather than a general comment. Ask what the first three sessions will cover and why those. And ask what they will do if your child sends a Personal Project draft two days before the deadline, because the honest answer is feedback the student must implement themselves, and two days may not be enough for that to help.

Then one question for the school rather than the tutor, and it is the most useful of all: what would you like us to work on at home? MYP teachers generally answer this precisely, naming a criterion and a skill, and it is free. A surprising number of tutoring commitments in this cluster would be shorter, cheaper or unnecessary if that question had been asked first.

One final point on what no provider should claim. No tutoring company is approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the IB, KHDA or any other authority unless it holds the specific thing it names and can produce the document; IB Gram holds none of them, operates no UAE office or centre, and does not publish a star rating it generated about itself. Private tutoring in the UAE does require the individual to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued free of charge for two years, so asking a prospective tutor whether they hold it is both reasonable and easy to answer.
bullets: Name the four criteria for this subject group and say what each rewards
Which criterion is holding the grade down, and what in the assessment shows that?
What will the first three sessions cover, and why those?
Ask the school directly what they would like worked on at home

process.title: Send the returned assessment, not the report card
process.description: The document with the criterion letters and levels written on it is the diagnostic. A photograph is enough. The report grade tells us a total; the criterion levels tell us which of four very different things is wrong, and that determines everything about what the sessions should contain.

process.title: Tell us the age and the afternoon shape
process.description: MYP covers eleven to sixteen, and an MYP 1 student and an MYP 5 student need different things at different times of day. Give the bus return time for your address and the committed afternoons, so the slot lands in the window where your child can actually produce work.

process.title: Ask the school what to work on
process.description: Before the trial, send the MYP coordinator or subject teacher one line asking what they would like supported at home. They usually answer with a criterion and a skill, it costs nothing, and it frequently shortens or removes the need for a tutoring commitment altogether. We would rather you asked.

process.title: Take the free trial on a real piece of work
process.description: One session at no cost, spent on something your child has already submitted and had assessed, with the criterion levels visible. You get a written note naming the criterion being targeted and what the first few sessions will do. Where the honest answer is approaches-to-learning work rather than subject content, the note will say so.

process.title: Review against the next reported levels
process.description: Progress in the MYP is judged on the criterion levels in the next reporting period, not on how sessions felt. If the targeted criterion has moved and the others held, it worked. If nothing moved, the target was wrong and we change it rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: We work from criterion levels, not from grades
whyPoints.description: A grade is a sum of four very different judgements, and one weak criterion drags it further than parents expect. Starting from the returned assessment rather than the report card is what stops a family spending a term improving the criterion that was already strong.

whyPoints.title: Approaches to learning treated as real work
whyPoints.description: For MYP 1 to 3, planning before writing, proofreading as a routine and managing a multi-week task move levels across every subject group at once. It is rarely what a parent asks for and it is frequently the highest-yield support in the programme.

whyPoints.title: Honest about when tutoring is not the answer
whyPoints.description: The MYP is the stage where tutoring is most easily sold on reassurance. We would rather you asked the subject teacher what to work on at home first, and we will say plainly when the answer is a shorter block, a different criterion, or nothing at all.

whyPoints.title: Personal Project coached, never produced
whyPoints.description: A tutor helps a student test the scope of their own idea, explains what the criteria reward, teaches research and referencing, coaches the process journal and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not choose, write or redraft the project. The school supervisor remains the person who confirms authorship.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled for a younger student's day
whyPoints.description: An eleven or thirteen year old produces little of value at 7:30pm after a bus and an activity. Sessions are placed in the window between the school run and the evening, or moved to a weekend morning where that window does not exist, because the slot affects the outcome more at this age than later.

whyPoints.title: A bridge into the Diploma with an end point
whyPoints.description: The expensive problem is the first Diploma term, not the MYP grade. A defined block covering algebraic fluency, quantitative science work and timed writing before Year 12 begins costs a fraction of remediation in November, and it finishes rather than continuing indefinitely.

faqs.question: What do the letters and numbers on my child's MYP report actually mean?
faqs.answer: Each subject group is assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, and each criterion is scored from nought to eight against published descriptors. The four scores are added to a total out of 32, and that total converts to a final grade from one to seven. The criteria differ between subject groups, so a five in mathematics and a five in individuals and societies are not the same achievement in any comparable sense. The practical consequence is that the criterion levels tell you far more than the grade does, because one weak criterion pulls the total down several points.

faqs.question: Why has my son's grade not moved even though his understanding has improved?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because the criterion holding him down is not the one he has been working on. Four criteria are summed, so a student at seven, seven, seven and three has a total of 24 and a grade well below what his subject understanding suggests. Improving the strong criteria changes very little. The weak one is where the points are. Look at the returned assessments rather than the report, find the lowest letter, and target that specifically. In the sciences it is frequently criterion C, processing and evaluating, which is a skills problem rather than a knowledge one.

faqs.question: Is an MYP tutor even necessary when there are no exams?
faqs.answer: Often not, and this is the stage of schooling where tutoring is most easily bought on reassurance. Before committing, send the subject teacher or MYP coordinator one line asking what they would like supported at home. They usually answer with a specific criterion and a specific skill, it costs nothing, and it frequently shortens or removes the need. Where support genuinely helps is narrow: one criterion in one subject group, or approaches-to-learning habits for a younger student. A general weekly hour with no defined target can run for a year and change nothing.

faqs.question: My daughter has just moved from PYP into MYP 1 and is struggling. What changed?
faqs.answer: Work started being judged against published descriptors rather than against effort and engagement, and that is a genuine shift rather than a harder syllabus. What usually holds a new MYP 1 student back is not content: it is writing without a plan, not proofreading, and producing in one evening something that was set three weeks earlier. Those are habits and they respond quickly. Reading the actual descriptor with the student, so they can see what is being judged, is often the single most useful hour anybody spends with them in that first year.

faqs.question: What is the most common reason a Personal Project goes wrong?
faqs.answer: Scope, not ability. Students choose something that cannot be completed in the time the school has allocated, and the realisation arrives too late to change direction cleanly. The second most common reason is an empty process journal: ten weeks pass, nothing is recorded, and the process cannot honestly be reconstructed afterwards because the journal is meant to document decisions as they happen. Thirty minutes spent testing the plan in the first fortnight prevents far more trouble than several hours spent on the report in the last one.

faqs.question: How much help is a tutor allowed to give with the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: A substantial amount, within clear limits. A tutor may help the student interrogate their own idea for scope, explain what the assessment criteria reward and in what language, teach research and referencing skills, coach the process journal, give feedback on a draft the student has written, and help with time management against the school's deadlines. A tutor must not choose the project, write the report, draft any section or edit it to completion. The school supervisor confirms the work is the student's own, and at least one provider in this market sells completed assessed work, which puts the student at risk rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Does our school enter MYP 5 students for eAssessment, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: Ask the MYP coordinator directly, because it is optional, schools decide, and it changes the final MYP year more than anything else. The route combines on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios and leads to the IB MYP Certificate. If your school enters, the final year contains timed external assessment in a programme that is otherwise internally assessed, and timed work is something many MYP students have had very little practice at. If your school does not enter, the final year finishes on internal assessment and the Personal Project, and the available time is better spent bridging into the Diploma.

faqs.question: What time of day works best for an MYP session in the Marina?
faqs.answer: Earlier than families expect. Buses from the Al Sufouh and Meadows schools return to Marina and JBR addresses between about 3:30pm and 4:30pm, with Al Barsha South, Sports City and Al Furjan routes later. Activities occupy two or three afternoons. What is left is a narrow window between roughly 4:30pm and 6pm on uncommitted days, and for an eleven to thirteen year old that is where a session has to go. Where the window does not exist, a Saturday morning with a rested student is worth considerably more than a 7:30pm weekday hour with a tired one.

faqs.question: Why is my child a seven in English and a four in maths under the same system?
faqs.answer: Because the criteria are different in each subject group and reward different abilities. Language and literature assesses analysing, organizing, producing text and using language. Mathematics assesses knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student who writes analytically and dislikes justifying a general rule will do well on one set and less well on the other, and the two grades are not measuring the same thing. It is not a contradiction and it does not mean one teacher is marking harder than the other.

faqs.question: What should we do in the final MYP terms to get ready for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Build the two things the MYP never required. Quantitative fluency, meaning algebraic manipulation at speed and without error, plus the mole and unit discipline for a chemistry-bound student and uncertainty handling for any science. And writing to time, which is a distinct skill from writing well, because criterion-referenced tasks are usually produced over days. Add graphic display calculator comfort if the school expects one. A defined block across the final term and the summer does it, with an end point, and it costs a fraction of repairing the same gap during a first Diploma term.

faqs.question: How much should MYP tutoring cost compared with Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: Less, and for a legitimate reason. Examination-specialist pricing reflects knowledge of a particular paper, markscheme and set of boundaries; MYP work rewards knowing how the criteria are applied and being able to teach a thirteen year old to plan, draft and proofread. Published Dubai figures recorded in October 2026 run from AED 33 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and Tutopiya, AED 150 upwards at Unitors for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, AED 270 at TutorChase, and AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists in Bestimate's rate table. For most MYP work the middle of that range is sufficient and the top is unnecessary.

faqs.question: Do you send an MYP tutor to our home in Dubai Marina?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. MYP tuition for UAE families is delivered one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For a younger student there is a specific advantage: a visiting tutor arriving at 6pm after a drive is arriving past the point at which an MYP 2 child can use the hour well, whereas a session with no journey attached can start at 4:45pm. The in-home rates quoted on this page are other providers' published market figures, not an offer.

faqs.question: What are interdisciplinary units and why is there a separate grade for them?
faqs.answer: They are units that deliberately combine two subject groups and are assessed against their own criteria, covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. They are reported separately, which is why a grade appears on the report that does not belong to any single subject. They confuse parents more than any other element of MYP reporting. For tutoring purposes they rarely need separate attention: a student who can plan, structure and reflect in their individual subjects usually performs adequately in the interdisciplinary unit as well.

faqs.question: Can one tutor help across several MYP subject groups?
faqs.answer: For approaches-to-learning work, yes, and that is the case where it is actually preferable: planning, note-taking, proofreading and long-task management are general habits and a single person teaching them consistently across subjects is better than three people teaching them separately. For criterion-specific subject work the answer is no, because the four criteria differ by subject group and someone who knows how criterion B is applied in mathematics will not necessarily know how criterion C is applied in the sciences. Decide which of the two you are buying before you book.

faqs.question: Should my child stay in the IB after MYP 5 or move to A Levels?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student rather than on the programmes, and it is a decision worth taking deliberately rather than by default because a continuum student is not obliged to continue. Several British-curriculum sixth forms in this cluster take students at 16 from MYP. The Diploma suits students who work across breadth and manage several deadlines at once; A Levels suit students who want depth in three or four subjects. Ask both your current school and any target school what they assume a student arriving from MYP 5 already has, because the answers differ and they tell you what bridging work is needed.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-marina.closingHeading: Start with the criterion, not the subject
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-marina.closingBody: If you are looking for MYP support for a child in Dubai Marina, two things make the decision straightforward. Find the returned assessment with the criterion letters and levels written on it, because that shows which of four very different things is holding the grade down. Then send one line to the subject teacher asking what they would like supported at home, which is free and frequently makes the tutoring shorter or unnecessary. If a session is still the right answer, the free trial is spent on a real piece of your child's assessed work, delivered one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, in a slot placed where a younger student can still think.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-media-city.tutorsIntro: These tutors work with Middle Years students from the Al Sufouh, Marina and Al Barsha communities. Each has marked against MYP criterion descriptors in a specific subject group, and each takes the evening slots this corridor needs after the bus gets back.

intro.heading: The Middle Years Programme is the hardest thing in Dubai to buy help for
paragraphs: Dubai Media City is a free zone of offices and studios in Al Sufouh, between Sheikh Zayed Road and the sea, with Dubai Internet City inland and Dubai Knowledge Park along the tram line. It has residential towers and no school. Middle Years students living here travel out, most often to the Al Barsha South continuum schools or to the IB schools in Emirates Hills, and come home in the late afternoon.

The scarcity problem is sharper for the MYP than for anything else. KHDA's 2024-25 figures record 387,441 students across 227 private schools licensed for 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian schools at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. The IB is the smallest of the four. Within it, the Diploma is the best-known programme, and the Middle Years Programme is smaller again because several Dubai continuum schools run a British middle school and only pick the IB up at 16.

Multiply that down and the pool of adults who have actually marked MYP work in a specific subject group becomes very thin. Plenty of good teachers around Al Sufouh can teach a thirteen-year-old science or English well. Far fewer can look at a criterion C score of 4 in MYP Sciences and say which sentence in the student's write-up stopped it being a 6. That second skill is the one you are trying to buy, and it is not distributed geographically.

This is made worse by the reporting. The MYP has no public paper in most subjects, so there is no artefact a parent can inspect. Grades arrive as four criterion scores out of eight, which the school converts with a published boundary table into a 1 to 7 subject grade, and alongside them sit comments about approaches to learning. A parent reading Criterion B: 4 has no way of telling whether that is a content gap, a method problem or a write-up problem, and those three need completely different interventions.

So the first useful hour of MYP tutoring is diagnostic rather than instructional. Put the student's own marked task and the school's rubric in front of someone who knows the descriptors, and the answer usually arrives within twenty minutes. Without that, buying MYP support is buying general subject teaching, which the school already supplies and which the criterion scores have already told you is not the issue.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm. For a programme where the scarce resource is criterion expertise rather than proximity, widening the pool to everyone teaching in this time zone is not a compromise. It is the only way the match gets made properly.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-media-city.programmesIntro: Around Media City, a child of Middle Years age may be in any of these. The programme decides whether tutoring is criterion work, paper practice or something else entirely.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups studied together, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, with the subject grade built from tasks across the year rather than from an examination. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project. Interdisciplinary units and service as action run alongside, and approaches to learning skills are reported on separately from subject achievement.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP is the minority middle-school route even inside IB schools, because several continuum schools enter students for IGCSE at 16 instead. For a Media City family that means a child in MYP 4 may have classmates heading for IGCSE and classmates heading straight into the Diploma, and the subject decisions taken in MYP 4 start to diverge from that point.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored out of 45. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth a fifth to a quarter of the grade. The step up from MYP is less about content than about carrying six sets of internal deadlines at once.
programmes.countryNote: UAE IB schools sit the May session, with November as the second sitting. Specific IB session and results dates are not published here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself; the school's IB coordinator is the authority. The Diploma is offered at GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh and Dubai American Academy in Al Barsha among others.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and organised by transdisciplinary themes, ending with the Grade 5 Exhibition. Reports describe approaches to learning rather than marks, which families arriving from British, Indian or American primaries find hard to interpret. The transition into MYP 1 is where the criterion system first appears, and it surprises most parents.
programmes.countryNote: The nearest full IB continuum primaries to Media City sit in Al Barsha South and Emirates Hills rather than in Al Sufouh, so primary families here are already making a reasonable journey. Where a child will continue into the MYP, the useful preparation is extended writing stamina and number fluency rather than coverage of a curriculum.

programmes.name: The IGCSE route at 16 instead
programmes.description: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, externally examined, with syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0620 Chemistry. This is what most 14 to 16 year olds in this part of Dubai are doing, and it is also the route some IB continuum schools switch their own students onto at MYP 4.
programmes.countryNote: The two systems assess almost nothing the same way. MYP marking rewards process, investigation and reflection against descriptors; IGCSE rewards answering a past-paper question in the language of a mark scheme. A tutor who is strong on one is not automatically useful on the other, and in MYP 4 and 5 that mismatch is the most common one in this corridor.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-media-city.subjectsIntro: MYP students study all eight groups simultaneously, so a request from this corridor is almost never a whole subject. It is one criterion inside one group. These are the places marks go.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.levels: English, plus other first languages by school
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Criterion A is the hard one: it wants interpretation supported by close textual reference, not summary. Strong readers narrate what happens. The work is annotation discipline and writing about how a writer builds an effect rather than what the passage contains.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.levels: Phases 1-6, usually French, Spanish or Arabic
subjects.description: Four criteria across listening, reading, speaking and writing, with the phase setting the expected standard. The frequent Dubai problem is a student placed in a phase above their measured ability because of years of informal exposure. Support is phase-appropriate output practice with a lot of structured speaking.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criterion A rewards specific terminology and examples; criterion D rewards evaluated sources and a defensible judgement. Students raised on narrative history describe. The repair is command-term drilling, because analyse, evaluate and justify ask for three different paragraph shapes and MYP marking notices which arrived.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.levels: Integrated, or separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics
subjects.description: Criterion B wants a method a stranger could repeat; criterion C the processing and evaluation of the student's own data. Criterion C is where most marks are lost: the graph is drawn, the trend described, and the evaluation of method limitations never arrives. Taught as a structure, it moves quickly.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B stalls capable students because it wants a general rule justified and tested, not a correct answer produced. The MYP 4 pathway decision also shapes what is comfortable in the Diploma.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The portfolio is the assessment and it fails on documentation rather than on making. Students build something that works and lose criterion A marks for a thin research stage. The design cycle write-up is where almost all the marks sit.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, responding. The process journal carries the marks, which means a genuinely talented student can sit at a 4 because the developmental record is thin. Support is journal structure, artist research and critical response language rather than technique coaching.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, reflecting on performance. The written and reflective criteria frequently pull the grade down, since practical ability carries only part of the mark. Support is usually short and focused on planning and reflection documents.

subjects.name: MYP Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. Support reinforces the school's own material rather than importing a syllabus.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed units that combine two subject groups, marked against their own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection. Students treat them as a project and lose marks for not making the synthesis explicit. One session on what synthesis looks like in writing usually fixes it.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Self-directed, with a process journal and a report, externally moderated. A supervisor at school signs off the process. A tutor may teach planning, research method, referencing and reflection and may give feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write, draft or produce any part of it.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Thinking, communication, social, self-management and research skills, which appear on the report in their own right. Self-management is the one that most often explains a scattered set of criterion scores, and it is addressed by fixing the week rather than by teaching more content.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-media-city.regionsTitle: Where Middle Years students around Media City live
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-media-city.regionsIntro: The MYP population in this corridor is dispersed, and the journey home varies more than the school choice does. These are the communities we work with and what each means for scheduling.

regions.note: Sharing the Metro station and the street pattern, with limited residential stock and similar school destinations. Requests here skew to MYP 4 and MYP 5, usually when a route decision at 16 is approaching and the criterion scores are inconsistent.

regions.note: University and training campuses along the tram line with residential towers attached. Fewer Middle Years students than the surrounding areas, and the requests that do come tend to be MYP 5 Personal Project coaching rather than subject work.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha South and the inland continuum cluster
schoolClusters.note: The nearest schools running the MYP through its full five years rather than switching to IGCSE. Short drive inland from Media City, and the cluster that produces most of the Design and Sciences criterion requests in this corridor.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills and the villa belt
schoolClusters.note: Two long-established IB continuum schools with full Middle Years provision. Families from the Media City towers often choose these and accept the longer bus journey, which is what pushes session times into the evening.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and the tram corridor
schoolClusters.note: The gates genuinely near Media City, where the IB appears mainly at Diploma level rather than in the middle years. Useful context because a neighbour's child at the same school may be on an entirely different system at 14.

sections.heading: Who actually teaches the MYP, and why the pool is so small
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in Dubai Media City means a subject-group specialist who has marked against MYP criterion descriptors, teaching one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The phrase sounds narrow and it is. Dubai has 227 private schools running 17 curricula, the IB holds roughly 7 per cent of enrolment, and the Middle Years Programme is a subset of that because several continuum schools switch to IGCSE at 14.

That arithmetic is why a local search for MYP help returns mostly general tutors. The people advertising in Al Barsha and the Marina are selected for being findable, not for having supervised an MYP Design portfolio or marked Individuals and Societies criterion D. Many are excellent teachers of the underlying subject, and for a student who simply needs algebra fluency that is sufficient. For a student whose criterion C scores are stuck, it is not.

There is a quick way to tell the difference in conversation. Ask which four criteria the subject group uses and what the top band of one of them asks for. Someone who has marked the work answers in descriptor language without hesitating. Someone who has not talks about building confidence and filling gaps, which is a description of general tutoring and an honest signal.

Once the subject-group question is settled, proximity stops being interesting. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run over live video, which means an Al Sufouh family can work with the person who has actually marked MYP Design in Sharjah rather than with the nearest available adult who holds an engineering degree.

sections.heading: The eight subject groups and what each criterion actually rewards
paragraphs: Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, each out of eight, and the school converts the raw total using a published boundary table into a 1 to 7 grade. The criteria are named differently across subject groups, which is precisely why a report card is hard to read, but the underlying structure is consistent enough to be diagnostic.

Broadly, the first criterion rewards knowing and understanding: accurate subject terminology applied to a situation rather than recalled in isolation. The second rewards process, which in Sciences is a repeatable method, in Mathematics a justified general rule and in Design a research stage with real analysis in it. The third rewards communication or the handling of results. The fourth rewards evaluation and reflection, and it is the most routinely abandoned because it comes last and students run out of time.

The practical consequence is that the highest-value tutoring move is rarely more content. It is reading the actual descriptor for the band above the student's current one and rewriting a single paragraph of their own recent work to match it. Students find this surprising the first time, because the descriptor for a top band almost never asks for more words. It asks for a judgement justified against evidence the student produced themselves.

The table maps the four criteria across the groups most requested from this corridor. Exact names and strands are set by the current subject guide and your child's school is the authority on which version it is running, so use this to read the report rather than to argue with the teacher.

sections.heading: Approaches to learning: what the report card is really telling you
paragraphs: Alongside criterion scores, an MYP report comments on approaches to learning: thinking, communication, social, self-management and research skills. Parents tend to skim these as pastoral commentary. They are frequently the most diagnostic part of the document, especially when the criterion scores are scattered rather than uniformly low.

A student with a 7 in one criterion and a 3 in another, across several subjects, usually has a self-management problem rather than a subject problem. Tasks are started late, drafts are not revisited, and the criteria that come last in a piece of work are the ones that suffer. No amount of subject teaching fixes that, and buying subject teaching for it is the commonest way MYP tutoring money is wasted in this corridor.

Research skills are the other quiet signal. The MYP asks students to find, evaluate and reference sources from quite early on, and a student who has never been taught to do it properly produces work that is penalised under criteria which look like subject criteria. This is cheap to fix, generalises across every subject group at once, and is almost never the thing a family asks for.

The practical reading is simple. Uniformly low criterion scores in one subject point at that subject. Scattered scores across several subjects point at the week, the organisation or the research habits, and the honest first intervention is a conversation about how the student works rather than an hour of teaching. We would rather say that than sell six sessions of Sciences to a student whose actual problem is that every task is started the night before.
bullets: Scattered criterion scores across subjects point at self-management, not content
Uniformly low scores in one subject point at that subject

sections.heading: Projects, service and the honesty line
paragraphs: The MYP carries project work through its whole length and ends with the Personal Project in MYP 5: a self-directed piece with a goal the student sets, a process journal kept across the year, and a report that is externally moderated. Some schools also run a community project in MYP 3 or MYP 4, and service as action runs throughout. All of it is the student's own work by definition.

The boundary is easy to state and routinely crossed in this market. A tutor may teach research method, referencing conventions, source evaluation, how to keep a journal that genuinely evidences development, and how to write a reflection that answers the criterion. A tutor may read the student's own draft and say precisely where a paragraph fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write any part of the project, may not restructure a draft on the student's behalf, and may not supply a model report to be adapted.

One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. The risk in that transaction sits with the student, not the provider: a moderator who sees a report written in an adult register, or a process journal with no development in it, has grounds to question authenticity, and the school supervisor is the person who signs the process off. Genuine coaching produces a journal that looks messy and dated, which is exactly what defends the work.

A good test of any provider, this one included: ask what their tutor does with a weak draft. The honest answer is that it comes back marked against the descriptor with instructions to rewrite. Any answer in which the tutor improves the text directly is an answer about that provider's risk appetite rather than about teaching.
bullets: A tutor teaches method, referencing, journal discipline and reflective writing
A tutor comments on the student's own drafts against published descriptors
A tutor never writes, drafts, restructures or supplies model project work

sections.heading: MYP 5 to Diploma or IGCSE: the decision and the gap
paragraphs: At 16, a Dubai MYP student takes one of two routes: into the IB Diploma, or into IGCSE and then A Levels or the Diploma afterwards. Some continuum schools make the decision for the cohort; others leave it to the family. Either way the groundwork was laid earlier, and the mathematics pathway chosen in MYP 4 is the single most constraining element.

The step into the Diploma is a step up in volume rather than in difficulty. Six subjects, three Internal Assessments running at once, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, all with school deadlines months before any examination. MYP students generally arrive with better extended writing and reflection habits than IGCSE students, and worse quantitative speed. Both gaps are visible in the first term and both are cheaper to close in the summer before it.

The step into IGCSE is a step sideways into a different assessment logic. A student who has spent five years being marked against descriptors has to learn to answer a past-paper question in mark-scheme language, under time, with no credit for process. That is a learnable skill and it takes a term, and it is the reason MYP students sometimes underperform in their first IGCSE mocks despite being perfectly well taught.

The table sets out what each route assumes, so a family can see where the work has to go. Confirm specifics with the school, since entry expectations differ between institutions and between intake years.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs, and the one thing a report card cannot price
paragraphs: Published rates in Dubai divide cleanly. Budget online tutoring runs from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors working online are published from AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors at IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutoring reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

For the MYP the tier question is unusual, because the thing you are paying for is criterion literacy rather than subject depth. A budget tutor can teach the content of MYP Sciences perfectly adequately and cannot tell you why criterion C is stuck at 4, which is the only question you actually asked. That pushes MYP work towards the qualified and specialist bands not because the content is hard but because the marking knowledge is rare.

In-home visits are published between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's band at AED 180 to AED 350. Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. For a programme where marks accumulate from weekly tasks, eight contacts beat four decisively, and the in-home package costs roughly double. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist support.

Those are other providers' published figures, not IB Gram prices. The thing a report card cannot price is the diagnosis: until someone who knows the descriptors has looked at the student's own marked task, you do not know whether you are buying four sessions or a term. That is why the first lesson is free and produces a written note, and why the note is worth reading before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects inside an MYP timetable
paragraphs: A Dubai MYP timetable has to carry eight subject groups plus the subjects every private school in the emirate is required to teach. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

The rules are specific, and they explain a good deal about why MYP timetables are tight. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic must be the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

For a parent, the practical effect is that eight MYP subject groups and the mandatory subjects compete for the same week, which is one reason criterion D so often goes unfinished. It is also why adding tutoring in three subjects is frequently counterproductive: the student does not have spare hours, and the hours you buy come out of the task time the criteria are actually measuring.

Two constraints shape what honest tutoring in the mandatory subjects looks like. KHDA requires schools to ensure all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach them, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support therefore reinforces the school's own material and builds language fluency rather than importing a parallel syllabus. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, and has no UAE office.

sections.heading: When the subject group we need is not covered
paragraphs: The genuinely hard matches in this corridor are predictable: MYP Design with a digital design focus, Language Acquisition in a specific phase, the Economics strand of Individuals and Societies, Arabic as a first language for a student schooled in English since nursery, and Arts where the process journal rather than the technique is the problem. Those are the requests where a local search returns nobody useful and families settle for a generalist.

We publish the limit rather than improvising. If no suitable specialist is free in the slot you want, you are told that with the earliest realistic alternative. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject group, the match may be a tutor based elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, and that is said before you book rather than concealed behind a local-sounding number. Two providers ranking for Dubai searches route parents to numbers in another country without disclosing it.

Timing changes difficulty sharply. September requests are easy. Requests in the second half of MYP 5, when the Personal Project, the route decision at 16 and content gaps are all live at once, are the hardest in the Middle Years calendar. The useful first step then is a diagnostic trial lesson that decides what to leave alone, because trying to fix everything in a term fixes nothing.

If a match turns out wrong after the first paid session, you are matched again. No tutor can guarantee a criterion score or a subject grade, and a provider offering one is describing their marketing. The testable promises are narrower: a diagnosis from the student's own marked task, a weekly slot that holds, criterion feedback you can line up against the school's own marking, and a re-match if the fit is wrong.

faqs.question: Why is it so hard to find anyone who knows the MYP in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the pool is genuinely small. Dubai has 227 private schools across 17 curricula, IB schools hold roughly 7 per cent of enrolment, and the Middle Years Programme is a subset of that again since several continuum schools enter students for IGCSE at 16 instead. Narrow that to a single subject group and the number of adults who have marked against those criterion descriptors is very low. Local search returns people who are findable, not people who are criterion-literate, which is why matching online widens the pool usefully.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a tutor really knows MYP marking?
faqs.answer: Ask which four criteria the subject group uses and what the top band of one of them asks for. Someone who has marked the work answers in descriptor language without hesitating: a method a stranger could repeat, a general rule justified and tested, an evaluated judgement supported by the student's own evidence. Someone who has not talks about confidence and filling gaps. That is a perfectly honest description of general subject tutoring, and it tells you which product you are being offered.

faqs.question: My child has a 7 in one criterion and a 3 in another. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Usually that the piece of work ran out of time rather than that the subject is misunderstood. The criteria that come last in a task, typically evaluation and reflection, are the ones that suffer when a deadline arrives. If that pattern repeats across several subjects, the diagnosis is self-management rather than content, and the approaches to learning comments on the report will usually confirm it. Buying subject teaching for that pattern is the commonest way Middle Years tutoring money is wasted.

faqs.question: What are approaches to learning skills, and should I care about them?
faqs.answer: They are thinking, communication, social, self-management and research skills, reported separately from subject achievement, and they are frequently the most diagnostic part of an MYP report. Research skills in particular get penalised through criteria that look subject-specific: a student who has never been taught to find, evaluate and reference sources properly loses marks that look like knowledge marks. Fixing research habits generalises across all eight subject groups at once, which makes it unusually good value.

faqs.question: How does the school turn four criterion scores into a grade out of seven?
faqs.answer: It adds them, giving a raw total out of 32, and applies a published boundary table to convert that into the 1 to 7 subject grade. This is worth knowing because it changes where effort should go: a student sitting on 5s is usually strong on one criterion and systematically missing what another asks for, and moving one criterion by two points can move the subject grade. Ask the school for the boundary table it uses; most will provide it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP community project as well as the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Within the same boundary, yes. A tutor may teach planning, research method, referencing, source evaluation and reflective writing, and may read the student's own draft and say where it fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write, draft or restructure any part of it and may not supply a model. For the community project in MYP 3 or 4 the most useful help is usually narrowing an over-ambitious goal, which is the same failure that catches MYP 5 students two years later.

faqs.question: What makes a process journal strong under moderation?
faqs.answer: Dated entries that show genuine development, including the attempts that did not work. A journal reconstructed in the final fortnight reads as a reconstruction, and a moderator who sees no development alongside a polished report has grounds to question authenticity. The habit is worth more than the content: ten minutes a week of honest recording produces something defensible, while a tidy summary written at the end produces something that undermines the student's own work.

faqs.question: Does MYP Sciences criterion C have a reliable fix?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is structural rather than conceptual. Criterion C asks for the processing and evaluation of the student's own data, and students consistently process and then stop. The missing element is evaluation of the method's limitations tied to the specific experiment rather than a generic list of errors. Taught as a structure, with the student writing it and the tutor marking it against the descriptor, it usually moves within two or three sessions. It also transfers directly to Diploma science.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Design and builds good products but scores 4s. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the portfolio is the assessment and the making is not. Criterion A rewards inquiring and analysing, which means a research stage with real analysis in it, and criterion D rewards evaluation against the design specification the student wrote. A student who builds something that works and documents it thinly loses marks in both. The fix is the design cycle write-up rather than the workshop, which is unwelcome news and reliably true.

faqs.question: Should a Media City MYP student be doing extra work in all eight subject groups?
faqs.answer: No, and the timetable is the reason. Eight subject groups plus the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies that KHDA requires in all Dubai private schools already fill the week, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Hours bought for tutoring come out of the task time the criteria are actually measuring. One subject group at a time, chosen from the report, is the shape that works for students in this corridor.

faqs.question: Is the MYP a disadvantage if my child moves to an IGCSE school at 14?
faqs.answer: Not a disadvantage in ability, but a real adjustment in assessment logic. A student marked against descriptors for five years has to learn to answer a past-paper question in mark-scheme language, under time, with no credit for process. That is learnable and takes about a term, and it explains why MYP students sometimes underperform in their first IGCSE mocks despite being well taught. Ask the new school in writing how it intends to place the student and on which tier.

faqs.question: What time do MYP sessions usually run from the Media City towers?
faqs.answer: Between six and eight in the evening. Middle Years students here are mostly bussed to Al Barsha South or Emirates Hills, the roads around those gates stall for about an hour after the final bell, and a route serving several communities adds stops, so a child is typically home between four and five. Add food and a start on school tasks and the workable window begins at six. Earlier bookings get rescheduled often enough to break the weekly rhythm the programme depends on.

faqs.question: How much should Middle Years support cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with budget options from AED 45 to AED 150 and premium named tutoring at AED 500 to AED 650. For the MYP the unusual part is that the premium you are paying is for marking knowledge rather than subject depth, which is why budget tutoring often teaches the content well and still cannot answer the question you asked.

faqs.question: Can Arabic and Islamic Education be tutored like any other MYP subject?
faqs.answer: Not quite, because the rules differ. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, since the expectations and the language of instruction differ, and it requires schools to ensure teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so honest support reinforces the school's own material rather than importing another syllabus.

faqs.question: It is already the second half of MYP 5. Is support still worth buying?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the job changes from improvement to triage. At that point the Personal Project, the route decision at 16 and any content gaps are all live together, and trying to fix everything fixes nothing. The usual plan is to stabilise the project process, close gaps only in the subjects the student will carry into the Diploma or IGCSE, and accept that one or two criterion scores will not move this year. A free diagnostic lesson is the quickest way to decide which.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-media-city.closingHeading: Bring the marked task, not just the worry
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-media-city.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB MYP tutor in Dubai Media City, the most useful thing you can do first is gather three documents: the school's task sheet, the rubric it was marked against, and your child's own work. Put those in front of someone who knows the descriptors and the diagnosis usually arrives within twenty minutes, which is a far better basis for spending than a report card nobody can read. The free trial lesson exists for exactly that, and it produces a written note before any money is paid. Lessons then run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, in a slot the week can actually hold.

intro.heading: The MYP has a calendar, and almost nobody explains it to parents
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme is assessed continuously, which sounds reassuring and means something quite specific: a student's reported grade is built from criterion scores collected at particular points across the year, using a best-fit judgement at reporting time. That makes the MYP year a sequence of assessment moments rather than a run-up to one examination, and a family that understands the sequence can act before a report rather than after it.

The structure is consistent across the eight subject groups. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each scored out of eight. The criteria are skills rather than topics: in the sciences, Criterion B is inquiring and designing and Criterion C is processing and evaluating; in mathematics, Criterion B is investigating patterns and Criterion C is communicating. A student can know the content thoroughly and score poorly on the criterion that measures how they present it.

That is the most common MYP problem we are asked to fix, and it is a fixable one. Communication marks, not content marks, are where most students in this cluster leave the largest share behind. A student who reads the descriptor for the band above theirs usually sees the gap immediately, which is why the first session in almost every MYP arrangement is spent on the descriptors rather than on the subject.

Then there is the Personal Project, which sits in the final MYP year and has a timeline the school sets. Goal, inquiry, process journal, product and a report, assessed against its own criteria. It is the single largest piece of independent work a student has produced to that point, and it runs alongside everything else, which is why it goes wrong on scheduling more often than on ambition.

Dubai Production City has no IB World School inside it. Students travel to Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, to the Al Barsha ring, or to Fairgreen International School to the south, and each campus sets its own assessment and Personal Project calendar. Ask for that calendar at the first parents' evening of the year, because it is what actually governs the student's months.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. Everything here was reviewed in October 2026. We do not publish IB dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification; the dates that matter in the MYP are set by the school in any case, and they are the ones to ask for. What we can set out safely is the criterion structure, the conversion to a reported grade and the shape of the Personal Project, all of which are published in documentation your child's school already holds and none of which changes from one year to the next.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-production-c.subjectsIntro: The eight MYP subject groups, with what the criteria actually measure in each and where students in this cluster most often lose marks. Criterion letters follow the published subject guides your child's school holds.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the one students neglect and the one that prepares them for the Diploma exploration. Communication marks are lost through unexplained working rather than wrong answers.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Inquiring and designing is where the Diploma investigation is won later, and students lose marks for a method that cannot be followed rather than for a wrong hypothesis.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is where the top band sits and where most students stop short, offering description where the descriptor asks for evaluation of sources or perspectives.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Analysing marks are lost when a student summarises content instead of examining how the text produces its effect, which is the single most common pattern in this subject group.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Phase placement matters enormously: a student in the wrong phase is either unchallenged or overwhelmed, and the fix is a conversation with the school rather than tutoring.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than students expect, and responding marks are lost when reflection describes what was made rather than evaluating the choices made.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Students over-invest in the product and under-invest in the design cycle documentation, which is where most of the available marks actually sit.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and reflective components surprise families who assumed the subject was practical only, and they are straightforwardly teachable.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills, and reflecting, supported by a process journal maintained throughout. The journal cannot be reconstructed at the end, which is the single most common and most avoidable failure in the whole project.

sections.heading: The MYP year as a sequence of assessment moments
paragraphs: Because the MYP has no terminal examination, families often assume there is nothing to plan around. There is: a calendar of assessment moments set by the school, in which each criterion in each subject is assessed at particular points, and a reporting judgement made from those scores at particular times. Knowing the sequence is what allows a family to act before a report rather than in response to one.

The practical shape is usually this. Early in the year, each subject assesses the knowledge criterion first, because it is the easiest to set and the content is fresh. Investigation and inquiry criteria arrive next, often with a longer task. Communication is assessed throughout and tends to be the weakest score on the sheet. Reflection and evaluation criteria cluster later, attached to extended pieces of work.

That shape has a consequence for tutoring. A student whose last report showed a weak communication score cannot wait for the topic to come round again, because communication is assessed in almost every task and the next opportunity is a fortnight away. A student with a weak inquiry score has longer, because the next inquiry task may be a term off, and that time should be used on the descriptor rather than on content.

Ask the school for the assessment calendar at the first parents' evening of the year, and ask specifically which criterion each upcoming task will assess. Teachers know and will usually tell you plainly. We plan around that calendar and re-check it every four to six weeks, because in the MYP the tasks move more than the dates do.

sections.heading: Criteria are skills, and the letters are the instruction
paragraphs: The most useful hour we spend with a new MYP student is reading the descriptors with them. Not a summary of the descriptors; the actual published wording from the subject guide their school holds. Students are routinely assessed against criteria they have never read, which is like being marked on a rubric kept in another room.

The letters mean different things in different subject groups, which adds to the confusion. In the sciences, Criterion B is inquiring and designing and Criterion C is processing and evaluating. In mathematics, Criterion B is investigating patterns and Criterion C is communicating. In Individuals and Societies, Criterion D is thinking critically. A student who has learned that Criterion C means communication in maths and assumes the same in science will be answering the wrong instruction.

The pattern in this cluster is clear. Communication and the critical or evaluative criterion carry the largest share of lost marks, and both are presentation skills rather than knowledge. A student who knows the material and cannot lay out reasoning in a form the descriptor rewards will sit a band or two below their understanding, consistently, across every subject.

The method is simple and it works. Take a returned piece of work with its criterion score. Read the descriptor for that band and the descriptor for the band above. Identify the specific difference in words. Redraft that one piece to meet the higher band. Most students see the gap within one session and start applying it without being told, because the descriptors are concrete once they have actually been read.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, planned backwards from the report
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the largest independent piece a student has produced by that point, and it is assessed on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, supported by a process journal maintained throughout. Almost every failure we see is a scheduling failure rather than an ambition failure.

The process journal is the specific trap. It is meant to be a record kept as the work happens, showing decisions, setbacks and changes of direction. It cannot be reconstructed at the end, and a journal assembled in the final fortnight reads exactly like one assembled in the final fortnight. Students who maintain it weekly, even briefly, score better on the reflection criterion without any additional work.

Goal feasibility is the second trap. A student chooses a goal that would take a professional three months, discovers in week six that it cannot be finished, and either abandons it or submits something unfinished. Testing the goal against the available hours in week one, honestly, is a single session that saves the project. The project rewards a well-documented process more than an impressive product.

Our role is bounded and stated plainly. We teach what each criterion requires, question whether the goal is achievable, check that the journal is being maintained, and give feedback on drafts the student wrote. We do not produce the product, write any part of the report, or contribute content to either. The line is authorship, and the consequence of crossing it falls on the student's record rather than on ours.

sections.heading: Why an MYP report confuses parents, and what to ask
paragraphs: Parents moving from a British or Indian system to the MYP often find the first report unreadable, and that reaction is reasonable. There are criterion scores out of eight, a converted grade out of seven, no percentages, and a best-fit judgement rather than an average. None of that maps onto what they are used to.

The mechanics are these. Each criterion is scored out of eight against published descriptors. The four criterion scores are totalled, and the total is converted to a 1-7 grade using boundaries published in the MYP documentation. Because a teacher applies a best-fit judgement across the evidence rather than averaging every mark ever given, a single poor task does not sink a grade and a single excellent one does not rescue it.

The question to ask at a parents' evening is therefore not what percentage your child is on. It is which criterion is lowest, what the descriptor for the next band up says, and which upcoming task will assess that criterion again. Three questions, all answerable, and together they give a family something to act on rather than a number to worry about.

The second question worth asking in the final MYP year is about Diploma readiness, and specifically about timed work. Because the MYP has no external examination, a student can hold strong criterion scores and still be unprepared for a three-hour paper. Asking what timed assessment the school will run before DP1 begins tells you whether a bridging block is needed.

sections.heading: The MYP to DP step, and the term that decides it
paragraphs: The transition from the MYP to the Diploma is the sharpest change in assessment style a student will meet in school, and it happens over one summer. Continuous criterion-based judgement with multiple opportunities is replaced by externally examined papers plus one internally assessed component per subject, under time pressure, with no second attempt.

The specific gap is timed work. An MYP student may never have sat a paper longer than an hour, and the Diploma asks for sustained performance across papers of two and three hours with command terms the MYP does not use. The first DP1 mock therefore reads as a content failure to parents and teachers, when in most cases it is a pacing and structure failure in a student who knows the material.

The second gap is content prerequisites in specific Higher Level subjects. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes algebraic fluency the MYP does not drill to that depth. Chemistry at Higher Level assumes quantitative speed. Physics assumes comfort with rearrangement and units. None of these is a criticism of the MYP; they are simply assumptions the Diploma makes from week one.

So the final MYP term and the summer after it are the highest-value tutoring window in the whole programme. Eight to twelve sessions introducing timed short-answer work, command-term reading, answer structure against mark bands, and the content prerequisites of the student's chosen Higher Levels. It is a defined block with a fixed end at the start of DP1, and it consistently produces more than the same hours spent in DP1 recovering from the first mock.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs in Dubai
paragraphs: MYP tutoring is cheaper than Diploma tutoring in this market, and it should be, because the work is different. Criterion literacy and redrafting do not require specialist examination knowledge; they require a tutor who will read the published descriptors with the student and hold them to the higher band. That sits comfortably in the qualified subject tutor band rather than the specialist one.

The Dubai bands, read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 rate table. Budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium or examiner-led from AED 500-650. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 budget and AED 600-1,200 mid-tier.

Where the specialist band is genuinely worth paying is the bridging block before DP1, because that requires somebody who knows what the Diploma assumes in a particular subject, and the Personal Project where criterion-level feedback matters. Weekly criterion work in Years 7 to 9 does not need it, and paying specialist rates for it is the standard MYP overspend.

Context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. These are market figures and not IB Gram prices. We publish no price list here and start with a free trial lesson instead.
