sections.heading: Honesty, regulators and what to verify
paragraphs: The Personal Project is where the honesty boundary matters most in the MYP, because it is a discrete deliverable with a deadline and a visible product. A tutor may teach the criteria, question the goal, check the journal is being kept, and give feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor may not produce the product, write any part of the report, or contribute content to either. The consequence of crossing that line is an academic honesty finding against the student.

The same applies to subject tasks. Feedback on a student's own draft against a descriptor is teaching. Supplying sentences, rewriting a paragraph to final form, or producing a diagram for them is not. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides or assessment materials, which are copyright; we reference the official source and work from what the school has provided to the student.

On regulation: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Individual tutors need the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with no published fine schedule for working without one.

IB Gram is not IB authorised, KHDA approved or ADEK approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence for training institutes with physical premises, and has no UAE office. Ask any provider describing itself as IB approved what exactly it means, because an MYP school is authorised by the IB and a tutoring service is not.

sections.heading: Starting MYP support at whatever point you are at
paragraphs: Send three things: the year group, the subject or subjects, and a returned piece of assessed work with its criterion scores on it. That last item is the one families leave out and the one that makes the first session useful, because the score plus the descriptor is the whole diagnosis.

Then take the free trial lesson, which is a real teaching hour spent on that returned work and the descriptor above it, with a short written note afterwards naming the criterion and the specific gap. No card is held, nothing renews, and if the match is wrong we rematch once at no charge.

On availability, MYP matches are generally quicker than Diploma ones because the pool is wider. Two to three days is normal across most subject groups. Language Acquisition at the higher phases and Arts subjects can take longer. If the specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book.

For Production City households, two shorter sessions a week usually work better than one long one at this age, given the bus day. Weekend mornings are better for Personal Project work. During Ramadan, post-Iftar slots are a normal request and the slot is held. What we will not do, in IMPZ or anywhere in the UAE, is send a tutor to your address; that service runs in India only. Independent home tutors operate in this community and for a younger child who needs somebody physically present they can be the right answer, which is worth saying plainly rather than arguing against a format we do not offer.

process.title: Ask the school for the assessment calendar
process.description: Which criterion each upcoming task will assess, and when the reporting points fall. Teachers know and will usually say plainly. In the MYP the tasks move more than the dates do, so we re-check this every four to six weeks and change the plan when the next task changes criterion.

process.title: Send returned work with its criterion scores
process.description: Not a report summary. A marked task with its criterion score is the whole diagnosis, because the score plus the published descriptor for the band above shows the specific gap in words. Families routinely leave this out, and it is the single most useful thing they can send.

process.title: Free trial lesson on that work
process.description: A real teaching hour spent reading the descriptor with the student and redrafting one piece to meet the higher band, followed by a short written note naming the criterion and the gap. No card held, nothing renews, and one free rematch if the tutor is not the right fit.

process.title: Work one criterion at a time
process.description: Not the subject, and not everything at once. One criterion per session, one piece of the student's own work, one concrete improvement they can apply to the next task. Most MYP students see the gap within a session once they have actually read the descriptor rather than a paraphrase of it.

process.title: Book the bridging block before DP1
process.description: In the final MYP term, eight to twelve sessions introducing timed questions, command-term reading and the content prerequisites of the chosen Higher Level subjects. Fixed end at the start of DP1. This consistently produces more than the same hours spent in DP1 recovering from the first mock.

whyPoints.title: Descriptors read, not paraphrased
whyPoints.description: We work from the published subject-guide descriptors the school holds, with the student reading the band above their own score. Students are routinely assessed against criteria they have never read, and simply reading them changes output within a session in most cases.

whyPoints.title: Criterion letters handled correctly by subject group
whyPoints.description: Criterion C is communicating in mathematics and processing and evaluating in the sciences. A tutor who treats the letters as universal is teaching the wrong instruction. We match by subject group for this reason, even when the topic looks superficially similar.

whyPoints.title: Personal Project planned backwards
whyPoints.description: From the school's report deadline, with the process journal started immediately and the goal tested against available hours in week one. Almost every Personal Project failure is a scheduling failure, and a journal assembled in the final fortnight reads exactly like one assembled in the final fortnight.

whyPoints.title: The DP step treated as a real transition
whyPoints.description: The MYP sets no external examination, so a strong MYP student can arrive in DP1 with no experience of a three-hour paper. We build timed work and command-term reading into the final MYP term, before the Diploma does it abruptly in October.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the band you need
whyPoints.description: Weekly criterion work does not require a specialist at AED 200-450 an hour, and we say so. The specialist band is worth paying for the DP bridging block and for Personal Project criterion feedback. Paying it for Year 8 descriptor work is the standard MYP overspend in this market.

whyPoints.title: The boundary on the Personal Project stated plainly
whyPoints.description: We teach criteria, question the goal, check the journal and give feedback on the student's own drafts. We never produce the product or write any part of the report. The consequence of crossing that line is an academic honesty finding carried by the student.

faqs.question: What do the MYP criterion letters actually mean?
faqs.answer: They label skills, and they mean different things in different subject groups, which is the source of most confusion. In the sciences, Criterion B is inquiring and designing and Criterion C is processing and evaluating. In mathematics, Criterion B is investigating patterns and Criterion C is communicating. In Individuals and Societies, Criterion D is thinking critically. Each is scored out of eight against published descriptors in the subject guide your child's school holds. A student who has learned what Criterion C means in one subject and assumes the same elsewhere will be answering the wrong instruction.

faqs.question: How does a score out of eight become a grade out of seven?
faqs.answer: The four criterion scores are totalled, giving a figure out of thirty-two, and that total converts to a 1-7 grade using boundaries published in the MYP documentation. Teachers apply a best-fit judgement across the evidence rather than averaging every mark ever recorded, which is why a single poor task does not sink a grade and a single excellent one does not rescue it. The practical consequence is that consistency matters more than peaks, and that a persistent weak criterion is the thing to attack.

faqs.question: Our MYP report has no percentages. What should we ask at parents' evening?
faqs.answer: Three questions. Which criterion is lowest? What does the descriptor for the next band up say, in its actual wording? And which upcoming task will assess that criterion again? Those three give you something to act on, whereas asking what percentage your child is on gets an answer that does not exist in this system. A fourth question is worth adding in the final MYP year: what timed assessment will the school run before DP1 begins, since the MYP itself sets none.

faqs.question: Why does my son know the content and still get a 4?
faqs.answer: Because the criteria measure how he presents and reasons as well as what he knows, and communication is the criterion most students in this cluster leave marks on. A student who understands the material thoroughly and lays out working without explanation, or writes a conclusion without reference to the evidence, will sit a band or two below his understanding on every task. It is a presentation problem rather than a knowledge problem, which is good news: reading the descriptor for the band above usually shows him the gap within one session.

faqs.question: When should the Personal Project process journal actually start?
faqs.answer: Immediately, in the same week the goal is agreed, and it should be maintained weekly even when entries are brief. The journal is meant to record decisions, setbacks and changes of direction as they happen, and it cannot be reconstructed afterwards: a journal assembled in the final fortnight reads exactly like one assembled in the final fortnight, and the reflection criterion suffers accordingly. Students who keep it as they go score better on reflection without doing any additional work, which makes it the cheapest mark available in the whole project.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether a Personal Project goal is realistic?
faqs.answer: Count the hours honestly. Take the weeks between the goal being agreed and the school's report deadline, subtract exam weeks, holidays and the time the report itself will take, and see what remains. Then ask whether the product could be completed in that, by a student who is also doing eight subjects. Students routinely choose goals that would take a professional three months and discover in week six that it cannot be finished. Testing feasibility in week one is a single session that saves the project.

faqs.question: Does the MYP prepare a student properly for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: For investigation and independent work, very well: MYP students arrive in DP1 able to frame an inquiry, which IGCSE entrants often cannot. For timed examination performance, not at all, because the MYP sets no external examination. A student may never have sat a paper longer than an hour and the Diploma asks for two and three-hour papers using command terms the MYP does not use. That is why the first DP1 mock so often reads as a content failure when it is a pacing and structure failure in a capable student.

faqs.question: What should the final MYP term be used for?
faqs.answer: Timed work and command-term reading, plus the content prerequisites of the chosen Higher Level subjects. Eight to twelve sessions introducing short timed questions, answer structure against mark bands, and whatever the student's Higher Levels assume from week one: algebraic fluency for Analysis and Approaches, quantitative speed for Chemistry, rearrangement and unit confidence for Physics. It is a defined block with a fixed end at the start of DP1, and it consistently achieves more than the same hours spent in DP1 recovering from the first mock.

faqs.question: My daughter is in the wrong Language Acquisition phase. Can tutoring fix that?
faqs.answer: Tutoring can help her cope, but the fix is a conversation with the school rather than extra hours. Language Acquisition runs in phases, and a student placed too low is unchallenged while one placed too high is assessed against descriptors she cannot yet reach, which produces low scores that look like a learning problem and are really a placement problem. Ask the school which phase she is in, what evidence placed her there, and what the process is for review. Then decide whether support is needed at all.

faqs.question: Is an MYP tutor cheaper than a Diploma tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It should be, because the work is different. Criterion literacy and redrafting need a tutor who will read the published descriptors with the student and hold them to the band above, which sits in the qualified subject tutor band of roughly AED 150-300 an hour rather than the IB specialist band of AED 200-450. Where the specialist band is genuinely worth paying is the bridging block before DP1 and Personal Project criterion feedback. Paying specialist rates for Year 8 descriptor work is the standard overspend we see at this stage.

faqs.question: What may a tutor legitimately do with my son's Personal Project drafts?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach what each criterion requires, question whether the goal is achievable in the time available, check that the process journal is being maintained, and give feedback on report drafts the student wrote. A tutor cannot produce the product, write any part of the report, contribute content to either, or make the design decisions. The test is authorship, and the consequence of crossing it is an academic honesty finding against the student rather than against anyone else.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion is most often neglected by students?
faqs.answer: Investigating patterns in mathematics and inquiring and designing in the sciences, because both attach to longer tasks that feel optional next to content revision. They are also the two that prepare a student directly for the Diploma exploration and the scientific investigation, so neglecting them costs twice: once in the MYP grade and again two years later. The practical move is to work on the descriptor before the extended task begins, since the next opportunity to be assessed on that criterion may be a full term away.

faqs.question: How often should MYP sessions run for a Production City student?
faqs.answer: Two shorter sessions a week usually beat one long one at this age. Students here bus out to Dubai Investments Park, Motor City or Al Barsha and arrive home mid-afternoon tired, and thirty to forty focused minutes on one criterion and one piece of their own work achieves more than an hour of diminishing attention. Weekend mornings are better for Personal Project work, which needs sustained thought. During Ramadan, post-Iftar slots are a normal request and we hold the slot rather than dropping it.

faqs.question: Do you visit homes in IMPZ for MYP sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. For MYP work the online format is practical rather than compromised: descriptors and the student's own returned work are read on screen together, and the written note after each session records the criterion and the gap. Independent home tutors do work in this area at roughly AED 180-350 an hour on published Dubai market rates, and for a younger child needing supervision they can be the better choice.

faqs.question: Which schools near Dubai Production City run the MYP?
faqs.answer: There is no IB World School inside the community itself. Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park is the nearest IB continuum campus, and Fairgreen International School serves the southern corridor. Beyond that, families use the Al Barsha ring, including Dubai International Academy Al Barsha and GEMS World Academy Dubai. Each sets its own assessment calendar and its own Personal Project timeline, and those differ by weeks between campuses, which is why we ask which school before planning anything. We name these as context and have no affiliation with any of them.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-production-c.closingHeading: Read the descriptor, then plan the year
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-production-c.closingBody: Two things make MYP support work. The first is reading the published descriptor for the band above your child's current score, with their own returned work in front of you, because that turns a vague grade into a specific sentence to act on. The second is knowing when each criterion gets assessed again, which the school will tell you if asked. Add the Personal Project timeline in the final year and a bridging block before DP1, and the programme stops being opaque. Send a returned task with its criterion scores and take a free trial lesson.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-oasi.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach MYP subjects and are matched to a subject group rather than to a year level. For calendar-led work the useful tutor is one who asks where the current unit sits in its cycle and which criteria the next task will be marked against, before proposing any content at all.

intro.heading: MYP runs on unit cycles, not on terms
paragraphs: Most parents plan tutoring against a term-and-examination rhythm, because that is how the British and Indian curricula around Dubai Silicon Oasis work. MYP does not run that way. Each subject moves through units of inquiry, and each unit ends in one or more tasks marked against specific criteria. The reported grade is a conversion of criterion marks accumulated across those tasks, so the moment that matters is the fortnight before a task, not the week before a report.

That changes when a session is worth buying. A tutoring hour three days before a criterion-marked task, spent reading the task sheet and the criterion descriptor against the student's draft, can move a band. The same hour spent on general subject content in the middle of a unit usually moves nothing, because nothing is being assessed and the student has no vehicle for applying it. Families who learn this stop buying weekly and start buying at points.

The second calendar fact is that criterion marks accumulate. A low mark on the investigating criterion in October is not erased by a high one in March; it contributes to a total that is converted using boundaries published in the subject guide. So the useful intervention is early in the year, on whichever criterion is structurally weak, rather than late in response to a report that has already absorbed several tasks.

In MYP 5 a third thread appears. The Personal Project runs across the year with its own criteria and a supervisor at the school, and it depends far more on documentation accumulated as the work proceeds than on the visible outcome. Its milestones are set by the school, they vary along this corridor, and the single most valuable act is asking for all of them in the first weeks of the year rather than meeting them individually.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Across Silicon Oasis, Cedre Villas, Academic City, The Villa and Nad Al Sheba, MYP lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. For criterion work the format fits the task: the assessment sheet, the criterion descriptor and the student's own draft sit side by side on a shared screen for both people at the same magnification.

What follows is the MYP calendar in detail. The unit cycle and where in it a session belongs. The accumulation problem and why early matters. The Personal Project timeline. What MYP eAssessment changes in the final year. And the window between MYP 5 and DP1, which is the cheapest intervention in the whole programme and the one nobody uses.

One framing to carry into the detail. Nothing here argues for buying more MYP tutoring than a family already does. It argues for buying it at different moments. Four sessions placed in the fortnight before four assessed tasks will usually move more criterion marks than a term of weekly hours spread across the units between them, and it costs considerably less. Timing is the whole lever in this programme, and almost nobody along this corridor is told where it sits.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-oasi.programmesIntro: MYP spans five years and the calendar shape changes substantially across them. These are the three phases a Silicon Oasis family is planning around.

programmes.name: MYP Years 1 to 3, roughly Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The years in which criterion-referenced habits form. Students meet the four-criteria structure, learn what an inquiry question looks like, and either develop the habit of reflecting on their own work in writing or do not. The Community Project typically closes this phase, in MYP 3 or MYP 4 depending on the school.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest phase to intervene in, because nothing is at stake in certificate terms and the habits built here carry into MYP 5 and then into the Diploma. A term aimed at how to write a justification or a reflection is a small purchase with a long return, and almost nobody along this corridor makes it.

programmes.name: MYP Years 4 and 5, roughly Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Criteria descriptors expect more independence and the subject demand rises. The Personal Project runs through MYP 5 against its own criteria with a school supervisor. Schools that enter students for MYP eAssessment do so at the end of MYP 5, leading to the IB MYP Certificate for those who meet the requirements.
programmes.countryNote: The mathematics stream is also set in this phase, and standard and extended routes in MYP 4 and 5 feed into Applications and Interpretation and Analysis and Approaches respectively. A family thinking about Higher Level mathematics in the Diploma should be asking about the stream now rather than at the end of MYP 5.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, after MYP
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The step is less about content than about timed external examination technique, which MYP rarely requires, and about mathematical fluency, which MYP assesses without drilling.
programmes.countryNote: Deira International School, GEMS Modern Academy at Nad Al Sheba and Uptown International School in Mirdif all run the IB continuum, so students along this corridor often move from MYP 5 to DP1 within the same campus. That continuity means the transition gap is frequently assumed to be smaller than it is.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-oasi.subjectsIntro: This grid is the eight MYP subject groups with the criterion that most often costs a band in each and when in a unit cycle to address it. Pick your child's weakest two and plan around their next task rather than around the term.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Bands are lost on analysing, because students summarise what a text says rather than examining how it achieves its effect. Best addressed in the fortnight before an analytical task, with the descriptor open.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Students sit in phases rather than year groups, so the first question is which phase, and productive communication is where bands most often go.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. Thinking critically loses the most bands: a student presents two views and offers no evaluation, which is a specific omission rather than a general weakness and is fixable in one session.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. That last criterion surprises parents most and is assessed, so a student writing nothing about impact leaves a whole criterion near the bottom.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students with strong arithmetic lose bands on investigating patterns, because generalising and justifying a rule is a different activity from calculating.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Process documentation carries substantial weight, so the useful session is at the start of a unit establishing folder habits rather than at the end admiring the product.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. As in Design, the process journal is heavily weighted, and journal entries cannot be reconstructed convincingly once a unit has finished, which makes timing decisive.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Written planning and reflection are assessed alongside performance, which is why a strong athlete can receive a middling grade.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project with criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, supervised at the school. Documentation accumulated as the work proceeds is what gets assessed, so the decisive sessions are at the goal-setting stage and on the process journal routine.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria covering evaluating, synthesising and reflecting across two or more subject groups. Students treat them as double workload rather than as distinct assessment, which costs bands in the synthesising criterion specifically.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-oasi.regionsIntro: MYP sessions are bought at points in a unit cycle rather than weekly, so what matters is whether a slot can be found at short notice. These notes cover what each community offers.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: Self-contained, with a large British-curriculum secondary school and several Indian-curriculum schools inside the community. Students attending locally are home early, which makes a short-notice session in the fortnight before a task genuinely arrangeable rather than theoretical.

regions.name: Cedre Villas and Silicon Gardens
regions.note: Villa and townhouse stock within Silicon Oasis with short internal journeys. Useful for point-in-cycle booking, because a slot can be used at a different hour from week to week without the journey making it impossible.

regions.name: Dubai International Academic City
regions.note: University district immediately south. The budget tutoring band is well supplied here and is adequate for MYP content support and homework supervision, and is not the right band for reading a criterion profile or a task descriptor.

regions.name: The Villa and Dubailand
regions.note: Villa communities west of the corridor and more car-dependent. Later arrival home means the evening window carries most MYP work, which suits criterion discussion and draft review better than it would suit mathematics problem solving.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba

regions.name: Mirdif

sections.heading: The unit cycle, and where a session belongs in it
paragraphs: A MYP unit runs for several weeks around a statement of inquiry, with content and skills developed through it and one or more criterion-marked tasks at or near the end. The marks from those tasks are what accumulate into the reported grade. So the unit, not the term, is the planning unit, and the position within the unit determines whether a tutoring hour can do anything useful.

Early in a unit, a session can establish habits: how the process journal will be kept, what the inquiry question is actually asking, what the task will be marked against. Mid-unit, a session is mostly content support, which is worth having if the content is genuinely missing and worth very little if the problem is criterion-related. In the fortnight before the task, a session reading the descriptor against a draft is where bands move.

This is why weekly booking is often the wrong shape in MYP. Four sessions placed at the right points across two unit cycles will usually do more than twelve sessions spread evenly, because eight of those twelve fall at moments when nothing is being assessed and the student has no vehicle for applying what is taught. The exception is a subject where the content itself has genuinely been missed.

To plan this way a family needs the task dates, and task dates sit with the subject teachers rather than in a single published calendar. Asking each teacher, or the year coordinator, for the assessment dates across the next two units is a short request and it is what converts MYP tutoring from an expense into an intervention. The table below sets out what to buy at each point in a cycle.

sections.heading: Criterion marks accumulate, so early beats late
paragraphs: Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each marked on a scale from 1 to 8, and the school converts the accumulated totals to the reported 1 to 7 grade using boundaries published in the subject guide. Your child's teacher holds that guide and can show you the boundary table; we do not reproduce board documents, so work from the school's copy.

Accumulation has a consequence most parents do not realise. A low mark on one criterion in the first unit of the year is not cancelled by a strong mark later; it sits inside a total. So a student who is structurally weak on, say, the investigating criterion in sciences will carry four or five low marks on that criterion by the time a mid-year report arrives, and the reported grade will reflect all of them. Addressing it in October therefore influences far more marks than addressing it in March.

This inverts the usual tutoring instinct, which is to respond to a report. By the time a report shows the problem, most of the marks that produced it are already banked. The useful trigger is the first marked task of the year rather than the first report: if a student comes back with a 3 on one criterion in week five, that is the moment to act, while there are still five or six tasks to come in that criterion.

The practical version is simple. Ask to see each marked task as it is returned rather than waiting for a report, and look at the criterion letters rather than the overall comment. One low criterion mark in September is information. Four of them in February is a grade. The difference between those two situations is a single conversation held five months earlier, and it costs nothing to have.

sections.heading: The Personal Project timeline in MYP 5
paragraphs: The Personal Project runs across MYP 5 with its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, and a supervisor appointed at the school. Milestones are set by the school and vary between the IB schools along this corridor, which is why the first useful act is asking for all of them in the opening weeks of the year rather than meeting each one as it arrives.

The decisive factor is documentation rather than the visible outcome. A student who builds something impressive and keeps no process journal has very little evidence to be assessed against, and a journal cannot be reconstructed convincingly at the end because reconstructed entries read exactly like reconstructed entries. Establishing the routine in the first weeks is therefore worth more than any amount of help later, and it costs almost nothing.

The second common failure is a goal too large to achieve or document in the time available, chosen for ambition rather than feasibility. The criteria reward evidence of planning, skill application and reflection rather than scale, so a narrow goal pursued thoroughly outscores a grand one pursued partially. Narrowing is a single conversation at the start and it is the highest-value support available on the project.

The boundary here is strict and it is where this market most often bends. A tutor may discuss the goal, explain each criterion, ask the questions a good supervisor would ask, model a comparable project on an unrelated topic, read what the student has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation. A tutor may not contribute to the product, draft the report, or write in the process journal. The project is the student's own work and is declared as such.

sections.heading: MYP eAssessment, and what it changes in the final year
paragraphs: Some schools enter MYP 5 students for MYP eAssessment, which combines on-screen examinations with moderated ePortfolios and can lead to the IB MYP Certificate for students meeting the requirements. Others do not and report MYP grades internally. Which applies to your child's school changes the final year substantially, and many parents along this corridor do not know which situation they are in.

Where eAssessment applies, MYP 5 acquires an external examination element the rest of the programme does not have: timed, on-screen, with its own question styles. A student assessed only through coursework-style tasks for four years meets a genuinely new format in the final year, and the useful tutoring there is practice with the format rather than more content. That is also a calendar fact, because the practice has to happen before the sitting.

Where eAssessment does not apply, MYP 5 remains criterion-referenced throughout and the Personal Project is the main set-piece. In that case examination practice is spending on a skill that is not being assessed, and the sensible focus is the criterion profile across subjects plus the project. The difference between the two scenarios is large enough that a plan built for the wrong one wastes most of a year.

So ask the school one question in September: does this school enter students for MYP eAssessment and the MYP Certificate? The answer is a single line. It is also a useful test of a prospective tutor, because somebody who has worked in MYP schools in Dubai knows that practice varies and will ask you the same question before proposing anything at all.

sections.heading: The window between MYP 5 and DP1
paragraphs: The spring and summer at the end of MYP 5 is the cheapest and least used intervention window in the whole programme. The Personal Project is finished or finishing, the year's criterion marks are settled, and the Diploma has not yet started. Nothing is at stake and nothing competes, which is precisely why no family buys anything and why the ones who do describe DP1 completely differently.

Two gaps are worth closing in that window. The first is mathematical fluency. MYP assesses mathematics against criteria including real-life application and does not drill algebraic manipulation to automaticity, so a student may reach DP1 unable to rearrange a formula without hesitation. Both Diploma mathematics courses assume that fluency from the first term, and a student without it experiences the Diploma as a sudden difficulty rather than a gradual one.

The second is timed examination technique. Unless the school uses eAssessment, an MYP student may have had very little experience of timed external papers with mark schemes behind them, and the Diploma is substantially externally examined. Command terms, working conventions and time management are new skills rather than improved ones, and four or five sessions in the summer installs the basics before they are needed under pressure.

On the other side, MYP students usually arrive at DP1 unusually well prepared for internal assessment and reflective writing, because four years of criterion-referenced tasks and process journals is exactly the training the Diploma's internal assessments and Extended Essay require. That is worth saying, because the transition is often described as uniformly hard when it is in fact uneven, and the uneven parts are the ones to spend on.

sections.heading: Reading a criterion-marked task properly
paragraphs: The skill that changes outcomes in MYP is reading a returned task rather than reading a report. A marked task carries criterion letters, a mark out of 8 for each one assessed, and usually a descriptor the teacher has worked from. That is a complete diagnosis, supplied free, several times a term, and most households look at the overall comment and file the paper.

The method takes ten minutes. For each criterion assessed, find the mark and then read the descriptor for the band above it. The descriptor says in plain language what the student would have had to do differently, and it is almost always something specific: offer an evaluation, justify a generalisation, discuss a limitation, define a variable. That gap is the thing to work on before the next task in that criterion.

What makes this powerful is that the descriptors repeat. The same criterion appears in every unit of a subject, so a student who learns what the band above requires can apply it next time and the time after. A family that does this across two or three tasks often finds that no tutoring is required at all, because the problem was never understanding the subject; it was never having read what the marking was asking for.

Where tutoring does help is in the subjects where the descriptor language is genuinely opaque to a non-specialist, and in holding the student to it. A tutor reading the descriptor aloud against a draft, asking where the evaluation is and where the limitation is discussed, does in one hour what a term of content teaching does not. That is the whole argument for buying MYP support at a point in the cycle rather than weekly.

sections.heading: What a local MYP tutor can and cannot be expected to know
paragraphs: A fair question, and the answer is uncomfortable. The International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of private school enrolment in Dubai in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum and 26 per cent Indian. So most tutors available in Silicon Oasis, Academic City, Al Warqa or International City come from British or Indian curriculum backgrounds, and criterion-referenced marking is unfamiliar territory for them.

That does not make them poor teachers. A strong mathematics teacher can teach MYP mathematics content very well. What they frequently cannot do is look at a criterion profile and say that the problem is the investigating-patterns strand rather than the arithmetic, because they have never marked against that descriptor. And in MYP, that identification is most of the value, which is why the test to apply is specific rather than general.

The test is four questions. Name the four criteria for this subject. What is each marked out of? How does the school convert those marks to the reported grade? Which criterion do students in this subject most often lose bands on? Somebody who has taught and marked MYP answers all four in sentences. Somebody who has not will talk about the subject instead, which is the tell, and you need no knowledge of the programme to hear it.

Local supply is best in Nad Al Sheba and Mirdif, where IB continuum schools sit, and thin elsewhere along this corridor. That is a cohort-size fact rather than a comment on any community. Removing the driving radius from the filter list is what makes a tutor who has actually marked against these criteria reachable from Cedre Villas or The Villa, which is the practical reason this service is delivered online.

paragraphs: Send five things: the subject, the MYP year, the four criterion marks from the most recent report, one or two returned marked tasks, and the dates of the next assessed tasks if you can get them. The marked tasks and the dates are what turn this from a weekly booking into an intervention. We then match a tutor to the subject group and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost.

Afterwards you receive a written note naming which criterion is costing the grade, what the descriptor for the band above actually requires, and which point in the next unit cycle a session should sit at. For a good number of families that note is the whole value and the engagement ends there, which is a success rather than a lost sale. Where more is needed it should be a criterion block, bought early in the year.

The limits, stated. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. There is no UAE office, centre or branch and we claim none. We hold no IB or regulator accreditation. We do not supply MYP subject guides, task banks or assessment criteria documents as downloads, because reproducing them is not ours to do; your child's teacher holds the school's copy and that is the one to use.

And the project boundary, again, because it is the most-bent rule in this market. A tutor may question, explain criteria, model a comparable project on a different topic, read what the student has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation. A tutor may not contribute to the product, draft the report or write in the process journal. Ask any provider to put that in writing before money moves, and keep the reply.

process.title: Ask each teacher for the next two assessment dates
process.description: MYP task dates sit with subject teachers rather than in one published calendar, and they are what a session should be booked against. A short request to each teacher, or to the year coordinator, converts MYP tutoring from a weekly expense into an intervention placed where it can move a band.

process.title: Read the returned task, not the report
process.description: For each criterion assessed, find the mark and read the descriptor for the band above it. The descriptor names something specific: offer an evaluation, justify a generalisation, discuss a limitation. That is the gap, and acting on it before the next task in that criterion is what changes the accumulated total.

process.title: Act on the first marked task of the year
process.description: Criterion marks accumulate, so a low mark in week five influences far more of the year than the same information arriving in a February report. One low criterion mark in September is information; four of them in February is a grade, and the difference is a conversation held five months earlier.

process.title: Ask whether the school uses eAssessment
process.description: If it does, MYP 5 carries on-screen timed examinations and that practice has to be scheduled. If it does not, examination practice is spending on an unassessed skill and the focus should be the criterion profile and the Personal Project. The answer is one line and it reshapes the final year.

process.title: Use the summer before DP1
process.description: Four to six sessions on marked algebraic drill, plus four or five on command terms and timed technique. Nothing competes, nothing is at stake, and both gaps are what DP1 assumes from the first term. Families who use that window describe the Diploma's first year in completely different terms.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the unit cycle, not the term
whyPoints.description: MYP runs on units ending in criterion-marked tasks, so a session in the fortnight before a task can move a band while the same hour mid-unit usually cannot. Four well-placed sessions often outperform twelve spread evenly, and that is a cheaper plan as well as a better one.

whyPoints.title: Accumulation explained
whyPoints.description: Criterion marks add up across the year, so a weakness addressed after the first marked task influences most of the year's marks while the same work after a mid-year report influences very few. Nobody in this market points that out, because responding to reports sells more hours.

whyPoints.title: The descriptor method handed over
whyPoints.description: For each criterion, read the band above the mark awarded. The descriptor names what was missing in plain language, and the descriptors repeat in every unit. Many families find they need no tutoring once they have done this, and we would rather say so than not.

whyPoints.title: A written boundary on the Personal Project
whyPoints.description: Questioning, criteria explanation, a comparable model on a different topic, and feedback on what the student has written. No product contribution, no drafting, no writing in the journal. The project is declared as the student's own work and assessed on documentation.

whyPoints.title: Honest about local MYP supply
whyPoints.description: IB enrolment was 7 per cent of Dubai's private school market in 2024-25, so most tutors nearby come from other curricula and criterion marking is unfamiliar to them. Four specific questions test that, and we expect you to use them on us as well.

whyPoints.title: The transition window named
whyPoints.description: The spring and summer at the end of MYP 5 is the cheapest intervention in the programme, aimed at algebraic fluency and timed technique. Nobody markets it, because nothing is failing and there is no deadline to point at, which is exactly why it appears here.

faqs.question: When in the MYP year is a tutoring session actually worth buying?
faqs.answer: In the fortnight before a criterion-marked task, spent reading the task sheet and the relevant descriptor against whatever the student has drafted. That is the point in a unit cycle where an hour can move a band. Mid-unit sessions are content support, which helps only if content is the genuine gap. Immediately after a marked task is also valuable, because it diagnoses which criterion lost the band and sets up the next unit.

faqs.question: Why do MYP criterion marks make early intervention so important?
faqs.answer: Because they accumulate. Each subject is marked against four criteria on a 1 to 8 scale, and the school converts the accumulated totals to the reported 1 to 7 grade using published boundaries. A low mark in the first unit is not cancelled by a strong one later; it sits inside the total. So acting after the first marked task influences most of the year's marks, while the same work after a mid-year report influences very few.

faqs.question: How do I read a returned MYP task from my child's Silicon Oasis school?
faqs.answer: Ignore the overall comment and look at the criterion letters. For each criterion assessed, find the mark out of 8 and then read the descriptor for the band above it. The descriptor says in plain language what the student would have needed to do differently, usually something specific like offering an evaluation or justifying a generalisation. Because the same criteria recur in every unit, that lesson transfers directly to the next task.

faqs.question: Is weekly MYP tutoring the right shape?
faqs.answer: Often not. Four sessions placed at the right points across two unit cycles usually do more than twelve spread evenly, because eight of the twelve fall at moments when nothing is being assessed and the student has no vehicle for applying what is taught. The exception is a subject where content has genuinely been missed, for instance after a period of absence, where steady weekly contact is the correct response.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to homes in Cedre Villas for MYP sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For criterion work the online format suits the task: the assessment sheet, the criterion descriptor and the student's own draft sit side by side on a shared screen at the same magnification for both people. Point-in-cycle booking is also easier, since a session can be placed at a different hour from one fortnight to the next.

faqs.question: How should the Personal Project be timed across MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Backwards from the school's milestones, which vary between IB schools along this corridor, so ask for all of them in the opening weeks. The goal should be narrowed early to something achievable and documentable, the process journal routine established in the first weeks rather than reconstructed later, and a complete report draft should exist in time for feedback to be acted on rather than merely received.

faqs.question: Where exactly does legitimate Personal Project support stop?
faqs.answer: With questioning and feedback, yes; with producing it, never. A tutor may help narrow the goal, explain each criterion, ask the questions a good supervisor would ask, model a comparable project on an unrelated topic, and read what the student has written and say where it falls short. A tutor may not contribute to the product, draft the report or write in the process journal. The project is declared as the student's own work.

faqs.question: Does our school enter students for MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Ask in September, because practice varies across Dubai and the answer reshapes the final year. Where eAssessment applies, MYP 5 carries on-screen timed examinations and moderated ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate for students who meet the requirements, so examination practice becomes relevant and has to be scheduled. Where it does not apply, MYP 5 stays criterion-referenced and examination practice is spending on an unassessed skill.

faqs.question: Which gaps should a Silicon Oasis family close before DP1 begins?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions of marked algebraic drill, plus four or five on command terms and timed examination technique. MYP assesses mathematics against criteria including real-life application without drilling manipulation to automaticity, and both Diploma mathematics courses assume that fluency from the first term. Timed external papers with mark schemes are also new unless the school used eAssessment. Nothing competes in that window, which is why it is the cheapest in the programme.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose MYP science marks despite understanding the content?
faqs.answer: Most often on the criterion covering reflection on the impacts of science, which is assessed and which students frequently leave blank because nobody told them a paragraph on implications was required. The other common loss is on inquiring and designing, where the student does not know how to frame a testable question or justify a method. Both are specific, both are visible on the criterion letters, and both are usually one-session fixes.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose MYP maths bands with good arithmetic?
faqs.answer: Almost always on the criterion covering investigating patterns, which asks the student to generalise a rule and justify it. That is a different activity from calculating accurately, and a student never taught to write a justification loses a band there consistently while getting the numbers right. The repair is a four to six session block using the student's own marked tasks, and it should be bought early because the criterion recurs in every unit.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a tutor near Silicon Oasis really knows MYP?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Name the four criteria for this subject and say what each assesses. What is each criterion marked out of? How does the school convert those marks to the reported grade? Which criterion do students in this subject most often lose bands on? Somebody who has taught and marked MYP answers in sentences with specifics; somebody from another curriculum background will talk about the subject instead, which is the distinction to listen for.

faqs.question: Is MYP tutoring supply genuinely thin along this corridor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a cohort-size fact rather than a comment on any community. IB enrolment was 7 per cent of Dubai's private school market in 2024-25, against 37 per cent UK curriculum and 26 per cent Indian, so most tutors available locally come from other curricula. Supply is deepest near the IB continuum schools at Nad Al Sheba and in Mirdif and thin elsewhere, which is why removing the driving radius widens the choice so much.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic timetable affect MYP study time in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It occupies school timetable space. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and a prohibition on combining the groups, and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Support in those subjects works from the school's approved material, because using different or additional content requires prior Ministry permission.

faqs.question: What should one well-timed MYP session achieve?
faqs.answer: Quite a lot, if it sits in the fortnight before a task. The student should leave able to say what the criterion descriptor for the band above actually requires, and the draft they bring should change in a specific way, usually by acquiring an evaluation, a justification or a discussion of limitations that was missing. That is checkable on the next returned task, which is a far better measure than a grade promise nobody can honestly make.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-oasi.closingBody: MYP rewards timing more than volume. A session placed in the fortnight before a criterion-marked task, with the descriptor open beside the student's own draft, does what a term of general subject teaching does not. So ask each teacher for the next two assessment dates, look at the criterion letters on the last returned task rather than at the report, and send us both along with the four criterion marks. The free trial lesson costs nothing, and the note that follows will name the weak criterion and the point in the cycle to act.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-south.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Middle Years Programme subjects to students across Dubai South, Emaar South, Al Furjan and Dubai Investments Park. Matching is done by subject group, because criterion B in Sciences and criterion B in Individuals and Societies ask for completely different things.

intro.heading: A programme with no public examination still has a calendar
paragraphs: Parents arriving in the Middle Years Programme from an examination-based system usually find the assessment opaque, and the reason is structural rather than a communication failure. There is no public examination in most schools. Instead each subject is marked against four criteria, labelled A to D, each on a 0 to 8 scale, assessed through tasks spread across the year and converted at the end into a grade from 1 to 7. A parent used to percentages and end-of-year papers has nothing familiar to hold on to.

The consequence is that the calendar is made entirely of internal deadlines, and those deadlines are where marks are won and lost. A task assessing criterion C in Sciences is a marked assessment even though it does not look like one. A student who treats it as homework will produce homework and be marked as though it were an assessment. Across a year that pattern produces a grade nobody can explain, including the student, who worked hard throughout.

The criteria are not the same across subject groups, which is the single most useful thing a Dubai South parent can learn about this programme. In Sciences, criterion B is inquiring and designing and criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science. In Mathematics, criterion C rewards communicating and criterion D rewards applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Individuals and Societies, criterion B is investigating. A student strong on content and weak on process will sit in the middle bands across every subject at once, for the same reason.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the task brief, the published criteria and the student's own draft open on a shared screen. For the Middle Years Programme that arrangement is particularly useful, because most of the work is reading a criterion descriptor against a piece of writing and the two documents sit better side by side than passed across a table.

One factual note on the wider context. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools annually and publishes the ratings. It also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, which means a Middle Years student in this emirate carries mandatory subjects alongside the programme. KHDA does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership and operates no UAE centre. Individual tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, which is the document a parent can reasonably ask to see.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-south.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme spans five years and then feeds the Diploma or a British-curriculum sixth form. Dubai South families ask about all three stages below, with Year 5 transition questions the most common.

programmes.name: Middle Years, the first three years
programmes.description: The years in which the criteria should be taught explicitly and usually are not. Students learn subject content and absorb the assessment grammar by osmosis, which works for some and leaves others permanently puzzled about why careful work receives a middling mark. Interdisciplinary units appear here and are assessed on their own criteria, which catches students who treat them as a side activity.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai South these are also the years in which a family often decides whether to stay in the IB continuum or move to a British-curriculum school for IGCSE at sixteen. That decision is easier made with a clear view of how the child performs against process criteria rather than content, because the two systems reward opposite things.

programmes.name: Middle Years, the final two years
programmes.description: Subject depth increases, the Personal Project runs across the final year, and some schools enter students for eAssessment to obtain the formal MYP certificate. Grades matter more here because they feed Diploma course placement decisions, including whether a subject is available at Higher Level, which is a decision made before anybody has sat a Diploma paper.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai South students in these years are typically weighing Diploma subject choices at the same time as managing the Personal Project. Schools in this cluster set Personal Project deadlines at different points, and the project competes for exactly the hours that Diploma preparation would otherwise use, which makes sequencing the two the practical problem.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: What most Middle Years students in this cluster move into. The Diploma reintroduces public examinations with papers worth 75 to 80% of each subject grade, which is the largest single change a Middle Years student faces. Criterion marking rewards reflection and communication; Diploma Paper 1 rewards accuracy under time with no credit for process.
programmes.countryNote: The transition is the most common reason Dubai South families book Middle Years support at all. Four to eight sessions across the summer before Year 12, focused on timed writing, notation and the assessment format rather than on content, closes most of the gap. Left undone, the same gap consumes a term of Year 12 while new content is arriving.

programmes.name: The British-curriculum alternative
programmes.description: The route a Middle Years student takes if the family moves to a British-curriculum school at fourteen. The content overlap is substantial and the assessment overlap is minimal: IGCSE is externally examined with tiered entries and grade ceilings, while the Middle Years Programme is criterion-marked internally across five years.
programmes.countryNote: Several British-curriculum schools in the Al Furjan and Jebel Ali arc take students out of Middle Years programmes at fourteen. That move needs gap mapping across a holiday, because a student with no experience of a timed external paper arrives in a Year 10 IGCSE cohort whose peers have been practising examination technique since Year 7.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-south.subjectsIntro: The Middle Years subject groups Dubai South families ask about, with the criteria that actually decide the grade in each rather than a description of the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Four criteria, with criterion C rewarding communicating mathematics and criterion D rewarding applying it in real-life contexts. A student can be procedurally strong and sit mid-band because the write-up does not show reasoning, or lacks a conclusion that answers the task question. Extended Mathematics adds content and is usually the prerequisite for Diploma Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion A is knowing and understanding, B is inquiring and designing, C is processing and evaluating, and D is reflecting on the impacts of science. Students strong on content and weak on investigation design lose most of their marks in B and D, not in A, and no amount of further content revision changes that.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criterion B is investigating, which rewards a research question and a documented process rather than an answer. Marks go on sources used without evaluation, and on conclusions that summarise rather than argue. Essay structure taught explicitly moves this subject faster than additional reading does.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language are the four criteria, which means a well-argued essay in weak prose and a fluent essay with no argument both sit mid-band for different reasons. Identifying which of the two a student is doing is the entire diagnosis, and it takes one marked piece to establish.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Organised by phase rather than year, with four criteria covering listening, reading, speaking and writing. Students placed in the wrong phase appear weak when they are actually misplaced, which is worth checking before any tutoring. Productive skills respond faster than receptive ones to a short block of drilled structures.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The design cycle is the assessment: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. Students lose marks by producing a good final product with a thin process folder, because three of the four criteria are about the process rather than the outcome. Documenting as you go is the whole technique.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. As in Design, the process documentation carries criteria of its own, so a strong performer with no reflective record sits below a thoughtful one with a complete process journal. This surprises families consistently.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Four criteria including planning for performance and reflecting on performance, which means written work matters in a subject most students assume is practical. Students who perform well and document nothing lose marks in two of the four criteria, and the written components are entirely learnable.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project across most of the final Middle Years year, assessed on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. The commonest failure is a goal too broad to achieve and document in the time, which caps the mark before work begins. The process journal is assessed, not just the outcome.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed on their own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. Students treat them as a side activity because they do not belong to a single subject, and then lose marks in an assessment that counted. Knowing they are assessed at all is most of the fix.

subjects.name: Arabic as a mandatory subject
subjects.description: Arabic is compulsory in Dubai private schools under KHDA rules whatever curriculum the school teaches, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language. It sits alongside the Middle Years programme rather than inside it, and it is frequently the subject a family seeks help with first.

subjects.name: Transition skills into the Diploma
subjects.description: Timed writing, note-taking from a lecture-style lesson, mathematical notation and the habit of producing under examination conditions. sections.heading: The four criteria, and why they differ by subject group
paragraphs: Every Middle Years subject is marked against four criteria labelled A to D, each on a 0 to 8 scale, and the labels are the same across subjects while the content of each criterion is not. That inconsistency is the source of most parental confusion, because a report showing criterion B at 4 in two subjects is describing two different weaknesses. In Sciences, B is inquiring and designing. In Individuals and Societies, B is investigating. In Mathematics, criterion C is communicating and D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts.

The practical reading of a Middle Years report is therefore to look at the pattern rather than the numbers. A student with high A scores and low B and D scores across every subject has a single problem appearing in many places: they know the content and do not show the process the criteria reward. That is one diagnosis and one fix. A student with uneven scores across criteria within one subject has a subject-specific gap, which is a different conversation entirely.

The criteria descriptors are published for every subject group, and reading the band above a student's current score is the fastest useful thing a parent can do. The descriptors are specific: they name whether a conclusion must be justified, whether sources must be evaluated, whether a reflection must consider implications. Students who have read them write differently, and most have never been shown one.

The table below sets out what each criterion actually asks in the subject groups Dubai South families most often raise. Use it with a marked task in hand rather than in the abstract. The question to ask of any task that scored below expectation is not whether the student understood the topic, which they usually did, but which named quality the descriptor required and the work did not contain.

sections.heading: The Middle Years calendar is made of internal deadlines
paragraphs: Without a public examination, the entire assessment calendar is internal, and that changes where tutoring is worth placing. In an examination system the fixed point is the paper and everything counts backwards from it. In the Middle Years Programme there are many small fixed points, each assessing one or two criteria, spread across three terms, and a weak task in October is not recoverable in May.

The practical consequence is that the useful unit of planning is the task rather than the term. Before each assessed task the student should know which criteria it addresses and what the band above their last score requires. That is a ten-minute conversation and it is worth more than an hour of content revision, because the content is usually present and the criterion is what was missed.

The second consequence is that reports are the diagnostic document rather than a summary. A Middle Years report shows criterion-level scores across subjects, which means a pattern is visible in a way it never is in an examination system until results arrive. Families who read the report by pattern rather than by subject find the single shared weakness, and that is the thing worth buying sessions for.

The table lays the year out against what support should do in each period. Schools in this cluster set their task calendars and Personal Project deadlines at different points, so the specific dates have to come from the school rather than from a general pattern. The one durable rule is that the final year carries the Personal Project on top of everything else, and that it competes for exactly the hours Diploma preparation would otherwise use.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, counted backwards
paragraphs: The Personal Project runs across most of the final Middle Years year and is assessed on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It is the first genuinely independent piece of work most students have produced, and the commonest failure is not effort. It is a goal too broad to achieve and document in the time available, which caps the mark before any work begins.

Counted backwards from the school's submission date, the sequence is: a goal narrowed until it is both achievable and evidenceable, a plan with criteria for success stated at the outset, the work itself with a process journal kept as it happens, then a report written against the published criteria, then submission. The step students skip is the journal, which they reconstruct at the end from memory. Reconstructed journals read as reconstructed and the criteria reward evidence of process.

The second common failure is a goal that is achievable but not documentable. A student who learns a practical skill and has nothing written down to show how will score poorly on criteria that reward exactly that record. Choosing a goal with the documentation in mind is the single most useful conversation a supervisor or tutor can have, and it has to happen at the start rather than halfway through.

The boundary on help is the same as everywhere in the IB. A tutor may discuss the goal, push back on one that cannot be achieved or documented, explain the criteria and what the band above requires, and give feedback on the student's own draft report. A tutor may not produce the project, write any part of the report, or construct the journal. The project is explicitly a demonstration of the student's own independent work, which is the whole point of the component.

sections.heading: What a 1 to 7 grade actually means, and what it does not
paragraphs: The four criterion scores in a subject are totalled and converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. Two things follow that parents regularly do not expect. First, the grade hides the pattern: a 5 built from an 8 in A and a 3 in D is a very different student from a 5 built from four 5s, and only the criterion scores distinguish them. Second, the grade is not a percentage and does not map onto one.

It also does not map onto an IGCSE grade. A Middle Years 6 and an IGCSE grade 6 are different statements, produced by different assessment of different content, and comparing siblings across the two systems tells a family nothing reliable. Households in this cluster frequently contain one child in each, which makes the temptation strong and the conclusion worthless.

Where the grade does matter is Diploma placement. Schools use final Middle Years grades to decide which subjects a student may take at Higher Level, and sometimes whether Analysis and Approaches is available in mathematics. That decision is made before anybody has sat a Diploma paper, which means the final year's criterion scores carry consequences well beyond the certificate. A student aiming at a Higher Level science or at Analysis and Approaches should know the school's threshold in advance.

For families considering a move to a British-curriculum school instead, the translation runs the other way. A strong Middle Years record built on process criteria does not guarantee a comfortable start in a Year 10 IGCSE cohort, because that cohort has been practising timed external papers since Year 7. The gap is examination technique rather than content, and it is best closed over a holiday rather than discovered in a first mock.

sections.heading: The transition into the Diploma, which is the real reason families call
paragraphs: Most Middle Years support requested from Dubai South is ultimately about the Diploma. The programmes are run by the same organisation and reward almost opposite things. Middle Years assessment is criterion-based, internal, spread across tasks, and gives explicit marks for reflection, communication and process. Diploma assessment is 75 to 80% external papers sat under timed conditions, where Paper 1 in several subjects gives no credit for method at all.

The gap is therefore not knowledge. It is four specific habits that the Middle Years Programme does not assess and the Diploma assumes from the first week. Writing to time, which a student who has only ever submitted coursework has never practised. Taking notes from a lesson delivered as exposition rather than inquiry. Mathematical notation and instruction words such as show that and hence, which have fixed meanings. And producing finished work in forty minutes without the option of revising it later.

All four are teachable and none of them takes long. Four to eight sessions across the summer before Year 12, built entirely on timed production, closes most of the gap. The most valuable single element is a full timed paper in a subject the student will take, sat under conditions before Year 12 begins, because the experience itself is the lesson. Students who have done that arrive in September knowing what the year is about.

Left undone, the same gap consumes a term of Year 12 while new content is also arriving, and the student concludes they are not suited to the Diploma when in fact they have simply never written under time. In this cluster the summer block is the most under-booked work we offer and the one with the clearest effect, partly because it happens when nothing is competing for the hours and partly because the problem it fixes is narrow enough to fix completely.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects alongside the programme
paragraphs: A Middle Years student in a Dubai private school does not only study the Middle Years Programme. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA requires these to be implemented by the start of the stated academic year. That is a real addition to the timetable and a frequent source of the grade a family is most worried about.

KHDA's requirements are specific. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the two groups, and combined classes are prohibited. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

There is also a constraint on material that affects how any tutoring in these subjects can honestly be described. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. A tutor working in this area supports the student with the school's own prescribed material rather than introducing a parallel syllabus, and any provider offering an alternative curriculum for these subjects is describing something that is not permitted.

KHDA also specifies that mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, that schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and that it is advised any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete credential a parent can ask a school about. It is not a credential that applies to private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA approval of any kind.

sections.heading: Fitting Middle Years sessions into a Dubai South week
paragraphs: Middle Years sessions are usually shorter than Diploma ones, sixty minutes rather than ninety, because the material is a single assessed task rather than a paper. That makes them easier to place in a Dubai South evening, which matters because the age group in this cluster skews towards the villa communities where the school run ends later.

Households here are generally home between 16:00 and 16:45 after a run into Dubai Investments Park or east to the Dubailand corridor. Green Community manages 15:45; Dubai Production City is closer to 17:00. For a twelve or thirteen year old the useful window is earlier than for a Diploma student, because concentration falls away sooner in the evening, which means the 16:45 to 18:00 band is the one that works and fills first in this community.

The Personal Project is the exception and needs longer stretches. Weekend mornings suit it, and so do the winter and spring breaks, where consecutive days allow the kind of sustained work a weekly hour cannot support. Families who plan the project around the breaks rather than around term weeks consistently produce better process journals, because the work and the documentation happen together rather than being separated by a week.

During Ramadan the pattern shifts. School hours shorten, concentration in the afternoon drops, and sessions move later into the evening after iftar. For this age group shortening from sixty minutes to forty-five and working on a single criterion rather than a whole task works better than persisting with the usual format. Dropping to a session a fortnight for the month is a reasonable choice and generally better than abandoning the arrangement and restarting in April.
