sections.heading: What Middle Years support costs in Dubai, and where to spend it
paragraphs: The published Dubai bands do not distinguish by programme, so the planning question is how much support a Middle Years student actually needs. The honest answer is less than a Diploma student, and concentrated in different places. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 a month for budget provision, AED 600-1,200 for mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, which is a Diploma band rather than a Middle Years one.

Hourly, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the budget end, both online. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for qualified subject tutors. TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is in the hour.

Where Middle Years spend works hardest is narrow and cheap. A single block teaching the criteria explicitly, once, across the subjects a student takes. A three or four session repair on one criterion where a report shows a consistent weakness. A Personal Project block at the start of the final year, when the goal is being set. And the summer transition block before Year 12, which is the highest-value item on the list by a clear margin.

Where it works least is a standing weekly session in a subject where the content is fine and the process marks are low. That arrangement reteaches content the student has and never addresses the criterion that cost the grade, which is a reasonable description of a lot of Middle Years tutoring. Every figure here belongs to the provider named; these are market bands rather than IB Gram prices, and our own conversation begins with a free trial lesson and a written diagnosis.

faqs.question: How is MYP assessment different from an exam system?
faqs.answer: There is no public examination in most schools. Each subject is marked against four criteria labelled A to D, each on a 0 to 8 scale, assessed through tasks spread across three terms and converted at the end to a grade from 1 to 7. That means the entire calendar is made of internal deadlines, and a weak task in October is not recoverable in May. It also means a task that looks like homework is often a marked assessment, which is the distinction that costs most students marks.

faqs.question: Why does criterion B mean something different in each subject?
faqs.answer: Because the labels A to D are constant while the content of each criterion is set per subject group. In Sciences, criterion B is inquiring and designing. In Individuals and Societies it is investigating. In Mathematics it is investigating patterns. In Language and Literature it is organising. So a report showing criterion B at 4 in two subjects is describing two different weaknesses. The descriptors are published for every subject group, and reading the band above a current score is the fastest useful action a parent can take.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but scores mid-band. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always that the process criteria are not being addressed. In Sciences, criterion B rewards inquiring and designing and criterion D rewards reflecting on the impacts of science, so a student with excellent recall and a thin method or no reflection will sit in the middle bands however well they understand the topic. The pattern to look for on a report is high A scores with low B and D scores across every subject at once, which is one problem appearing in many places and one fix.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai South student start their Personal Project?
faqs.answer: At the goal-setting stage, which is the earliest point in the final year, and that is also when support is worth most. A goal too broad to achieve in the time, or achievable but impossible to document, caps the mark before any work begins. The process journal is assessed and has to be kept as the work happens; reconstructed journals read as reconstructed. Ask the school for the goal-setting window, the draft deadline and the submission date in the autumn, because schools in this cluster set them weeks apart.

faqs.question: Can I compare an MYP grade to an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Not usefully. A Middle Years 6 and an IGCSE grade 6 are different statements, produced by different assessment of different content. The Middle Years grade comes from four criterion scores totalled and converted using published boundaries, and it hides the pattern that produced it: a 5 built from an 8 and a 3 is a different student from a 5 built from four 5s. Households in this cluster frequently contain one child in each system, which makes the comparison tempting and the conclusion unreliable.

faqs.question: Do MYP grades affect Diploma subject choices?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the consequence families most often discover late. Schools use final Middle Years grades to decide which subjects a student may take at Higher Level, and sometimes whether Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is available at all. That decision is made before anyone has sat a Diploma paper. A student aiming at a Higher Level science or at Analysis and Approaches should ask the school what its threshold is, in writing, at the start of the final Middle Years year rather than at the end of it.

faqs.question: What does the Diploma assume that MYP never assessed?
faqs.answer: Four habits. Writing to a time limit, which a student who has only submitted coursework has never practised. Taking notes from a lesson delivered as exposition rather than inquiry. Mathematical notation and instruction words such as show that and hence, which carry fixed meanings. And producing finished work in forty minutes with no option to revise it later. None is knowledge and all four are assumed from the first week of Year 12. Four to eight summer sessions closes them, including one full timed paper sat under conditions.

faqs.question: Are interdisciplinary units actually assessed?
faqs.answer: Yes, on their own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. Students treat them as a side activity because they do not belong to a single subject and because they often feel less serious than a subject task, and then lose marks in an assessment that counted towards a report. Knowing they are assessed at all is most of the fix. The second part is reading the specific criteria for the unit, which are published and which name what synthesis has to look like to earn the top band.

faqs.question: Is Arabic compulsory for an MYP student in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, under KHDA's requirements. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes are prohibited. These subjects sit alongside the Middle Years Programme rather than inside it, and they are often the grade a family is most concerned about.

faqs.question: Can a tutor use a different Arabic syllabus from the school's?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider offering one is describing something that is not permitted. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. Support in Arabic, Islamic Education or Social Studies therefore works with the school's own prescribed material rather than introducing a parallel curriculum. KHDA also requires that school teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval, which is a school credential rather than one that applies to private tutors.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to a Dubai South address?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the task brief, the published criteria and the student's own work open on a shared screen. For the Middle Years Programme that arrangement suits the work well, since most of a session is reading a criterion descriptor against a piece of writing, and two documents side by side read better on a monitor.

faqs.question: How long should an MYP session be for a Year 8 student?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes generally works better than ninety for this age group, because the material is a single assessed task rather than a paper and concentration falls away sooner. In Dubai South the practical window is 16:45 to 18:00 once the school run from Dubai Investments Park or the Dubailand corridor is done, and those slots fill first in Emaar South where the age profile is youngest. During Ramadan, shortening further to forty-five minutes and working on one criterion rather than a whole task holds up better than persisting with the usual format.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful MYP tutoring block to buy?
faqs.answer: Three or four sessions teaching the criteria explicitly, read against the student's own work, because that pays into every subject at once and most students have never been shown a descriptor. After that, a single-criterion repair block where a report shows one consistent weakness while the others are fine. The weakest use of money is a standing weekly session in a subject where the content is sound and the process marks are low, because it reteaches what the student has and never touches what cost the grade.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project report?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, and those limits still leave the useful work available. A tutor may discuss the goal, push back on one that cannot be achieved or documented in the time, insist on the process journal being kept as the work happens, explain the criteria and what the band above requires, and give feedback on the student's own draft report. A tutor may not produce the project, write any part of the report or construct the journal. The project exists specifically to demonstrate the student's own independent work.

faqs.question: What if we move from MYP to a British-curriculum school at fourteen?
faqs.answer: The content overlap is substantial and the assessment overlap is minimal, so the gap to close is examination technique rather than knowledge. A Year 10 IGCSE cohort has been practising timed external papers since Year 7, while a Middle Years student may never have sat one. Four to eight sessions over a holiday on timed writing, tiered paper structures and command-word reading closes most of it. intro.heading: Two systems, and a report that explains neither
paragraphs: A Middle Years Programme report is harder to read than the system it describes. There are four criterion marks, each out of eight, and a grade from one to seven produced by published boundaries. A parent in Dubai Sports City looking at three sixes and a two in a subject has been told something quite specific, and almost nobody explains what. The comparison with the system next door — IGCSE, in schools a few minutes away — makes it clearer, which is why this page starts there.

IGCSE measures content against written papers at the end of two years. MYP measures performance against named criteria across five years, continuously. The practical difference is that an IGCSE student can be behind and look behind, while an MYP student can be behind in one specific strand and look adequate, because three strong criterion marks carry the grade while one weak strand sits inside it untouched for two years.

That is the most common thing a tutor finds in this programme. A student with a steady 5 in Sciences who has never scored above a three on the criterion covering processing and evaluating data. A student with a solid grade in Mathematics whose investigating-patterns mark has been weak since MYP 2. Those gaps are invisible in a grade and obvious in the criterion breakdown, and they are exactly what the Diploma or IGCSE will later price.

The second comparison families in Sports City run is between neighbourhoods. Is the Middle Years Programme better supported here than in Motor City or Arabian Ranches? For tutoring delivered online the answer is that it makes no difference. MYP cohorts are small in every community in this belt, specialists who know the criterion wording rather than just the subject are scarce everywhere equally, and the only genuine local variable is what time a 13-year-old can sit down after the school run.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a Sports City address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For this age group sessions are deliberately shorter — forty-five to sixty minutes is usually the ceiling for useful concentration — and the written note home matters more than it does for older students, because the student will not report back accurately.

The third comparison, and the one with the longest consequences, is between MYP 5 and whatever comes next. Students in this part of Dubailand move at 16 into either the Diploma or an IGCSE year group, sometimes at a different school. Those two destinations expect different things, and a student can be well prepared for one and not the other without anyone noticing until the first term.

What follows is those comparisons set out properly: the two systems side by side, the four criteria by letter and subject group, the eAssessment question, the real gap to the Diploma subject by subject, and what a block of MYP support costs and should contain.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP tutor in Dubai Sports City is for
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in Dubai Sports City means one-to-one Middle Years Programme teaching arranged outside school for a student in or around the Sports City master plan, and IB Gram provides it live online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a UAE address; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and that is stated plainly rather than discovered later.

The job divides into two quite different things, and families usually want the first while needing the second. The first is criterion work: reading the report's four marks, identifying the weak strand, and teaching what that strand actually rewards. This is fast, satisfying and produces a visible change in the next assessed task. The second is fluency work on the skills the programme assumes — manipulation, structured writing, reading for argument — which is slow and shows up two years later in the Diploma.

For a student in MYP 1 to 3 the second is almost always the better purchase. There is time, the content pressure is low, and the skills built there determine what the final two years can be. For a student in MYP 5 with a Diploma place waiting, the first is usually more urgent, with bridging work in the summer immediately afterwards.

Session length matters for this age group in a way it does not for older students. Forty-five to sixty minutes is the ceiling for useful concentration in most cases, and a ninety-minute session with a 12-year-old produces thirty minutes of work and an hour of fatigue. Shorter and more frequent beats longer and weekly, and because lessons are online a second short session in a week costs no travel on either side.

sections.heading: MYP against IGCSE, system by system
paragraphs: In this part of Dubai a family can have one child in the Middle Years Programme and another on an IGCSE course a few minutes away, and the two reports are not comparable. Understanding why makes both more useful. IGCSE is a two-year course ending in written papers against a published content list. MYP is a five-year programme of continuously assessed tasks against named criteria.

The consequences run in both directions. IGCSE gives a clearer signal about content knowledge, because a paper mark is a paper mark, and a weaker signal about process skills, which are barely assessed. MYP gives a detailed signal about process — inquiring, communicating, evaluating — and a weaker signal about content density, because no task asks a student to hold two years of material at once.

That asymmetry is what produces the familiar September difficulty for MYP students entering the Diploma. They arrive with stronger research and writing habits than their IGCSE-educated peers and with less experience of being examined on volume. Their IGCSE peers arrive the other way round. Both gaps are closable and neither is a deficiency in the programme; they are simply what each system measures.

For tutoring, the practical reading is that an MYP student should be assessed on both axes. The criterion breakdown shows the process picture. A short content and fluency check — manipulation under time, a piece of sustained writing, a reading-for-argument task — shows the other. A block planned from only the report addresses half the student.

sections.heading: The four criteria, and the strand hiding inside a grade
paragraphs: Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, with published boundaries converting the combination into a grade from one to seven. The criteria differ by subject group, and their wording is the thing being marked. A well-informed answer that does not do what the strand asks for will score in the middle band regardless of accuracy, which students experience as unfairness and is in fact a rubric they have not read.

The arithmetic is where the hidden problem lives. Three strong criterion marks and one weak one still produce a respectable grade, so a student can carry the same weak strand for two or three years while the report looks acceptable. In Sciences that strand is most often processing and evaluating. In Mathematics it is investigating patterns. In Language and Literature it is organising. In Individuals and Societies it is thinking critically.

Those four are not a coincidence. Each is the strand that asks for something other than knowing the material: generalising a pattern, evaluating whether data supports a claim, structuring an argument, weighing a source. Those are teachable skills, each takes four to six short sessions, and none of them is taught explicitly in most schemes of work because the content has to be covered.

The practical instruction for a Sports City parent is to stop reading the grade and start reading the four numbers. If one of them has been two or three points below the others for a year, that is the block. sections.heading: eAssessment at the end of MYP 5
paragraphs: Some schools enter MYP 5 students for the optional eAssessment, which produces an externally validated result at the end of the programme. Others do not, and complete the programme on internal assessment alone. Whether a school enters students is a school decision, and a Sports City family should establish it early because it changes what the final year is working towards.

Where eAssessment applies, the final MYP year acquires an external deadline and a format students have not met before. That changes the usual MYP pattern, in which nothing is examined in the conventional sense, and it tends to expose the content-density gap earlier than the Diploma otherwise would. Students accustomed to task-based assessment find sitting an assessment of the whole year unfamiliar rather than difficult.

Where it does not apply, the final year's assessment remains internal, and the transition shock arrives in the first Diploma term instead. Neither arrangement is better, but they argue for different preparation. A student facing eAssessment benefits from timed practice during MYP 5. A student not facing it benefits more from bridging work in the summer that follows.

Either way, the question to ask the school is simple and specific: are students in this year group entered for eAssessment, and if so for which subjects? The answer determines whether a block in MYP 5 should include timed work or should be entirely criterion-focused, and getting that wrong wastes half the sessions. It is worth asking in the autumn of MYP 5 rather than in the spring, because a block that has to add timed practice needs the weeks to do it in.

sections.heading: The gap from MYP 5 to the Diploma, subject by subject
paragraphs: The transition from MYP 5 to the Diploma is described in general terms far too often. In practice the gap is specific and differs by subject, which means a bridging block can be targeted rather than diffuse. Families in Sports City who ask for general preparation usually get a general result; those who ask for the two named gaps in the two subjects that matter get something useful.

In mathematics the gap is algebraic fluency and the absence of a calculator in parts of the Diploma assessment. MYP assessment rewards investigation and communication, and a student can be strong in both while manipulation remains slow. Diploma mathematics assumes it is automatic from the first term, which is why the first-term shock is so consistently reported by Dubailand families each September.

In the sciences the gap is content density and quantitative confidence. MYP science assesses inquiry and evaluation well and rarely asks a student to hold a term's content in mind simultaneously. In Language A the gap runs the other way: MYP students are usually well prepared, because analysing and organising transfer directly, and their difficulty is more often the volume of reading than the technique.

The table sets these out so a bridging block can be specified rather than described. Six sessions aimed at two named gaps in the summer between the programmes is the cheapest intervention available in the entire MYP sequence, and it is the one most often skipped because nothing appears to be wrong in July.

sections.heading: Why the neighbourhood comparison resolves the same way
paragraphs: Families comparing Sports City with Motor City or Arabian Ranches for MYP support expect one community to be better served. The structural reality is that none of them is. The Middle Years Programme is run by fewer schools in this belt than the British curriculum, cohorts are small within each subject group, and the pool of tutors who know what a criterion strand actually rewards is thin everywhere rather than thin in one place.

That thinness is specific. Plenty of tutors can teach science to a 14-year-old. Rather fewer can read a Sciences criterion breakdown, identify that processing and evaluating has been three points below the other strands for two years, and teach the student what an evaluation needs to contain. Criterion literacy is a different qualification from subject knowledge, and it is what MYP support actually requires.

What differs between the communities is the clock and the commute. Sports City students are home early because their schools sit inside the master plan, which for a 13-year-old is the difference between a productive 4pm session and an unproductive 6pm one. Motor City loses weekday evenings to clubs. DAMAC Hills and Remraam add bus time. Those are real constraints and they are solved by scheduling, not by location.

So the comparison worth running is the same one as in every other subject on this site: a tutor chosen from those available nearby on a given evening, against a tutor chosen from those who can read the rubric. For a programme assessed entirely against rubrics, the second pool is the only one with a different answer at the end of it.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project is completed in MYP 5 and assessed against published criteria, with the process journal forming part of the assessment rather than preparation for it. That single fact resolves most of the difficulty students have with it. A strong product documented thinly scores below a modest product documented well, which feels wrong to a 15-year-old and is exactly what the criteria say.

What support can usefully do is explain the criteria, question whether the stated goal is achievable, check that the journal is being kept as the work proceeds rather than reconstructed afterwards, and give feedback on what the student has written. Choosing a goal that can actually be completed and documented is the single highest-value conversation, and it belongs at the start rather than halfway through.

What support must not do is produce any part of the project or the report. A tutor does not write, complete or draft the submission, and does not create the artefact. This is an academic-honesty requirement rather than a house preference, and work a student did not produce becomes a finding against the student. The same line applies to every assessed task in the programme, including interdisciplinary units.

For a Sports City family the practical sequence is: agree a feasible goal early, keep the journal weekly from the beginning, read the criteria at the start rather than at the end, and self-mark a draft against each criterion before submission. Four short sessions spread across the project period does more than eight in the final fortnight, and costs less.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs, and what it should buy
paragraphs: MYP blocks are usually shorter than Diploma blocks and should be, because the targets are narrower and the sessions are shorter. The published hourly rates in this market are these. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutors.

In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors once travel is counted. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Local packages advertised include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. All of these are provider-published figures read in October 2026 and none is IB Gram's price list.

For MYP the budget band is a better fit than it is for Diploma work in one specific case: homework supervision and company for a younger student who is coping but disorganised. It is a poor fit for criterion work, because reading a rubric and teaching what a strand rewards is a specialist skill and the band does not buy it. Families often pay the low rate for the high-skill task and conclude tutoring does not work.

The spending advice is therefore unusual for this age group. Buy few sessions and buy them specialist. A four to six session single-criterion block, or a six-session summer bridge, at the qualified or specialist band, beats two years of weekly budget-band support in both cost and effect. The expensive pattern is the familiar one: an unmeasured weekly hour from MYP 2 to MYP 5, which nobody reviews because nothing is obviously wrong.

sections.heading: Permits, the regulator and what is not claimed
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For an MYP student that means a fuller school week than the subject-group list suggests.

IB Gram holds no International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. No grade, criterion mark or admission outcome is promised. No part of a Personal Project, interdisciplinary unit or any other assessed task is produced for a student, and no statistic appears on this page without a sample size, a date and a method.

process.title: Short diagnostic trial session
process.description: Forty-five to sixty minutes with the proposed tutor, spent on a recent assessed task and the strand descriptors it was marked against. It ends with a written note to parents naming the strand to target and what that strand actually rewards. Nothing is committed.

process.title: Pick one strand or buy fluency
process.description: For MYP 4 and 5 with a weak strand, a four to six session criterion block. For MYP 1 to 3, usually a fluency block instead, because there is time and the skills built there decide what the final two years can be. Trying both at once does neither well.

process.title: Short, frequent sessions with a note home
process.description: Forty-five to sixty minutes, twice a week rather than ninety minutes once, since concentration rather than content is the limit at this age. A written note after each session, because a 13-year-old will not relay what was covered accurately and parents need to know what was set.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: The target is measured against the next assessed task's criterion mark, in writing. If it has not moved, the strand may have been misread, or the task may not have assessed it. Both are fixable, and catching it at four sessions avoids a term spent polishing the wrong thing.

whyPoints.title: Criterion marks read before anything is taught
whyPoints.description: A grade of five can contain three strong strands and one that has been weak for two years, and the four numbers say which. Starting from the breakdown rather than from the grade is what makes an MYP block short and targeted instead of general and long.

whyPoints.title: Criterion literacy, not just subject knowledge
whyPoints.description: Teaching science to a 14-year-old and teaching what the processing and evaluating strand rewards are different skills. MYP support needs the second, and it is the scarcer one in every community in this belt, which is why matching by rubric rather than by distance matters here.

whyPoints.title: Session length set by the age group
whyPoints.description: Forty-five to sixty minutes is the useful ceiling for most students at this stage, and twice weekly beats one long session. Because lessons are online, a second short session in a week adds no travel for anybody, which makes the better pattern practical rather than theoretical.

whyPoints.title: Fluency bought early, criterion work bought late
whyPoints.description: In MYP 1 to 3 the better purchase is manipulation and written structure, which decide how the Diploma goes. In MYP 5 with a place waiting, criterion work is more urgent. Spending in the wrong order is the most common and least visible MYP mistake.

whyPoints.title: A bridging block that names its targets
whyPoints.description: Six sessions in the summer aimed at algebraic fluency and sustained writing closes most of the first-term Diploma gap. General preparation produces general results, which is why the gap is specified subject by subject on this page rather than described.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: No part of a Personal Project, interdisciplinary unit or assessed task is written, completed or produced for a student. Tutors explain criteria, question feasibility and give feedback on the student's own writing, and the process journal stays the student's own record throughout.

faqs.question: How do I read an MYP report with four criterion marks?
faqs.answer: Ignore the grade first and look at the four numbers. Each criterion is marked out of eight, and published boundaries convert the combination into a grade from one to seven. Three strong marks and one weak one still produce a respectable grade, so the weak strand can persist for years unnoticed. If one criterion has sat two or three points below the others across several reports, that single strand is the block, and it is usually four to six sessions of work.

faqs.question: Can an MYP tutor come to a home in Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. All UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For this age group the online format also makes the better session pattern practical: two short sessions a week rather than one long one, with no travel on either side. Published in-home market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion is most often the weak one?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject group, and the pattern is consistent. In Sciences it is processing and evaluating. In Mathematics it is investigating patterns. In Language and Literature it is organising. In Individuals and Societies it is thinking critically. Each of those asks for something other than knowing the material — generalising, judging whether data supports a claim, structuring an argument, weighing a source — and none is usually taught explicitly, because content has to be covered.

faqs.question: Is the Middle Years Programme good preparation for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: For process skills, yes: research habits, extended writing and evaluation transfer directly and MYP students often arrive stronger in those than their IGCSE-educated peers. The gap is content density and examination stamina, because no MYP task asks a student to hold a term's material in mind at once. In mathematics specifically the gap is algebraic fluency without a calculator. Both are closable with a six-session summer block aimed at those two named things.

faqs.question: Should my child in MYP 2 have a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but for fluency rather than for criterion polishing. At that stage there is time, content pressure is low, and the skills built — algebraic manipulation, written explanation structure, reading for argument — determine what the final two years can be. A single-criterion block makes more sense in MYP 4 or 5, where the report's weak strand has a direct effect on the grade and on the move at 16.

faqs.question: Does the Personal Project journal count towards the mark, or just the report?
faqs.answer: Published criteria covering the whole process, with the process journal forming part of the assessment rather than preparation for it. A strong product documented thinly scores below a modest product documented well. Support can explain the criteria, question whether the goal is achievable, check the journal is kept as the work proceeds, and give feedback on the student's own writing. No tutor writes, drafts or produces any part of the project or report.

faqs.question: How does MYP eAssessment change what the final year should work towards?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly, because it is a school decision and it changes what the final year is working towards. Where eAssessment applies, MYP 5 acquires an external deadline and a format students have not met, so timed practice during the year is worth including in any block. Where it does not, assessment stays internal and bridging work in the following summer is the better use of the same money. Getting this wrong wastes half a block.

faqs.question: Why does my child write well and still score low on organising?
faqs.answer: Because organising is marked separately from producing text and from using language. Fluent expression earns credit under a different criterion; structure that serves an argument earns it under this one. A student who writes beautifully in a sequence that does not build towards a point will be marked accordingly, and most find this genuinely surprising. It is teachable in four to six sessions: plan before writing, make each paragraph do one job, and signpost the argument.

faqs.question: How long should a session be for a 12-year-old?
faqs.answer: Forty-five to sixty minutes in most cases. Concentration rather than content is the limiting factor at this age, and a ninety-minute session usually produces half an hour of work and an hour of fatigue, which also damages willingness to attend the next one. Two shorter sessions a week beat one long one, and because lessons are online the second session adds no journey for anyone, which makes the better pattern practical.

faqs.question: Is MYP mathematics enough preparation for Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Not on its own, for most students. MYP mathematics assesses investigation and communication well, and a student can score strongly on both while manipulation remains slow. Diploma Analysis assumes manipulation is automatic from the first term and includes assessment without a calculator. The fix is short daily algebraic drills over the summer between the programmes rather than reading ahead, which adds content on top of an unresolved fluency problem.

faqs.question: Why are MYP specialists hard to find in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because fewer schools in this belt run the programme than run the British curriculum, cohorts are small within each subject group, and criterion literacy is a separate qualification from subject knowledge. Plenty of tutors can teach science to a 14-year-old; rather fewer can read a criterion breakdown and teach what a specific strand rewards. That scarcity is identical across Sports City, Motor City and the Ranches rather than concentrated in one community.

faqs.question: What does a short MYP block cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A four to six session single-criterion block at the qualified or specialist band — published from AED 150 for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB by Unitors, with specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more — is the usual shape. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle. All figures are provider-published and were read in October 2026; none is IB Gram's price list.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an interdisciplinary unit task?
faqs.answer: A tutor can explain the criteria, which cover disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting, and can give feedback on what the student has written. A tutor cannot write, complete or produce any part of the task. Students frequently treat these units as a double dose of two subjects rather than as a separate assessment with its own requirements, and simply reading the criteria at the start resolves most of the difficulty without any teaching at all.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP 5 to an IGCSE year group. What changes?
faqs.answer: The assessment model entirely. IGCSE measures content against a published syllabus list in terminal written papers, so the skills to build are examination technique, timed recall and working shown for method marks. MYP has probably prepared the student well for research and extended writing and less well for sitting a paper to time. A short summer block on timed practice and written-method discipline covers the main difference.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubai-sports-city.closingBody: For an IB MYP tutor in Dubai Sports City, the most useful first message is the criterion breakdown rather than the grade. Four numbers out of eight per subject usually identify the block immediately, and if one strand has been consistently below the others the target is already named. The trial session is forty-five to sixty minutes with the proposed tutor, spent on a recent assessed task and the descriptors it was marked against, delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time, and it ends with a written note home.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubailand.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work with Middle Years Programme students across the Dubailand communities. Profiles state the subject group and the MYP year, because a criterion-based brief in MYP 2 and a pre-Diploma brief in MYP 5 are different pieces of work.

intro.heading: The MYP marks criteria, and the school run decides when that work happens
paragraphs: Two things make Middle Years Programme tutoring different, and a Dubailand family needs both of them understood before booking anything. The first is academic: MYP subjects are not marked as percentages against a syllabus. Each subject carries four criteria, labelled A to D, each judged on a 0-8 scale against published descriptors, and the final subject grade is built from those judgements. A student can know the content and score poorly because they answered the question rather than the criterion. A tutor who has never read a descriptor cannot diagnose that.

The second is logistical. MYP covers roughly Years 6 to 11, and across that span a Dubailand student's day changes completely. An MYP 1 or 2 student at a school inside Motor City or Mudon can be home by three in the afternoon. An MYP 4 or 5 student travelling out of the belt to a school on Al Khail Road or in the Al Barsha and Jumeirah corridor is often not home before half past four, and later from Town Square or DAMAC Hills. Households with children at both ends of the programme are trying to serve two incompatible timetables in one evening.

The belt itself makes this harder than it sounds. Dubailand is a development zone rather than a neighbourhood, stretching south-east along Al Ain Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and taking in Arabian Ranches and its two later phases, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, DAMAC Hills, Town Square, Mudon and Remraam. A visiting tutor who can reach one of those communities at a usable hour frequently cannot reach another, and the one who claims both is pricing the drive into the fee.

There is a third factor that shapes an MYP week specifically. Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. KHDA calculates instructional time for those subjects on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. An MYP student therefore carries more taught subjects than an outside observer counting eight subject groups would expect, and the homework follows.

IB Gram's answer to all of it is to take travel out of the arrangement. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so an MYP 2 session can start at half past three and an MYP 5 session at six on the same evening, with different specialists and no second journey. Home visits are a service we operate only in India; nobody is sent to a Dubailand address. What follows is the detail: how criterion marking actually works, what the Personal Project needs, where the MYP to Diploma step breaks, and what the market charges.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubailand.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme spans five years and changes character substantially across them. These notes describe what each phase actually demands.

programmes.name: MYP 1 and 2, the early years
programmes.description: The transition out of the Primary Years Programme or into the IB from another curriculum. Content is manageable; the new demand is being assessed on process. Criterion B in sciences and mathematics asks students to investigate and design rather than to answer, and most children arrive with no experience of being judged on that. Early work here is mostly about understanding what is being asked.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools inside the Dubailand communities cover these years, so students are home early and a 3.30pm or 4pm session is genuinely workable. Families in Mudon, Remraam and Arabian Ranches 2 use that window more than anyone else in the belt.

programmes.name: MYP 3, the pivot year
programmes.description: The year subject choices start to narrow and the gap between students who write explanations and students who write descriptions becomes visible in grades. Interdisciplinary work appears, and the quality of written communication begins to drive marks across every subject group rather than only in language and literature.
programmes.countryNote: This is also the year many Dubailand families decide between continuing into MYP 4 and 5 or moving to a British school for International GCSE. Either way, the reasoning and writing skills built here transfer, which makes MYP 3 work unusually good value regardless of the route chosen afterwards.

programmes.name: MYP 4 and 5, the final phase
programmes.description: Subject content deepens and the Personal Project arrives. Some schools enter students for MYP eAssessment, on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, and some do not; ask the school which applies, because it changes the final year's shape entirely. Criterion descriptors become more demanding and the language of the top band is noticeably more exacting.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 and 5 students in this belt travel out of Dubailand to school and are the latest home. A 6pm or 6.15pm start that holds every week is worth more than a 5pm slot that collapses after a fortnight, and online delivery is the only version that can be pinned that precisely.

programmes.name: The Diploma Programme that follows
programmes.description: Six subjects across two levels plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. The step from MYP is less about content than about volume and independence, and students who never built a research and drafting habit in the Personal Project feel it immediately in the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: UAE school candidates sit the May session. The internal deadlines a Diploma student works to are set by their own coordinator months ahead, which is why a student who learned to manage a long project in MYP 5 has a real advantage over one who did not.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubailand.subjectsIntro: The MYP has eight subject groups and each applies its four criteria differently. These are the groups Dubailand families most often ask about, with the criterion that typically costs the marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the one students neglect and it is the direct ancestor of the Diploma exploration. Communication marks are lost to working that is correct and unreadable.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Students lose most in processing and evaluating, where data is presented without the uncertainty or the limitations the descriptor asks for, and in evaluations that stay general.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is where the top band separates: a student who summarises two sources accurately but never weighs their reliability against each other cannot reach it.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Analysing means explaining how a text produces an effect, not what happens in it, and the distinction is the single most common reason a confident reader scores in the middle band.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written text, communicating, and using language. Students are assessed within a phase rather than a year group, so a parent should know their child's phase before any tutoring is planned.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The documentation carries the marks rather than the artefact, and students who build something impressive without recording their decisions against the criteria score poorly.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal is where marks live, and it is the part students treat as an afterthought because the finished work feels like the point.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Written reflection is assessed as seriously as physical performance, which surprises both students and parents.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An extended independent project with a process journal and a report, assessed against its own criteria. Planning, applying skills and reflecting are what is marked, not the ambition of the product, and the report is where otherwise strong projects lose bands.

sections.heading: Criterion marking, and why a good answer can score badly
paragraphs: This is the thing most parents new to the Middle Years Programme find genuinely confusing, and it is worth setting out properly because almost every MYP tutoring problem traces back to it. Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each judged on a 0-8 scale against a published descriptor. The descriptor describes a quality of work, not a quantity of correct content. So a student can produce a factually accurate piece of work and sit in the middle band because the descriptor asked for something the work does not contain.

A concrete example makes it clear. In sciences, the processing and evaluating criterion asks students to present data, interpret it, and evaluate the method's validity and limitations. A student who records results neatly, draws a correct graph and writes that the experiment went well has done the content and missed two of the three things the descriptor names. Adding a paragraph that identifies a specific limitation and its specific effect on the result can lift the judgement a band without changing a single number.

The same pattern recurs across subject groups. In Individuals and Societies, thinking critically asks for sources weighed against one another, not summarised in turn. In Language and Literature, analysing asks how a text produces an effect, not what happens in it. In Design, the documentation of decisions is what is marked, not the artefact. In Arts, the process journal carries more weight than the finished piece. In every case the content-strong student who has never read the descriptor is leaving marks on the table.

The teaching response is specific and it is not revision. Take the student's returned work and the rubric it was marked against, read the band they achieved and the band above, and have the student rewrite one section to meet the higher descriptor. Three or four cycles of that changes how a student writes permanently. The table below sets out the four criteria across the subject groups Dubailand families ask about most.

sections.heading: Placing MYP sessions in a Dubailand week
paragraphs: The scheduling problem here is unusual because the Middle Years Programme spans five years with two very different school days inside them. Earlier-phase students in this belt often attend schools inside the communities and are home by three in the afternoon. Later-phase students travel out to the Al Khail corridor or the Al Barsha and Jumeirah area, and the bus route serving several Dubailand communities frequently delivers the last student home an hour after the bell.

That produces a household pattern families recognise immediately. An MYP 2 child is home, fed and available at half past three. Their MYP 5 sibling walks in at half past four, needs time to stop being a passenger, and is only properly usable from six. A single visiting tutor can serve one of them well. Two online slots at the hours each child can actually work serve both, and the second slot carries no travel cost because there is none.

What also has to be accounted for is the rest of the week. Academy training in Dubai Sports City and Motor City takes five until seven on several weekdays. The mandatory UAE subjects add taught periods and homework beyond the eight MYP subject groups. And MYP assessment tends to arrive in clusters rather than evenly, because several subjects set criterion-assessed tasks in the same fortnight, so a plan with no slack collapses in those weeks.

The practical answer is to decide what each slot is for before deciding when it is. Criterion coaching on returned work suits a short weekday session. Personal Project work, long-form writing and interdisciplinary tasks need a longer weekend morning. A family that plans both from the start gets more from two well-placed sessions than from four badly placed ones, which is also the cheaper arrangement.

sections.heading: Criterion levels are not percentages, and the conversion matters
paragraphs: Parents arriving from a percentage-based system try to translate MYP judgements into marks out of a hundred, and the translation does not work. Each criterion is judged on a 0-8 scale, the four judgements are combined, and the result is converted into a subject grade using boundaries the programme publishes. A student can hold a strong judgement in two criteria and a weak one in a third and land in a middle grade that does not reflect what they can do in their stronger areas.

That has two practical consequences. The first is that the route to a better grade is usually to lift the weakest criterion rather than to polish the strongest. A student who is consistently strong on knowing and understanding and weak on communicating is losing more to the second than they can gain from the first, and the work required is quite different. The second is that a parent reading a report needs the criterion breakdown rather than the overall grade, because the breakdown is what tells you where the effort should go.

Ask the school for two things: the criterion-level breakdown behind each subject grade, and the boundaries the school applies for the conversion. Schools hold both and most will share them readily. We do not publish boundary tables on this page, because grade boundary information belongs to the programme and reproducing it would be both a copyright matter and a risk of publishing something out of date.

The planning conclusion is simple and it is different from how most families approach tutoring. Do not buy support in the subject with the lowest grade. Buy support for the criterion that recurs as weakest across several subjects, because that is a transferable skill. A student who cannot evaluate is usually weak in evaluation in sciences, in Design and in Individuals and Societies at once, and one block of work on it improves three subjects.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and where the band is really decided
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the Middle Years Programme's culminating piece of independent work in MYP 5, with a process journal and a report assessed against its own criteria. Parents reasonably assume the band reflects the ambition of the product. It does not. It reflects the quality of the planning, the application of skills, the evidence in the journal, and the reflection in the report.

That misunderstanding produces a predictable failure. A student builds something genuinely impressive, keeps no usable record of the decisions made along the way, and writes a report describing what they made. The project is excellent and the band is middling, and nothing can be done about it afterwards because the evidence was never captured. The opposite case is just as common and much happier: a modest project with meticulous documentation and honest reflection scores well.

So the useful work happens at two points. At the start, testing whether the goal is achievable and whether the success criteria are specific enough to be tested against later. Vague success criteria make a good evaluation impossible, and the evaluation is marked. Then throughout, treating the process journal as assessed evidence rather than as a diary: dated entries, decisions with reasons, problems with responses, sources recorded properly.

The boundary on this support is firm and worth stating explicitly. A tutor may test the goal and the success criteria, explain what each criterion rewards, teach the journal as an assessed document, read the student's own report and identify where it is losing marks, and teach referencing. A tutor must never produce the project, write the report, or supply any part of it. One page ranking in this market sells completed assessed work; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: The MYP to Diploma or International GCSE step, and what breaks
paragraphs: In this belt the transition out of the Middle Years Programme happens in two directions, because the Dubailand school supply mixes British and IB settings within a few kilometres. Some students move from MYP 5 into the Diploma Programme; others move at MYP 3 or 4 into a British school and International GCSE. Both steps break in predictable ways, and both are cheaper to prepare for than to repair.

Moving into the Diploma, the thing that breaks is volume and independence rather than content. MYP assessment arrives in criterion-marked tasks with a rubric attached; Diploma assessment arrives as papers with markschemes that reward method and precise command-term reading. Students who relied on a rubric to tell them what was wanted find the Diploma does not supply one. The Extended Essay also lands on students who never managed a long project, which is exactly why the Personal Project experience matters beyond its own grade.

Moving into International GCSE, the thing that breaks is the opposite. These students are often strong at explaining and reflecting and comparatively weak at the procedural fluency that Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 rewards, and at recall-based science questions. They also meet tiering for the first time: Cambridge Core and Extended entries cap grades differently, and a student arriving mid-course can be placed on evidence from a system that measured something else.

Either way the fix is a short diagnostic rather than a long programme. Three to five sessions against the destination's actual assessment style identifies what is missing, and a written summary gives the receiving school something concrete to work with. Families in Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon and Town Square ask for this most, because mid-year moves are most common in the newer communities.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs around the Dubailand belt
paragraphs: MYP support sits lower in the market than Diploma support, for a defensible reason: the content depth is less and the work is often about assessment literacy rather than advanced subject knowledge. That makes the mid band the sensible target rather than the specialist one, and it makes the budget band genuinely usable for the earlier phases.

The sourced figures. Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. Premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED.

For MYP 1 to 3, the budget band is often adequate where the task is reading fluency, number work or getting a child to explain their reasoning out loud. For MYP 4 and 5, and for any criterion coaching that requires reading a descriptor properly, the mid band is the realistic floor. Personal Project support sits in the mid band too, because it is a process and documentation skill rather than an advanced subject one. Monthly, Bestimate's estimates give AED 240 to 600 for budget provision and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range for a weekly session.

The in-home premium in this belt deserves a specific mention for MYP families, because they are the households most likely to have two children at different phases. Three of the six most visible pages in this market publish no price at all, and in-home packages of four two-hour sessions are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. For two children at different hours, a visiting arrangement means two journeys or one compromised slot. None of these figures is an IB Gram price list, and the MoHRE private tutor permit is free, so no licensing charge belongs in any quote.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and claims a parent should refuse
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit and the detail is simple. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting a figure is speculating. There is a second rule that matters particularly for a family tempted by a convenient local arrangement: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. That reporting is press-sourced rather than quoted from the policy text, so verify against the current ADEK document.

School regulation sits with the emirate. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education and inspects on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education.

What that permits a tutoring platform to say is limited, and the limit is worth stating. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. A business with premises in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. We publish no grade promise and no statistic without the number of students, the date and the method behind it, and we do not reproduce IB programme documents or assessment material, which are the organisation's copyright.

process.title: Ask the school for the criterion breakdown
process.description: Not the subject grade but the four criterion judgements behind it, and the boundaries the school applies for the conversion. That breakdown tells you which criterion is weakest across subjects, which is where the effort should go.

process.title: Send a piece of marked work with its rubric
process.description: The returned task and the descriptor it was marked against is the most useful document a parent can supply. It makes the first session a diagnosis of a specific criterion rather than a general conversation about confidence.

process.title: Give the real arrival time for each child
process.description: MYP phases differ by more than an hour in this belt. An MYP 2 student is available at half past three and an MYP 5 sibling not until six. Two online slots serve both; one visiting tutor serves one of them well.

process.title: Use the free trial to test band language
process.description: A full session, no charge, no card. Ask the tutor to show what the next band up requires in the descriptor's own words and have the student rewrite a section to it. If that cannot happen in the hour, the match is wrong.

process.title: Target the weakest criterion, not the lowest grade
process.description: A student weak in evaluation is usually weak in it across sciences, Design and Individuals and Societies at once. One block of work on that criterion improves several subjects, which no subject-by-subject plan achieves for the same money.

whyPoints.title: Taught from the descriptors, not around them
whyPoints.description: MYP grades come from criterion judgements against published descriptors, so the work is the student's own returned task, the rubric it was marked against, and a rewrite to the band above. A subject tutor who has never read a descriptor cannot do that.

whyPoints.title: The weakest criterion targeted across subjects
whyPoints.description: Weakness in evaluating or communicating usually appears in three subject groups at once. Treating it as one transferable skill rather than three subject problems is both cheaper and faster, and almost nobody structures tutoring that way.

whyPoints.title: Phases scheduled separately within a household
whyPoints.description: An MYP 2 student and an MYP 5 sibling in this belt arrive home more than an hour apart. Online delivery lets each have the hour they can actually work in, with different specialists and no second travel cost.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project treated as process, not product
whyPoints.description: The band reflects planning, applied skills, journal evidence and reflection rather than the ambition of what was made. Support concentrates on the goal, the success criteria and the journal, because those are what is assessed and what cannot be fixed later.

whyPoints.title: No programme material reproduced
whyPoints.description: IB programme documents, assessment material and grade boundary information are the organisation's copyright, and we do not reproduce or supply them. Ask the school for its own boundaries and criterion breakdowns; both are legitimately available to a parent.

whyPoints.title: No approval claimed and no outcome promised
whyPoints.description: No KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry or IB approval, no UAE office, no grade promise, and no statistic without the number of students, the date and the method. The MoHRE private tutor permit is free of charge, so no licensing fee belongs in a quote.

faqs.question: What does the MYP actually assess, and how is the grade built?
faqs.answer: Each MYP subject carries four criteria, labelled A to D, each judged on a 0-8 scale against a published descriptor. The descriptors describe a quality of work rather than a quantity of correct content, and the four judgements are combined and converted into a subject grade using published boundaries. That is why a factually accurate piece of work can sit in a middle band: it answered the question without meeting what the descriptor asked for. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown behind each grade, because the breakdown is what tells you where effort should go.

faqs.question: Why does my child's correct work still get a middling MYP mark?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answer satisfies the content and not the criterion. In sciences, processing and evaluating asks students to interpret data and state limitations with their effect on the result; a neat table and a correct graph plus a sentence saying the experiment went well misses two of three things. In Individuals and Societies, thinking critically asks for sources weighed against each other rather than summarised in turn. The remedy is to work from the returned task and its rubric and rewrite one section to the band above.

faqs.question: How early can an MYP session start in the Dubailand communities?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the phase. MYP 1 and 2 students often attend schools inside the communities and are home between half past two and a quarter past three, which makes a 3.30pm or 4pm start genuinely workable. MYP 4 and 5 students travel out of the belt to schools on the Al Khail corridor or in the Al Barsha and Jumeirah area and are rarely home before half past four, later from Town Square or DAMAC Hills, so six o'clock is the first slot that holds through a term.

faqs.question: What does a Personal Project tutor actually do?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of which is producing the project. They test whether the goal is achievable and whether the success criteria are specific enough to be evaluated against later, because vague criteria make a good evaluation impossible and the evaluation is marked. They teach the process journal as assessed evidence rather than a diary: dated entries, decisions with reasons, problems with responses, sources recorded properly. And they give criterion feedback on the student's own report. The project, journal and report are the student's work entirely.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion is worth fixing first?
faqs.answer: Whichever one recurs as weakest across several subjects, because criteria are transferable in a way subject content is not. A student weak in evaluating is usually weak in evaluation in sciences, in Design and in Individuals and Societies simultaneously, so one block of work on it lifts three subjects. Communicating is the other common cross-subject weakness, and it shows as correct mathematics nobody can follow and strong ideas in disorganised paragraphs. Buying support in the subject with the lowest grade is the intuitive move and usually the less efficient one.

faqs.question: How do we find out whether MYP 5 here ends in eAssessment?
faqs.answer: That is a question for the school, because practice differs. Some schools enter MYP 5 students for eAssessment, involving on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, and some assess internally throughout without external entry. The answer changes the final year's shape completely: an eAssessment cohort needs timed on-screen practice and portfolio discipline, while an internally assessed cohort needs consistent criterion performance across a longer run of tasks. Ask the MYP coordinator directly rather than inferring it from a report.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP 5 into the Diploma. What should we prepare?
faqs.answer: Volume and independence rather than content. MYP tasks arrive with a rubric that tells the student what is wanted; Diploma papers arrive with markschemes that reward method and precise command-term reading, and nobody supplies the rubric. The Extended Essay also lands on students who may never have managed a long project, which is why Personal Project experience matters beyond its own grade. A short diagnostic against Diploma-style assessment, three to five sessions, identifies the gap more cheaply than a term of discovering it.

faqs.question: We are leaving the MYP for International GCSE. What breaks?
faqs.answer: The reverse of the Diploma problem. MYP students usually arrive strong at explaining and reflecting and comparatively weak at procedural fluency, which Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 reward heavily, and at recall-based science questions. They also meet tiering for the first time, and Cambridge Core and Extended entries cap grades differently. A student placed on evidence from a system that measured something else can end up on the wrong tier, so ask how the placement was made and when it can be revisited.

faqs.question: How much does MYP tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours. For MYP 1 to 3 fluency work, budget online provision at AED 45 to 150 an hour is often adequate, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For criterion coaching in MYP 4 and 5, and for Personal Project support, the qualified band of AED 150 to 300 is the realistic floor, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 for budget and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range for a weekly session.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two children at different MYP phases?
faqs.answer: They can, and in this belt it is usually better that they do not. An MYP 2 student needs reading fluency and help understanding what a criterion is; an MYP 5 student needs subject depth and Personal Project discipline. They also arrive home more than an hour apart. Two consecutive online slots with two specialists solves both problems at once, and the second slot carries no travel cost because nothing is travelling. Households in Mudon and Remraam request this arrangement more than any other.

faqs.question: How do mandatory UAE subjects affect an MYP timetable?
faqs.answer: They lengthen it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. An MYP student therefore carries more taught subjects, and more homework, than someone counting eight subject groups would expect.

faqs.question: Will you give us the MYP grade boundary tables?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is twofold. Grade boundary information and programme assessment documents are the IB's copyright, so reproducing them is not ours to do. And boundaries can be revised, so a table restated on a tutoring page risks being wrong without anybody touching it. Ask the school for the boundaries it applies and for the criterion breakdown behind each subject grade. Both are legitimately available to a parent, and the school's own figures are the ones that apply to your child.

faqs.question: Is MYP tutoring worth it if the grades are already fine?
faqs.answer: Often, though for a different reason than remediation. The criteria that MYP assesses, investigating, evaluating, communicating and thinking critically, are exactly the skills the Diploma and International GCSE then assume. A student holding a comfortable grade by being strong on knowing and understanding while weak on communicating will meet a problem later, when no rubric arrives to explain what is wanted. A short block on the weaker criterion is cheap insurance, and it reads as development rather than rescue, which students respond to better.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a permit to teach MYP students in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, the same permit applies regardless of programme. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no amounts are published. Ask also whether your child attends the tutor's own school.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubailand.closingHeading: Start with the rubric and the arrival time
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-dubailand.closingBody: An IB MYP tutor in Dubailand needs two things from you before the first session: a piece of marked work with the descriptor it was judged against, and the hour your child is genuinely able to work. The first makes the teaching specific, because MYP grades come from criterion judgements rather than from content coverage. The second makes it survive a term, because phases in this belt differ by more than an hour. Book a free trial lesson, ask the tutor to show what the next band up requires in the descriptor's own words, and plan the Personal Project separately.
