dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-emaar-beachfront.tutorsIntro: Our MYP tutors work criterion by criterion rather than topic by topic, because that is how the work is marked. Mathematics, the sciences, language and literature, individuals and societies and design are the subject groups families in this cluster ask for most.

intro.heading: A different marking system, and the comparison parents here are making
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme does not mark out of a hundred. Each subject is assessed against four published criteria, each scored from zero to eight, and the school converts the criterion profile into a grade from one to seven using a boundary table it publishes itself. A student can hold a strong criterion A and a weak criterion D and receive a grade that reveals neither. Parents reading a report see the number and not the shape, which is why MYP progress so often feels unreadable compared with a percentage.

This matters because the shape is the actionable part. In mathematics, criterion A rewards knowing and understanding, criterion B rewards investigating patterns, criterion C rewards communication and criterion D rewards applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student who is accurate but never generalises a pattern will sit in the middle bands forever, and no amount of extra practice on calculation will move them, because the marks they are missing are not awarded for calculation. The fix is specific and it is invisible without the criterion breakdown.

The second thing families in Emaar Beachfront are doing is comparing routes. Several schools serving this cluster run the MYP to Year 9 and then switch to IGCSE, while others carry the programme to Year 11 before the Diploma. That means a child in one Beachfront tower can be criterion-marked at fifteen while the child in the next tower sits tiered written papers. Parents compare notes and reasonably conclude one route must be better. The honest position is that they prepare students differently for different things, and this page sets out how.

Emaar Beachfront's practical situation sets the timetable for any of this. The peninsula has one road link, no school and no tuition centre inside it, and visitor access to tower basements needs a resident escort. Children travel to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah, leaving before 07:00 and returning after 15:30. MYP work is frequently project-shaped rather than problem-shaped, which means it needs longer uninterrupted blocks than a Diploma revision session does. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits exist only in our India service.

What follows explains the criteria for each subject group, compares the MYP and IGCSE routes at 16 on the things that actually differ, describes what changes between MYP 1 and MYP 5, sets out how the Personal Project is marked and when coaching helps, names the step into the Diploma and the two gaps MYP students typically carry into it, and explains the honesty boundary on project work. Confirm your school's own criterion boundaries and reporting practice, because conversion tables are set at school level rather than by the IB.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Criterion marking begins and the habits that decide later grades form here. Students learn to investigate, to communicate a method and to apply knowledge in unfamiliar contexts, which are the three things later criteria keep rewarding. A student who is accurate and silent will hold a middle grade through all three years without anybody identifying why.

programmes.description: The final two years, where criterion demands rise sharply and the Personal Project runs. Subject work moves towards extended tasks and longer written responses, and the gap between students who can structure an argument and students who can recall content widens considerably.
programmes.countryNote: Some schools enter MYP 5 students for the IB's optional external assessment leading to the MYP certificate; others award school-based grades only. Ask which applies, because it changes what the final year is preparing for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme after MYP
programmes.description: Six subjects with published component weightings plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. MYP students usually arrive comfortable with investigation and extended writing, and short of procedural speed under timed conditions, which is the one gap worth addressing in the first term of DP1.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-emaar-beachfront.subjectsIntro: MYP subjects are grouped, and each group has its own four criteria. These are the groups families in this cluster ask for, with the criterion that most often holds a student back.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where accurate students stall, because generalising a pattern and justifying the generalisation is a different skill from calculating correctly.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C is the usual weakness: students process data competently and write an evaluation that names no specific limitation of their own method.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students who read well and write fluently often lose marks under organising, because a response with good ideas in no deliberate order cannot reach the upper bands however well written it is.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed within a phase rather than a year group. A student can be in different phases in different skills, and support has to be matched to the phase the school has placed them in rather than to their age.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the criterion that separates grades at MYP 4 and 5, and it rewards a judgement supported by evidence rather than a balanced list of points.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Students who build first and document afterwards cannot reconstruct the evidence the criteria require, which is the single most common cause of a disappointing design grade.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than students expect, and a strong final piece with no documented development will not reach the top bands.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and reflective criteria are often where marks are available to students who are not the strongest performers.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project marked on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. The process journal is evidence rather than decoration, and students who leave it until the end cannot produce the record the criteria ask for.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria, these units ask students to integrate two subject groups and explain the integration. Students treat them as double work rather than as a distinct task, and lose marks for not making the connection explicit.

sections.heading: What an MYP grade actually tells you, and what it hides
paragraphs: A grade of five in MYP mathematics is a conversion, not a score. Behind it sit four criterion marks, each from zero to eight, and the school's own boundary table that turns the profile into a single digit. Two students with the same grade can have opposite profiles: one strong on knowing and understanding and weak on communication, the other the reverse. They need completely different support and the report gives you no way to tell them apart.

This is why the first useful request a parent can make is for the criterion breakdown rather than the grade. Most schools hold it and many will share it when asked directly, often through the online reporting platform rather than the printed report. With the breakdown, a tutor can target the criterion that is costing the grade. Without it, the first two sessions go on reconstructing the profile from the student's work, which is possible but slower and less precise.

The hidden pattern worth looking for is a consistently low criterion across several subjects. A student weak on communication in mathematics, organising in language and literature, and processing and evaluating in sciences does not have three subject problems. They have one skill gap appearing three times, and a single block of work on structuring and justifying written responses will move all three grades. That diagnosis is only visible when the criterion profiles are read side by side, which almost nobody does.

Ask for the breakdown in writing rather than in a corridor conversation at a parents' evening, and ask for it termly. A single profile tells you where the student is; three profiles tell you whether the targeted criterion is actually moving, which is the only question that matters once support has started.

sections.heading: MYP to Year 11, or IGCSE from Year 10: the real comparison
paragraphs: Schools serving this cluster do both, which makes this a live question rather than an academic one. Carrying the MYP to Year 11 keeps a student inside criterion assessment for two more years, with extended tasks, the Personal Project and interdisciplinary work. Switching to IGCSE at the end of Year 9 moves them into tiered written examinations with published syllabus codes, external marking and a clear reference point at 16.

Each prepares a student well for something. MYP to Year 11 builds investigation, extended writing and reflection, which are exactly the skills the Diploma core demands, so MYP students often handle the Extended Essay and internal assessments better than their IGCSE-educated classmates. IGCSE builds procedural speed, mark-scheme literacy and examination stamina, which are exactly the skills Diploma written papers demand. Neither route is a disadvantage; each leaves a predictable gap.

The decision usually is not the family's to make, because it follows the school. Where it is a choice, the useful questions are about the student rather than the programme: does this child produce better work over three weeks or in ninety minutes, and do they need an external reference point at 16 for any reason, such as a possible move between school systems? An IGCSE grade travels more legibly between countries and systems than an MYP criterion profile does, which matters for families who may relocate.

One further point, often decisive in this cluster. Families who may relocate within the next few years should weigh portability heavily, because an admissions officer in another country reads a subject grade immediately and reads a criterion profile only if someone explains it to them. That is not an argument about educational quality; it is an argument about how a transcript is received by a stranger under time pressure.

sections.heading: What changes between MYP 1 and MYP 5
paragraphs: The criteria keep their names across the five years and the descriptors behind them do not stay still. In MYP 1 a student meets a criterion asking them to communicate a method and satisfies it with a clear explanation. By MYP 5 the same criterion expects appropriate mathematical language, consistent notation, and a form of presentation chosen for the audience. Parents reading the criterion name across a report series assume nothing changed, and then cannot explain why a student who scored six in Year 7 is scoring five in Year 10.

The second change is task length. Early MYP assessment tends to be contained: a task set, completed, marked. By MYP 4 and 5 students are producing extended work over weeks, with documentation requirements, and the skills that decide the grade shift from knowing the content to managing a process. A student who is organised scores above a student who is knowledgeable, which is uncomfortable and is what the criteria are designed to reward.

The third change is the Personal Project, which arrives in the final MYP year and is marked on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It is the first genuinely independent piece of work most students have produced, and the process journal is assessed evidence rather than a diary. Students who leave the journal until the project is finished cannot produce the record the criteria ask for, and no amount of quality in the final product compensates for it.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, coached from planning rather than writing
paragraphs: The Personal Project is marked on criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, and the grade is determined substantially by evidence the student generates while working rather than by the finished product. That inverts how students naturally approach it. They choose something ambitious, build it, and then write about it, discovering at the end that the criteria wanted a documented record of decisions, setbacks and adjustments that no longer exists in any retrievable form.

Coaching helps most at the start and barely at all at the end. In the first two sessions a tutor can test whether the goal is achievable in the time available, whether the student has access to whatever the project needs, and whether a credible success criterion can be stated. They can also establish the journal habit: short, dated entries recording decisions and reasons, kept throughout rather than assembled afterwards. That habit is worth more to the final grade than any amount of polish on the report.

The boundary is firm and worth stating. A tutor may question the goal, help the student articulate their own success criteria, ask what the journal is missing, read a draft report and give feedback on its structure and clarity. A tutor may not choose the project, do any part of the work, write or rewrite the report, or produce the journal entries. The project is explicitly the student's own, the school supervises it, and our tutors decline the other request directly rather than negotiating around it.

sections.heading: The step from MYP 5 into the Diploma
paragraphs: MYP students usually arrive in DP1 with two clear strengths and one clear gap. The strengths are investigation and extended writing: they have designed their own inquiries, documented process, written at length and reflected on their own work, so the Extended Essay, the internal assessments and Theory of Knowledge feel like familiar territory rather than a new genre. That advantage is real and it tends to show up in DP2 rather than in the first term.

The gap is procedural speed under timed conditions. Criterion assessment rewards a justified approach developed over time; Diploma written papers reward a correct answer produced quickly, with method visible and nothing extraneous. A student who has spent five years being assessed on reasoning and reflection meets a paper that wants neither, and the first mock exposes it. The repair is a term of timed procedural work, and it is cheap in September and expensive in March.

The second, smaller gap is command-term discipline. The Diploma uses a published command-term vocabulary where state, describe, explain, analyse and evaluate each set a ceiling, and MYP criterion language does not map onto it directly. A student who writes a thorough, reflective answer to a question that said state is spending time for nothing, and one who writes descriptively in response to evaluate cannot reach the top band. Two or three sessions on this early in DP1 changes every answer afterwards.

The practical version of all this is one conversation in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1. Twenty minutes spent identifying which of the two gaps applies, followed by six to eight sessions in the autumn, is worth more than a term of general subject tutoring in the spring of DP1 after a mock has already set the student's view of themselves.

sections.heading: Why MYP tutors are harder to find than Diploma tutors
paragraphs: There are fewer people who can tutor the MYP well than there are who can tutor the Diploma, and the reason is not difficulty. Diploma content is public, specific and examined externally, so a strong subject graduate can teach it credibly after reading the subject guide. MYP assessment depends on criterion descriptors applied with judgement, and judgement comes from having marked against them. A tutor who has never read a band descriptor can teach the content beautifully and leave the grade exactly where it was.

This produces a recognisable pattern in families around the Marina. A subject tutor is engaged, the sessions are good, the student enjoys them, the content knowledge improves, and the grade holds at five. The missing marks were in communicating, or in investigating patterns, or in thinking critically, and nothing in the sessions addressed those because nobody looked at which criterion was short. Parents conclude the child has reached their level, which is usually wrong.

The question to ask any prospective MYP tutor is direct: which criteria does this subject group use, and which one do you think is costing my child marks? A tutor who can name the four criteria and ask to see the breakdown is working in the right system. A tutor who answers in terms of topics has not noticed that the topics are not what is being marked. Removing travel from the equation widens the pool of people who can pass that test, which is the main practical argument for online delivery in this part of the programme.

sections.heading: What a first month of MYP support should produce
paragraphs: Session one should end with a criterion profile, assembled from the school's breakdown if available and from the student's work if not, plus a judgement about which criterion is costing the most across subjects. That document is the plan. If a tutor finishes the first session talking about topics rather than criteria, the sessions that follow will improve content knowledge and not the grade, which is a genuinely common outcome and the reason this page spends so long on the point.

By the end of the first month, the student should be able to say in their own words what the targeted criterion rewards, and should have produced at least two pieces of work in the format that criterion is assessed in. Not practice questions, but work shaped like the real task: an investigation with a generalisation, a response with a deliberate structure, an evaluation naming specific limitations of their own method. Those pieces are the evidence that the work is landing.

Then the measure becomes the school's own marking. The honest checkpoint is the next piece of assessed work in that subject, read against the criterion that was targeted. If the criterion mark moves, continue. If it does not, the diagnosis was wrong or the practice was not in the right format, and that is a conversation to have immediately rather than at the end of the term. We would rather change a tutor or a plan in week four than defend either in week twelve.

sections.heading: Booking MYP support from Emaar Beachfront
paragraphs: Send the year group, the subject groups you are concerned about, the criterion breakdown if your school publishes it, whether the school intends to continue the MYP to Year 11 or switch to IGCSE, and the hours that genuinely exist after a bus that leaves before 07:00 and returns after 15:30. The route question matters as much as the subject, because criterion coaching for a student switching to IGCSE in nine months is a different investment from criterion coaching for a student who has two more MYP years.

We match a tutor who works criterion by criterion in that subject group and propose a slot in Gulf Standard Time. Project work goes to weekend mornings because it needs ninety uninterrupted minutes. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, producing a criterion profile and a target rather than a sales conversation. If the match is wrong after the trial or in week four, we change the tutor.

The limits. MYP specialists are scarcer than Diploma specialists in every subject group, so matching can take longer, and for the smaller subject groups there are weeks when nobody suitable is free. We will say so and offer alternatives rather than putting a content tutor into a criterion problem. We cannot promise a grade, and for the Personal Project in particular the student has to do the work, which is not a policy position but what the criteria require.

One last note on expectations. MYP support rarely produces a dramatic result in a single term, because criterion marks move on assessed pieces and assessed pieces arrive on the school's schedule rather than ours. What it does produce, within a month, is a student who can say what the criterion rewards and work in that shape. That is the leading indicator, and it is the one to watch.

process.title: Ask the school for the criterion breakdown
process.description: The four criterion marks behind the grade, which many schools hold on their reporting platform even when the printed report shows only the digit. With the breakdown a tutor targets the criterion costing the grade. Without it, the first two sessions reconstruct the profile from the student's work.

process.title: Read the profiles across subjects together
process.description: A low criterion appearing in three subject groups is one skill gap, not three subject problems. Communication in mathematics, organising in language and literature and processing in sciences failing together points at a single block of work that moves all three grades at once.

process.title: Confirm the route at 16
process.description: Whether the school carries the MYP to Year 11 or switches to IGCSE after Year 9 changes what the next two years are preparing for. Criterion coaching for a student leaving the programme in nine months is a different investment from coaching one with two MYP years remaining.

process.title: Free trial producing a target criterion
process.description: One trial lesson per student, no card required, ending with a criterion profile and a named target. You keep that document whether or not you continue, and it is useful to any MYP tutor you engage, including one you find elsewhere.

process.title: Check against the school's next assessed piece
process.description: The measure is the criterion mark on the next real task, not a practice score. If the targeted criterion moves, continue. If it does not, the diagnosis or the practice format was wrong, and we change the plan in week four rather than defending it in week twelve.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-led, not topic-led
whyPoints.description: MYP work is marked against four published criteria per subject group. We target the criterion costing the grade, because content teaching with no criterion work is the most common reason good sessions leave a grade exactly where it was.

whyPoints.title: The profile read across subjects
whyPoints.description: A criterion failing in three subject groups is one skill gap appearing three times. Reading the profiles side by side is how that becomes visible, and it turns three separate tutoring decisions into one block of work.

whyPoints.title: Personal Project coached at the planning stage
whyPoints.description: The grade rests heavily on documented process. We work on goal feasibility, success criteria and the journal habit in the first sessions, because none of that can be reconstructed once the project is finished.

whyPoints.title: An honest view of the route at 16
whyPoints.description: MYP to Year 11 and IGCSE from Year 10 prepare students well for different things and leave different gaps. We set that out rather than recommending whichever route happens to generate more tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Transition work scheduled before habits set
whyPoints.description: MYP students entering the Diploma usually need timed procedural work and command-term discipline. Both are cheap in September and expensive in March, which is why we propose them before the first mock rather than after it.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: We publish no success rates, no average criterion gains and no grade promises, because none could be evidenced with n, date and method. What you get is a target criterion and a checkpoint on the school's own next assessed piece.

faqs.question: What does an MYP grade of 5 actually mean for my child in Emaar Beachfront?
faqs.answer: It means the four criterion marks behind it, converted by your school's own boundary table. Each criterion is scored from zero to eight, so two students with the same grade can have opposite profiles: strong content and weak communication, or the reverse. The grade is a conversion rather than a score, which is why it feels unreadable next to a percentage. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown, which is usually available on the reporting platform even when the printed report shows only the digit.

faqs.question: Why has my child's grade dropped when the criterion name is the same?
faqs.answer: Because the descriptor behind the name rises each year while the name stays still. A criterion asking a Year 7 student to communicate a method is satisfied by a clear explanation. The same criterion in Year 10 expects appropriate subject language, consistent notation and a presentation form chosen for the audience. A student who has not noticed the escalation keeps producing Year 7 work and receives a falling grade, which looks like decline and is actually a standard moving.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion holds most mathematics students back?
faqs.answer: Investigating patterns. Students who calculate accurately satisfy knowing and understanding without difficulty and then stall, because generalising a pattern and justifying the generalisation is a different skill that no amount of additional calculation practice develops. A student stuck at a five in mathematics with strong arithmetic almost always has a low criterion B, and the work that moves it is pattern tasks with explicit generalisation rather than more exercises.

faqs.question: Should our school have switched to IGCSE after Year 9?
faqs.answer: Both routes prepare students well for different things. Continuing the MYP builds investigation, extended writing and reflection, which makes the Diploma core feel familiar. Switching to IGCSE builds procedural speed, mark-scheme literacy and exam stamina, which makes Diploma written papers feel familiar. Neither is a disadvantage and each leaves a predictable gap. Where it matters most is portability: an IGCSE grade in a named subject travels between school systems more legibly than a criterion profile does.

faqs.question: How is the Personal Project marked?
faqs.answer: On its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a substantial share of the grade resting on evidence the student generates while working rather than on the finished product. The process journal is assessed material, not a diary. Students who build something impressive and then write about it discover that the criteria wanted a documented record of decisions and setbacks which no longer exists. The journal habit is worth more than polish on the final report.

faqs.question: How early should Personal Project coaching begin in MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Most usefully at the very beginning. A tutor can test whether the goal is achievable in the time available, whether the student can access what the project needs, and whether credible success criteria can be stated, and can establish the journal habit of short dated entries recording decisions and reasons. A tutor may not choose the project, do any of the work, write the report or produce journal entries. The project is explicitly the student's own and the school supervises it.

faqs.question: Why did a good subject tutor not move my child's MYP grade?
faqs.answer: Because the missing marks were probably in a criterion the sessions never addressed. Diploma content is public and examined externally, so a strong graduate can teach it credibly from the subject guide. MYP assessment depends on criterion descriptors applied with judgement, and that comes from having marked against them. A tutor who teaches topics well and has never read a band descriptor improves content knowledge and leaves the criterion profile untouched, which is exactly what you observed.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective MYP tutor?
faqs.answer: Two questions. Which four criteria does this subject group use, and which one do you think is costing my child marks? A tutor working in the right system can name the criteria and will ask to see the breakdown before answering the second question. A tutor who answers in terms of topics and chapters has not registered that the topics are not what is being marked. The answers to those two questions tell you more than any amount of qualification listing.

faqs.question: My child is moving into DP1 from MYP 5. What should we do first?
faqs.answer: Timed procedural work, starting in September rather than after the first mock. MYP students generally arrive strong on investigation and extended writing, which makes the Diploma core feel familiar, and short on producing correct answers quickly under exam conditions, because criterion assessment rewarded a justified approach developed over time. Add two or three sessions on Diploma command terms, which do not map onto MYP criterion language and quietly cap answers until someone explains them.

faqs.question: Is a low criterion in several subjects three problems or one?
faqs.answer: Almost always one. A student weak on communicating in mathematics, organising in language and literature, and processing and evaluating in sciences has a single gap in structuring and justifying written work, appearing three times. Treating it as three subject problems means three tutors and three times the cost for the same repair. Reading the criterion profiles side by side is what makes this visible, and it is the reason we ask for all of them rather than one.

faqs.question: How long should an MYP project session be from this peninsula?
faqs.answer: Ninety minutes, which on a weekday from Emaar Beachfront means a 17:30 start at the earliest and in practice usually a weekend morning. Project work needs continuity: a student who has to stop fifteen minutes after loading their materials achieves very little. Subject criterion work runs well in sixty minutes on a weekday slot. Splitting the two across the week rather than alternating within one session is what makes both productive.

faqs.question: Does the MYP have external examinations in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Optionally, and it depends on your school. Some schools enter MYP 5 students for the IB's optional external assessment leading to the MYP certificate, and others award school-based grades only. Ask which applies, because it changes what the final year is preparing for and whether examination technique needs any attention at all. A student with no external assessment ahead of them should be spending that time on criterion work and the Personal Project instead.

faqs.question: Are language acquisition phases the same as year groups?
faqs.answer: No, and conflating them is a common source of mismatched support. Students are placed in a phase based on prior exposure to the language, so a Year 9 student may sit in a lower or higher phase than their classmates, and may even be at different phases across the four skill criteria of listening, reading, speaking and writing. Support must be matched to the phase the school has placed them in, which is a question for the language teacher rather than a guess from the year group.

faqs.question: What should the first month of MYP support produce?
faqs.answer: A criterion profile and a named target criterion from session one, then two pieces of work shaped like the real task rather than practice questions: an investigation with a genuine generalisation, a response with a deliberate structure, an evaluation naming specific limitations of the student's own method. The checkpoint is the school's next assessed piece in that subject, read against the targeted criterion. If the criterion mark does not move, the plan changes rather than continuing.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-emaar-south.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Middle Years Programme subjects to students living in Emaar South, Golf Links, Urbana, Expo Golf Villas and the wider Dubai South area. Matching runs on subject group, because criterion B in Sciences and criterion B in Individuals and Societies ask for completely different things.

intro.heading: The honest answer: lots of tutors, very few who have read a descriptor
paragraphs: Ask whether anyone near Emaar South knows this programme and the surface answer is yes, easily. Middle Years students study ordinary subjects, and there is no shortage of people who can teach mathematics, science, English or humanities to a thirteen year old. What is genuinely scarce is somebody who can take a marked task, open the published criterion descriptors for that subject group, and say which band the work sat in and what the band above required. That is the skill the programme actually rewards, and almost nobody advertising for it has it.

The reason is structural rather than anybody's fault. In an examination system a shared mark scheme culture develops: teachers and tutors handle the same past papers, compare the same official schemes, and acquire a common language for where marks sit. The Middle Years Programme has no public examination in most schools. Assessment is internal, task by task, against four criteria labelled A to D on a 0 to 8 scale, converted at the end into a grade from 1 to 7. There is no shared bank of papers around which that culture could form.

The second complication is that the labels are constant and their content is not. Criterion B in Sciences is inquiring and designing. In Individuals and Societies it is investigating. In Mathematics it is investigating patterns. In Language and Literature it is organising. So the phrase Middle Years tutor, with no subject group attached, is close to meaningless as a claim, and a tutor who has worked with one subject group's criteria does not automatically understand another's.

Third, the components most families want help with are the ones fewest tutors have supervised. The Personal Project runs across most of the final year and is assessed on its own criteria including a process journal that cannot be convincingly reconstructed. Interdisciplinary units are assessed on their own criteria and treated by students as a side activity. Both are common requests and both have a very small pool of people who have actually marked them.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and no tutor is dispatched to an Emaar South address, which matters here because the community has no school inside it and a visiting tutor would absorb a twenty-five to forty-five minute journey each way. Students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the task brief, the published criteria and the student's own work open side by side on a shared screen, which is how most of a useful session is actually spent.

One factual note. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools annually and publishes the reports, and requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it is licensed for. KHDA does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership and operates no UAE centre. Individual tutors need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-emaar-south.subjectsIntro: The Middle Years subject groups Emaar South families request, each with the criterion that actually decides the grade and a note on how rare real criterion experience is in it.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion C rewards communicating mathematics and criterion D rewards applying it in real-life contexts, so a procedurally strong student can sit mid-band because the write-up shows no reasoning or no conclusion answering the task question. Plenty of maths tutors; very few who have marked criterion C.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion A is knowing and understanding, B is inquiring and designing, C is processing and evaluating, D is reflecting on the impacts of science. Students strong on content lose marks in B and D, not A, and a science tutor who has only taught content will treat that as a content problem.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criterion B is investigating, which rewards a research question and a documented process rather than an answer. Marks go on sources used without evaluation and conclusions that summarise rather than argue. Essay structure taught explicitly moves this faster than further reading does.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. A well-argued essay in weak prose and a fluent essay with no argument both sit mid-band for opposite reasons, and identifying which a student is doing is the entire diagnosis. One marked piece establishes it.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Organised by phase rather than year, with four criteria across listening, reading, speaking and writing. A student placed in the wrong phase appears weak when they are misplaced, which is worth checking before buying anything. Productive skills respond faster than receptive ones.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The design cycle is the assessment: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. Three of the four criteria concern process rather than outcome, so a good final product with a thin process folder scores poorly. Documenting as you go is the whole technique.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, responding. As in Design, process documentation carries criteria of its own, so a strong performer with no reflective record sits below a thoughtful one with a complete journal. This surprises families consistently.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Four criteria including planning for performance and reflecting on performance, which means written work matters in a subject most students assume is practical. A student who performs well and documents nothing loses marks in two of four criteria, and the written components are entirely learnable.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal that is itself assessed. The commonest failure is a goal too broad to achieve and document in the time, which caps the mark before work begins. The smallest pool of genuinely experienced supervisors.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed on their own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. Students treat them as a side activity because they belong to no single subject, then lose marks in an assessment that counted. Almost nobody tutors them, and knowing they are assessed is most of the fix.

subjects.name: Arabic as a mandatory subject
subjects.description: Arabic is compulsory in Dubai private schools under KHDA rules whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language. It sits alongside the programme rather than inside it and is often the first thing a family seeks help with.

subjects.name: Transition skills into the Diploma
subjects.description: Timed writing, note-taking from exposition, mathematical notation and producing under examination conditions. None is a Middle Years criterion and all are assumed from day one of the Diploma. Better covered than criterion work, because the skills are shared with examination systems.

sections.heading: Why a long list of names is the wrong kind of comfort
paragraphs: Middle Years students study subjects with ordinary names, so the search returns ordinary subject tutors, and most of them are perfectly competent at the subject. That is why a family in Emaar South will find somebody quickly and why the find frequently disappoints. The programme does not grade subject knowledge directly. It grades work against four published criterion descriptors, and the gap between knowing a subject and knowing its descriptors is where the money goes.

The absence of a public examination is the root of it. In an examination system, tutors and teachers handle the same past papers and the same official mark schemes, and a shared language about where marks sit develops over years. In most Middle Years schools there is no public examination, assessment is internal and task-based, and there is no common bank of material around which that language could form. A tutor who has never worked inside an IB school has had no route to acquiring it.

That produces a specific and very common failure. A student with high criterion A scores and low B and D scores across every subject has one problem appearing in many places: they know the content and do not show the process the criteria reward. A general subject tutor reads the low grade, concludes the content needs reinforcing, and spends a term reinforcing the one thing that was never weak. Nothing moves, and nobody involved understands why.

So the recommendation for this programme is the same shape as for chemistry and the opposite of the one for physics. Assume you can find somebody. Spend the effort you saved on verification instead, using a test that takes one task and five minutes. The next section sets it out, and it works on us as readily as on anybody advertising locally.

sections.heading: The one-task test
paragraphs: Take a marked task your child has already had returned, with whatever the teacher wrote on it, and ask the tutor one question: which criterion is this assessing, and what did the band above the one it received require? That is the whole test. It needs no preparation on your part and it separates the two populations described above in about five minutes.

Somebody with real criterion experience answers specifically. They will name the criterion, say which strand of the descriptor the work satisfied and which it did not, and quote the sort of thing the next band demands: a conclusion that answers the task question rather than summarising, a method that accounts for a variable the student ignored, sources evaluated rather than listed, a reflection that considers implications rather than restating what happened. That is the language of the descriptors and it cannot be improvised.

Somebody without it answers in subject terms. They will tell you the science is sound, the essay reads well, the mathematics is correct, and perhaps suggest more practice. All of that may be true and none of it addresses why the mark was what it was. It is not incompetence, it is the wrong competence, and for this programme specifically the wrong competence produces a term of pleasant sessions and an unchanged report.

Two follow-ups sharpen it further. Ask what criterion B asks in this subject, where the right answer differs by subject group and a vague reply reveals a lot. And ask what they would look at first if the report showed high A and low D across every subject, where the right answer is the process criteria treated once rather than each subject separately. Three questions, three short right answers, and most of the risk removed before any payment.

sections.heading: Why the subject group matters more than the subject
paragraphs: The phrase Middle Years tutor carries almost no information without a subject group attached, and that is not a pedantic point. The criteria are labelled A to D consistently across subjects and their content is set per subject group, so a tutor who has worked with one group's descriptors has learned a vocabulary that does not transfer.

The clearest illustration is criterion B. In Sciences it is inquiring and designing, which concerns method and variables. In Individuals and Societies it is investigating, which concerns a research question and a documented process. In Mathematics it is investigating patterns. In Language and Literature it is organising, which concerns structure. Four different demands behind one letter, and a tutor applying the wrong one will give confident advice that moves the mark in the wrong direction.

This also explains a confusion families report regularly. A report showing criterion B at 4 in two subjects looks like one weakness and describes two. A parent who takes that to a tutor as my child is weak at criterion B has asked an unanswerable question, and a tutor who accepts the framing rather than correcting it has told you something about their familiarity with the programme.

The practical consequence for matching is that we ask which subjects and therefore which groups, before anything else. It also means a single tutor can sometimes cover two subjects in the same group coherently, because the descriptor vocabulary is shared, and should not be assumed to cover two subjects in different groups. For an Emaar South household trying to use one session well, knowing which pairings are coherent is a genuine saving.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the smallest pool of all
paragraphs: This is the single most requested item from Emaar South families at the top of the programme and the one with the fewest genuinely experienced people available. The Personal Project runs across most of the final year, is assessed on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, and includes a process journal that is itself assessed and cannot be convincingly reconstructed afterwards.

The common failures are known and all three happen before any work is done. A goal too broad to achieve in the time, which caps the mark in advance. A goal that is achievable but not documentable, so a student learns a practical skill and has nothing written to show how. And criteria for success that are never stated at the outset, leaving nothing to evaluate the outcome against at the end. A supervisor who has marked projects raises all three in the first conversation. One who has not will discuss the topic enthusiastically.

The scheduling problem compounds it in this community. Each stage needs a stretch of time a weekday evening cannot give after a twenty-five to forty-five minute journey, and the journal has to be kept as the work happens rather than written up later. That makes weekend mornings and the winter break the only realistic home for it, which is a planning decision to be taken in the autumn rather than discovered in the spring.

The limit on help is firm and worth stating because the pressure to cross it is real. A tutor may discuss the goal, reject one that cannot be achieved or documented, insist on the journal being kept as the work runs, explain the criteria and what the band above requires, and give feedback on the student's own draft report. A tutor may not produce the project, write any part of the report, or construct the journal. The project exists specifically to demonstrate the student's own independent work.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units, which almost nobody tutors
paragraphs: These are assessed, on their own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting, and they are the component students are most likely to treat as optional. The reason is simple: they belong to no single subject, so no subject teacher owns them in the student's mind, and they often feel less serious than a subject task. Then a mark arrives and counts.

The tutoring market reflects that neglect. Almost nobody advertises experience with interdisciplinary units, because almost nobody has marked one, and a general subject tutor has no basis for helping with an assessment that explicitly asks a student to connect two disciplines. For an Emaar South family the practical upshot is that this is not a component to go shopping for; it is one to handle inside a criteria block with somebody who knows the programme.

What actually helps is narrow. Establishing that the unit is assessed at all is most of it, because students who know a mark is coming behave differently. Reading the specific criteria for the unit, which are published, is the next part, particularly the synthesising criterion, which asks for a genuine connection between the disciplines rather than two separate treatments stapled together. That distinction is where most of the lost marks sit.

There is a second-order benefit worth mentioning. A student who learns to read the criteria for an interdisciplinary unit has practised exactly the skill the whole programme rewards, on a task where the stakes are lower than a subject report. Several families here have used an interdisciplinary unit as the vehicle for teaching descriptor reading, which is a more efficient use of three sessions than treating it as a one-off problem to be solved.

sections.heading: What a general subject tutor can honestly do
paragraphs: This section exists because the previous ones could be read as saying a general subject tutor is useless for this programme, which would be unfair and untrue. There is real work they do well, and for some students it is exactly the right purchase. The point is to know which situation you are in before paying.

Where a general subject tutor earns their place is genuine content gaps. A student who missed a term of mathematics through illness, or who has arrived from another system and never met a topic, needs teaching rather than descriptor analysis, and a competent subject tutor delivers that efficiently. The same applies to language acquisition, where drilled structures and vocabulary respond to ordinary good teaching regardless of criterion knowledge.

They also do well on confidence and habit. A thirteen year old who will not start work without company, or who needs somebody to establish a routine, is buying supervision, and supervision does not require criterion expertise. For an Emaar South household where the problem is that nothing gets done after a long journey rather than that the work is wrong, that is the honest purchase.

Where they cannot help is the characteristic Middle Years failure: a student whose content is sound and whose criterion B and D scores are low across every subject. That is a descriptor problem and reinforcing content will not touch it. The test in this page distinguishes the two situations in five minutes, and a family who runs it will know which kind of tutor they actually need rather than guessing.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects alongside the programme
paragraphs: An Emaar South student in a Dubai private school is not only studying the Middle Years Programme. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, under KHDA's requirements, and they are frequently the grade a family is most concerned about.

KHDA's rules are specific. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the groups, and combined classes are prohibited. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

There is also a constraint that affects how any tutoring here can honestly be described. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. Support in these subjects therefore works with the school's own prescribed material rather than introducing a parallel syllabus, and a provider offering an alternative curriculum for them is describing something that is not permitted.

KHDA also specifies that mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, that schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and that it is advised any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a school credential a parent can ask about. It does not apply to private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA approval of any kind.

sections.heading: What this should cost, and what is being overcharged
paragraphs: Middle Years support should cost less than Diploma support and frequently does not, because the published bands do not distinguish by programme and a provider has no reason to volunteer the distinction. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates run AED 240-600 a month for budget provision at one hour a week, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, which is a Diploma figure rather than a Middle Years one.

Hourly, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the budget end, both online. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for qualified subject tutors. TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is in the hour, and from Emaar South that sits at the top of its band because the journey is long.

A family paying an examination-year specialist rate for a Year 8 student with a criterion problem is overpaying for the wrong thing twice: the rate reflects Diploma scarcity, and the work needed is three or four sessions of descriptor reading rather than a standing arrangement. The right spend here is narrow and bounded. A criteria block. A single-criterion repair. A Personal Project block at goal-setting stage. A Diploma transition block the summer before Year 12.

What is poor value is a standing weekly session in a subject where the content is sound and the process marks are low, which is a fair description of a great deal of Middle Years tutoring in this market. Every figure above belongs to the provider named; none is an IB Gram price, and our conversation starts with a free trial lesson where the one-task test should be run.

sections.heading: What is available now and what has to wait
paragraphs: Disclosing this is unusual in this market and more useful than a reassurance. Subject-group criteria work in Mathematics, Sciences, Individuals and Societies and Language and Literature is reasonably covered and a match usually takes a few days. Language Acquisition is well covered. Design and Arts criteria work is thinner, because fewer tutors have marked a process folder.

Personal Project supervision is the thinnest request we take, and a September enquiry is filled on different terms from a February one, because the small number of people who have genuinely supervised projects are allocated by then. Interdisciplinary unit work is not something we match separately at all; it is handled inside a criteria block with somebody who knows the programme, which is the honest description rather than a limitation dressed up.

Diploma transition blocks are the best-covered thing on this page, because the skills are shared with examination systems and many tutors have taught them. That is worth knowing for an Emaar South family planning the summer before Year 12: it is both the highest-value purchase at the end of the programme and the easiest to arrange, which is an unusual combination.

Where nothing suitable is free we say so and give a date. What we do not do is put a general subject tutor in front of a student whose criterion B and D scores are low across every subject, because that produces a term of competent subject teaching and an unchanged report. Declining work is uncommon enough in this industry to be worth stating as a policy rather than as a sentiment.

process.title: Send the last report and one marked task
process.description: The report shows criterion-level scores across every subject, which makes the pattern visible in a way no examination system allows until results. The marked task, with the criteria the teacher applied, is what the one-task test needs. Those two documents are worth more than any description a parent can write.

process.title: Name the subjects, and therefore the subject groups
process.description: Criterion B means different things in Sciences, Individuals and Societies, Mathematics and Language and Literature, so a request for Middle Years help without the subjects named cannot be matched properly. Two subjects in the same group can often share a tutor; two in different groups usually should not.

process.title: Run the one-task test on the trial
process.description: Ask which criterion the task assessed and what the band above required. A real answer names the strand missed and quotes what the next band demands. A weak answer comments on the subject content and suggests more practice. Five minutes, no preparation, and most of the risk removed.

process.title: Ask the school for the Personal Project dates
process.description: The goal-setting window, the draft deadline and the submission date. They are school dates and differ by several weeks across this catchment, and the project competes for exactly the hours Diploma preparation would otherwise use. Knowing them in the autumn is what makes sequencing possible.

process.title: Buy the criteria block before anything else
process.description: Three or four sessions on what each criterion in each of the student's subject groups actually asks, read against their own work. It pays into every subject at once and most students have never been shown a descriptor, which is why it is both the cheapest and the most reliable purchase available here.

process.title: Book the Diploma transition block for the summer
process.description: Four to eight sessions on timed writing, note-taking from exposition, notation and producing without revision, including one full timed paper before Year 12 begins. It is the best-covered item on this page and the one that prevents a term of Year 12 being spent on a habit gap.

whyPoints.title: The test is published, including for us
whyPoints.description: Take a returned task and ask which criterion it assessed and what the band above required. A real answer names the strand missed and quotes the demand; a weak one comments on the subject. Handing a parent the test we expect to be judged by is a different kind of claim from an assurance about experience.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject group, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: Criterion B is inquiring and designing in Sciences, investigating in Individuals and Societies, investigating patterns in Mathematics and organising in Language and Literature. A tutor applying the wrong vocabulary gives confident advice that moves a mark the wrong way, so we ask which groups first.

whyPoints.title: Reports read by pattern rather than by subject
whyPoints.description: High criterion A with low B and D across every subject is one problem appearing in many places, and it is a descriptor problem rather than a content gap. Reading the report that way identifies the single shared weakness, which is what the criteria block then treats once.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project addressed at goal setting
whyPoints.description: A goal too broad to achieve, or achievable but not documentable, caps the mark before work begins, and the process journal cannot be convincingly reconstructed. Support in the autumn of the final year is worth several times the same support in the spring, which is when most families ask.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what a general subject tutor does well
whyPoints.description: Genuine content gaps, language acquisition, supervision and routine all respond to ordinary good teaching without criterion expertise. What does not is the characteristic failure of sound content and low process marks. Knowing which situation you are in is the point of the test.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims and no UAE centre
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE or IB approval, accreditation or partnership and operates no office or centre in the UAE. KHDA requires its own approval for school teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education, which is a school credential and not one we hold or claim.

faqs.question: Is it hard to find an IB MYP tutor near Emaar South?
faqs.answer: Finding a name is easy, because Middle Years students study subjects with ordinary names and there is no shortage of competent subject tutors. Finding somebody who can read a criterion descriptor against a marked task and say which band it sat in is hard. The programme grades work against four published criteria rather than grading subject knowledge directly, and that gap between knowing a subject and knowing its descriptors is where most tutoring money in this programme is wasted.

faqs.question: Why is criterion knowledge so rare among tutors?
faqs.answer: Because most Middle Years schools set no public examination, so there is no shared bank of past papers and official mark schemes around which a common language about marks could develop. In examination systems that culture forms over years as tutors and teachers handle the same material. Here, assessment is internal and task-based against descriptors published per subject group, so a tutor who has never worked inside an IB school has had no route to acquiring the vocabulary.

faqs.question: What single question tests a Middle Years tutor best?
faqs.answer: Hand them a returned marked task and ask which criterion it assessed and what the band above the one it received required. Somebody with real experience names the criterion, says which strand of the descriptor the work satisfied and which it did not, and quotes the kind of thing the next band demands, such as a conclusion that answers the task question rather than summarising. Somebody without it comments on the subject content and suggests more practice.

faqs.question: Does criterion B mean the same thing in every subject?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the commonest misunderstanding families bring. The labels A to D are constant and their content is set per subject group. In Sciences criterion B is inquiring and designing, which concerns method and variables. In Individuals and Societies it is investigating, which concerns a research question and documented process. In Mathematics it is investigating patterns. In Language and Literature it is organising. A report showing criterion B at 4 in two subjects is describing two different weaknesses.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but scores mid-band everywhere. What now?
faqs.answer: That is a descriptor problem, not a content problem, and reinforcing content will not touch it. The pattern to look for on the report is high criterion A with low B and D across every subject, which is one weakness appearing in many places: the student knows the material and does not show the process the criteria reward. Three or four sessions on what each criterion in their subject groups actually asks, read against their own marked tasks, pays into every subject at once.

faqs.question: When should we get help with the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: At goal setting, in the autumn of the final year, which is also when the people who have genuinely supervised projects are still available. Three failures all happen before any work is done: a goal too broad for the time, a goal achievable but not documentable, and criteria for success never stated at the outset. Each caps the mark in advance. A supervisor who has marked projects raises all three in the first conversation; one who has not will discuss the topic enthusiastically.

faqs.question: Where exactly does Personal Project help have to stop?
faqs.answer: At production. A tutor may discuss the goal, reject one that cannot be achieved or documented in the time, insist the process journal is kept as the work happens, explain the criteria and what the band above requires, and give feedback on the student's own draft report. Producing the project, writing any part of the report or constructing the journal is not permitted, because the project exists specifically to demonstrate the student's own independent work and the journal is itself assessed.

faqs.question: Are interdisciplinary units really assessed?
faqs.answer: Yes, on their own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting, and they are the component students most often treat as optional because no subject teacher owns them. Almost nobody in the tutoring market has marked one, so this is not a component to shop for separately; it is handled inside a criteria block with somebody who knows the programme. The synthesising criterion asks for a genuine connection between disciplines rather than two separate treatments stapled together.

faqs.question: When is a general subject tutor the right choice here?
faqs.answer: When there is a genuine content gap: a term missed through illness, or a topic never met after arriving from another system. Also for Language Acquisition, where drilled structures and vocabulary respond to ordinary good teaching, and for supervision, where a thirteen year old needs somebody to establish a routine rather than analyse descriptors. In an Emaar South household where the problem is that nothing gets done after a long journey, that is the honest purchase.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to Emaar South homes?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Students here are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the task brief, the published criteria and the student's own work open side by side on a shared screen. For this programme that arrangement suits the work particularly well, since most of a useful session is reading a descriptor against a piece of writing and two documents read better on a monitor.

faqs.question: Should Middle Years support cost the same as Diploma support?
faqs.answer: It should cost less and frequently does not, because the published bands do not distinguish by programme and no provider volunteers the distinction. Bestimate's monthly estimates put specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more, which is a Diploma figure, against AED 600-1,200 mid-market. A family paying an examination-year rate for a Year 8 student with a criterion problem is overpaying twice: for Diploma scarcity, and for a standing arrangement where three sessions would do.

faqs.question: What is the best first purchase for a Year 8 student here?
faqs.answer: Three or four sessions teaching the criteria explicitly, read against the student's own marked tasks, across whichever subject groups they take. It pays into every subject simultaneously, most students have never been shown a descriptor, and the gain is reliable precisely because the fix is structural rather than conceptual. It is also the cheapest thing on the list, and in Emaar South where the age profile is young it is the purchase most households should make and almost none do.

faqs.question: How long should a session be for a Middle Years student in Emaar South?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes generally works better than ninety, because the material is a single assessed task rather than a paper and concentration drops sooner at this age. With no school inside the community, households here get home between about 16:00 and 17:30 depending on destination and whether the journey was by bus or car, so the practical window is 17:00 to 18:30 and those slots fill first given the community's age profile.

faqs.question: Do MYP grades affect which Diploma subjects are available?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the consequence families discover latest. Schools use final Middle Years grades to decide which subjects a student may take at Higher Level, and sometimes whether Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is available at all, and that decision is made before anybody has sat a Diploma paper. A student aiming at a Higher Level science or at Analysis and Approaches should ask the school for its threshold in writing at the start of the final Middle Years year.

faqs.question: Is Arabic tutoring allowed to use a different syllabus?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider offering one is describing something that is not permitted. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so support in Arabic, Islamic Education or Social Studies works with the school's own prescribed material. KHDA also requires that school teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval, which is a school credential rather than one applying to private tutors.

faqs.question: What is the easiest thing to arrange at the end of the programme?
faqs.answer: The Diploma transition block, which is both the highest-value purchase at this stage and the best covered, because the skills are shared with examination systems and many tutors have taught them. Four to eight sessions across the summer before Year 12 on timed writing, note-taking from exposition, mathematical notation and producing without revision, including one full timed paper sat under conditions. In Emaar South the summer also removes the journey, so the hours genuinely exist.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-emaar-south.closingHeading: Bring one marked task and ask which criterion it was assessing
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-emaar-south.closingBody: An IB MYP tutor in Emaar South is easy to find and worth verifying, because the programme grades work against published criterion descriptors rather than against subject knowledge. Send the last report, one marked task with the criteria the teacher applied, and the subjects your child takes so we know the subject groups. Then run the one-task test on the free trial lesson. It needs no card, and if the answer is three sessions rather than a term we will say so. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are an India-only service.

intro.heading: Two routes through ages 14 to 16, inside one residential cluster
paragraphs: This corner of Dubai contains an unusual choice. Inside Emirates Hills and The Meadows sit IB continuum schools running the Primary Years Programme into the Middle Years Programme and on into the Diploma. One community away, inside Springs 3, sits a British-curriculum secondary running IGCSE at sixteen. Families move between The Springs, The Meadows, The Lakes and Emirates Hills without changing their children's friendships, and they compare these two routes constantly over coffee at the Springs Souk.

The comparison is worth doing properly, because the two systems do genuinely different things in MYP 4 and 5. IGCSE gives a fourteen-year-old a terminal examination at sixteen, a syllabus with a published code, and a grade that universities and sixth forms recognise instantly. MYP gives the same child criterion-based assessment across eight subject groups, interdisciplinary work, a Personal Project, and a report in which each subject carries a grade from 1 to 7 derived from criterion bands rather than from an exam mark.

Neither is better in the abstract, and this page will not pretend otherwise. What matters is that they produce different kinds of sixteen-year-old. An IGCSE student has sat papers under timed conditions and knows what an examiner rewards. An MYP student has planned and executed independent work, has been assessed against descriptors, and can usually write at length. Each arrives at post-16 with a strength the other lacks, and that is the real content of the comparison.

What the two routes share is where tutoring helps. In both systems the thing that moves a grade at fourteen to sixteen is not more content. It is the ability to read what the assessment asks for and produce it: a command term on an IGCSE paper, a criterion descriptor in MYP. A student who understands the material and cannot see the difference between a band 5 and a band 7 response is losing marks to a translation problem, and translation problems are teachable. That is why the recommendation does not change by route or by community.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time to fit the school run in Emirates Hills, The Meadows and The Springs. IB Gram does not run a UAE office and does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service offered only in India. Everything below is the MYP: how the criteria and bands work, why a strong report can hide a weak exam skill, the Personal Project, eAssessment, the transition into the Diploma, and what this costs in Dubai. Where a figure belongs to a named source, the source is given so that you can check it rather than take it on trust, and where a fact could not be verified against an official page it has been left out of this page entirely.
