dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-emirates-hills.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme sits in the middle of a longer arc, and a tutoring decision at MYP 4 is really a decision about what happens at sixteen and eighteen. These are the four stages as the schools in this cluster run them.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, assessed against published criteria rather than by a single examination. Most subject groups use four criteria marked in bands out of eight, giving thirty-two marks that convert to a grade from 1 to 7. Interdisciplinary units, approaches to learning, global contexts and service as action run alongside the subject content and are assessed in their own right.
programmes.countryNote: The IB continuum schools serving Emirates Hills and The Meadows run MYP directly into the Diploma, which means the MYP 5 subject grades are the main evidence a school uses when advising on Higher and Standard Level choices. That makes MYP 4 a more consequential year than most families treat it as.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The years before MYP, built around transdisciplinary inquiry rather than subject silos. Children arriving into MYP 1 from PYP are generally confident at asking questions and presenting findings, and less practised at the formal written forms that MYP criteria begin to require from MYP 3 onwards.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving into this cluster from a British or Indian primary often meet PYP reporting for the first time and find it hard to read. One session translating a PYP report into what the child can and cannot yet do is usually more useful than a term of tutoring bought on the strength of a worry.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The assessment model changes substantially: external examinations return, internal assessments carry fixed percentages, and the criterion bands of MYP are replaced by mark schemes and command terms. The transition is felt most in the first term of DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places in the emirate. For families in this cluster that widens the post-16 choice without requiring a move, which makes the MYP 5 decision less final than it used to feel.

programmes.name: The IGCSE alternative at ages 14 to 16
programmes.description: The route taken by students at the British-curriculum secondary inside Springs 3 and at the campuses along Al Sufouh. Eight to ten linear courses with published syllabus codes, examined terminally, with Cambridge splitting most subjects into Core and Extended tiers. It produces a student practised at timed papers and at reading a command term.
programmes.countryNote: UK-curriculum schools account for 37 per cent of private enrolment in Dubai, so the IGCSE route is the default rather than the alternative across the emirate as a whole. Inside this particular residential cluster the two routes are unusually evenly matched, which is why the comparison comes up so often.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-emirates-hills.subjectsIntro: MYP assessment is criterion-based, and the criteria differ by subject group. These are the eight groups with the criteria a report card is actually reporting against, which is the vocabulary a parent needs in order to read it.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where most marks are lost, because it asks a student to generalise and then justify the generalisation rather than to find an answer.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Inquiring and designing is the best single predictor of how a student will handle the Diploma's scientific investigation two years later.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criteria: analysing, organizing, producing text, and using language. Students frequently score well on producing text and poorly on analysing, because they write fluently about what a text says rather than about how it achieves its effect.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Assessed on comprehension of spoken and visual text, comprehension of written and visual text, communicating in response, and using language. Phase placement rather than year group determines the expectation, which surprises parents whose child is strong in the subject and placed in an earlier phase.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the band that separates students, and it requires evaluating sources and perspectives rather than reporting them accurately.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The design cycle is assessed as a process, so a brilliant finished product with a thin research and testing record scores less than a modest product documented properly.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. Process journals carry real weight here, and students who treat them as an afterthought lose marks that the final piece cannot recover.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Written reflection is assessed alongside physical performance, which is a frequent surprise to both students and parents.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: Marked out of 24 across three criteria: planning, applying skills, and reflecting. It is the closest thing MYP has to the Diploma's independent work, and it is the task on which students most often ask for outside help too late in the year.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed in their own right on disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. Students who are strong in individual subjects can still score poorly here, because the work asks them to combine two subject lenses rather than to apply either one well.

sections.heading: MYP in Emirates Hills, IGCSE one gate away: the comparison parents actually make
paragraphs: Ask a parent in The Lakes what they are weighing and it is rarely a tutor. It is whether to keep a thirteen-year-old in the IB continuum school they have attended since PYP, or to move them to the British-curriculum secondary a few minutes away so that they come out at sixteen with IGCSE grades. The children in question often already know each other. This is a genuinely close call in this cluster in a way it is not in most of Dubai.

The honest case for IGCSE at fourteen to sixteen is legibility and exam practice. The syllabus is published with a code, the content is finite, the grade is produced by a terminal examination, and the student spends two years learning what a command term requires and what a mark scheme rewards. A sixteen-year-old with IGCSE grades can be assessed by any sixth form or university in the world without explanation, and they have sat real papers under real timing.

The honest case for MYP is breadth and independence. Eight subject groups rather than a narrowing set of options, interdisciplinary work, approaches to learning taught explicitly, service as action, and a Personal Project that asks a fifteen-year-old to plan and complete something substantial on their own. Students come out able to write at length, used to being assessed against descriptors, and considerably more comfortable with open-ended tasks than their IGCSE contemporaries.

What the comparison table below sets out is that the strengths are mirror images, and so are the weaknesses. The IGCSE student arrives at post-16 with examination technique and sometimes without independence. The MYP student arrives with independence and sometimes without examination technique. Whichever route your family chooses, the tutoring that helps at fourteen to sixteen is the same in shape: it teaches the student to read what the assessment is asking for and produce exactly that. Only the vocabulary changes, from command terms to criterion descriptors.

sections.heading: How MYP marking actually works, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The single most common MYP conversation is a parent holding a report and not knowing whether a 5 is good. The answer requires understanding the structure, which is not complicated once set out. Each subject group is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D. Each criterion is marked in bands out of eight against published descriptors. The four criterion marks add to a maximum of thirty-two, and the total converts to a subject grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries.

The crucial point is that the criteria are different in every subject group. In mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In language and literature they are analysing, organizing, producing text, and using language. A parent who knows only that their child scored 5 in criterion B knows nothing until they know which subject it was.

This is also where the most useful tutoring happens, and it is specific rather than general. A student sitting at band 5 in science criterion C, processing and evaluating, is not failing to understand science. They are producing graphs and conclusions that meet the band 5 descriptor and not the band 7 one, and the difference between those two descriptors is written down and can be read. A session spent reading the descriptor against the student's own work, then rewriting one paragraph to meet the higher band, teaches more than a term of content revision.

Confirm the detail with your child's school, which holds the current subject-group guides and the boundaries it applies. Criteria and descriptors are revised, schools receive the authoritative versions, and no tutoring page should be the last word on how your child's work is being marked.

sections.heading: Why a comfortable MYP report can hide a weak examination skill
paragraphs: This is the thing families in this cluster most often discover a year too late. A student can carry a respectable set of MYP grades into DP1 and struggle immediately, not because the content is harder but because the assessment has changed shape. MYP tasks are frequently completed over several lessons, with a task sheet in front of the student, with the criteria visible, and sometimes with a redraft. Diploma examinations are none of those things.

The gap is specific and it has three parts. The first is timing: writing a good answer in thirty-five minutes with no task sheet is a skill, and it is not practised by a student whose assessments have mostly been extended tasks. The second is command terms, which do the job that criterion descriptors do in MYP but in a single word, compressed into the question. The third is the mark scheme, which rewards particular content in a particular form rather than describing a quality of work in a band.

None of this is an argument against MYP. The student who arrives in DP1 from MYP typically writes more fluently, plans independent work better and is far less rattled by an open-ended question than a student arriving from a purely examined system. The point is narrower: the one thing MYP does not reliably build is examination technique, and it is the one thing the Diploma assesses heavily. A term of timed written work in MYP 5, or over the summer before DP1, closes it.

Schools that opt into MYP eAssessment reduce the gap considerably, because their MYP 5 students sit on-screen examinations and build ePortfolios under conditions. Whether your child's school does this is worth asking directly, because it changes what the bridge year needs to contain. Families who assume eAssessment is universal are sometimes surprised at the first DP1 mock.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: three criteria, 24 marks, and a year that disappears
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the most demanding single piece of work in MYP and the one students most consistently underestimate. It is marked out of twenty-four across three criteria: planning, applying skills, and reflecting. There is a product or outcome, a process journal kept throughout, and a report. The grade comes from the process as much as from the result, which is precisely the part fifteen-year-olds find counter-intuitive.

The commonest failure is a goal that is too large, chosen in the first fortnight out of enthusiasm and never narrowed. Everything downstream inherits it. A student who set out to build something ambitious has no time left for the journal, so the evidence of applying skills is thin, and the reflection becomes an account of running out of time rather than an analysis of what was learned. The second commonest failure is a journal written retrospectively in the final week, which an experienced supervisor can spot immediately.

So the useful intervention is early and it is about scope. Narrow the goal until it is achievable with a term to spare. Define what the product actually is, in a sentence, before any work starts. Set up the journal as a working record with dates rather than as a document to be produced later. Decide in advance what evidence will demonstrate each criterion. None of that requires subject expertise; it requires somebody asking harder questions than a busy supervisor has time for.

The boundary is firm and it matters more here than almost anywhere in MYP. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a goal is achievable, point out that a journal entry contains no evidence, and give feedback on the student's own draft report. A tutor must never write, complete or produce the project, the product or the report. Work submitted to the IB has to be the student's own, and a Personal Project that is not is a malpractice matter for the student, not for the person who helped.

sections.heading: MYP eAssessment and the IB MYP Certificate
paragraphs: A question that comes up repeatedly in this cluster is whether MYP produces a certificate the way IGCSE produces grades. The answer depends on the school. The IB offers eAssessment at the end of MYP 5, consisting of on-screen examinations in a set of subjects together with ePortfolios in others and the Personal Project, leading to the IB MYP Certificate. Schools choose whether to register their students, and a substantial number do not.

The practical consequences of that choice are worth understanding before MYP 4. A school that offers eAssessment gives its students an externally validated outcome at sixteen and, just as importantly, the experience of sitting an examination under conditions. A school that does not offer it reports MYP grades internally, which are perfectly meaningful to the Diploma school upstairs and require more explanation to anybody outside the IB system.

If your family might move, or might send a child to a non-IB sixth form, this is a question to ask the school directly rather than infer. The same applies in reverse: a family weighing the IB continuum school in Emirates Hills against the British secondary in Springs 3 should ask the former whether it registers for eAssessment, because the answer narrows or widens the gap in the comparison table above more than any other single factor.

What a tutor can do here is narrow. If the school does sit eAssessment, preparation looks much more like conventional examination preparation: on-screen practice, timing, and the discipline of producing a complete answer in a fixed window. If it does not, the same work is still worth doing in MYP 5 as preparation for the Diploma, because that is where the examination skill becomes consequential. Either way the content is identical; only the deadline changes.

sections.heading: The MYP to DP transition, subject by subject
paragraphs: The move from MYP 5 into DP1 is the transition this cluster asks about most, and it is uneven across subjects. In mathematics the jump is real and it is about pace: the Diploma courses, whether Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, cover ground faster than MYP and assume algebraic fluency that criterion A did not always demand. Students who were comfortable at MYP 5 and find DP1 maths hard are usually meeting speed rather than difficulty.

In the sciences the change is in the written demand. MYP criterion C, processing and evaluating, is genuine preparation for the Diploma's scientific investigation, which is the good news. The less good news is that Diploma papers ask for extended explanation under timing, and MYP science assessment rarely does. A student who has done criterion B and C work seriously is well placed for the internal assessment and underprepared for the papers.

In language and literature the transition is the smoothest of all, because MYP's analysing criterion is the same intellectual act the Diploma demands. The main adjustment is length and timing. In individuals and societies the critical-thinking criterion maps closely onto Diploma expectations, and students who scored well in criterion D generally transfer without difficulty. Language acquisition depends heavily on which phase the student reached, and phase rather than year group is the thing to ask about.

The subject-choice conversation deserves to happen while it is still open, which in practice means the spring of MYP 5. A student's MYP criterion profile is a better guide to Higher Level suitability than their overall grade: strong criterion A with weak criterion B in sciences points somewhere different from the reverse. That is a conversation to have with the school first, with a tutor's read as a second opinion rather than the other way round.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs here, and why acting early is the cheaper decision
paragraphs: MYP sits in an awkward place in a family budget. There is no public examination at the end of it in most schools, so the urgency that loosens a wallet in Year 11 or DP2 is absent. The result is a predictable pattern: nothing is bought during MYP 4 and 5, and a considerably larger amount is bought in DP1 when the same weakness becomes expensive. The arithmetic argues for the opposite order.

A single weekly session during MYP 4, working on criterion descriptors in the weakest subject group, costs what one weekly session costs. On published Dubai market estimates, a qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, which Bestimate's tables put at around AED 600 to 1,200 a month for one session a week. Budget online tutoring is advertised from about AED 45 to 150 an hour, estimated at AED 240 to 600 a month on the same basis.

Compare that to the DP2 version of the same problem. An IB specialist working with an examination-year candidate is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above by Bestimate, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED publishing AED 650 at the premium end; two sessions a week in DP2 lands at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and more per month, and the weeks available are fixed. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour, with monthly in-home packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against an online package advertised at AED 799. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so that band is market context only.

Two notes on reading any of these numbers. They are market rates published by named providers and read in October 2026, not a price list, so ask for a current quote. And none of it is a statistic about outcomes: no page here publishes a claim about grades, because such a claim without a sample size and a method tells a parent nothing. For context on the wider cost picture, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: The Dubai layer: mandatory subjects, the regulator and the permit
paragraphs: An MYP timetable in Dubai is fuller than an MYP timetable elsewhere, and this is the main local fact a tutoring plan has to respect. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory lesson is shorter than 25 minutes.

The organisation of those lessons is specified too. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. For these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which constrains how any tutoring material for them can be described.

On the regulator more broadly: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and its published inspection reports are free to read and far more informative than any marketing page about a school. Abu Dhabi families fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority. No tutoring provider should describe itself as approved by any of them; a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises, and IB Gram does not hold one or claim to.

Finally, the permit position for individual tutors, which parents are entitled to ask about. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, any figure quoted to you should be treated with suspicion.

process.title: Send one criterion-marked task
process.description: The most useful thing you can share is a single piece of work the school has marked against criteria, with the band awarded. That document tells a tutor more than a full report card, because it shows the gap between what your child wrote and what the descriptor asked for.

process.title: A free first lesson spent on the descriptor
process.description: The matched tutor reads the task, the band awarded and the descriptor for the band above, then works with your child on rewriting one section to reach it. You see the method rather than hear about it, and decide afterwards whether to continue.

process.title: One criterion at a time, named in writing
process.description: The plan says which subject group, which criterion and which descriptor is being targeted over the next six weeks. Naming the criterion is what makes progress visible on the next report rather than being a matter of impression.

process.title: Weekly sessions with band-marked work
process.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on a held Gulf Standard Time slot, with a task set between them that the tutor marks against the band descriptors rather than as a percentage. A percentage tells an MYP student nothing they can act on.

process.title: Personal Project scope checked early
process.description: If your child is in MYP 5, the first substantive session tests whether the project goal is achievable with a term to spare and whether the journal is a working record. Both problems are only fixable at the start.

process.title: A transition review before DP choices close
process.description: In the spring of MYP 5 the criterion profile is read against Higher and Standard Level options, as a second opinion to the school's advice. Timed written practice is built into the bridge term regardless of which route follows.

whyPoints.title: Taught against descriptors, not percentages
whyPoints.description: MYP work is marked in bands against published descriptors, so feedback expressed as a percentage is unusable. Sessions work from the descriptor for the band above and close the specific distance to it.

whyPoints.title: The right criteria for the right subject group
whyPoints.description: Criterion B means investigating patterns in mathematics and inquiring and designing in sciences. A tutor who knows which criteria apply where can act on a report that a generalist can only sympathise with.

whyPoints.title: Project help at the scope stage
whyPoints.description: Personal Projects fail on goals that were never narrowed and journals written retrospectively. Both are fixable in the first three weeks and almost impossible to fix in the last three.

whyPoints.title: Examination technique built deliberately
whyPoints.description: MYP does not reliably produce timed-paper skill unless the school opts into eAssessment. Whichever route follows, timed written work in MYP 5 is the single most useful preparation available.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on whose work it is
whyPoints.description: A tutor explains criteria, questions a goal and responds to the student's own draft. They do not write any part of a Personal Project or any assessed task. The student carries the consequence, so the line is not negotiable.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly up front
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There is no UAE office and no tutor is sent to a UAE address; home visits are an India-only service. Coverage limits are disclosed before you book.

faqs.question: Should my child stay in MYP or move to the IGCSE school one community away?
faqs.answer: Both routes work and they produce different sixteen-year-olds. IGCSE gives a published syllabus, a terminal examination and extensive timed-paper practice, which is immediately legible to any sixth form. MYP gives eight subject groups maintained to sixteen, interdisciplinary work, approaches to learning taught explicitly and a Personal Project that builds genuine independence. The practical questions to ask are whether the IB school registers for MYP eAssessment, which narrows the examination-practice gap, and where your child is likely to go at sixteen. Tutoring helps the same way on either route, because both reward reading the assessment accurately.

faqs.question: What does a 5 mean on an MYP report card?
faqs.answer: It is a subject grade from 1 to 7, derived from four criterion marks rather than from an examination. Each criterion is marked in bands out of eight against published descriptors, giving a maximum of thirty-two marks per subject, which converts to the 1-7 grade through boundaries the school applies. A 5 therefore tells you the total was in a particular band; it does not tell you which criterion is weak. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown, because a student at 7 in criterion A and 3 in criterion B needs something very different from one who is even across all four.

faqs.question: Which four criteria does MYP mathematics use?
faqs.answer: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where most marks go missing, because it asks a student to find a general rule and then justify it, which is a different act from solving a problem correctly. Communicating is the second common loss: a student who reaches the right answer with no visible reasoning, no notation and no explanation of method scores well in one criterion and poorly in another. Both are teachable, and both respond to work on the descriptor rather than to more practice questions.

faqs.question: Why do MYP science criteria matter for the Diploma two years later?
faqs.answer: Because criterion B, inquiring and designing, and criterion C, processing and evaluating, are the same skills the Diploma's scientific investigation is marked on. A student who has had those criteria marked rigorously arrives in DP1 able to control variables, state uncertainty and justify a conclusion from data. A student whose school marked them generously arrives unable to do any of that, and discovers it when a fifth of their science grade depends on it. Asking to see criterion B and C marked work is one of the most informative things a parent of an MYP 4 student can do.

faqs.question: How many marks is the MYP Personal Project worth, and across which criteria?
faqs.answer: Out of twenty-four, across three criteria worth eight marks each: planning, applying skills, and reflecting. There is a product or outcome, a process journal kept throughout, and a report. The grade comes substantially from the process rather than from how impressive the product looks, which students find counter-intuitive. Planning is where the project is usually lost, because a goal chosen out of enthusiasm in the first fortnight is rarely narrowed afterwards. Reflecting is the second loss: the top band wants analysis of what was learned, not a description of what went well.

faqs.question: When should a MYP 5 student start the Personal Project properly?
faqs.answer: At the beginning, and the first three weeks are the ones that matter most. Narrow the goal until it is achievable with a term to spare. Define the product in one sentence before any work begins. Set up the process journal as a dated working record rather than as a document to be produced later. Decide in advance what evidence will demonstrate each of the three criteria. A project that has done those four things in September is almost impossible to fail; one that has done none of them is very hard to rescue in March whatever help is bought.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without crossing an IB line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that is firm. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a goal is achievable, point out that a journal entry contains no usable evidence, and give feedback on your child's own draft report. A tutor must never write, complete or produce the project, the product or the report, and must not edit the writing until it stops being your child's. Work submitted to the IB has to be the student's own. The student is the person who carries a malpractice finding, which is why the line sits where it does.

faqs.question: Does MYP give my child a certificate at sixteen?
faqs.answer: Only if the school registers for eAssessment. The IB offers on-screen examinations and ePortfolios at the end of MYP 5, together with the Personal Project, leading to the IB MYP Certificate, and schools choose whether to participate. Many do not, reporting MYP grades internally instead, which is perfectly meaningful to a Diploma school and needs more explanation outside the IB system. Ask your school directly rather than assuming either way, because the answer affects both the comparison with IGCSE and what a bridge year into DP1 needs to contain.

faqs.question: Why did my child go from strong MYP grades to struggling in DP1?
faqs.answer: Usually because the assessment changed shape rather than because the content got harder. MYP tasks are often completed across several lessons with the task sheet and criteria visible, sometimes with a redraft. Diploma examinations allow none of that. The gap has three parts: writing a complete answer under timing, reading command terms that compress into one word what a descriptor spells out, and producing what a mark scheme rewards rather than a quality of work. A term of timed written practice in MYP 5 or over the summer closes most of it.

faqs.question: How does MYP language acquisition phase placement work?
faqs.answer: Placement is by phase rather than by year group, so a capable student may sit in an earlier phase than their age peers and a new arrival may be placed ahead of them. The criteria assess comprehension of spoken and visual text, comprehension of written and visual text, communicating in response, and using language. Parents are frequently puzzled by a strong child in a low phase; the phase describes the language stage, not the ability. Ask the school which phase your child is in and what moving up would require, because that is the actionable question.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough for an MYP 4 student?
faqs.answer: For nearly all cases, yes, and it is the right place to start. One weekly hour spent on the weakest criterion in one subject group, working from the school's own task sheets and the published descriptors, is enough to change a band over a term. More than that rarely helps at MYP level, because the limiting factor is how much criterion-marked work the student produces and absorbs rather than how much teaching they receive. The exception is MYP 5 with a Personal Project running alongside, where a short second block is often worth it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to a villa in Emirates Hills or The Meadows?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists in India only, and there is no UAE office or centre. For MYP work this matters less than parents expect: the core activity is reading a descriptor against a piece of the student's own writing and rewriting a section, which works at least as well on a shared screen, and the annotated version can be kept for the next task rather than left on a table.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai family budget for MYP support?
faqs.answer: Published market figures rather than our prices. Bestimate's Dubai tables put one weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, with the hourly band at AED 150 to 300. Budget online tutoring is advertised from about AED 45 to 150 an hour, estimated at AED 240 to 600 a month for one session a week. The argument for spending during MYP rather than waiting is arithmetic: the same weakness addressed in DP2 needs an examination-year specialist, quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with fewer weeks available.

faqs.question: How do the Dubai mandatory subjects affect an MYP timetable?
faqs.answer: They fill it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates instructional time for them on a 40-minute lesson unit, advising that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in several of these subjects, with combined classes strictly prohibited. The effect on a tutoring plan is simple: an MYP week in Dubai has fewer spare hours than the equivalent elsewhere, so one well-targeted session beats three optimistic ones.

faqs.question: What if no tutor covers my child's MYP subject group at our hour?
faqs.answer: You are told before anything is booked. Mathematics, sciences, language and literature, and individuals and societies at evening Gulf Standard Time slots are reasonably well covered. The requests that cannot always be met are specific arts, design or language acquisition phases at an awkward hour. In that case you are offered the nearest available specialist and a slot that genuinely exists, or an honest no with a suggestion of what would help instead. No competing provider in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is why it appears here.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-emirates-hills.closingHeading: Bring one marked task, not the whole report
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-emirates-hills.closingBody: The most useful thing in a first conversation about MYP is a single piece of work the school has marked against a criterion, with the band written on it. From that, a tutor can show your child the descriptor for the band above and work with them on closing the distance, which is what actually changes a report. Whether your family is inside the IB continuum school or weighing the IGCSE route one community away, the method is the same. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time for students in Emirates Hills, The Meadows, The Springs, The Lakes, The Greens and The Views.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-green-community.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover MYP subject groups for students in Green Community, Dubai Investments Park and The Sustainable City, from MYP 1 through the Personal Project year and into the transition that follows it.

intro.heading: The MYP has five years and they are not interchangeable
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme has no external examinations for most students, which makes all five years feel the same from outside. They are not. Each one has a job, and tutoring that ignores which year a student is in tends to do the right work at the wrong time, which in a programme this long is an expensive mistake to repeat.

MYP 1 to 3 are for fluency and habits. There are no certificates attached and no external deadlines, which is precisely why gaps form unnoticed: arithmetic that stays slow, reading stamina that never builds, writing that is never produced to a clock. None of it is examined, so none of it is flagged, and all of it surfaces later as something that looks like a subject weakness.

MYP 4 is for evidence. It is the last year in which a criterion profile can be read, acted on and changed before the decisions start. A student whose communication or inquiry criteria are low across several subjects has a transferable problem, and MYP 4 is when a term of work on it still has two years to pay off rather than two months.

MYP 5 is for the Personal Project and for a decision. The project has its own criteria and a school-set deadline, and the decision - IB Diploma, Career-related Programme, or a move to an IGCSE and A Level route - is usually taken on predicted grades partway through the year, before the project is even finished. Both of those have dates, and neither waits for a family to feel ready.

Green Community makes the sequence easy to picture because everything else here is close. The community sits inside Dubai Investments Park, low-rise and walkable, with schools within a short drive, and two of the schools serving it run an IB continuum from the Primary Years Programme through to the Diploma. A child here may spend fourteen years inside IB assessment language, and the five MYP years sit in the middle of that.

There is one more calendar feature worth naming before the detail, because it recurs five times rather than once. Ramadan shortens school hours and reorganises the household evening around iftar, and it moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so across five MYP years a family meets it in five different positions. For an MYP 5 student it can land uncomfortably close to the Personal Project deadline. The long summer break, by contrast, is the only stretch in the whole programme with nothing competing for it, which makes it the natural window for the fluency work the early years need and for the transition work the last year needs.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What follows: the five years with what each is for, the Personal Project counted backwards, when criterion data actually arrives and how to use it, when the post-MYP decision closes, and how Ramadan and the UAE school year change the plan.

programmes.name: MYP 1 to 3: the fluency years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four lettered criteria out of eight, taught through inquiry organised around global contexts and key concepts, with interdisciplinary units linking subjects. No external examinations and no certificates, so the entire record is a sequence of criterion judgements.
programmes.countryNote: For families in Green Community and Dubai Investments Park this is the cheapest window in the whole school career and the one least used. Arithmetic fluency, reading stamina and writing produced against a clock all cost a term here and cost a year if left until MYP 5.

programmes.name: MYP 4: the evidence year
programmes.description: Subject choices begin to narrow and the criterion profile becomes genuinely informative, because there is enough of it to show a pattern. Still no external papers for most students, so the pressure remains invisible while the usefulness of the data peaks.
programmes.countryNote: This is the year to find out whether a low criterion is a subject gap or an approaches-to-learning problem repeating across subjects. Acted on in MYP 4, a skills problem has two years to pay off. Discovered in the second Diploma year, it costs marks while being fixed.

programmes.name: MYP 5: the project and the decision
programmes.description: The Personal Project is completed, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight, with a product or outcome, a process journal and a report. Some schools also enter students for optional on-screen eAssessments and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Two dates dominate this year and neither is the end of it. The Personal Project deadline is school-set and lands well before the summer. The post-MYP decision is taken on predicted grades partway through the year, which means it is made before the project has demonstrated anything.

programmes.name: The transition out
programmes.description: The IB Diploma with six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, or an IGCSE and A Level route at a UK-curriculum school nearby. Both make assumptions about what an MYP student arrives able to do.
programmes.countryNote: Both routes are available within a short drive of Green Community, so this is a genuine choice. The gap to close before either is narrow and specific: writing against a clock, formal mathematical notation at speed, and recall at volume, none of which the MYP requires.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-green-community.subjectsIntro: The eight subject groups, each noted with the MYP year in which its characteristic difficulty usually appears. The year is the organising idea on this page, so the notes follow it.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowledge and understanding, investigating patterns, communication, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The investigating criterion starts biting around MYP 3, when a general rule has to be found, justified and tested rather than an answer reached.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowledge and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The design criterion becomes the limiting factor in MYP 4, where a method another person could replicate is expected.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Paraphrase instead of analysis appears as early as MYP 2 and is cheapest to correct then, because it is the same habit that later limits Diploma Paper 1.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover comprehending spoken and written text, communicating, and using language, organised by phase rather than year group. Phase placement should be reviewed in MYP 1 and again in MYP 3, because a misplaced phase reads as a weakness.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. Source summary instead of source evaluation shows from MYP 3 onward and is the criterion that most often caps an otherwise strong profile.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating, with the design folder assessed directly. Under-documenting starts in MYP 2 and becomes expensive by MYP 5, when the Personal Project rewards the same habit.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding, with the process journal assessed. Students who work hard and record nothing lose marks the work itself earned, from the first year onward.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The planning and reflecting criteria are written work, which surprises families expecting a wholly practical subject.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Criteria cover planning, applying skills and reflecting, each out of eight, with the process journal as the evidence base for all three. A journal reconstructed near the deadline cannot evidence a process that was not recorded as it happened.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Communication, social, self-management, research and thinking skills, taught across subjects rather than in one timetabled slot. A criterion profile low in the same way across several subjects is nearly always one of these.

sections.heading: The five MYP years and what each one is actually for
paragraphs: Without external examinations, the MYP presents as a long undifferentiated stretch, and families treat all five years as the same opportunity. Separating them changes what tutoring is worth buying and when.

MYP 1 to 3 are the fluency years, and their defining feature is that nothing in them is examined externally. That is both the opportunity and the trap. A student can progress with reasonable criterion scores while arithmetic stays slow, while reading stamina never builds past a few pages, and while no piece of writing is ever produced under time pressure. None of those appear on a report, and all of them are assumed by everything that follows.

MYP 4 is the evidence year. By then there is enough criterion data to show a pattern rather than a snapshot, and the pattern is the useful part: whether low marks cluster in one subject, which is a content problem, or in one criterion type across several subjects, which is a skills problem wearing several costumes. Acting on that in MYP 4 leaves two years for it to pay off.

MYP 5 is the year of the Personal Project and the post-MYP decision, and it is busier than families expect because both land before the end of it. The project has a school-set deadline well short of the summer, and the decision about what comes next is taken on predicted grades partway through the year. A family that starts thinking about either in the spring term of MYP 5 has missed both.

sections.heading: The Personal Project counted backwards from its deadline
paragraphs: The Personal Project is assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight, with a product or outcome, a process journal and a report. All three criteria draw their evidence from the process, which means the journal is not administration; it is the assessed material.

Counted backwards, the project has four stages and the first is the one that decides the mark. The goal has to be narrowed until it is achievable with the time and resources available and until progress on it can actually be evidenced. A goal that is too large produces either an unfinished product or a quietly downgraded one, and in both cases the reflecting criterion suffers because the student ends up defending a decision rather than evaluating a process.

The second stage is the journal, kept weekly from the start. This is where most marks are lost in this catchment and the loss is entirely avoidable. A journal written in the fortnight before the deadline reads smoothly and cannot evidence what the criteria reward: decisions taken, obstacles met, approaches changed, skills acquired. A rough weekly entry recording what was tried and what failed outperforms an elegant retrospective account every time.

The third is the product or outcome itself, and the fourth is the report, which should be written against the criteria rather than as a narrative. The boundary throughout is firm: a tutor may challenge the goal, explain what each criterion rewards, teach a skill the project needs, show the student how to keep a usable journal, and read the draft report against the descriptors. A tutor may not plan it, make it, write it or edit it to completion.

sections.heading: When criterion data arrives, and how to use it that term
paragraphs: Criterion marks arrive at reporting points set by the school, and the useful question is not what they say but what can still be done with them in the time before the next ones. That is the practical difference between reading a report in MYP 2 and reading the same report in MYP 5.

The first move is always the same and takes twenty minutes. Find the criterion that scored lowest, in that subject, and read the published descriptor for the band above. The descriptor states specifically what the work would have to do differently - justify a general rule rather than state it, write a method a stranger could follow, evaluate sources against one another rather than summarise them in turn. Ask the school for the descriptors rather than for a clearer comment, because the descriptor is the specification.

The second move is to look across subjects rather than down one. Four subjects with low communication marks is one problem; two subjects with low knowledge marks is two problems. The MYP's own approaches-to-learning framework names the skill categories - communication, social, self-management, research and thinking - and a pattern repeating across subjects is almost always one of those rather than several subject gaps.

The third is to match the response to the remaining time. In MYP 2 or 3 a skills pattern can be addressed slowly, inside ordinary subject work, and it will compound. In MYP 5, with the Personal Project live and a decision approaching, the same pattern needs a short targeted block, because there is no longer room for slow compounding. The diagnosis is identical and the prescription is not.

sections.heading: eAssessment, where a school uses it, and what it changes
paragraphs: Some schools enter MYP 5 students for optional on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate, and some do not. Which applies is a school decision rather than a student one, and it changes the shape of MYP 5 considerably, so it is worth asking directly rather than assuming.

Where a school does enter candidates, the year acquires an external examination date it would not otherwise have, and the preparation for it is largely timed on-screen writing. That is a genuinely new demand for a student who has spent five years producing coursework against criteria, and it is also the single most useful possible preparation for whatever comes next, because both the Diploma and an A Level route assume writing to a clock from the first term.

Where a school does not enter candidates, MYP 5 ends without any external result, which has a practical consequence families should know: the student arrives at the post-MYP route with criterion grades and a Personal Project and no subject certificates. That is normal and it is accepted by IB continuum schools, and it matters when a family is considering a move to a UK-curriculum sixth form that is used to reading IGCSE results.

Either way the question to ask the school is specific: does it enter students for eAssessments, for which subjects, and when do the components fall? The answer determines whether MYP 5 contains an examination window or only an internal calendar, and that is the difference between two quite different term plans.

sections.heading: When the post-MYP decision actually closes
paragraphs: Families expect the Diploma or A Level decision to be made at the end of MYP 5, with results or predictions in hand. In practice it is made partway through the year, on predicted grades and criterion profiles, because schools need to build timetables and sixth forms need to issue offers. By the time the Personal Project is submitted the decision has usually been taken.

That timing has two consequences. The first is that the evidence used is the criterion profile from MYP 4 and the first part of MYP 5, which is one more reason to take MYP 4 seriously as the evidence year. The second is that any work intended to change the available options - lifting a subject profile, demonstrating readiness for a Higher Level science - has to happen before that point rather than after it.

The profile is also genuinely informative about which route suits. A student scoring well on inquiry, communication and reflection criteria is usually well placed for the Diploma, where internally assessed components and the Extended Essay reward exactly those. A student strong on knowledge criteria and weaker on the others may do better taking three or four A Levels in depth. Both routes exist within a short drive of Green Community, so this is a real choice rather than a constraint imposed by geography.

Whichever route is chosen, the gap to close is the same and it is narrow. The MYP does not require writing against a clock, formal mathematical notation at speed, or recall at volume, and both destinations assume all three from the first term. A term of timed writing, daily manipulation by hand and deliberate retrieval practice in MYP 5 removes most of the first-term shock, which is otherwise read as a capability problem rather than a preparation one.

sections.heading: Ramadan and the UAE school year across five MYP years
paragraphs: Every plan written for a UAE family has to survive Ramadan, and across five MYP years it will be encountered five times in five different positions, because Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar. It currently falls inside the spring term, which for an MYP 5 student can sit awkwardly close to the Personal Project deadline.

School hours shorten and households reorganise their evening around iftar, so a late-afternoon slot becomes either an early-afternoon or a post-iftar one for the month. For MYP students the thing worth protecting is the writing habit rather than the content pace: a shorter session that still produces one piece of written work holds more than a longer discussion that produces none.

The long summer break is the opportunity the MYP calendar offers and almost nobody takes. It is the only stretch with no competing demands, which makes it the natural window for fluency work in MYP 1 to 3 and for transition preparation between MYP 5 and the Diploma. A student who spends part of one summer writing to a clock arrives at the Diploma with the main gap already closed.

Because nobody is travelling to your address, all of this is a diary exercise. Moving a slot from 5pm to 2pm for a month is a change two calendars absorb. Asking an in-home tutor to shift their commute by three hours for a month is a request they may be unable to accommodate, and that asymmetry matters more over five years than over one term.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs, and what is worth buying at each stage
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures, read October 2026 and attributed. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 online. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independent home tutors advertising to AED 500. Specialists are published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650.

The MYP is the stage where the entry band deserves a fairer hearing than it gets. For MYP 1 to 3, where the work is often arithmetic fluency, reading stamina or simply sitting down to produce something, a capable and patient tutor at the lower end can be genuinely good value. The expensive specialist adds less here than they will in three years.

What changes the calculation is criteria literacy, and it changes it sharply from MYP 4 onward. A tutor who has never read an MYP descriptor will teach content, and content is frequently not what the report is pointing at. For a criterion profile review, for the Personal Project and for transition preparation, the work is interpretive rather than instructional, and the specialist band is where those people are.

Plan it by MYP year rather than by hour, because the staging argument above has a price attached. Dubai rate guidance converts one weekly hour into roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Across a nine-month school year that budget band is AED 2,160-5,400 and the specialist band is AED 9,000-18,000 or more. So a family that buys the entry band through MYP 1 to 3 and moves up to the specialist band for MYP 4 and 5 pays substantially less over five years than one that commits to either tier for the whole run, and gets the better tutor at the point the descriptors start deciding the report. Advertised packages give a third reference point: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. None of these are IB Gram prices; our fee is quoted after the free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one across the MYP years, honestly
paragraphs: The format suits MYP work from about MYP 3 onward without qualification, because so much of the work is document work: a criterion descriptor beside a piece of the student's own writing, a process journal read together, a method rewritten so a stranger could follow it. A shared screen where both people annotate is better for that than a single paper copy across a table.

For MYP 1 and 2 the honest answer depends on the child rather than on the format. An eleven or twelve-year-old who will settle at a desk and engage with a screen does fine. One who needs an adult physically present to begin and to stay started does better with someone in the room, and no amount of good teaching compensates for that. We would rather say so than take the booking.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, stated near the top of this page rather than left to be discovered, because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote. If your MYP 1 child needs a person in the room, hire locally and ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first lesson.

The other practical limits apply across all five years: a weak connection shortens the hour whatever the clock says, and a shared study space, more common in the apartment blocks here than in the villas, undermines any lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room. Both are worth testing in the first fortnight rather than discovering in the second term.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and how to start from the right year
paragraphs: Worth knowing before the first MYP session, and there is a detail inside it that surprises parents at this stage. The private tuition work permit arrived under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and the UAE government states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Look closely at who may hold one: registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18 - which means an MYP 5 pupil in Green Community is old enough to be licensed to tutor. That is the clearest demonstration available that the permit certifies lawfulness rather than criteria literacy, and it is why the rest of this page spends its time on descriptors instead. Tutoring without the permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule. And whatever the permit says, never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher.

On the Personal Project and every assessed MYP task, the boundary is the same as anywhere in the IB and worth stating for a fifteen-year-old's first substantial independent piece. A tutor may challenge the goal, explain what each criterion rewards, teach a skill the work needs, discuss how to keep a usable journal and read a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not plan, make, write or edit any part of it. Every word submitted must be the student's own.

What we do not claim: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, a KHDA Educational Services Permit being issued to training institutes with physical premises that we neither hold nor occupy. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE or IB accreditation or partnership, publish no self-asserted rating, promise no grade or criterion improvement, and quote no statistic without its source and date.

To start, tell us the MYP year first, then the subject group, the school, and send the most recent criterion report with one piece of the student's marked work. The year tells us what the available time can achieve; the report tells us which criterion is low; the work tells us why. A specialist then teaches a free one-to-one trial lesson online built on that work and writes up what the descriptor and the work together showed. The note is yours whether or not you continue.

faqs.question: Which MYP year is the best time to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: MYP 1 to 3 for fluency and MYP 4 for evidence, and almost all families start later than either. The early years are the only part of the programme with no external deadline, which makes them cheap, and the things that go unbuilt there - arithmetic speed, reading stamina, writing produced to a clock - are assumed by everything that follows. MYP 4 is the last year a criterion profile can be read and acted on with two years left for it to pay off rather than two months.

faqs.question: When does my child's Personal Project actually need to be finished?
faqs.answer: The deadline is set by the school rather than by the IB, and it lands well before the end of MYP 5, because the school needs time before submission. Working backwards, the goal should be narrowed in the first weeks of the year and the journal begun in the same week, because all three criteria - planning, applying skills and reflecting - draw their evidence from the process. Ask the coordinator for the internal deadline in writing at the start of the year rather than looking for it in the spring.

faqs.question: Why does the Personal Project journal matter more than the product?
faqs.answer: Because the criteria assess the process and the journal is the only evidence of it. Planning, applying skills and reflecting all ask what the student decided, what obstacles appeared and what approach changed, and a journal written in the fortnight before the deadline cannot supply any of that: it reads smoothly and records nothing. A rough weekly entry naming what was tried and what failed outperforms an elegant retrospective account, and it takes a few minutes a week to keep.

faqs.question: When is the Diploma or A Level decision taken in MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Partway through the year, on predicted grades and the criterion profile, because schools build timetables and sixth forms issue offers before any MYP 5 work is complete. By the time the Personal Project is submitted the decision has usually been made. That means the evidence used is the MYP 4 profile plus early MYP 5 work, and any effort intended to widen the options - lifting a subject profile, demonstrating readiness for a Higher Level science - has to happen before that point.

faqs.question: Does my child's school enter students for MYP eAssessments?
faqs.answer: That is a school decision rather than a student one, and it changes the shape of MYP 5 considerably, so ask directly. Some schools enter MYP 5 students for optional on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate and some do not. Where a school does, the year acquires an external examination window and the preparation is largely timed on-screen writing, which is also the best possible preparation for whatever follows. Ask for which subjects and when the components fall.

faqs.question: How do I use a criterion report in MYP 2 differently from MYP 5?
faqs.answer: The diagnosis is the same and the prescription is not. In MYP 2 or 3 a skills pattern - low communication or inquiry marks across several subjects - can be addressed slowly inside ordinary subject work, and it compounds over the remaining years. In MYP 5, with the Personal Project live and the route decision approaching, the same pattern needs a short targeted block, because there is no longer room for slow compounding. Read the descriptor for the band above in either case; just match the response to the time left.

faqs.question: What is the transition gap between the MYP and the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Narrow and specific. The MYP builds inquiry, independent work, extended purposeful writing and comfort with criteria-based assessment, all of which pay in the Diploma's internally assessed components and the Extended Essay. What it does not require is writing against a clock, formal mathematical notation at speed, or recall at volume, and both the Diploma and an A Level route assume all three from the first term. A term of timed writing, daily manipulation by hand and retrieval practice closes most of it.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring suitable for an MYP 1 student in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: It depends on the child, and we would rather say so than take every booking. From about MYP 3 onward the format works without qualification, because the work is document work: a descriptor beside a piece of writing, a journal read together. For MYP 1 and 2, a child who will settle at a desk and engage with a screen does well, while one who needs an adult physically present to begin and stay started does better in person. IB Gram runs no home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without doing it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful help is mostly questioning rather than teaching. A tutor can challenge whether the goal is achievable with the time and resources available, explain what each criterion rewards, teach a specific skill the project needs, show the student how to keep a journal that will actually evidence their process, and read the draft report against the descriptors. A tutor cannot plan it, make it, write it or edit it to completion. Every word of the report must be typed by the student.

faqs.question: Should we use the summer break for MYP work?
faqs.answer: It is the opportunity the MYP calendar offers and almost nobody takes. The long summer is the only stretch with no competing demands, which makes it the natural window for two things: fluency work between MYP 1 and 3, where arithmetic speed and reading stamina are cheap to build, and transition preparation between MYP 5 and the Diploma, where a few weeks of writing to a clock and manipulation by hand removes most of the first-term shock that is otherwise read as a capability problem.

faqs.question: How many MYP subjects should we tutor at once?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and sometimes none in the sense parents expect. If the criterion profile shows one subject genuinely low on knowledge criteria, that is one subject tutor. If the same criterion type is low across several subjects, the right purchase is a skills block rather than several subject tutors, and it improves all of them at once. Starting with three MYP subject tutors is the most common overspend we see from this catchment, and the criterion report usually shows why it was unnecessary.

faqs.question: What happens to MYP sessions during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: The hour moves and the shape changes. School hours shorten and households reorganise their evening around iftar, so a weekday 5pm slot typically becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. For MYP students the thing to protect is the writing habit rather than the content pace: a shorter session that still produces one piece of written work holds more than a longer discussion that produces none. Because nobody is travelling to your address, moving the slot is a diary change rather than a negotiation.

faqs.question: Why are MYP-literate tutors hard to find near Green Community?
faqs.answer: Because IB continuum provision here is concentrated in a few schools. KHDA reported the International Baccalaureate at 7% of Dubai private enrolment across 227 private schools and 17 curricula, and this catchment is not where that minority concentrates, so the surrounding tutoring market grew up around UK and Indian curricula. The practical effect is that a local search returns tutors who know the subject and have never read an MYP descriptor, and the descriptor is where the actual diagnosis lives.

faqs.question: Does the MYP leave my child without any certificates at 16?
faqs.answer: Unless the school enters candidates for optional eAssessments, yes, and that is normal rather than a problem. An MYP 5 student arrives at the next stage with criterion grades and a Personal Project rather than subject certificates, which IB continuum schools read fluently. It matters more if a family is considering a move to a UK-curriculum sixth form accustomed to reading IGCSE results, so ask the receiving school what evidence it wants and when, well before the decision point partway through MYP 5.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here work in the Middle Years Programme specifically, by subject group and by criterion, rather than treating MYP as junior Diploma. Each works from the descriptors the student's own school publishes in its assessment policy.

intro.heading: Why the neighbourhood matters less for MYP than for almost anything else
paragraphs: Families in Hor Al Anz comparing tutoring options usually start by comparing places. Is there more choice in Deira? Does Al Qusais have better coverage? Would moving the search to Al Garhoud, where more of the international schools sit, turn up a stronger shortlist? Those are reasonable questions and for some subjects they have real answers. For the Middle Years Programme they mostly do not, and it is worth understanding why before spending a fortnight on the comparison.

The first reason is cohort size. MYP is carried by a small slice of the Dubai private sector; International Baccalaureate students make up roughly seven per cent of the emirate's private school population against thirty-seven per cent on UK curricula and twenty-six per cent on Indian ones. In the older northern districts that slice is thinner still, because the schools closest to Hor Al Anz lean British and Indian. The pool of locally resident tutors who genuinely know MYP assessment in any single district is therefore small no matter which district you pick.

The second reason is what MYP tutoring actually requires. There is no external paper for most of the programme, no past-paper archive to drill, and no mark scheme in the IGCSE sense. Marks come from four criteria per subject, each scored out of eight against published descriptors, and the gap between a 5 and a 7 is usually a gap in how the student addresses the descriptor rather than in what they know. A tutor who has read those descriptors and marked against them is useful. A strong graduate in the subject who has not is often not.

The third reason is scheduling. MYP students are younger than Diploma students, their homework load is lumpy around unit deadlines rather than steady, and the useful session often needs to happen the evening before a task is due. A tutor who has to drive from one district to another cannot absorb that kind of last-minute shift. A tutor on video can.

Put those together and the honest answer to the comparison question is that Hor Al Anz, Al Muteena, Deira and Al Qusais are the same market for MYP, and the variable that actually changes outcomes is whether the tutor understands criterion-based assessment. That is a selection question, not a geography question. The rest of this page is about how to answer it, and what the programme asks of a student in each subject group.

One more thing is worth saying plainly before the detail. A parent comparing districts is usually trying to answer a different question underneath: am I paying for something I cannot judge? MYP makes that worse than most programmes, because there is no percentage to check and no past paper to compare against. The antidote is to insist on the criterion language in every conversation. Ask the tutor which criterion the session targeted, which band the work sat in before and after, and what the descriptor for the next band requires. A tutor who can answer those three questions every week is accountable in a way a district search can never make them, and a tutor who cannot is expensive at any hourly rate.
