programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups studied concurrently, each assessed against four criteria out of eight. Criteria names differ by group: Sciences uses knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Language and Literature uses analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. The criteria are the assessment, so they are also the curriculum for tutoring purposes.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, MYP schools are inspected by KHDA on the same six-band scale as every other private school, and they must also deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the IB framework. That means a Hor Al Anz MYP student carries mandatory UAE subjects on top of eight subject groups, which compresses the week more than the programme outline suggests.

programmes.name: MYP 5 and the Personal Project
programmes.description: The year that decides what MYP looks like on paper. Students carry out the Personal Project, an extended independent piece assessed on its own criteria, alongside final subject assessment. Schools that enter candidates for MYP eAssessment produce an IB-validated certificate; schools that do not award school-based MYP grades instead. The two routes feel similar in class and look different on an application.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families moving between schools mid-MYP sometimes cross between an eAssessment school and a school-based one without being told. It changes nothing about teaching and quite a lot about what the final record says, so it is worth asking the school directly which route it uses before MYP 5 begins.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most common destination for an MYP 5 student in Dubai. The jump is real: DP is examined externally, graded 1 to 7 per subject on papers rather than criteria, and adds Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Students who excelled at MYP criteria work sometimes stumble in DP term one purely on timed written examination technique, which MYP never asked them to develop.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating around sixteen thousand eight hundred new places across the sector. For an MYP 3 or 4 student in the Deira belt that widens the DP options available by the time they reach Year 12, including schools currently full.

programmes.name: The IGCSE alternative at 16
programmes.description: The other thing a Dubai student of this age might be doing, and the comparison most Hor Al Anz parents are implicitly making. IGCSE is externally examined with public past papers, tiered in several subjects, and produces a subject-by-subject certificate at 16. MYP produces criterion-referenced grades and, on the eAssessment route, an IB certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Many schools near Hor Al Anz run IGCSE rather than MYP, which is why a family here often has one child on each. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 or better are required, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. MYP alone is not an equivalency route; the Diploma that follows it is the qualification that matters.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.subjectsIntro: These are the MYP subject groups Hor Al Anz families most often ask about, described by what the criteria reward rather than by syllabus content, because in MYP the criteria are what is marked.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion A rewards accurate knowledge and understanding; Criterion B asks the student to investigate a pattern and justify a general rule; Criterion C is communication, where working and notation carry marks; Criterion D applies mathematics to a real-life context. Most lost marks sit in B and D, where students produce an answer without the justification the descriptor demands.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Inquiring and designing is the criterion that separates grades: a testable question, a hypothesis with scientific reasoning, named independent, dependent and controlled variables, and a method someone else could follow. Processing and evaluating wants real error discussion, not a sentence saying the experiment went well.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing asks for interpretation supported by specific textual evidence; organising marks structure and register; producing text marks creative and critical choices; using language marks accuracy and range. Students who write fluently but never quote precisely stall at a 5 and cannot see why.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Phase placement, not year group, decides what is expected. A student placed in Phase 3 is assessed against Phase 3 descriptors across listening, reading, speaking and writing, so a parent comparing two children's grades is often comparing two different standards entirely.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigating rewards a focused research question and a documented process; the thinking critically criterion rewards weighing evidence and recognising different perspectives. Narrative answers that retell events score in the middle band however well written.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Assessed almost entirely on the design cycle: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The finished artefact matters less than the documented reasoning, which surprises students who put their effort into the build and their last hour into the folder.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: The process journal carries real marks. Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding are all evidenced through documented development rather than through the final performance or piece alone.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Planning for performance and reflecting and improving performance are written criteria, and they are where students who are strong athletes lose grades. The evidence is the written plan and the reflection, not the sport.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal as the evidence base. The commonest failure is a product completed well and a journal assembled in a weekend, which caps the grade regardless of how good the product is.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed with their own criteria on disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. Students treat them as a double homework and lose marks for not making the connection between subjects explicit, which is the entire point of the unit.

sections.heading: Hor Al Anz against the next district over: what actually differs for an MYP family
paragraphs: Set Hor Al Anz beside Al Muteena, Deira, Al Qusais and Al Garhoud and compare the things that genuinely vary. School stock varies: Al Garhoud carries more IB provision than the northern districts, which lean British and Indian. Commute varies: a student at a school inside the Deira grid is home by mid-afternoon, a student bussed to Oud Metha often is not. Housing stock varies, which changes whether a student has a quiet room for a video session or shares a table with siblings.

What does not vary in any useful way is the supply of tutors who understand MYP assessment. IB students are a minority of the Dubai private sector, the northern districts carry less of that minority than Dubai Hills or the Marina corridor, and MYP specifically is a narrower specialism than IB Diploma teaching. A family that spends three weeks widening its search from Hor Al Anz to Deira to Al Qusais has widened the radius without widening the pool in any meaningful way.

The comparison that does pay is between tutors, not districts. Ask a candidate which criteria the subject uses and what the top band of Criterion B actually says. A tutor who answers from the descriptors is useful at any distance. A tutor who talks about the subject in general terms will produce a student who understands more and scores the same, which is the specific failure mode MYP tutoring is prone to.

That is why the answer comes out the same in every district in this cluster: choose on criterion fluency and on the ability to take a session the evening before a deadline, and accept that the tutor will not be local. Once the lesson is on video the geography stops being a variable at all, which is a better outcome for a Hor Al Anz family than it first sounds.

sections.heading: How MYP marking works, and why a 5 and a 7 can look identical to a parent
paragraphs: MYP does not produce percentages. Each subject group is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, and the four marks are combined into a total out of thirty-two which the school converts to a 1 to 7 grade using published boundaries. The consequence is that a student can know the subject well and still sit at a 5, because one criterion is dragging the total down while the others are strong.

That is almost invisible on a report card. A parent reads a 5 in Sciences and assumes a general weakness. The underlying marks might be seven for knowing and understanding, seven for processing and evaluating, six for reflecting, and three for inquiring and designing, because the student never writes a properly controlled method. The fix there is narrow and fast, and it is a completely different intervention from more science teaching.

So the first thing a useful MYP tutor asks for is the criterion breakdown, not the grade. Most Dubai schools publish it on the reporting portal, strand by strand. With that in hand the tutoring plan writes itself: find the lowest criterion, read the descriptor for the band above, and work on exactly the behaviour the descriptor names.

This is also why MYP tutoring resists the format that works for IGCSE. There is no large public archive of past papers to drill through. The raw material is the student's own task, the school's descriptors, and the gap between them. A tutor who cannot work that way has to invent generic exercises, and generic exercises do not move criterion marks.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the honest limit of what a tutor can do
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the visible landmark of MYP 5 and the piece of work families most often want help with. It is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, and the evidence is the process journal as much as the product. Students routinely build something good and document it badly, which caps the grade in a way that feels unfair and is entirely predictable.

What a tutor can do here is coach the process. That means helping the student set a goal that is specific enough to be assessed, planning backwards from the school's internal deadlines, keeping the journal honest and contemporaneous rather than reconstructed, and reading the criteria descriptors together so the student knows what evidence each band expects. It also means asking hard questions at the halfway point, which is when most projects quietly stall.

What a tutor must not do is produce any part of the work. Not write the journal, not draft the report, not make the product, not edit the writing to completion. The project has to be the student's own, and a tutor who crosses that line has created an academic-honesty problem for the student that no grade is worth. This is a real distinction in this market: some operations selling IB support in the Gulf advertise finished assessed work outright, and families should ask any provider directly what it will and will not produce.

The practical version of the boundary is easy to apply. If the tutor is typing, something has gone wrong. If the tutor is asking what evidence the student has for a claim in the journal and the student is doing the typing, the session is doing its job.

sections.heading: What MYP does not teach, and why that shows up in Year 12
paragraphs: MYP builds a set of genuinely useful habits: inquiry, documented process, reflection, making connections between subjects. It does not build timed written examination technique, because almost nothing in the programme is a timed written examination. Students arriving in the IB Diploma or in an A Level course from a strong MYP background frequently have a difficult first term for that reason alone.

The specific gaps are consistent. Writing to a clock, where a good answer unfinished scores less than an adequate answer completed. Command-term discipline, where state, explain, evaluate and discuss carry different mark expectations and MYP descriptors do not drill that distinction. Recall under pressure, because MYP tasks are usually open-resource. And answering the question asked rather than the question the student prepared for, which coursework rewards and examinations punish.

None of that is an argument against MYP. It is an argument for spending part of MYP 5 on the transition rather than only on the current year's grades. A block of timed writing under examination conditions in the final MYP terms costs a handful of sessions and removes most of the first-term DP shock. Families in Hor Al Anz whose children are heading to a DP school in Al Garhoud or further south are the ones who benefit most, because the school change and the assessment change land in the same September.

The same logic applies in reverse for a student leaving MYP for IGCSE at the end of Year 9, which happens often in this part of Dubai because so many nearby schools are IGCSE centres. That student needs past papers, mark schemes and tier awareness quickly, and the switch in how work is judged is larger than the switch in content.

sections.heading: eAssessment or school-based: two MYP 5 routes that look the same in class
paragraphs: Not every MYP school ends the programme the same way. Some enter candidates for MYP eAssessment, which produces an IB-validated certificate based on on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios. Others award school-based MYP grades against the same criteria without external validation. Day to day the teaching is similar; the record at the end is not.

For most Dubai families this matters only at the edges, because the Diploma that follows is the qualification universities read. It matters more for a family likely to move country or school at 16, where an externally validated certificate travels better than a school report does. It also matters for a student who wants evidence of achievement at 16 and will not have an IGCSE certificate to show.

The question is worth asking the school early rather than discovering the answer in MYP 5. A school's assessment policy states the route, and the admissions office will say plainly if asked. In the Deira belt, where several families move children between an MYP school and an IGCSE school at the end of Year 9, knowing which route the current school uses changes the calculation about whether to move at all.

For tutoring purposes the route changes the final term rather than the programme. An eAssessment cohort needs on-screen examination practice and ePortfolio curation to a deadline. A school-based cohort needs the same criterion work it has needed all along, carried through to the final tasks. Either way the preparation is the student's own work, coached rather than produced.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs in Dubai, and why the cheapest tier rarely fits
paragraphs: Published Dubai tutoring rates split into bands that are worth reading before shortlisting anyone. The lowest band is genuinely cheap: EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. That band is mostly university students and group-adjacent delivery. The next band up, qualified subject tutors working online, is where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. Specialist work runs higher: TutorChase lists around AED 270, Bestimate's specialist band is AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED charges AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. These are the providers' own published figures.

MYP is the case where the cheapest band fits worst, and the reason is structural rather than snobbish. A budget tutor can usually teach the content of MYP Mathematics or Sciences perfectly well, because the content is not advanced. What that tutor often cannot do is mark a student's work against four published criteria and explain why a response sits in the fourth band rather than the sixth. Without that, the student learns more and the grade does not move, which is the outcome families complain about most.

Monthly figures are the more useful frame for a parent budgeting. Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages circulating in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Worth adding for context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the following academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family already paying Dubai school fees, a flat fee year is the window in which a tutoring line becomes affordable, and it is a reasonable moment to commit to a weekly slot rather than ad hoc crisis sessions.

sections.heading: Online delivery, in-home tutoring and what IB Gram actually sells in the UAE
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real Dubai market with published rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to 300 for comparably qualified tutors working online. Families choose it for reasons that make sense: a younger child who concentrates better with someone in the room, a parent who wants to overhear the session, a household where screen time is already contested.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time. Stating that on the page is more useful than letting a family find out after a booking.

For MYP the online argument is unusually strong. The material a session works on is the student's own digital task, the school's descriptors and the reporting portal, all of which live on a screen anyway. Sharing and annotating a Design folder or a Sciences lab report over video is easier than passing a laptop across a table. And because MYP deadlines arrive in bursts, a session that can be moved to Thursday evening because a task is due Friday is worth more than a fixed Tuesday that cannot shift.

There is one honest caveat. A twelve-year-old working alone at a screen needs more structure than a sixteen-year-old does, which is why early MYP sessions run shorter, with clearer written follow-ups and an expectation that a parent sees the session notes. That is a design choice rather than a limitation of the format, and it is how the younger end of the programme is handled.

sections.heading: The UAE subjects and the Ramadan term that shape an MYP week
paragraphs: An MYP student in Dubai carries more than eight subject groups. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in every Dubai private school whatever international curriculum it is licensed for, with its requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those subjects occupy real timetable hours, and they come with rules about how they are organised: schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are strictly prohibited.

Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and schools may vary lesson length so long as the weekly total is met, with KHDA advising that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can reasonably ask the school about.

The scheduling consequence for tutoring is simple: the week is fuller than the MYP subject list suggests, so a plan that assumes several free evenings will fail. One well-used weekly session plus bookable clinics around deadlines is a more realistic shape than three fixed sessions a student cannot sustain.

Ramadan compresses the school day and moves family routines, and in the older northern districts that usually means sessions shift to after Iftar or to the weekend for the month. Because delivery is online, that shift costs nothing but a calendar change. Students in MYP 5 with a Personal Project deadline in the spring term should plan the Ramadan weeks explicitly rather than hope to absorb them, because the journal is the part that suffers first.

process.title: Send the criterion breakdown, not the grade
process.description: Most Dubai schools publish MYP marks strand by strand on the reporting portal. A screenshot of that breakdown for the weakest subject tells a tutor more than a term's worth of general conversation, because it names which of the four criteria is dragging the total.

process.title: Free trial lesson on the student's own task
process.description: The trial works on a real piece of the student's work with the school's descriptors open, and ends with the tutor naming the criterion to target and what the band above actually asks for. No payment is taken before this happens.

process.title: Pick a weekly slot that survives the school run
process.description: Students bussed from Hor Al Anz to Al Garhoud or Oud Metha often are not home before five, so the slot is set from the real arrival time rather than the timetable. Ramadan and mock weeks move the slot rather than cancelling the habit.

process.title: Add clinics around unit deadlines
process.description: MYP workload arrives in bursts. Alongside the weekly session, a short bookable clinic in the days before a Design folder, an investigation or a Personal Project checkpoint is where most of the grade movement happens, because it addresses the task being marked.

process.title: Review against descriptors every few weeks
process.description: Progress is checked by re-reading the criterion descriptors and asking which band the student's latest work sits in and why. That is a harder conversation than asking whether they feel more confident, and it is the one that predicts the next report.

whyPoints.title: Descriptors open, every session
whyPoints.description: MYP is marked against published criteria, so that is the material a session works from. A tutor paraphrasing the criteria from memory is guessing at the thing being assessed, and the student's grade reflects the guess.

whyPoints.title: The lowest criterion first
whyPoints.description: One weak criterion out of four caps an otherwise strong profile. Finding it and working the specific behaviour the next band describes moves a grade faster than broad subject revision does, and it is cheaper in sessions.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project coached, never written
whyPoints.description: We help a student plan, keep an honest journal and read the criteria. We do not draft, edit to completion or produce any part of the work. The project is the student's and the honesty rules exist to keep it that way.

whyPoints.title: Transition planned in MYP 5
whyPoints.description: MYP does not train timed written examinations, and DP and IGCSE are built on them. A short block of timed writing before the programme ends removes most of the first-term shock at the next school.

whyPoints.title: No district premium, because there is no district
whyPoints.description: Lessons run live over video on Gulf Standard Time, so the tutor is chosen on MYP experience rather than on willingness to drive to Hor Al Anz. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted as the market, not as a boast
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a published market rate attributed to the provider or study that published it. We do not publish statistics about our own outcomes, and we claim no KHDA, IB or Cambridge accreditation, because we hold none.

faqs.question: Does it matter that an MYP tutor is not based in Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: For the Middle Years Programme, no. IB students are a minority of the Dubai private sector, the northern districts carry less of that minority than the newer communities, and MYP assessment experience is a narrower specialism than IB Diploma teaching. Widening a search from Hor Al Anz to Deira or Al Qusais adds radius without adding specialists. What changes outcomes is whether the tutor can mark against four published criteria and explain the band above. That is a selection question rather than a geography question, and online delivery removes the distance variable entirely.

faqs.question: How is an MYP grade out of 7 actually calculated?
faqs.answer: Each subject group is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, giving a total out of thirty-two. The school converts that total to a 1 to 7 grade using published boundaries. There is no percentage. The practical consequence is that one weak criterion can hold down an otherwise strong profile, so a student sitting at a 5 may be scoring sevens in three criteria and a three in the fourth. Ask the school for the strand-by-strand breakdown rather than the single grade; it is usually on the reporting portal and it tells you where to work.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria in MYP Sciences?
faqs.answer: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Each is marked out of eight. Inquiring and designing is where most Dubai students lose ground, because the descriptors want a testable question, a hypothesis with scientific reasoning, named independent, dependent and controlled variables, and a method another person could follow. Processing and evaluating wants genuine discussion of error and reliability rather than a sentence saying the experiment worked. Those two criteria are narrow enough to fix in a handful of focused sessions.

faqs.question: Where does a tutor's help with the Personal Project have to stop?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes. A tutor can help set a goal specific enough to be assessed, plan backwards from the school's deadlines, keep the process journal contemporaneous, read the criteria descriptors with the student and ask hard questions at the halfway point where projects usually stall. A tutor cannot write the journal, draft the report, make the product or edit the work to completion. If the tutor is typing, the session has gone wrong. Some operations in this market sell completed assessed work; that is a malpractice risk carried by the student.

faqs.question: Is MYP harder or easier than IGCSE at the same age?
faqs.answer: They are differently difficult, which is why direct comparison frustrates parents. IGCSE is externally examined with public past papers, tiering in several subjects and a clear mark scheme, so preparation is concrete and the ceiling is visible. MYP is criterion-referenced with no external paper for most of the programme, which rewards sustained process work and documented thinking. Strong writers and organised students often do better in MYP; students who perform under timed pressure often do better in IGCSE. Neither is a softer option, and the difference matters most when choosing a school at the end of Year 9.

faqs.question: Will my child struggle moving from MYP into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Usually in one specific way. MYP builds inquiry, documented process and reflection, and it does not build timed written examination technique because almost nothing in the programme is a timed written examination. The gaps that show in DP term one are writing to a clock, command-term discipline, recall without open resources, and answering the question asked rather than the one prepared for. A short block of timed writing under examination conditions during the final MYP terms absorbs most of that, and it is far cheaper than firefighting in Year 12.

faqs.question: What is MYP eAssessment and does my child need it?
faqs.answer: It is the externally validated route at the end of MYP 5, based on on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios, and it produces an IB certificate. Schools that do not use it award school-based MYP grades against the same criteria. Day to day the teaching is similar. The route matters most for a family likely to move country or school at sixteen, where external validation travels better than a school report, and for a student who will not hold an IGCSE certificate as evidence at that age. Ask the school's assessment policy which route it uses.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to pay for MYP tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market bands put budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist work runs AED 200 to 450 and above. Monthly, Bestimate estimates roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band for a weekly hour. For MYP, the cheapest band usually teaches content well and cannot mark criteria, which is the gap that matters.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups do families in the Deira area ask about most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and Sciences lead, mostly because of Criterion B in both: investigating a pattern and justifying a general rule in Mathematics, and designing a controlled investigation in Sciences. Language and Literature is next, where students write fluently but never quote precisely and stall in the middle band. Design comes up around folder deadlines, since the documented design cycle carries more marks than the finished artefact. Individuals and Societies appears when a student is retelling events instead of weighing evidence, which the thinking critically criterion does not reward.

faqs.question: Do MYP students in Dubai also have to study Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with its requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. The scheduling effect is that an MYP week is fuller than the eight subject groups imply.

faqs.question: What time of day do sessions usually run for students in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: It follows the school rather than the postcode. Students at schools inside the Deira grid are often home by mid-afternoon and can take a four o'clock slot. Students bussed to Al Garhoud, Oud Metha or Bur Dubai frequently arrive back nearer five, which pushes a realistic start to six. Families commuting across the Sharjah boundary through Al Nahda prefer later evenings or weekends. Because lessons are online, the slot moves for a mock week or shifts to after Iftar during Ramadan without anyone losing a journey.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. For MYP this suits the work: the task, the descriptors and the reporting portal are already on a screen, so sharing and annotating a lab report or a Design folder over video is easier than passing a laptop around a table. The published in-home band in Dubai is AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to 300 online.

faqs.question: My child is twelve and in MYP 2. Is online tutoring suitable at that age?
faqs.answer: It works, with adjustments. Younger students need shorter sessions, clearer written follow-ups and an expectation that a parent reads the session notes, because a twelve-year-old working alone at a screen drifts faster than a sixteen-year-old does. Sessions at that age run tighter, with one concrete task rather than open-ended discussion, and the tutor sets something short and specific for the week. Families who want to be in earshot usually have the student work in a shared room, which is straightforward with a laptop and headphones.

faqs.question: Does MYP count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: MYP by itself is not an equivalency route; the qualification that matters is what the student holds at eighteen. On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade no lower than E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. The Ministry has not published an IB points threshold that we can source, so we do not state one. Verify your own case with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority; we describe the process rather than perform it.

faqs.question: How quickly can an MYP grade actually move?
faqs.answer: It depends which criterion is weak. A criterion that fails on a documented behaviour, naming controlled variables, structuring a method, quoting evidence precisely, can move within two or three assessed tasks because the student is not learning new content, only changing what they put on the page. A criterion that fails on knowledge and understanding takes longer, because the content has to be taught. Honest answers here come after one marked task, not before. Nobody can promise a grade, and a provider offering one is telling you something about its standards.

faqs.question: What if no MYP specialist is free for our subject and time slot?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of filling the slot with whoever is available. MYP specialisms are narrow, and an unusual combination, a particular subject group at a particular hour on a particular evening, does occasionally come up empty. The options then are a different time, a different tutor with a proper handover, or a wait with a date attached to it. A mismatched tutor in a criterion-based programme costs a term, because the student keeps producing work the tutor cannot mark against the descriptors.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.closingHeading: Bring the criterion breakdown and the next task
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.closingBody: If you are weighing an IB MYP tutor in Hor Al Anz against a search in Deira, Al Muteena or Al Qusais, the comparison will keep returning the same answer, because MYP specialists are thin on the ground in every northern district and the format that fixes that is video. The useful first step is to open the school portal, screenshot the criterion breakdown for the subject that worries you, and send it with the next task sheet. The trial lesson works on that task with the descriptors open and ends with a named criterion to target. No payment is taken before it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not offer home visits in the UAE.

intro.heading: The cheapest stage to buy tutoring, and the easiest to overspend on
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme is the point in a child's education where tutoring costs least and is most often bought in the largest possible quantity. The reason is the report. There are no percentages, the grades run 1 to 8, and a parent with no reference points reads a 4 and panics into an open weekly arrangement across three subjects, which at the qualified band of AED 150 to 300 an hour is a substantial monthly commitment for work nobody can evaluate afterwards.

What the report is not telling you is where the actual problem sits. Each MYP subject is assessed against four published criteria, each marked out of eight, and the four marks convert to the single grade. A science profile of 7, 7, 3, 2 and a flat profile of fives can produce similar grades while describing entirely different children. The first needs investigation design and data evaluation; the second needs something else; and neither needs three subjects tutored generally.

So the first action is free and it is not a purchase. Ask the school for the criterion-level breakdown rather than the report. Most schools hold it, many will share it when asked directly, and with four criterion marks in hand a tutor can say within one session what a term of work should contain. That conversation routinely turns a three-subject arrangement into a single term aimed at one criterion.

The second thing worth knowing is that the budget band genuinely works at this stage, which is not true at Diploma Higher Level. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For Middle Years content support that band contains usable help. What it less often contains is criterion literacy, which is the narrower and more valuable skill here.

International City adds its own arithmetic. There is no international school inside the district, so MYP students travel to Al Warqa, Al Qusais, Silicon Oasis or Mirdif and come back late. Published in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 online, and from these clusters that premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour buys a long journey rather than a better-informed tutor.

IB Gram delivers this online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are an India-only service for us. What follows sets out which Middle Years purchases earn their money, what each band buys at this stage, and the one purchase almost nobody makes that is worth more than all the others. Every figure is attributed to the provider who published it and dated, because three of the six leading pages in this market publish no price at all.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-international-city.programmesIntro: Three stages within the programme, with the spending question answered differently at each.

programmes.name: MYP years 1 to 3
programmes.description: Criteria applied more gently and reports hardest for parents to read. The two things worth paying for are number fluency to automatic recall and structured writing, because the programme does not systematically drill either and both become expensive to fix later.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where the lowest market band is entirely adequate, because the work is skill-building rather than criterion interpretation. A term of weekly sessions on one named skill at AED 45 to 150 an hour is a modest commitment, and it is the right shape: short, specific and finite rather than open-ended.

programmes.name: MYP years 4 and 5
programmes.description: Criteria applied at full strength, the Personal Project running alongside, and in many schools a split of mathematics into standard and extended routes. This is where criterion literacy starts to matter and where the qualified band begins to earn its difference over the budget one.
programmes.countryNote: For families in these clusters the mathematics route decision made at the end of MYP 3 has a long tail, because the extended route builds the algebraic fluency the Diploma later assumes. If Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is a possibility, a term of targeted work producing marked evidence at the extended route is better value than two years of general support.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent long-term project with a supervisor, assessed against published criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and the product. The MYP's largest single piece of independent work and the clearest rehearsal for the Diploma's Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: Coaching here is naturally finite - four to six sessions scheduled backwards from the school's deadline - which makes the total cost known at the start. It is also the purchase where the boundary matters most: the student sets the goal, does the work, keeps the journal and writes the report, and anybody offering otherwise is selling your child a malpractice finding.

programmes.name: MYP 5 into the Diploma
programmes.description: The transition most students in this cluster find hardest, because the MYP assesses skills against criteria with generous time and the Diploma assesses a product written in two hours. The gap is a specific list rather than a general standard, which is what makes it cheap to close.
programmes.countryNote: Six to eight sessions in the summer between MYP 5 and the first Diploma year, on algebraic automaticity and timed essay structure, is the best-value tutoring available to a family here and is bought by almost nobody - because the subject it helps has not started. For a commuting household it also lands in the one period with no school run in it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-international-city.subjectsIntro: Each subject below names the criterion that usually costs marks, because that is the level at which Middle Years tutoring is either targeted or wasted.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics, standard and extended
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the usual weak one: finding a rule is manageable, expressing it in correct general notation and justifying it is what scores and is rarely taught directly.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Marks go on criteria B and C rather than A, because investigation design and data evaluation are skills most schemes of work assume rather than teach explicitly.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. The critical-thinking criterion carries the marks students lose, because it requires source evaluation addressing provenance and perspective rather than a summary of content.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students strong on analysis frequently score poorly on using language, where accuracy, register and range are assessed separately from ideas - a split that is invisible in one grade and obvious in the criterion marks.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Assessed by phase rather than year group, so two children in one class can be working at different phases, which parents are rarely told explicitly.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Process documentation carries more marks than the finished product, which is why capable makers often score moderately and why the fix is cheap once named.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The developmental workbook and reflective responses carry substantial weight beside the final piece, so a student who only produces work forfeits the criteria that reward process.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Written and reflective components matter, which regularly startles families who assume the subject is assessed on sport alone.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills, running across every subject. Work on self-management and research often raises grades in several subjects at once, which makes it unusually good value for a single short block.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and the product. Coaching covers goal scoping, criteria interpretation and process-journal discipline. The student sets the goal, does the work, keeps the journal and writes the report.

subjects.name: Diploma bridging in mathematics
subjects.description: Indices, surds, algebraic fractions, rearranging with the unknown appearing twice, function notation and expanding without hesitation - all assumed automatic from the first Diploma week. Six to eight summer sessions, and the cheapest decisive purchase in the programme.

subjects.name: Diploma bridging in writing
subjects.description: Essay structure under timed conditions, command-term discipline, and argument built on evidence rather than assertion. The MYP rewards drafting and reflection; a Diploma paper rewards one well-structured answer produced to time, which catches strong MYP writers.

sections.heading: The free step that usually shrinks the purchase
paragraphs: Before spending anything, ask the school for the criterion-level breakdown in the subject that worries you - the four criterion marks out of eight, not the overall grade. Most schools hold them, many will share them on a direct request, and the difference it makes to a tutoring decision is larger than any choice of provider.

The reason is that the four marks localise the problem. A science profile of 7, 7, 3, 2 says the content is understood and investigation design and data evaluation are not, which is a term of targeted work rather than a year of general science support. A mathematics profile weak only on investigating patterns says the student can calculate and cannot yet generalise and justify a rule, which is a handful of sessions.

Two further questions are worth asking alongside it, because they stop a misreading. How many times has each criterion been assessed? Early-year reports are noisy when some criteria have been assessed once and others three times. And does the mark reflect the most recent evidence or an average across the term? A single poor task in September should not still be dragging a criterion mark in May.

With those answers, a tutor can say in one session what a term should contain. Without them, any provider is guessing, and the guess is usually generous to itself: general support across the subject, or across three subjects, which is the most expensive possible response to a problem nobody has located.

sections.heading: What each AED band buys at this stage
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme is the one stage where the lowest market band is genuinely competitive, which is worth saying plainly because it is not true at Diploma Higher Level. Every figure here was published by the provider named and read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram rate - ours is quoted after the free trial against the work the breakdown identifies.

Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For Middle Years content support - arithmetic fluency, structured writing, a topic that did not land - that band contains usable help. What it less often contains is somebody who can name the four criteria for your child's subject and teach against the descriptors, which is the narrower skill.

Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. At this stage the extra money should be buying criterion literacy specifically rather than greater subject depth, because the subject content in the Middle Years Programme is not where the difficulty lies for most students.

The specialist and premium bands - AED 200 to 450 and AED 500 to 650, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 - are hard to justify for Middle Years work in almost every case. Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, with published online packages at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. For household context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year.

sections.heading: Middle Years purchases ranked by what they return
paragraphs: If the monthly figure is fixed, the order of spending matters more than the rate. The Middle Years Programme ranks unusually clearly, because one purchase sits outside the programme entirely and beats everything inside it, and because two of the others transfer across several subjects at once.

First is the summer bridging block between MYP 5 and the first Diploma year, if your child is at that point. Six to eight sessions on indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation, timed essay structure and command-term discipline. Nothing is urgent, the commute has gone, and the effect runs across two years of Diploma teaching rather than one term of Middle Years grades.

Second is the approaches-to-learning block: self-management and research skills, which run across every subject and frequently raise grades in several at once. Third is a criterion-targeted term in the single subject the breakdown names. Fourth is the Personal Project coaching block, which is finite and well defined but matters only in MYP 5.

At the bottom of the ranking sits open weekly support across two or three subjects, which is the easiest arrangement to sell and the hardest for a parent to evaluate afterwards. It is not useless - a child who enjoys the sessions and does the work will improve - but it costs several times the alternatives for progress nobody can attribute. The practical test before any purchase at this stage is whether you could state, in one sentence, what you expect to be different at the end of it. If the answer names a criterion and a subject, the money is well aimed. If it names a general hope, the criterion breakdown has not been read yet.

sections.heading: Why investigation design is the science criterion worth paying for
paragraphs: In the sciences, criterion A - knowing and understanding - is usually the strongest, because it is closest to conventional content teaching. Criteria B and C, inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating, are usually the weakest, because investigation design and data evaluation are skills most schemes of work assume rather than teach. The result is a student who knows the science and scores moderately.

That is good news financially, because it is a narrow and teachable gap. Criterion B asks for a testable research question, variables identified and explained, a method that controls what needs controlling, and justified choices. Students fail it in consistent ways: an untestable question, controlled variables listed with no mention of how they will be held constant, and no justification for range, interval or repeats.

Criterion C fails in a matching pattern: data presented without processing, processed without spread or uncertainty, graphed without a line of best fit, and an evaluation saying more repeats would have helped - which earns nothing - instead of naming the largest error source and proposing a specific change.

A handful of sessions on those two criteria produces a visible change in the criterion marks, and it is also the clearest investment in Diploma readiness available in MYP 4 and 5. The Diploma's scientific investigation is assessed against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation for twenty-four marks, and it asks for precisely the skills criteria B and C are building.

sections.heading: Reading a 1 to 8 grade without overspending
paragraphs: Parents in these clusters ask whether a 4 or a 5 is a problem, and the honest answer is that the grade alone cannot tell you - which matters because panic is expensive. Four criterion marks out of eight each, converted using published boundaries, can produce the same overall grade from very different profiles, and only one of those profiles justifies a sustained purchase.

A flat profile of fours or fives across all four criteria usually reflects a student who is working steadily and has not yet been shown what the top bands look like. That responds to a short block aimed at the criterion with the clearest descriptor gap, not to a year of support. A profile with one collapsed criterion against three strong ones reflects a specific, nameable failure and responds to a specific, nameable intervention.

A genuinely weak profile across all four criteria in several subjects is a different situation, and it is the one case where a broader conversation with the school matters more than any tutoring purchase. Sometimes the cause is organisational or attendance-related rather than academic, and in those cases buying teaching is buying the wrong thing at full price.

MYP grades are also not percentages, and a 5 is not half marks - a point worth stating because families arriving from percentage-based systems routinely assume the worst. The programme is reporting what a student can currently do against published descriptors, which is more informative than a percentage and much less familiar.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the two failures that cost money
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the Middle Years Programme's largest independent undertaking, assessed against published criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and the product, with a process journal throughout and a report at the end. It is also the purchase where getting the shape right matters most, because the two dominant failures both happen early and neither can be fixed late.

The first is a goal too large and too vague. A student intending to build an application, compose an album or run an event discovers in the final month that the product cannot be completed and the criteria cannot be evidenced. The remedy is a scoping conversation in the first fortnight, testing the goal against both assessability and the available weeks - half a session, and the best-value item in the whole block.

The cheapest insurance in the whole Personal Project is a weekly journal habit started in the first month, and it is the one thing an International City family can set up tonight without buying a single session. It exists because of the second dominant failure: a process journal written retrospectively. The journal is meant to be contemporaneous evidence of planning, decision-making and reflection, and a fortnight of entries reconstructed the night before submission reads exactly like what it is. Fifteen minutes a week, kept honestly from the start, protects two criteria that cannot be recovered afterwards at any price.

The boundary matters here more than anywhere else in the programme, because the search results this page sits in include operators who sell completed coursework. The student sets the goal, does the work, keeps the journal and writes the report. A tutor interrogates the goal, explains what each criterion rewards, asks the questions a supervisor would ask, and comments on the student's own drafts. A malpractice finding falls on the student.

sections.heading: Fitting a session into a commuting week
paragraphs: A Middle Years student travelling out of these clusters to Al Warqa, Al Qusais, Silicon Oasis or Mirdif spends an hour or more a day on the journey, and the evening that remains has homework in it. The good news is that the Middle Years load is lighter than the Diploma load, so one weekly session plus its homework fits comfortably - which is not true two years later.

The practical constraint at this age is tiredness rather than timetable. A child who has been travelling since seven in the morning is genuinely spent by five, and a session booked then is often an hour nobody benefits from. From these clusters a 6pm start is realistic, and for younger Middle Years students a weekend morning frequently produces more than any weekday slot even though the weekday slot looks more convenient.

The other thing worth protecting is the work between sessions. A session with no homework after it delivers roughly a third of its value at the full price, and homework with no slot in the week displaces what the school set. Agreeing both - the work and the evening it happens in - is free and roughly triples the return on everything else.

During Ramadan the pattern should change deliberately. School days shorten so the bus returns earlier, but late-afternoon concentration is poor and a session at four is often wasted. Weekend mornings and post-Iftar slots work. Because no tutor is travelling, changing the pattern is a scheduling decision rather than a logistical one, and it should be fixed before the month starts.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and the mandatory subjects
paragraphs: Middle Years students in Dubai also carry the mandatory UAE subjects, and new arrivals in these clusters are regularly surprised by this at the first report rather than at the open day. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states the requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

The rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with Arabic primary for Social Studies for Arab students and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a concrete point a parent can ask about directly.

What constrains tutoring is a content rule: for these subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support for Arabic as an additional language is ordinary language teaching, freely available, and in the Middle Years Programme it maps onto the language acquisition phases. Help with the mandatory Islamic Education and Social Studies content needs a conversation with the school about acceptable material first.

sections.heading: What to ask before paying, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Five questions, deliberately about money and accountability. Can you name the four criteria for my child's subject? Does the individual teaching my child hold a current MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? Is the figure per hour or per session, and does it include VAT? What is the replacement policy if the match fails? And what will you do with the Personal Project, and what will you refuse to do?

The first question is the Middle Years-specific one, and it is the sharpest. A tutor who cannot name the four criteria for the subject is offering general secondary tutoring, which may be perfectly good and should be priced at the lower band accordingly. Paying the qualified band for general support is the commonest overspend at this stage.

On the permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted at you. Because the permit is free, it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate. It applies regardless of the student's age or programme.

And what we do not claim: no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE; no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai; no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or the IB; no promises about grades and no published predicted scores; no ratings we cannot evidence with countable dated reviews; and no IB material supplied as downloads, since we cite and link the official sources instead.

process.title: Ask the school for the criterion marks
process.description: The four criterion marks out of eight in the subject that worries you, plus how many times each has been assessed. It is free, it localises the problem, and it routinely turns a three-subject arrangement into a single term aimed at one criterion.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the criterion and the budget
process.description: Including the monthly figure, which changes the recommendation. At this stage the lowest market band is genuinely usable for content support, so we would rather point you at the right band than sell you a higher one.

process.title: Free trial lesson and a written note
process.description: A real lesson on the actual criterion in question, with the student working. Afterwards a plain summary of what the tutor found and what a term would target. Say no and nothing further is owed, and the figure is only quoted after this.

process.title: Buy a term, not a year
process.description: A term has a known end and a known total, and it is long enough for one criterion to move visibly. Open weekly arrangements across several subjects cost several times as much and leave nobody able to say what changed.

process.title: Protect the homework slot
process.description: A session with no work after it delivers about a third of its value at the full price, and work with no slot in the week displaces what the school set. We agree both, which costs nothing and roughly triples the return.

whyPoints.title: We send you to the school first
whyPoints.description: The four criterion marks are free, they localise the problem, and they usually shrink the purchase. Asking for them before contacting any tutor is advice against our own interest, and it is still the right first step at this stage.

whyPoints.title: We will point you at a cheaper band
whyPoints.description: For Middle Years content support the AED 45 to 150 band genuinely works, which is not true at Diploma Higher Level. The extra money at the qualified band should be buying criterion literacy specifically, not generic subject depth.

whyPoints.title: The purchase nobody makes, ranked first
whyPoints.description: Six to eight summer sessions between MYP 5 and the first Diploma year, on algebraic automaticity and timed essay structure. It affects two years of Diploma teaching and is bought by almost nobody because the subject it helps has not started.

whyPoints.title: Terms, not years
whyPoints.description: A term aimed at one named criterion has a known end and an evaluable result. Open weekly support across two or three subjects is the easiest arrangement to sell and the hardest for a parent to assess afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Three of the six leading pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote dollars. Ours name the provider and the month they were read, and none is presented as our own rate.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on the Personal Project
whyPoints.description: The student sets the goal, does the work, keeps the journal and writes the report; we question the goal, explain criteria and comment on drafts. Operators in these search results sell completed coursework, and that finding lands on a sixteen-year-old.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB MYP tutor in International City?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one-to-one online tuition rather than a tutor coming to your flat, since IB Gram offers home visits only in India. No MYP is taught inside International City, so families here already travel to Al Warqa, Mirdif or further for the programme itself. The relevant scarcity for Middle Years tutoring is not subject knowledge but criterion literacy - a tutor who cannot name the four criteria for your child's subject is offering general secondary tutoring.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school before paying for anything?
faqs.answer: The four criterion marks out of eight in the subject that worries you, not the overall grade. Also how many times each criterion has been assessed, because early-year reports are noisy when some have been assessed once and others three times, and whether the mark reflects the most recent evidence or a term average. All three questions are free and they routinely turn a three-subject arrangement into one term aimed at a single criterion.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor good enough for the Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: For content support, often yes - and this is the one stage where that is true. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from 33 to 52, and that band handles arithmetic fluency, structured writing and a topic that did not land. What it less often contains is criterion literacy, which is the narrower skill and the thing the qualified band should be buying.

faqs.question: How much should a Middle Years arrangement cost per month?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget support at AED 240 to 600 a month and mid-range at AED 600 to 1,200, with published online packages at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. The specialist and premium bands - AED 200 to 450 and AED 500 to 650 - are priced for Diploma Higher Level and are hard to justify for Middle Years work. Those are market figures from the sources named, not IB Gram rates.

faqs.question: Which Middle Years purchase gives the best return?
faqs.answer: The summer bridging block between MYP 5 and the first Diploma year, if your child is at that point. Six to eight sessions on indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation, timed essay structure and command-term discipline. Nothing is urgent, the commute has gone for the summer, and the effect runs across two years of Diploma teaching rather than one term of Middle Years grades. Almost nobody buys it, because the subject it helps has not begun.

faqs.question: Why does my son score well on content and poorly overall in science?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly criteria B and C. Knowing and understanding is closest to conventional content teaching and is usually strongest; inquiring and designing asks for a testable question, identified variables and a justified method, and processing and evaluating asks for processed data and an evaluation of method and reliability. Most schemes of work assume rather than teach those, so a student who knows the science scores moderately. A handful of sessions moves both visibly.

faqs.question: Is a grade 5 in the MYP something to worry about?
faqs.answer: The grade alone cannot tell you, which matters because panic is expensive. A flat profile of fives usually reflects steady work and a student who has not been shown what the top bands look like, which responds to a short block rather than a year of support. A profile with one collapsed criterion against three strong ones is a specific nameable failure. And MYP grades are not percentages - a 5 is not half marks.

faqs.question: Which maths criterion do students lose most marks on?
faqs.answer: Investigating patterns, consistently. It asks a student to find a rule, express it in correct general notation and then justify it. Finding the rule is the part most students manage; expressing and justifying it is the part that scores and is rarely taught directly. The structure of a strong response is consistent enough that a handful of sessions produces a visible change in the criterion mark, which makes it one of the most efficient targets in the programme.

faqs.question: How should the Personal Project money be spent?
faqs.answer: On scoping first and drafting last. Four to six sessions scheduled backwards from the school's deadline, with the first half session spent testing whether the goal is small enough to finish and specific enough to assess. The two dominant failures - a goal too large and a process journal written retrospectively - both happen in the first month and neither can be fixed in the last. The scoping conversation is the best-value item in the whole block.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Interrogate the goal, explain what each criterion rewards, ask the questions a supervisor would ask, and read and comment on your child's own drafts and journal entries. A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product, write journal entries or supply text for the report. The search results this page sits in include operators selling completed coursework outright, and a malpractice finding from that falls on the student rather than on the seller.

faqs.question: Should we pay for help with the maths route decision?
faqs.answer: Only if Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is a realistic ambition later. Many schools split mathematics into standard and extended routes at the end of MYP 3, and the extended route builds the algebraic fluency the Diploma assumes. If it matters, a term of targeted work producing marked evidence at the extended route is better value than two years of general support. Ask the school which route they intend and what evidence would change their view.

faqs.question: What time can a Middle Years session start from these clusters?
faqs.answer: Around six on a weekday, and for younger students a weekend morning often produces more even though the weekday slot looks more convenient. The constraint at this age is tiredness rather than timetable: a child travelling since seven in the morning is genuinely spent by five, so a session booked then is frequently an hour nobody benefits from. Because no tutor is travelling, a weekend slot costs nothing extra to arrange.

faqs.question: Does my child take Arabic and Islamic Education in an MYP school here?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's guidance requiring implementation from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on 40-minute lesson units, with any such lesson advised to run at least 25 minutes.

faqs.question: Can we get help with Arabic as an additional language?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it maps onto the MYP language acquisition phases, which is worth knowing because students are assessed by phase rather than by year group - two children in the same class can be working at different phases and parents are rarely told so explicitly. Note the constraint on the mandatory subjects: for Islamic Education and Social Studies, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so ask the school what material it will accept first.

faqs.question: Is a permit needed for someone tutoring Middle Years subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it applies regardless of the programme or the student's age. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted at you as unverified.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-international-city.closingHeading: Ask the school for four numbers first
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-international-city.closingBody: If your child is in the Middle Years Programme and you live in International City, the most useful thing you can do before contacting any tutor is ask the school for the four criterion marks in the subject that worries you. With those, plus the monthly figure you have in mind, we can say which band is appropriate, whether a term aimed at one criterion is the right shape, and whether the summer bridging block would be worth more than anything happening now. The trial lesson is free; lessons are one-to-one and online, on Gulf Standard Time.

Each teaches one-to-one over live video, works from your child's own school assessment calendar, and marks against the published MYP criteria rather than a generic worksheet pack.

intro.heading: What an IB MYP tutor in JBR costs, and what the money actually buys
paragraphs: JBR is a one-kilometre strip of towers between Dubai Marina and the sea, and almost nobody who lives there goes to school inside it. The Walk has no secondary school on it. Children in the JBR towers commute out, to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim and Barsha South, and come home between 15:30 and 16:45 depending on which bus route the school runs. That commute is the reason tutoring here is priced the way it is. A visiting tutor is not selling you an hour of teaching; they are selling an hour of teaching plus the forty minutes of Sheikh Zayed Road that got them to your lobby, and the hour is the cheaper half of the invoice.

Market rates make the point in numbers. Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts in-home one-to-one tutoring at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, which matches Unitors' published figures of AED 150 upward for IGCSE and AED 200 upward for IB. EdFlik advertises budget online help from AED 45 to 65, and Tutopiya starts lower again at AED 33 to 52. The spread between cheapest and dearest is more than tenfold, and the Middle Years Programme is where families most often pay at the top of it for work that did not need it.

The Middle Years Programme runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, for roughly ages 11 to 16. Marks do not come from end-of-year papers in the way a parent who sat O Levels expects. Every subject group is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, each marked out of 8, giving 32 raw marks that the school converts to a 1 to 7 grade using its own published boundaries. A child can know the content thoroughly and still sit at a 4, because criterion C is usually about communication and criterion D about transfer to an unfamiliar context, and neither improves by doing more practice questions of the kind already mastered.

That is where JBR money goes astray. A parent sees a 4 in MYP 4 Sciences, books two hours a week of general science tutoring at AED 300 an hour, and eighteen weeks later the grade is still a 4, because the child was always secure on criterion A and was losing marks on B and C. The cheaper and more effective intervention is often six focused sessions on inquiry design and data processing, costed at a few hundred dirhams in total, rather than a standing weekly booking that runs to the end of the academic year and quietly reaches five figures.

IB Gram delivers to JBR as one-to-one online tuition over live video. There are no home visits in Dubai; that is a service we run only in India, and we say so rather than quietly routing an enquiry. What the format buys a JBR family is selection. Your child works with a MYP Sciences specialist who marks to the criteria, instead of whichever qualified person is willing to drive to the Marina for a 17:00 start on a Tuesday. The travel premium comes off the price and the pool of available specialists widens at the same time.
