dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jbr.programmesIntro: A JBR family rarely buys tutoring for one year in isolation. The MYP sits between the Primary Years Programme and whatever comes at 16, and the cost of support in MYP 4 and 5 is really the cost of arriving at the Diploma without a gap to close. Here is how the four IB programmes relate, and what each means for a household in the towers.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, organised around six units of inquiry a year rather than separate subject syllabuses. There is no external examination and no published grade, which is why parents often arrive at MYP 1 with no benchmark for where their child sits. Support at this stage is almost always about securing number fluency, reading stamina and written structure, because those three carry directly into MYP criteria C and D in every subject group.
programmes.countryNote: JBR children in the PYP generally travel to Al Sufouh or Al Barsha, and the school day ends earlier than for secondary siblings, so a 16:00 session is realistic. Families with two children at different stages usually stagger a 16:00 and a 17:30 slot rather than paying a visiting tutor to wait between them, which is an hour nobody should be charged for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria each, every criterion marked out of 8. The programme adds Approaches to Learning skills, Service as Action, and in MYP 5 the Personal Project, which is externally moderated. Some Dubai schools also enter MYP 5 students for on-screen eAssessment in a subset of subjects. The practical consequence for tutoring is that a session has to target a criterion, not a topic: 'fractions' is not a diagnosis, 'criterion D in Mathematics' is.
programmes.countryNote: In JBR the MYP years are when the commute and the workload collide. A MYP 4 student leaving Al Barsha at 15:20 is home by 16:10 on a good day and 16:50 when Sheikh Zayed Road is heavy, which leaves one usable session slot before homework. Online delivery protects that slot; a tutor stuck in the same traffic does not, and a late arrival is still a billed hour.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Scored out of 45. The Diploma is where the money in Dubai tutoring actually concentrates, because the stakes are university admission and the content load doubles. A MYP 5 student who is weak on algebraic manipulation will meet it again in the first fortnight of Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and closing the gap then costs several times what closing it in MYP 5 would have cost.
programmes.countryNote: JBR and Marina families often choose between a Diploma at a nearby IB school and A Levels at a British-curriculum school in Al Barsha. That decision is usually made during MYP 4, which means a MYP tutor in JBR is frequently asked to advise on readiness rather than only on marks. An honest answer sometimes is that the child is better suited to three A Levels than to six Diploma subjects.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a service-learning component. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is sometimes the right route for a student with two strong subjects and three weak ones. Tutoring for the CP concentrates on the Diploma courses the student does take, plus the language-development portfolio, which is marked internally and rewards consistency rather than last-minute work.
programmes.countryNote: Very few schools serving the JBR and Marina catchment offer the CP, so a family considering it is usually looking at a change of school as well as a change of programme. That is worth knowing before paying for a year of MYP support aimed at Diploma readiness the student may not need. Ask the school's IB coordinator which pathways they actually run in Year 12.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jbr.subjectsIntro: MYP assessment is organised by subject group, and each group has its own four criteria with its own letters. The grid below names what each group marks and where JBR students most often drop marks, so you can brief a tutor in one sentence instead of paying for three sessions of diagnosis.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Marks are rarely lost on A. They go on B, where students spot a pattern but never generalise it or justify the rule, and on D, where a correct answer is given without reflecting on whether the model is reasonable.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. The commonest JBR pattern is a student who can recite the content for A and then writes a method for B with no controlled variables named, which caps the mark at 4 of 8 regardless of how good the practical was.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criterion A analysing, B organising, C producing text, D using language. Secure readers lose marks on B because an essay has ideas but no visible structure, and on D for register rather than grammar. A tutor's work here is paragraph architecture and evidence selection, not vocabulary lists.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criterion A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, each out of 8 and each assessed against the phase the school has placed the student in. Movement between phases matters more than the grade itself, and a student can appear to plateau simply because they were moved up a phase mid-year.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D is where most of the marks sit untouched: students describe sources instead of evaluating their origin, purpose and limitation, which is a teachable technique rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criterion A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. Design is the group most often ignored until the folio is due, and it carries the same 32 marks as Mathematics. Tutoring here is mostly documentation discipline: specifications written as testable statements, and evaluation against those tests.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criterion A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. The process journal carries more weight than students expect, and a strong final piece with a thin journal lands well below a competent piece with a documented process. That is a scheduling problem a tutor can fix early.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. Written components are real marks, and students who perform well in the pool or on the pitch sometimes carry a 3 in criterion A because the theory was never revised.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: MYP schools must assess interdisciplinary learning against its own criteria: evaluating, synthesising and reflecting. These units are frequently the lowest marks on a MYP report because nobody taught the student how to combine two disciplines' methods, and they are quick to lift with two or three targeted sessions.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal and a report. A tutor may coach the planning, question the goal, and give feedback on the student's own drafts. No tutor should write any part of the Personal Project, and any service offering to produce one is a malpractice risk for the student.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jbr.regionsIntro: IB Gram works with families across the Marina and New Dubai belt. The notes below are about session timing and school routes rather than scenery, because those are the two things that decide whether a tutoring plan survives past February.

regions.name: JBR
regions.note: Forty-odd towers across two rows, no secondary school on the strip. Nearly every secondary student commutes out, so the first realistic session start on a school night is 16:30, and 17:00 is safer during the February to April exam-season traffic.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Immediately inland from JBR and sharing the same school routes. Marina families tend to book slightly later slots because the bus loop through the towers adds fifteen to twenty minutes on the way home.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: Connected to JBR by footbridge, which makes the school run shorter than the postcode suggests. Small resident population, so a locally based subject specialist is rarely available and online delivery is the practical option.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Where a large share of JBR's secondary students actually attend school, including several IB and British-curriculum campuses. A session timed to 17:00 works for most Al Sufouh school finishes.

regions.name: The Greens
regions.note: Low-rise and family-heavy, with children spread across Al Barsha and Barsha South schools. Parents here often run two siblings in back-to-back slots, which is straightforward online and expensive with a visiting tutor.

regions.name: The Views
regions.note: Adjacent to The Greens and sharing its school routes. Golf-course side traffic clears earlier, so a 16:30 start is usually achievable for MYP students here.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Not a residential base for most JBR families but the destination for many of their school runs. Knowing which Barsha campus your child attends matters more for session timing than knowing your own tower.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Reached from JBR in under fifteen minutes off-peak but considerably longer at 16:00. Families on the fronds tend to prefer 18:00 sessions after the commute has settled.

schoolClusters.city: JBR, Marina and Al Sufouh
schoolClusters.note: The schools JBR secondary students most often travel to. Several run the MYP, several run IGCSE at 16 instead, and a few offer both routes, which is the single most useful thing to confirm before planning MYP 4 and 5 support.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Barsha South
schoolClusters.note: The second destination cluster for the JBR and Marina catchment, with a mix of IB and British provision. Bus routes from Barsha South add the most time to a JBR commute, which is why some families there settle on 17:30 as their standing slot.

schoolClusters.city: Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah
schoolClusters.note: A longer run from JBR along Jumeirah Beach Road, chosen by families who want a specific curriculum rather than the nearest campus. Students on this route are home latest of all, and 18:00 is often the only workable start.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jbr.modesIntro: Three formats are worth costing before you commit to a standing weekly booking. The difference between them for a MYP family is rarely teaching quality; it is how many paid hours go on things that are not teaching, and how narrowly the work can be targeted at a criterion.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one over live video
modes.description: A fixed slot with one tutor, 60 or 90 minutes, running to your child's own school assessment calendar rather than a generic scheme of work. The tutor sees the MYP task sheet and the criteria strands before the session, so the hour starts on the gap rather than on diagnosis. Screen sharing and a shared whiteboard mean working is visible, which matters for criterion C in Mathematics and Sciences.

modes.title: A short targeted block
modes.description: Four to eight sessions aimed at one named criterion in one subject group, with a defined finish. This is the format most JBR families should price first, because a MYP grade stuck on a 4 is usually one strand rather than a whole subject. It also makes the spend legible: a block of six 60-minute sessions has a total, where a weekly standing booking has a direction.

modes.title: Personal Project and Approaches to Learning coaching
modes.description: Fortnightly process sessions through MYP 5, aimed at the planning, research and reflection skills the Personal Project is marked on. The tutor questions the goal, pushes on the process journal and gives written feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is drafted for the student, and nothing is edited to completion, because the project must be their work to be accepted.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring in the JBR and Marina belt costs, by format
paragraphs: A MYP hour in this part of Dubai is priced between AED 45 and AED 650, and the number you pay depends far more on format than on the year group. The table below sets out the bands that are actually quoted in the market, with the source for each attributed. These are market rates and not IB Gram's price list: our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and the figure for a given family depends on subject, level and session length.

Read the monthly column first rather than the hourly one. Hourly rates flatter the cheapest tier and hide the cost of the arrangement as a whole, because a budget tutor at AED 60 an hour who needs three sessions to do what a specialist does in one is the more expensive choice. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist exam-year support.

Package pricing is where the gap widens. Monthly packages advertised in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. On a per-hour basis the online package works out at roughly AED 100 and the in-home one at roughly AED 200 to 225, for the same contact time. The difference is travel, and in JBR, where a tutor arrives through the Marina at 17:00, travel is the largest single line in the invoice nobody itemises.

sections.heading: The MYP criteria, letter by letter, and where the marks really are
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group is marked against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8. Thirty-two raw marks become a 1 to 7 grade through boundaries the school publishes. This is the single most useful thing a JBR parent can learn before spending anything, because it converts a vague complaint into a purchase order. 'He is weak at science' buys you a year of general tutoring. 'He is at 7 of 8 on criterion A and 3 of 8 on criterion B in Sciences' buys you four sessions on inquiry design.

The criteria are not interchangeable between groups, and that trips up tutors who have only taught one subject. In Mathematics, criterion B is investigating patterns and criterion D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences, B is inquiring and designing and D is reflecting on the impacts of science. In Individuals and Societies, D is thinking critically. A tutor who treats D as 'the hard one' without knowing which D is being marked will teach the wrong skill competently.

Ask your child's teacher for the criterion-level breakdown rather than the overall grade. Most Dubai MYP schools record it in the reporting platform even when the printed report shows only the 1 to 7. With that breakdown in hand, the honest answer is often that no tutoring is needed yet, or that six sessions will do, and a tutor willing to say so is worth more than one who books you in until June.

sections.heading: Where JBR families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: The commonest waste is buying hours instead of buying a diagnosis. A standing two-hour weekly booking from October to June is around seventy hours. At a mid-market AED 220 that is roughly AED 15,000 for one subject, and a large share of those hours will be spent on content the student already holds, because without a criterion-level breakdown neither parent nor tutor knows where to aim.

The second waste is paying a travel premium for a service that does not require presence. A visiting tutor in the JBR towers is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour by the sources above, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. For a MYP maths session built around a shared whiteboard and a set of past tasks, there is nothing in the room that the room provides. The premium buys proximity, and proximity shrinks the pool of candidates to whoever can reach the Marina on a weekday evening.

The third is duplicating school provision. Many Dubai schools run free after-school clinics, subject surgeries and Approaches to Learning sessions that cover exactly the strand a parent is about to pay for. Ask the form tutor what already exists before booking anything. The fourth is starting in April. A MYP grade is built from tasks completed across the year, so support bought in the last six weeks has very little left to influence, and that is the moment families pay the highest rates.

sections.heading: Online versus a visiting tutor in a JBR tower, costed honestly
paragraphs: This is the comparison that matters most on this strip, so here it is as a table rather than as an argument. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and stating that plainly is more useful than pretending the choice does not exist. Many families genuinely prefer someone in the room, and for a seven-year-old needing handwriting support that preference is well founded.

For MYP work it is less well founded. The tasks are typed, the drafts are shared documents, the maths is worked on a whiteboard, and the science method is a written plan. All four transfer to a screen without loss. What does not transfer is the forty-minute drive, and that is the part you are paying a premium for. The practical test is simple: ask what the session would look like, step by step, and then ask which of those steps needs the tutor to be physically present.

There is a second-order effect that is worth more than the money. A JBR family hiring locally picks from the people who can reach the Marina at 17:00. A JBR family hiring online picks from specialists in the subject and the criterion they actually need. For a common requirement such as MYP 3 Mathematics, the local pool is adequate. For MYP 5 Sciences criterion B with eAssessment ahead, it usually is not. A family on the second row of JBR towers who insists on presence is choosing from perhaps a handful of people who will make that drive on a weekday evening, and is paying the upper end of the in-home band for the privilege of that short list.

sections.heading: MYP 5 to the Diploma: the gap that costs most to close late
paragraphs: The expensive version of MYP tutoring is the version bought in Year 12 because MYP 5 was left alone. The Diploma's first term assumes fluency that the MYP assesses but does not drill, and the subjects where that shows most are Mathematics, the sciences and the essay-based humanities. A student arriving in Analysis and Approaches without secure algebraic manipulation will meet it in the opening fortnight and will be behind for the rest of the course.

The table maps the common transitions. The last column is the honest part: how many weeks of focused support families typically find they need when the gap is addressed in MYP 5 rather than Year 12. The numbers come from the shape of the work rather than from a published study, and any tutor quoting a precise figure for your child before seeing their work is guessing.

This is also the section that should save you money rather than spend it. If your child is secure on MYP Mathematics Extended criterion A and B, the honest advice is to buy nothing now and revisit in MYP 5 term two. The point of mapping the transition is to spend in the right term, not to spend in every term. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator which route they expect your child to take at 16, because the gap for Analysis and Approaches is algebra and proof while the gap for Applications and Interpretation is statistics and calculator technique, and the two plans share almost nothing. A family that buys the wrong one pays twice, once for the sessions and once again in Year 12 when the real gap surfaces.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a parent in JBR can check the position in a single conversation. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligibility is broader than most parents expect. It covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anybody, including us.

There are two boundaries worth knowing. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct pointing the same way. 'Your child's own teacher, privately' is not an arrangement to seek out, however convenient it looks from a JBR tower five minutes from the school gate. The permit is the one credential a parent can check without specialist knowledge, so check it.

sections.heading: What KHDA requires alongside the MYP, and what that costs you in time
paragraphs: A JBR family budgeting for MYP support should know that their child's timetable already carries subjects the IB does not set. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. These sit alongside the MYP subject groups, not instead of them.

The organisation rules are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson is at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which is why tutoring in these subjects must track the school's own material rather than import a parallel syllabus. Schools are also required to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach them.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in the MYP, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The MYP carries less coursework than the Diploma, but it carries enough for this to matter, and MYP 5 carries the Personal Project, which is externally moderated. The boundary is the same as at Diploma level. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the criterion, question the plan, and give feedback on work the student has already produced. A tutor may not draft, rewrite to completion, or supply text that then appears in a submission.

That boundary is not a formality in this market. One page in the Dubai search results sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Buying one is a malpractice trigger for the student, and the consequence lands on the child rather than the seller. No tutor working through IB Gram will produce assessed work for a student, and we would rather lose the enquiry than take it.

There is a practical version of the rule for parents. Look at the drafts. If each one is visibly the child's own writing improving over time, with the tutor's feedback showing up as changes the child made, the support is legitimate. If a draft arrives in a different voice from the one your child uses in conversation, something has gone wrong, and it will be visible to a moderator too. Similarly, official syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes should be referenced and linked from the board's own site, never reproduced or supplied as downloads. A provider that emails you a folder of scanned mark schemes has told you something about how it treats rules in general, and that is worth noticing before MYP 5 becomes Year 12 and the stakes rise.
bullets: Teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts: legitimate

sections.heading: Getting started from a JBR address, including what we will tell you not to buy
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the school, the MYP year, the subject group and, if you have it, the criterion-level breakdown. We propose a tutor and a slot that fits the commute home, you take a free trial lesson with no card details required, and only then do you decide on anything paid. Matching usually takes two to four working days for common MYP subjects and longer for a niche combination.

Availability is disclosed rather than assumed. For MYP Mathematics, Sciences, English and Individuals and Societies, a UAE-hours tutor is normally available in that window. For a less common Language Acquisition phase, a specific arts discipline or a Design folio in a particular software environment, the honest answer is sometimes that we do not have the right person this term, in which case we say so and you are free to look elsewhere. Nobody is well served by a weak match held in place to avoid an awkward message.

The last part of getting started is the part most providers skip: being told what not to buy. If the criterion breakdown shows a single weak strand, we will propose a short block with a finish date instead of a standing weekly slot. If your school already runs an after-school clinic covering that strand, we will say to use it first. A plan that ends because it worked is the outcome worth paying for. And if the criterion breakdown shows nothing wrong at all, which happens more often than a tutoring company has any commercial reason to admit, the right answer is to keep your money and come back if the next marked task disagrees.

faqs.question: How much should an IB MYP tutor for a JBR family cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates for the Marina and JBR belt run from AED 33 to 65 an hour for budget online help, on Tutopiya's and EdFlik's published figures, to AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, on Unitors' rates. In-home visiting tutors are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour by Bestimate and independent home tutors, and premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. For MYP work, the qualified online band is where most families land. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson and a consultation rather than publishing a flat rate, because subject, level and session length all move the figure.

faqs.question: Why is my child's MYP grade stuck on a 4 when the content is understood?
faqs.answer: Because the MYP marks four separate criteria and content knowledge is usually only one of them. Each criterion is out of 8, and the 32 raw marks convert to the 1 to 7 you see on the report. A student can score 7 of 8 on criterion A, which is knowing and understanding, and 3 of 8 on criterion B or C, which concern investigation and communication. The grade averages out at a 4 and more content revision will not move it. Ask the school for the criterion-level breakdown; it names the strand that is actually costing marks.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for MYP tutoring before the Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is usually cheaper than the alternative. The Diploma's opening term assumes fluency the MYP assesses but does not drill, so a student entering Analysis and Approaches without secure algebraic manipulation meets that gap in the first fortnight and stays behind. Closing it in MYP 5 typically takes six to ten weeks of focused work; closing it in Year 12 competes with six new subjects and an Extended Essay. If the criterion breakdown shows your child is secure, buy nothing and revisit in MYP 5 term two.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a single weak MYP criterion usually take to fix?
faqs.answer: For one named criterion in one subject group, four to eight sessions is the realistic range, and that is how we prefer to scope MYP work. Criterion B in Sciences, which is inquiring and designing, is largely a set of teachable conventions: naming controlled variables, writing a testable hypothesis, justifying a method. Those land quickly once taught explicitly. Criterion D, which asks for transfer to an unfamiliar context, takes longer because it needs varied practice. Anyone quoting an exact number before seeing marked work is guessing.

faqs.question: What do the four MYP criteria letters actually mean?
faqs.answer: They differ by subject group, which is the part that catches parents and some tutors out. In Mathematics, A is knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating and D applying maths in real-life contexts. In Sciences, B is inquiring and designing and D is reflecting on the impacts of science. In Language and Literature, A is analysing and D using language. In Individuals and Societies, D is thinking critically. Each is marked out of 8. A tutor who treats D as a generic hard criterion will teach the wrong skill well.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both maths and sciences for the same MYP student?
faqs.answer: Up to a point, and the point is the criteria. The content overlap in MYP 1 to 3 is wide enough that one strong tutor can handle both. From MYP 4 the criteria diverge: Sciences criterion C is processing and evaluating data, while Mathematics criterion C is communicating mathematical reasoning, and they reward different habits. If both subjects sit at a 4 for different reasons, two short blocks with two specialists usually costs less in total than one generalist working through the year.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tutor for the MYP Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Coaching helps; authorship is prohibited. The Personal Project is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal and a report, and it is externally moderated. A tutor can interrogate the goal, push on the quality of journal entries, and give written feedback on drafts the student has written. No tutor should write any part of it, and any service offering a finished project puts the student at risk of a malpractice finding. Keep the drafts: a legitimate improvement trail is visible in them.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to buy MYP support in JBR?
faqs.answer: Get the criterion breakdown from school first, since it costs nothing and removes two sessions of diagnosis. Check whether the school runs a free after-school clinic on that strand. Then buy a defined block of four to eight online one-to-one sessions scoped to the single weakest criterion, rather than a standing weekly booking. At qualified-tutor market rates of AED 150 to 300, a six-session block is a known total. Seventy hours of weekly tutoring across the year at AED 220 is roughly AED 15,000 for one subject.

faqs.question: Do MYP tutoring rates in Dubai rise closer to assessment season?
faqs.answer: The published bands do not change, but availability does, and availability is what sets your real price. From February onward the specialists with strong MYP 5 and Diploma records fill their evening slots, so the tutors still free at 17:00 in April are not the same group who were free in October. Families then pay at the upper end of the band for a narrower choice. Booking a short block in term one or two is the cheaper path, and it also leaves marked tasks in the year for the work to influence.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups do JBR and Marina parents ask about most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, by a wide margin, then Sciences, then Language and Literature. Individuals and Societies arrives later, usually in MYP 4 when criterion D starts to bite. Design and the Arts are the two most often neglected until a folio or process journal is due, even though each carries the same 32 marks as Mathematics. Language Acquisition enquiries cluster around phase movement rather than grades, because a student moved up a phase mid-year can look as though they have stalled when they have not.

faqs.question: How does Arabic fit alongside the MYP in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: It runs in addition to the MYP subject groups. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements due by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited. Instructional time is counted in 40-minute lesson units. Tutoring in these subjects must follow the school's own material, since additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: Is a visiting MYP tutor in a JBR tower better than an online specialist?
faqs.answer: For MYP work, rarely, and the test is mechanical. List what the session involves: shared drafts, a whiteboard for working, a marked task to review, a method to redraft. Then ask which of those needs the tutor physically present. Usually none. What presence costs is the AED 180 to 500 in-home band against AED 150 to 300 online, plus forty minutes of Sheikh Zayed Road each way. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; lessons are one-to-one over live video, which also widens the shortlist to actual MYP specialists.

faqs.question: When should a MYP 5 student start preparing for Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: Term two of MYP 5 is the sensible window, once the school has indicated whether Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation is the likely route. The work is narrow: algebraic fluency without a calculator, function notation, and the language of proof for Analysis and Approaches; statistical vocabulary and calculator technique for Applications and Interpretation. Six to ten weeks of focused sessions covers it for most students. Starting in the summer before Year 12 also works, but competes with a holiday, and starting in Year 12 competes with the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: What happens to our JBR sessions during Ramadan and the summer?
faqs.answer: Timings move and the slot stays. During Ramadan, school days shorten and most families shift sessions to a post-Iftar window, which online delivery handles without renegotiating a tutor's travel. Over the summer, some families pause and hold the slot, while others use July and August for transition work such as MYP 5 to Diploma algebra, which is easier without a school timetable competing. If you travel between Dubai and another time zone, the session follows you as long as the clock difference is workable for both sides.

faqs.question: How do we check a MYP tutor is permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first paid session. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system under the service 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted figure with caution. A tuition centre with premises needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit instead.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jbr.closingBody: An IB MYP tutor in JBR should be a short, scoped purchase, not a standing order that runs to June. intro.heading: What an MYP report is telling you, and why it does not feel like one
paragraphs: A parent in Jebel Ali who grew up with percentages opens an MYP report and finds something else entirely. Four letters per subject - A, B, C and D - each carrying a mark out of eight, and a final grade from 1 to 7 derived from the total. No percentage, no class rank, and a comment that describes the criteria rather than the child. The natural reaction is to ask whether 5 out of 8 is good, and the honest answer is that it depends which criterion in which subject.

That is not an evasion. The four criteria assess genuinely different things, and they differ by subject group. In the sciences, one criterion covers knowledge and understanding while another covers inquiring and designing; in mathematics, one covers investigating patterns and another covers applying mathematics in real-life contexts; in language and literature, the criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. A 5 in a criterion about designing an investigation describes a different gap from a 5 in a criterion about knowledge recall.

So the first useful thing a tutor does for an MYP family is read the report properly: find the descriptor for the criterion that scored lowest, in that subject, and compare it against the work the student actually produced. That single comparison usually identifies the gap more precisely than a term of general subject practice, because the descriptors are specific about what the next band requires.

The second useful thing is to look at the whole profile rather than the lowest number. A student scoring well on knowledge criteria and poorly on inquiry or communication criteria across several subjects does not have a subject problem; they have a transferable skills problem, and it will follow them into the Diploma where it costs more. The MYP's approaches-to-learning framework exists precisely to name those skills, and it is rarely used by families as the diagnostic tool it is.

Jebel Ali's geography is why this page also talks about delivery. The district sits at the industrial western edge of Dubai, with its residential communities spread through Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Green Community, Dubai South and Emaar South. The schools running an IB continuum here are few, so the local supply of tutors who have ever read an MYP criterion report is thin. IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

What follows is the criteria explained by subject group, how to read a report, what the Personal Project actually requires, the approaches-to-learning skills worth working on directly, the step into the Diploma or IGCSE, and the AED market bands with their sources.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jebel-ali.programmesIntro: The MYP spans five years and changes character as it goes. The requests we receive from this catchment cluster in three places, and they are different problems with different remedies.

programmes.name: MYP 1 to 3, the early years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four lettered criteria out of eight. Inquiry-led teaching organised around global contexts and key concepts, with interdisciplinary units linking subjects. There is no external examination, so the record of these three years is a sequence of criterion judgements rather than test scores.
programmes.countryNote: This is where gaps form invisibly. A student can progress through MYP 2 and 3 with reasonable criterion scores while arithmetic fluency and writing stamina quietly fail to develop, because neither is examined under time pressure. Families in Al Furjan and Green Community who intervene here spend a term; those who wait until MYP 5 spend a year.

programmes.name: MYP 4 and 5, the decision years
programmes.description: Subject choices narrow, the Personal Project arrives in MYP 5, and some schools enter students for optional on-screen eAssessments and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate. These two years also carry the decision about what comes next: the IB Diploma, the Career-related Programme, or a move to an IGCSE and A Level route.
programmes.countryNote: In this catchment the decision is a live one rather than a formality, because both IB and UK-curriculum sixth forms are available locally. That makes MYP 4 the right year to find out whether a student's criterion profile predicts Diploma success, and to work on the specific skills the Diploma will assume.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent project of the student's own choosing, with a product or outcome, a process journal and a report, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight. It is the MYP's culminating piece of independent work and the closest thing in the programme to the Diploma's Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project is where MYP 5 students in this catchment lose marks they did not need to lose, and almost always for the same reason: the process journal is reconstructed near the deadline rather than kept as the work happened. The criteria reward evidence of process, and a journal written in retrospect cannot supply it.

programmes.name: What the MYP leads into
programmes.description: The IB Diploma takes six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, graded out of 45. The alternative within this catchment is an IGCSE and A Level route at a UK-curriculum school. Both make assumptions about what an MYP student arrives able to do.
programmes.countryNote: The gap that matters is not content. It is notation discipline, timed written work and formal mathematical fluency, none of which the MYP requires at speed. Students who were strong on investigation criteria frequently find the first Diploma term harder than their MYP record predicted, and that is a preparation problem rather than a capability one.

sections.heading: Reading a criterion report: what 5 out of 8 actually tells you
paragraphs: An MYP criterion mark is a judgement against a written descriptor, not a percentage of questions answered correctly. Each criterion is marked out of eight, and the eight marks are grouped into bands, each band described in words. A 5 means the student's work matched the description of that band. The descriptor for the band above says, in specific language, what the work would need to do differently.

That is the whole diagnostic, and it is far more useful than a percentage would be. A percentage tells you how much was wrong; a descriptor tells you what kind of thing was missing. If the next band asks for a general rule to be justified rather than stated, the student knows exactly what to add. If it asks for evaluation of sources rather than summary, the same. Families who ask the school for the descriptors rather than for a clearer comment usually find the answer immediately.

The four marks together total 32 and are converted into a 1 to 7 subject grade using published boundaries, which is why two students with the same final grade can have quite different profiles. One may be even across all four criteria; the other may be strong on knowledge and weak on inquiry. The second student has the more urgent problem, because inquiry and communication skills transfer into every subject and into the Diploma.

So the useful first question is not which subject is lowest but whether the same criterion type is low in several subjects at once. Low knowledge marks in two subjects is two content problems. Low communication or inquiry marks in four subjects is one skills problem wearing four costumes, and it is both cheaper and more valuable to fix.

sections.heading: The eight subject groups, and where each one quietly loses marks
paragraphs: The MYP's eight subject groups each have four criteria, and the criteria are subject-specific even where the names sound similar. That specificity is why a tutor who has taught the subject but never read its MYP descriptors will miss the actual gap. They will teach content, which is usually not the problem.

Mathematics is the clearest example. A student can be fluent and accurate and still score poorly on the investigating-patterns criterion, because that criterion asks for a general rule to be found, justified and then tested against further cases. Arriving at the right answer is not the task. Similarly, the real-life-contexts criterion asks for a model to be applied and its limitations discussed, and a correct calculation with no discussion of the model scores below what the student knows.

In the sciences, the design criterion rewards a method another person could replicate: variables identified, controls stated operationally, apparatus specified. Many students write a method that works for them and would not work for a stranger, and lose marks they never see as marks. In Design and the Arts, the process journal is assessed directly, so a student who works hard and documents nothing has done the work and not the assessment.

In language and literature the recurring loss is paraphrase instead of analysis, which is worth naming early because it is the same habit that costs marks on Diploma English Paper 1 three years later. In individuals and societies it is source summary instead of source evaluation. In language acquisition it is often not a weakness at all but a phase placement issue, where a student sitting in the wrong phase reads as struggling.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the journal that decides it
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight, with a product or outcome, a process journal and a report. It is the MYP's culminating independent work, and it is the closest thing the programme offers to the Diploma's Extended Essay in both character and failure mode.

The failure mode is the journal. All three criteria draw their evidence from the process, and a journal written in the fortnight before the deadline cannot evidence a process that was not recorded as it happened. Students reconstruct plausibly, the report reads smoothly, and the marks fall short because what the criteria reward - decisions made, obstacles met, approaches changed - has been smoothed into a narrative. Keeping even a rough weekly entry from the start outperforms an elegant retrospective account.

The second failure is scope. A goal that cannot be achieved in the available time with the available resources produces a project that is either unfinished or quietly downgraded halfway through, and in both cases the reflecting criterion suffers because the student is defending a decision rather than evaluating a process. Narrowing the goal early is the highest-value intervention a tutor can make, and it takes one session.

The boundary is the same as everywhere in the IB and it is worth restating for a 15-year-old's first big independent piece. A tutor may question the goal, explain what each criterion rewards, teach a skill the project needs, discuss how to keep a usable journal, and read the draft report against the descriptors. A tutor may not plan it, make it, write it or edit it to completion. Every word of the report must be the student's own.
bullets: Keep a rough journal weekly from the start; retrospective accounts lose marks
Narrow the goal until it is achievable with the time and resources available
Record decisions and obstacles, not just progress

Every word of the report must be typed by the student

sections.heading: Approaches to learning: the skills behind a repeating low mark
paragraphs: The MYP names five categories of approaches-to-learning skills - communication, social, self-management, research and thinking - and expects them to be taught across subjects rather than in a timetabled slot. Because they belong to nobody in particular, they are the skills most likely to go unaddressed, and they are the usual explanation for a criterion profile that is low in the same way across several subjects.

Self-management is the one that shows up most in this catchment. A student who cannot plan a two-week task backwards from its deadline produces rushed work in every subject, and the criteria notice. The fix is not a conversation about effort; it is a repeated exercise in mapping a real school task backwards, with the student doing the mapping, until they do it unprompted.

Research skills come second. Finding sources is easy; judging them is not, and the thinking-critically and investigating criteria across several subject groups reward judgement. A student who collects six sources and summarises each in turn has researched and not evaluated. Practising evaluation on the student's own current assignments, rather than on a worked example, is what makes it transfer.

Communication is the third, and it is the one with the longest tail. A student whose good thinking is hard to follow loses marks in the MYP and goes on losing them in the Diploma, where structure is marked explicitly in almost every subject. Working on structure in MYP 3 or 4 is cheap. Working on it in the second Diploma year, alongside six subjects and the core, is not.

sections.heading: From the MYP into the Diploma or into IGCSE: the real gap
paragraphs: Families in this catchment face a genuine choice at 16, because both routes exist locally: the IB Diploma at one of the area's IB schools, or an IGCSE and A Level path at a UK-curriculum school. The MYP prepares students well for one half of either and leaves a predictable gap in the other half.

What the MYP builds well is inquiry, independent work, extended writing with a purpose and comfort with criteria-based assessment. A student coming out of a good MYP programme is usually better at designing an investigation and writing a reflective evaluation than a student arriving from a purely examined system. That is real and it pays in the Diploma's internally assessed components and in the Extended Essay.

What the MYP does not require is speed under timed conditions, formal mathematical notation, or recall at volume. There is no external paper in most MYP years, so a student may reach MYP 5 having never written anything substantial against a clock. Both the Diploma and IGCSE assume that from the first term, and the first set of Diploma or Year 10 results frequently reflects the shock rather than the ability.

The practical preparation is therefore narrow and specific: timed written work, formal notation discipline in mathematics, and recall practice. None of it needs to wait for a school to teach it. A MYP 5 student in Al Furjan or Green Community who spends a term writing to a clock and rearranging equations by hand arrives at the Diploma with the gap already closed, and that is the single most useful thing tutoring does at this stage.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs in Dubai, and what is worth paying for
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures, read October 2026 and attributed to whoever published them. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 online. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors advertising to AED 500. Specialists are published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650.

The MYP is the stage where the entry band deserves a fairer hearing than it gets elsewhere. For MYP 1 to 3, where the task is often arithmetic fluency, reading stamina or sitting down to work at all, a capable and patient tutor at the lower end of the market can be genuinely good value. The expensive specialist adds less here than they will in two years.

What changes the calculation is criteria literacy. A tutor who has never read an MYP descriptor will teach content, and content is frequently not what the report is pointing at. For MYP 4 and 5, for the Personal Project, and for any report showing a repeated low criterion across subjects, the specialist band is where the useful people are, because the work is interpretive rather than instructional.

Read it by the term, which is how school deadlines actually arrive. Dubai rate guidance estimates one weekly hour at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support - so a three-month term comes to AED 720-1,800, AED 1,800-3,600 and AED 3,000-6,000 or more respectively. Lined up that way the trade is plain: one term at the specialist end costs about what several terms cost at the entry end, and it is worth paying only where reading the criterion is the real problem rather than the content behind it. Advertised packages sit between the two, around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, the second of which is pricing the drive out to Jebel Ali at least as much as the teaching. None of these are IB Gram prices; our fee is quoted after the free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one for an MYP student, with the limitations named
paragraphs: The format suits MYP work because so much of it is document work: a criterion descriptor beside a piece of the student's own writing, a process journal read together, a method rewritten so a stranger could follow it. A shared screen with both people annotating is better for that than a single paper copy across a table.

The age range is where honesty is needed. For MYP 4 and 5, online one-to-one works essentially as well as in person. For MYP 1 and 2, it depends entirely on the child. An 11-year-old who will settle at a desk and engage with a screen does fine; one who needs an adult physically present to begin and to stay started does better with someone in the room, and no amount of good teaching compensates for that.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and this page states that rather than leaving it to be discovered, because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote. If your MYP 1 child needs a person in the room, hire locally - and ask the tutor whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first lesson.

The other practical limitations: a weak home connection shortens the hour regardless of the clock, and a shared study space, common in Discovery Gardens apartments, undermines any lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room. Both are worth testing before committing to a term rather than discovering in week three.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and how to start
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, and the UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

One arrangement to avoid: paid private tuition from your own child's class teacher. The permit carries a code of conduct, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff are reported as barring paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Dubai sits under KHDA rather than ADEK, but the principle is the same and the permit's conditions apply across the country.

What we do not claim: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, a KHDA Educational Services Permit being a licence issued to training institutes with physical premises that we neither hold nor occupy. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE or IB accreditation or partnership, publish no self-asserted ratings, promise no grade or criterion improvement, and quote no statistic without its source and date. On the MYP specifically, we do not write, rewrite or complete any part of a Personal Project or any assessed task.

To start, send the subject group, the year, the school, and a photograph of the most recent criterion report - ideally with one piece of the student's marked work. The report alone tells us which criterion is low; the work tells us why. A specialist then teaches a free one-to-one trial lesson online, built on that work, and writes up what the criterion descriptor and the work together showed. The note is yours whether or not you continue, and if no suitable specialist has a slot at your hour we say so and offer alternatives.

faqs.question: Is 5 out of 8 a good MYP criterion mark?
faqs.answer: It depends which criterion in which subject, and that is a real answer rather than an evasion. Each criterion is marked against a written descriptor, and a 5 means the work matched one band's description. The useful step is to read the descriptor for the band above: it states specifically what the work would need to do differently, whether that is justifying a general rule, writing a replicable method, or evaluating sources rather than summarising them. Ask the school for the descriptors rather than for a clearer comment.

faqs.question: How do the 32 criterion marks turn into a 1 to 7 MYP subject grade?
faqs.answer: Because MYP assessment is criterion-referenced rather than norm-referenced. Each subject has four criteria, each marked out of eight against a written descriptor, totalling 32, which is then converted into a 1 to 7 subject grade using published boundaries. A percentage would tell you how much was wrong; a descriptor tells you what kind of thing was missing, which is more actionable. The consequence is that two students with the same final grade can have very different profiles, and the profile matters more than the grade.

faqs.question: My child is strong in maths but scores low on investigating patterns. Why?
faqs.answer: Because that criterion is not assessing calculation. It asks for a pattern to be explored, a general rule to be found and expressed, that rule to be justified, and then tested against further cases. A fluent student who reaches the correct answer quickly has often done none of those four things in writing. The fix is specific rather than remedial: practise producing the general rule and the justification as written work, every time, until it becomes the expected shape of an answer rather than an optional extra.

faqs.question: What does the MYP Personal Project actually need from a student?
faqs.answer: A product or outcome, a process journal and a report, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight. The journal is the critical piece, because all three criteria draw their evidence from the process. A journal reconstructed in the fortnight before the deadline reads smoothly and cannot evidence decisions, obstacles and changes of approach that were never recorded. A rough weekly entry kept from the start outperforms an elegant retrospective account every time.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without doing it for them?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful help is mostly questioning rather than teaching. A tutor can challenge whether the goal is achievable with the time and resources available, explain what each criterion rewards, teach a specific skill the project needs, show the student how to keep a journal that will actually evidence their process, and read the draft report against the descriptors. A tutor cannot plan it, make it, write it or edit it to completion. Every word of the report must be typed by the student.

faqs.question: My child's criterion marks are low in the same way across four subjects. What is that?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly one approaches-to-learning problem rather than four subject problems. The MYP names five skill categories - communication, social, self-management, research and thinking - and because they are taught across subjects rather than in a timetabled slot, they are the skills most likely to go unaddressed. Self-management and research skills are the usual culprits: a student who cannot plan a two-week task backwards produces rushed work everywhere. One skills tutor is both cheaper and more useful than four subject tutors for this.

faqs.question: How well does the MYP prepare a student for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Well in one half and predictably poorly in the other. The MYP builds inquiry, independent work, extended purposeful writing and comfort with criteria-based assessment, all of which pay in the Diploma's internally assessed components and the Extended Essay. What it does not require is writing against a clock, formal mathematical notation at speed, or recall at volume, and both the Diploma and IGCSE assume all three from the first term. A term of timed writing and manual manipulation in MYP 5 closes most of the gap.

faqs.question: Should a Jebel Ali MYP 5 student choose the Diploma or an A Level route?
faqs.answer: Both are available in this catchment without moving house, which makes it a genuine decision rather than a formality. The criterion profile is useful evidence: a student who scores well on inquiry, communication and reflection criteria usually suits the Diploma, where internally assessed components and the Extended Essay reward exactly those. A student strong on knowledge criteria and weaker on the others may do better with three or four A Levels in depth. Read each school's published entry requirements before deciding, and treat predicted grades as the constraint they are.

faqs.question: Does my child need to sit the MYP eAssessments?
faqs.answer: That depends on the school rather than on your child. Some schools enter MYP 5 students for optional on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate, and others do not. Ask the school directly whether it enters candidates, for which subjects, and when the components fall, because the answer changes the shape of the MYP 5 year considerably. Where a school does enter students, the preparation is largely timed on-screen writing, which is the same skill the Diploma will assume afterwards.

faqs.question: Why does my child's language acquisition mark look weak?
faqs.answer: Before assuming a weakness, check the phase. Language acquisition in the MYP runs across phases rather than year groups, and a student placed in a phase above their current level reads as struggling when they are simply misplaced, while one placed below coasts and stops progressing. Phase placement is a school decision and it can be reviewed. This comes up frequently in the apartment communities in this catchment, where home languages are very mixed and a child's spoken fluency and written accuracy can sit at different phases.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring suitable for an MYP 1 student in Jebel Ali?
faqs.answer: It depends on the child, and we would rather say so than take every booking. For MYP 4 and 5 online one-to-one works essentially as well as in person, because the work is document-based: a descriptor beside a piece of writing, a journal read together. For MYP 1 and 2, a child who will settle at a desk and engage with a screen does fine, while one who needs an adult physically present to begin and stay started does better in person. IB Gram runs no home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: What should we work on between MYP 3 and MYP 4?
faqs.answer: Fluency and structure, in that order, because both are cheap now and expensive later. Arithmetic and algebraic manipulation done by hand, at speed, accurately, since the MYP does not require it under time pressure and everything after the MYP does. Then structure in extended writing: planning a piece before writing it, so that good thinking becomes thinking a reader can follow. Communication marks that are low in MYP 3 tend to stay low through the Diploma, where structure is marked explicitly in nearly every subject.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor at once in the MYP?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and sometimes none at all in the sense parents expect. If the criterion profile shows one subject genuinely low on knowledge criteria, that is one subject tutor. If the same criterion type is low across several subjects, the right purchase is a skills block rather than several subject tutors, and it will improve all of them. Starting with three MYP subject tutors is the commonest overspend we see from this catchment, and the criterion report usually shows why it was unnecessary.

faqs.question: Do MYP sessions need to change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: The hour moves and the content usually does not. School hours shorten during Ramadan and households reorganise their evening around iftar, so a weekday 5pm slot typically becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. For MYP students the thing worth protecting is the writing habit rather than the content pace: a shorter session that still produces a written piece holds more than a longer discussion. Because nobody is travelling to your address, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation of a commute.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jebel-ali.closingHeading: Send the criterion report and one piece of work
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jebel-ali.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB MYP tutor in Jebel Ali, the two documents that matter are the criterion report and one piece of your child's marked work. The report shows which of the four criteria is low; the work shows why, when read against the published descriptor for the band above. A specialist in that subject group reads both, tells you whether this is a subject gap or an approaches-to-learning pattern repeating across subjects, and teaches a free one-to-one trial lesson online at a Gulf Standard Time hour that works from Jebel Ali, Al Furjan, Green Community or The Sustainable City.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jlt.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Middle Years Programme subjects to JLT families over live video. When you speak to one, ask which subject group and which criteria they have assessed against, and whether they are willing to work from your school's task-specific clarifications rather than from a generic scheme.

intro.heading: The Middle Years Programme has no content list, which is why this search keeps failing
paragraphs: A parent in Jumeirah Lakes Towers whose child is in MYP 3 or MYP 4 types the obvious search and gets a wall of pages promising expert MYP tutors. Then the conversations begin, and something does not add up. One tutor talks about topics the school has not mentioned. Another sends a worksheet that looks like a British Year 9 textbook page. A third asks what level your child is at and seems confused by the answer. The parent concludes that nobody in Dubai really knows the programme, and often gives up.

The misunderstanding is structural rather than anybody's fault. The Middle Years Programme does not publish a content syllabus the way Cambridge publishes 0580 or Pearson publishes 4MA1. It publishes subject-group guides that set out aims, objectives, four assessment criteria per subject, and a framework of key concepts, related concepts and global contexts. The school then writes its own units within that framework. Two IB World Schools a short drive apart can teach entirely different content in MYP 4 sciences and both be completely correct.

So a tutor cannot know your child's syllabus, because your child's syllabus is a set of documents held by the school. What a good MYP tutor can know is the assessment architecture, which is fixed and public: eight subject groups, four criteria each, every criterion marked out of eight, and a conversion from a criterion total out of thirty-two into a grade from one to seven. They can know what Criterion B rewards in sciences and how that differs from Criterion B in mathematics. They can know why a student who understands the content scores five rather than seven, which is almost always a criterion-language problem rather than a knowledge problem.

That reframes the hiring question usefully. Instead of asking whether a tutor knows the MYP syllabus, ask whether they will read your school's task sheet, the task-specific clarifications attached to it, and your child's last marked assessment with the criterion bands circled. A tutor who says yes to that and can then explain what the circled band means is worth more than one who claims familiarity with content nobody outside your school has seen. A tutor who refuses, or who immediately suggests a textbook, has told you what you need to know.

There is a geographical wrinkle for this community. JLT has nurseries and early-years provision but no IB school of its own, so MYP students here travel to Emirates Hills, The Meadows, Al Barsha, Al Sufouh or further, and the schools they travel to run different unit plans. That means a tutor who worked successfully with a neighbour's child may be starting from scratch with yours. The rest of this page covers the criteria by subject group, how the grade is actually calculated, the Personal Project, the step into the Diploma, what MYP tuition costs in dirhams, and the honest position on which subject groups we can staff.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jlt.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme sits in the middle of a continuum, and what a tutor should be doing depends on which end of it your child is nearer. The notes below describe each stage as JLT families actually meet it, including the two routes out at sixteen.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary with no external examinations and no prescribed scheme. Learning is organised through transdisciplinary units and reported against descriptive learning outcomes rather than percentages. Mathematics and literacy sequences vary more between schools than they would in a British primary, because the units are written locally within the programme framework.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving a child from a Dubai primary into MYP 1 often find the first reports hard to read, because descriptive bands replace the marks they are used to. The useful tutoring work at this transition is not content acceleration. It is teaching the child to read a rubric and to recognise what a task is asking for, which is the skill the whole of the Middle Years Programme then assesses.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, physical and health education, and design. Each is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project, and schools may optionally enter students for on-screen eAssessment leading to the IB MYP Certificate.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the variation between schools is wide. Some run the full five years with interdisciplinary units and a formal Personal Project cycle; others compress MYP 4 and 5 around IGCSE entries and treat the criteria more lightly. Ask your school's coordinator which model it follows before hiring anyone, because it changes what a tutor should be working on in MYP 4.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma with six subject groups at Standard or Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment moves to external examinations with internally assessed components, which is a different kind of assessment from anything the Middle Years Programme asks for.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is the one JLT families most often need help with, and it is not a content gap. Middle Years assessment rewards investigation, process and reflection; Diploma assessment rewards accuracy and speed under timed conditions. A student with strong criterion grades can be caught out by the first Diploma mock purely because nothing in MYP 5 trained them to finish a paper against the clock.

programmes.name: The sideways move to IGCSE
programmes.description: Several Dubai schools move students from the Middle Years framework into Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses for the last two years before sixteen, either alongside the MYP or in place of it. Those courses do have prescribed content, syllabus codes and terminal examinations.
programmes.countryNote: For a JLT family, this move is the one that most changes a tutor's job. A student who has been assessed on criteria for three years suddenly meets a specification with named content and a mark scheme per question. The tutoring need flips from criterion language to content coverage and examination technique, and a tutor who is good at one is not automatically good at the other.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jlt.subjectsIntro: The list below gives each MYP subject group its four criteria and the place marks most often go missing. Use it to name a criterion when you ask for help, because a criterion is something a tutor can work on and a subject name is not.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5, four criteria out of eight each
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B is where most marks go missing: students write a method without a testable hypothesis or without identifying which variables are controlled. Criterion D is the one students treat as an afterthought and it carries the same eight marks as the rest.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5, standard and extended from MYP 4
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B asks the student to find a general rule and then justify it, and justification is where the marks sit. Criterion C penalises correct mathematics presented without notation, units or a line of reasoning a reader can follow.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5, four criteria out of eight each
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students who read well lose marks on Criterion B because an essay has no visible structure, and on Criterion D because register and vocabulary are not adapted to the task. Analysis means showing how an effect is created, not stating that it exists, and that distinction is teachable in a few sessions.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5, four criteria out of eight each
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Criterion D is the hardest to score and the least taught: it rewards evaluating sources, recognising perspective and weighing competing interpretations. Students who write accurate narrative history and no evaluation sit at a five whatever their knowledge.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5, taught in phases rather than year groups
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, each with its own criterion. Phases run across year groups, so a child in MYP 3 may be in phase two or phase four of Arabic, French or Spanish. Marks are lost when a student produces accurate language that does not address the specific task purpose or audience named in the prompt.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5, four criteria out of eight each
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The design cycle is the assessment, so a beautiful final product with thin research documentation scores poorly. Students routinely underweight Criterion A, where existing products must be analysed, and Criterion D, where the solution must be tested against the student's own design specification.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. The process journal carries much of the mark, which surprises families whose child is talented in performance or production. Documentation of the development, with artistic intention stated and revised, is where a strong practical student most often loses two or three criterion marks.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5, four criteria out of eight each
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Two of the four criteria are written work, which is the detail parents are most often unaware of. A strong athlete can sit at a four because the planning and reflection components have not been taken seriously.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project with a goal, a process journal and a report, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It is the single largest piece of independent work a student has produced to that point and the one most likely to be left late. Support must be process coaching; the goal, the work and the report are the student's own.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units that combine two or more subject groups and are assessed against their own interdisciplinary criteria: disciplinary grounding, synthesising, and reflecting. Students often treat them as a lighter version of two subjects, which is exactly what the criteria do not reward, and the marks are reported separately on the school report.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning and global contexts
subjects.description: The skills framework covering thinking, research, communication, social and self-management skills, plus the six global contexts that frame every statement of inquiry. These are not examined directly and they determine how tasks are worded, so a student who cannot read the vocabulary of a task sheet loses marks across every subject at once.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and Dubai Media City
