sections.heading: What a tutor can honestly claim to know before seeing your school's documents
paragraphs: Separate the fixed from the local and the hiring question becomes answerable. The fixed part of the Middle Years Programme is substantial. Eight subject groups. Four assessment criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. A set of named objectives per subject group that the criteria are drawn from. Six global contexts. A framework of key concepts and related concepts. A requirement for a Personal Project in the final year, and a set of approaches-to-learning skill categories. All of that is public, consistent between schools, and knowable by a tutor who has taught the programme.

The local part is everything a parent assumes is the syllabus. Which topics MYP 3 sciences covers and in which order. Whether MYP 4 mathematics is taught as standard or extended and where the split happens. How many summative tasks a unit carries. What the task-specific clarifications say, which is the document that turns a generic criterion descriptor into the thing your child is actually marked against. Whether the school enters students for on-screen eAssessment at the end of MYP 5 or reports internally.

This is why the two useful questions to ask a prospective tutor are not about content. The first is whether they will teach from your school's task sheet and rubric rather than from their own material. The second is whether they can explain, from your child's last marked assessment, why the criterion band is where it is. A tutor who answers both well is useful in any MYP school in Dubai. A tutor who claims to know your MYP syllabus has either misunderstood the programme or is telling you what they think you want to hear.

The table sets out the division explicitly, so you can take it into a conversation. It is also worth asking the school for two documents before you hire anybody: the current unit planner summary and the task-specific clarifications for the next assessed task. Most Dubai coordinators will provide both. With those in hand, a good tutor is productive in the first session instead of the third.

sections.heading: How thirty-two criterion marks become a one-to-seven, and why the grade surprised you
paragraphs: The most common Middle Years conversation we have with JLT parents is about arithmetic. A child comes home with criterion marks of six, five, six and five across the four criteria in a subject, the parent reads that as mostly good, and the report shows a grade of five. Nothing has gone wrong. The four criterion marks are added to give a total out of thirty-two, and that total is converted to a grade from one to seven using a boundary table.

The boundaries are not evenly spaced, which is where the surprise comes from. The widely used general boundaries place a total of twenty-eight to thirty-two at grade seven, twenty-four to twenty-seven at six, nineteen to twenty-three at five, fifteen to eighteen at four, ten to fourteen at three, six to nine at two and below that at one. Confirm the table your own school applies, because schools report against the published framework but collect and combine criterion marks on their own cycle.

Two consequences follow, and both are practical. First, a grade seven needs an average of seven across all four criteria, not strength in two of them. A student at eight, eight, five and five totals twenty-six and reports as a six, while a student at seven, seven, six and six totals twenty-six as well. Evenness is worth more than peaks, which is the opposite of how most students allocate effort. Second, the cheapest grade movement available is almost always the weakest criterion, and in most subjects that is the written, reflective or evaluative one.

This is also why asking for help with mathematics or with sciences is the wrong request. Ask for help with Criterion B in mathematics, or with Criterion D in individuals and societies, because that is a specific, trainable, bounded piece of work. A tutor can take a student from a five to a seven on a single criterion in a handful of sessions by teaching the band descriptors explicitly and having the student rewrite their own marked work against them. Doing that across the subject takes a year.

sections.heading: Criterion B and Criterion D: the two that cost JLT students the most
paragraphs: Across the Middle Years enquiries that reach us from this part of Dubai, two criteria account for most of the gap between what a student knows and what the report says. They sit in different places in different subjects, but the pattern repeats with enough regularity to be worth naming.

The first is the investigation criterion. In sciences, Criterion B asks the student to design an investigation: a testable hypothesis with a reason, named independent and dependent variables, controlled variables identified, and a method another person could follow. Students write the method and skip the rest, because the method is the part that feels like the work. In mathematics, Criterion B asks for a general rule found from a pattern and then justified, and justification is routinely replaced with a second example. In design, Criterion A asks for analysis of existing products, which is regularly replaced with a description of them.

The second is the reflective or critical criterion, which carries the same eight marks as the rest and receives a fraction of the effort. Criterion D in sciences asks the student to discuss the impacts of science with reference to a specific context. Criterion D in individuals and societies asks for evaluation of sources and perspectives. Criterion D in design asks for the solution to be tested against the student's own specification. In each case the student who writes accurate content and no evaluation is capped in the low fives whatever they know.

Both are faster to fix than content gaps, which is the encouraging part. The work is to read the band descriptors aloud with the student, show them a seven-band response to a task they have already attempted, and have them rewrite their own answer against the descriptor rather than against a model answer. Three or four sessions of that on one criterion, with the school's own clarifications in front of both people, reliably moves a band. It is also the kind of work that transfers: a student who learns to evaluate in one subject starts doing it in the others without being asked.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: In MYP 5 every student completes a Personal Project: an independent piece of work with a goal they choose, a process journal kept throughout, and a report assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It is externally moderated, it is the largest independent project most fifteen-year-olds have attempted, and it is the item JLT families contact us about latest in the year.

Three things go wrong, reliably. The goal is too large or too vague to evidence, so the report cannot show achievement against it. The process journal is written retrospectively in the last fortnight, which produces a report with nothing concrete to reflect on, and the criteria can tell. And the report is treated as a write-up of the product rather than as the assessed piece it actually is, so a student with an impressive outcome scores modestly.

Legitimate support addresses all three without touching the work. A tutor can discuss whether a goal is achievable and evidenceable before it is registered. A tutor can set journal habits in the first weeks so the evidence exists later. A tutor can teach the criteria, read a draft and give written feedback on it. What a tutor must never do is write the project, produce the artefact, or rewrite a paragraph into its final form. The project must be the student's own work, and the IB's academic-honesty rules make the consequences of anything else serious for the student rather than for the tutor.

We put that boundary in writing at the start of any Personal Project support, listing what was discussed and what feedback was given, so that the school can see the help was legitimate if it is ever asked. That is not caution for its own sake. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, and a parent shopping in this category should know that the honest version of this service looks different and says so.

sections.heading: From MYP into the Diploma, or sideways into IGCSE
paragraphs: At sixteen a JLT student leaves the Middle Years framework in one of two directions, and each creates a different tutoring need. Knowing which one is coming changes what should happen in MYP 4 and MYP 5, which is a year or two before most families think about it.

The move into the Diploma is a change in the kind of assessment rather than a content cliff. Middle Years tasks are often extended, researched and completed over days, with criteria rewarding process and reflection. Diploma assessment is largely examination-based: accuracy, speed, command terms and a mark scheme per question. A student with strong criterion grades can be rattled by the first Diploma mock because nothing in MYP trained them to finish a paper under time pressure. The preparation that helps is timed practice in MYP 5, not more content.

The sideways move into IGCSE is the sharper change for most students. Suddenly there is a specification with named content, a syllabus code, a tiering decision in some subjects and a terminal examination. Students who have been assessed against criteria for three years often find the first IGCSE mock easier in style and harder in volume, because content coverage now matters in a way it did not. A tutor who is excellent at criterion language is not automatically the right person for 0580 or 4MA1 content coverage.

The specific subject risks are worth naming. Mathematics is the big one: MYP standard mathematics does not cover everything IGCSE Extended expects, and the gap is in algebraic fluency rather than in topics. Sciences transfer reasonably well on content and poorly on examination technique. Language and literature transfers well. Design and arts transfer least cleanly, because the assessment architecture is so different. The table sets out where to look.

sections.heading: Who actually tutors the Middle Years Programme, and the honest supply answer
paragraphs: Here is the part of the question that deserves a direct answer. The pool of tutors who have genuinely assessed against MYP criteria is smaller than the pool who have taught IGCSE or Diploma content, and it is smaller still in the subject groups that are mostly written: individuals and societies, design, arts and the language acquisition phases. That is not a Dubai problem specifically. It follows from the programme being taught in fewer schools and assessed internally, so fewer teachers accumulate the experience.

What this means in practice is that the right question changes by subject. For mathematics and sciences, there is reasonable depth of tutors who know the criteria and can work from a school rubric, and a specialist is usually available in a normal week. For language and literature, the pool is decent and the work is transferable from other written criteria. For design, arts and physical and health education, the pool is thin, and a family asking for help there should expect either a wait or a tutor from an adjacent subject who will work from the rubric carefully rather than from experience of that exact criterion set.

We would rather say that plainly than place a mismatched tutor. Where the exact MYP subject-group specialist is unavailable, we will say so and offer one of three things: a different time when a specialist is free, a tutor from an adjacent subject group who is explicit about working from your school's clarifications, or a recommendation to focus the money on the transferable written criteria instead, which lifts grades across several subjects at once.

Nothing in this section is a statistic. It is a description of what we can staff, stated because no competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-local delivery behind a phone number. sections.heading: What Middle Years tuition costs in Dubai, and what you can verify yourself
paragraphs: Every number in this section is one you can check in about ten minutes, which is the point of publishing it. Open each provider's own pricing page, note the figure and the date you read it, and you will have better information than any aggregated claim. The figures below were read in October 2026 and belong to the providers named, not to us.

EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialist work at AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium named tutors at BartyED quoted at AED 650. In-home one-to-one is published at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by home tutors generally, with travel inside the rate. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 for a budget weekly hour, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work.

Middle Years work usually sits below the Diploma examination-year bands, because the tasks are not examinations and the hours needed are fewer and more targeted. A criterion block of six sessions is a modest, knowable total. That makes it unusually good value compared with Diploma support, and it is also the stage where improvement compounds: a student who learns to read a rubric at thirteen carries that skill into every subject and into the Diploma.

Two context figures help frame the spend. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula. And KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion out of AED 2.5 billion in total. A stable fee year is the right year to spend a modest amount on the assessment skills that pay off in the Diploma.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and starting from a JLT tower
paragraphs: Before the practical steps, two rules worth knowing. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, with no fee stated and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published.

A separate rule matters for a Middle Years family in particular, because the obvious tutor is often a teacher at the child's own school. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Check the current policy document before relying on this, and do not build a plan around that arrangement. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not approved, accredited or licensed by the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education.

Starting is short. Send the subject group, the year or MYP level, the criterion where the band is lowest, the school, and two windows that work after your child is actually home. Attach the school's task sheet and the last marked assessment if you can get them. Those two documents do more for the first session than any amount of description, because they contain the task-specific clarifications your child is marked against.

Then take the free trial lesson. It runs in full, online, with no payment and no card details. Watch whether the tutor opens your child's own task sheet or their own worksheet, and ask them to say which criterion they would target first and why. If they cannot answer that from the marked assessment in front of them, they are not the person for a Middle Years brief. Review the arrangement every four to six weeks against criterion bands rather than against how the sessions felt, and stop or change when a band has moved.

process.title: Get two documents from the school
process.description: Ask for the current unit planner summary and the task-specific clarifications for the next assessed task. Most Dubai coordinators provide both without difficulty. With them in hand a tutor is productive in the first session rather than the third, because the clarifications are what your child is actually marked against.

process.title: Name the subject group and the criterion
process.description: Not help with sciences, but help with Criterion B in sciences. Add the MYP level or year group, the school and the most recent criterion marks. A criterion is a bounded, trainable piece of work; a subject name is a year-long project, and the difference shows up in both cost and result.

process.title: Send the last marked assessment
process.description: With the criterion bands circled by the teacher if possible. Photographs are fine. This is the single most useful thing you can send, because the gap between what your child knows and what the band says is usually visible on the page to anyone who reads rubrics for a living.

process.title: Use the free trial as a test of method
process.description: A full lesson online, no payment, no card details. Ask the tutor to name the criterion they would target first and to justify it from the marked work. Watch whether they teach from your school's task sheet or from their own material. Both answers tell you whether this is a Middle Years tutor or a content tutor.

process.title: Agree a block on one criterion
process.description: Six to eight sessions aimed at one named criterion, with the student rewriting their own previously marked responses against the band descriptors. A block has an end point, which keeps the total knowable, and criterion work tends to transfer into other subjects without being taught again.

process.title: Review against criterion bands
process.description: Every four to six weeks, check whether the band on that criterion has moved in the school's own marking. If it has, move the focus to the next weakest. If it has not after six weeks, change the approach or the tutor rather than continuing out of habit, because criterion work should show movement quickly.

whyPoints.title: We teach from your school's rubric
whyPoints.description: The Middle Years Programme sets criteria and objectives; your school writes the units and the task-specific clarifications. So our tutors work from the documents your child is actually marked against rather than from a generic scheme that would be wrong in half of Dubai's IB schools.

whyPoints.title: Matched by criterion, not by year
whyPoints.description: A request for help with mathematics is a year of work. A request for help with Criterion B in mathematics is a block of six sessions with a visible end point. We match on the criterion where the band is lowest, which is both the cheaper and the faster route to a grade change.

whyPoints.title: An honest coverage answer
whyPoints.description: Our depth is good in mathematics and sciences, reasonable in language and literature, and thin in design, arts and some language acquisition phases. We say which before you book rather than after, because no page competing for this search discloses a coverage limit at all.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on Personal Project help
whyPoints.description: Process coaching, goal feasibility, journal habits and written feedback on the student's own draft. Never writing the project, producing the artefact or rewriting a paragraph into final form. We record what help was given so the school can see it was legitimate if it is ever asked.

whyPoints.title: Online, so the tutor pool is not a postcode
whyPoints.description: Lessons run over live video with a shared workspace where the task sheet, the rubric and the student's draft sit side by side. Nobody travels to a JLT tower, which is what makes a Middle Years specialist available at a time a school-run week can hold.

faqs.question: Is there an IB MYP tutor near JLT who actually knows the programme?
faqs.answer: There are tutors who know the Middle Years assessment architecture well, and that is the thing worth hiring. What no tutor can know in advance is your child's content, because the programme sets objectives and criteria while each school writes its own units. So ask two questions instead. Will they teach from your school's task sheet and task-specific clarifications? And can they explain, from your child's last marked assessment, why the criterion band sits where it does? A tutor who answers both is useful in any Dubai MYP school.

faqs.question: Why does my child's MYP report not show percentages?
faqs.answer: Because Middle Years subjects are marked against four criteria, each out of eight, rather than as a percentage of a test. The four criterion marks are added to give a total out of thirty-two, and that total converts to a grade from one to seven using a boundary table. A percentage would hide which criterion is weak, which is the only information that tells you what to work on. Ask the school for the criterion marks behind each grade; they are usually available and they are far more useful than the grade itself.

faqs.question: My child has criterion marks of six, five, six and five but reports a grade five. Is that right?
faqs.answer: Yes. Those four marks total twenty-two out of thirty-two, and under the widely used general boundaries a total of nineteen to twenty-three reports as a grade five. The boundaries are not evenly spaced, so a grade six needs twenty-four and a seven needs twenty-eight. The practical consequence is that evenness across criteria is worth more than strength in two of them, and the fastest route to the next grade is almost always lifting the single weakest criterion by two bands. Confirm the boundary table your school applies.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion is usually worth working on first?
faqs.answer: Whichever band is lowest, and in practice that is usually the investigation criterion or the reflective one. In sciences that means Criterion B, where students write a method and omit the hypothesis, variables and controls, or Criterion D, where impacts must be discussed in a specific context. In mathematics it is Criterion B, where a general rule must be justified rather than illustrated with a second example. In individuals and societies it is Criterion D, source evaluation. These are bounded and trainable in a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: Can MYP criterion work be taught properly over video?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the work is document-based. A session has your child's task sheet, the task-specific clarifications, the band descriptors and their own marked response open side by side on a shared screen, with both people annotating. The core exercise is for the student to rewrite a response they have already been marked on against the descriptor, which is easier to do with the rubric visible than with it on a desk. What video cannot replace is practical or performance work, which belongs in the school.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's school for before hiring an MYP tutor?
faqs.answer: Two documents and one fact. The unit planner summary for the current term, so a tutor knows what content is being covered. The task-specific clarifications for the next assessed task, which is the document that turns a generic criterion descriptor into the thing your child is marked against. And whether the school enters students for on-screen eAssessment at the end of MYP 5 or reports internally, because that changes what the final year should look like. Most Dubai coordinators provide all three on request.

faqs.question: How is the MYP Personal Project supported without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: A tutor may discuss whether a goal is achievable and evidenceable before it is registered, set journal habits early so there is something concrete to reflect on later, teach the assessment criteria, and give written feedback on the student's own draft report. A tutor may not write the project, produce the artefact or rewrite a paragraph into final form. The work must be the student's own, and the IB's rules make the consequences of anything else serious for the student. We record what help was given so the school can verify it.

faqs.question: What is the difference between standard and extended MYP mathematics?
faqs.answer: From MYP 4 most schools split mathematics into two pathways. Extended covers additional content and is generally the route towards Analysis and Approaches Higher Level in the Diploma or towards IGCSE Extended; standard covers the core and leads more naturally to Applications and Interpretation or IGCSE Core. The placement is made by the school, usually a full year before anyone discusses the Diploma. Ask for the placement criteria and whether a move is possible, because the decision quietly sets a ceiling two years ahead.

faqs.question: Will MYP prepare my child for the IB Diploma or for IGCSE exams?
faqs.answer: It prepares them well for the thinking and poorly for the clock. Middle Years tasks are extended, researched and completed over days, with criteria rewarding process, investigation and reflection. Both the Diploma and IGCSE then assess largely by timed examination with a mark scheme per question. A student with strong criterion grades can be rattled by a first mock purely because nothing has trained them to finish under time pressure. The fix is timed practice in MYP 5, not more content, and it takes a short block.

faqs.question: Do MYP tutors in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no amounts are published.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher tutor them privately for MYP?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement families ask for most and the one carrying the most exposure, so check before arranging it. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy document. In practice, an experienced tutor from outside the school who works from your school's rubric achieves the same thing without the question.

faqs.question: What does Middle Years tutoring cost in Dubai compared with Diploma support?
faqs.answer: Generally less, because the hours needed are fewer and more targeted. You can verify the market yourself in ten minutes: EdFlik publishes online tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour, Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, Unitors IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 table puts specialist work at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those were read in October 2026 and belong to those providers. A criterion block of six sessions is a knowable total rather than an open commitment.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups are hardest to find a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Design, arts and physical and health education, followed by some language acquisition phases. The pool of tutors who have genuinely assessed against those criterion sets is thin, because the programme runs in fewer schools and is assessed internally, so fewer teachers accumulate the experience. Mathematics and sciences have reasonable depth, and language and literature is workable because written criteria transfer. Where we cannot staff a subject group we say so and suggest either a wait or spending the money on transferable written criteria instead.

faqs.question: Are interdisciplinary units marked separately on the report?
faqs.answer: Yes, in most schools they are reported against their own interdisciplinary criteria rather than folded into the contributing subjects. The criteria cover disciplinary grounding, synthesising the disciplines and reflecting on the process. Students commonly treat an interdisciplinary unit as a lighter version of two subjects, which is the one approach the criteria do not reward, because synthesis has to be demonstrated explicitly rather than implied. If an interdisciplinary grade is dragging a report, it is usually the synthesis criterion rather than either subject's content.

faqs.question: How long does criterion-focused tutoring usually take to show up in a grade?
faqs.answer: Faster than content work, which is why it is worth starting there. Three or four sessions on one criterion, with the band descriptors read explicitly and the student rewriting their own marked response against them, commonly moves a band in the school's next marking. Review at four to six weeks against the criterion band rather than against how the sessions felt. If nothing has moved in six weeks, change the approach or the tutor; criterion work that is working tends to show quickly and visibly.

faqs.question: How do we book a free MYP trial lesson from a JLT address?
faqs.answer: Send the subject group, the MYP level or year, the criterion with the lowest band, the school, and two windows that work after your child is genuinely home from the school run. Attach the school's task sheet and the last marked assessment if you have them. We match a tutor for that subject group and criterion, and the trial lesson runs in full online with no payment and no card details. During it, watch whether the tutor opens your child's task sheet or their own worksheet.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach Middle Years Programme subjects to the published criteria rather than to a textbook sequence. Each works from the student's own task-specific clarifications and marked criterion sheets, which is the only document set that explains why a strong piece of work scored five rather than seven.

intro.heading: A year with no external timetable, and why that is the problem
paragraphs: Families looking for an IB MYP tutor in Jumeirah 1 usually arrive with a different complaint from families on the IGCSE track. The grade has moved and nobody can say why. A student who scored seven for criterion C in one unit scores four in the next, the teacher comment refers to analysis and evaluation, and the report gives a single number out of seven that nobody can reverse-engineer. There is no past paper to work from and no public mark scheme to drill, so the usual remedies do not apply.

That happens because the Middle Years Programme is criterion-marked rather than examined. Each subject group carries four criteria, labelled A to D, each marked out of eight against published descriptors, and each unit assesses only some of them. A grade out of seven is produced at the end of a reporting period by converting criterion totals through boundaries the school sets within the IB framework. The practical consequence is that progress depends on reading descriptors accurately, and most of the marks a student loses are lost to the wording of the task rather than to the content of the subject.

The second difference is the calendar. On the IGCSE or A Level track, the dates come from outside: Cambridge publishes final entry deadlines and exam windows, Pearson publishes its timetables and results dates, and the year arranges itself around them. In the MYP almost every date is internal. Unit assessment windows, interdisciplinary deadlines, the Personal Project checkpoints and the Year 5 subject choice all sit with the school's MYP coordinator. A Jumeirah 1 family that has not asked for that calendar in writing is planning blind.

Jumeirah 1 sits inside the largest private-school market in the country. KHDA's 2024-25 figures record 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai across 17 curricula, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for 7% of enrolment. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them IB, creating 16,846 new places. In this district the MYP cohort is a minority inside a mostly British-curriculum neighbourhood, which is why MYP-literate teaching is harder to find locally than IGCSE teaching.

A delivery note, stated early rather than buried. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. For criterion-marked work that is a reasonable trade, because the scarce skill is reading a Design criterion B descriptor accurately, not being available on Beach Road at five o'clock.

What follows is the MYP year laid out in order: the term-by-term shape, how criterion marking actually works, the Personal Project counted backwards from submission, what eAssessment adds in Year 5, where marks disappear, how the bridge into the Diploma is built, and the mandatory UAE subjects running alongside all of it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.programmesIntro: A Jumeirah 1 family on the IB continuum is usually looking at three or four years ahead at once: where the student is now, what the Year 5 decision opens, and what the Diploma will demand. The programmes below are described in that order rather than alphabetically.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four published criteria marked out of eight: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Students also meet interdisciplinary units, Approaches to Learning skills, Service as Action, and a Personal Project in the final year. Nothing in the programme is assessed by a terminal paper unless the school enters students for eAssessment.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses within reach of Jumeirah 1 run the MYP, mostly in the Al Safa and Umm Suqeim cluster, and some run it alongside an IGCSE pathway so that families choose at Year 4 or 5. In Dubai every MYP school also delivers the KHDA mandatory subjects, with separate Arabic and Islamic Education classes for Arab and non-Arab students, which adds timetable load the programme guide does not describe.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher and three Standard Levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and the Creativity, Activity, Service strand. Each subject carries an internally assessed component and externally marked papers. The step up from the MYP is not content so much as timed written performance, because the Diploma reintroduces the external examination the MYP left out.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and Diploma candidates in Dubai work to internal coursework deadlines their coordinator sets months before it. Published IB session and results dates should be confirmed with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from a tutoring page, and nothing on this page states one.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, organised around transdisciplinary themes and finishing with the Exhibition. Assessment is formative and descriptive rather than graded, which is why the move into MYP Year 1 is the first time many students meet a criterion descriptor and a mark out of eight. The transition is more often a shock of format than of difficulty.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah 1 and the surrounding coastal districts hold several continuum campuses, so a student can move from PYP to MYP without changing school or district. Families who do change school at that point are the ones who most often ask for a term of support, because two PYP programmes can be two very different preparations for criterion marking.

programmes.name: IGCSE as the Year 5 alternative
programmes.description: The route many Dubai schools offer instead of MYP Years 4 and 5, examined by Cambridge or Pearson terminal paper. It is worth understanding even for a committed MYP family, because it is the comparison every Year 4 option evening makes, and because its external deadlines are hard where the MYP's are internal.
programmes.countryNote: The contrast is concrete. A UAE candidate sits Cambridge in June or in November, and choosing between them is a resit decision as much as a scheduling one: June is the main series Dubai schools enter, and November sits five months behind it, so a single subject that falls short costs a term rather than a year. Entries for either close months ahead of the papers, on a date the centre confirms by statement of entry. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran to 19 November 2026, and those results reached students the following January. An MYP family switching track inherits that externally fixed calendar, and the first planning task is to get the series and entry deadline from the school's exams officer in writing.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.subjectsIntro: MYP subject groups are listed below with the criterion that most often costs marks in each. The pattern across the programme is that criterion A rewards knowledge and criteria B to D reward process, and process is what thin preparation shows up in first.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Standard and Extended)
subjects.description: Criterion C, communicating, and criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, carry the losses. Students who compute accurately still drop marks by omitting the reasoning line, mislabelling a model, or failing to say whether their answer is reasonable in the context the task supplied.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion B, inquiring and designing, and criterion C, processing and evaluating, dominate. A hypothesis with no scientific reasoning behind it, variables listed without a control method, or an evaluation that proposes repeating the experiment without saying what that achieves, are the three recurring deductions.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criterion B, analysing, and criterion C, producing text, separate grades here. Strong readers lose marks by summarising rather than analysing, and by discussing a writer's choice without linking it to an effect on the reader. Oral components are graded on the same criteria as written work.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Phased rather than year-grouped, so two students in the same class can be marked against different descriptors. Most of the recoverable marks sit in criterion A, listening, and criterion B, reading, where the task asks for inference rather than retrieval.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criterion B, investigating, and criterion D, thinking critically, are where grades are won. Source work is the common weakness: a student who describes a source's content without evaluating its origin, purpose, value and limitation is capped well below the top band whatever the essay reads like.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The subject group most often underestimated, and the one with the clearest process requirement. Criterion A, inquiring and analysing, and criterion B, developing ideas, demand a documented research and specification trail. A finished product with no design folder behind it scores poorly however good the product is.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.levels: Visual arts, music, drama, MYP Years 1-5
subjects.description: Criterion B, developing skills, and criterion D, responding, require a process journal that is genuinely kept over time rather than assembled at the deadline. Students with real ability often lose marks here purely on documentation, which is a habit a tutor can fix inside a term.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Marked substantially on planning for performance and on reflecting and improving, not on athletic ability. The written components surprise families, and the criterion D reflection is where a confident athlete most often sits mid-band.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Separately assessed against their own criteria, requiring a student to integrate two subject groups and then evaluate the integration itself. Because they sit outside any single teacher's subject, they are the component most often left unprepared.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal and a report submitted alongside the product. Marks are lost in the journal and the reflection far more often than in the product. Supervision belongs to the school; tutoring here is process coaching on the student's own material.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.regionsIntro: MYP families in this part of Dubai are spread across the coastal and inland districts behind Beach Road. The notes below concern where the MYP cohort actually studies and what the afternoon looks like from each address.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: The inland district holding the nearest IB continuum provision to Jumeirah 1, which is why a sizeable share of the local MYP cohort commutes here rather than along the coast.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Home to several of the larger international campuses the Jumeirah MYP cohort attends. The afternoon pinch is the Umm Suqeim Road junction, which pushes a safe session start towards 5pm.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2 and Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Short runs along the coast with the same campus options. Families here often have one child on the MYP and another on an IGCSE track, which makes a single weekly tutoring slot per child the realistic ceiling.

regions.name: Al Wasl and City Walk
regions.note: Apartment and townhouse living with short school runs. Study space rather than travel is the limiting factor, so sixty-minute sessions hold attention better than ninety-minute ones for Years 1 to 3.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: One causeway and one tunnel govern the afternoon. The Personal Project year is when this matters most, because supervision meetings at school and tutoring sessions compete for the same narrow window.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira and La Mer
regions.note: No campuses inside either development, so every family commutes out and the journey is predictable. A fixed weekly slot is easier to defend here than in districts with school-gate congestion.

regions.name: Satwa and Al Hudaiba
regions.note: Closer to the city and denser. Journeys are short, but the pick-up window at primary campuses absorbs the saving, so the practical session start is earlier than the distance suggests.

regions.name: Al Manara and Al Barsha fringe
regions.note: The inland edge of the catchment, where several campuses with MYP provision sit within a Sheikh Zayed Road crossing. Thursday sessions survive better than midweek ones for families making that crossing.

schoolClusters.city: IB continuum campuses within reach of Jumeirah 1
schoolClusters.note: The campuses a Jumeirah 1 address can reach without a long crossing, including the continuum schools running PYP, MYP and Diploma in sequence. Families here change route more often than they change district, which is why MYP and IGCSE cohorts overlap on the same streets.

schoolClusters.city: The British-curriculum neighbours
schoolClusters.note: The campuses that make Jumeirah 1 a mostly IGCSE neighbourhood, which is relevant to an MYP family for two reasons: the option evening comparison at Year 4, and the fact that local tutoring supply is shaped by IGCSE demand rather than by criterion marking.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.modesIntro: MYP support divides naturally by what the student is actually short of: criterion literacy, a specific subject group, or project management on a long piece of work. The three formats below map onto those three problems.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on one subject group
modes.description: A fixed slot through the term on a single subject group, working from the live unit and its task-specific clarifications. The session cycle is to read the descriptor, plan against it, draft, then compare the draft to the descriptor again. This is what moves a persistent five to a seven, because the gap is almost always process rather than knowledge.

modes.title: Criterion literacy block
modes.description: Three or four sessions on reading and using the descriptors themselves, across whichever subject groups the student takes. Deliberately subject-light. For a student who has just moved from PYP, or from a British or Indian middle school, this is usually the highest-value spend of the first term because it transfers to every subject at once.

modes.title: Personal Project process coaching
modes.description: Scheduled against the school's own checkpoint dates in Year 5, focused on the process journal, the goal and criteria the student sets, and the reflection. The student's supervisor at school holds the formal role; the coaching is on planning, time management and reflective writing, using only material the student has produced themselves.

sections.heading: The MYP year laid out term by term
paragraphs: The first thing to establish with a Dubai MYP school is the internal calendar, because nothing about the year is externally timetabled until eAssessment or the Diploma. A UAE school year opening in late August and closing in late June typically runs three terms with a half-term break in each, and unit assessment windows land in clusters inside them. Reports arrive two or three times a year, and by the time one arrives the criterion scores behind it are weeks old.

Working forwards from that, the useful shape is: diagnose in the first term from returned criterion sheets, build process habits in the second, and in Year 5 spend the second and third terms on the Personal Project and the route decision. The common error is to wait for the report, which arrives too late to change the unit it describes. Returned unit work carries the same information three to six weeks earlier, and it carries the task-specific clarifications the teacher actually marked against.

The table below sets that year out. It is written for a Dubai school on an August-to-June year; campuses on an April start shift the whole sequence, which also shifts their KHDA mandatory-subject implementation to April rather than September. Either way the principle holds: the dates belong to the school, so they have to be requested rather than assumed.

One date is worth putting in a diary in Year 4 regardless of school. The option evening where MYP Years 4 and 5 are compared against an IGCSE pathway happens earlier than most families expect, and it is the decision with the longest reach. A family that walks into it without having looked at what the destination sixth form expects is choosing between two routes on presentation rather than on consequence.

sections.heading: Criterion marking, and how a seven is actually produced
paragraphs: Each MYP subject group carries four criteria labelled A to D, each marked out of eight in bands described by published descriptors. A single unit rarely assesses all four. At the end of a reporting period the criterion totals are converted to a grade out of seven using boundaries, which is why a student can feel they did well on every task and still see a five. The mechanism is additive across criteria, not an average of test scores, so one neglected criterion drags a grade that four strong pieces of content knowledge cannot rescue.

The document that does the work is the task-specific clarification the teacher issues with each assessment. It restates the general descriptor in the language of that particular task, and it is as close to a mark scheme as the MYP offers. Students who read it before planning score differently from students who read it after submitting. A surprising share of MYP tutoring value is simply making that read a habit, which is why the criterion literacy block exists as a format.

The pattern across subject groups is consistent enough to name. Criterion A rewards knowledge and understanding, and most students in a selective Dubai campus already clear it. Criteria B, C and D reward process: investigating, communicating, evaluating, reflecting. Those are the bands where mid-range scores cluster, and they are the bands that respond to being taught explicitly. A student who can explain the difference between describing a source and evaluating it has moved a whole band in Individuals and Societies without learning any new history.

The table sets the four criteria against what each one actually asks for in three different subject groups, which is the comparison that makes the system legible to a parent. The labels differ by group; the shape does not.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, counted backwards from submission
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP Year 5 is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal and a report submitted alongside whatever the student has made. Marks are lost in the journal and the reflection far more often than in the product, and they are lost for a structural reason: a journal reconstructed in the final fortnight cannot show development over time, and development over time is exactly what the criteria ask to see.

Counted backwards from the school's submission date, the sequence that works is roughly this. Six months out, the goal and the success criteria the student sets for themselves are agreed and written down. Five months out, the research and the skills audit are under way with journal entries carrying real dates. Three months out, the product is in development and the journal records decisions and changes rather than progress reports. Six weeks out, the report is being drafted by the student against the criteria. Two weeks out, the reflection is written on what actually happened, including what went wrong.

The boundary here has to be explicit, because the Personal Project is the component where UAE search results contain outright malpractice offers. The supervisor at school holds the formal role. A tutor may coach planning, discuss time management, explain what the criteria reward, and give feedback on journal entries and report drafts the student has produced alone. A tutor may not author any part of the report, the product or the journal, and may not supply text or research for them. Work submitted under a student's name has to be the student's own, and the consequences of a malpractice finding sit entirely with the student.

In Jumeirah 1 the practical constraint on all of this is competition for the same weekday window. Supervision meetings at school, co-curricular commitments and a tutoring session all want the hour after the school run. Fixing the project slot at the start of the year, including on the weekend if that is what survives, is worth more than a better slot that gets renegotiated every fortnight.

sections.heading: What eAssessment adds in Year 5, and what it does not
paragraphs: Some MYP schools enter Year 5 students for the IB's optional MYP eAssessment, which leads to an externally validated certificate. Where a school does, the year gains an external component it otherwise lacks: on-screen examinations in several subject groups, and externally moderated ePortfolios in others, including Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education. Where a school does not, Year 5 is assessed entirely internally and the record is the school's own.

This matters for tutoring because it changes what the final year is preparing for. An eAssessment cohort has to add timed on-screen performance to criterion literacy, which is a genuinely different skill: reading a stimulus under clock pressure and producing a structured response in a fixed window. A non-eAssessment cohort does not, and spending the year rehearsing exam technique there would be effort misdirected. The first question to the coordinator is therefore simply whether the school enters students at all.

UAE schools sit the May session. Specific IB session and results dates are not stated on this page: ibo.org is the authority for them and the school's IB coordinator is the practical route, and any date taken from a third-party page should be checked against one of those before a revision plan rests on it. Cambridge and Pearson publish their dates openly and those are quoted elsewhere on this page; the IB's are not treated the same way here for that reason.

For families whose school does not enter students, the external benchmark arrives instead at the Diploma, and the Year 5 to Diploma transition becomes the real event. That is the next section, and it is the one most Jumeirah 1 MYP families should read twice.

sections.heading: The MYP to Diploma bridge, and the habits that have to change
paragraphs: The move from MYP Year 5 into Diploma Year 1 is where criterion-marked students most often stumble, and the reason is specific. The MYP assesses process generously and timed recall barely at all. The Diploma reintroduces external papers with fixed durations, and a student who has spent five years redrafting against a rubric has not built the habit of producing a complete structured answer once, under time, without feedback.

The content gap is usually smaller than families fear. MYP Extended Mathematics prepares a student reasonably for Analysis and Approaches; MYP Sciences prepares them for Standard Level and, with a quantitative push, for Higher Level. The genuine gaps are narrower and more fixable: algebraic fluency under time pressure, the convention of showing working so method marks survive a slip, and writing to a word limit rather than to a rubric. Each of those is a term's work rather than a year's.

The second shift is independence of a different kind. In the MYP, a teacher's feedback cycle is built into the assessment design. In the Diploma, internal assessment carries strict limits on how much feedback a teacher may give, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay are written under tight academic-honesty rules. An MYP student used to iterative feedback has to learn to produce a defensible first draft alone, and that is a habit best started in Year 5 rather than discovered in Year 12.

For a Jumeirah 1 family the local version of this decision is unusually live, because both routes sit within a short drive. The same student can reach a British sixth form offering A Levels and an IB continuum campus offering the Diploma without changing district. The choice should be made on what the student does well under which conditions, and a year of criterion scores read criterion by criterion is better evidence for that than a single grade out of seven.

Working shown line by line so method marks survive arithmetic slips

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai delivers Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of its licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For an MYP family that means the timetable carries subjects the programme guide does not describe, and the grades in them appear on the same report as the criterion scores.

The rules are more specific than most families realise. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

There are also constraints on content and on time. Instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and the advice is that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. The use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, and schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects.

That last point sets a real boundary on what external tutoring can offer in these subjects. Support here is best framed as language work and study skills around the school's own material rather than as an alternative syllabus, and the school remains the authority on what content is used. It is also worth knowing that for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required GCSE or IGCSE subjects, which is a separate rule from the mandatory-teaching one and is frequently confused with it.

sections.heading: What MYP tuition costs in Dubai, and the in-home question
paragraphs: Parents in this district usually ask about a tutor coming to the villa before they ask about anything else, and the question deserves a direct answer. In-home one-to-one tutoring is a substantial Dubai market with published prices. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home visits at roughly AED 180-350 an hour, independent home tutors reach AED 500, and qualified subject tutors working online sit at roughly AED 150-300. Monthly packages seen in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What the in-home premium buys is travel. The pool of people prepared to drive to Jumeirah 1 at five o'clock is set by where they live, not by whether they can read a Design criterion B descriptor. For a mainstream IGCSE subject that trade is survivable, because local supply is deep. For MYP criterion marking in a neighbourhood where the IB cohort is a minority, it is a much worse trade, and it is the single strongest practical argument for teaching over video in this specific case.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; our UAE teaching is one-to-one over live video, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. That is a narrower offer than some agencies advertise and it is stated plainly for that reason. The compensating benefit is that a Jumeirah 1 family can be matched on MYP subject-group literacy rather than on driving distance.

Every figure below was published by the organisation named against it and is dated October 2026. None of it is an IB Gram price list. Our own arrangement begins with one free 45-minute trial lesson per family, no card details collected, with a rate quoted afterwards against the subject group and the number of weeks involved. School fees are worth one line of context too: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in criterion-marked work
paragraphs: Criterion-marked coursework raises the honesty question more often than exam-based courses do, because almost everything is produced at home over weeks. The boundary is the same in every subject group and it is not ambiguous. A tutor may teach content, explain what a descriptor rewards, model a technique on a different example, and give feedback on work the student has already produced alone. A tutor may not author any part of a submitted piece, may not supply text, data, research or analysis for it, and may not edit a draft into a finished state on the student's behalf.

In the Dubai search results this is not a theoretical distinction. Operations in this market sell finished Internal Assessments at fixed prices, and the same logic is applied to Personal Projects and MYP coursework. A student who submits purchased work faces a malpractice process rather than a poor grade, and the school's own academic-honesty policy, not a tutoring contract, governs the outcome. An agency willing to discuss producing a submitted piece is describing a risk, not a service.

There is a second boundary around materials. The IB's subject guides, descriptors, past eAssessment material and teacher support documents are the school's to hold and the IB's to publish. We reference them and point families to ibo.org and to the school's coordinator, and we do not reproduce or distribute them. A tutor offering an unlimited private library of IB documents is usually offering something they are not entitled to distribute.

Saying this out loud narrows the offer and improves it. What a family is buying is teaching, diagnosis and feedback on the student's own work. In a programme where the assessment is the student's own extended output, that is the only kind of help whose benefit survives into the Diploma, where the rules get tighter and the consequences get larger.

process.title: Send returned unit work, not the report
process.description: The useful documents are the student's marked criterion sheets and the task-specific clarifications that came with them. Those show which criteria are costing marks and in what language the teacher is marking. A report gives a grade out of seven that cannot be reverse-engineered, which is why diagnosis from a report wastes the first paid session.

process.title: Ask the coordinator three questions in writing
process.description: Whether the school enters students for MYP eAssessment, what the Personal Project checkpoint dates are, and when the Year 4 option decision is taken. All three change the plan materially, and all three are internal dates that are not published anywhere a family can look them up.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One free 45-minute lesson per family, no card details collected. It is spent on a live unit from the student's own work rather than on a general assessment, and written feedback follows. If the match is not right, say so and a different tutor is proposed before any payment is made.

process.title: Agree the format and the output
process.description: A weekly subject-group slot, a criterion literacy block, or Personal Project coaching scheduled against the school's own dates. Each carries a named weekly output: a plan written against the clarification, a redraft, a dated journal entry. The output is what makes progress auditable.

process.title: Review against criterion scores, not feelings
process.description: At the halfway point, compare criterion scores from the start of the block with current returned work, criterion by criterion. Bands that have moved come off the plan. Bands that have not either get more time or are set aside deliberately in favour of one that will move.

whyPoints.title: Descriptors before content
whyPoints.description: Most MYP marks are lost to the wording of the task rather than to the subject. Sessions start from the published criteria and the task-specific clarification, because that is the document the teacher marks against and the one students read last.

whyPoints.title: Subject-group literacy, not driving distance
whyPoints.description: MYP families are a minority in a mostly British-curriculum district, so a proximity-based search returns IGCSE tutors. Teaching over live video changes the selection criterion to whether the tutor can read a criterion B descriptor in the right subject group.

whyPoints.title: The calendar belongs to the school
whyPoints.description: Unit windows, project checkpoints and option-evening dates are internal and unpublished. Any plan here is built against dates obtained from the coordinator in writing rather than against an assumed term structure.

whyPoints.title: A project plan that starts early enough
whyPoints.description: The Personal Project criteria reward development over time, which a journal assembled at the deadline cannot show. Coaching is scheduled backwards from the school's submission date so that dated entries exist across months.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated before payment
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no part of a submitted piece authored by a tutor, no IB documents redistributed, no grade promised, and no IB session date published that has not been confirmed with the school or ibo.org.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed
whyPoints.description: Market rates here are credited to the organisation that published them and dated October 2026. Regulatory statements are credited to KHDA, u.ae or MoHRE. Nothing is presented as an IB Gram statistic without the data behind it.

faqs.question: Why does my child's MYP grade move up and down between units?
faqs.answer: Because different units assess different criteria. Each MYP subject group has four criteria marked out of eight, and a unit usually samples only two or three of them. A student who is strong on knowing and understanding but weak on evaluating will score well in a unit weighted towards criterion A and poorly in one weighted towards criterion D, with no change in effort or ability. The fix is to read the criterion scores individually rather than the grade out of seven, which is a conversion of criterion totals and hides exactly the information a parent needs.

faqs.question: What is a task-specific clarification and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: It is the sheet a teacher issues with an MYP assessment that restates the general criterion descriptors in the language of that particular task. It is the closest thing the programme has to a mark scheme. Students who read it before planning their work score differently from students who read it after submitting, because the descriptors tell them what shape the response has to take. Asking for it, filing it, and planning against it line by line is one of the cheapest grade improvements available in the MYP, and it transfers to every subject group at once.

faqs.question: My child moved from a British school into MYP Year 3. What should the first term cover?
faqs.answer: Criterion literacy, not content. A student arriving from a British or Indian middle school usually has solid subject knowledge and no experience of being marked against descriptors, so the early losses are in criteria B, C and D: method stated without justification, communication marks dropped on terminology, evaluation offered as description. Three or four sessions reading descriptors band by band, then re-marking their own returned work against them, moves more marks in that first term than any amount of extra subject teaching. Content gaps can be audited afterwards, once the marking system is legible.

faqs.question: Does my child's Dubai school enter students for MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Only the MYP coordinator can tell you, and it is worth asking in writing because it changes what the final year prepares for. Schools that enter students add on-screen examinations in several subject groups and externally moderated ePortfolios in others, including Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education. Schools that do not assess Year 5 internally, and the record is the school's own. An eAssessment cohort needs timed performance practised alongside criterion work; a non-eAssessment cohort does not, and rehearsing exam technique there would be misdirected effort.

faqs.question: How early should Personal Project work start in MYP Year 5?
faqs.answer: About six months before the school's submission date, which usually means the goal and the student's own success criteria are agreed in the first term. The criteria reward development over time, and a process journal assembled in the final fortnight cannot show it, so late starts cost marks structurally rather than through poor work. The sequence that works is goal and criteria at six months, research and skills audit at five, product in development at three with the journal recording decisions, report drafting at six weeks, and the reflection written in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be stated before any session. A tutor may coach planning and time management, explain what the criteria reward, and give feedback on journal entries and report drafts the student has produced alone. A tutor may not author any part of the report, the product or the journal, and may not supply text or research for them. The supervisor at school holds the formal role. This matters because operations in the UAE search results sell finished assessed work, and a student who submits purchased material faces a malpractice process rather than a low mark.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject group causes the most trouble in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: Design, more often than families expect, followed by Individuals and Societies. Design is marked substantially on a documented inquiry and development trail, so a strong finished product with no design folder behind it scores poorly, and students who treat it as a practical subject are surprised by the written weighting. Individuals and Societies loses marks on source evaluation: describing a source's content without assessing its origin, purpose, value and limitation caps a student well below the top band regardless of how the essay reads. Both are process problems and both respond quickly to explicit teaching.

faqs.question: Is MYP Mathematics Extended necessary for Higher Level maths later?
faqs.answer: It is the more natural preparation, particularly for Analysis and Approaches, but the decisive question is algebraic fluency under time pressure rather than the course label. A student on Extended who computes well but omits reasoning lines will still find Higher Level hard, and a Standard student with secure algebra can be bridged in a term. The honest audit is to look at criterion C and criterion D scores across a year of returned work, then test the student on timed, unaided algebra. That is better evidence than a grade out of seven or a course title.

faqs.question: What actually changes between MYP Year 5 and Diploma Year 1?
faqs.answer: Timed external performance, and the feedback cycle. The MYP assesses process generously and timed recall barely at all, so a student used to redrafting against a rubric has rarely produced a complete structured answer once, under time, without help. The Diploma also restricts how much feedback a teacher may give on internally assessed work, and its Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge rules are tighter. The content gap is usually smaller than the habit gap, and the habits are best started in Year 5 rather than discovered in the first Diploma term.

faqs.question: How many MYP subject groups can we realistically tutor at once?
faqs.answer: One with real weekly depth, or two if the student's independent-study time can absorb the work set between sessions. Beyond that the sessions become attendance rather than progress, because criterion work requires drafting and redrafting outside the hour. The more efficient alternative for a student struggling across several subjects is a criterion literacy block: three or four subject-light sessions on reading and using the descriptors, which transfers to all eight subject groups at once and usually moves more marks than a second subject-specific slot would.

faqs.question: Does the Arabic and Islamic Education timetable affect MYP study time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a real load the programme guide does not describe. Every Dubai private school delivers Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside its licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and at least 25 minutes advised per lesson. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. The practical effect for a family is fewer free periods and a fuller week than an MYP timetable alone suggests.

faqs.question: Can tutoring in Arabic or Islamic Education follow a different syllabus?
faqs.answer: No, and it should not try to. KHDA states that for the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, and that schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. Support outside school is therefore best framed as language work and study skills around the school's own material, with the school remaining the authority on content. Families should also know that Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track Ministry of Education equivalency, which is a separate rule.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost in Jumeirah 1 and the surrounding districts?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market bands put qualified subject tutors online at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, in-home visits at AED 180-500 with travel included, and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or more. Bestimate's Dubai table gives in-home at AED 180-350; TutorChase publishes AED 270; monthly packages around AED 799 for eight online sessions appear in the market. Those are other organisations' published figures as at October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27.

faqs.question: Is there any point tutoring an MYP student in Years 1 to 3?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but for a different reason than in Year 5. Early MYP years are where criterion habits form, and a student who learns in Year 2 to plan against a task-specific clarification carries that through to the Personal Project and into Diploma internal assessment. A short block at that stage is cheap and compounds. What rarely works in the early years is content acceleration: the programme is not content-limited, so pushing ahead of the class produces boredom rather than better criterion scores. One sixty-minute session a week is the sensible ceiling.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers a niche MYP subject group that week?
faqs.answer: We say so and give a date rather than substituting someone who does not know the criteria. Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education have thinner coverage than Mathematics and Sciences, and a specific phase of Language Acquisition can be thinner still. Where the wait is longer than the deadline allows, the honest options are a criterion literacy block with an available tutor, which transfers across subject groups, or starting on the subject that is covered now. Both are explained before any payment, with the limitation named rather than concealed.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with UAE families need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service states a two-working-day completion time.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.closingHeading: Ask the coordinator for the dates, then read the criterion sheets
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.closingBody: Two things make an MYP year plannable. The first is the school's internal calendar: unit windows, Personal Project checkpoints, whether eAssessment applies, and when the Year 4 option decision is taken. The second is the student's returned work with its criterion scores and task-specific clarifications, which show in the school's own language where the marks are going. Send the second and ask the coordinator for the first, and the opening conversation can be about which criterion will move rather than about the programme in general. The trial is one free 45-minute lesson per family, no card details collected, taught on a live unit. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.
