intro.heading: What five years of MYP tutoring actually costs a Jumeirah 2 family
paragraphs: Most families in Jumeirah 2 do not start MYP tutoring because of a crisis. They start because a report card in MYP 2 or MYP 3 carries four criterion marks per subject, nobody at home can read them, and the school's parent evening gives twelve minutes per teacher. The question that follows is almost never "how much per hour". It is "how long are we doing this for", and the honest answer is that a Middle Years Programme runs five years. Priced at one weekly hour from MYP 1 to MYP 5, even the cheapest end of the Dubai market adds up to a sum nobody budgeted for.

That is the first place money goes wrong. A tutor booked at the bottom of the market for AED 45 to 65 an hour, as EdFlik publishes, is good value for a specific job: unblocking homework, keeping a child company through a worksheet, holding a routine together during a hard term. Bought as a five-year subscription it becomes an expensive way to supervise work the child could have finished alone. The spend produces attendance rather than movement, and the criterion marks on the next report look the same.

The second place money goes wrong is the opposite error. A premium rate at the BartyED end of the market, AED 650 an hour, buys genuine subject expertise, but in MYP 2 there is often nothing for that expertise to do. The content is not yet hard. What is hard is the assessment model: four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, each with its own descriptor ladder, and a conversion to a 1 to 7 grade that most parents have never seen explained. A teacher who can read that ladder costs the middle of the market, not the top of it.

So this page is built around the middle. Unitors publishes online rates from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB; TutorChase publishes AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts a qualified subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, and in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. Those are the real numbers a Jumeirah 2 family will be quoted. We publish them because almost nobody ranking for this search does, and a parent who knows the bands cannot be overcharged by much.

What IB Gram sells into that market is one-to-one tuition delivered live online, on Gulf Standard Time, to addresses across Jumeirah 2 and the coast. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The practical consequence is that the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching rather than an hour of teaching plus a drive down Al Wasl Road, and the tutor is chosen for knowing MYP Sciences criteria B and C rather than for living four streets away.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.programmesIntro: Jumeirah 2 sits inside a corridor where IB continuum schools and British-curriculum schools are a few minutes apart, so the same street often holds MYP, IGCSE and DP families. These are the programmes our Dubai tutors cover, with what each one costs a family in time rather than money.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups taught through key concepts, related concepts and six global contexts, with every subject assessed against four published criteria rather than a single exam mark. Each criterion is marked out of 8 and reported separately, which is why an MYP report looks nothing like a British one. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project and, in schools that register for it, the on-screen eAssessment route to the IB MYP Certificate.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP is the middle section of an IB continuum school, so the children on your street in Jumeirah 2 may be in MYP 4 while their neighbours sit IGCSEs the same year. Families here most often ask for MYP Sciences, Mathematics and Individuals and Societies, because those three carry the heaviest investigation criteria and the most unfamiliar command terms.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher Level and three Standard Level choices, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessments carry fixed weightings in every subject, and final grades run 1 to 7 with up to three bonus points from TOK and the Extended Essay. The jump in written volume between MYP 5 and DP1 is the single steepest step in the IB.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB cohort is small relative to the British-curriculum majority, which makes DP subject specialists scarcer locally than IGCSE ones. For a Jumeirah 2 family that is an argument for booking online: the pool of DP Chemistry or Maths Analysis and Approaches teachers is national and international rather than whoever is free within a twenty-minute drive.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses with syllabus codes that matter: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, and Pearson Edexcel equivalents such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson runs a different paper structure for the same content. The board decides the mark scheme, so tutoring that ignores the code wastes half its time.
programmes.countryNote: Several of the schools nearest Jumeirah 2 run IGCSE at 16 and then split into A Level or the IB Diploma, so a household can hold one child in MYP 4 and another in Year 11. Families here commonly book a single tutor across both children only when the subject and board genuinely overlap, which for maths they often do not.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry organised around six themes, with no formal external examinations and a PYP Exhibition in the final year. Reporting is descriptive rather than numerical, which makes the first MYP report card a shock for parents who have only ever read PYP comments. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and written structure.
programmes.countryNote: The transition from PYP 6 to MYP 1 inside the same Dubai school is where many Jumeirah 2 families first notice a gap, because the child moves from one teacher to eight subject teachers in one August. A short block of support over the summer costs far less than a year of catch-up in MYP 2.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.subjectsIntro: MYP tutoring is organised by subject group, not by school textbook, because the criteria live at group level. These are the eight groups plus the interdisciplinary strand, with the part of each that Dubai families most often pay to fix.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A to D cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Marks are lost in criterion B, where students write a method without a controlled variable, and in criterion C, where a graph is drawn but never interpreted. This is the group Jumeirah 2 parents book most.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion B, investigating patterns, is the strand with no equivalent in a British maths course: the student must find a general rule, justify it and test it. Criterion D asks for mathematics applied to a real context with a reasoned conclusion. Pure procedural practice raises criterion A alone and leaves the other three flat.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organizing, producing text and using language. Most mark loss sits in criterion A, where a student retells a plot instead of analysing how the writer builds meaning. Tutoring here is close reading plus paragraph architecture, not vocabulary lists, and it transfers directly to DP Language A later.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. Criterion D is where grades are made: evaluating sources, recognising bias and weighing evidence. Students who write confident narrative history often sit at a 4 or 5 here until someone teaches them what evaluation looks like on the page.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Assessed in phases rather than year groups, across comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Dubai schools place children into phases on arrival, and a misplacement is common after a mid-year move. Tutoring targets the phase descriptors the school is actually marking against.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The written design cycle carries most of the marks, which surprises families who assume the group is practical. Students lose criterion B marks by sketching one idea instead of generating and justifying several against a specification.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. The process journal is the assessed artefact as much as the finished piece, and criterion D rewards reflection a student can be taught to write. Support here is usually a short block before a summative rather than weekly work.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, reflecting on and improving performance. The written strands can be tutored even though the practical ones cannot, and criterion A often carries an anatomy or nutrition knowledge test that students revise for badly.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units and the Personal Project
subjects.description: Interdisciplinary units are assessed against their own criteria and are frequently the lowest marks on an MYP report because nobody revises for them. The MYP 5 Personal Project is supervised in school; a tutor may coach process, planning and reflection, and must never produce any part of the student's own work.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP tutor in Jumeirah 2 costs, by provider model
paragraphs: An MYP tutor in Dubai is quoted anywhere between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour, and the spread is not noise. Each band corresponds to a different person doing a different job, and the table below names who publishes each figure so a Jumeirah 2 parent can check it rather than take our word for it. Every rate is a market rate collected from the provider's own site; none of them is an IB Gram price list.

Read the table left to right rather than top to bottom. The hourly figure is the least useful column, because a one-hour weekly booking across a five-year programme is a very different purchase from six sessions before a criterion B investigation. The indicative monthly column, drawn from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session, is closer to what actually leaves a family's account.

The pattern that repeats in this market is that the bottom band is bought for too long and the top band is bought too early. A generalist at AED 45 to 65 an hour is a sensible purchase for one difficult term in MYP 2 and an expensive habit by MYP 4. A specialist at AED 500 and upwards is the right call for a DP Higher Level subject and usually overpowered for an MYP 3 Sciences unit, where the obstacle is the descriptor rather than the physics.

There is one figure families are rarely shown: the monthly in-home package. Quotes of AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits circulate widely in Dubai, which works out close to AED 200 to 225 an hour before anyone accounts for the travel window either side. sections.heading: The travel premium, priced out for a Jumeirah Beach Road address
paragraphs: The gap between the online band and the in-home band in Dubai is roughly AED 50 to 200 an hour depending on where you look. That gap is not a quality difference. It is a logistics charge, and in this corridor it is a large one, because Jumeirah Beach Road and Al Wasl Road both carry school traffic and office traffic through the same window a tutoring session wants to occupy.

Work it through for a single weekly hour. A tutor crossing from Al Barsha or Business Bay to Jumeirah 2 at five in the afternoon is unlikely to spend less than fifty minutes in the car for the round trip, and often considerably more in the weeks either side of a long weekend. Somebody pays for that time. Either it is priced into the rate, which is what the AED 180 to 500 band reflects, or it is absorbed by the tutor, in which case the pool of people willing to take the booking shrinks to those who live nearby.

That second effect is the one that quietly costs a family the most. A ten-kilometre radius around Jumeirah 2 contains a limited number of teachers who can mark MYP Sciences criterion B properly. Restrict the search to that radius and the constraint stops being subject expertise and becomes driving distance. Remove the radius and the constraint is availability at 5pm Gulf Standard Time, which is a far weaker one.

IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE at all, so this is not a product comparison we have an easy answer to; home visits are an India-only service for us. sections.heading: Reading an MYP report card before you spend anything
paragraphs: The cheapest hour of MYP tutoring is the one you decide not to buy, and the report card tells you which hours those are. Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, each marked out of 8. Four strands at 8 marks gives a subject total out of 32, which the school converts into a 1 to 7 grade using published boundaries. A parent who can read the four numbers instead of the single grade can usually see the problem without paying anybody to find it.

The diagnostic pattern is simple. A child with high criterion A marks and low B and C marks does not have a knowledge problem; they have an inquiry and processing problem, and no amount of content revision will move it. A child with the reverse profile is thinking well and has not learned the material. A child flat across all four is usually in the wrong phase or set rather than in need of a tutor. Each of those three profiles costs a different amount to fix, and the third is often free.

The criteria are not identical across the eight subject groups, which is where parents lose the thread. Criterion B in Sciences is inquiring and designing; criterion B in Mathematics is investigating patterns; criterion B in Language and Literature is organizing. Same letter, different skill, different fix. The table lists the four strands for the five groups Dubai families book most often, so the letters on the report mean something before the first session is paid for.

One practical note for Jumeirah 2 households with children in two systems: an MYP 4 report and a Year 10 report cannot be compared. A 5 in MYP Sciences is not a grade 5 at IGCSE, and treating them as equivalent is how families end up buying tuition for the child who needs it less.

sections.heading: Where Jumeirah 2 families waste money on MYP tutoring
paragraphs: Four spending mistakes account for most of the wasted money in this market, and all four are avoidable without knowing anything about the IB. The first is buying hours instead of buying a target. A booking described as "maths help, ongoing" has no finish line, so it renews indefinitely and nobody ever asks whether it worked. A booking described as "raise criterion D in Mathematics from 4 to 6 by the next summative" either succeeds or is cancelled.

The second is buying too many subjects at once. An MYP report shows eight subject groups, and a weak-looking report usually has one root cause expressed in several places: a child who cannot structure written analysis will look weak in Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies and Sciences criterion D simultaneously. Three tutors at mid-market rates is roughly AED 2,400 a month. One tutor working on written structure is a third of that and often fixes all three.

The third is paying premium rates for pre-DP content. The genuine scarcity premium in Dubai sits on Higher Level Diploma subjects, where few local teachers have taught the current syllabus. MYP content, for a qualified subject teacher, is not scarce. Paying AED 500 an hour for MYP 3 Sciences buys a very good teacher doing something a competent one does equally well, and the money would do more work two years later.

The fourth is paying for the school's own job twice. The Personal Project has a school supervisor. Interdisciplinary units are set and marked in school. Service as action is logged in school. Hiring external help for any of those before speaking to the coordinator who runs them is the most common unnecessary line on a Dubai tutoring invoice, and the conversation is free.

sections.heading: The school run, and when a session can realistically start
paragraphs: Dubai school days in this corridor finish between roughly 2.30pm and 3.30pm, and the bus or car run adds twenty to fifty minutes depending on which direction the child is travelling and whether the route crosses Al Wasl Road at the wrong moment. For a Jumeirah 2 family the practical first slot is therefore around 4.30pm, with 5pm the time that holds up reliably across a whole term rather than for the first fortnight.

Online delivery matters here in a way that has nothing to do with teaching quality. An online session can start at 4.35pm because the child walks from the front door to a desk. An in-home session cannot start at 4.35pm with any confidence, because the tutor is somewhere on Sheikh Zayed Road. Families who have run both formats usually report the same thing: the online slot is the one that survives contact with a real week.

The second half of the evening is underused. Sessions at 7pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time are widely available, and for households where both parents work in DIFC or Business Bay they are frequently better, because a parent can be present for the last ten minutes when the tutor summarises what moved. For MYP 4 and MYP 5 students a later slot also sits after sport and after the worst of the homework fatigue.

Ramadan reshapes all of this, and it is worth planning for rather than improvising. School hours shorten, and the useful tutoring window moves either to the early afternoon or to after Iftar. Both work online. Both are difficult to hold together if somebody has to drive. Families who shift to a post-Iftar slot for the month generally keep the same tutor and the same weekday, which is the point of booking a format that does not depend on traffic.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what an MYP tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: This matters more in the MYP than families expect, because so much of the assessment is coursework produced at home. The IB's academic honesty requirements apply from MYP 1, not just in the Diploma, and the Personal Project in MYP 5 carries a declaration that the work is the student's own. A tutor who crosses that line exposes the student, not the tutor.

The boundary is workable and clear. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain what a descriptor is asking for, model the technique on a different example, read a finished draft and say where it falls short of the criterion, and ask questions that make a student rethink their own argument. A tutor may not supply sentences to be copied, restructure a draft on the student's behalf, choose the research question, or hand over a method for a criterion B investigation.

Some of this market does cross the line. Research into the UAE tutoring search results found a provider selling completed Internal Assessments outright, which is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for any student who buys one. No tutor on this platform produces a Personal Project, an interdisciplinary task or a Sciences investigation for a student, and no tutor here will edit a draft to the point where the words are no longer the student's.

For parents the practical test is the one you can apply yourself after a session. Ask your child to explain the change they made and why the descriptor required it. If they can, the help was teaching. If they cannot, it was production, and the mark it earns belongs to someone else. That question costs nothing and is the most reliable quality check available to a family buying coursework support.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and what a Jumeirah 2 parent can verify
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through its app, website and e-services.

Two consequences follow for a family comparing quotes. First, nobody can justify a higher rate on the grounds of permit costs, because there are none. Second, a tutor who has no view on the permit question at all is worth a second look. Individuals providing private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted at you is unverified.

The school side is a different regulator. Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which inspects them annually and publishes the outcome. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. A permit to tutor privately is not a KHDA school licence and does not imply one, and IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or any examination board.

There is one more figure worth knowing while budgeting. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a family planning a five-year MYP spend, a flat school fee year is the right moment to decide how much of the tutoring budget is genuinely needed rather than habitual.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and the subjects that sit alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Families moving into Jumeirah 2 from outside the UAE are regularly surprised that their child's IB timetable includes subjects the IB does not set. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The rules are specific, and they explain timetable decisions that otherwise look arbitrary. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary the length of a lesson provided the total weekly time is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory UAE subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which is a genuine constraint on how any tutoring in these subjects can be described or delivered.

The budgeting point is that these subjects carry real marks on a Dubai school report and real consequences for progression, yet they are almost never included when a family plans tutoring spend. An MYP student struggling in Arabic as an additional language is a common and fixable case; an MYP student whose parents discover the requirement in MYP 4 has lost years of easy progress. Ask the school which stream your child is in before you assume the subject is decorative.

sections.heading: Getting started without losing the first month
paragraphs: The first month is where most of the avoidable spend happens, because families begin paying before anybody has agreed what success looks like. The sequence that avoids it is short. Pull the last two MYP reports and write down the four criterion marks per subject rather than the grades. Identify the lowest strand, not the lowest subject. Name the next assessment that strand will be tested in, and its date. That is a brief, and a tutor can work to it from the first session.

Then take the free trial lesson. A trial is worth having for one reason: it shows whether the tutor can explain a descriptor to your child in language your child uses. If a tutor talks about the criterion without ever showing what a 7-out-of-8 answer looks like against a 4, that is the wrong tutor regardless of credentials or rate. The trial is free and carries no obligation to continue.

Be honest with yourself about volume at the start. One subject, one hour a week, reviewed after six weeks against the criterion mark you wrote down, is the booking that both works and stays affordable across five years of the programme. Two subjects is sometimes right. Four is almost never right in the MYP, and families who start at four usually end the term having spent a great deal to learn which one mattered.

If no specialist is free at the hour you want, we say so rather than filling the slot. For a niche MYP combination the honest answer is sometimes a different weekday, a different time, or a wait of a few days. For a Jumeirah 2 family that is a far better outcome than being matched with whoever was available, which is the failure mode of booking by postcode rather than by subject.

process.title: Send the report, not a summary
process.description: Share the last two MYP reports and the subject-group criterion marks. Four numbers per subject tell us more than a paragraph of description, because they show whether the obstacle is knowledge, inquiry, communication or evaluation. It takes a parent five minutes and saves a paid diagnostic session.

process.description: We write down the strand to move, the mark it sits at now, the mark we are aiming for and the assessment that will test it. A target with a date is what makes it possible to stop. Open-ended bookings are the main reason Dubai families overspend on tutoring across a five-year programme.

process.description: Matching is done on who can teach that subject group's criteria at the hour you want on Gulf Standard Time, not on who lives nearest Jumeirah 2. process.title: Take the free trial lesson

If that does not happen in the trial, it will not happen in week six either, and you should ask for a different tutor.

process.description: At six weeks we compare the criterion mark with the one written down at the start. If it has moved, the booking continues. If it has not, we change the tutor, change the target or stop. Reviewing against a number rather than a feeling is what keeps a five-year spend honest.

faqs.question: What does an IB MYP tutor in Jumeirah 2 cost per hour in 2026?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai run from roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour depending on who is teaching. EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 for budget online tutoring and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; Unitors publishes online rates from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB; TutorChase publishes AED 270; BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts a qualified specialist at AED 200 to 450 and upwards. For MYP work specifically, the AED 150 to 300 band is where a qualified subject teacher who can mark against the criteria normally sits.

faqs.question: Is MYP tutoring usually cheaper than IB Diploma tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. Diploma Higher Level subjects need a teacher who has taught that exact syllabus recently, and in Dubai there are fewer of those than there are Middle Years Programme teachers, so the scarcity premium sits on DP. A competent subject specialist handles MYP content comfortably, which keeps the sensible band at AED 150 to 300 rather than AED 400 and upwards. The practical conclusion for a family planning five years of spend is to buy mid-market during the MYP and reserve the premium budget for DP1 and DP2.

faqs.question: How many MYP sessions a week do families on the Jumeirah coast usually start with?
faqs.answer: One hour a week on one subject group is the most common and usually the right start. An MYP report shows eight subject groups, so a weak-looking report tempts parents into booking three or four tutors at once, which in Dubai costs roughly AED 1,800 to 2,400 a month at mid-market rates. In most cases a single underlying skill, such as written analysis or interpreting data, is producing low marks in several subjects simultaneously. Fix the skill once, review the criterion mark after six weeks, and add a second subject only if the first one has moved.

faqs.question: Where do parents most often waste money on MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four places. Buying hours with no target, so the booking renews forever and nobody asks whether it worked. Buying several subjects when one root skill is causing all the low marks. Paying premium Diploma rates for MYP content that a mid-market teacher handles equally well. And paying externally for work the school already supervises, such as the Personal Project or an interdisciplinary unit. The fix for all four is the same: write down a criterion mark and a date before paying, and talk to the MYP coordinator first, which costs nothing.

faqs.question: Does a budget tutor at AED 50 an hour understand MYP criteria A to D?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it is not what you are buying at that rate. The lower band of the Dubai market mostly delivers homework supervision: keeping a child on task, unblocking a question, holding a routine together. That has real value in a difficult term. What it rarely includes is the ability to look at a criterion B descriptor, explain why an investigation method sits at 4 out of 8 rather than 7, and rework the skill. Ask a direct question before booking: which criterion are we targeting, and what does a top-band response look like?

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in Jumeirah 2 for MYP lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one tuition online over live video everywhere in the UAE, and we do not provide home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors in Dubai do exist and are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits circulating widely. The difference between those figures and the online band is largely travel, not teaching quality.

faqs.question: What does the in-home travel premium actually buy on this part of the coast?
faqs.answer: Mostly it buys physical presence and a shorter pool of available teachers. A round trip to Jumeirah 2 through the 5pm window on Jumeirah Beach Road or Al Wasl Road rarely takes less than forty minutes, and that time is either priced into the hourly rate or absorbed by the tutor. When it is absorbed, the people willing to take the booking are those who live nearby, so the search narrows from subject expertise to driving distance. If a child genuinely needs someone in the room to stay on task, that premium can be worth paying.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Mathematics and Sciences for the same MYP child?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in the Middle Years Programme it is more workable than it would be at Diploma level, because the content is not yet specialised. What matters is whether the tutor knows both sets of criteria, which are different: criterion B in Mathematics is investigating patterns, while criterion B in Sciences is inquiring and designing. A teacher who treats them as the same strand will raise one and leave the other flat. Ask the question directly before booking a combined slot, and expect a specific answer about both descriptor sets.

faqs.question: How is an MYP grade out of 7 worked out from the criterion marks?
faqs.answer: Each of the four criteria in a subject is marked out of 8, giving a subject total out of 32. The school then converts that total into a 1 to 7 grade using published boundaries. This is why two children with the same grade 5 can need completely different help: one may have 7, 4, 4, 5 across the strands and the other 4, 6, 6, 4. Reading the four numbers rather than the single grade is the most useful thing a parent can do before spending anything on tutoring.

faqs.question: Should we start MYP support in MYP 3 or wait until MYP 5?
faqs.answer: It depends on which strand is weak. If criterion A marks are low, the gap is knowledge and can be caught up later without much loss. If criterion B, C or D marks are low, the gap is a skill that compounds, and waiting two years means the same skill is now being tested on harder content under more time pressure. Investigation, data processing and critical evaluation are all cheaper to build in MYP 3 than to repair in MYP 5, and they transfer directly into Diploma internal assessments afterwards.

faqs.question: What is a paid tutor allowed to do on the MYP Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. The Personal Project is supervised in school and carries a declaration that the work is the student's own. A tutor may coach the process: how to narrow a goal, how to keep a usable process journal, how to read the criteria, and what a strong reflection does. A tutor must not choose the topic, supply text to be copied, restructure the report, or produce any part of it. The test a parent can apply is simple: ask your child to explain each change and why the criterion needed it.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the MYP in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited. These subjects carry real marks on a Dubai report, so include them when you plan a tutoring budget rather than discovering them in MYP 4.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with a Jumeirah 2 family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat specific amounts you are quoted as unverified. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if we stop after the free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Nothing is owed. The trial lesson is free and carries no obligation to book anything further, and no card details are needed to take it. If you continue, you pay for the sessions you book and nothing else; there is no registration fee, no joining charge and no minimum term across a programme that runs five years. If the match is wrong after the trial, say so and we will offer a different tutor rather than asking you to persist with one your child did not respond to.

faqs.question: How should MYP eAssessment change what we pay for in MYP 5?
faqs.answer: If your school registers students for the on-screen eAssessment route to the IB MYP Certificate, MYP 5 stops being purely coursework-driven and gains a timed, externally marked component. That shifts the useful spend from open-ended weekly support towards short, targeted blocks on exam technique: reading the command term, allocating time across a paper, and writing to the descriptor under pressure. Ask the MYP coordinator whether your child is entered, because the answer changes the shape of the booking and usually reduces the total number of hours needed.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the MYP subject groups Jumeirah 3 families ask about most: Mathematics, Sciences, Language and Literature, and Individuals and Societies in Years 7 to 11. Each works in criterion language because that is the language the report card uses.

intro.heading: Why a Jumeirah 3 parent searches for this, and what the search is really about
paragraphs: Jumeirah 3 sits between Al Wasl Road and the beach, a low-rise strip of villas with Umm Suqeim on one side and Jumeirah 2 on the other. Families here send children to a handful of schools within a ten-minute drive, and several of those schools run the IB Middle Years Programme. That is the practical reason this search exists. The emotional reason is different: an MYP report card does not say 62 per cent. It says Criterion A: 5, Criterion B: 3, Criterion C: 6, Criterion D: 4, and a parent who grew up with percentages cannot tell from that whether their child is in trouble.

So the question behind "IB MYP tutor in Jumeirah 3" is rarely about distance. It is about translation. Each MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of 8, giving 32 marks that the school converts to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. A child scoring 6, 6, 6, 3 and a child scoring 5, 5, 5, 6 can land on the same overall grade while having completely different problems. The first child can do the subject and cannot reflect on it. The second is competent everywhere and brilliant nowhere. Those two children need opposite interventions, and a tutor who treats the report card as a single number will give them the same lessons.

The second thing worth saying early is geographic, and it is the angle this page is built on. Parents in Jumeirah 3 compare themselves to Jumeirah 2 and Umm Suqeim constantly, because the three areas share schools, share the Al Wasl Road crawl at 3:15pm, and share a WhatsApp group where tutor recommendations circulate. The comparison feels important. It is not. The supply of people who can mark MYP Sciences Criterion B properly does not change between Jumeirah 2 and Jumeirah 3, because there are not enough of them in either place for distance to be the deciding factor.

That is why IB Gram delivers tuition to Jumeirah 3 as one-to-one live online lessons rather than visits. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers in India only, and no page on this site should suggest otherwise. The trade is deliberate: instead of whoever is free within a short drive of Al Manara, a Year 10 student gets someone who has marked MYP Mathematics Criterion D investigations against the real descriptors and can explain why a real-life context paragraph that reads perfectly well scores 4 rather than 7.

What follows is written for the decision, not for the brochure. You will find a neighbourhood-by-neighbourhood comparison table, the criterion structure of every MYP subject group, the specific places marks leak between Year 7 and Year 11, what the Dubai market charges per hour and per month with the sources named, how MYP 5 eAssessment and the Personal Project work, where KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirements sit alongside the MYP, and the academic-honesty line a tutor must not cross on a Personal Project. If a section does not apply to your child, skip it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.programmesIntro: Jumeirah 3 children move through IB programmes in sequence, and the MYP is the long middle stretch where habits either form or do not. Here is how the four programmes connect, and what each one means for a family living between Al Wasl Road and the beach.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examinations. Children work through transdisciplinary themes and finish with the Year 6 Exhibition, a group inquiry that is the first time most of them plan, research and present something extended. Reporting is descriptive rather than numerical, which is why the jump to criterion marks in Year 7 catches families by surprise.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Jumeirah 3 run the PYP, and KHDA inspects them annually on the same six-band scale as every other private school in Dubai. Parents here often report that the PYP suited a confident reader well and left a reluctant writer without the volume of practice a British-curriculum classroom would have demanded by Year 6. That gap shows up in MYP Criterion C.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, four criteria in each, every criterion marked out of 8. Assessment is continuous and teacher-marked against published descriptors, with the Personal Project in the final year and optional eAssessment at the end of MYP 5. The programme rewards process: planning, investigating, reflecting. A child who can answer questions but cannot document how they got there loses marks they would have kept in a British classroom.
programmes.countryNote: This is the programme your search names. In Jumeirah 3 the MYP sits next to British-curriculum schools running IGCSE in the same years, so dinner-table comparisons with neighbours are inevitable and usually unhelpful - the two systems reward different things. The practical consequence locally is that MYP families cannot borrow a cousin's IGCSE past-paper routine, because the MYP has no past papers in that sense.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment is mostly external, sat in the May session that UAE schools use. HL Paper weightings and Internal Assessment criteria replace the MYP's criterion letters with a different and heavier set.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah 3 students usually decide between the DP and A Levels during MYP 5, and the decision is often made on school availability rather than suitability. International Baccalaureate schools account for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, so the DP is a minority route in the emirate even though it is heavily represented along the Jumeirah coast. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new International Baccalaureate schools.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is far less common than the DP and is not offered by most schools, but it exists and occasionally suits a student who wants IB rigour in two subjects rather than six.
programmes.countryNote: CP availability in Dubai is limited and changes year to year, so a Jumeirah 3 family considering it should check the current KHDA school listing rather than an older blog post. Where it is offered, the MYP 5 Personal Project turns out to be good preparation for the CP reflective project, because both are assessed on process documentation rather than on a finished artefact alone.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: The MYP has eight subject groups and two cross-cutting components. Each group has its own four criteria, and the criterion names tell you what the marks are actually for. Below is the list with the criteria that cause most of the trouble for students in Jumeirah 3 schools.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating patterns, C Communicating, D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. B and D are where capable students stall: B wants a conjecture tested and generalised, D wants a real context modelled and the model criticised. Pure fluency carries A and nothing else.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.levels: Integrated or separate Biology, Chemistry, Physics
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Inquiring and designing, C Processing and evaluating, D Reflecting on the impacts of science. B and C are a lab-skills pair; D asks for the ethical and global dimension and is usually the lowest mark on a Jumeirah 3 report card because it is the least taught.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.levels: English, Arabic and other school languages
subjects.description: Criteria A Analysing, B Organizing, C Producing text, D Using language. Strong readers often score well on A and lose B because their essays have no visible structure. C and D reward craft and accuracy separately, so a stylish but error-strewn piece drops only on D.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria A Comprehending spoken and visual text, B Comprehending written and visual text, C Communicating, D Using language. Phase placement matters more than year group: a child moved up a phase too quickly will look weak on every criterion when the real issue is placement.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating, C Communicating, D Thinking critically. D is the criterion that separates grades at the top: it wants sources interrogated, perspectives weighed and limitations named, not more content recalled.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria A Inquiring and analysing, B Developing ideas, C Creating the solution, D Evaluating. The design cycle is the assessment. Students who build something impressive and document nothing lose A, B and D and keep only C.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Developing skills, C Thinking creatively, D Responding. The process journal is not optional decoration; it is the evidence base for B and C, and a missing journal caps the grade regardless of the finished work.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Planning for performance, C Applying and performing, D Reflecting and improving performance. Sporty students routinely score 7 on C and 3 on B and D, because planning and reflection are written tasks they treat as an afterthought.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against its own criteria on the synthesis of two or more subject groups. Schools run these differently, so ask for the unit's task-specific clarification before assuming it mirrors a single-subject rubric.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Criteria A Planning, B Applying skills, C Reflecting, assessed on the process journal and report rather than the product. A tutor may teach project management, questioning and reflective writing; the project itself, and every word of the report, must be the student's own work.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah 3 parent is actually asking when they search for an MYP tutor
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in Jumeirah 3 is someone who can read a criterion profile and act on it. That is the whole job description. The MYP does not produce percentages, ranks or past papers, so the usual tutoring reflex - buy a question bank, do it twice - has nothing to grip. What the programme produces is four numbers per subject group, each out of 8, and a set of descriptor bands that explain what separates a 5 from a 7 in words rather than marks.

This matters because the obvious reading of a report card is almost always wrong. Take a Year 9 student with Sciences at 6, 4, 4, 3. The instinctive diagnosis is that the child is weak at science. The actual diagnosis is that the child knows the content well, cannot design a controlled investigation, cannot process data into a defensible conclusion, and has never been taught to write about the social implications of a scientific issue. Three of those four problems are skills, not knowledge, and none of them is fixed by revising harder. A tutor who starts by re-teaching the topic list will spend a term improving the only criterion that was already fine.

There is a second question hiding inside the search, which is whether proximity helps. Parents in Jumeirah 3 assume that a tutor based in Jumeirah 2, Al Safa or Umm Suqeim will somehow understand their child's school better. Occasionally that is true at the level of gossip. It is almost never true at the level of assessment, because MYP task-specific clarifications are written by individual teachers for individual units, and no tutor knows them in advance regardless of where they live. What a tutor can know in advance is the published criterion structure, and that is identical across every MYP school in Dubai.

So the honest answer to the search is this: pick for subject-group specialism and for the ability to work in criterion language, and treat location as irrelevant. IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition into Jumeirah 3 for exactly that reason. The next section puts the geography question to bed properly, with the neighbourhoods side by side.

sections.heading: Jumeirah 3 against Jumeirah 2, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim: the comparison that changes nothing
paragraphs: Here is the comparison parents make, done properly. The four areas below share arterial roads, share several school gates and share a market for tutors. The columns that look like they should differ - realistic session start, specialist availability - barely move. The column that does differ is drive time, and drive time only matters if somebody is driving.

Read the table and the pattern is plain. Every one of these neighbourhoods empties onto Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road between 3:00pm and 3:45pm. Every one of them is a twenty-to-forty-minute drive from where a specialist MYP Sciences or Mathematics tutor is likely to live, because specialists cluster around where they teach rather than around any one residential strip. And every one of them has the same realistic earliest session start once a child is home, fed and out of uniform: somewhere between 4:30pm and 5:00pm.

The one real difference is what the travel premium buys, and the answer is nothing academic. The Dubai market charges more for an in-home visit than for an online session of the same length - roughly AED 180-500 per hour in-home against AED 150-300 online for a qualified subject tutor - and that gap pays for fuel, parking and the tutor's unpaid driving time. It does not pay for better criterion feedback. A Jumeirah 3 family paying the in-home premium is buying a smaller pool of people, selected by who can reach Al Manara by 5pm.

Which is why the answer is the same in Jumeirah 3, Jumeirah 2, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim: choose the tutor who can mark the criterion, and take the lesson over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India - and the comparison above is the reason we are comfortable saying so plainly rather than burying it.

sections.heading: The MYP criterion structure, read as a diagnostic tool
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each marked on a scale of 0 to 8. Four criteria of 8 give a raw total of 32, which the school converts into a grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries it publishes. Because the criteria are named rather than numbered - Investigating patterns, Processing and evaluating, Thinking critically - the report card is a diagnosis if you read it as one.

The table below sets out the criteria for the subject groups Jumeirah 3 families most often ask about, with the failure mode that produces a low mark in each. It is worth going through it with the report card in hand, because the pattern across subjects is usually more informative than any single mark. A student low on Sciences C and Mathematics D and Individuals and Societies D does not have three subject problems. They have one problem - they cannot build an argument from data - showing up three times.

Two structural points are worth knowing before you read it. First, criteria are not weighted equally in importance even though they are weighted equally in marks: in practice the investigation and reflection criteria are the ones that cap a confident student, because they ask for documented process rather than correct answers. Second, each summative task comes with a task-specific clarification written by the teacher, which rewords the generic descriptors for that unit. Ask for it. It is the most useful single document in MYP tutoring and most parents never see one.

A tutor working properly will ask for the last two marked summative tasks, the clarification grids that went with them, and the teacher's comments. From those three things the criterion profile is obvious, and the first session can start on the actual weakness rather than on a tour of the syllabus.

sections.heading: Where MYP marks leak between Year 7 and Year 11
paragraphs: The MYP is five years long and loses marks in different places at each end. In Year 7 the problem is almost always the transition from a PYP or primary classroom where work was described rather than banded. A child who has never been marked against a descriptor writes a competent piece, scores 4, and concludes they are average. They are not average; they have not been shown what an 8 looks like. The fix is short and cheap: read three exemplars at different bands and annotate them against the criterion. Most students jump a band from that exercise alone.

By Year 8 and Year 9 the leak moves to process documentation. Sciences starts demanding a designed investigation with controlled variables and a method someone else could follow. Mathematics starts demanding a conjecture, tested cases, a generalisation and a justification. Students who are quick arrive at the right answer and write down only the answer, and the criterion that rewards the working is the one they lose. This is the point in the programme where a Jumeirah 3 parent typically starts searching, because the grade drops while the child's understanding has not.

In Year 10 the leak is breadth. Eight subject groups, each with four criteria and multiple summative tasks, produce a calendar that punishes students with no system. The marks lost here are organisational: a journal entry not made, a draft not submitted, a reflection written the night before. A tutor cannot fix a timetable, but teaching a student to log evidence as they go - a photograph, two lines, a date - protects Criterion B and C marks across every subject at once.

Year 11 is the Personal Project and the MYP 5 endgame. The project is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, and the most common failure is a student who built something genuinely good and cannot evidence how. Alongside it sits the decision between the DP, A Levels and other routes, which deserves its own conversation with the school's coordinator rather than a tutor's opinion. What a tutor can do in Year 11 is make the reflective writing specific, because 'I developed my research skills' scores nothing and 'I abandoned my first search strategy after it returned only commercial sources, and switched to the school database' scores.
bullets: Year 7: no mental model of the band descriptors - fix with annotated exemplars
Year 8-9: right answers with no documented process - the investigation criteria fall
Year 10: eight subject groups and no evidence-logging habit
Year 11: a strong Personal Project with weak reflective evidence

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs around Jumeirah 3, by the month rather than the hour
paragraphs: Most families budget monthly, so start there. A single weekly one-hour session for a full month costs roughly AED 600-1,200 at mid-market online rates, and Bestimate's Dubai rate guidance puts monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the numbers a Jumeirah 3 household is actually comparing against school fees that KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year.

Converted to hours, the published bands run as follows. Budget online tuition and university-student tutors sit at AED 45-150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor working online runs AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, sits at AED 180-500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200-500. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. At the premium end, named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650. These are other providers' published rates, dated to the October 2026 research round, not IB Gram's price list.

Two things follow for an MYP family specifically. First, the MYP has no past papers, so the cheap end of the market - tutors who work by drilling question banks - has less to sell you than it does to an IGCSE family. Paying AED 45 an hour for someone who cannot read a clarification grid is the one genuinely wasted spend in this market. Second, the in-home premium is a travel premium. The AED 180-500 band is not a better-teaching band; it overlaps almost entirely with the online specialist band and the difference is mileage.

What a parent can verify independently: ask any provider for the rate per 60 minutes rather than per lesson, ask whether the figure includes VAT, ask what happens to a cancelled session, and ask for the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit position. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service. A provider who cannot discuss it has not thought about it.

sections.heading: MYP 5 eAssessment, the Personal Project and the choice at the end of Year 11
paragraphs: Not every MYP school in Dubai enters students for eAssessment, and that is the first thing to establish rather than assume. Where a school does enter, MYP 5 results come from a mixture of on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios, plus the Personal Project, and lead to the MYP Certificate. Where a school does not, MYP 5 ends with internal reporting and the student moves on to the DP or another route without an external MYP result. Both are legitimate. Ask your school's MYP coordinator which applies, because the answer changes what Year 11 should look like.

The specific requirements for the MYP Certificate - which results count and what totals are needed - should be taken from the IB or from the school's coordinator rather than from a tutoring page, and this one deliberately does not publish a threshold. What is safe to say is the shape: on-screen examinations are sat in a session window, ePortfolios are coursework-based and moderated, and the Personal Project is assessed against its own criteria on process rather than product. Dates for IB sessions change and ibo.org is the only place to confirm them; UAE schools sit the May session.

The Personal Project deserves separate attention because it is where academic-honesty questions concentrate. The project is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, evidenced through a process journal and a report. A tutor may teach goal setting, research method, time management and reflective writing, may ask hard questions about a journal entry, and may explain what the criteria reward. A tutor may not write the report, draft the journal, produce the product or edit a submission into shape. IB academic-honesty rules make that the student's problem as well as the provider's, and the consequences for the student are severe.

On the end-of-MYP route decision, the useful tutoring contribution is evidence rather than advice. A student's criterion profile across five years says something real about whether they will cope with DP Higher Level subjects: strong investigation and reflection marks travel well into Internal Assessments, while a student carrying 3s and 4s on every reflective criterion will find the DP's coursework load heavier than the content. That is a conversation worth having in MYP 4, not in the week option forms are due.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and what inspection bands actually mean
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. A Jumeirah 3 family deals with KHDA, and the practical contact points are the annual inspection rating and the mandatory-subject rules.

Inspection ratings run on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. A band is a judgement about a school at a point in time across many measures, and it is not a prediction about any individual child's MYP criterion marks. Parents sometimes read a Good rating as a reason to add tuition and an Outstanding rating as a reason not to; neither inference holds. The report's subject-level commentary is far more useful than the headline band, and it is published on KHDA's own site.

The mandatory subjects are the part most tutoring pages ignore entirely. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states those requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

For an MYP student this creates a real timetable squeeze that nobody warns families about. The eight MYP subject groups plus mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies fill a week completely, which is why Year 9 and Year 10 students in Jumeirah 3 schools often look overloaded rather than weak. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited - a constraint any honest provider should state before offering to support them.

sections.heading: Getting started from Jumeirah 3, including what happens when nobody suitable is free
paragraphs: The useful first step is not booking a tutor. It is assembling three documents: the most recent report card with its criterion marks, the last two marked summative tasks, and the task-specific clarification grids that went with them. Those three things take ten minutes to find and make the first session twice as useful, because the tutor can start on the criterion that is actually low rather than on a diagnostic quiz the student has already sat at school.

From there the sequence is short. You describe the subject group and the criterion profile; we match a tutor who works in that subject group at MYP level; you take a free trial lesson before paying anything; and if the match is wrong you say so and we change it. Sessions run over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which in practice means a slot from 4:30pm onwards on a school day, or a morning slot in the holidays. Lessons can shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, which is worth arranging in advance rather than in the first week.

The honest part, which most providers skip: sometimes nobody suitable is free. MYP Design, MYP Arts and some Language Acquisition phases are thinly covered, and a request in exam season can take longer than a request in October. When that happens the options are a waiting position for a named tutor, a different tutor in the same subject group who can cover the specific criterion, or a straight answer that we cannot help with that combination at that time. A provider who always says yes within an hour is telling you something about their matching rather than their depth.

What we will not do is also worth stating. We do not send anybody to a UAE address; home visits are an India-only service and the comparison table earlier on this page explains why we are relaxed about that. We do not claim KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge approval, because IB Gram holds none. We do not write, complete or edit a Personal Project, an Internal Assessment or any assessed work. And we do not publish grade promises, because no tutor can honestly make one.
