process.title: Send the criterion profile
process.description: Share the latest MYP report card, the subject group you are worried about and the two most recent marked tasks. Criterion letters are enough; you do not need to diagnose anything yourself. This is the step that lets a tutor skip the first session's guesswork.

process.title: Agree the target criterion
process.description: We name the one or two criteria the first block will work on, and say what evidence of progress will look like - usually a redrafted summative response banded against the same descriptors. Vague goals produce vague lessons, so this step is written down.

process.title: Meet the tutor on a free trial
process.description: A full-length one-to-one lesson over live video at no cost, with the student's own work on screen. You are judging one thing: does this person talk about the work in criterion language and does your child follow them.

process.title: Settle a weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Pick a time that survives the Jumeirah 3 school run and sport fixtures, usually 4:30pm or later. Consistency beats intensity in the MYP because the investigation criteria improve through repetition, not through a holiday crash course.

process.title: Review against the descriptors each half term
process.description: Every six to eight weeks we compare the marked work from before and after against the same criterion bands, and either continue, change focus, or stop. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we will say so when the criterion has moved.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-first, not syllabus-first
whyPoints.description: The MYP has no past papers, so a tutor who cannot work from descriptors and clarification grids has nothing to teach from. Every match for a Jumeirah 3 MYP student is made on subject-group and criterion fluency rather than on general subject confidence.

whyPoints.title: Specialist supply instead of driving distance
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the pool is everyone qualified in that subject group rather than everyone who can reach Al Manara by 5pm. That is the single largest practical difference between this and an in-home arrangement, and the comparison table on this page shows why.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the academic-honesty line
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback. They do not write Personal Projects, journals or Internal Assessments. Competitors in this market sell completed assessed work; that is an IB malpractice trigger for the student and we say so on the page rather than in small print.

whyPoints.title: Rates discussed with sources, not slogans
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are other providers' published figures with the provider named and the reading date stated. You can check them. We would rather you compared us against a real market than against an unnamed competitor straw man.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around the UAE calendar
whyPoints.description: Sessions sit in Gulf Standard Time, move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, and pause around school assessment weeks when that is the sensible thing. A tutoring plan that ignores the local calendar gets abandoned by November.

whyPoints.title: Disclosed limits
whyPoints.description: Some MYP subject groups and Language Acquisition phases are thinly covered, and exam-season requests take longer. You get told that rather than put on a tutor who is learning the criteria alongside your child.

faqs.question: What does an MYP report card with four criterion marks actually tell me about my child in Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: It tells you four separate things, which is why averaging them hides the problem. Each MYP subject group is assessed on criteria A to D, each marked out of 8, and the names of those criteria describe different skills: knowing content, designing an investigation, communicating, and reflecting or thinking critically. A child on 6, 6, 6, 3 understands the subject and cannot reflect on it. A child on 4, 4, 4, 4 is thin everywhere. Both might show the same overall grade. Read the lowest criterion first, then check whether the same criterion is low across other subjects, because a repeated pattern is a skill gap rather than a subject gap.

faqs.question: Is a tutor based in Jumeirah 2 or Umm Suqeim better for us than one further away?
faqs.answer: Not for MYP work. Proximity would matter if somebody were driving, and it would matter if local tutors had inside knowledge of your school's assessments. Neither holds: task-specific clarifications are written by individual teachers for individual units, so no tutor has them in advance, and the published criterion structure is the same at every MYP school in Dubai. What does vary is whether a tutor can mark Sciences Criterion C or Mathematics Criterion D properly, and that pool is small across the whole emirate. Choosing by neighbourhood shrinks a small pool further for no academic return. Lessons run over live video, so the pool stays whole.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay per month for weekly MYP tuition in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Budget around AED 600-1,200 a month for one weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor online, based on published Dubai market guidance. Bestimate's rate guidance puts weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240-600 monthly at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. In-home packages run higher, at AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour visits, and that gap is travel cost rather than teaching quality. Ask any provider for the rate per 60 minutes and whether VAT is included before comparing.

faqs.question: Why does my child get good marks in class tests but low MYP criterion marks?
faqs.answer: Because class tests usually reward recall and MYP criteria mostly do not. Criterion A is the recall-shaped one; B, C and D ask for a designed investigation, data processed into a defensible conclusion, structured communication, or reflection on wider impact. A quick student arrives at the right answer and writes down only the answer, which scores on A and nothing else. The fix is not more content revision. It is practising the documented process: a conjecture tested across cases, a method someone else could follow, a conclusion that names its own limitations. That is learnable in a term and it moves two or three criteria at once.

faqs.question: Do you have MYP tutors who know the schools near Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: Tutors are matched by MYP subject group and criterion experience rather than by school, and that is deliberate. Students we support attend IB continuum schools along the Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim coast, and a tutor who has worked with several MYP schools recognises how task-specific clarifications are usually written. But IB Gram has no affiliation with any school, claims none, and would be wary of a provider implying otherwise. What matters at the first session is the clarification grid and the marked task from your child's own teacher, not a tutor's claimed familiarity with the gate.

faqs.question: What is the Personal Project and how far can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: The Personal Project runs in MYP 5 and is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, evidenced through a process journal and a report rather than through the product itself. A tutor may teach goal setting, research method, project management and reflective writing, may ask the hard questions a supervisor will ask, and may explain what each criterion rewards. A tutor may not write the report, draft journal entries, build the product or edit a submission into shape. IB academic-honesty rules put that risk on the student, and any provider offering to produce the work is selling something that can end a child's MYP.

faqs.question: Does my child's MYP school enter students for eAssessment, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: Not every MYP school in Dubai enters students, so ask your MYP coordinator rather than assume. Where a school does enter, MYP 5 results come from on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios alongside the Personal Project, leading to the MYP Certificate. Where it does not, MYP 5 ends with internal reporting and the student moves on without an external MYP result. It matters for planning: an eAssessment cohort needs timed on-screen practice in Year 11, and a non-eAssessment cohort is better served by strengthening criterion habits for the Diploma Programme. Confirm session details on ibo.org, since dates change.

faqs.question: My child is moving from PYP into MYP 1 this year. What should we do first?
faqs.answer: Show them what the bands look like before the first summative lands. The commonest Year 7 shock is a competent piece of work scoring 4, which a child reads as a verdict on themselves rather than as a descriptor band. Ask the teacher for exemplars at two or three different bands for the same task, read them with your child, and annotate against the criterion wording. Most students move a band from that exercise alone, with no tuition at all. If a tutor is involved, this is the right first session: translation, not re-teaching, because the content in MYP 1 is rarely the problem.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups are hardest to find a specialist for?
faqs.answer: Design, Arts and certain Language Acquisition phases are the thinnest, and Sciences Criterion B and C work is competitive in exam season. Mathematics and Language and Literature are the easiest to cover. We would rather tell you a combination is hard to staff than place a tutor who is learning the criteria alongside your child, so the honest answer in a thin subject is sometimes a waiting position, sometimes a tutor in the same subject group who can cover the specific criterion, and sometimes no. A provider who confirms any request within the hour is describing their sales process rather than their bench.

faqs.question: How do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies fit around eight MYP subject groups?
faqs.answer: They are required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states the requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited, and calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. Added to eight MYP subject groups, the week is full. That is why Year 9 and Year 10 students often look overloaded rather than weak, and it is worth factoring in before adding two tuition slots.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one MYP subject group for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but the limit is real. The criteria differ by subject group: Sciences Criterion B is about designing an investigation, Individuals and Societies Criterion B is about investigating sources, and the descriptors reward different things. A tutor genuinely fluent in two adjacent groups - Mathematics and Sciences, or Language and Literature and Individuals and Societies - can work across both. A tutor claiming all eight is claiming something unlikely. For a child whose weakness is one skill repeating across subjects, one tutor working on that skill in one subject often lifts the others anyway.

faqs.question: Does an MYP tutor working with a Jumeirah 3 family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is listed as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' and is applied for through its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted figure with caution. Ask your provider directly.

faqs.question: When can a session realistically start on a school day in Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: Allow 4:30pm at the earliest, and 5:00pm if there is a club or a sport fixture. School gates along Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road empty between roughly 3:00pm and 3:45pm, and the ten minutes the drive takes on paper is not the ten minutes it takes at 3:20pm. Add changing, eating and a short break and a child is ready somewhere between 4:30pm and 5:00pm. Online delivery helps here in a dull but genuine way: there is no second journey to build into the evening, so the slot can sit tighter to when the child is actually able to work.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan or school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning it in advance works better than improvising. Sessions can shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, and holiday weeks often suit a morning slot better than a late-afternoon one, which is useful for concentrated work on an investigation criterion. Term-time slots can also pause around a school's heaviest summative weeks, when adding tuition to an already full calendar makes things worse rather than better. The practical ask is simply to tell us the school's assessment calendar when you book, so the plan is built around it rather than colliding with it.

faqs.question: How will I know whether the tuition is working rather than just happening?
faqs.answer: By comparing marked work against the same criterion before and after, which means agreeing at the start which criterion is the target. Every six to eight weeks we look at a redrafted or new summative response in the same subject group, banded against the same descriptors, and ask whether the criterion has moved. A grade can stay still while a criterion rises, which is still progress. If nothing has moved after a full block, the sensible responses are a change of tutor, a change of target criterion, or stopping. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we will say so.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.closingHeading: Start with the criterion, not the postcode
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.closingBody: If you are in Jumeirah 3 holding a report card with one low criterion letter, the useful next move costs nothing: send the criterion profile and the last two marked tasks, take a free trial lesson, and judge the tutor on whether they talk about the work in the same language the school does. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Al Wasl Road school run. Whether you live in Jumeirah 3, Jumeirah 2, Al Safa or Umm Suqeim, the answer is the same, because the thing in short supply around here is not proximity - it is someone who can mark Criterion D properly.
